suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'cron routes POST /api/v1/cron and PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id are wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler.' Detection should flag role=1 (RoleMember) accounts successfully calling admin-only endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST/PATCH requests to /api/v1/cron* endpoints where authenticated user role field = 1 (RoleMember) returns HTTP 2xx and response contains cron creation confirmation, indicating privilege-boundary bypass.

suggestion.title: File-system modification of /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd by Nezha-managed agents
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names '/etc/passwd and /etc/shadow' as T1003.008 targets. Detection flags file creation or modification on these paths where initiating process traces back to shell/Nezha context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FileCreated or FileModified events on /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd where InitiatingProcessName is shell (sh, bash, dash) or CommandLine contains credential-dumping utilities (cat, head, awk, grep) and parent process is nezha-agent or Nezha-spawned cron.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Commits to Popular Language Packages
suggestion.rationale: Attack required initial repository compromise; 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos' precedes package poisoning. Detection must catch the compromise phase before malicious packages reach users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to Laravel-Lang repositories from new/anomalous IP addresses, commits lacking PR review, commits modifying dependency versions or package manifests, and commits outside normal maintenance windows. Flag commits that add unexpected external dependencies.

suggestion.title: Installation of Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' compromised; detection must trigger when developers install affected versions. This is the primary execution vector for the supply-chain attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer require / npm install / pip install of laravel-lang packages, correlate installed version against known-compromised range, and alert on unexpected code execution from vendor/laravel-lang/ directories within seconds of install. Track hash mismatches between composer.lock and installed artifact.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from Laravel Locale Package
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Laravel-Lang packages would execute attacker-controlled code in production; 'Compromised 233 Versions' implies active payload delivery on dependency load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process spawning (bash, powershell, curl, wget, nc) originating from PHP-FPM, Apache, or Nginx processes after laravel-lang namespace code execution. Monitor for unexpected DNS queries or outbound connections (port 80/443/53/5353) from web application processes post-package-load.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Untrusted or Attacker-Controlled Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires malicious packages reach package managers; 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos' likely involved pushing malicious versions to official repositories or intercepting downloads. Must detect installation from non-canonical sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (composer, npm, pip) connection logs for Laravel-Lang installs from non-packagist.org (Composer) sources. Alert on hash/signature mismatches. Detect environment variable overrides (COMPOSER_HOME, npm registry redirects) that could redirect package installs to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Takeover - Bulk Commits to Multiple Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Initial access required compromising GitHub accounts controlling Laravel-Lang and related repos; '700 GitHub Repos' hacked indicates coordinated account compromise or SSH key theft. Early-stage detection must catch unusual GitHub activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk commit activity from single IP/session to multiple popular repositories within short timeframe. Detect SSH key additions from new geographic locations or unusual IP ranges. Monitor for disabling of branch protection rules or forcing of commits to main/master branches by service accounts.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—this is the initial access vector and should trigger detection for anomalous requests to F5 management/API interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to F5 BIG-IP default management ports (443, 8443) with suspicious URI patterns (e.g., /tmui, /mgmt/tm/), especially from external sources or unusual source IPs. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and privilege escalation logs.

suggestion.title: SSH Credential Access from F5 BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers gaining 'SSH Access'—the pipeline should detect extraction or generation of SSH credentials on the BIG-IP appliance, a classic post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH key generation, export, or retrieval operations on F5 BIG-IP systems. Monitor /root/.ssh, authorized_keys modifications, and SSH-keygen invocations. Flag extraction of credentials from /etc/passwd or /etc/shadow equivalents on appliance.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: BIG-IP to Enterprise Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states pivoting 'Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—this is the lateral movement phase where BIG-IP (a trusted network appliance) is used as a pivot point to compromise downstream Linux infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP management network to internal enterprise Linux servers. Flag SSH brute-force attempts, mass parallel SSH connections, or use of extracted SSH keys from unusual source appliances. Correlate BIG-IP compromise timeline with downstream Linux authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Bypass: Appliance-to-Enterprise Pivot
suggestion.rationale: The attack leverages a network appliance (BIG-IP) as an entry point to bypass perimeter controls and reach enterprise systems—detection should focus on abnormal egress from trusted infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH, RDP, or WinRM traffic from F5 BIG-IP internal segments to enterprise server subnets. Establish baseline of legitimate BIG-IP-to-server communications and alert on deviations: new destination IPs, mass parallel connections, off-hours activity, or connections to systems normally not accessed by BIG-IP.

suggestion.title: SSH Public Key Injection / SSH Key Installation to Persist Access
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence via SSH typically involves injecting attacker-controlled public keys into authorized_keys on compromised systems—a technique implied by the pivot narrative but not explicitly detected by the pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, /home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys, and SSH daemon configuration files on enterprise Linux systems. Monitor for injection of new public keys alongside lateral movement from BIG-IP. Correlate file changes with SSH login attempts using newly added key fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious helpers.php Addition to Composer Autoload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the malicious releases introduced a malicious file named src/helpers.php, which was automatically loaded by Composer'. This is the initial payload delivery mechanism after tag rewrite. No detection generated for this critical indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications or version installations that introduce unexpected entries in the autoload sections, particularly 'src/helpers.php'. Alert when legitimate package versions suddenly gain new autoload declarations not present in public repository commits.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Callbacks to flipboxstudio[.]info C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dropper that downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info'. Explicit C2 domain mentioned but not extracted as IOC or detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/S connections initiated by PHP interpreter processes (php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php-fpm) to domain flipboxstudio[.]info or IP resolution thereof. Flag as high-risk if source process is loading from vendor/laravel-lang/ directory.

suggestion.title: Multi-Format Credential Harvesting Regex Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Regular expression patterns used to extract AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Slack tokens, Stripe secrets, database credentials, JWTs, SSH private keys, and cryptocurrency recovery phrases from files and environment variables.' Credential extraction is the attack objective but no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes invoking regex-matching operations or string-scanning libraries against sensitive file paths (.env, .ssh/*, browser storage paths, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config). Alert on sequential access to multiple secret-bearing locations within short time window.

suggestion.title: Windows DebugElevator Embedded Executable Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals: 'Windows infostealer shows it is named DebugElevator and designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys'. Embedded base64 executable decoded and written to %TEMP% folder. This is a distinct Windows-specific payload stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process writing binary content (via base64 decode) to %TEMP% directory with random .exe filename, followed immediately by process creation of that executable. Correlate with parent process owning suspicious Laravel Lang package references.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Tag Rewrite with Org-Wide Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'rewrote every existing git tag in each repository to point at a new malicious commit' across 'laravel-lang/lang (502 tags)' and other repos using 'one compromised credential with org wide push access'. This is the supply-chain entry point but no GitHub-activity detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk tag rewrite operations against organization repositories, especially when tags are rewritten to point to commits in forked or external repositories rather than the canonical repository commit history. Flag accounts performing org-wide tag rewrites outside normal release workflows.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Credential Blob Exfiltration to C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'once the sensitive data has been extracted, the malware encrypts it and sends it back to the C2 server'. The final exfiltration phase to flipboxstudio[.]info involves encrypted payloads but no detection rule generated for this telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes establishing persistent or repeated connections to flipboxstudio[.]info or subdomains, especially transmitting POST/PUT requests with binary or base64-encoded body content of suspicious size and entropy patterns. Correlate with prior credential-access activity on the same host.

suggestion.title: Suspicious require() / autoload injection in PHP packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised' — supply chain attack likely injected malicious code into composer package autoload or require statements. Pipeline missed the core execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP processes for unusual require() or include() of external URLs or temporary file paths immediately after package installation. Detect autoload.php modifications outside package manager control. Alert on PHP spawning child processes (curl, wget) to fetch remote payloads.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration from PHP web applications
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Credential Stealer' — pipeline should detect credential access behavior: keystroke logging, environment variable theft, .env file access, or HTTP exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes reading .env files, environment variables, or session storage. Detect unusual outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from PHP processes to non-CDN IPs. Alert on PHP accessing password managers, browser keystroke capture libraries, or curl/wget commands to exfiltration URLs.

suggestion.title: Compromised package version spike in dependency graph
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack requires malicious version push or account takeover. Monitor for unusual version bumps, yanked/re-released versions, or rapid version iteration within hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Laravel-Lang or dependency packages with version released outside normal cadence (e.g., patch released at 2 AM UTC outside business hours). Monitor for version deletions and re-uploads. Correlate with package maintainer account login anomalies or MFA bypasses.

suggestion.title: PHP malware persistence via composer.json modifications
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package persists by modifying composer.json scripts or require directives. Article describes 'cross-platform' stealer suggesting multiple deployment vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json, composer.lock, and autoload.php for modifications outside manual DevOps workflows. Alert on PHP scripts auto-executing on framework initialization (ServiceProvider registration in Laravel). Detect script-based privilege escalation or user creation post-installation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Laravel framework internals by malicious package
suggestion.rationale: A credential stealer needs to discover application config, database credentials, and API keys. Likely probes Laravel's config directory, env() calls, or DI container for secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes reading config/database.php, config/app.php, or calling env() functions immediately after package load. Monitor directory traversal from PHP webroot to parent directories containing .env or config. Alert on reflection/introspection of Laravel Application container.

suggestion.title: Network beaconing from compromised Laravel application
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer exfiltrates stolen data to attacker-controlled C2. Should detect outbound connections from PHP application server to unknown domains or IPs, especially over non-standard ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS from application servers to IPs without reverse DNS or SSL certs matching known cloud CDNs. Detect DNS lookups for newly registered domains from PHP processes. Alert on exfiltration of environment variables, database credentials, or session tokens in HTTP POST payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Autoload File Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injected helpers.php file was wired into Composer's autoload.files entry, causing it to run on every PHP request.' Core execution vector bypassing normal code review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to composer.json autoload.files array where newly-added .php files appear, especially in src/helpers.php or bootstrap locations. Correlate with Composer install events; flag automatic loading of unexpected PHP code at application startup.

suggestion.title: Git Tag Spoofing Across Organization Boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases of the official package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package org tags (laravel-lang/*) resolve to commits in fork repositories outside the organization. Cross-reference tag metadata with actual commit source; flag when tag points to attacker-controlled fork SHA.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication to flipboxstudio[.]info
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents two C2 channels: 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block and alert on all outbound traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info domain. Monitor PHP runtime, composer, and shell process network calls for HTTPS/HTTP communication to this C2; flag both payload delivery (port 443 POST to /payload) and exfiltration (POST to /exfil).

suggestion.title: Credential and Secrets Multi-Source Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Second-stage stealer 'walks through a long list of sources looking for anything of value: Cloud provider credentials... Kubernetes kubeconfig files... SSH private keys... .env files... Browser data... Password manager vaults... Cryptocurrency wallet files... Messaging tokens.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process chains enumerating multiple secret storage locations (AWS ~/.aws, Kubernetes ~/.kube, SSH ~/.ssh, browser profile directories, LastPass/1Password vaults) within short time window. Alert when single process accesses 3+ distinct credential sources sequentially.

suggestion.title: Infection Marker Guard File Creation in Temp Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: payload 'writes an infection marker to a per-host temporary directory so the host is only infected once.' Indicates single-execution guard mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor system temp directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp) for suspicious marker files created by PHP or web application processes. Flag UUID-style or hash-named temporary files that correlate temporally with Composer installs or application startup.

suggestion.title: Platform-Aware Polyglot Malware Execution Branch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The launcher logic is platform-aware and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows.' Unusual OS detection branching in typical web application context indicates staged/polyglot malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning that includes OS detection logic (uname, $OSTYPE, wmic, powershell -Command 'Get-Host') before execution. Flag polyglot scripts or shell invocations containing conditional branches on operating system in web application runtimes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 LiteSpeed Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states CVE-2026-48172 is being exploited. No detection rule generated for the known vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to LiteSpeed cPanel plugin endpoints with payloads characteristic of CVE-2026-48172 exploitation. Track failed authentication or suspicious parameter injection attempts against known vulnerable paths.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution via LiteSpeed Service
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'scripts as root' — privilege escalation is the core impact. Pipeline missed this privilege escalation indicator entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent processes running as lighttpd or cPanel service spawning child processes with system/root privileges. Flag unexpected script interpreters (bash, perl, python) launched from LiteSpeed directories with UID 0.

suggestion.title: Script Execution from LiteSpeed Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'scripts' execution from the plugin. No detection generated for code execution via the vulnerable plugin component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation originating from LiteSpeed plugin paths (typically /usr/local/lsws/ or /opt/lsws/). Track execution of scripting engines (sh, bash, perl, python) with command-line arguments suggesting remote input.

suggestion.title: Abnormal cPanel Administrative Action via LiteSpeed Plugin
suggestion.rationale: LiteSpeed integrates with cPanel for hosting control. Exploitation enabling root access suggests admin-level actions. No detection for cPanel API abuse or privilege escalation from the service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudo invocations or administrative API calls initiated by lighttpd, www, or nobody users. Flag cPanel administrative functions executed outside normal user context.

suggestion.title: Nginx Malformed Request Pattern - Poolslip Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'enables DoS and Code Execution Attacks' via unspecified request patterns. Pipeline generated no detection for exploitation attempts. Citation: 'Enables DoS and Code Execution Attacks'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Nginx HTTP requests with abnormal header counts, oversized payloads, or rapid sequential requests to the same connection that precede 5xx errors or process crashes. Correlate request patterns with memory pool allocation patterns if available.

suggestion.title: Nginx Worker Process Crash and Restart Cascade
suggestion.rationale: DoS capability implies crash-based disruption. No detection logic captures repeated process termination cycles characteristic of pool exhaustion. Citation: 'DoS and Code Execution Attacks'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nginx worker process crashes (segfaults, signal 11) occurring within 10-second windows of unusual HTTP request sequences. Detect master process spawning replacement workers at abnormal frequency (>3 in 60s).

suggestion.title: Nginx Memory Exhaustion During Connection Pooling
suggestion.rationale: Pool-related DoS typically starves memory via connection object accumulation. No behavioral detection for resource anomalies during specific request patterns. Citation: 'poolslip Vulnerability' targeting pool management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx worker memory growth trajectories; alert when single worker exceeds configured pool size limits or grows >50MB/min. Correlate with request arrival rates to distinguish legitimate traffic spikes from exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution in Nginx Context
suggestion.rationale: Article claims 'Code Execution' capability, but no use case detects process injection, shell spawning, or binary execution from Nginx PID. Citation: 'Code Execution Attacks'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from Nginx workers (bash, sh, curl, wget). Flag any file writes from Nginx to /tmp or executable directories. Monitor for unexpected library loading via LD_PRELOAD or LD_LIBRARY_PATH from Nginx context.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Package Publish Without 2FA
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 2FA-gated publishing as the core control. Absence of use case to detect publishes bypassing or circumventing 2FA is critical gap. Article states npm is adding controls specifically to prevent unauthorized package release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish API calls from accounts with disabled or missing 2FA enforcement. Correlate successful publishes with auth events lacking MFA verification. Alert on version releases from previously inactive maintainers or outside normal publish windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Dependency Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'package install controls' as mitigation. Pipeline should surface detection for installation patterns that bypass installation restrictions, as described in the control mechanism article proposes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installs of packages with mismatched version signatures, installs from non-standard registries not in org whitelist, or installs that override local package restrictions. Alert on install attempts of packages flagged as high-risk in npm's malware detection.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover of Package Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Article context is supply chain attack prevention. Maintainer account compromise (credential access) is the precursor to malicious publishes. No detection use case addresses this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual geolocation or device on npm account logins, multiple failed auth attempts followed by success, API key creation immediately preceding publish events, or publish activity outside maintainer's normal patterns (time, IP, device).

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article references controls on package installation. Attackers may modify package.json, tarball signatures, or registry metadata to evade install controls. No use case addresses metadata tampering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package metadata changes (description, dependencies, dist integrity) that occur post-publication. Alert on packages where npm-reported hash differs from download hash, or where dependency tree unexpectedly changes between minor versions.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Registration Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses package controls. Attackers circumvent these by registering lookalike names. Pipeline should detect registration of packages with names similar to popular packages or internal org packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registration of new packages with names that are off-by-one character, homograph variants, or scope-confusion patterns (e.g., @legit/package vs @legit-package). Cross-reference against known popular packages and org internal package lists.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Code Execution via Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes install controls. Attackers may use npm's postinstall hooks to execute malicious code despite package being 'allowed'. This execution vector is not covered by generated use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by npm during install phase, particularly shells (cmd.exe, bash, powershell). Alert on packages with install scripts that download additional payloads, modify system files, or establish persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Upload to Package Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages'—indicates attackers compromised or uploaded malicious packages to a package repository. No detection coverage was generated for this initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository upload events for Laravel-Lang namespace for packages authored by previously unseen accounts, packages with suspicious naming variations (typosquatting), or sudden ownership changes. Alert on packages uploaded within hours of known maintainer activity gaps.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article headline identifies 'Credential Stealer' as payload. Typical supply chain attack pattern: malicious package executes install hooks or post-install scripts to exfiltrate credentials. No detection was surfaced for this execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install / composer install processes spawning unusual child processes (Python, PowerShell, curl, wget) immediately after Laravel-Lang package installation. Alert on post-install script execution that makes unexpected network connections or accesses credential storage locations (.env, .aws, .ssh).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials via HTTP/DNS from Development Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implant must exfiltrate stolen data. Article indicates credential theft but pipeline generated no detection for data exfiltration channels or suspicious outbound connections from affected developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation hunt: identify hosts running Laravel-Lang packages (composer.json or package-lock analysis) with simultaneous outbound HTTP/DNS activity to unknown or suspicious domains within 5–30 minutes of npm install completion. Flag TLS/DNS traffic not matching known CDN or package registry IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment File Access by Package Installation Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealers commonly target .env files in Laravel projects to steal database and API credentials. Article mentions credential stealing but no detection was generated for file system access patterns typical of this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file read operations on .env, .env.local, config/ directories, or ~/.aws, ~/.ssh by processes spawned during or immediately after package manager operations (npm, composer). Alert on non-root processes reading .env files outside normal application runtime.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerable Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CISA KEV entry with 'currently exploited in the wild' status. 'Asset-exposure hunt' is explicitly recommended in the article; requires detection of vulnerable Drupal Core versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner outputs and asset inventory systems for Drupal Core installations matching CVE-2026-9082 affected versions. Cross-reference with Drupal version reporting from web server fingerprinting. Flag publicly accessible instances on ports 80/443.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attacks Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'SQL injection vulnerability... specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' This is the exploitation mechanism and should generate network/WAF detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal instances for SQL injection patterns targeting database abstraction API endpoints. Flag requests containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, WHERE, DROP) in unusual parameters. Correlate with POST requests to Drupal API endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, /db/*).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation via SQL Injection RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'privilege escalation and remote code execution.' Pipeline did not surface execution or privilege escalation techniques despite clear description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution and file creation following HTTP 200/302 responses to suspicious Drupal API requests. Track database user privilege changes, unusual sudo/su execution from web server process context, or shell spawning from PHP/Apache processes.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database User Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'privilege escalation' outcome from SQL injection. Database activity monitoring should detect unauthorized privilege grants or role changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database logs for GRANT/ALTER statements or privilege changes on Drupal database users. Flag unexpected elevation of web-server-owned database accounts or role assignments that elevate permissions beyond normal application scope.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Drupal SQL Injection Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'remote code execution' as possible outcome. Pipeline should detect command execution phase post-SQL-injection exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected shell command execution (sh, bash, powershell) spawned from web server processes (apache, nginx, PHP-FPM) or database backend processes. Track file writes to webroot directories followed by HTTP requests. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP requests to Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core Patch Application Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date (2026-05-27) and states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Asset verification should confirm patches are applied despite scanner false negatives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare Drupal Core file hashes and version markers against known patched versions for CVE-2026-9082. Monitor instances where vulnerability scanners report 'patched' but file integrity checks or version strings indicate vulnerable code is still present. Flag version mismatches.

suggestion.title: LNK shortcut executing remote PowerShell via Command Line obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' No use case for this critical initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for explorer.exe or cmd.exe spawning PowerShell with -Command or -EncodedCommand flags referencing remote HTTP(S) URLs or base64 payloads. Parent process LnkStub.exe or direct explorer.exe child. Alert on suspicious LNK creation in temp directories or Downloads.

suggestion.title: Registry Run key masquerading as legitimate browser name
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup.' No detection for this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKCU equivalent for new values pointing to temp directories or non-standard paths. Flag entries using browser names (YandexBrowser, Chrome, Edge, Firefox) with mismatch to actual binary location or .ps1 extension.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH tunnel establishment and termsrv.dll patching for RDP persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'Reverse SSH tunneling,' 'Patched OpenSSH,' and 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll.' No coverage of SSH+RDP-based C2 or persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH processes with reverse port forwarding flags (-R, -D) or unusual SSH parent processes (PowerShell, services.exe). Monitor termsrv.dll (typically %windir%\system32\) for write access or in-memory patching. Track RDP listener port changes and non-standard RDP session configurations.

suggestion.title: Tor and RevSocks proxy usage for C2 obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'Tor tunneling,' 'RevSocks,' and describes multi-proxy C2. No use case for detecting these legitimate tools abused for C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to known Tor exit nodes or directory authorities. Alert on RevSocks proxy spawning (revsocks.exe or variants) or unusual local port listening combined with forwarding rules. Detect Tor bridge configurations or .onion domain resolution attempts.

suggestion.title: PowerShower credential grabber execution and input capture
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber)' but no detection use case for this malware capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShower execution or PowerShell scripts performing GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx, or LSA/credential store enumeration. Alert on clipboard access loops, keylogger-like API patterns, or SAM/LSASS dump attempts.

suggestion.title: ZIP archive with LNK shortcut delivery via phishing email
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Cloud Atlas remains consistent in using phishing... emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file as an attachment.' No IOC extraction or detection for this delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ZIP archives with LNK files inside arriving via email gateway. Monitor for multiple recipients or same subject/sender creating LNK files in user Downloads/temp. Track detonation of suspicious LNK files that execute remote script downloads.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payloads in HTTP Requests to Drupal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' — detection must target HTTP parameters containing SQL keywords or metacharacters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs for requests to Drupal paths (admin, user, search, api) containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR, INSERT, DROP) or URL-encoded metacharacters ('%27', '%3D'). Correlate with 400/500 error responses indicating failed or error-based injection attempts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Query Log Syntax Errors and Malformed SQL
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the flaw 'affects Drupal's database abstraction API' and targets 'sites using PostgreSQL' — detection must identify injection indicators in database error logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL error logs for syntax errors (unexpected token, relation does not exist) in queries from web server or Drupal application user contexts; UNION-based payloads; access to system catalogs; and rapid-fire query patterns deviating from baseline.

suggestion.title: Process Execution Following SQL Injection (RCE Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution' — detection must identify shell process spawning post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PHP process (php-fpm, php-cgi) spawning bash/sh or command utilities (curl, wget, nc) following detected SQL injection attempts. Correlate with unexpected file writes to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Database Privilege Escalation via Injected SQL
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'privilege escalation' as a potential impact — detection must capture GRANT, ALTER USER, or SET ROLE commands executed post-injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL security logs for GRANT, ALTER USER, CREATE ROLE, or SET ROLE issued by the Drupal application user context. Flag elevation of www-data or drupal user to superuser; assumption of unintended administrative roles.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Extraction from Drupal Core Tables
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'information disclosure' as a threat — detection must capture large-scale SELECT queries from users, sessions, and sensitive Drupal tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SELECT queries from users, sessions, and field_* tables with result sets exceeding baseline (10k+ rows). Monitor for outbound HTTP responses >50MB gzipped coinciding with database activity; correlate with egress to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Drupal Instance Detection (CVE-2026-9082 Version Ranges)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions: 8.9.x, 10.4.x<10.4.10, 10.5.x<10.5.10, 10.6.x<10.6.9, 11.0–11.1<11.1.10, 11.2.x<11.2.12, 11.3.x<11.3.10 — detection must identify unpatched deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint Drupal version via X-Drupal-Version headers or response patterns. Flag instances matching vulnerable ranges: 8.9.x, 10.4.0–9, 10.5.0–9, 10.6.0–8, 11.0–1.9, 11.2.0–11, 11.3.0–9 as active exploitation targets.

suggestion.title: VPN Takedown Infrastructure—Ransomware C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states VPN was used by '25 Ransomware Groups'—indicates shared C2 infrastructure. Pipeline should surface detection for command and control traffic to compromised VPN endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from corporate endpoints to VPN infrastructure IPs/domains identified in takedown. Ransomware operators typically establish persistent beaconing patterns through shared infrastructure. Correlate with known ransomware C2 signatures and behavioral indicators (regular intervals, obfuscated payloads, DNS tunneling attempts).

suggestion.title: Ransomware Staging & Delivery via Confiscated VPN Servers
suggestion.rationale: Takedowns typically recover stage-2 payloads, ransom notes, and staging tools on seized infrastructure. Article title indicates law enforcement action—should detect payload hosting/delivery from confiscated servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on script execution, binary drops, or suspicious downloads originating from identified VPN infrastructure. Ransomware campaigns commonly use seized infrastructure to host secondary payloads, credential dumpers, and extensibility tooling post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Through VPN Compromise Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Multi-group VPN compromise suggests shared pivot infrastructure for internal reconnaissance and lateral spread. Article mentions organized ransomware operations—should detect secondary target reconnaissance through VPN nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internal hosts establishing connections through identified VPN endpoints followed by network scanning activity, process enumeration, or privilege escalation attempts. Ransomware operators stage post-compromise discovery and pivoting through shared infrastructure.

suggestion.title: VPN Infrastructure—Ransomware Persistence & Backdoor Communication
suggestion.rationale: Takedowns of shared criminal infrastructure target persistence mechanisms. Article indicates dismantling of active operational infrastructure—should surface persistence IOCs and backdoor communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation, registry persistence artifacts, or WMI event subscriptions with callbacks to identified VPN infrastructure. Ransomware groups often install persistent backdoors through shared infrastructure for multi-stage attacks.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Through VPN Provider Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: VPN used by 25 ransomware groups likely facilitates data exfiltration and ransom negotiation. Article title indicates infrastructure takedown—should surface exfiltration patterns through confiscated endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data transfers (archive creation + network egress) to identified VPN infrastructure IPs. Ransomware operators typically exfiltrate sensitive data through anonymous infrastructure before encryption. Look for consistent connection timing, encrypted tunnels, or HTTPS traffic with high entropy payloads.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Affiliate Network Coordination via VPN
suggestion.rationale: 25 discrete ransomware groups using single VPN suggests affiliate coordination hub. Article scope indicates organized multi-group operations—should detect traffic patterns consistent with criminal infrastructure pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify cluster of internal compromised hosts connecting to same VPN infrastructure across different threat groups' campaigns (temporal clustering, divergent payload signatures). VPN infrastructure used by multiple affiliates shows characteristic multi-hop patterns and traffic desynchronization to evade correlation analysis.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Access and Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes typosquatting: 'domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions' with example fifa26[.]shop. No detection rule for lookalike FIFA/World Cup domains or character-substitution variations on sporting event domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolution and HTTP access to domains matching World Cup/FIFA patterns using suspicious TLDs (.shop, .info, .xyz) or single-character substitutions of legitimate domains. Correlate with certificate issuance timing around major sporting events.

suggestion.title: Fake Registration Form Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article details fake registration page collecting 'name, email address, and phone number' as first step in credential theft. Figures 4 and 5 show near-identical forms on legitimate vs. fake sites. No detection for PII collection on phishing domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to registration endpoints on non-FIFA domains containing form fields for email, phone, full name, and account password. Correlate requests on typosquatted domains with legitimate FIFA domain SSL cert mismatches.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Details Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site'. Figures 9 and 12 show credit card form fields on fake checkout pages. No detection for payment card harvesting on fraudulent merchant domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on form submissions containing credit card patterns (card number, expiry, CVV) to non-PCI-compliant or unregistered domains. Flag multi-field payment forms on typosquatted ticket/merchandise domains, especially with short response times before redirect.

suggestion.title: High-Fidelity Phishing Site Clone Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes visual deception: 'copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow'. Figures compare fake vs. legitimate pages side-by-side with near-identical structure. No detection for DOM/CSS similarity to legitimate sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform fuzzy hash matching (SSDEEP, pHash) or DOM-tree similarity analysis on HTTP responses from suspected phishing domains vs. known-good FIFA domain baseline. Alert on >85% structural similarity hosted on non-FIFA infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Sponsored Search / Social Media Ad Click to Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email messages'. No detection for referrer chain analysis linking ad platforms to typosquatted domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP referrer headers originating from Google Ads, Facebook Ads, and sponsored search platforms pointing to World Cup/FIFA typosquatted domains. Alert on campaigns with high conversion rates to registration or checkout pages.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Phishing Funnel Completion: Register → Select → Cart → Checkout
suggestion.rationale: Article traces complete attack sequence: 'register, add tickets for a game, jerseys or other merchandise to the cart, and pay'. Figures 10-12 show sequential registration, match selection, cart, and payment pages. No detection for users completing multiple stages of fraudulent purchasing flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequential HTTP requests on phishing domain: POST /register → GET /events → POST /cart → POST /payment with credential fields. Alert on single source completing ≥2 stages within minutes, especially with subsequent suspicious login attempts on legitimate services.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exposed Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack beginning with 'exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or access patterns. Need detections for unauthenticated or abnormal admin panel requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to F5 BIG-IP admin interfaces (port 443, /admin, /tmui paths) from external sources without corresponding authenticated sessions. Detect POST requests to configuration endpoints from untrusted IPs.

suggestion.title: Confluence RCE or Credential Extraction via Java Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'pivot to internal Confluence server for credential theft and identity compromise' but no exploitation path, request patterns, or Java process anomalies were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Confluence process spawning unexpected Java child processes or bash shells. Monitor for POST requests to /wiki/pages with serialized object payloads or unusual Content-Type headers indicating gadget chain exploits.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping from Confluence Database or Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'credential theft and identity compromise' but pipeline missed detection of LDAP queries, SQL reads against user tables, or memory access patterns from Confluence process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Confluence Java process executing LDAP queries with wildcard filters or direct reads of /var/confluence/database files. Flag unusual network egress from Confluence toward identity providers (LDAP/AD servers) with large result sets.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay / GSS-API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'attempted Kerberos relay' but zero IOCs, token patterns, or HTTP negotiation anomalies were surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound HTTP Negotiate-Auth headers being relayed outbound without credential confirmation. Detect ntlmrelayx or similar tools via repeated 401 → 200 sequences without NTLM signature validation or Kerberos AP-REQ reuse.

suggestion.title: Linux Process Lateral Movement from F5 / Confluence Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-stage attack on 'Linux devices' with lateral movement but pipeline extracted zero process execution IOCs, SSH key theft, or inter-host communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag SSH or RCP process execution from Confluence or F5 process contexts, especially with stolen credentials. Detect unexpected bash or python spawning from Java processes (Confluence) or tcpdump/tshark from root.

suggestion.title: ADCS / Domain Controller Takeover via Kerberos Relay + Confluence Creds
suggestion.rationale: Kerberos relay often chains to ADCS certificate enrollment or S4U2Self abuse; article mentions 'identity compromise' suggesting domain-level impact, but pipeline missed detection of ESC8/ESC1 enrollment or S4U ticket generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual ADCS certificate enrollment requests from low-privilege service accounts or via relay. Flag certreq.exe spawning from Confluence-compromised context or Certificate Request events (Event 4887) with template abuse signatures.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Phishing Malware Delivery via Spear-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware'—explicitly names phishing as delivery vector and Prometheus as payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails to Ukrainian government domains (*.gov.ua, rada.gov.ua, security ministry domains) containing macro-enabled Office documents, .exe/.dll attachments, or shortened URLs. Correlate sender reputation with Ghostwriter OSINT artifacts. Baseline: typical spear-phishing has <5 targets per organization.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Process Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in phishing+malware delivery; victims must execute payload. Article provides no technical details but common for dropper execution via user action (double-click, macro enable).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process spawning from user Downloads, Desktop, or Temp directories immediately post-email interaction. Prometheus likely executes via rundll32, powershell, or cmd wrappers. Alert on unsigned executables or known-malicious parents.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter C2 Communication from Compromised Government Systems
suggestion.rationale: Malware payload (Prometheus) must establish command channel; article provides no C2 infrastructure details, yet this is core to any APT persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP from .gov.ua networks to non-Ukrainian, non-CDN IPs with abnormal TLS certificates or domains registered post-2024. Prometheus C2 likely mimics legitimate traffic; profile baseline gov.ua egress first.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Ukraine Government to Ghostwriter C2
suggestion.rationale: Ghostwriter is state-nexus APT with intelligence collection mandate; phishing malware on government entities strongly implies data theft objective. Article context (Ukraine + Russia-linked actor) confirms this motivation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk file access (>100 files/hour, unusual patterns) on sensitive shares with suspicious archive creation (.zip, .rar, .7z) and subsequent C2 uploads. Flag access to classified/intelligence directories followed by exfil within 24h.

suggestion.title: Registry/Persistence Mechanism for Prometheus Malware
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated APT malware establishes persistence; Prometheus on government systems likely employs Run keys, scheduled tasks, or WMI for lateral movement persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for suspicious entries. Alert on alternate data streams (ADS) on system binaries. Correlate with Prometheus execution metadata.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter Actor Attribution via OSINT/Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Ghostwriter' as threat actor; pipeline should surface attribution indicators (infrastructure, TTPs, historical campaigns) to enable blocking and threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Prometheus C2 IPs/domains against known Ghostwriter infrastructure (previous campaigns, joint attribution reports). Alert on historical malware families (NotPetya, BadRabbit, etc.) re-use. Block at perimeter; add to EDR watchlist.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection payload in YesWiki Bazar form-import POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement' but pipeline has no detection for actual SQL syntax (UNION, OR 1=1, comment sequences, SLEEP, etc.) in HTTP POST parameters to vue=formulaire endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to YesWiki Bazar form-import (path contains 'formulaire' or 'BazaR') where request body or URL parameters contain SQL keywords (UNION, OR, AND, SLEEP, BENCHMARK, /\*.*\*/, --, #) common in injection attacks. High-confidence if coupled with FROM/SELECT targeting database tables.

suggestion.title: Access to yeswiki_users password table via form-import
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically notes attacker goal: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Pipeline missed data-access layer detection targeting credential extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If database query logs available: SELECT queries on yeswiki_users table, particularly filtering or exfiltrating password column, correlated with injection attempts in HTTP logs. If HTTP only: look for POST responses with large result sets or binary/hash-like data patterns returned from form-import endpoint.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500 errors with SQL error verbosity from YesWiki Bazar form-import
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection probing typically generates database error messages that leak schema/syntax info. Article describes 'INSERT' statement sink but doesn't exclude error-based detection path common in SQLi reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Bazar form-import endpoint (vue=formulaire) for HTTP 500 responses whose body contains SQL error keywords (syntax error, unexpected, column, table, check constraint) when correlated with suspicious parameter values in the request.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum PATCH path traversal with hash-based share authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'hash-based authentication token in uri_query combined with traversal payload in body'. Pipeline hunts missed the **compound pattern** — successful exploitation requires both hash parameter AND path traversal. UC_21_1 searches for traversal but doesn't correlate hash usage as bypass signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH /public/api/resources requests where: (1) uri_query contains hash parameter, (2) request_body contains fromPath or toPath with .. traversal, (3) HTTP status is 2xx (successful) or 4xx attempting unauthorized path. Cross-correlate successful attempts with subsequent file system events.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum post-exploitation: file operations outside share root
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows file ops outside shared directory' but recommended hunts focus only on HTTP detection. Missing impact-phase hunt for downstream file system consequences: move/copy/rename operations reaching parent directories or other shares.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileBrowser process (or service account) for rename/move/copy operations initiated by HTTP request to /public/api/resources, where destination path traverses above configured share_root or targets sibling directories. File system ACLs should prevent this; any success indicates successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public-facing instance enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of 'public share' endpoint. Missing reconnaissance hunt for internet-exposed FileBrowser instances. Asset exposure template only matches vulnerable CVE version; doesn't detect public accessibility misconfiguration itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200/404 responses to /public/api/resources from external/non-whitelisted sources. Successful schema enumeration (200) indicates public-facing FileBrowser; 404 from authenticated routes indicates version fingerprinting. Pattern: external source probing /public/* paths without authentication headers.

suggestion.title: Telecom ISP C2 Infrastructure Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'large-scale command-and-control operations' via 'Middle East telecom networks'—threat actors leveraging carrier infrastructure for C2. Pipeline produced no detection for abuse of ISP/carrier IP ranges or ASNs for C2 beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume or anomalous DNS/HTTP traffic to known Middle East telecom ASNs or carrier-hosted C2 domains. Correlate outbound connections from compromised internal hosts to telecom infrastructure with known malware C2 signatures. Alert on sustained communication to new or rare Middle East telecom IP ranges from a single internal source over extended periods.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Botnet C2 Beaconing Cluster Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'large-scale' operations—suggesting multiple compromised hosts reporting to shared C2. Pipeline missed opportunity to detect characteristic botnet beacon patterns (uniform intervals, shared destinations, similar payloads).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of internal hosts establishing similar connection patterns to a single external destination on the same port/protocol within a time window. Alert when more than N hosts (threshold: 10+) connect to the same C2 endpoint with identical User-Agents, request intervals, or payload signatures.

suggestion.title: Telecom Network Lateral Movement via C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Abuse of 'telecom networks' for C2 implies attacker movement within carrier infrastructure. Pipeline produced no lateral movement detection despite article describing scale suggesting multi-stage compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate C2 communications with subsequent lateral movement attempts (RDP, SMB, SSH) to adjacent hosts within the same telecom carrier environment. Alert on internal pivoting that follows established C2 communication patterns—e.g., beaconing host initiates SMB/RDP to peer after C2 callback.

suggestion.title: Middle East Telecom ISP Carrier Account Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale operations against carrier networks imply reconnaissance phase. Article describes targeting of 'Middle East telecom networks' but pipeline missed discovery/reconnaissance use cases preceding abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries or connections to Middle East telecom carrier administrative interfaces, BGP route leak detection tools, or carrier-specific vulnerability disclosures before C2 abuse manifests. Alert on reconnaissance of carrier infrastructure (WHOIS, AS number enumeration, mail server discovery) from internal hosts followed within hours by C2 callbacks to carrier IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious process execution spawned from node_modules context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes backdoor in npm package — when application loads or installs art-template, malicious code would execute; detection should flag cmd.exe/powershell child processes with node.exe/npm parent or cwd under node_modules
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe or npm.cmd spawns suspicious children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl.exe, wget) with working directory or image path under node_modules. Correlate timing with npm install or application startup.

suggestion.title: Unexpected outbound connections from npm package directory
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole backdoors beacon to attacker infrastructure — 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' implies C2 callbacks from compromised package context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS from node.exe processes whose cwd or loaded modules are under node_modules. Flag connections to domains not in allowlist or newly registered/rare domains.

suggestion.title: Installation of malicious art-template npm package version
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names art-template as backdoored package — detection should intercept when compromised version is installed via npm registry or downloaded to disk
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands targeting art-template; cross-reference against known-malicious version hashes. Flag presence of suspicious code in post-install scripts (Base64, obfuscation, network calls).

suggestion.title: Suspicious package.json or install script modification
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies injected code in package; detection should catch unusual edits to package.json or build/install scripts containing exfiltration or payload-download logic
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file write events to package.json, package-lock.json, or */node_modules/art-template/* containing obfuscated strings, URLs, or shell commands in postinstall/preinstall fields.

suggestion.title: Detect secondary payload download triggered by npm package
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks often stage a second-stage payload — detection should identify network requests or file downloads originating from npm package execution context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on curl/wget or Node.js http module requests from node processes downloading files to %TEMP% or unusual paths immediately after art-template install or package load.

suggestion.title: Detect Cron Job C2 Polling (INJ3CTOR3 Layer 1)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Layer 1 uses 'scheduled cron jobs poll[ing] the C2 server every 1-3 minutes, continuously downloading and re-executing the dropper.' Pipeline missed entire persistence layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or modified cron entries executing curl/wget with high frequency (sub-5-minute intervals) to external URLs. Cross-reference against known C2 IPs (45.95.147.178). Alert on cron jobs downloading and executing stage-2 payloads from HTTP endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Shell Profile Injection (INJ3CTOR3 Layer 2)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Layer 2 as 're-infection payload fires on every root login and system reboot via shell profile injection.' Pipeline missed this critical detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, /etc/profile, or /etc/profile.d/ that add command execution or file downloads. Specifically monitor for curl/wget execution embedded in shell initialization files or commands that re-download dropper payloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Immutable File Attributes on Persistence Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states Layer 3 uses 'Eight immutable crontab copies stored in hidden directories, protected by file attributes blocking deletion even by root.' Pipeline missed this defensive evasion signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for chattr +i (immutable) flag being set on system files, particularly in /var/spool/cron/, hidden directories, or FreePBX web tree. Alert on any file with immutable flag set by non-root or during off-hours. Cross-correlate with recently-modified cron or web-accessible PHP files.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Respawn/Watchdog Behavior (INJ3CTOR3 Layer 4)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Layer 4: 'Process watchdog immediately re-downloads the dropper if beacon processes disappear.' This loop should be detectable as repeated process resurrection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated execution of identical process chains (same binary/args, same parent) with sub-minute intervals after parent termination. Flag bash/sh spawning curl/wget fetching from 45.95.147.178 in tight loops. Correlate with absence of legitimate cron scheduling.

suggestion.title: Detect Webshell Distribution Across FreePBX Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Layer 5 as 'Webshell copies distributed across twelve+ FreePBX web tree paths.' Pipeline failed to capture this web-accessible persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected .php files in /var/www/html/freepbx/*, /opt/freepbx/*, and /etc/asterisk/agi-bin/ with signatures matching JOMANGY (base64/ROT13 obfuscation, watermark 'trace_e1ebf9066a951be519a24140711839ea', MD5 hashes b506fc82, 100259af, d40180f7). Flag any authenticated HTTP POST/GET to these files followed by shell execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Backdoor Account Creation with Obfuscated Passwords
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 18 backdoor accounts including 'nine root-equivalent accounts: newfpbx, newfpbxs, xhimax (base64-obfuscated); centos, admin, support, issabel, sangoma, emo' and describes MD5-crypt/SHA1 password hashes. Pipeline extracted zero credential indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of user accounts with names mimicking legitimate FreePBX service accounts (newfpbx, issabel, sangoma, centos) especially if UID >= 0 (root-equivalent). Monitor /etc/shadow for insertion of accounts with non-standard password hashes or identical MD5-crypt hashes across multiple accounts. Flag MySQL ampusers table for unexpected SHA1 hash 6ea9c6d2d932532a4cd44c7974fb1a0a87dbfcf9.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command-and-Control Outbound Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Kimwolf DDoS Botnet Operator' — botnet operations mandate C2 infrastructure and communication. This foundational attack phase was entirely unaddressed by the pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from compromised hosts to botnet C2 domains or IPs. Flag systematic, periodic beaconing patterns on non-standard ports characteristic of DDoS botnet clients checking in for commands.

suggestion.title: Network Denial of Service Traffic Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'DDoS-for-Hire Attacks' yet no detection logic for volumetric or protocol-based DDoS traffic anomalies was proposed. This is the primary impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric floods (UDP, DNS amplification) and protocol-based patterns (SYN flood, HTTP GET flood). Correlate traffic spikes with timing of known DDoS-for-hire operator campaigns and bot activation events.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Installation and Execution Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: DDoS botnets require malware deployment and execution on compromised hosts. No detection for bot installation, lateral movement, persistence mechanism, or execution behavioral signatures was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bot malware artifacts exhibiting DDoS botnet client behaviors: dormant processes with periodic C2 beaconing, command execution on scheduled intervals, network reconnaissance activities, and privilege escalation attempts for persistence.

suggestion.title: DDoS-for-Hire Operator Infrastructure and Monetization
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'DDoS-for-hire' service model yet no detection for backend operator infrastructure (bot admin panels, customer portals, payment processors) used to manage and monetize botnets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to suspected DDoS-for-hire operator infrastructure: admin panels, bot rental customer portals, payment APIs, and C2 node management interfaces. Detect anomalous web portal access patterns inconsistent with legitimate traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Driver Loading - Unsigned or Non-Standard Path
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits legitimate but vulnerable drivers already on disk to bypass user-mode security and gain kernel access. Article title 'Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware' establishes driver-loading as the core attack vector; pipeline missed detection of unusual or unsigned driver load operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LoadDriver/NtLoadDriver calls, unsigned driver file execution, or drivers loaded from non-System32/Drivers paths. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable driver hashes (e.g., RTCore64.sys, WinRing0). Alert on registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\<DriverName> creating new kernel-mode service entries.

suggestion.title: Registry-Based Driver Persistence - Suspicious Service Creation
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires installing the vulnerable driver as a Windows service to load at boot or on-demand. Article's 'without hardware' framing implies persistence without UEFI/firmware modifications, moving the attack to OS-level service registry paths that pipeline failed to flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\ for new service creation where ImagePath points to a .sys file with a known vulnerability, has no publisher signature, or references archived/obfuscated paths. Flag service start-type changes from Disabled to Boot or Auto.

suggestion.title: Known-Vulnerable Driver Hash Execution
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD relies on a curated list of exploitable drivers (RTCore, GDRV, Novell, Gigabyte, etc.). Pipeline should cross-reference file hashes and driver names against public BYOVD driver lists but produced no IOCs or hash-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a threat-intel feed of known-vulnerable drivers by name and hash. Alert when these drivers are executed, copied to disk, or loaded into kernel space. This is the most reliable BYOVD indicator—legitimate but weaponized code with strong forensic traction.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Legitimate Driver for Memory/Kernel Access
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD differentiates itself by using existing drivers for direct kernel read/write (e.g., Winring0, RTCore). Article establishes 'exploitable without hardware' meaning kernel-level code execution; pipeline failed to suggest detection of user-mode processes invoking kernel-access driver functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-mode processes (especially non-administrator ones) opening handles to known BYOVD drivers or issuing IOCTL calls (DeviceIoControlRequest events) to drivers with known kernel-access CVEs. Correlate process creation with subsequent handle opens to %SystemRoot%\System32\Drivers\<vulnerable-driver>.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Kernel Access - LSASS Dumping Post-Privilege-Escalation
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD grants kernel access, enabling post-exploitation techniques like LSASS process dumping. Article's threat context (critical severity) implies adversary objectives beyond elevation; pipeline missed detection of kernel-access follow-on actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting kernel driver exploitation, monitor for handle opens to protected processes (LSASS, csrss) with PROCESS_VM_READ or PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION access. BYOVD-enabled attackers often immediately dump credentials post-privilege-escalation. Flag this sequence: unknown driver load → elevated process → LSASS access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Creation from Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'malicious CI/CD workflows' targeting 5,561 repos. Expected attack vector is creation or modification of workflow files in .github/workflows/ by compromised accounts. No detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for workflow file creation/modification by users not in the contributor list, or workflows added outside normal business hours. Alert on workflows that invoke external shell scripts or create secrets.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Runner Exfiltration of Credentials and Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows would exfiltrate build credentials. Article describes CI/CD-targeted attack but no detection addresses credential theft from build environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CI/CD runner processes that access secret manager APIs or environment variable dumps, followed by unexpected outbound HTTPS/SSH to non-whitelisted domains. Look for base64-encoded credential patterns in process arguments.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Compromise via Account Takeover or SSH Key Injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack scale (5,561 repos) suggests either mass account compromise or supply chain injection. Article implies coordinated repo mutation but no initial-access detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk workflow commits from single actor across multiple repos in short window, SSH key additions to high-privilege accounts, or repository settings changes (branch protection disable) preceding workflow commits.

suggestion.title: Malicious External Script Invocation in GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Typical CI/CD attack delivery: workflows invoke external curl/wget of obfuscated payloads. Article references 'malicious CI/CD workflows' but no detection for inline script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows containing curl/wget/powershell.exe -Command with inline base64, or downloading executables from non-CDN domains. Flag workflows referencing secrets.${{ runner.environment }} in curl headers.

suggestion.title: Repository Forking and Workflow Injection for Supply Chain Attack
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale GitHub attacks often involve forking public repos and injecting malicious workflows to target dependent projects. No UC addresses this initial-compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual fork creation by single account across multiple popular open-source projects, followed by workflow file creation on new branches and pull requests to upstream projects with suspicious build commands.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Enumeration and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Compromised workflows would extract and abuse GITHUB_TOKEN env var to move laterally across orgs/repos. No lateral-movement detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GITHUB_TOKEN usage from non-official GitHub Actions steps (e.g., custom scripts), API calls to enumerate repos/teams/secrets from build logs, or token reuse across different workflow runs in different repos.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Exfiltrating Secrets to External Host
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration' — attack vector is malicious or compromised workflows sending secrets to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag workflows containing references to GitHub secrets (${{secrets.*}}) paired with curl/wget/HTTP calls to non-GitHub domains, or environment variable injection of secrets into external API calls. Aggregate by repository and workflow SHA to identify templated attacks.

suggestion.title: Repository Secrets Accessed by Compromised or Malicious GitHub Actions Principal
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repositories affected suggests single point of compromise — a malicious principal with write access to workflows across multiple public repos, or a supply-chain attack injecting the same malicious workflow template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify GitHub Actions principals or runners accessing repository secrets across an anomalously high number of distinct repositories (>15) in a 24-hour window. Correlate with commit/push activity from the same principal across unrelated repositories.

suggestion.title: Workflow File Added to Public Repository by Low-Reputation Account
suggestion.rationale: 'Public Repositories' and 5,500+ scale suggests mass injection of malicious workflows. Attack requires initial access — either compromised legitimate accounts or accounts with limited history added to many repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new .github/workflows/ files added by GitHub accounts with minimal prior contribution history (created <30 days ago) or commits spanning >5 unrelated repositories. Correlate account creation date with workflow addition timing.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token or Secret Exposed in Public Action Run Logs
suggestion.rationale: Public repositories publish workflow run logs publicly; exfiltrated secrets may appear in stdout/stderr if workflows log environment variables or API responses containing credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public GitHub Actions run logs for patterns matching GitHub PAT/token formats, AWS access key IDs, and common secret names (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, DATABASE_PASSWORD). Cross-reference exposed secrets with accounts using them across multiple repositories.

suggestion.title: Mass Exfiltration Traffic from GitHub Actions Runner to Uncommon Destination
suggestion.rationale: Coordinated secret theft across 5,500 repos produces detectable outbound traffic signature — either aggregated HTTP exfiltration to single domain, or distributed to attacker C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate public IP addresses of GitHub-hosted runners with outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to low-reputation or newly-registered domains during workflow execution. Alert on >100 connections to same external host from runner fleet in 6-hour window.

suggestion.title: Detect Traffic to Sanctioned Hosting Infrastructure (Stark Industries / WorkTitans / THE.Hosting)
suggestion.rationale: Article states infrastructure 'enabled cyberattacks, interference operations, and disinformation campaigns' while 'indirectly provide[d] economic resources to Russian and Belarusian entities sanctioned by the European Union.' Organizations must block or monitor connections to known sanctioned hosting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS requests and network connections to infrastructure operated by or registered to Stark Industries, WorkTitans B.V., THE.Hosting, or their identified IP ranges. Alert on sustained C2-like beaconing patterns and correlate with EU sanctions list metadata.

suggestion.title: NoName057(16) Pro-Russian DDoS Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Danish authorities and infrastructure providers linked WorkTitans to attacks by the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify volumetric DDoS signatures associated with NoName057(16): multi-source flooding attacks against critical infrastructure, public sector organizations, and financial systems. Correlate traffic patterns with known NoName057(16) TTPs from public threat intelligence and prior campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Infrastructure Transfer to Newly Registered Shell Companies
