suggestion.rationale: Article states dropper 'fetches secondary payloads from command-and-control servers' via disabled SSL verification. No detection for secondary payload retrieval or in-memory code execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes (especially those loaded via Composer autoloader) initiating HTTP requests with SSL verification disabled (stream_context_set_option). Detect subsequent eval(), assert(), or create_function() calls on data received from external URLs. Flag patterns where src/helpers.php or vendor autoload scripts spawn file_get_contents() or curl requests to external domains.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' — this is the attack's entry point and pipeline generated zero IOCs or kill-chain phases around it. Should detect exploitation payloads and access patterns for known BIG-IP CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP management interfaces (tmsh, web console) and virtual server logs for exploitation signatures: malformed HTTP requests, CGI argument injection, or known BIG-IP vulnerability URI patterns (e.g., /mgmt/tm/, /config/rest). Alert on unexpected access to sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: SSH Lateral Movement from Load Balancer to Backend Linux Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' establishes SSH as the attack's lateral-movement vector, yet pipeline produced zero detection use cases for this critical phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SSH connections (port 22) originating from F5 BIG-IP IP addresses to internal backend systems. Flag SSH connections to root or service accounts, especially in bursts or from IPs not normally seen as SSH clients. Correlate with BIG-IP compromise evidence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Activity on BIG-IP Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must gain or maintain administrative control of the BIG-IP to execute the pivot. No detection generated for unauthorized login attempts, credential reuse, or out-of-band admin access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP login logs for failed authentication bursts followed by success, access from unexpected networks, or login events during abnormal hours. Flag successful logins after multiple failures (brute force success). Alert on simultaneous logins to admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance from Compromised BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: The phrase 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' implies post-compromise discovery scanning. No use case generated for lateral probing or internal network enumeration from the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning or connection attempts from BIG-IP to a large number of internal hosts across multiple ports (22, 3306, 5432, 1433). Flag unusual fan-out connection patterns inconsistent with normal load-balancer traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Command Execution or Module Loading on BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Pivoting and persistent access likely requires command execution or malicious code injection on the appliance itself. Pipeline generated no detection for process execution, script execution, or iRule injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP for unexpected shell script execution, iRule modifications with suspicious logic, or tmsh command execution outside normal maintenance windows. Alert on creation of unexpected files in /var/tmp or /tmp on the appliance.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration or C2 Communication from BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Compromised load balancer is a vantage point for data collection and C2 callbacks. Article's sustained access narrative ('Pivot Into Enterprise') implies persistent control, yet no exfiltration or C2 detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from BIG-IP to non-whitelisted external hosts, especially on HTTPS or alternative ports. Flag DNS queries from the appliance to suspicious domains. Alert on large data volumes egressing from the BIG-IP to untrusted IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Autoload.Files Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious payload 'was hidden in a newly added file, src/helpers.php, and registered in composer.json under autoload.files. Composer's autoloader unconditionally requires every file in that list, so the malicious code runs at the very start of the PHP request lifecycle.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new or unexpected entries in composer.json autoload.files arrays, especially additions of helpers.php files. Alert on autoload.files entries pointing to recently modified files in vendor directories outside official package source commits.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback to flipboxstudio[.]info Payload Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states first-stage 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it in the background' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info or subdomains. Flag DNS queries resolving flipboxstudio[.]info. Monitor for POST requests to /payload or /exfil URI paths with encrypted payloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential and Secret Enumeration Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second-stage behavior: 'it walks through a long list of sources looking for anything of value: Cloud provider credentials... Kubernetes kubeconfig files, HashiCorp Vault tokens, and CI/CD secrets... SSH private keys... Application .env files... Browser data, including cookies, history, and stored logins. Password manager vaults... Cryptocurrency wallet files... Messaging and collaboration tokens'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process chains accessing multiple credential sources in rapid sequence: ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, kubeconfig, .env files, browser cache, password manager vaults, /vault/ paths. Flag processes spawned by PHP/Composer runtime accessing these paths without security scanning context.

suggestion.title: Packagist Package Version Anomalies and Fork-Based Tag Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article explains attack vector: 'a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases' and 'Republication of historical tags continues in bursts... Total count climbs past 700 versions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist for unexpected re-release of historical version tags. Flag composer.lock updates to laravel-lang/* packages where resolved commit differs from official laravel-lang GitHub. Alert on lock file entries showing fork repositories outside laravel-lang/* organization.

suggestion.title: Post-Exfiltration File Deletion and Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file deletion activity immediately following outbound C2 traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil. Flag cascading deletes of credential-related files within minutes of credential enumeration. Alert on rm/del commands executed by background PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Malicious Payload Execution (Windows/Linux/macOS)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'The launcher logic is platform-aware and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows' and payload downloads and runs 'in the background' across all platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of non-native script interpreters spawned by PHP/Composer with suspicious patterns: HTTP(S) downloads, temp directory writes, background job spawning. Alert on same payload hash executed across Windows AND Linux/macOS assets within hours.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Repository Compromise—Malicious Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—direct code injection into open-source packages. No detection UC for identifying installation of compromised Composer packages via dependency resolution or unusual source URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/require commands pulling from non-standard package registries, local .git directories, or forked repositories. Flag installations of known-compromised package versions or those bypassing Packagist integrity checks.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Exfiltration via Package Build Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article goal: 'Steal CI Secrets.' No UC for detecting code within post-install scripts (composer.json scripts) that enumerate or transmit CI environment variables (GitHub Actions secrets, GitLab CI tokens, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on child processes spawned by PHP/Composer interpreting package scripts that perform env-variable enumeration (printenv, env, Set-Variable in CI runners) followed by DNS/HTTP egress to external domains not in allow-list.

suggestion.title: Git Repository Tag Rewriting—Unauthorized Version Control History Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' No UC for detecting git push --force-with-lease to change immutable package releases or forceful tag rewrites in upstream repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on force-push events or tag deletion/recreation in production package repositories, especially when source IP differs from maintainer baseline or Merkle tree of code changes between old and new tags indicates large injection.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Integrity Mismatch—Hash Verification Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vector requires code substitution undetected by package managers. Pipeline should suggest detecting when installed package hashes deviate from published checksums (composer.lock mismatches, unsigned tags).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected SHA-256/SHA-512 hashes for tagged releases from Packagist or official source control. Alert when local installed files fail hash verification or composer.lock references packages with modified sha256 vs. upstream registry.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance—Composer/PHP Package Dependency Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must survey target application dependencies before injecting malicious versions. No UC for detecting automated composer show, php -m, or vendor/ directory scanning that precedes supply-chain targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid/automated execution of composer show --direct, composer list, or grep patterns over vendor/ directory followed shortly by suspicious composer update/install from non-standard sources.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via CI Secrets—GitHub/GitLab Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Steal CI Secrets'—implies stolen tokens enable further compromise. Pipeline should suggest detecting exfiltrated CI tokens used for unauthorized Git operations (clone of private repos, push to attacker-controlled branches).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CI tokens used from IP addresses outside expected CI runner pools, or token use in non-standard Git operations (git clone of repos unrelated to build, git push to new remotes, or cross-org access).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'CVE-2026-48172 Exploited' with zero IOCs or detection coverage. Known vulnerability ID must be mapped to detection signatures. Establish baseline for vulnerable plugin versions and request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to known vulnerable LiteSpeed cPanel plugin endpoints or parameters. Monitor for exploitation payloads in web server logs, focusing on plugin handler paths and unusual request parameters.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Spawning from cPanel/LiteSpeed Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Run Scripts as Root'—privilege escalation. Pipeline missed detection for non-privileged processes (cPanel, LiteSpeed workers) spawning child procs with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when cPanel/LiteSpeed processes (normally unprivileged) fork or exec children with UID 0. Monitor sudo logs, /etc/sudoers modifications, and capability escalation (setuid/setgid abuse).

suggestion.title: Script Execution with Elevated Privileges via Plugin Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes scripts executed as root via plugin. Pipeline should detect shell interpreter invocation (bash, perl, python) with root context from plugin-controlled execution paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when interpreted scripts (shell, perl, python) spawn from cPanel/LiteSpeed plugin directories with elevated privilege. Correlate parent process UID, command-line args, and working directory.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin File Tampering and Unauthorized Module Loading
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation 'to Run Scripts' implies plugin code injection or module installation. Post-exploitation, file modifications to plugin code and cPanel module registries should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate LiteSpeed/cPanel plugin directories. Alert on unexpected file writes, binary modifications, or addition of new .pm/.so modules. Cross-reference with cPanel module-load audit logs.

suggestion.title: cPanel Audit Log Clearing Post-Root Execution
suggestion.rationale: After 'exploited to run scripts as root,' adversaries typically erase evidence. cPanel audit logs (/var/log/cpanel/audit.log) should be monitored for tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncation, deletion, or suspicious modification of cPanel audit log files, particularly following root-level process activity. Cross-correlate timing with exploitation detection signals.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Root Command Execution from Web-Accessible cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Plugin exploitation creates path: HTTP request → plugin handler → root command execution. Detection must chain web access anomalies to privileged execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious HTTP requests (to plugin endpoints, unusual POST/GET params) with root-level process creation within seconds. Flag multi-stage indicators: web access → cPanel process → shell execution as UID 0.

suggestion.title: Nginx Poolslip Memory Pool Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Nginx-poolslip Vulnerability Enables DoS and Code Execution' — no detection for exploit traffic targeting memory pool handling
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with malformed headers, oversized connection pool parameters, or unusual packet sequencing patterns to nginx instances. Baseline normal connection pool behavior and alert on anomalous pool exhaustion requests.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from Nginx Worker
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Code Execution Attacks' — no detection for shells or commands spawned by nginx worker processes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawn from nginx worker PIDs (parent UID nginx/www-data) executing shells, interpreters, or network tools. Baseline legitimate child processes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Nginx Repeated Crash / Restart Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'Enables DoS' — no detection for repetitive nginx master/worker crashes consistent with DoS exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track nginx process restarts and abnormal exits. Flag if master process restarts >3 times within 5-minute window or worker processes exit with segfault/abort signals in correlated patterns.

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration Modification Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE via poolslip enables config tampering for persistence — article does not detail but is standard post-exploitation behavior
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to nginx.conf, conf.d/, sites-available/ outside of scheduled package updates. Alert on appended proxy_pass directives, new upstream definitions, or load module directives added by non-root UID.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell Initiation from Nginx Context
suggestion.rationale: Code execution impact requires attacker command shell — common post-RCE pattern not captured by pipeline despite explicit 'Code Execution' in title
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound connections from nginx worker processes (non-standard ports: 4444, 5555, 8888, 9999, 31337) with /bin/bash or /bin/sh spawning from nginx UID. Flag as reverse shell indicator.

suggestion.title: NPM Package Published Without 2FA Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes npm's new '2FA-Gated Publishing' control, indicating prior exposure to unauthorized package publishes. Detection should flag publishing events from accounts without 2FA enabled or from new publishing sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for package publish events from accounts lacking required 2FA authentication. Alert on first-time publishers or publish from geographic/IP anomalies. Cross-reference against account creation dates to flag suspicious new publishers targeting existing popular packages.

suggestion.title: NPM Account Takeover Indicators (Auth Spike + Publish)
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'Package Install Controls' implicitly addresses compromise of maintainer accounts. Detection should identify authentication anomalies followed by package modifications—classic supply-chain attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed authentication attempts against npm account with successful publish/modification of packages within short time window. Flag if publish originates from IP/geolocation not seen in baseline account activity. Alert especially on packages with high download counts (indicates attacker prioritizing popular targets).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Dependency Addition to Popular NPM Package
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise often manifests as injection of new dependencies into legitimate packages. This is the attack vector npm's install controls are designed to prevent, and should be detected at publish/install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For packages above configurable popularity threshold (e.g., >100k weekly downloads), flag additions of new dependencies not previously declared. Correlate against commit history in source repo (GitHub, GitLab) to identify orphaned/unmotivated dependency additions. Alert on transitive dependencies added that aren't traced to deliberate code changes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Package Version Releases with Minimal Code Changes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package accounts often push multiple versions quickly to evade detection or maximize infection window before remediation. This activity pattern indicates potential account compromise or attacker behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on packages releasing 3+ versions within 24-hour window where code deltas between versions are <5% of file size (indicating metadata/patch version spam). Flag if rapid releases include addition of outbound network calls, child process spawning, or file I/O that wasn't in prior stable versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Composer
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Laravel-Lang packages' — supply-chain attacks are triggered by dependency installation. Pipeline should detect composer install/update with suspicious network activity, file writes to sensitive dirs, or process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer.phar or php processes executing with install/update flags, followed by child process spawning (bash, curl, wget) or writing to config/cache directories. Credential-stealing payloads often exfiltrate via curl/wget to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential stealer' payload. Should detect env var access, config file reads, or outbound HTTPS/HTTP from Laravel application processes to suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes reading .env, config/*, or app directories immediately after package installation, or Laravel app processes making outbound connections to non-CDN, non-API infrastructure. Credential stealers typically exfil via POST to attacker C2.

suggestion.title: Post-Install PHP Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Composer packages can execute arbitrary code via 'post-install-cmd' scripts. Pipeline should detect PHP execution with elevated privileges or from vendor directory during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php binary execution with -r flag or script includes from vendor/*/composer.json scripts, especially scripts defined in 'post-install-cmd' or 'post-autoload-dump'. Look for env var enumeration or network connections immediately after.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Version or Checksum Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies laravel-lang as the target. Should detect installation of unexpected versions, missing signature verification, or composer.lock modifications suggesting typosquatting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.lock for laravel-lang version changes between runs, or detect php/composer processes with --no-verify or --ignore-platform-reqs flags. Flag installations from non-standard Composer registries or unsigned packages.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: Laravel apps store DB passwords, API keys, tokens in .env. Credential stealer would access these. Should detect getenv(), file_get_contents('.env'), or env variable enumeration from non-app processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes executing functions like getenv() or file operations on .env, config/database.php, or bootstrap/cache/ from vendor paths or symlinked code. Look for env var dumps to temp files or exfil via curl in the same process lineage.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealers often spawn shells (bash, sh) or downloaders (curl, wget) from post-install hooks to fetch additional payloads or exfil data. Pipeline missed this obvious parent-child process pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php or composer.phar spawning bash, sh, curl, wget, powershell, or cmd during package installation (detected via composer.phar parent). High fidelity if child process makes network connections or touches credential files.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Against Ghost CMS Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to steal the admin API keys' via SQL injection. This is the critical initial compromise step that enables everything downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS application logs and WAF for SQL injection payloads targeting admin endpoints or API key tables. Detect unusual SQL UNION/SELECT patterns in requests to /ghost/api/ endpoints. Alert on successful queries that extract admin_api_keys or similar sensitive data fields.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Modification of Article Content with JavaScript Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles' after obtaining API keys. This persistence mechanism modifies published content to include loaders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost admin API logs (specifically POST /articles and PUT /articles/{id}) for modifications using compromised or new API keys. Detect when article HTML/markdown suddenly contains <script> tags, JavaScript loaders, or iframe injections. Flag changes occurring outside business hours or from new API tokens.

suggestion.title: Execution of Second-Stage Cloaking & Fingerprinting Scripts from Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'JavaScript code is a lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure, which is essentially a cloaking script that fingerprints visitors.' This is active script execution in visitor browsers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests from legitimate domains (universities, media sites) to attacker-controlled second-stage payload servers. Monitor for JavaScript dynamically fetching content and executing device fingerprinting code (checking OS, browser, screen resolution, plugins). Identify domains hosting loader scripts and feed to Sentinel.

suggestion.title: Delivery of Fake Cloudflare Verification Prompt via Malicious Iframe
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page, which contains the ClickFix lure.' This is the social engineering delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iframe injection on legitimate domains where src attributes point to attacker infrastructure or IP addresses. Flag when legitimate news/university domains serve UI that mimics Cloudflare/browser security prompts (visual similarity matching on legitimate domains). Monitor for sudden insertion of modal dialogs requesting user action on normally read-only content.

suggestion.title: Command Execution from ClickFix Phishing Lure - Payload Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'instructs victims to verify that they are human by pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt, which drops a payload on their systems.' The command contains malware delivery payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or powershell.exe execution with suspicious command lines containing download/execution commands (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest, certutil, bitsadmin) from user command-line paste events. Correlate with visits to compromised legitimate domains immediately preceding execution. Alert on UtilifySetup.exe, DLL loaders, or JavaScript droppers being created immediately after suspicious command execution.

suggestion.title: UtilifySetup.exe and Associated Malware Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific payloads: 'UtilifySetup.exe' (Electron-based malware), DLL loaders, and JavaScript droppers. These are the final malware delivery artifacts that should trigger immediate response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures and behavioral detections for UtilifySetup.exe and observed DLL loaders from this campaign. Monitor for Electron-based executables spawned from suspicious parent processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, browser). Detect DLL injection patterns and unsigned binary execution. Cross-reference file hashes and parent process command lines with ClickFix indicators.

suggestion.title: Nezha API: RoleMember privilege escalation via cron cross-tenant access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'cross-tenant RCE'—RoleMember should only manage their own tenant's servers, but the vulnerability allows cron creation for all servers. Article: 'The per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' Should detect RoleMember (Role==1) creating cron tasks with server IDs outside their assigned tenant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nezha /api/v1/cron POST requests from RoleMember accounts where the server list includes servers not owned by that user's tenant. Correlate user role from authentication logs with server ownership/ACL data.

suggestion.title: Nezha cron: Cover flag exploitation (single task→all-servers execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the 'CronCoverAll' bypass—setting cover=1 on a single cron task forces it to execute on every monitored server, bypassing per-server ACLs. Article: 'POST /api/v1/cron with empty servers + CronCoverAll' in UC title. This warrants a dedicated hunt for the cover flag anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST /api/v1/cron where (servers field is empty OR null) AND (cover parameter == 1). Flag any such requests from RoleMember accounts as high-confidence exploitation.

suggestion.title: Nezha: Unusual cron job payload with shell metacharacters from non-admin user
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker running arbitrary shell commands. Article phrase: 'RoleMember can create a scheduled cron task with …[shell command]'. Should detect cron task creation payloads containing shell metacharacters, redirects, pipes when created by non-admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PATCH /api/v1/cron request bodies for shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, >, <, backticks, $(…)) from accounts with Role==1. Flag payloads containing cat, curl, wget, nc, bash -i, python -m socket, etc.

suggestion.title: Nezha cron execution: Credential-harvesting commands spawned by cron process
suggestion.rationale: Article lists credential-access techniques T1003.008 (shadow/passwd), T1552.005 (cloud metadata). These manifest as shell commands executed by the cron daemon. Article: 'run shell on every server'—should detect specific credential harvesting post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution (cat, head, awk, curl, wget) targeting credential stores (/etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, /proc/*/environ) or cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, metadata.azure.com) when the process tree includes cron or Nezha agent.

suggestion.title: Nezha authentication: RoleMember account followed by cron API abuse within 5 minutes
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires valid authentication before cron API call. Article: 'RoleMember can create'—implies an authenticated RoleMember. Should correlate authentication success with subsequent cron exploitation attempts to catch opportunistic lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join authentication logs (successful login as RoleMember) with API logs (POST /api/v1/cron from same user within 5 minutes). Escalate if cron request includes cover=1 or empty servers array or out-of-tenant server IDs.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Package Version Releases via Unusual Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'—attacker injected malicious code into package repositories; detection requires commit pattern anomalies from compromised maintainer accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify commits to Laravel-Lang and related package repositories from unusual geographic locations, off-hours activity, or deviating from established maintainer patterns. Alert on commits modifying core source files without corresponding issue tracker references or standard PR reviews. GitHub audit logs showing new SSH keys or API tokens preceding malicious commits should escalate.

suggestion.title: Monitor Installation of Specific Compromised Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article: '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages compromised'—downstream systems will install malicious versions via Composer; requires tracking install/require/update events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/require operations for installation of known-malicious version ranges. Establish baseline of normal version distributions; alert on unexpected concentration of installs from specific version numbers matching compromise timeline. Correlate package installation events with subsequent process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect GitHub Maintainer Account Compromise via Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: '700 GitHub Repos hacked'—requires detection of compromised maintainer accounts before malicious code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub logins from new geographic regions, VPN/proxy services, or impossible travel scenarios for known maintainers. Flag creation of new SSH keys, API tokens, or deploy keys not associated with known CI/CD infrastructure. Correlate new authentication artifacts with subsequent suspicious repository activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Lateral Movement: Cascading Code Execution in Dependent Projects
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes ecosystem-wide scope (700 repos, 233 versions)—any downstream project installing backdoored Laravel-Lang package will execute attacker code, enabling lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation events with unexpected child process spawning, shell execution, or network connections originating from application servers minutes after package install. Detect cascading execution patterns where code execution in one dependent project triggers execution in its own dependencies. Monitor for C2 traffic or data exfiltration following backdoored package installation.

suggestion.title: Detect Obfuscated or Malicious Code in Package Source Files
suggestion.rationale: Article: hackers 'compromised' packages—requires detection of embedded malicious code before or after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package.json, composer.json, src/ directory, and autoload files for obfuscated PHP, base64-encoded payloads, or eval() calls. Detect packages spawning shell processes, performing unsolicited network requests, or accessing credential stores. Validate package signatures and file hashes against upstream sources.

suggestion.title: Monitor Package Registry Metadata Tampering and Unusual Version History
suggestion.rationale: Article: '233 Versions compromised'—attacker modified package releases and metadata; detection requires monitoring registry version listings for unauthorized changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid version releases deviating from maintainer's historical cadence. Monitor for version deletion and re-upload, unexpected dependency injection into composer.json, changes to package ownership, or tampered release metadata (timestamps, checksums). Flag versions released outside normal CI/CD deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Exploit F5 BIG-IP Via Unpatched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' but pipeline extracted no exploitation indicators, techniques, or initial-access detection. This is the first phase of the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP access logs for POST requests to known-vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /mgmt paths, configuration endpoints). Look for error codes 400-404 followed by 200 responses indicating exploitation. Correlate with BIG-IP system event logs for failed authentication attempts followed by successful admin-level actions.

suggestion.title: SSH Access Spawned from F5 BIG-IP Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Gain SSH Access' via BIG-IP exploitation. No detection use case was generated for SSH sessions originating from the appliance to internal Linux hosts.
log_sources: SSH auth logs on target Linux systems
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP management or data-plane interfaces to Linux hosts, especially if sourced from non-standard SSH client libraries or with atypical handshake patterns. Correlate BIG-IP process execution (if shell access achieved) with outbound SSH initiations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from F5 BIG-IP into Linux Network
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' but pipeline extracted zero lateral-movement detection use cases. No guidance on detecting reconnaissance or multi-hop access patterns from the appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track port scanning or service enumeration from BIG-IP appliance targeting internal Linux subnets. Monitor for unexpected SSH brute-force patterns or credential reuse attempts from BIG-IP IP. Flag any interactive session spawned on compromised BIG-IP that initiates outbound scanning or connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process or Shell Execution on F5 BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: If attackers gained SSH or shell access to BIG-IP (implied by 'Gain SSH Access'), no use case was generated to detect local execution or persistence mechanisms on the appliance itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BIG-IP audit and system logs for tmsh or bash shell invocations by non-root or non-standard users. Flag creation of scheduled tasks (cron), persistence scripts, or unusual modification of startup configurations. Alert on execution of wget, curl, or other data-transfer utilities from BIG-IP shell context.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Credential Theft or API Key Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Lateral movement from BIG-IP into Linux networks suggests attackers may have harvested credentials or API keys from the appliance. No detection use case addresses credential dumping or reuse from BIG-IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual reads of F5 configuration files (e.g., /config/bigip.conf, .ha files) that contain credentials or API keys. Alert on use of extracted credentials in SSH logins or API calls to internal Linux systems. Flag high-volume SSH attempts using credentials consistent with F5 admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Autoload PHP Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious 'helpers.php' was 'automatically loaded by Composer' via composer.json autoload section—direct artifact of supply chain execution requiring detection on deployment systems
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .php files in vendor/composer/autoload* directories or composer.json modifications adding files to autoload sections from non-standard vendors. Correlate with unusual PHP interpreter spawning child processes shortly after Composer install operations.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon Traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies flipboxstudio[.]info as attacker C2 receiving 'encrypted' stolen credentials from both Linux and Windows payloads—explicit network IOC with high signal-to-noise ratio for web application environments
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/DNS queries to flipboxstudio[.]info from web servers or development machines, especially correlating with PHP process execution and subsequent file system reads of sensitive files (.env, .ssh, .kube).

suggestion.title: PHP Process Dropping and Executing DebugElevator Windows Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article details PHP payload that 'extracts a base64-encoded executable... written to %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched'—specific cross-platform execution pattern with DebugElevator as named artifact
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php.exe, php-cgi.exe, wp-cli) spawning child processes to %TEMP%/%TMP% with randomized .exe names, or writing files followed immediately by execution. Flag base64 decode operations preceding binary writes in web application contexts.

suggestion.title: Bulk .env and Cloud Credential File Access by Non-Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article lists malware harvesting '.env configuration files' alongside 'cloud credentials, Kubernetes secrets, Vault tokens, Git credentials, CI/CD secrets'—systematic environmental credential enumeration pattern
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes accessing .env files, ~/.ssh directories, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, ~/.aws/credentials, or environment variables matching AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, STRIPE_* patterns outside normal service deployments. Sequence: file reads → data encoding → network write to external IP.

suggestion.title: Browser App-Bound Encryption Key Extraction Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies DebugElevator 'designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys needed to decrypt stored browser credentials'—targeted credential access technique requiring OS-level visibility
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser processes accessing Chrome/Brave/Edge Local State, Profiles/*/Login Data, or Sync Data files. Flag attempts to read DPAPI master keys, local state encryption metadata, or browser profile directories from service/PHP/scheduled-task contexts.

suggestion.title: Mass Git Tag Rewriting in Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism: 'attacker rewrote every existing git tag in each repository to point at a new malicious commit' starting at 22:32 UTC across 502 tags—audit log anomaly signaling source repository compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub/GitLab repository audit logs for bulk git tag modifications (>10 tags in <60 min), especially tags repointing to commits outside official repository history or from fork repositories. Alert on org-wide push credentials used outside normal CI/CD windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states Laravel-Lang PHP packages were compromised and distributed. Pipeline should detect when applications install or update to malicious package versions from package managers (Composer for PHP). Attack vector: 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of `composer install`, `composer update`, or `composer require` followed by new binary execution from vendor/ directory. Flag if install targets versions known to be compromised. Correlate package timestamps against compromise disclosure dates.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery of cross-platform credential stealer via compromised packages. Detection should focus on malicious code execution triggered by PHP package initialization (autoload, Laravel service providers). Phrase: 'deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of shell interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd) or credential access tools (curl, wget, reg query, Get-Credential) immediately after PHP/Laravel initialization. Establish baseline of legitimate post-install behavior and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from System Stores by Injected Code
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'credential stealer' payload. Pipeline should detect techniques for harvesting credentials once malware is executing in-process with application context. Stealer behavior implies accessing password stores, environment variables, configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of credential storage paths: ~/.ssh/, ~/.gnupg/, ~/.aws/credentials, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings, Browser Profile directories. Flag when PHP processes access these paths outside normal application flow.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control Communication from PHP Application
suggestion.rationale: Cross-platform credential stealer implies C2 callback to exfiltrate stolen credentials. Article context suggests malware will beacon out after stealing. Pipeline must detect suspicious network behavior from PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from PHP-FPM or CLI PHP processes to non-whitelisted domains, especially on non-standard ports. Flag if destination IPs resolve to bulletproof hosting, residential proxies, or newly registered domains. Correlate with post-package-install timeline.

suggestion.title: PHP Source Code Modification or Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package implies malicious PHP code added to vendor/ tree or package initialization code. Detection should identify when package contents deviate from official repositories or contain obfuscated/suspicious code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to vendor/ directory after package installation, especially in autoload files, service provider registrations, or framework bootstrap. Compare file hashes against official package repository records. Flag if .git, .github, or CI config files are added to package installations.

suggestion.title: Detection of Laravel Service Provider or Middleware Hooks Executing Suspicious Code
suggestion.rationale: Laravel-specific attack: compromised packages likely use service providers or middleware (documented Laravel extension points) to inject stealer code at framework boot. Article mentions 'Laravel-Lang' packages specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Laravel config/app.php for unexpected service provider registrations, and middleware stacks for unknown entries. Flag if a service provider or middleware is loaded from vendor/ and immediately spawns child processes, makes network calls, or accesses system credential stores without known legitimate use.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Autoload Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injected helpers.php file was wired into Composer's autoload.files entry, causing it to run on every PHP request the moment the package is installed.' This persistence mechanism via package manifest is a clear detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on additions to composer.json autoload.files pointing to suspicious paths (helpers.php, bootstrap, obfuscated names). Correlate with unauthorized package version changes or vendor directory modifications. Flag if autoload entries lack commit history or originate from non-official forks.

suggestion.title: Second-Stage Payload Download from C2 Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'reaches out to flipboxstudio[.]info, downloads a cross-platform second stage, and runs [it] in the background.' HTTP/HTTPS requests from PHP to attacker infrastructure is a high-fidelity detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from PHP-FPM or web server processes to flipboxstudio[.]info (especially /payload endpoint). Flag on connection establishment + subsequent process spawning or execution. Include DNS resolution + network connection correlation.

suggestion.title: Credential and Secrets Enumeration via Multi-Source File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential stealer that scrapes cloud keys, Kubernetes and Vault secrets, CI/CD tokens, SSH material, environment files, browser data, password manager vaults, crypto wallets, and messaging tokens.' Systematic enumeration of secrets across multiple sources in seconds is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single process (especially PHP-spawned children) accesses 5+ credential sources within 60 seconds: ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, .env files, browser cookie databases, password manager vaults, cryptocurrency wallet paths. Include registry access on Windows (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Credentials).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Attacker C2 with Subsequent File Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil. After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery.' Combined exfil + cleanup is a behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with encrypted/obfuscated payloads to flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil. Correlate with antecedent credential enumeration (file accesses to credential stores). Follow with file deletion events (unlink, Remove-Item) on temporary or vendor directories. Combined chain is high-confidence breach indicator.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Resolution from Attacker-Controlled Fork
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases.' This exploits SCM/package registry integration weakness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist tag ingestion and correlate with GitHub fork activity. Alert if: tag in official namespace resolves to commit in external fork; commit timestamp is recent (within hours of tag creation); commit introduces new files (helpers.php) or modifies autoload sections. Implement signed commits/tags and fork-resolution restrictions.

suggestion.title: Infection Marker Creation to Prevent Re-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It writes an infection marker to a per-host temporary directory so the host is only infected once.' Marker file creation followed by cleanup is a defense-evasion signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of suspiciously-named marker files in /tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%, or similar locations (patterns: .infected, .lock, .processed, .marker) immediately after Composer initialization or autoload execution. Alert if marker is created, then deleted shortly after (cleanup attempt). Correlate with PHP process lifecycle.

suggestion.title: Rewritten Git Tags in Managed Package Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector stated: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'. Pipeline missed detection for git history manipulation and tag recreation patterns typical of supply-chain persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on force-pushes to tag refs, tag deletions followed by identical tag recreations with different commit SHAs, or timestamps where tag metadata predates commit authorship. Supply-chain adversaries rewrite tags to inject malicious code while maintaining apparent legitimacy.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Source Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromise of Composer packages. Pipeline produced no detection for unexpected package repository sources, version constraints bypass, or mirror substitution attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.lock for package sources deviating from primary registry, unusual version selections that skip security patches, or composer-repo-plugin hooks altering package resolution. Flag when security-critical projects unexpectedly pull from alternative mirrors.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Exfiltration from Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective stated: 'Steal CI Secrets'. Pipeline has no detection for secrets being collected, logged, or transmitted from CI pipelines during dependency installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CI logs where environment variables containing tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN, CI_PAT, AWS_CREDENTIALS) are printed, passed to network calls, or written to artifacts. Correlate against unexpected post-install script execution or new CI job permissions (especially secret access scope changes).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Composer post-install scripts provide natural execution point for supply-chain payloads to exfiltrate secrets. Article implies code execution but pipeline missed detection of script invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Composer post-install scripts spawning child processes (curl, bash, python) with inline commands, particularly those writing to world-readable locations or contacting external IPs. Flag if vendor package install hooks invoke utilities not declared in composer.json.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of stolen secrets requires outbound communication. Pipeline missed detection for CI runner network activity to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/HTTP POST requests from CI runners to domains lacking package registry or CDN reputation, especially those receiving URL-encoded or base64 payloads. Baseline normal package downloads and flag deviations; alert on requests from build agents to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Hash Mismatches
suggestion.rationale: Rewritten tags produce different content hashes than historical versions. Pipeline missed integrity verification as a detection vector for package tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer.lock entries where expected package hashes diverge from repository-published hashes, silently ignored verification errors in dependency resolution, or Composer invocations with integrity checks disabled (--no-verify flags). Cross-reference against package security advisories.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48172 Exploited' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or detection logic for this active exploit
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel-related HTTP endpoints for requests matching known CVE-2026-48172 payloads or parameter injection patterns. Correlate timing and source IP with post-exploitation activity (root process creation).

suggestion.title: Root Process Execution via LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'run scripts as root' privilege escalation outcome, but no detection rules generated for privilege boundary violation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned as root (uid=0) with parent PID originating from cPanel/httpd daemon (apache, www-data, or equivalent). Filter on absence of legitimate privileged execution paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Execution in LiteSpeed Context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes running scripts as root but pipeline missed detection for script execution (bash, perl, python) spawned from cPanel plugin handler
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect invocation of interpreters (sh, bash, perl, python, ruby) or script files with command-line arguments, parent process matching LiteSpeed/cPanel service accounts, and escalation to root context.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin File Modification or New File Write in Root Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE 'as root' implies file system write capability at elevated privilege; no file system change detection use case generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor write/create events in sensitive cPanel directories (/usr/local/cpanel, /etc/cpanel) and system paths (/usr/local/bin, /etc) with source process tracing to LiteSpeed plugin handler or spawned children.

suggestion.title: Unexpected HTTP Method or Path to LiteSpeed cPanel Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely requires HTTP POST/PUT to cPanel or LiteSpeed management endpoint; no HTTP anomaly detection rule suggested
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to cPanel admin paths (/frontend, /cpsess*, /backend) or LiteSpeed control endpoints with unusual methods, body sizes, or parameter encodings (base64, hex, URL encoding chains).

suggestion.title: Nginx Pool Exhaustion DoS — Connection Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'DoS' attacks; title mentions 'poolslip,' implying connection/memory pool exhaustion. No use case was generated to detect abnormal nginx connection rates or pool depletion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx access logs and process telemetry for sustained spike in concurrent connections, unusually high SYN arrival rates, or rapid connection churn. Correlate with nginx error logs for 'connection pool exhausted' or similar messages.

suggestion.title: Nginx Process Crash or Restart Following Exploit Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Code execution or crash as outcome of 'poolslip' attack is mentioned in title. No use case detects nginx unexpected termination or rapid restart cycles post-attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on nginx process exit with non-zero exit codes, unexpected nginx service restarts within short time windows, or nginx child process crashes preceded by anomalous HTTP request patterns in preceding logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Nginx Configuration or Module Injection
suggestion.rationale: 'Code execution' in title suggests attacker may attempt to inject malicious nginx config or load rogue modules post-exploitation. No detection for config tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx config file (/etc/nginx/nginx.conf and included dirs) and module directories for unauthorized writes or modifications. Cross-reference with known admin change windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Package Version Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes '2FA-gated publishing' as defense; implies malicious actors are currently able to publish unauthorized versions. Detection should alert on unexpected package version bumps from legitimate publishers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API logs for package_publish events on high-value packages where publisher account has not issued a commit/tag in source control within the expected release window. Flag new versions published without corresponding git tag or CI/CD artifact.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Account Access (Pre-2FA)
suggestion.rationale: The threat model—2FA-gated publishing—assumes attackers can currently compromise npm accounts. Detection should identify behavioral anomalies preceding unauthorized publishes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm account login from new geography, new device, or off-hours if publisher typically works specific timezone. Correlate with failed login attempts. Flag if 2FA prompt is answered by attacker before publish attempt.

suggestion.title: Installation of Trojanized Package Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article frames 'install controls' as defense; supply-chain attacks deliver payload at install time. Should detect when dev/CI environment installs package versions with unexpected code changes or metadata anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / package-lock.json updates; alert if resolved version differs from package.json pinned version or if package hash diverges from expected NPM registry hash. Correlate with unusual child process spawning during install.

suggestion.title: npm Account Enumeration / Typosquatting Package Registration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often precede by registering similar-named packages. Article implies package controls are now scoped to prevent installation; should detect attacker reconnaissance or registration of suspicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag registration of new npm packages with names close-matching (edit distance <2) to high-dependency packages, published by new accounts with no prior publish history or published within seconds of legitimate version update.

suggestion.title: 2FA Bypass or Token Theft (Post-Control Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output omitted discussion of 2FA itself as a control being bypassed. If the article describes 2FA as new defense, attackers will target 2FA tokens directly; should detect token reuse or MFA prompt interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 2FA prompt followed by successful publish from different IP/user-agent than expected. Flag if npm session tokens are used from multiple geographies within impossible-travel window.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion / Private Registry Fallback Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'install controls' suggest mitigating attacks where public packages are installed instead of private ones; should detect when internal dependencies resolve to public npm instead of private registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install traffic; alert if internal/scoped package (e.g., @company/util) resolves to public npm registry instead of internal registry, or if version > internal max-version is installed.

suggestion.title: Malicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes supply-chain compromise of Laravel-Lang packages. Pipeline produced no detection for suspicious package installation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation or import of laravel-lang packages from non-official repositories or with unexpected version strings. Detect when composer or npm install commands pull packages with modified checksums or from mirrors not matching official Packagist/npm registry URLs. Correlate with first-execution of PHP or JavaScript payloads in package vendor directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction Post-Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'credential stealer' functionality. Zero use cases generated despite this being the primary malicious payload behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from PHP/Node interpreter that access credential stores (DPAPI, SAM registry, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, browser credential vaults). Flag unexpected registry queries to HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\PasswordLess or HKU hives. Monitor for keylogging APIs or clipboard access from package code.

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration from Package Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies command-and-control communication or data exfiltration. No network-based detection use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS or raw socket connections from PHP/Node processes running package code. Detect DNS queries to newly-registered or low-reputation domains from composer/npm child processes. Flag credential-containing POST payloads or base64-encoded exfiltration in HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Execution in Package Files
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware typically uses obfuscation to evade static analysis. No execution-layer detection for code obfuscation patterns in vendor directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded strings or hex-encoded payloads being executed via eval(), passthru(), or system() calls within vendor directories. Flag PHP files using variable function calls ($var() syntax) where $var is populated from obfuscated data. Monitor for excessive string decoding operations in package bootstrap files.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Cache Poisoning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack implies repository-level compromise. No detection for suspicious package metadata, altered composer.lock, or registry tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to composer.lock or package-lock.json files that predate the install timestamp or contain hash mismatches. Detect when package metadata (version, source URL, checksum) differs between local Composer cache and official registry. Alert on fallback to unofficial mirrors or retries to non-official package sources.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer harvests authentication material that enables follow-on attack. Pipeline provided no detection for credential use or authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After package installation, detect use of harvested credentials (SSH keys, API tokens, database passwords) for authentication outside the original deployment context. Monitor for authentication failures followed by successful logins from different source IPs or off-hours. Flag SSH connections using private keys extracted from ~/.ssh or AWS API calls with exfiltrated credentials.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS SQL Injection Exploitation (CVE-2026-26980)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-26980) in Ghost CMS to inject malicious JavaScript code' – zero detection rule generated for SQLi attack vector on Ghost endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Ghost CMS (versions 3.24.0–6.19.0) containing SQL metacharacters or union-based injection payloads in query parameters. Monitor for unusual admin endpoint access or 200 responses returning database metadata or API keys to unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Admin API Key Exfiltration via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'read arbitrary data from the website database, including the admin API keys' – no credential-access detection despite explicit key theft step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SQL query results containing Ghost admin API key patterns (long alphanumeric strings from sensitive tables) being returned to external IPs. Alert on immediate API calls from that same IP using extracted keys within minutes of injection exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles' and 'JavaScript code is a lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure' – pipeline missed persistent JavaScript injection and loader chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS article modifications via admin API for addition of script tags or iframes. Baseline expected JS size and libraries; alert on new loader scripts with external fetch calls. Track second-stage payload domains referenced in injected code.

suggestion.title: Visitor Fingerprinting and Conditional Content Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cloaking script that fingerprints visitors to determine whether they qualify as targets. Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt' – no coverage of defense-evasion via fingerprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript performing excessive device fingerprinting (Canvas API, WebGL, navigator enumeration) followed by conditional iframe rendering. Flag suspicious iframe injections claiming to be Cloudflare with unusual styling or domain typos. Correlate with bot/headless browser detection evasion patterns.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering – Command Execution via Windows Shell
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'instructs victims to verify that they are human by pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt, which drops a payload' – no detection for ClickFix lure execution or cmd prompt payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as child of web browsers (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe, iexplore.exe) with command lines containing download/decode/execute patterns. Flag obfuscated PowerShell invocations. Monitor for process chains: browser → shell → executable drop.

suggestion.title: Electron-Based Malware Payload Execution (UtilifySetup.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Electron-based malware sample named UtilifySetup.exe' – despite explicit malware name, no payload-specific detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Blacklist UtilifySetup.exe and variants by name. Monitor for execution from temp directories, Downloads, or AppData. Track DLL injection patterns and unusual module loads (particularly Node/Chromium DLLs indicating Electron framework). Alert on execution chains originating from browser-spawned shell commands.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Anthropic Claude Model Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Claude Mythos Preview' as subject. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite title clearly indicating suspicious interaction with Anthropic's AI systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal API calls to Anthropic Claude endpoints from internal networks. Flag authentication attempts to Claude preview environments using non-standard service account credentials. Alert on bulk queries or high-volume API usage inconsistent with baseline.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Intelligence Gathering
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '10,000+ 0-Days'—clear vulnerability research/collection activity. Pipeline failed to map any discovery-phase detections despite this central threat indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk downloads of CVE databases, PoC repositories (GitHub, ExploitDB), or zero-day threat feeds. Alert on vulnerability scanning tools targeting systems tagged as critical infrastructure. Track access to internal vulnerability management platforms by non-security accounts.

suggestion.title: Project Glasswing Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Project Glasswing' as target. Zero collection-phase or exfiltration-phase use cases generated despite obvious data-theft scenario implied by zero-day context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file access or downloads tagged with 'Glasswing' project metadata. Alert on unusual data transfers to external storage or cloud services from developer/research accounts. Track copying of sensitive project artifacts to USB or network shares.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Unauthorized Push by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'hacked 700 GitHub repos'—requires detection of commits pushed by compromised developer accounts injecting malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits authored by previously-dormant accounts, pushed outside historical activity windows, or bypassing branch protection rules. Flag mass commits to package files (composer.json, version tags, language files) with atypical author/committer metadata.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Version Published to Packagist Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '233 versions of Laravel-Lang Packages compromised'—requires detection of poisoned releases reaching the package registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist for releases from compromised maintainer accounts with unexpected version bumps, unsigned builds, or rapid sequential releases. Alert on versions that revert previous security patches or carry suspicious metadata.

suggestion.title: Leaked GitHub Personal Access Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 700+ repos implies stolen credentials; 'hacking' GitHub accounts requires detecting exposed tokens being used for repository modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference GitHub secret-scanning alerts with audit logs showing API calls from leaked PATs. Detect PAT usage from new geolocations, non-standard user agents, or CI/CD environments not previously seen for that account.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Package Initialization Files
suggestion.rationale: Laravel-Lang packages typically load translations via service providers; article indicates code compromise, requiring detection of unauthorized modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on diffs adding executable PHP to non-code files (language JSON files, config arrays) or new function calls to external infrastructure in package entry points (ServiceProvider, boot methods). Flag obfuscated or Base64-encoded strings added to translation files.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Credential Compromise Indicator – Repo Access Spike
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 700 GitHub repos at scale implies either bulk token theft or credential reuse across multiple accounts; detect anomalous access concentration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub organizations where unique accounts performing commits spike >3σ above baseline in short windows. Correlate with authentication from non-standard locations, residential ISPs, or shared VPN/proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: End-User Composer Install of Poisoned Laravel-Lang Package
suggestion.rationale: Developers worldwide pulling the compromised package via 'composer install/update' represents the execution/impact phase for downstream victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer.phar execution followed by instantiation of compromised Laravel-Lang classes, loading of translation files, or unexpected subprocess spawning from vendor/laravel-lang directories. Correlate with external DNS queries or network connections not typical for language package initialization.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for the initial exploitation vector (likely CVE-2020-5410, CVE-2023-46805, or similar). Requires monitoring for malicious HTTP requests to BIG-IP admin console or iControl REST API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: F5 BIG-IP receives HTTP POST/GET requests to sensitive endpoints (/mgmt/tm/sys, /icontrol, /admin) with encoded payloads or unusual query strings. Look for 4xx followed by 200 response (auth bypass) or direct shell metacharacters in request URI.

suggestion.title: Unexpected SSH Session from Network Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Title states attackers 'Gain SSH Access'. Pipeline missed detection for SSH egress from F5 BIG-IP (a network appliance, not typically SSH-active) to internal Linux hosts. Establish baseline of BIG-IP outbound SSH (should be none or minimal).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: BIG-IP device initiates SSH connection (TCP/22) to internal Linux subnets. Correlate source=BIG-IP, destination_port=22, and compare against known admin SSH workflows. Flag any SSH session lasting >10 minutes or repeated reconnects.

suggestion.title: BIG-IP-to-Linux Command Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'. Pipeline did not capture lateral movement detection for post-compromise activity. Need to detect when a compromised BIG-IP executes commands or copies files to downstream Linux systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SSH connections from BIG-IP to Linux targets with subsequent process creation events (bash, sh, curl, wget) on those targets. Windows hosts: look for lateral movement tools (PsExec, WinRM) being staged from BIG-IP. Detect if BIG-IP is used as pivot point for reconnaissance (net view, ip route, arp, ssh-keyscan).

suggestion.title: BIG-IP Credential Misuse or Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article headline implies attacker gained 'SSH Access'—likely via credential theft from BIG-IP config or admin password compromise. Pipeline did not suggest detection for credential enumeration on BIG-IP or unusual authentication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BIG-IP authentication logs for failed login attempts followed by success (T1110 brute force), or exported secret files (/etc/passwd, SSH keys, config backups). Detect if root/admin credentials are replayed on Linux systems outside normal change windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation of BIG-IP implies arbitrary code execution. Pipeline did not suggest detection for unusual processes spawned during BIG-IP compromise (e.g., shell, curl, wget, ncat).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: BIG-IP system spawns shell processes (bash, sh, tmux) or network utilities (curl, wget, nc, ssh, scp) from unexpected parent processes or as SYSTEM/root. Look for scheduled task creation (cron) added by non-admin accounts or persistence mechanisms (crontab, rc.local modifications).

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Configuration Export or Backup Access
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of BIG-IP suggests attacker may have exfiltrated configuration files (which contain credentials, SSL certs, internal network topology). Pipeline missed collection/exfiltration detections specific to appliance data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BIG-IP configuration export commands (tmsh save sys config, scf dump) or file transfers (scp, sftp, HTTP PUT) exfiltrating /config, /var/backup, or SSL key directories to external IPs. Detect large data transfers from BIG-IP to untrusted destinations.

suggestion.title: Composer Autoload Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'injected a malicious file named src/helpers.php, which was automatically loaded by Composer' and that it was 'added to autoload section of composer.json'. No detection use case was provided despite this clear persistence/execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected PHP files being added to Composer autoload directives in active projects, especially helpers.php or utility files in src/. Correlate with git tag rewriting events or package version downgrades. Alert on execution of PHP files from Composer vendor paths that were not present in previous package versions.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to flipboxstudio.info
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious PHP payload 'downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info' but no network-based detection was generated despite explicit domain IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info from development machines or CI/CD runners. Flag connections originating from PHP processes, particularly those spawned during Composer install/update operations or post-installation hooks.

suggestion.title: PHP Credential Stealer Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents sophisticated credential harvesting via regex patterns for 'AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Slack tokens, Stripe secrets, database credentials, JWTs, SSH private keys' and extraction of '.env configuration files'—yet no behavioral detection for credential enumeration was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes accessing .env files, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube config directories, or password manager stores in rapid succession. Flag regex operations or string matching against common credential patterns. Monitor for subprocess invocation of git, kubectl, vault, or cloud CLI tools from PHP processes running as composer-installed code.

suggestion.title: Windows Embedded Executable Extraction from PHP
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'embedded Windows executable extracted within the file, which is written to the %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched'—the DebugElevator component targeting browser credential decryption is a critical payload stage not addressed in detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes writing randomized .exe files to %TEMP%. Correlate with process execution of those temp executables. Flag any process with DebugElevator PDB path references or those targeting Chrome/Brave/Edge processes with App-Bound Encryption key extraction attempts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Version Rollback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector relies on rewriting git tags to point to malicious commits; article states 'rewrote every existing git tag in each repository'. No detection for suspicious package version manipulation or tag-based installation anomalies was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Composer installations pinning to historical version tags of laravel-lang packages (or any Composer package) where the tag's commit hash differs from the published release history. Monitor git webhook events for sudden tag rewrites across multiple repositories within the same org. Flag installations of packages immediately after tag rewrite events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Package Repository Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article documents attackers 'compromised 233 versions across three repositories' and that 'all four repositories share the same fake author identity, the same modified files, and the same payload behavior'. No use case for detecting this coordinated multi-repo attack pattern.
