suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware commonly steals credentials, source code, or environment variables post-install (article: 'supply chain trapdoor malware' in URL suggests espionage payload). Pipeline produced zero exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic from package manager contexts to non-whitelisted IP ranges. Alert on access to .ssh, .aws, .git directories or credential files immediately following package installation. Flag base64-encoded or compressed exfiltration payloads.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Package Repository or Mirror Access
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit package manager trust. Article implies attacker control over package distribution. Pipeline generated zero IOCs or detections for unexpected registry/mirror access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager connections to non-standard registries, typosquatted domains, or mirrors with unusual TLS certificates. Alert on suspicious HTTP headers, authentication token leakage, or repeated failed authentications preceding successful installation.

suggestion.title: Version Downgrade or Dependency Substitution Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit namespace confusion and typosquatting. Article references '34 Packages'—suggests multiple substitution vectors—but pipeline surfaced no version-control or dependency-manipulation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manifest files (package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml) for sudden version downgrades, wildcard pinning, or dependencies resolving to unexpected sources. Correlate with audit logs of manifest modifications.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation of Ghost CMS Admin API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to steal the admin API keys' and notes the vulnerability affects 'Ghost 3.24.0 through 6.19.0' allowing 'unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary data from the website database.' Pipeline must detect SQLi payloads targeting Ghost's known vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to Ghost CMS endpoints (commonly /ghost/api/admin, /members/api) containing SQL syntax patterns (UNION SELECT, comments, subqueries). Baseline requests from known Ghost admin tools; alert on 401/200 responses indicating successful auth bypass or data exfiltration followed by API key extraction patterns.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Stolen Ghost Admin API Keys for Article Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'then use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles' and notes admin keys 'can be used to modify article pages.' Pipeline must detect anomalous admin API calls post-compromise (API key creation, article edits from unusual IPs/user agents, bulk article modifications).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls using admin keys from IPs outside known editorial ranges or outside business hours. Alert on rapid successive article updates (>5 edits in <1 minute) or updates to articles not previously modified by that key's owner. Cross-reference against Ghost version to identify calls from unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into CMS Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injected 'lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code' and 'JavaScript code... loaded via an iframe on top of the article page.' Pipeline must detect JavaScript snippets with loader/iframe/external-fetch patterns in article HTML.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan article HTML for dynamically-inserted <iframe> tags, <script src=> patterns pointing to attacker infrastructure (especially non-CDN domains), and JavaScript containing 'fetch', 'XMLHttpRequest', or 'eval'. Baseline articles to identify legitimate embeds; alert on new inline or remote-loaded scripts appearing in previously-clean articles.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Fake Cloudflare Prompt Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page, which contains the ClickFix lure' and 'instructions [to] verify that they are human by pasting a provided command.' Pipeline must detect Cloudflare impersonation in iframes and social-engineering text patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for iframes loading HTML containing 'Cloudflare', 'verification', 'security check', or 'challenge' text alongside suspicious command-copy instructions (cmd.exe, PowerShell references). Flag mismatched domain ownership (iframe SRC from non-Cloudflare domain). Alert on iframe z-index or overlay CSS designed to obscure underlying content.

suggestion.title: UtilifySetup.exe and Electron-Based Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Electron-based malware sample named UtilifySetup.exe' and mentions 'DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers' deployed post-ClickFix infection. Pipeline must alert on execution of this file and related payload staging patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation of UtilifySetup.exe or similar .exe files with Electron-based code signatures. Monitor for child processes spawned by these samples (cmd.exe, PowerShell). Flag unusual parent processes (explorer.exe, browser.exe) launching these files or network connections to attacker C2 during execution.

suggestion.title: Visitor Fingerprinting and Cloaking Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes cloaking infrastructure that 'fingerprints visitors to determine whether they qualify as targets' before serving ClickFix payload. Pipeline must detect reconnaissance and selective targeting behavior in compromised content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to injected scripts for User-Agent collection, IP/geolocation queries, browser fingerprinting (navigator object), or conditional rendering logic. Alert when a single IP receives different content from the same URL (cloaking detection). Flag scripts that conditionally load the ClickFix iframe only for specific User-Agents or geographies.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Drupal Core SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks'—this is the primary attack vector and warrants detection of SQL injection payloads in HTTP requests to Drupal installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal endpoints (e.g., /admin/*, /node/*, /user/*) for SQL injection patterns. Look for UNION-based, time-based blind, and error-based SQL injection signatures in query parameters and POST data. Flag requests containing SQL keywords (SELECT, UNION, WHERE, OR 1=1) combined with typical Drupal parameter names.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Drupal Database Query Activity
suggestion.rationale: Once SQL injection succeeds, attacker executes arbitrary database queries. Article indicates exploitation in active attacks, suggesting data exfiltration or enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for high-frequency UNION queries, information_schema enumeration, or queries outside normal Drupal ORM patterns. Flag SELECT statements executed by the web application user that bypass expected ORM frameworks or target system tables.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Fingerprinting via Changelog/README Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploiting known Drupal CVEs typically first fingerprint the target version. CISA advisory implies specific version targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated access to version-disclosure endpoints: /CHANGELOG.txt, /README.txt, /includes/bootstrap.inc, or Drupal admin status pages from external sources. Correlate with subsequent SQL injection attempts from the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Detect Installation of Known-Malicious Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Compromised 34 Packages'—must detect when environments pull or execute these versions. Package names, version numbers, and hashes should feed detection rules before victims install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm, pip, cargo install/pull operations and correlate package version against threat intelligence feeds of known-malicious package releases. Alert on installation of flagged versions and block execution of code from those package directories.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Process Execution from Package Installation Paths
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages execute malicious payloads on victim machines. Article mentions 'trapdoor malware'—need execution detection from node_modules, site-packages, target/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with parent or image path in node_modules/, .venv/lib/pythonX.X/site-packages/, or cargo target/ directories. Correlate with recent package installations and alert on unexpected spawning of shell, powershell, curl, or nc.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Package Repository Publish Events
suggestion.rationale: Attack required uploading malicious package versions to npm, PyPI, Crates registries. Need detection of publish/upload operations with unauthorized credentials or anomalous account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registry APIs (npm publish, pip upload, cargo publish) for authentication from unusual IP ranges, VPNs, or geolocations. Alert on accounts with no prior publish history or publish events outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Dependency Chain Poisoning via Transitive Imports
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks propagate through dependency resolution. Alert when environments pull new transitive dependencies or unexpected version cascades from compromised packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor lock files (package-lock.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.lock) for additions of previously-unseen transitive dependencies or version pins differing from manifest files. Flag rapid cascading dependency updates across multiple sub-packages.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Network Behavior Originating from Package Installation Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages may exfiltrate data or callback to C2. Article references 'trapdoor'—need network monitoring of package execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network connections (DNS queries, TCP/UDP flows) initiated by processes spawned from package directories against reputation feeds. Alert on connections to newly registered domains, bulletproof hosters, or infrastructure associated with threat actors.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Browser-Locking Scareware Modal / Full-Screen Overlay
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Browser-Locking CypherLoc Kit' — describes malware that renders full-screen warning overlays to prevent browser navigation. No detection was created for this signature behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript execution within browser processes that disables back/close buttons, prevents tab switching, or displays full-screen modal with lock/warning imagery. Correlate with network requests to scareware C2 or fake-Microsoft domains.

suggestion.title: Fake Microsoft Support Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Microsoft Support Calls' — social engineering campaign impersonating Microsoft support. No detection for lookalike Microsoft domains was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and HTTP connections to domains spoofing Microsoft support infrastructure (e.g., 'support-microsoft.net', 'msft-security.org', 'microsoft-help.tk'). Flag subdomains of non-Microsoft registrars mimicking official Microsoft support URLs.

suggestion.title: CypherLoc Malware Execution / File Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'CypherLoc Kit' as the specific malware tool. No malware signature, file hash, or behavioral detection for this family was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CypherLoc execution via known file hashes, behavioral analysis (e.g., unsigned DLL injection into browser processes, mshta/rundll32 spawning obfuscated payloads), or yara signatures matching CypherLoc variant code patterns.

suggestion.title: Known Tech Support Scam Callback Phone Number / Email Beacon
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Fake Microsoft Support Calls' — the scareware displays callback phone numbers. Detection of users contacting or reporting these numbers to security teams should be triggered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain IOC list of known tech support scam phone numbers and emails. Alert on internal reports of employees calling these numbers, receiving support-scam callback attempts, or visiting associated SMS links.

suggestion.title: Browser Extension Installation / Persistence by CypherLoc
suggestion.rationale: Browser-locking malware commonly persists via unsigned extensions or hijacks extension stores. Article's 'Browser-Locking' mechanism suggests persistence layer. No detection for abnormal extension installation was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned browser extensions installed without user interaction, especially those that execute at startup, disable safety features, intercept navigation, or prevent tab closure.

suggestion.title: Malvertising / Compromised Website Redirect Chain to CypherLoc
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Hackers Use' CypherLoc but omits delivery vector. Scareware typically arrives via malvertising redirects. No detection for suspicious ad network redirects or landing page chains was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for redirect chains originating from legitimate advertising networks or legitimate websites that lead to scareware hosting domains. Alert on double-redirect patterns and known malvertising infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Postinstall Hook Execution from Package Managers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware spreads 'via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' implying execution through package install hooks. Pipeline generated no detection for postinstall script or setup.py execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell or interpreter process spawning (bash, python, node) from package manager context (npm node_modules/.bin, pip site-packages) with execution within 1-2 minutes of package install completion. Parent process should show installation context.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from Installed Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing malware' but pipeline provided no detection use case for credential enumeration following package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by node.js, Python, or Rust interpreters that open/read files in credential storage paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, Windows Credential Manager APIs) or access environment variables containing API keys or tokens.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Package Namesquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via package managers commonly use similar names to legitimate packages. Article mentions attack on multiple registries but no detection for package name anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline popular package names and flag installations of similar variants (edit distance < 2, homoglyph substitution, namespace confusion). Correlate against rapid growth in download counts relative to publish date.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials via Package Process Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware must exfiltrate stolen data; pipeline included no exfiltration detection despite article describing credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from processes spawned by installed packages to destinations outside of package CDN and official repository ranges. Flag domains contacted with high frequency from short-lived package processes.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack Package Repository Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'spreads via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' but pipeline failed to suggest package metadata or installation logging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package manifest integrity (track package.json/requirements.txt versioning), validate package signatures, and alert on installations where package author, size, or dependencies changed unexpectedly between versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt (SQL Injection vs. Ghost CMS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'exploiting [CVE-2026-26980] to steal the admin API keys.' This is the initial access vector. No detection logic generated despite being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS endpoints for SQL injection payloads (UNION, OR 1=1 variants). Flag requests to authentication or admin API routes with SQL metacharacters or encoding patterns typical of SQLi. Ghost versions 3.24.0–6.19.0 are in scope.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin API Key Access or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal the admin API keys' and 'can be used to modify article pages.' No detection for anomalous API key queries or exfiltration of admin credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database queries (SELECT statements) against Ghost admin credential tables or config stores. Monitor API calls from unusual source IPs, high request volumes, or requests accessing sensitive admin endpoints (users, themes, API keys) without prior activity from that credential.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject malicious JavaScript into articles' and 'JavaScript code is a lightweight loader.' No detection for content integrity or persistence via article modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor article/content update logs for modifications containing JavaScript, <script> tags, iframe tags, or references to external attacker infrastructure. Compare article snapshots to previous versions to detect injected payload code. Flag rapid successive modifications to the same article.

suggestion.title: Iframe-Based ClickFix Lure (Fake Cloudflare Prompt)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page.' No detection for suspicious iframes or social engineering payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iframes with fake Cloudflare branding, unusual iframe sources pointing to attacker C2 domains, or iframes that obscure legitimate page content. Monitor HTTP responses for unexpected Content-Security-Policy violations or injected <iframe> elements in legitimate articles.

suggestion.title: Command-Line Execution from Browser or Script Context (ClickFix Payload Drop)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'instructs victims to verify that they are human by pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt, which drops a payload.' Detection for cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from browser or JavaScript context is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag parent-child process chains where cmd.exe or powershell.exe are children of browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) or script interpreters. Alert on suspicious command-line flags like /c with multi-part commands, certutil, bitsadmin, or download-execute patterns. Correlate with time of user web browsing.

suggestion.title: Payload Delivery: UtilifySetup.exe or DLL Loader Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'UtilifySetup.exe' as a specific malware sample and mentions 'DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers' but no file-based detection generated. This is a concrete IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of UtilifySetup.exe or unknown executables in TEMP/Downloads following ClickFix interaction. Monitor for DLL load events from unexpected paths, parent-child chains typical of Electron-based loaders, or unsigned binaries with execution policies violated. Alert on file writes to System32 or registry modifications during payload drop window.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Drupal Core SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks' but pipeline generated zero use cases. SQL injection is the core attack vector and should be detected via WAF logs, application logs, or HTTP request analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests containing SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, OR, --) targeting Drupal endpoints (e.g., /user, /node, /admin). Correlate with Drupal version enumeration (e.g., CHANGELOG.txt requests) and look for 5xx or database-error responses immediately following payload attempts.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Enumeration and Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'CISA Warns' of vulnerability, implying active reconnaissance. Attackers typically enumerate Drupal version before exploitation (accessing CHANGELOG.txt, /admin paths, or checking CSS/JS version headers).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of HTTP requests to known Drupal version-disclosure endpoints (CHANGELOG.txt, .git/config, sites/default/settings.php) followed by SQLi payloads within 10 minutes. Flag on multiple failed requests to /admin or /user with varying query parameters.

suggestion.title: Database Query Anomaly Post-SQLi Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful SQL injection execution would result in unauthorized database queries. Article implies 'exploited in attacks' but no detection scenario covers resulting data access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal database connection patterns (e.g., queries from web application service account selecting from user tables, accessing _sessions, or dumping schema) correlated with preceding web application error logs or slow query logs indicating SQLi execution.

suggestion.title: CISA Vulnerability Alert Ingestion and Threshold Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'CISA Warns'—this is a formal government advisory. Pipeline should flag when CISA advisories are parsed and correlate to known-vulnerable systems in inventory.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Database Export or Credential Harvesting via SQLi
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection implies potential access to user_data, passwords, or session tokens in Drupal database. Article states exploitation is 'in attacks' but no detection covers post-SQLi data exfiltration.

Correlate with base64-encoded or GZIP-compressed data in HTTP headers.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Compromise—New Package Versions Uploaded
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 34 packages compromised across npm, PyPI, Crates—this is initial_access (attacker controls package registry or maintainer account). Pipeline produced zero use cases covering malicious package delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories for unexpected version releases from known authors (version bumps outside cadence, new authors on existing packages, unusual publishing timestamps). Cross-reference with hash submissions to VirusTotal or MD5 databases flagged as malicious within 24 hours of package release.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks achieve impact when compromised dependencies are installed and executed in downstream CI/CD or dev environments. Pipeline missed detection for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package manager commands (npm install, pip install, cargo fetch) are followed within seconds by unsigned or suspicious child processes (downloads from attacker infrastructure, spawning shells, writing to temp directories). Correlate package versions against known-bad hashes.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Download from Dependency Initialization Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware commonly hides payload delivery in post-install or build scripts. Article describes attacker-controlled packages but pipeline surfaced no detection for obfuscated code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm run-scripts, pip setup.py, or cargo build scripts that decode/decompress staged payloads (base64, gzip, uuencode strings in script source). Flag any exec() or subprocess calls within initialization hooks pointing to external URLs or temp file execution.

suggestion.title: Cross-Registry Supply Chain Attack—Same Malware Family Across Ecosystems
suggestion.rationale: Attackers compromised packages in npm, PyPI, AND Crates simultaneously—article title explicitly notes multi-ecosystem targeting. Pipeline generated zero cross-registry correlation rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate alerts for malicious packages detected in npm, PyPI, and Crates registries deployed within 6-hour windows. Group by common hash, C2 beacon pattern, or exfiltration target. Flag as high-confidence supply-chain campaign if same code signature or actor infrastructure appears across all three ecosystems.

suggestion.title: Browser Lock Screen Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CypherLoc 'locks browser'—fundamental attack signature. Article: 'Browser-Locking CypherLoc Kit'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes creating fullscreen/modal dialogs blocking user interaction, modifying browser start pages to unreachable URLs, or injecting persistent overlay windows that disable task manager/browser controls.

suggestion.title: Fake Microsoft Support Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly uses 'Fake Microsoft Support Calls'—scareware redirects to spoofed domains. Article: 'Push Fake Microsoft Support Calls'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser navigation to domains mimicking Microsoft support (e.g., microsoft-support, ms-help, support-microsoft variations) especially when combined with aggressive popup/alert rendering or certificate validation bypasses.

suggestion.title: Tech Support Scam Call Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Push Fake Microsoft Support Calls' as distribution/monetization method—implies social engineering callback chain. Article: 'Fake Microsoft Support Calls'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CypherLoc infection timestamp with outbound phone call records or VoIP session logs; flag infections followed by social-engineering callback patterns (credential entry attempts post-support contact).

suggestion.title: CypherLoc Malware Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CypherLoc kit identified as active malware family but zero file hash IOCs extracted. Must detect on behavioral signature: browser process spawning, code injection, registry persistence. Article: 'CypherLoc Kit'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or suspicious scripts/exes establishing browser persistence (RunOnce, Startup folders), injecting into browser processes, or installing browser extensions without user consent; correlate with simultaneous browser lock and fake-domain activity.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Harvesting Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Tech support scams commonly exfiltrate credentials typed during fake-support sessions. Scareware payloads often enable clipboard logging to capture payment/credential data. Article: 'Push Fake Microsoft Support Calls'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes repeatedly accessing clipboard APIs or reading clipboard via command-line (Get-Clipboard, xclip, pbpaste) immediately after CypherLoc execution or browser-lock events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Install Script Execution from Public Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—these ecosystems execute install hooks automatically during 'npm install' / 'pip install' / 'cargo build'. Attack vector is script execution at dependency resolution time, not runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from npm/pip/cargo with unusual command lines (powershell, curl, base64-decode, reverse shells). Correlate process lineage: npm.exe→cmd.exe→powershell.exe or equivalent Python/Rust patterns. Cross-reference with recently installed packages.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting API Hooks Post-Package-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies payload as 'credential-stealing malware'—harvesting mechanism must be present. Typical post-install malware hooks Win32 credential APIs (Advapi32, WinHTTP) or Python/Rust credential libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process injection into LSASS or credential management processes, DLL/module load of credential libraries post-install, or suspicious registry access to HKLM\Security\SAM or HKCU\Volatile Environment (cached credentials). Watch for API hooking patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'credential-stealing'—stolen data must leave the host. Supply chain malware commonly establishes HTTPS/DNS tunnels for exfiltration to centralized C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS POST/PUT or DNS queries from processes spawned during package install, particularly to newly registered domains or non-package-registry IPs. Correlate with credential-formatted payloads (base64, JSON with auth tokens, plaintext passwords).

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Compromised Maintainer Account Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise occurs via either typosquatted package names or stolen maintainer credentials. Article does not specify which variant; detection must surface both patterns in npm/PyPI/CratesIO registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package uploads with: names Levenshtein-distance-close to popular libraries, unusual metadata (different maintainer email/account from legitimate versions), version anomalies (stable published before pre-release), or re-uploads of withdrawn versions.

suggestion.title: Discovery of Credential Stores During Post-Install Execution
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must enumerate where credentials are stored (browser caches, git config, .ssh, environment variables, credential managers). This reconnaissance typically occurs in install scripts before harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes forked from npm/pip/cargo running 'find', 'ls -la', or 'dir' against credential locations: ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.git-credentials, Windows Credential Manager, browser profile directories. Flag unusual filesystem enumeration from install context.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Unexpected Code Execution in Package Manager Contexts
suggestion.rationale: npm/PyPI/CratesIO install scripts bypass traditional code-signing enforcement. Article describes distribution of malware through these unsigned contexts—detection should flag when install-time code violates expected behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes executed from package cache directories (node_modules/.bin, site-packages, ~/.cargo/registry) that exhibit anomalous behavior: network I/O, persistence mechanisms (registry writes, cron/systemd additions), in-memory code injection, or unsigned binary execution.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Parameter Probe Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited'—core attack vector. Zero detection use cases generated despite this being the primary exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal web server logs for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, EXEC, DROP, OR 1=1, SLEEP, BENCHMARK) in query parameters, POST bodies, and HTTP headers. Baseline common injection points: search fields, views filters, exposed REST endpoints, menu parameters. Alert on encoding bypass attempts (%%32%30, 0x, backticks).

suggestion.title: Post-SQLi Unauthorized Database Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploited in attacks'—implies active compromise and data harvesting. Pipeline surfaced zero collection-phase detections for database access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database audit logs showing SELECT * or table enumeration queries originating from Drupal application service account within 5 minutes of suspicious HTTP error spike (40x/50x patterns). Correlate to source IP reputation and database connection timing.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Implant via Drupal File API Post-SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Active SQL injection exploitation chains to persistence via web shell upload or PHP file creation. Article implies ongoing attacks but zero persistence-phase detections offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal web root directories (/modules, /themes, /sites/default/files, /core) for unexpected PHP/Perl/JSP file creation or write events, especially with timestamps correlating to SQLi probe spikes or database error logs. Flag files with modified/access times mismatched from Drupal core update cycles.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE Advisory Timeline-Based Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CISA Warns'—indicates published CVE, advisory ID, and patch timeline. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs (CVE, affected versions, remediation dates).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate discovered Drupal installations (via /admin, Server header, /user/login URIs on ports 80/443) against CISA CVE database for matching version. Flag unpatched instances >7 days post-advisory publication. Cross-reference with web server access logs for 40x/50x error spikes or SQLi pattern matches within 30-day post-disclosure window.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database Credential Harvesting via SQLi
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection against Drupal's settings.php or database abstraction layer typically leaks database credentials, enabling lateral movement. Article describes active exploitation but no credential-access phase coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Drupal application processes (php-fpm, httpd, nginx) spawn command shells (bash, cmd.exe) post-SQLi probe, or when settings.php/database config files are read via unexpected process chains. Monitor for environment variable exfiltration (DRUPAL_DB_PASSWORD, $db_url export).

suggestion.title: Drupal Module Staging via Database Schema Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Advanced SQLi exploitation can insert malicious modules into Drupal's database module registry without filesystem writes. Article implies sophisticated attacks; zero detection for this anti-forensics technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database audit logs for INSERT/UPDATE statements targeting drupal_modules, drupal_system, or system_table with suspiciously short activation timestamps. Correlate to HTTP requests with admin-level privileges or newly registered user accounts. Flag module names or namespaces not in official Drupal package index.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Firewall Interface Scanning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states '597,000 Sessions Observed' targeting SonicWall firewall interfaces. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear scanning attack pattern described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume connection attempts or port scans against known SonicWall management interface ports (typically 4444, 8443, 443). Correlate source IP geolocation and ASN against threat intel. Flag patterns with >50 failed login attempts or repeated port probes from unique external IPs within 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance - Firewall Device Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active scanning of firewall interfaces as reconnaissance activity. No use case created to detect enumeration of network perimeter devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to default SonicWall admin paths (/admin, /login, /config) from external IPs. Alert on User-Agent strings or request patterns consistent with automated reconnaissance tools (curl, nmap, Shodan-like probes).

suggestion.title: Brute Force Attack on SonicWall Admin Interface
suggestion.rationale: 597,000 sessions implies sustained connection attempts; if article mentions failed auth or repeated logins, this indicates brute force. Pipeline missed persistence/credential access angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >10 failed authentication attempts against SonicWall admin interface from single source IP in 10 minutes. Baseline normal admin login rates; anomalous spikes indicate credential brute force.

suggestion.title: CypherLoc Browser Lock Overlay Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Browser-Locking CypherLoc Kit'—malware renders full-screen overlay/lock preventing user interaction. Phrase: 'browser-locking'. Pipeline missed all execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on browser processes creating full-screen windows with disabled task-switching, DisableTaskMgr registry modifications, or JavaScript patterns using window.moveTo(), focus traps, and ESC/F12 keypress suppression. Correlate with obfuscated script execution in browser context.

suggestion.title: Fake Microsoft Support Credential Harvesting via Form Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'push fake Microsoft support calls'—social engineering attack harvesting credentials. Phrase: 'fake Microsoft support'. Pipeline should detect form overlays and credential entry patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clipboard reads/writes of high-entropy data (passwords) by browser processes during suspicious form submission, or detect outbound exfiltration of form field values containing common credential patterns. Alert on JavaScript keyloggers or form-submission interception.

suggestion.title: CypherLoc Malware Dropper via Drive-by or Email
suggestion.rationale: CypherLoc is a 'kit'—implies packaged distribution payload. Article context suggests initial infection vector. Phrase: 'CypherLoc Kit'. Pipeline produced no execution chain or IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious script execution (PowerShell, VBScript, HTA) with deobfuscation behavior, or process trees where browser/email spawns base64-decoded executables. Monitor for downloads with mismatched MIME types or double-extension patterns.

suggestion.title: Scamware Command & Control Communication to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Browser-locking + credential theft malware requires exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. Article implies ongoing C2 for call redirection and payment processing. Phrase: 'push fake Microsoft support calls' suggests remote orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS requests and HTTPS connections from infected browsers to newly-registered or suspicious domains hosting fake support pages. Alert on high-volume outbound connections to non-standard ports from browser processes during credential-harvesting sessions.

suggestion.title: Registry/File System Persistence by CypherLoc Malware
suggestion.rationale: Browser-locking malware requires persistence across reboots. Pipeline should detect malware installation and auto-start mechanisms. Phrase: 'CypherLoc Kit' suggests sophisticated installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry writes to HKLM/HKCU RunOnce, Run, or shell override keys, or file creation in Startup folders with obfuscated names. Alert on browser extension installation from unsigned sources or BHO (Browser Helper Object) registration.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only RAT Execution via Indirect Syscalls
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly emphasizes 'memory-only RAT' and RemotePE as fileless malware; no disk artifacts should be detectable. Pipeline missed detection for in-memory code execution and indirect syscall patterns typical of evasion-focused RATs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with minimal command-line arguments, absence of associated on-disk executable, or unusual parent-child relationships indicative of in-memory injection. Alert on ntdll.dll / kernel32.dll virtual alloc + write + execute sequences, and syscall stubs patched inline.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beacon Pattern Recognition
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus attribution is explicit in title; pipeline failed to capture actor name or typical C2 communication signatures. Financial/crypto targets suggest network-based C2 over HTTPS with certificate spoofing or beaconing intervals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 traffic via anomalous DNS queries to newly registered domains, HTTPS connections to IPs with minimal SSL certificate history, or beaconing patterns (fixed intervals, small payloads, repeating sequences).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Financial Admin Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'financial and crypto firms,' implying post-compromise lateral movement to reach high-value accounts and systems. Pipeline missed detection for credential access and lateral movement to admin/privileged systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track lateral movement via RDP, SMB, or WMI to financial workstations from initial beachhead. Alert on local admin logons from unusual source IPs, pass-the-hash indicators (identical NTLM hashes across logons), and remote process execution on finance-tier systems.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Crypto firms are explicitly mentioned; article likely discusses credential harvesting from exchange platforms, wallets, or associated admin panels. Pipeline missed credential-access detections for finance-vertical targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for keylogger/screencapture tool execution, process injection into browsers, or credential-dumping utilities. Alert on unusual child processes spawned by crypto exchange software or high-frequency clipboard access.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Loader Detection via VirtualAlloc Patterns
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE is explicitly named as the malware; it is a known memory loader used by Lazarus. Pipeline should have generated specific detection logic for RemotePE's characteristic VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect/CreateRemoteThread call sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RemotePE behavior via sequence of VirtualAlloc (PAGE_READWRITE) followed by WriteProcessMemory, then VirtualProtect (PAGE_EXECUTE_READ), then CreateRemoteThread. Look for process hollowing or reflective DLL injection patterns on legitimate processes.

suggestion.title: Azure-Hosted Domain C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Azure-Hosted C2 Domains' but pipeline generated zero network-based detections. This is a command-and-control pattern with high operational relevance: legitimate cloud infrastructure repurposed for malicious callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from endpoints to known Azure C2 domains (once extracted from article). Detect periodic beaconing patterns (regular temporal intervals, repeating connection sizes) and correlate with MiniUpdate execution events. Cross-reference Azure IP allocation databases to identify abuse of legitimate cloud ASNs for C2.

suggestion.title: MiniUpdate RAT Process Execution and Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'MiniUpdate RAT' as the attack vector but no execution-phase use case was generated. RAT implantation and process manipulation are critical detection points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signatures for MiniUpdate RAT execution: process name anomalies, unsigned binaries, suspicious command-line obfuscation, DLL sideloading patterns, and memory injection into system processes. Correlate process creation time with subsequent C2 network initiation to confirm compromise chain.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Over C2 to Azure Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Targeted Espionage Campaigns,' indicating data theft, yet no exfiltration use case addresses data egress over the identified C2 channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor connections to Azure-hosted C2 domains for abnormal data transfer volume, uploads of sensitive file types (documents, databases, credential stores), or sequential data exfiltration patterns coinciding with user-initiated file access. Flag scenarios where file read + network transmit occur in rapid succession to Azure endpoints.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection Post-RAT Execution
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns typically establish persistent lateral movement after initial RAT foothold. No use case covers post-compromise enumeration or network propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After MiniUpdate RAT execution, detect reconnaissance activity: net/ipconfig/arp commands, SAM/LSASS access, credential dumping tools, or PSEXEC/WMI lateral pivots. Correlate timing and source process (MiniUpdate child processes) to establish causality with C2-directed attacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Compromised Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO.' Supply chain attacks target package repos. Need detection for installation of malicious package variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/pip/cargo installation logs and processes for packages named similarly to legitimate libraries (typosquatting). Alert on installation of packages absent from project manifest or dependency files. Flag rapid mass-installation patterns from single source.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Package Installation Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing malware.' Detect when package install scripts access credential stores, env vars, SSH keys, or cloud config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes of npm/pip/cargo that read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .git config, or environment variables containing secrets. Detect file exfiltration from credential directories during install phases. Monitor for inline scripts in package.json/setup.py referencing credential paths.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Package Manager Build Phase
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware typically executes via postinstall scripts or build hooks. Article: 'spreads...malware via package managers' implies execution during install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of curl, wget, bash, powershell, or python from npm/pip/cargo package installation processes. Flag process trees where child processes of package managers execute arbitrary code. Monitor for scripts defined in lifecycle hooks (preinstall, postinstall, prepare) that download/execute remote code.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing payload requires exfiltration channel. Article payload is credential theft, implying C2 callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections from node_modules, site-packages, or .cargo processes to non-ASN enterprise destinations. Flag DNS exfiltration patterns from package manager processes. Detect HTTPS POST with encoded credential payloads to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Package Lock File Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks persist through package manifests and lock files. Detect modifications to package-lock.json, requirements.txt, or Cargo.lock that inject malicious dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to package lock files in version control. Alert on lock files that reference packages absent from source manifest. Detect version mismatches between declared and resolved package hashes.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Against Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack entry: 'attacks that XLab observed begin by exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to steal the admin API keys' via unauthenticated SQL injection on Ghost 3.24.0–6.19.0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS installations for SQL injection patterns in request parameters targeting database metadata or sensitive tables. Alert on unexpected database errors, timeouts, or UNION-based query responses. Correlate SQLi attempt timing with subsequent suspicious admin API key usage within minutes for high-confidence exploitation detection.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin API Key Exfiltration and Privilege Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability impact: attackers 'read arbitrary data from the website database, including the admin API keys' and 'use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles' and modify themes/users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost admin API key usage for anomalies: new source IPs, bulk article/user modifications, theme alterations, or API calls to sensitive endpoints occurring outside normal admin patterns. Alert on single API key making hundreds of changes within hours or accessing database schema endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'inject malicious JavaScript into articles. The JavaScript code is a lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect article content modifications and HTTP responses for injected JavaScript: inline script tags, external loader sources, obfuscated payloads, or iframe injection within article bodies. Correlate with suspicious API key usage. Flag scripts that dynamically fetch and execute third-stage code from attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloaking Script Visitor Fingerprinting and Selective Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Defense evasion layer: 'cloaking script that fingerprints visitors to determine whether they qualify as targets. Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt.' This selective targeting hides compromise from casual inspection and security scanners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript that harvests system/browser fingerprinting data (User-Agent, screen resolution, installed plugins, WebGL capabilities, timezone, language). Alert on iframe injection mimicking legitimate vendors (Cloudflare, reCAPTCHA). Identify response variance for identical content paths served to different user agents, indicating conditional/cloaked payload logic.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering: Fake Cloudflare Verification and Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Payload delivery mechanism: 'fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page, which contains the ClickFix lure... instructs victims to verify that they are human by pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt, which drops a payload.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe/powershell.exe execution chains initiated from browser context (parent: explorer.exe with article-hosting domain in recent history). Look for encoded/obfuscated arguments using rundll32, certutil, or other LOLBins. Correlate command timing with iframe injection and user copy-paste activities from fraudulent Cloudflare verification pages.

suggestion.title: UtilifySetup.exe Electron Malware and DLL Loader Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific payloads: 'XLab has observed multiple payloads being used in these attacks, including DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers, and an Electron-based malware sample named UtilifySetup.exe.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for UtilifySetup.exe execution, particularly from %TEMP%, AppData, or Downloads directories. Monitor DLL loader chains via rundll32/regsvcs with suspicious ordinal exports. Alert on Electron-based executables contacting non-Microsoft domains. Flag DLL loaders spawning secondary processes or injecting into legitimate services; correlate with article-based infections.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'exploited in attacks' but pipeline created no detection for SQL injection payloads targeting Drupal. Web logs showing POST/GET requests with SQL syntax to Drupal endpoints are the primary forensic artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, INSERT, EXEC) and SQL metacharacters in URI parameters and POST bodies targeting Drupal endpoints (e.g., /admin, /user, /node). Correlate with HTTP 500/400 responses indicating query errors.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Query Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection, if successful, grants attacker ability to read/write database directly. Article implies active attacks but no detection for unusual DB query patterns was produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries originating from web-application service accounts with unusual patterns: DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, CREATE USER, GRANT PRIVILEGES, or SELECT INTO OUTFILE. Baseline normal query frequency and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core File System Access Following SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection in Drupal can lead to file write/read; article warns of 'exploited attacks' implying post-compromise activity but pipeline missed file-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/modification in Drupal directories (sites/default/files, modules) from web server process with suspicious timing (coinciding with web requests containing SQL keywords). Flag executable file creation in web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: Database Credential Harvesting via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection may grant attacker ability to query user tables for credential hashes. Article does not detail but is standard post-exploitation: 'SELECT * FROM users_table' extraction not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries from web-application service accounts targeting authentication/user tables (e.g., users, admin, credentials). Flag bulk data export patterns via SQL (INTO OUTFILE, LOAD DATA) or web-response size anomalies.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor Installation via SQL Injection to File Write
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection frequently leverages INTO OUTFILE or LOAD_FILE to write PHP/ASP shells; article cites 'exploited' attacks but no web shell detection pattern created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php, .jsp, .aspx file creation in web-accessible directories following SQL injection attempts. Correlate with HTTP GET requests to newly-created web paths with suspicious parameter passing. Cross-reference with web shell signature detection (e.g., shell.php, cmd.aspx patterns).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Targeting Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Kali365...phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal' and 'AI-generated phishing lures.' Device code phishing is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or text mentioning device code, device login, authorization code, or device verification. Flag lures with urgency language and urgency around account verification, MFA setup, or security alerts. Correlate with Office 365 Defender for phishing and suspicious link detection.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth Device Code Grant Followed by Immediate MFA Completion
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it...Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token.' This is the core credential theft mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authorization grant flow (RequestType=Device or AuthenticationMethod=DeviceCode) followed by immediate MFA completion from anomalous geographic location, unusual ISP, or user agent not associated with the user's baseline. Flag impossible travel patterns between code generation and MFA completion.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation for Activity Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Inbox rules are a defense evasion technique to remove evidence of intrusion and reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbox rule creation from untrusted IP ranges, unusual client applications (mobile, third-party apps), or outside business hours. Flag rules that delete, move to folder, or permanently delete emails. Alert on rules created by compromised accounts with no history of rule management, or rules forwarding/copying to external domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Entra Following Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Device registration enables persistent access even if password changes occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new device registrations (DeviceRegistered event) from unusual geographic regions, from ISPs never seen for the user, or at times inconsistent with user behavior. Flag device registrations immediately following OAuth token grant activity or phishing email delivery to that user. Alert on device names containing malware names or generic identifiers.

suggestion.title: Session Hijacking via Adversary-in-the-Middle Proxy (Cookie Link Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' Session cookies enable account access without MFA re-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AitM patterns by identifying identical or very similar user agents from disparate IP subnets connecting within minutes. Monitor for session cookies issued from legitimate Microsoft endpoints (login.microsoft.com) that are subsequently used from geographically distant or uncommon networks within the same day. Flag unusual geolocation jumps between cookie issuance and usage.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise OAuth Token Reuse Across Multiple SaaS Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms, which are then used to steal data.' Stolen OAuth tokens are used for lateral spread and data collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for a single OAuth token or user session accessing multiple disparate SaaS platforms (Salesforce, Box, Slack, ServiceNow, Workday) in rapid succession or outside normal user behavior patterns. Alert when a user accesses SaaS applications they have never accessed before, or accesses more applications in one day than their historical average. Correlate with mailbox access for bulk export activity.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Management Port Scanning Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '597,000 Sessions Observed' scanning 'SonicWall Firewall Interfaces'—direct evidence of coordinated reconnaissance (T1595.002) at scale. Pipeline missed the most obvious detection: abnormal scanning patterns to firewall admin ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag source IPs performing high-frequency connection attempts to SonicWall management ports (443, 8443, 8000, 4444) with rapid-fire unsuccessful handshakes. Aggregate by source IP and alert when any source exceeds 50 failed connections/hour or targets >5 distinct internal SonicWall IPs within 6 hours.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Exploitation Post-Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale firewall scanning campaigns of '597,000 Sessions' typically precede exploitation of known CVEs. Pipeline must surface follow-on attack patterns: T1190 exploitation attempts (likely SonicWall auth bypass, RCE).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to SonicWall authenticated endpoints (/login, /admin, /api/authenticate) from source IPs that previously exhibited scanning behavior. Flag payloads containing SQL injection, path traversal, or command injection patterns. Alert on successful 200 responses following failed login attempts.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Firmware Fingerprinting Requests
suggestion.rationale: Systematic scanning of '597,000 Sessions' implies attacker enumeration of SonicWall firmware versions. Should detect T1592.001 (query version endpoints).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to information disclosure endpoints (/api/version, /api/system, /system-info, /cgi-bin/admin.cgi with no payload) from external IPs. Flag scripted request patterns (identical User-Agents, rapid sequential requests, curl/wget/python-requests signatures). Alert when same source queries version endpoints across multiple SonicWall IPs.

suggestion.title: Distributed Scanning Campaign Coordination Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents '597,000 Sessions'—volume and consistency suggest coordinated botnet or proxy-based campaign. Should detect T1595 patterns indicating command-and-control (C2) orchestration of scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate scanning source IPs by targeting pattern: flag when multiple IPs probe identical SonicWall ports in identical sequence within same time window. Detect shared user-agent strings or TLS JA3 fingerprints across sources. Alert on scanning waves that reset at fixed intervals (indication of C2 tasking).

suggestion.title: Browser Full-Screen Scareware Lockdown with Control Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Full-screen mode with right-click menus disabled, Hidden cursor and screen overlays, Automatic relocking when users attempt escape'—behavioral signature unique to scareware/malicious browser state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser process creating full-screen overlay with disabled input controls (right-click suppression, cursor hiding). Correlate with unsuccessful attempts to exit full-screen (F11, Escape key events followed by re-fullscreen). Baseline: legitimate full-screen rarely re-locks on escape attempt.

suggestion.title: AES Payload Decryption Triggered by URL Fragment Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'uses AES encryption and only executes when specific URL fragment values are present' with 'cryptographic integrity checks before executing anything.' No public sandbox detection because conditions must be met for activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript performing AES decryption (crypto.subtle.decrypt calls), particularly when code path checks URL.hash or location.fragment before executing payload. Correlate with subsequent DOM manipulation or redirection. Alert on uncommon cryptographic operations in unexpected browser contexts.

suggestion.title: Developer Tools Trigger Anti-Analysis Asset Reload Loops
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies that 'Opening browser developer tools triggers asset reloads and repeated layout recalculations, overwhelming analysis capabilities.' This is a direct anti-sandbox evasion mechanism exploitable for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scripts that detect debugger presence (e.g., console.clear() loops, performance.memory checks) followed by rapid successive HTML/CSS asset reloads from same origin. Flag script pattern: devtools-detection → high-frequency fetch/reload → layout thrashing.

suggestion.title: Fake Credential Forms with No Functional POST Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Fake login forms appear requesting credentials—they never process input but serve to intensify panic.' Non-functional forms on scareware pages are distinct behavioral pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form submission events (POST/GET from HTML form) on pages displaying browser-lock scareware patterns, where submission targets non-existent endpoint or loops back to same page. Correlate: fake-login-form + full-screen-lock + warning-sounds = high-confidence scareware.

suggestion.title: Public IP Address Retrieval and Injection into Malicious Page
suggestion.rationale: Article notes kit 'retrieves and displays victims' public IP addresses, creating a false sense of targeted danger.' IP geolocation calls followed by DOM injection are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to IP geolocation services (ipinfo.io, geoip.json, etc.) originating from browser context with subsequent DOM mutation events injecting returned IP into visible page content. High signal when correlated with scareware indicators.

suggestion.title: DOM Content Replacement and Page Scrubbing After Payload Decryption
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'After successful decryption, the original page content is erased and replaced entirely with new scareware content, resetting live inspection scripts.' Rapid wholesale content replacement is behavioral anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script executing document.body.innerHTML = '', followed by large-scale DOM tree replacement. Alert on innerHTML / outerHTML mutations removing >80% of original page structure. Correlate with prior crypto operations and URL-fragment checks.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Modular Payload Staging and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'modular espionage ecosystem'—implies multi-stage execution. Article body unavailable, but modular malware families typically load components from temp directories or registry; needs detection for unsigned DLL injection or process hollowing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or suspicious executables spawning from Temp, AppData, or Downloads directories followed by rapid DLL loading or injection patterns. Kazuar modular architecture likely stages payloads in-memory; correlate process creation with network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Kazuar C2 Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware described as 'espionage ecosystem' for 'Secret Blizzard operations' strongly indicates persistent C2. Pipeline should have extracted C2 IOCs and beacon signatures from article but received no content.

Flag DNS queries for C2 domains not in allow-list; correlate with local discovery activity (process/file enumeration).

suggestion.title: Kazuar Credential Dumping Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Espionage families routinely dump OS credentials and application secrets; title mentions 'Secret Blizzard operations' suggesting high-value target reconnaissance. Pipeline output contains no credential access techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LSASS.exe process access from non-System/Svchost processes, registry queries to HKLM\SAM, or execution of credential dumping utilities (mimikatz, secretsdump) on systems with Kazuar process artifacts. Correlate with C2 exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Kazuar System Discovery and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Modular espionage malware collects system/network inventory before exfiltration. Article unavailable; standard gap for reconnaissance-focused APT families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of native discovery tools (tasklist, systeminfo, net view, wmi queries) in rapid succession post-Kazuar execution or from its child processes. Flag if tool output piped to suspicious destinations (temp files, network sockets).

suggestion.title: Kazuar Data Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Espionage ecosystem inherently exfiltrates collected intelligence. No exfiltration IOCs or detection use cases generated despite article title explicitly naming espionage operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic to Kazuar C2 domains for large or unusual payload sizes post-discovery activity. Flag compression/encryption signatures (ZIP headers, base64 patterns) in network streams. Correlate exfiltration timing with credential dumping or file access events.

suggestion.title: DPAPI-based Loader Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes DPAPILoader decrypting and loading RemotePELoader using Windows DPAPI: 'DPAPILoader decrypts and loads RemotePELoader from disk using the Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI)'. Detection must capture this specific decryption behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DPAPI key access patterns followed by unexpected DLL loading from parent processes (loader chain). Look for CreateRemoteThread or similar injection after DPAPI calls. Flag sequences where legitimate Windows processes access DPAPI keys immediately before loading suspicious binaries.

suggestion.title: Chrome Zero-Day Exploitation via Fake Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack vector: 'hackers posing as legitimate trading firm employees on Telegram and luring victims to fake meeting sites like counterfeit Calendly portals' followed by 'suspected Chrome zero-day exploit' for 'silent code execution on the victim's machine'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect visits to typosquat or fake domain variants of Calendly, Picktime, and similar meeting portals (calendly-meeting.com, picktime-booking.com, etc.). Correlate with Chrome process crashes, unexpected child processes, or sudden endpoint logging gaps. Flag domains registered to hosting providers with high abuse rates.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only RAT Polling Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article defines RemotePE as executing 'entirely in memory and never written to disk' and describes it 'polls a command-and-control (C2) server for further instructions'. The memory-only nature and polling behavior are distinct IOA signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for memory-resident processes with consistent periodic outbound connections (polling intervals) to Namecheap-hosted or similar shared hosting providers. Correlate with absence of corresponding disk artifacts and EDR evasion indicators. Flag non-browser processes initiating HTTP/HTTPS connections at fixed intervals.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'After several months of reconnaissance and lateral movement, the Lazarus subgroup cleans up earlier artifacts and installs the more advanced RemotePE RAT to solidify long-term access'. Multi-stage cleanup and upgrade pattern indicates established persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences where PondRAT (early-stage loader) activity ceases abruptly, followed by ThemeForestRAT appearance in memory, and eventually RemotePE installation. Monitor for credential enumeration and network reconnaissance between first and third-stage deployments. Detect process cleanup (deletion of early artifacts) before final RAT installation.

suggestion.title: Telegram-Coordinated Social Engineering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack initialization: 'The actor impersonates an existing employee of a trading company on Telegram and sets up a meeting with the victim, using fake meeting websites'. This is the initial social engineering vector requiring user-behavior monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for employee reports of unsolicited Telegram contacts claiming to be internal staff. Cross-reference with employee directories for credential spoofing. Flag clicks on shortened URLs or unusual domains received via Telegram from new contacts. Identify fake Calendly/Picktime URLs in Telegram conversations and associated IP/ASN patterns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Malware Family Deployment Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes precise progression: 'attackers immediately deploy PondRAT as a first-stage loader, followed by the stealthier ThemeForestRAT running purely in memory. After several months of reconnaissance...installs the more advanced RemotePE RAT'. Each stage has unique behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rules detecting the ordered deployment of PondRAT → ThemeForestRAT → RemotePE (or RemotePE variants). Flag systems where memory-based implants appear following named-loader activity. Monitor for rapid RAT family succession within days/weeks of initial compromise, correlating with cleanup activities.

suggestion.title: MiniUpdate RAT C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Azure-Hosted C2 Domains for Targeted Espionage Campaigns.' Pipeline extracted zero detection for C2 beaconing. This is the core attack vector and demands immediate detection logic.

Detect periodic beacon patterns to C2 infrastructure. Monitor DNS queries to subdomains or dynamic resolution patterns consistent with RAT callbacks.

suggestion.title: MiniUpdate RAT Process Execution & Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'MiniUpdate RAT' as the threat but pipeline produced zero execution-phase detections. RATs typically involve process spawning, injection, or living-off-the-land execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MiniUpdate malware execution via process hollowing, DLL injection into legitimate processes (explorer.exe, svchost.exe), or obfuscated PowerShell/CMD spawning. Monitor for suspicious parent-child process chains or unsigned DLL loads from temp directories.

suggestion.title: Azure Infrastructure Abuse for Malicious Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically highlights 'Azure-Hosted' C2—pipeline missed defense-evasion opportunity. Adversaries abuse Microsoft-trusted cloud services to evade reputation filters and blend with legitimate traffic.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to MiniUpdate C2
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Espionage Campaigns'—implying data theft—but pipeline extracted zero exfiltration detection. No use cases for monitoring data staging, archiving, or exfil to C2.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from npm/PyPI/CratesIO
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'Malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—core attack vector is compromised package distribution. Pipeline missed fundamental detection for supply chain execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager calls (npm install, pip install, cargo install) for execution of unusual post-install scripts or network callbacks. Alert on package versions matching known TrapDoor indicators or on installation from unusual/newly-created accounts.

suggestion.title: Package Post-Install Script Execution to Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Credential-Stealing Malware'—payload execution must occur during/after package installation. Pipeline missed the execution → credential-access transition.

Watch for obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads in package.json/setup.py/Cargo.toml.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Installed Package
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Credential-Stealing Malware'—malware must exfiltrate stolen credentials. No use case covers the exfiltration phase.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Package Maintainer Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack requires either account compromise or typosquatting. Article implies packages were uploaded to legitimate registries; missing detection for suspicious account login/publishing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/PyPI/CratesIO API logs for login anomalies: new geographic locations, unusual times, credential reuse from known breach databases, or publishing from previously dormant accounts. Flag version bumps that include suspicious dependencies.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion / Version Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use version precedence tricks or typosquats (e.g., 'urllib3' vs 'urlib3'). Article mentions three registries; pipeline missed naming/version anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation of packages with names very similar to popular libraries (Levenshtein distance 1-2), or packages with unexpected dependency trees (pulling in unrelated transitive deps). Flag version numbers with unusual tags (pre-release, build metadata abuse).

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from Compromised Package Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware must communicate exfil data; article does not specify C2 IOCs, but pipeline should detect callback patterns from package execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS from package-manager-spawned processes to IPs/domains not in known CDN/mirror allowlists. Correlate with timing of credential-access indicators (suspicious file reads, API calls to secret managers).

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt - Application Error Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited' with CISA warning. No SQL injection detection UC was generated despite active exploitation.

Alert on patterns like UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comment sequences (--,/*) in GET/POST parameters targeting vulnerable Drupal versions. Correlate with 500-level or 403-level HTTP responses indicating failed injection or WAF block.

suggestion.title: Drupal Post-Exploitation PHP Execution via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection to RCE pattern is standard in Drupal—payload executed into database then called. No execution-phase detection suggested.

suggestion.title: Drupal Webshell Persistence - Suspicious File Creation in Document Root
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection exploits typically install webshells for persistence. Article describes 'exploited in attacks' (plural/ongoing) suggesting post-compromise persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file creation in Drupal web root (sites/default/files, modules/, themes/) with .php, .phtml, .phar extensions written by web server user. Correlate timing with HTTP 4xx/5xx spikes. Alert on .htaccess or web.config modifications bypassing access controls.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database Direct Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection grants database query capability. No detection rule covers subsequent database enumeration or credential harvesting from wp_users or similar tables.
