Flag SELECT * queries on sensitive columns (password, hash, email) from non-admin accounts or script runners.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE-Specific Signature - Core Module Parameter Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'Drupal Core' vulnerability but no CVE ID or vulnerable parameter name extracted. Pipeline should correlate known-bad parameters with module versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate signatures for known-vulnerable Drupal module parameters (e.g., views module parameter injection, autocomplete disclosure endpoints). Log HTTP requests with parameter values matching the CVE payload signature and cross-reference against Drupal version headers or module presence fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Flow Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers abuse 'OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization grant flow' to 'trick targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page via phishing and social engineering.' This is the core attack vector yet no detection for it was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Entra Sign-in logs for device code authentication flows (grantFlowType='DeviceCodeFlow' or clientAppUsed containing device code indicators). Correlate with impossible travel, off-hours activity, or source IPs inconsistent with user baseline. Alert on device code flows immediately followed by MFA completion but token issuance to different principal or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Inbox Rules Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'in some of the attacks, attackers also created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Yet no UC for detecting suspicious inbox rule creation by compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ExchangeAdmin AuditLog (OfficeActivity) for New-InboxRule operations, especially rules created outside business hours, from unusual IPs, or rules that move/delete messages (properties containing 'DeleteMessage', 'MoveToFolder', 'SoftDeleteMessage'). Baseline per user and alert on first-time rule creators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Enrollment in Entra
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'in some of the attacks, attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access.' No detection UC for unauthorized device registrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Entra AuditLogs for 'Register device' operations (ResultDescription='Success'). Alert on device registrations from unusual IP addresses, off-hours registration, or registrations by users with no device management baseline. Correlate with concurrent unauthorized mailbox access.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass via OAuth Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Detection for this token bypass sequence missing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth Application Consent Grants

Pipeline missed detection for unusual OAuth permissions granted during phishing compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AuditLogs for 'Consent to application' operations by non-admin users, especially if the application name or publisher is suspicious, newly registered, or infrastructure-related. Correlate with concurrent device code activity or unusual mailbox access patterns from the same user session.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Containing Device Code References

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for payloads or request patterns exploiting CVE-2026-26980. Baseline expected Ghost version numbers and flag requests targeting known vulnerable endpoints with unusual parameter values, encoded payloads, or SQL injection syntax.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix-attributed malicious JavaScript, fake security warnings, or scareware popups in HTTP responses from Ghost CMS instances. Alert on sudden injection of foreign iframe or script tags referencing known ClickFix infrastructure domains.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Firewall Interface Scanning Activity

Flag scanning-pattern behavior: rapid sequential port/interface probes, malformed HTTP requests, or scanning tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Mass Reconnaissance on SonicWall Assets

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline session count for SonicWall-directed inbound traffic; alert on sustained scanning threshold (e.g., >500 sessions/day to firewall admin interfaces). Correlate with geoIP clustering and scanning tool fingerprints.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'scanning' of firewall interfaces, implying potential credential probing or exploitation attempts following reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Malicious SEO Poisoning Domain Detection via Fake Software Installers

suggestion.title: MiniFast Backdoor C2 Communication via HTTP Masquerading as Chrome
suggestion.rationale: Article states MiniFast 'masquerades as Chrome browser traffic' and uses 'HTTP endpoints' for C2. suggestion.rationale: Article specifies MiniFast 'exploits AppDomain hijacking, abusing how the .NET runtime loads application configuration files' allowing 'malicious DLL to execute inside the context of a legitimate, trusted process.' suggestion.title: Modular malware component injection and in-memory loading

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect in-memory deobfuscation loops (XOR, ROT13, AES decryption) followed by execution, use of legitimate system binaries (rundll32, powershell, regsvcs) to load encoded payloads, and suspicious memory allocation patterns preceding code execution.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploited.' Pipeline must detect POST/GET requests to LMS endpoints with injection payloads, malformed parameters, or crafted input triggering application-level errors indicative of CVE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /api/*, /admin/*, /user/*, /upload/* endpoints with unusual Content-Length, high-entropy parameters, multiple URL-encoding layers, or requests originating from non-standard User-Agents. Correlate with HTTP 500/400 errors.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell File Creation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Deploy BLUEBEAM Web Shell'—requires detection of .php, .aspx, .jsp files written to web-root directories with BLUEBEAM signatures, suspicious permissions, or creation timestamps outside maintenance windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on script-file creation in /var/www/*, C:\inetpub\*, or KnowledgeDeliver installation paths with file hashes matching known BLUEBEAM variants; flag ownership by system account writing to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Launch from Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Web shell execution implies non-standard command execution from IIS/Apache (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe spawned by w3wp.exe)—core post-exploitation activity after shell persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx parent processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or whoami.exe with command-line arguments; correlate with file creation in web directories.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTP(S) Callback from Web Server to Non-Standard Destination
suggestion.rationale: BLUEBEAM web shell requires command-and-control callback—detect outbound connections from application server processes to non-whitelisted domains, high-risk IP space, or recently-registered infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTP(S) from w3wp.exe or httpd to non-standard ports, domains flagged by threat-intel feeds, or IPs without WHOIS/DNS history; prioritize connections during off-hours.

suggestion.title: POST Request with Encoded/Obfuscated Payload to LMS Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation typically encodes payloads in POST body—article describes RCE via LMS, suggesting multipart or base64-encoded injection in request body or form parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to LMS endpoints with Content-Type multipart/form-data and file uploads with suspicious extensions, or URL-decoded payloads containing script tags, eval(), or system-command syntax.

suggestion.title: File System Access Pattern Anomaly in Web Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE leading to web shell implies unusual read/write activity in KnowledgeDeliver installation folder outside normal application behavior—detect sequential rapid file operations by web-server process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web-server process performing directory enumeration (sequential GetFileAttributes calls) or creating >5 files in <1 minute in web directories; baseline normal application I/O patterns.

suggestion.title: RemotePE RAT Process Execution and Memory Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'RemotePE Memory-Only RAT' as the malware deployed—the primary attack tool. The 'memory-only' characteristic implies process injection and in-memory execution to avoid disk IOCs. No execution detection was generated despite this being the core payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned DLL loads or inline assembly execution patterns that indicate process injection. Monitor for parent processes (e.g., explorer.exe, svchost.exe) spawning unusual child processes or allocating RWX memory. Flag obfuscated PowerShell or cmd.exe launches with encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Lazarus APT Command and Control Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes campaign to Lazarus by name. Lazarus has known C2 infrastructure signatures; pipeline should surface command-and-control callbacks, domain registration patterns, or IP ranges attributed to this actor. No C2 IOCs were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound connections from compromised financial systems against known Lazarus C2 infrastructure (IP/domain blocklists, SSL certificates). Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains with Lazarus-associated registrant patterns. Detect HTTP/HTTPS traffic with suspicious User-Agent strings or encrypted payloads matching known Lazarus protocol signatures.

suggestion.title: Anti-Forensics: Memory-Only Malware Execution Without Disk Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Memory-Only RAT'—this is a defense evasion characteristic designed to leave no PE files on disk, complicating forensics. No defense evasion techniques were mapped despite this being the core evasion mechanic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LOLBIN (e.g., rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, mshta.exe) launching with suspicious parameters or DLL-side-loading patterns. Monitor for processes with no associated on-disk binary or processes whose file path cannot be resolved. Alert on suspicious unsigned drivers or kernel-mode code injection.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft and Data Exfiltration from Financial/Crypto Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Financial and Crypto Firms'—these are data-rich environments. RATs deployed against financial institutions typically exfiltrate credentials, account information, and transaction data. No credential access or exfiltration use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data transfers from financial systems (database queries, file copies to staging directories). Detect credential dumping tool execution (mimikatz, procdump, sekurlsa). Track encrypted or obfuscated exfiltration channels (HTTP POST with large payloads, DNS tunneling, ICMP tunneling).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement and Privilege Escalation Within Financial Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates deployment 'Against Financial and Crypto Firms' (plural systems). Compromising multiple systems requires lateral movement and privilege escalation within the target environment. No lateral movement techniques were mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect remote service execution patterns (WMI, PsExec, RDP) originating from compromised systems. Monitor for unusual SMB shares being enumerated or accessed. Flag service creation and scheduled task establishment from non-standard accounts.

suggestion.title: Initial Access: Phishing or Spear-Phishing to Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus APT typically gains initial access via spear-phishing with malicious attachments or links targeting the financial sector. Article does not describe initial vector, but Lazarus' known TTPs strongly suggest phishing. No initial-access detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious email attachments (especially Office macros, executables, archives) received by employees in financial/crypto firms. Detect macro execution from recent documents. Flag users clicking links to attacker-controlled domains hosting exploit kits or credential-harvesting pages.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Hijacking – .NET Security Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states MiniUpdate 'employ[s] AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET security features before the host application loads, effectively blinding standard security monitoring tools.' No detection UC offered despite explicit evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AppDomain.CurrentDomain.SetData() calls with security-disabling parameters, especially in CLR initialization. Alert on registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\.NETFramework with security-reduction values, or suspicious managed code reflectively disabling AppDomainManager constraints.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task – Fixed Daily Execution Time
suggestion.rationale: MiniUpdate 'creates daily scheduled tasks firing at 09:30 local time.' Standard scheduler monitoring may not alert on suspicious *consistency* of execution timing. Article indicates deliberate operational rhythm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new scheduled tasks with daily recurrence and fixed 09:30 UTC/local trigger time, especially created by non-admin users or via WMI/PS. Correlate with suspicious parent processes (rundll32, regsvcs, regasm, mshta).

suggestion.title: File Size Inflation – Padding with Multilingual Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk V2 uses '12 megabytes containing thousands of meaningless code strings from languages like Java and Python' to evade scanning. No detection offered for this entropy-based obfuscation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag executables >5MB with low opcode density (>60% repeated padding bytes or auto-generated comment blocks) or High entropy sections misaligned with typical binary layout. Cross-reference against legitimate software baselines in target environment.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading – Dual-Layer with Benign Decoy Window
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dual-layer DLL sideloading' and 'benign decoy windows while silent infection proceeds background.' No use case captures the temporal correlation between decoy UI and background process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process pairs: legitimate application spawning alongside unsigned/mismatched DLL load, with UI window display within <1s. Correlate CreateProcess and LoadLibrary events; flag mismatched signer info between host EXE and loaded DLL.

suggestion.title: Azure-Hosted Domain C2 Communication – Behavioral Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Six Azure/spoofed domains listed (licensemanagers.azurewebsites[.]net, business-central.azurewebsites[.]net, PremierHealthAdvisory[.]com, Ramiltonsfinance.azurewebsites[.]net, etc.). Article notes 'per-target compartmentalized infrastructure.' No network UC; detection should target Azure subdomain C2 pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS POST to *.azurewebsites[.]net domains from non-browser processes, or to domains matching theme/licensing semantic patterns (licensemanagers, PeerDistSvcManagers, etc.). Alert on beaconing behavior (fixed interval, consistent URI paths).

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Activation Delay – Timestamp-Based Sandbox Evasion
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk V2 includes 'hardcoded activation delays (March variant: March 27, 2026, 13:30 UTC)' to defeat sandbox analysis. No use case for timestamp-gated execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument process execution to log and compare current system time against embedded constants in malware memory or binary. Flag executables with future-dated activation logic. Monitor for excessive early-exit paths or sleep loops tied to date/time API calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Public Repositories Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware spreading 'via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — packages installed from compromised public repositories are the attack vector, yet no use case exists to detect installation of poisoned versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager execution (npm install, pip install, cargo add, etc.) for installation of known-compromised package versions. Correlate with process tree to identify if package installation precedes credential access or C2 communication attempts.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Following Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies payload as 'credential-stealing malware' but pipeline suggests no detection for credential access/exfiltration that logically follows the installation phase of the supply chain attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious credential-stealing behaviors post-package installation: LSASS dumps, browser credential store access, Windows Credential Manager queries, API hooking patterns, or unusual keylogging-style input capture activity immediately following installation of packages from compromised registries.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from Compromised Package Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks universally establish command and control once malware executes; article describes credential-stealing which implies exfiltration, yet no C2 detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections initiated by Node.js, Python, or Rust runtime processes executing code from recently-installed packages, especially to suspicious or newly-registered C2 domains. Flag exfiltration of credential material over HTTPS or DNS.

suggestion.title: Package Registry Account Compromise or Takeover
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must have compromised or spoofed legitimate package accounts on npm/PyPI/CratesIO to publish malicious versions; article mentions 'spreads...via' these registries implying account or infrastructure compromise upstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository logs for anomalous publisher activity: new account registrations publishing to established namespaces, unusual geographic IP locations for account logins, rapid version publications, or changes to maintainer access controls on previously-dormant packages.

suggestion.title: Execution of Malware Payload Within Package Installation Hooks
suggestion.rationale: npm/Python/Crates ecosystem supports lifecycle hooks (install scripts, setup.py) that execute arbitrary code during package installation; article implies executable payload delivery but no detection for script-stage execution exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unexpected binaries or scripts spawned by package manager processes during install phase: shell spawning from npm/pip/cargo, execution of obfuscated or downloaded scripts, or runtime injection into interpreter processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 SQL Injection Exploitation (Ghost CMS)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to steal the admin API keys' and 'allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary data from the website database'. Clear initial access vector; pipeline generated zero detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances (3.24.0–6.19.0) for SQL injection patterns in unauthenticated endpoints: encoded payloads, union-based syntax, time-delay functions in parameters. Flag requests combining database enumeration (information_schema queries) with admin/settings API paths.

suggestion.title: Admin API Key Exfiltration and Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This key gives management access to users, articles, and themes, and can be used to modify article pages.' No detection for stolen key usage patterns or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin API authentication tokens obtained from database queries (non-human-initiated context) followed immediately by bulk article modification API calls. Alert on repeated API calls with legitimate credentials modifying content with JavaScript payloads or iframes.

suggestion.title: Persistent Malicious JavaScript Injection into Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'then use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles. The JavaScript code is a lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure'. Persistence mechanism entirely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS article update API calls and database writes for injected JavaScript, particularly script tags with external `src` attributes, fetch() calls to non-whitelisted infrastructure, or loader patterns with base64/URL-encoded payloads. Alert on articles modified by stolen admin tokens.

suggestion.title: Visitor Fingerprinting and Cloaking Script Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure, which is essentially a cloaking script that fingerprints visitors to determine whether they qualify as targets.' No detection for selective payload delivery or evasion behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript enumerating device/browser characteristics (screen resolution, installed plugins, user agent, timezone, language) followed by conditional branching to deliver payloads only to non-automated targets. Monitor for fetched scripts that gate content delivery on environment checks.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Lure via Spoofed Cloudflare Iframe
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page, which contains the ClickFix lure. The page instructs victims to verify that they are human by pasting a provided command.' No detection for social-engineering payloads or command-injection lures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iframes within article content mimicking Cloudflare's UI (CSS, logo injection, domain spoofing). Monitor for JavaScript that overlays/auto-scrolls to iframe content and prompts users to copy-paste commands. Correlate iframe load events with subsequent command-prompt process spawning.

suggestion.title: Payload Execution from Command Prompt (ClickFix Delivery)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt, which drops a payload on their systems... multiple payloads being used in these attacks, including DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers, and an Electron-based malware sample named UtilifySetup.exe.' No detection for post-compromise execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command prompt/PowerShell execution of curl/wget/certutil followed by local file execution shortly after ClickFix lure exposure. Alert on UtilifySetup.exe spawning, DLL injection patterns into legitimate processes, and JavaScript droppers executing via `wscript.exe` or `cscript.exe`.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Code Authentication Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page via phishing.' Detect anomalous device code OAuth flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authentication flows preceded by phishing email clicks or from suspicious IP ranges. Detect device code auth followed by immediate token creation without standard MFA re-validation. Flag logins to http://microsoft.com/devicelogin from non-standard referrers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Detect suspicious forwarding/deletion rules created after token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rules created within 30 minutes of anomalous OAuth token usage or device code authentication. Flag rules that delete or forward all emails, especially if targeting sensitive keywords or moving to external domains.

suggestion.title: Device Registration via Compromised OAuth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Persistence via Entra device registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registration events correlated with OAuth token usage from non-standard geographic locations or IP ranges within 1 hour of initial compromise. Alert on multiple device registrations from the same session token.

suggestion.title: Session Token Capture via Adversary-in-the-Middle (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' Detect AitM attack mode.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful MFA-completed authentication from victim IP immediately followed by session activity from geographically distant attacker IP. Detect cookies/tokens issued to legitimate user, then used from different IP/ASN within seconds of creation.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Reuse Bypassing MFA Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Token reuse is the core MFA bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens used from mismatched geographic locations or IP ranges vs. initial device code authentication. Alert on token-based sign-ins with zero MFA challenges when user has MFA enabled. Flag cross-tenant token usage or reuse outside normal time windows.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Phishing Campaign to Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal.' Detect phishing-at-scale with device code lures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing emails with URLs linking to legitimate microsoft.com/devicelogin portal. Correlate email delivery with device code OAuth flows within 15 minutes. Flag emails with urgency/impersonation language directing users to 'verify identity' or 'confirm access.'

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited'—this is the attack vector and should have minimal false-positive baseline for Ghost CMS installations. Pipeline extracted nothing.
log_sources: OLE2 logs from Ghost CMS modules
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS installations for HTTP POST/GET requests to known-vulnerable endpoints matching CVE-2026-26980 patch patterns. Flag version headers ≤vulnerable Ghost CMS versions or requests with serialization payloads targeting Ghost API routes. Correlate with 5xx response codes or admin panel login anomalies within 5 minutes of exploit attempt.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Injection Detection on Web Properties
suggestion.rationale: Article states '700+ Sites for ClickFix Attacks'—ClickFix is a known malware campaign that injects fake browser update prompts. Pipeline failed to identify this as a malware signature or detection scenario despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix indicators: (1) JavaScript injection patterns on high-traffic web domains (fake update prompts, browser-driver detection), (2) outbound C2 connections from web servers to known ClickFix C2 ASNs, (3) anomalous HTTP response size/encoding changes on previously clean pages, (4) presence of known ClickFix domains (https://updatereq[.]click, variants) in HTTP requests from web server logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Site Hijacking & Content Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'Hijack 700+ Sites'—successful exploitation resulted in site takeover. No detection logic for page modification, admin credential misuse, or unauthorized content injection was extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of web root files (index.html, .php, template files) by non-deployment service accounts or during off-hours. Monitor for rapid file changes across multiple web server instances in short time window (suggests worm-like propagation). Detect unexpected script injection in HTTP responses by comparing response hashes against baseline CDN/static asset signatures.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Panel Credential Compromise Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful hijacking of 700+ sites implies admin access was obtained; article context strongly suggests credential theft or account takeover post-CVE exploitation, but no detection use case for anomalous admin authentication was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin login logs for: (1) logins from unusual geographies/ASNs relative to baseline, (2) failed login attempts followed by successful login within 30s (brute force + success), (3) admin password reset events followed by immediate login from new IP, (4) admin actions (post/page creation, plugin install) within 5 min of first-ever login from IP.

suggestion.title: Mass Ghost CMS Version Scanning & Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attack on 700+ sites suggests attacker performed reconnaissance to identify vulnerable Ghost instances. No detection use case covers pre-exploitation scanning activity that would precede mass exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning patterns: same source IP querying /ghost/api/, /.well-known/ghost-version, or /package.json across 10+ distinct Ghost CMS domains within 1-hour window (fingerprinting behavior). Flag User-Agent strings consistent with vulnerability scanners (masscan, nuclei, Shodan API queries) targeting Ghost CMS paths.

suggestion.title: ClickFix C2 Callback Detection from Compromised Web Servers
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked sites for 'ClickFix Attacks' implies exfiltration of data or callbacks to attacker infrastructure. No detection use case for C2 communication from web servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server egress for DNS queries or connections to ClickFix-attributed domains (updatereq.click, variants) or to ASNs hosting known ClickFix infrastructure. Flag HTTPS POST requests from web server processes to non-standard ports (8080, 443, 8443) going to IPs with low reputation. Correlate with file modification events on the same host within last 24h.

suggestion.title: Detect newly registered domains hosted on shared CDN IP ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'hackers abuse shared CDN infrastructure to bypass domain reputation'—the core attack vector is routing low-reputation/newly created domains through legitimate CDN providers (Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Akamai) to inherit their reputation scores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS resolutions where domain registration age is <7 days (WHOIS lookup) and A/AAAA records resolve to known shared CDN IP ranges. Cross-reference against domain reputation feeds—legitimate CDN IPs with newly registered domain names indicate abuse pattern.

suggestion.title: Detect domain-fronting via CDN HTTPS with mismatched SNI/Host headers
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: using legitimate CDN domains as a masking layer while delivering malicious payload. TLS SNI/Host header mismatch to CDN infrastructure indicates potential domain fronting to bypass reputation filters and WAF controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when HTTPS traffic exhibits SNI/Host header specifying known CDN domain (e.g., *.cloudflare.net, *.cloudfront.net) but destination IP falls outside that CDN's official IP range. Exclude legitimate CDN-fronting use cases via allowlist.

suggestion.title: Detect phishing URLs leveraging trusted CDN domains for reputation bypass
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'bypass domain reputation security controls.' Phishing/malware distribution URLs embed CDN domains in requests to evade URL filtering, spam filters, and email security gateways that whitelist high-reputation CDN infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag URL clicks and email attachments containing legitimate CDN domains (e.g., *.azureedge.net, *.akamaized.net) in the URL authority when request path/query contains phishing indicators: base64 encoding, URL shorteners, .exe download requests, or embedded credential-request parameters.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP/HTTPS command-and-control traffic over CDN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes infrastructure abuse to bypass security controls—attackers leverage CDN's legitimate SSL certificates and global IP reputation to host C2 endpoints that evade network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS connections to known CDN domains with anomalous HTTP patterns: non-standard User-Agents, unusual request frequency (beaconing intervals), POST-heavy traffic without preceding GET requests for static content, or traffic outside business hours from corporate network.

suggestion.title: High-Volume External Access to SonicWall Web Interface Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers actively scanning SonicWall firewall interfaces'—suggests repeated attempts to reach port 4343 or 443 on SonicWall appliances. Pipeline missed detection for multi-source or distributed scanning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained connection attempts from external IP ranges to known SonicWall management ports (443, 4343) within short time windows. Alert on distributed sources (>5) hitting same target port within 1 hour, or single source with >50 failed connection attempts to SonicWall-identified subnets.

suggestion.title: Scanning Reconnaissance Pattern—597K-Scale Session Surge
suggestion.rationale: Article quantifies threat as '597,000 sessions observed'—anomalous scanning volume that should trigger thresholding UCs. Pipeline failed to translate raw metric into detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate SonicWall interface connection attempts. Alert when session count to firewall management interfaces exceeds 95th percentile by 5x or more within 6-hour rolling window, particularly if sources span multiple ASNs.

suggestion.title: SonicWall-Specific Reconnaissance Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Title and context imply attackers fingerprinting SonicWall endpoints; article mentions 'interfaces' specifically. Pipeline should detect HTTP User-Agent strings, response patterns, or banner-grabbing behavior characteristic of SonicWall recon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests containing SonicWall-specific User-Agents (e.g. curl, wget, custom scanners), requests to /admin, /login, /.sslvpn paths without subsequent authentication, or responses containing SonicWall version banners sent to non-whitelisted sources.

suggestion.title: Execution of Fake SQL Developer Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake SQL Developer malware installer'—the delivery mechanism and execution trigger. Pipeline missed detection for suspicious execution originating from user download of trojanized installers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of .exe/.msi files from Downloads or Temp folders with SQL Server/Developer/MSSQL keywords in filename, launched shortly after browser activity to newly-registered domains. Flag parent-child process chains where installer spawns powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or rundll32.exe within seconds of launch.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Search Result Navigation to Malicious Installer Site
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector is 'SEO poisoning to deliver'—users finding and clicking malicious search results leading to fake download sites. Pipeline provided no initial-access detection for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for navigation from search engine result pages to newly-registered domains containing SQL Server/Developer product keywords or closely-misspelled variants. Correlate domain creation date (days/weeks old) with spike in requests. Flag if destination site hosts executable downloads.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from Fake Installer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage attack structure (SEO → installer → payload) implies post-execution callback. Article indicates malware delivery but pipeline reconstructed zero command-and-control phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections from processes spawned by the fake installer. Flag destinations to non-Windows/non-infrastructure ASNs, unusual ports, or domains registered within same timeframe as malicious installer site.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence Installed by Malware Payload
suggestion.rationale: Fake installer delivers multi-stage payload with persistence requirements; article implies sustained access but pipeline omitted persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run* and user Startup folder modifications within minutes of suspicious installer execution. Alert on entries pointing to unsigned binaries, recently-modified system paths, or LOLBin invocations.

suggestion.title: Malware File Staging in AppData or System Temp
suggestion.rationale: Fake installer payload must write malware files to disk before execution. Article describes delivery and execution but pipeline missed file-activity detection for this critical step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious file writes to AppData/Local/Temp, ProgramData, or %SYSTEMROOT%\\Temp with double extensions (.exe.scr, .msi.bat) or mismatched icons/metadata (claiming SQL Server but actually executable). Baseline against known SQL Server installer file lists.

suggestion.title: Malware Binary Signed with Spoofed or Stolen Certificate
suggestion.rationale: Attackers distributing 'fake SQL Developer installer' likely used stolen or fraudulent code-signing certificates to bypass SmartScreen/UAC. Pipeline failed to identify signature-spoofing indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables with code signatures appearing legitimate (Microsoft-like company names, valid timestamp) but created recently or signed by unfamiliar CAs. Compare file metadata against official SQL Server binaries from Microsoft; flag mismatches in ProductVersion, FileVersion, or embedded resources.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Module/Component Loading Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'modular espionage ecosystem'—no UC captures DLL injection or module-load patterns that distinguish modular malware. Core execution tactic is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious DLL loads into legitimate processes; flag LoadLibrary calls with unusual paths or obfuscated module names. Monitor for parent-child process chains indicating module-loader patterns.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Espionage malware requires persistent C2; no use case detects outbound C2 handshake or command beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP/S to non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 9090) with abnormal user-agents. Flag persistent connections to IP ranges or domains linked to prior Kazuar C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Registry Persistence Modification
suggestion.rationale: Modular malware uses registry for persistence and config; no UC detects registry-write patterns indicative of malware initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag REG_BINARY/REG_EXPAND_SZ writes to HKLM/HKCU Run keys by non-system processes. Correlate registry modifications with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Credential/Screen Capture Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Espionage toolkit core function is data theft; screen-capture and credential-access techniques (T1113, T1056.004) not mapped despite central to malware purpose.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned executables invoking screen-capture APIs (BitBlt, GetDC) or clipboard-access calls (GetClipboardData). Alert on LSASS access or SAM registry enumeration.

suggestion.title: Kazuar File System Discovery Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance of local system and file enumeration (T1005, T1007, T1083) is foundational espionage malware behavior; no detection use case present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential file-system traversals (Documents, Desktop, Downloads) by suspicious processes. Flag bulk enumeration API calls (EnumFiles, FindFirstFile) inconsistent with user behavior.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Data Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: End-stage exfiltration (T1041, T1020.001) is malware's objective; no UC detects abnormal data-volume transfers or ex-filtration encoding signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large outbound data transfers to known/suspected C2 with process reputation. Flag encoded/chunked streams characteristic of exfiltration wrappers; alert on sensitive-folder exports to untrusted destinations.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Artifact Upload to LMS Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes deployment of BLUEBEAM web shell via zero-day. No detection UC generated for the upload or file artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation/upload events in LMS web-accessible directories (.php, .asp, .aspx, .jsp extensions) occurring shortly after HTTP POST requests to unpatched KnowledgeDeliver endpoints. Cross-correlate with failed exploitation signatures (unusual POST bodies, parameter injection patterns).

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP POST/PUT to KnowledgeDeliver Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation requires malicious HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoint. Article mentions exploit but pipeline missed C2 initiation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/PUT requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS paths with anomalous payloads, particularly those containing encoded/binary data or shell metacharacters. Correlate with subsequent file creation in web root and process execution from web server parent.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Web Server (BLUEBEAM Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Web shell enables command execution. Article establishes BLUEBEAM as deployed shell, implying remote code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters spawned with w3wp.exe, httpd, or tomcat as parent process. Alert on execution with suspiciously short parent command line or network-originated arguments (indicating HTTP parameter passthrough).

suggestion.title: Known Malware Family - BLUEBEAM Web Shell Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names BLUEBEAM as the deployed malware artifact. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file hashes, content signatures, or behavioral patterns associated with BLUEBEAM family (web shell command syntax, typical response headers, callback patterns) against collected files and HTTP content from compromised LMS instances. Flag any match as confirmed persistence.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS Tunneling from Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Web shell typically uses HTTP for C2. Article describes BLUEBEAM as shell but pipeline missed command-and-control inference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by web server processes (w3wp.exe, httpd, etc.). Prioritize long-lived connections, high-frequency small packets, or POST requests to non-standard ports. Cross-reference with known C2 infrastructure if available.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Error Log Anomalies (Exploitation Attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation may leave forensic traces in application logs (stack traces, input validation failures). Article mentions CVE but pipeline missed log-based detection path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal KnowledgeDeliver LMS error/warning patterns. Alert on spike in HTTP 500/502 responses, PHP/Java stack trace leakage, or SQL errors tied to POST parameters characteristic of known payload patterns. Correlate with subsequent file creation.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only RAT Process Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'memory-only RAT' deployment. RemotePE loads entirely in memory to avoid disk forensics, requiring detection of process injection patterns (T1055). Missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, or SetWindowsHookEx calls preceded by unusual parent process relationships (e.g., svchost spawning Explorer or Office). Memory-only RATs typically reflectively load shellcode into system processes without touching disk.

suggestion.title: RemotePE C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: RAT deployment implies command-and-control traffic. Article mentions 'deploys' but pipeline captured no C2 signatures or network indicators despite this being core to RAT detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from injected processes to previously unknown destinations, especially encrypted channels on non-standard ports. Lazarus RATs typically use RC4 or custom encryption. Correlate with process injection events from same parent.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Lateral Movement in Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'financial and crypto firms,' implying intra-network movement post-compromise. Pipeline missed lateral movement phase entirely despite Lazarus's documented worm-like propagation in banking sector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual service creation, admin share access, or PSEXEC-style lateral movement originating from compromised financial workstations. Alert on execution of typical Lazarus staging payloads (PowerShell Empire, Mimikatz) within 2 hours of initial RAT callback.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credential Harvesting Post-RAT Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus RAT deployments against financial firms are historically followed by credential dumping (Mimikatz). Article context strongly implies follow-on credential access, but pipeline generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect in-memory execution of credential dumpers (lsass.exe access, Mimikatz signatures) spawned from memory-resident RAT or injected process context. Correlate with LSASS access denials in 4692 events.

suggestion.title: Indicative Removal by Memory-Only RAT
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only payloads inherently leave minimal forensic footprint—article emphasizes this property. Pipeline should have flagged anti-forensics as defense evasion phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious clearing of event logs (Security, System), deletion of MFT entries, or NTFS alternate data streams on financial systems during same window as process injection events. Memory-only RATs often stage anti-forensics scripts.

suggestion.title: Azure Domain C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Azure-Hosted C2 Domains' — core attacker infrastructure; pipeline must detect outbound HTTPS traffic to Azure-hosted domains with beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for recurring outbound connections from internal hosts to Azure CDN/App Service domains (*.azurewebsites.net, *.cloudapp.azure.com, *.azure.com) with regular interval timing (beaconing), POST requests, or SSL cert mismatches typical of C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: MiniUpdate RAT Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'MiniUpdate RAT' as the threat — pipeline should detect known process signatures, file artifacts, or behavioral indicators of this malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation matching MiniUpdate signatures (known filenames, parent-child chains, command-line patterns with C2 URLs or obfuscated payloads) or behavioral indicators (registry access, file write to temp directories, network calls post-execution).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Delivery of RAT Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'targeted campaigns' implying delivery phase; RATs typically arrive via script (PowerShell, VBScript, Batch).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious PowerShell/cscript/wscript execution with command-line flags (ExecutionPolicy Bypass, -nop, -enc, -c) followed by file download from HTTP/HTTPS sources or process spawning MiniUpdate-related executables.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence Linked to Azure C2
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns require persistence; article describes 'targeted campaigns' implying sustained compromise and access maintenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor RegistryEvent for modifications to Run/RunOnce keys (HKLM/HKCU) that reference newly-created executables or scheduled tasks correlated with MiniUpdate-related file artifacts or Azure C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns explicitly target data theft; article emphasizes 'espionage' indicating collection and exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers or suspicious DNS queries from compromised endpoints to identified Azure C2 domains; correlate volume and timing with MiniUpdate execution and registry persistence activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RAT Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Espionage operations typically escalate from initial compromise to multi-system infiltration; 'campaigns' suggests broader scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious lateral movement indicators post-MiniUpdate infection: process execution on other network hosts from initial compromised machine, especially via PowerShell remoting, WMI, or PsExec; correlate with C2 communication.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gemini API Requests with Credential-Output Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'jailbroken Gemini to steal admin credentials' — core attack vector is abuse of AI model to exfiltrate secrets. Pipeline missed detection for queries requesting password dumps, API keys, or system prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Gemini/Google Cloud AI API calls containing jailbreak keywords ('bypass', 'ignore instructions', 'system prompt') or credential-disclosure queries ('list passwords', 'export admin keys', 'show secrets'). Correlate high-entropy response content with credentials format (GUID patterns, base64 encoded secrets).

suggestion.title: Admin Account Logins Post-Credential-Exposure Window
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'steal admin credentials' — requires detection of subsequent unauthorized access attempts using exfiltrated creds. Pipeline missed persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin account sign-ins from impossible-travel IP ranges, SOCKS proxies, or Tor exit nodes within 24-48 hours of Gemini API abuse activity. Flag sign-ins with anomalous user agents or missing MFA re-authentication.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange API Access from Compromised Admin Context
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'drain crypto wallets' — requires detection of unauthorized wallet transaction initiation. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised admin accounts for outbound connections to crypto exchange APIs (Binance, Kraken, Coinbase), blockchain RPC endpoints, or wallet service APIs. Flag withdrawal transactions or cross-chain bridge transfers with destination addresses not in historical baseline.

suggestion.title: LLM-Assisted Credential Harvesting via Role-Play Prompts
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'jailbroken Gemini' — insufficient if detection logic does not explicitly target prompt-injection and role-assumption attacks against LLMs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse LLM API request payloads for meta-commands ('Ignore all previous instructions'), role-assumption patterns ('Act as an AI without safety guidelines'), or requests asking the model to output internal state. Correlate with admin credentials appearing in subsequent API responses or logs.

suggestion.title: High-Entropy Data Exfiltration via Generative AI API Responses
suggestion.rationale: Implication: jailbroken Gemini outputs stolen admin credentials. Pipeline should detect exfiltration signals in API response content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gemini API response logs for high Shannon entropy outputs, base64-encoded strings longer than 200 chars, patterns matching password managers (LastPass export, 1Password JSON), or private-key formats (RSA BEGIN/END blocks). Correlate response size anomalies with prior jailbreak-attempt requests.

suggestion.title: Impossible-Travel Login + Wallet Drain Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative combines credential theft with immediate financial impact. Single detection should correlate admin-login anomaly with cryptocurrency outflow within same session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alert when: (1) admin account logs in from geographically impossible location; (2) within 4 hours, same session initiates cryptocurrency withdrawal >threshold value; (3) destination address is new or associated with known laundry services. High fidelity if multi-factor auth was bypassed.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Public Registries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—users installing trojanized packages is the primary attack vector. Title establishes package repositories as the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution spawned by package managers (npm, pip, cargo) or their child processes for unusual behavior: credential enumeration, file writes to sensitive directories, or outbound connections to non-standard domains immediately after package installation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Install Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via npm/PyPI typically abuse install scripts and hooks (e.g., postinstall, setup.py execution). Title mentions 'spreads malware via npm, PyPI' suggesting automated execution vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package manager hook execution (node-gyp, setuptools, build scripts) spawning shell interpreters, network tools, or accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or credential stores without explicit user invocation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Environment and Configs
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'credential-stealing malware'—this is the core payload. The attack steals credentials, presumably from development environments where malware executes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by package managers reading .env files, .git/config, AWS credential files, SSH keys, or calling credential enumeration tools (env, env | grep, aws sts get-caller-identity, git config).

suggestion.title: C2 Exfiltration from Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware implies stolen data is sent to an attacker server. Article describes malware 'spreads via' registries; exfiltration to C2 is the completion of the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unusual outbound HTTPS/DNS from package-manager-spawned processes, particularly to newly registered domains or IPs with low reputation. Flag beaconing patterns and large data transfers initiated by child processes of npm/pip/cargo.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Package Signature Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'spreads credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, CratesIO'—this requires malicious code to be accepted by repository registries. Unsigned or signature-mismatched packages may evade basic validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track installations of packages with mismatched, expired, or missing signatures; correlate package metadata (upload time, author change, version jump) with known compromise patterns. Flag rapid version pushes by newly-created accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Spread via Dependency Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks spanning npm, PyPI, and Crates.io suggests potential for cross-language exploitation and dependency injection. Lateral spread occurs when developers pull malicious packages in other projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a single workstation installs packages from multiple public registries in short succession or when multiple developers in same org pull the same malicious package within a time window; correlate with credential exfiltration indicators.

suggestion.title: Mass Account Creation from Synthetic Identities
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'verified bank and fintech mule accounts' are sold—implying bulk account provisioning with compromised or forged identities. Pipeline failed to generate detection for account creation velocity anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid account creation (10+/hour) from single IP, device fingerprint, or email domain. Flag accounts completing KYC with reused identity documents or synthetic identity markers (stock photos, mismatched metadata). Alert on accounts created with disposable email/phone that immediately proceed to credential validation or fund transfers.

suggestion.title: Telegram Client as Persistent C2 on Financial Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Telegram as operational hub ('Use Telegram Channels to Sell'). Pipeline did not identify Telegram process/network activity as command-and-control infrastructure or persistence mechanism on endpoints with fintech access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Telegram client (telegram.exe, Telegram.app, tdata folder) spawning or maintaining persistent connections on endpoints with fintech VPN/session access. Correlate Telegram login timing with account creation or credential provisioning events. Flag Telegram groups/channels with underground-marketplace keywords in metadata.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Credential Validation and Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Selling 'verified' accounts requires either stolen working credentials or post-compromise session hijacking (defeating MFA). Article does not describe the initial compromise vector, but pipeline should detect both credential validation and MFA bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA bypass attempts or circumvention (OTP reuse, session token replay, SIM swap). Monitor for bulk credential validation (login attempts + account data pulls) from datacenter/residential IPs targeting fintech platforms. Flag accounts showing takeover patterns: failed MFA → credential reset request → successful login from new device/location.

suggestion.title: Mule Account Transaction Velocity and Destination Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates accounts are sold as 'mule accounts'—money laundering vehicles. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection: rapid transfers, geographic mismatches, and beneficiary chain anomalies post-account-creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on verified accounts (KYC-complete, low transaction history) showing immediate high-velocity transfers (>5 txns/day) to multiple beneficiaries or crypto exchanges. Detect login geography mismatch: account created in US, logins from Eastern Europe within 48 hours, transfers to Russian/Chinese banks. Flag account lifecycle anomaly: creation → validation login → 0-4 hour dormancy → high-value transfer.

suggestion.title: Underground Recruitment via Telegram Link Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Telegram as recruitment channel for money-mule enrollment. Pipeline did not flag initial recruitment phase: phishing, social engineering, or malicious Telegram invites targeting job-seekers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks on Telegram invite links from work-from-home recruitment emails or shortened URLs. Monitor for Telegram group/channel joins with recruitment-theme messaging (money mule, verified account, fast cash, Western Union). Alert on patterns: user receives recruitment email → clicks Telegram link → joins group → follows with fintech account signup from same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Coordinated Account Verification Workflow Abuse
suggestion.rationale: The term 'verified accounts' suggests abuse of KYC/identity verification systems—either bulk verification via synthetic identities or workflow bypass. Pipeline failed to detect verification anomalies as an initial-access foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk identity verification completions using visually similar or duplicate documents (same ID scan, same selfie). Flag verification workflow anomalies: accelerated approval, manual review bypasses, or identity data matching known fraud repositories (synthesis services, stolen ID data). Alert on verification data tied to known Underground forum users or Telegram merchant accounts.

suggestion.title: Device Code Portal Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers to access their accounts.' Direct initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails from external senders containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or variations. Correlate with successful device code authentication flows occurring within minutes of email delivery. Flag emails with OAuth consent pretext, identity verification urgency language, or repeated distribution patterns.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Post-OAuth Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Persistence mechanism indicating post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device registration (Intune enrollment, device trust setup) occurring within minutes of OAuth token issuance via device code flow. Flag registrations from source IPs absent from user's 90-day login history. Monitor for bulk device registration from single attacker IP across multiple user accounts.

suggestion.title: OAuth Device Code Flow Token Theft and Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack: 'OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization grant flow...Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Token capture and immediate usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalies in device code flow completion: code entered by user from different IP/device than attacker-initiated flow. Alert when OAuth access token issued via device code flow is immediately used for API calls from distinct geographies. Flag device code flows on non-device-class OAuth clients (web apps, service principals, traditional auth clients).

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rules for Activity Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'they created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Defense evasion post-compromise to avoid audit trail detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation (Add-InboxRule, Set-InboxRule) with forwarding to external addresses, rule deletion of incoming messages, or suppression of delivery notifications shortly after OAuth compromise indicators. Correlate rule-creation user accounts with device code MFA completion or suspicious token usage events. Flag cascading rules designed to prevent message visibility.

suggestion.title: Session Hijacking via Adversary-in-the-Middle Proxy (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second attack mode: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' MFA bypass via session interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing pages or redirect chains pointing to attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure. Look for successful user authentication followed by OAuth token issuance, then token/session usage from geographically remote IP. Monitor for unusual authentication telemetry: MFA challenges originating on non-Microsoft IPs, session cookies captured in proxy logs, abnormal OAuth scope requests (offline access, mail.modify).

suggestion.title: Bulk Mailbox Access and Data Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates successful compromise grants 'full access to their account' and 'which are then used to steal data' from M365 and connected SaaS platforms. Post-compromise collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk mailbox reads, message exports, or forwarding of message batches shortly after OAuth token compromise indicators. Flag large Search-Mailbox operations, EWS API calls with GetFolder/GetItem enumerating sensitive folders, or external email forwarding rules. Correlate suspicious mailbox activity with OAuth consent to high-risk scope applications (Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Sites.ReadWrite).

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 as the attack vector ('Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites'). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or detection logic for exploitation attempts against this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS endpoints for HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-26980 exploit payloads. Look for unusual POST requests to admin/API endpoints, requests with malformed JSON bodies, or attempts to bypass authentication. Correlate with Ghost version identification probes (User-Agent, version endpoint queries) immediately preceding exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Account Creation on Ghost CMS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hijacking' 700+ sites, implying persistent access post-exploitation. Likely achieved via admin account creation or credential manipulation ('to Hijack').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new administrative user creation events in Ghost CMS that occur outside normal change windows, lack supporting documentation/tickets, or are created by system accounts rather than authenticated admins. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or exploitation signatures preceding account creation by <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection in Ghost Content/Templates
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix attacks rely on injected fake-support JavaScript overlays and popups; article describes sites being hijacked for ClickFix attacks, indicating payload injection post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to Ghost template files, handlebars theme files, or inline script injection in published posts that include: (1) addEventListener/onclick handlers for fake popup triggers, (2) requests to known ClickFix C2 domains (support-urgent.*, helpdesk-alert.*, etc.), (3) obfuscated or base64-encoded JavaScript within otherwise text-only content, (4) script tags inserted into pages that don't normally contain them.

suggestion.title: Mass Ghost CMS Instance Compromise Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 700+ sites hijacked indicates coordinated, multi-target campaign. Pattern-based detection on multiple Ghost instances exhibiting identical compromise signatures within short timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate across Ghost-hosted domains: (1) identical malicious DNS CNAME changes (e.g., all pointing to attacker infrastructure), (2) SSL certificate reissue/modification by non-legitimate CAs within hours, (3) HTTP response body delta analysis showing identical injected JavaScript across multiple independent domains, (4) WHOIS/registrar API changes on multiple domains to the same rogue contact within 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: ClickFix C2 Domain Registration and Activation
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix attacks require attacker-controlled domains for fake-support popups and credential harvesting. New domain registrations correlated with campaign launch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag newly registered domains (created <7 days before mass hijack campaign start date) matching ClickFix naming patterns (urgent-support, admin-alert, verify-account, security-check, fast-fix, etc.). Cross-reference with registrant details used for other malware/scam campaigns. Correlate SSL cert issuance dates on these domains with campaign timeline.

suggestion.title: Email Phishing Link via Legitimate CDN Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hackers abuse shared CDN infrastructure' to 'bypass domain reputation controls'—directly implying phishing delivery using trusted CDN domains that pass email gateways. No detection use case generated despite this being the clear initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails containing URLs from major CDN domains (Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS CloudFront, etc.) that resolve to attacker infrastructure or are detonated in sandboxes. Correlate trusted CDN domains in email subject/body with rare or newly-registered backend hosts.

suggestion.title: Legitimate CDN Domain with Suspicious Behavior Divergence
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism is masquerading malicious traffic as legitimate CDN domain—yet no detection for reputation mismatches (legitimate domain, malicious TLS certificate, C2 beacon patterns, or unusual outbound ports).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when traffic to known-legitimate CDN FQDN exhibits anomalies: mismatched TLS cert issuer/subject, non-standard HTTP headers, unusual outbound ports (not 80/443), or beaconing intervals. Compare network profile for the CDN domain against baseline for that org.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Shared CDN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies hackers use CDN infrastructure for command-and-control or data staging; no detection use case for identifying exfiltration-sized data transfers disguised as legitimate CDN traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusually large outbound data volumes to CDN endpoints from individual hosts, particularly outside normal business patterns. Flag rapid succession of requests to obscure CDN paths (e.g., /uuid/random/chunks) that mirror exfiltration staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Shared Infrastructure Abuse for C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Using 'shared CDN infrastructure' as C2 is implied in bypass-controls narrative; no detection for C2 beaconing over legitimate CDN domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify beaconing patterns (fixed intervals, fixed payload sizes) to CDN FQDNs. Cross-reference CDN destination IPs against threat feeds; alert on CDN domains resolving to IPs not in official CDN provider IP ranges, or resolving to reseller/proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Shared CDN Domain Bypassing Reputation Controls in Email Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Direct attack goal stated: 'bypass domain reputation security controls.' No detection for emails passing reputation checks because sender domain or embedded link resolves to whitelisted CDN provider.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with embedded CDN links (identified via DNS resolution) where the downstream or redirected destination has no explicit whitelist approval. Log reputation bypass events where CDN domain passed filters but later telemetry shows malicious downstream content.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Management Interface Brute-Force Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Actively Scanning SonicWall Firewall Interfaces'—explicit evidence of automated probing against firewall admin endpoints. Pipeline generated zero detection rules despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume HTTP GET/POST requests to known SonicWall management paths (/nsm/, /gvc/, /cgi-bin/welcome) on ports 443/8443 from suspicious sources. Alert on >50 distinct URIs probed from single source within 5-minute window, or >10 failed 401/403 responses from same client IP.

suggestion.title: Mass Firewall Reconnaissance: Session-Count Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article reports '597,000 Sessions Observed'—a clear statistical anomaly indicating at-scale, systematic discovery. No kill-chain phases reconstructed despite this being structured reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline SonicWall firewall connection session counts by source IP. Alert when single source initiates >1000 sessions in 24-hour window to firewall management interfaces or triggers >5 connection resets/timeouts. Correlate with known scanner signatures (User-Agent patterns, TLS fingerprints from Censys/Shodan scanners).

suggestion.title: SonicWall SSL VPN Credential Enumeration Probes
suggestion.rationale: Scanning 'firewall interfaces' targeting VPN/NetExtender endpoints is a precursor to credential attacks. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for this secondary phase despite article emphasizing breadth of scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to SonicWall NSM/GVC login endpoints (/cgi-bin/index.cgi, /gvc/login.html) followed by repeated failed login attempts from same IP within 30 seconds. Combine with absence of valid session cookies or X-Forwarded-For header manipulation to flag automated brute-force tools.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Firmware/Version Fingerprinting via Banner Grab
suggestion.rationale: Active scanning includes service enumeration to identify versions. Pipeline did not suggest detection for information disclosure via banner responses, HTTP headers, or SSL certificates that leak SonicWall product version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to SonicWall diagnostic/info endpoints (e.g., /cgi-bin/sysinfo, /software-version) or unusual HTTP HEAD requests to firewall IPs from non-managed sources. Alert on TLS ClientHello patterns matching known automated reconnaissance tools (Censys, Shodan scrapers).

suggestion.title: SSH-like Process Name Executed Outside SSH Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hide Linux Payload Under SSH-Like Filename'—attackers masquerade executables as SSH components (sshd, ssh-agent, ssh_key, etc.). Pipeline missed obvious detection: processes matching SSH naming patterns (regex: ^ssh|sshd|ssh-|_ssh_) spawning from non-canonical paths (not /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, ~/.ssh).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution where ProcessName or CommandLine contains SSH-like patterns (sshd, ssh-agent, ssh-keygen variants) but parent or working directory is outside /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /bin, /etc/ssh, ~/.ssh. Correlate with unusual parent processes (apt, dpkg, pip, rpm) indicating package-installation context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation with SSH-Like Name in Package Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload delivery during 'package installation'—files with SSH-like names should not appear in /tmp, /var/tmp, or staging directories during apt/dpkg/pip/rpm execution. Pipeline missed file monitoring baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of files matching SSH naming patterns in package-manager working directories, /tmp variants, or package-cache paths during active package installation. Validate against known SSH binaries: unknown SHA256 + SSH-like basename = high-fidelity indicator.

suggestion.title: Child Process with SSH-Like Name Spawned from Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article implies payload is delivered and executed during installation (apt/dpkg/pip/rpm initiates attacker code). Pipeline failed to identify parent-child relationship detection covering 'installation → execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes with SSH-like names (sshd, ssh_key, ssh-payload, etc.) spawned by package managers (apt-get, dpkg, pip, rpm, yum). Cross-reference against /etc/ssh and official SSH package hashes to confirm not legitimate installation/update.

suggestion.title: Network Connections from SSH-Named Processes with Untrusted Origin
suggestion.rationale: Hidden payload under SSH-like filename will likely exfiltrate or beacon. Pipeline did not generate network-behavior detections for disguised processes. Article phrase 'Hide Linux Payload' implies command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated by processes bearing SSH-like names but which originate from unusual executables (not /usr/sbin/sshd, /usr/bin/ssh). Correlate source executable hash against official openssh-package digests; deviation = suspicious.

suggestion.title: SSH-Named Binary Not Signed by OpenSSH or Distro Repository
suggestion.rationale: Obfuscation via filename only; signature verification will expose fraudulent binary. Article's core attack is name-squatting, implying code is not authentic. Pipeline missed integrity-baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Validate Authenticode/GPG signatures on any binary matching SSH naming patterns. If /usr/bin/sshd or equivalent is unsigned, unsigned-by-canonical-distro, or hash-mismatched against distro package manifest: escalate. Baseline SSH binary hashes per distro.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Search Result Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'SEO Poisoning' as the delivery vector. No UC generated despite this being the initial access technique. Article phrase: 'Iranian APT Uses SEO Poisoning to Deliver'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on search results followed by suspicious binary downloads or installer executions from domains not associated with SQL Server official distribution. Track HTTP referrers from search engines (Google, Bing) leading to executable downloads. Alert on SQL-themed domains (sql-developer.*, mssql-installer.*) hosting PE files with unsigned or invalid code signatures.

suggestion.title: Fake SQL Developer Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer'—a masquerading technique. No UC generated. Pipeline should have flagged process execution from non-Microsoft-signed installers claiming to be SQL Server software.
