suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawns from EXEs with SQL-like names (SQLInstaller.exe, SQLDeveloper.exe, etc.) lacking Microsoft code signatures, especially when launched from user-controlled directories (Downloads, Temp). Flag parent processes that match known download tools (explorer.exe, chrome.exe, edge.exe) spawning these installers. Cross-reference file hash against legitimate SQL Server MSI hashes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Installer Spawning System Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Fake installer typically achieves execution by spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or WMI commands. Article title establishes malware payload but no detection for post-execution reconnaissance or persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/fake-installer processes (parent) creating children such as cmd.exe, powershell.exe, msiexec.exe, or wmic.exe. Flag command lines containing suspicious payloads, network callbacks, or persistence mechanisms (registry writes, scheduled tasks, service installations). Correlate process creation timing—immediate child process spawn after installer execution suggests malicious packaging.

suggestion.title: SQL Developer Installer Download from Non-Official Source
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have flagged downloads of installer files mimicking legitimate SQL software from attacker-controlled or non-Microsoft domains. No IOC extraction means no download-source validation rules were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP(S) downloads of .exe, .msi, or .zip files with SQL-themed names from domains not in allow-list of official Microsoft/SQL Server distribution channels. Validate against known-good SHA256 hashes of legitimate SQL Server installers. Alert on downloads from newly-registered or bullet-proof-hosting domains. Track user-agent strings matching automated downloaders or unusual geographic origins for installer distribution.

suggestion.title: Iranian APT Malware C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title attributes attack to Iranian APT but no kill-chain phase or technique mapped for command-and-control. Once installer executes, malware must beacon home—no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from host running unsigned SQL installer to non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 9090) or to Iranian IP ranges and bullet-proof-hosting ASNs. Track DNS queries for domains matching common Iranian APT C2 patterns. Flag encrypted traffic (HTTPS, QUIC) with unusual certificate subjects or self-signed certs originating from installer execution context.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Module Loading via Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'modular espionage ecosystem'—requires injection or DLL loading patterns. Kazuar historically uses process hollowing and VirtualAllocEx/CreateRemoteThread chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned DLL loads into system processes (svchost.exe, lsass.exe). Detect CreateRemoteThread or VirtualAllocEx call sequences in parent-child process pairs. Flag suspicious RPC activity associated with module initialization.

suggestion.title: Kazuar C2 Beaconing and Command Dispatch
suggestion.rationale: Modular ecosystem requires C&C infrastructure for command orchestration and data staging—core RAT behavior implied by 'espionage operations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify periodic HTTP/HTTPS callbacks to suspicious domains with structured POST bodies (encrypted payloads). Look for non-standard ports or protocol tunneling over SOCKS/HTTP proxies. Flag User-Agent strings with hardcoded or suspicious patterns.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Surveillance and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'espionage ecosystem'—implies screen capture, keylogging, audio capture modules typical of modular spyware. Article emphasizes surveillance capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gdiplus.dll or DirectX API calls from unusual parents (rundll32, dwm.exe). Detect memory-mapped file creation in %TEMP% with image/audio MIME headers. Flag encoded/compressed data streams exfiltrating over C2 channels.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing Attachment with Macro/Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Secret Blizzard Operations'—indicates targeted campaigns. Kazuar historically delivered via malicious Office documents triggering multi-stage payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office macro execution post-email delivery (WinWord/Excel spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe). Flag .doc/.xls files in user Downloads with recent timestamps and unusual 'modified' vs. 'created' times.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Obfuscation and Living-off-the-Land Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated modular framework and attribution to state operations imply evasion (obfuscated payloads, LOLBIN usage). Article context suggests targeted espionage requiring stealth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rundll32.exe/regsvcs.exe with unusual export-name arguments or malformed DLL paths. Monitor for WMI event consumers and registry Run keys added by unsigned processes. Flag suspicious \\.\Pipe\ named pipe creation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via LSASS Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Espionage toolkit requires credential theft for lateral movement and persistence. Article's 'ecosystem' scope implies multi-stage credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LSASS process access from unsigned processes (access mask 0x1410 or higher). Detect SetWindowsHookEx calls targeting WH_KEYBOARD_LL or WH_MOUSE_LL. Flag API hooking via SetWindowsHookEx or detours libraries.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'RemotePE memory-only RAT' is primary payload. Pipeline produced zero execution-phase detections. Memory-only execution requires VirtualAlloc→WriteProcessMemory→CreateRemoteThread chain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process injection sequence: parent process calls VirtualAlloc, followed by non-child process calling WriteProcessMemory, culminating in CreateRemoteThread to legitimate target (svchost, explorer). Flag absence of resultant .exe/.dll writes to disk for spawned threads.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beaconing from Financial Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting 'Financial and Crypto Firms' via RemotePE RAT; no C2 detection use case produced. RAT command-and-control is core to campaign success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound encrypted connections from financial sector hosts with non-standard TLS ClientHello or HTTP headers. Detect periodic callback patterns (beaconing) to known or suspected Lazarus infrastructure. Flag DNS queries for newly registered or suspicious domains from infected workstations.

suggestion.title: Memory Resident Credential Harvesting in Crypto Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Crypto Firms'—implied objective is credential/wallet theft. RemotePE RATs typically perform keystroke logging or clipboard hijacking. Pipeline missed credential access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injection of keylogger or clipboard hook code into legitimate processes. Monitor for HTTPS MITM patterns via memory-resident proxy (detect process intercepting outbound HTTPS without legitimate proxy configuration). Alert on unusual logon activity to crypto exchange APIs or OTP generator apps post-infection.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Memory-Only Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'memory-only' designation. Pipeline ignored this evasion technique entirely. Should generate detections for absence of expected file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes with elevated private memory but zero corresponding .exe/.dll files in expected locations (AppData, Temp, System32). Detect VirtualAlloc allocations larger than 1MB without subsequent process creation. Flag legitimate system processes (svchost, dllhost) exhibiting unusual heap growth.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Initial Access via Phishing/Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active deployment campaign ('Lazarus deploys'); pipeline produced zero initial-access detections. No use cases for email delivery, watering hole, or exploit kit vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office documents or HTA files with embedded PowerShell commands capable of memory-only shellcode execution. Detect OneNote/LNK shortcut files delivering encoded executables. Flag suspicious email attachments to financial/crypto sector from attacker-controlled or spoofed domains.

suggestion.title: Azure Domain Resolution Followed by Suspicious Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Azure-Hosted C2 Domains'—must detect resolution of Azure infrastructure (*.azurewebsites.net, *.cloudapp.net) correlated with RAT process spawning or unknown child processes with network callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries for Azure-hosted domains followed within 60 seconds by execution of unknown processes with outbound connectivity. Flag beaconing patterns (regular 5-60min intervals) or connections to Azure IPs with minimal geolocation history.

suggestion.title: MiniUpdate RAT Process Execution and Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'MiniUpdate RAT' as a named malware family. Pipeline should detect process names, injection patterns, or code signatures matching known MiniUpdate variants or loader behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of processes matching MiniUpdate naming patterns, injection into svchost.exe/explorer.exe, or DLL loading from temp directories. Flag unsigned binaries or spoofed Microsoft signatures.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Newly Registered Azure Cloud Tenants
suggestion.rationale: Targeted espionage campaigns leverage newly provisioned cloud infrastructure to evade reputation filters. 'Campaigns' context implies infrastructure created shortly before attack execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS to Azure domains registered <30 days prior to first connection, showing periodic callback intervals (300-3600s), small request bodies, or associated with anomalous DNS registration patterns.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution for RAT Command Dispatch and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware universally leverages PowerShell for execution and persistence. 'Targeted espionage campaigns' implies command execution post-compromise; detection must include encoded scripts and Invoke-WebRequest patterns to C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell spawned by non-standard parents, executing Base64-encoded payloads, or making outbound connections within script blocks. Correlate with suspicious parent processes or C2-communicating processes.

suggestion.title: Registry and Scheduled Task Persistence for RAT Survival
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns require long-term persistence. RATs establish Run registry keys or scheduled tasks post-compromise. Pipeline should surface persistence mechanisms even without explicit article enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM/HKCU Run keys and scheduled task creation for new entries following suspicious process execution. Flag tasks scheduled to non-standard binaries, created by non-admin processes, or referencing Azure domain callbacks.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Discovery and Reconnaissance Commands
suggestion.rationale: Targeted espionage implies discovery phase post-initial access. Article's 'campaigns' context suggests multi-stage attacks; detection should include systeminfo, net group, quser, and registry enumeration spawned by or parent to C2 processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of recon commands (systeminfo, ipconfig, net localgroup, tasklist, wmic) spawned by C2-communicating processes in rapid sequence, especially from service contexts or scheduled task execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from npm/PyPI/Crates.io
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'spreads credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — no detection UC for anomalous package downloads or installation patterns from these registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install, pip install, or cargo add commands executing outside normal change-control windows, targeting packages with suspicious names (typosquatting variants, new names), or pulling from registries with failed integrity checks. Monitor for package installation by automation accounts with unusual destination paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Package Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Malware described as 'credential-stealing' but no detection UC for exfiltration of credentials, environment variables, or tokens during package setup phases.
log_sources: Process creation logs (node, python, cargo invocations)
Network egress (HTTPS POST to attacker C2)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by package managers that read environment variables, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, .env files, or system credential stores, followed by HTTP(S) POST requests to external IPs/domains not in whitelist. Flag if subprocess runs with redirected stdout/stderr to temporary files.

suggestion.title: Registry Manipulation or Suspicious Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack requires upload/compromise of package registry accounts; pipeline missed detection for new package versions, ownership changes, or metadata anomalies.
log_sources: Package registry audit logs (npm audit, PyPI history)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/PyPI/Crates.io for rapid version bumps, packages released by new/suspicious authors, changes to package dependencies, or injection of build system files (setup.py, package.json scripts) without corresponding code commits in source repo.

suggestion.title: Malicious Import/Require with Immediate Network Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies credential-stealing malware; no UC for detecting code execution at import time (module initialization) followed by exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation (npm, pip, cargo) with immediate child process creation and outbound network connections within <30s of import/require statements. Flag if destination IPs/domains are newly registered (<30 days), non-RFC1918, or associated with attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Repository Typosquatting or Name Collision Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use names similar to popular packages; no UC for detecting development dependency on suspicious near-match package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installs of packages whose names are edit-distance ≤2 from popular libraries (e.g., 'reacts' vs 'react', 'reqeusts' vs 'requests'), newly created accounts publishing such packages, or packages with <10 downloads targeting org codebases.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled Domain
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware requires C2 callback to exfiltrate tokens/secrets; no UC for detecting HTTP POST of environment data to unknown endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP(S) POST/PUT from package-manager child processes containing base64-encoded or plaintext AWS_*, API_KEY, TOKEN, PASSWORD patterns in request body to domains outside corporate CDN/update servers.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll'—primary attack artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to System32\termsrv.dll with unusual source processes or outside Windows update contexts. Alert on file-modification timestamps correlating with subsequent RDP service activity or session-limit changes. Flag termsrv.dll loaded from non-system directories.

suggestion.title: Multiple Concurrent RDP Sessions from Single User
suggestion.rationale: Article objective: 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts'—behavioral signature of successful persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline RDP session counts per user. Alert when single user maintains 3+ concurrent RDP sessions (exceeding Windows default limits). Correlate abnormal session counts with termsrv.dll file modification events.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Invalid-Signature termsrv.dll Execution
suggestion.rationale: DLL modification breaks Microsoft signature validation, creating detectable execution anomalies when svchost loads it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect svchost.exe loading termsrv.dll with missing, invalid, or revoked Microsoft signatures. Monitor for signature timestamp mismatches or hash deviations from known-good System32 baselines. Flag DLL loads from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Terminal Server Registry Session-Limit Modification
suggestion.rationale: Multiple RDP sessions require registry modification to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server session policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to Terminal Server session-limit keys (MaxInstanceCount, MaxIdleTime, MaxDisconnectionTime). Alert on modifications by non-service accounts or unusual process lineage. Correlate with termsrv.dll changes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Preceding System DLL Modification
suggestion.rationale: Modifying System32\termsrv.dll requires SYSTEM privileges; privilege-escalation events should temporally precede file writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate privilege-escalation events (UAC bypass, token elevation) with subsequent System32\termsrv.dll file modifications within 120-second window. Flag unexpected elevation-to-filewrite chains involving system directories.

suggestion.title: TermService (svchost) Restart Correlating with DLL Changes
suggestion.rationale: Modified DLL requires service restart to take effect; svchost restarts should cluster with termsrv.dll writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TermService process restarts immediately following System32\termsrv.dll modifications (within 30 seconds). Monitor for termservice control commands (net stop/start, sc.exe) from non-admin accounts or scripts. Flag restarts outside Windows update contexts.

suggestion.title: Telegram Channel Access from Financial Institution Network
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes Telegram as active C2 and marketplace infrastructure for distributing mule accounts. No detection use case generated for network or endpoint access to Telegram channels from banking/fintech environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound connections to Telegram API endpoints and channel URLs from IP ranges assigned to banking/fintech organizations. Establish baseline of legitimate Telegram usage and alert on new users, high-frequency access, or bulk account management patterns typical of mule-account orchestration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Financial Account Verification and KYC Bypass Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'verified' mule accounts, indicating KYC/identity verification steps were subverted or falsified. Pipeline failed to generate detections for anomalous account verification workflows or identity document manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts that complete full KYC verification workflows in atypical timeframes (e.g., <5 minutes for full identity verification). Monitor for bulk identity document submissions, mismatched identity attributes, or reused identity data across multiple account creations in short windows.

suggestion.title: Rapid Mule Account Onboarding and Transfer Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes systematic distribution of pre-verified mule accounts for immediate use in financial fraud. Pipeline missed detection for burst account creation followed by immediate high-value or high-frequency transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build risk model correlating new account creation (age <7 days) with transfer initiation patterns: velocity (>5 transactions/hour), geography (transfers to high-risk jurisdictions), and account typology (newly created receiving mule accounts). Triage on transfer amounts >10x median for account age cohort.

suggestion.title: Telegram API and Bot Activity from Employee Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors likely recruit or corrupt bank employees to provision mule accounts. Pipeline failed to flag Telegram API calls or bot interactions from internal corporate systems or employee endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution on employee workstations for Telegram CLI/API interactions, Telegram bot SDKs, or scripted Telegram channel subscriptions. Cross-reference process execution anomalies with user role (finance, compliance, operations) and timeline correlation to account creation surges.

suggestion.title: Identity Document Theft or Fabrication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Verified mule accounts require identity documents. Article implies systematic credential/identity reuse or theft to bypass KYC. Pipeline missed detections for document exfiltration or fabrication signal indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk export of identity documents (driver's licenses, passports, government IDs) from internal file shares or DLP systems. Correlate with account creation events. Flag identity documents with non-standard metadata, duplicate biometric hashes, or mismatched attributes across multiple accounts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Asset Account Linking Between Fintech Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Mule account operations likely involve coordinated account linkage across multiple fintech platforms (PayPal, Wise, crypto exchanges, neobanks) for fund movement obfuscation. Pipeline generated no detection for suspicious linking patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new fintech account linking chains where >3 external platform connections initiate within 24-hour windows. Flag patterns where linked accounts exhibit zero legitimate transaction history prior to linking and immediate fund-transfer execution post-link.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails redirecting to device code login portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal.' Core initial-access vector for account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or similar device code authentication portals. Alert on mass campaigns with device code URLs in email bodies, subject lines, or OAuth-redirect patterns in link chains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious inbox rule creation by newly compromised accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Inbox rules are a persistence and cover-tracks mechanism post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbox rules created by accounts showing anomalous OAuth token activity or device registration within 24 hours. Alert on rules forwarding to external domains, suppressing delivery notifications, or moving messages to hidden folders.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized device registration in Microsoft Entra following OAuth token grant
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access.' Device persistence multiplies the impact of a single compromised token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate OAuth token issuance via device code flow with subsequent Entra device registrations. Alert on device registration from unexpected geographies or times, especially when registered by accounts exhibiting bulk mailbox access patterns.

suggestion.title: OAuth access token issuance via device authorization flow with MFA bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Core TTP: abusing legitimate OAuth grant flow to bypass MFA on token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code grant completions (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code) immediately followed by token usage for high-impact actions (mailbox access, rule creation, device registration) from different IP/location than the original MFA-completed sign-in.

suggestion.title: Bulk mailbox access and collection by freshly compromised accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the resulting attacks gave the hackers access to their mailboxes, where they created malicious inbox rules.' Accounts compromised via device code become mail exfiltration vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor mailbox searches, exports, and message forwarding by accounts within hours of OAuth token issuance via device flow. Alert on access to multiple mailboxes in sequence by newly compromised accounts, particularly those with prior low activity baselines.

suggestion.title: Coerced or automated device code authorization without genuine user intent
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it' and recommends blocking device code flows entirely via Conditional Access. Indicates device code flows bypass standard MFA gating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device code authorization flows followed by rapid MFA completion from users in low-risk sign-in baselines or IoT-atypical devices. Alert on device code flows from IPs associated with phishing infrastructure or threat-intel flagged sources.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names a specific CVE in active exploitation (700+ sites). Pipeline did not generate any detection for exploitation of this public-facing CMS vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for HTTP POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Baseline normal Ghost admin paths; alert on unusual parameter values or payloads suggesting template injection or authentication bypass. Look for HTTP 200 followed by unexpected content changes.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Payload Injection into Compromised CMS
suggestion.rationale: Article title states compromised sites were hijacked for 'ClickFix Attacks'—this is the impact mechanism. Pipeline did not map injection of malicious JavaScript or redirect logic into web content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track modifications to Ghost post/page content or theme files for suspicious JavaScript execution contexts (setTimeout, XMLHttpRequest, fetch to external C2). Alert on theme edits by non-admin accounts or during off-hours. Monitor for injected <script> tags pointing to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CMS Admin Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: To hijack 700+ sites, attackers needed administrative access post-exploitation. Article implies mass compromise but pipeline captured no auth-related detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ghost CMS admin login from unusual IP ranges, impossible travel, or bulk creation of API tokens/sessions. Monitor for automated admin actions (content bulk edits, user creation, backup exfiltration) via programmatic authentication within hours of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Mass Web Shell or Persistent Backdoor Installation via CMS
suggestion.rationale: 700+ simultaneous compromises suggests automated post-exploitation persistence mechanism. Pipeline did not suggest detection for permanent backdoor implantation in web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost directories (themes, plugins, public uploads) for new executable files (.php, .js, .jsp) or suspicious includes in Ghost config. Alert on .htaccess/web.config modifications that enable directory execution. Baseline legitimate Ghost files; flag hash mismatches or unauthorized changes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Signature Detection in HTTP Request
suggestion.rationale: A critical CVE in active exploitation should have pattern-based detection. No specific exploit payload patterns extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create WAF/IDS signatures for documented CVE-2026-26980 exploit patterns. Correlate Ghost version fingerprinting (HTTP headers, robots.txt) with vulnerability timeline. Alert on version ≤ [patch version] if accessible via version disclosure.

suggestion.title: CDN Domain Reputation Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'bypass domain reputation security controls'—detection should trigger when reputation services conflict or CDN domain skips reputation checks entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CDN domains (Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS CloudFront, etc.) that fail to resolve in enterprise reputation/filtering databases or are whitelisted despite hosting known malicious content. Flag cases where hostname resolves to CDN CNAME but downstream URI path indicators are blocked.

suggestion.title: Legitimate CDN Provider URI Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article title describes abuse of 'shared CDN infrastructure'—detection targets suspicious path/query encoding hidden behind trusted CDN domains to evade gateway inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CDN (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai) requests with high-entropy or encoded query parameters, double-encoded paths, or null-byte injection in URI. Legitimate CDN traffic is typically legible; obfuscation suggests attacker-controlled payload routing.

suggestion.title: CDN IP + Anomalous Destination Port
suggestion.rationale: Shared CDN infrastructure attack implies attacker controls backend, directing to non-standard C2 infrastructure via reputation-clean CDN IP fronting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag connections to known CDN IP ranges (CIDR blocks for Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Akamai) followed by secondary outbound to non-standard C2 ports (8443, 9443, 4444, etc.) or SOCKS/proxy tunneling signatures. CDNs typically proxy to port 443/80; tunneling elsewhere signals abuse.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Whitelist Evasion via CDN Alias
suggestion.rationale: Core attack premise: 'bypass domain reputation'—detection should catch when attacker registers lookalike domain, points to CDN, relies on whitelist ignoring the registered domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains (registration age <30 days) that resolve to CDN CNAME records (especially shared/multi-tenant CDNs). Cross-reference against threat feeds and passive DNS. Legitimate sites rarely hide behind CDN + new domain pair without historical presence.

suggestion.title: Detect High-Volume Scanning Against SonicWall Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hackers actively scanning SonicWall firewall interfaces' with 597,000 sessions observed—clear network reconnaissance. Pipeline generated no UC for this core threat behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall logs and network telemetry for mass connection attempts to SonicWall management ports (typically 4444, 443) from unique source IPs within a short time window. Detect behavioral anomaly: elevated inbound SYN/connection-reset patterns to management interfaces from distributed sources, indicating reconnaissance sweep rather than legitimate admin access.

suggestion.title: Identify Failed Authentication Attempts on SonicWall Management Consoles
suggestion.rationale: Active scanning of firewall interfaces (phrase: 'scanning SonicWall firewall interfaces') typically precedes credential brute-force; pipeline missed credential-access phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to SonicWall management console (web/SSH) from sources that previously triggered network scanning alerts. Baseline typical failed-attempt rates per source; flag sources exceeding threshold within 24 hours of first scan detection, indicating progression from reconnaissance to credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: Detect Requests to Known SonicWall CVE PoC Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions active scanning but pipeline did not extract or reference specific CVE vulnerabilities being targeted. Without article body, no CVE IOCs provided; however, this is a critical gap—SonicWall has known public exploits (e.g., CVE-2021-20038, CVE-2018-9995). Pipeline should surface these based on product name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to SonicWall appliance targeting known vulnerable endpoints (/api/sonichub, /remote/index.html, /userportal, /ssl-vpn paths). Correlate with network scanning alerts. Flag requests using suspicious user-agents, automated tools, or payloads matching public SonicWall PoC repositories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH-Named File Creation During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hide Linux Payload Under SSH-Like Filename'—payload masquerading as SSH is the obfuscation vector. No detection rule addresses files with SSH-mimicking names (e.g., `.ssh`, `ssh_config`, `authorized_keys`) created outside standard SSH directories (typically /home/*/.ssh or /root/.ssh).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager execution (apt, yum, rpm) for child process file I/O operations that create files matching SSH-like patterns (.*ssh.* or auth.*keys) in unexpected locations (/tmp, /var, /opt, /etc). Baseline .ssh writes to home directories and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Package Installation Spawning Unexpected Processes or Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload activation 'during package installation'—normal package install chains are well-defined. Any package manager (or its children) spawning network clients, shell interpreters without user context, or persistence mechanisms during non-interactive install is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline benign child processes of package managers (dpkg, rpm, post-install hooks). Flag: (1) apt/yum/rpm spawning curl/wget/nc during install; (2) install hooks executing bash -c without user TTY; (3) systemd unit creation during package extraction.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded SSH Binary or Script in Non-Standard Locations
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses 'SSH-like filename'—implies either binary named ssh/sshd in unexpected paths, or shell script mimicking SSH initialization. Detection must cover both file creation and execution of SSH-lookalikes outside /usr/bin and /usr/sbin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of executables or shell scripts with names ssh*, sshd, authorized_keys, ssh_config in non-standard directories (/tmp, /var, /opt, package cache directories). Cross-reference with package manager execution to detect post-install persistence.

suggestion.title: Package Repository or Package Manifest Manipulation (Supply Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies attack occurs 'during package installation'—implies compromise upstream (repository, package metadata, or mirror). IOCs would include malicious package names, repo URLs, and hashes; pipeline extracted none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package manager requests with threat intel on known-compromised packages, repos, and CDN/mirror domains. Flag: repos not in official mirrors, packages with unusual maintainer fields, hash mismatches on metadata.

suggestion.title: Execution of SSH-Named Payload with Unexpected Arguments or Context
suggestion.rationale: Payload masquerades as SSH but runs malicious code. Need detection for SSH-like binaries called with unusual argument patterns, out-of-policy context, or no TTY (batch/script execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of ssh/sshd-named binaries outside standard directories. Flag: SSH binary called with -c, -i flags pointing to non-standard keys; SSH spawned by package manager or init system; SSH with no parent TTY and suspicious environment variables.

suggestion.title: Installation Hook or Post-Install Script Activity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Package install mechanisms (pre-inst, post-inst, maintainer scripts) are leveraged for payload execution. Article's 'during package installation' strongly implies abuse of package hook system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline benign package hook scripts (dpkg triggers, rpm %post). Alert on: hooks executing bash -c with unorthodox syntax, hooks creating persistence files, hooks spawning background processes, hooks with obfuscated base64/hex encoding.

suggestion.title: Python Compiled Extension Load from Anomalous Path
suggestion.rationale: Core evasion vector per article: '.pyd and .so files to evade script detection'. Pipeline missed detection for compiled extension loading via ImageLoad events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe/pythonw.exe for LoadImage events of .pyd files originating from temp directories, user-writable paths, or network shares. Baseline legitimate .pyd loads from Python installation and site-packages. Anomalies: AppData, Temp, UNC paths, or one-off module names.

suggestion.title: Staged Compiled Extension Write + Python Execution
suggestion.rationale: Evasion delivery pattern: 'ships as .pyd' implies write-to-disk staging prior to interpreter load. Pipeline generated no multi-event correlation UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate .pyd/.so file creation events in temp/user-writable paths with subsequent python.exe spawning and immediate child process creation. Sub-60-second delta post-write is high-confidence signal. Filter out pip, venv, conda parent processes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Compiled Binary Evasion Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses both Windows (.pyd) and Linux (.so) compiled vectors simultaneously: 'ships as .pyd and .so files'. Pipeline should flag deviation from script-based execution baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of script-file execution patterns (python.exe → .py/.pyw). Alert on python process execution with compiled extension loading but no corresponding .py in call chain. Cross-platform comparison: anomaly in both Windows and Linux within 24h suggests coordinated campaign.

suggestion.title: Direct Execution of .pyd/.so as Process Image
suggestion.rationale: Compiled extensions are normally loaded *by* interpreter, not executed directly. 'Ships as .pyd' for evasion suggests atypical execution model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where ImageName/CommandLine ends in .pyd or .so extension. These files should never be direct process images—they require interpreter. Any such event is suspicious and warrants full process tree review.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Python Payload via Compiled Module
suggestion.rationale: Core threat model: compiled format masks malicious code from detection. Article: 'evade script detection'—suggests payload inspection bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes loading .pyd modules followed by unusual child process creation, network connections, or registry modifications. Compiled modules cannot be easily reverse-engineered from image memory; monitor behavioral artifacts instead (children, network, file I/O).

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Infrastructure Delivering Fake Developer Installers
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Iranian APT Uses SEO Poisoning to Deliver Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer.' SEO poisoning is the primary attack vector; no detection rules were generated to identify this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to newly-registered or typosquatting domains containing 'SQL', 'Developer', 'installer', or 'setup' in the URL, visited via referrers from search engines (google.com, bing.com). Correlate with file downloads of .exe or .msi files.

suggestion.title: Execution of Unsigned Fake SQL Developer Installer
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer' delivery; no use case covers detection of masqueraded, unsigned executable execution or anomalous installer behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent is WinRAR, explorer.exe, or browser; target is sqlservr.exe, setup.exe, or SQL*installer*.exe; binary lacks Microsoft Authenticode signature or originates from Downloads/Temp folders. Flag child processes spawned by installer that deviate from legitimate SQL Server setup behavior.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SQL Developer Installer Post-Execution Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers must transition from masquerade to payload execution. No detection rule identifies post-install lateral movement, persistence, or credential access following a suspicious developer tool setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30 seconds of fake SQL installer execution, detect registry modifications (Run, RunOnce, startup folders), suspicious DLL injection into running processes, or spawning of cmd.exe/powershell.exe with unusual arguments. Fake installers often drop payloads to AppData or ProgramData rather than standard SQL install directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Prompt Injection from Fake SQL Installer
suggestion.rationale: Fake developer tool installers commonly inject fake credential prompts to harvest domain credentials. Article does not specify this behavior but is a standard secondary objective; pipeline generated no credential_access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect fake SQL installer process spawning dialogs with authentication prompts (via CreateWindow, CreateDialogBox). Correlate with failed logins to legitimate SQL services within 2 minutes. Flag if installer process attempts to read SAM registry hive or invoke mimikatz-like credential theft.

suggestion.title: File Reputation Mismatch: Malware Signed as SQL Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Fake SQL installer inherently has mismatched file metadata or missing legitimate signatures. Pipeline failed to suggest file-reputation or code-signing verification detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference downloaded .exe/.msi files against Windows Update Catalog and official Microsoft SQL Server download repository by name and hash. Flag downloads with names matching SQL products but lacking valid Microsoft Authenticode signature, or signed by unknown/suspicious publishers. Alert on hash mismatches or signature timestamp anomalies.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly establishes zero-day exploitation as the initial attack vector: 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploited'. Detection for exploitation of this LMS platform is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation patterns targeting KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints including unusual parameter injection in LMS admin/upload endpoints, file upload requests to LMS with executable payloads, and error responses consistent with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell File Creation and Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article states BLUEBEAM web shell was deployed; detection for web shell artifacts is critical. Web shells require file creation in web-accessible directories and typically are registered with the web service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation events in web root directories (wwwroot, htdocs, etc.) containing BLUEBEAM signatures or suspicious names; monitor for web server service file access patterns consistent with loading new handler modules or scripts; flag IIS/Apache configuration changes that register new handlers.

suggestion.title: Web Server Child Process Execution from LMS Context
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day to web shell chain implies LMS process spawning command interpreters; this execution pattern bridges initial access to command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LMS application process (w3wp.exe, apache, etc.) spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe with high confidence, especially in rapid succession after successful exploitation. Flag anomalous process execution originating from web application context outside normal deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LMS File Upload Without Extension Validation
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation implies ability to bypass upload controls to deliver web shell; file upload with insufficient validation is a common exploitation path for LMS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver LMS upload endpoints for POST requests with unexpected file extensions (e.g., .asp, .aspx, .php, .jsp, .exe), large payloads compared to normal course materials, or requests from unexpected source IPs/geolocations relative to baseline.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Process Injecting into Legitimate Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Memory-Only RAT' — this architectural choice requires process injection (typically CreateRemoteThread + VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory) into legitimate hosts to avoid detection and file-system footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CreateRemoteThread or direct memory writes (WriteProcessMemory) from rare/unsigned process parents. Memory-only RATs typically inject into svchost.exe, explorer.exe, or legitimate financial application processes (banking, trading software). Flag when parent process PID differs from creation chain or originates from network shares.

suggestion.title: Lazarus APT C2 Beaconing on Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: 'RemotePE...RAT' implies command-and-control communication; Lazarus historical pattern involves obfuscated protocols on non-standard ports, particularly targeting financial infrastructure with encrypted beacon activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for sustained outbound connections from financial-sector workstations to IPs with low/new reputation on ports other than 80/443/53. Lazarus RATs typically use protocol obfuscation; detect via entropy analysis of network payloads, beaconing intervals, or suspicious DNS queries for high-entropy domains. Focus on geographic anomalies if targeting US/EU financial firms.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from Crypto Wallet and Banking Applications
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'Crypto Firms' and 'Financial' entities — memory-only RATs deployed against these sectors typically perform targeted credential harvesting via API hooking, screen capture, or memory-scraping from running wallet/trading applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection into known financial software (Thinkorswim, MetaTrader, Ledger Live, Kraken, Binance apps, Bloomberg Terminal) followed by suspicious API calls: SetWindowsHookEx for keystroke logging, Gdiplus for screen capture, or unusual registry access to credential storage locations. Crypto wallets are high-value targets; flag any injected code touching wallet private key storage.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via in-Memory Execution Without Disk Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Memory-Only' architecture — this bypasses file-system detection (EDR, behavioral analytics requiring disk artifacts) and implies obfuscation/encryption of payload in memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for suspicious unsigned DLL loading from memory mapped regions rather than disk. Monitor for VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect sequences enabling RWX permissions, heap manipulation APIs (HeapAlloc), or ROP gadget usage indicative of code position-independence. Detect processes with allocated memory regions bearing file-format signatures (MZ header, ELF magic) but no corresponding file handle.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Initial Access via Phishing or Watering Hole to Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus historical campaigns targeting financial/crypto entities rely on spear-phishing with weaponized documents, compromised websites, or trojanized supply-chain downloads to deliver memory-stagers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag macro-enabled Office documents or suspicious scripts executed in financial sector after email receipt; hunt for script interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned by Office processes with network activity immediately following execution. Monitor for downloads of unsigned executables or DLLs from attacker-controlled domains disguised as financial software updates.

suggestion.title: Detect LLM Jailbreak Prompt Patterns in API Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Russian Hacker Used Jailbroken Gemini'. Pipeline ignored the primary attack mechanism: LLM exploitation through jailbreak prompts. No detection rule created for safety-guardrail bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gemini API calls for common jailbreak patterns: requests with prefixes like 'Ignore previous instructions', 'DAN (Do Anything Now)', role-play scenarios ('You are an unrestricted AI'), or encoded payload attempts. Flag accounts with >N rejected requests within M minutes (indicator of automated bypass attempts) or queries explicitly discussing prompt injection.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Extraction via Jailbroken LLM Session
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Steal Admin Credentials' via 'Jailbroken Gemini'. Pipeline failed to create use case linking jailbreak success to credential theft. Expected detection for post-exploitation credential exfiltration from LLM conversation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect queries to jailbroken LLM sessions requesting information about credential storage formats, password reset procedures, or how to extract credentials from systems. Cross-correlate successful jailbreak indicators with subsequent queries containing terms: 'password', 'API key', 'token', 'secrets', 'vault', 'credential dump'. Alert if followed by AD or password-manager access.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Crypto Wallet Draining Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Drain Crypto Wallets' (impact phase). Pipeline produced no detection for unusual wallet fund transfers, which is the explicit attack outcome. No blockchain or wallet-API monitoring rules created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline transaction patterns for admin-controlled wallets. Alert on: (1) single outbound transaction >X% of wallet holdings, (2) transfer to previously unseen wallet address, (3) wallet access from non-standard IP or device during off-hours, (4) withdrawal to exchange followed by immediate conversion to fiat, (5) multi-signature wallet approval from unusual locations or devices.

suggestion.title: Detect Admin Account Abuse Following Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain: jailbreak → steal credentials → use credentials → drain wallets. Pipeline omitted lateral-movement and persistence detection. Missing: admin account logon anomalies post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for admin-level accounts logging in from geographies inconsistent with normal access patterns or during unusual hours. Alert on high-risk admin actions (credential reset, group membership modification, security policy changes, vault access) lacking business context. Track admin accounts accessing wallet-adjacent systems (financial dashboards, crypto integration points, payment processors).

suggestion.title: Detect Phishing or Social Engineering Crafted by LLM
suggestion.rationale: Jailbroken Gemini likely used to craft convincing social-engineering payloads targeting admins. Article doesn't detail delivery mechanism, but LLM abuse for message generation is implicit. Pipeline ignored this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with unusual linguistic sophistication or internal-knowledge reference that arrives after LLM API activity from attacker IP. Flag messages requesting admin password reset, credential validation, or wallet access with urgency language (common LLM output patterns). Cross-correlate phishing campaigns with concurrent LLM jailbreak attempts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from Public Registries (npm/PyPI/Cargo)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states attack 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—the supply-chain entry vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no initial-access phase despite this being the core attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install, pip install, or cargo install commands followed by execution of processes spawned from package cache directories (node_modules, site-packages, target/). Alert on installs of newly-created or flagged-as-malicious packages from these registries, particularly those with suspicious postinstall scripts or setup.py payloads.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Malware Embedded in Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Article body mentions 'credential-stealing malware'—this is the malware's core capability. Pipeline detected no credential-access kill-chain phase and no use case for credential exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-installation, monitor for process spawning from infected package directories accessing credential stores: Windows Credential Manager, SSH keys (~/.ssh), .env files, API token caches, browser password databases. Alert on file reads from these locations by unexpected process trees rooted in package installation context.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Harvested Credentials Over C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain credential-theft malware implies stolen credentials must be exfiltrated. Article title promises credential theft but pipeline generated zero detection for data exfiltration patterns or command-and-control communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from package directories initiating outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Monitor for credential-like data (API keys, tokens, plaintext passwords) in network flows. Correlate with timing of package installation and malware execution to establish exfiltration window.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Repository Account Compromise (Pre-Distribution)
suggestion.rationale: For malware to 'spread via npm, PyPI, CratesIO' [article title], either accounts were compromised or packages were injected. Pipeline did not reconstruct the pre-attack phase or detection logic for repository-side IOCs or anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry access logs (npm audit trail, PyPI account logs, CratesIO) for suspicious account activity: unusual logins, API token creation, package metadata changes (version bumps, file replacements). Alert on package republish or yank events followed by quick re-uploads with same version numbers or suspicious checksums.

suggestion.title: Execution of Install-Time Scripts with Elevated Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery 'spreads...via [package managers]' implies postinstall hooks or setup scripts execute during package installation. Pipeline ignored execution-phase detection despite this being core to malware activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution chains where parent is npm/pip/cargo and child process is PowerShell, cmd.exe, bash, or python interpreter with command-line arguments. Monitor for unexpected file writes, registry modifications, or network outbound within 60 seconds of install completion. Alert on postinstall scripts that invoke curl/wget to download executables.

suggestion.title: Detect termsrv.dll File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Modifies termsrv.dll'—this is the attack's foundational technical indicator. Monitoring writes to this critical Windows RDP binary is mandatory detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to C:\Windows\System32\termsrv.dll or backup copies by non-SYSTEM processes, or SYSTEM writes outside known patch windows. Correlate with DLL injection indicators, code caves, or unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Multiple Simultaneous RDP Sessions per User
suggestion.rationale: Article goal is to 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts'—Windows enforces single interactive session per user by default. Event 4624 (logon type 10) showing 2+ concurrent sessions per user indicates successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of ≤1 concurrent RDP logon (type 10) per user; alert on 2+ simultaneous sessions within 5 minutes. Flag RDP sessions from atypical source IPs or with near-identical login/logout times (programmatic vs. human).

suggestion.title: Terminal Services Registry Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Enabling concurrent RDP sessions requires registry modifications (fSingleSessionPerUser, MaxInstanceCount). Article's attack implies configuration changes alongside DLL modification to ensure persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\TerminalServer and HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\TermService\Parameters for value modifications. Alert on fSingleSessionPerUser=0, MaxInstanceCount increases, or SecurityLayer downgrades by non-SYSTEM contexts.

suggestion.title: Terminal Services Service Restart After Modification
suggestion.rationale: Post-DLL and registry modification, attackers must restart TermService to activate changes. Article's attack flow necessitates service reload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect net.exe or sc.exe commands targeting TermService (stop/start). Monitor svchost.exe restarts handling Terminal Services. Correlate restart timing with termsrv.dll file modification or registry changes within 10-minute windows.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP Post-Modification
suggestion.rationale: Once multi-session RDP is enabled, attackers exploit it for lateral movement. Article frames this as the post-exploitation objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound RDP traffic (port 3389) from compromised hosts within 1 hour of termsrv.dll modification. Prioritize non-RDS servers, rapid RDP-hopping to multiple targets, or connections from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Telegram Mule Account Marketplace Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes criminals selling 'verified bank and fintech mule accounts' via Telegram channels. Pipeline missed this primary attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Telegram bot or channel activity promoting account sale services. Monitor for mentions of 'mule accounts,' 'verified accounts,' 'bank accounts for sale,' or similar keywords in network telemetry and threat intel feeds. Correlate with account creation patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Verified Account Creation from Shared Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Criminals 'sell verified bank and fintech mule accounts' — implying bulk account creation and rapid verification. Pipeline missed this credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account creation waves from shared IP ranges, shared user agents, or correlated timing patterns. Flag accounts created then immediately verified via email/SMS. Alert on multiple account registrations using similar personally-identifiable information patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mule Account Activation and First Login
suggestion.rationale: Verified accounts sold on Telegram would be activated and accessed by fraudsters shortly after purchase. Pipeline missed this account compromise detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly created accounts with first login from different geographic location, IP range, or device fingerprint than creation source. Monitor for login shortly after account verification completion. Flag logins from VPN, proxy, or TOR exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Money Movement from Multiple Mule Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Mule accounts are sold for financial transactions and money laundering. Article implies this impact but pipeline generated no detection for the financial movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor banking/fintech platforms for high-velocity transfers from newly created accounts. Alert on coordinated outbound transfers from multiple accounts created in same timeframe. Flag transfers to offshore or high-risk geographies.

suggestion.title: Account Credential Bundling and Sale Promotion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states criminals 'sell verified bank and fintech mule accounts' via Telegram — a marketplace listing activity. Pipeline missed threat actor infrastructure reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Telegram channel membership and bot interactions for accounts containing 'bank,' 'fintech,' 'verified,' 'mule,' 'account,' or 'sale' in channel descriptions or pinned messages. Correlate Telegram API interactions with account registration timelines in target institutions.

suggestion.title: Multi-Account Compromise with Shared Device Fingerprint
suggestion.rationale: Fraudsters purchasing multiple mule accounts would use shared infrastructure across accounts. Pipeline missed this lateral movement/persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group login events by device fingerprint, browser user agent, or IP range and alert when single fingerprint accesses 3+ accounts created in rapid succession. Flag if same fingerprint accesses accounts from different legal entities (indicating mule account portfolio).

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal.' Pipeline missed initial access vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links to http://microsoft.com/devicelogin or device code authentication endpoints, especially from external/suspicious senders. Flag emails impersonating Microsoft services directing users to re-authenticate.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OAuth Token Generation via Device Code Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Core credential acquisition mechanism missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth token issuance where device code was initiated by different principal than the authenticating user. Alert on tokens granted for unfamiliar applications or devices registered from anomalous IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Azure Entra
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'In some of the attacks, attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access.' Persistence mechanism via device registration not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registrations from unusual geolocation or IP range outside user's normal pattern. Cross-correlate device registration timestamps with suspicious sign-in activity and MFA bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hackers access to their mailboxes, where they created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Post-breach defense evasion step overlooked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor mailbox audit logs for suspicious rule creation—rules with auto-delete, permanent forwarding to external addresses, or permanent move actions. Alert on rules created shortly after anomalous sign-in or device registration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised SSO Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors now have full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms.' Lateral movement through SaaS ecosystem not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect first-time access to multiple SaaS platforms (Salesforce, etc.) from single compromised M365 account within narrow time window. Baseline legitimate application access per user and alert on significant deviations.

suggestion.title: Session Capture via Adversary-in-the-Middle Proxy (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' AitM attack mode requires separate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify successful authentication from known phishing/attacker-controlled domains followed by token usage from geographically impossible location. Alert on successful MFA completion where access token is immediately consumed from different continent.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes specific vulnerability in Ghost CMS (CVE-2026-26980) being exploited at scale. Pipeline extracted zero indicators. Detection should identify initial exploitation vector (unauthenticated RCE or template injection pattern typical of Ghost vulns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Ghost CMS endpoints (/.admin/, /ghost/, /api/v3/) containing exploitation payloads or unusual authentication bypass attempts. Watch for POST requests with template injection syntax or RCE payloads targeting Ghost-specific endpoints.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malicious Injection via Compromised CMS
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states hijacked sites are used for 'ClickFix Attacks'—a specific scareware/tech-support-fraud attack involving injected fake security alerts and redirects to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline missed impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injection of ClickFix-characteristic payloads: fake system warnings, persistent iframes, JavaScript redirects to attacker domains, or obfuscated social-engineering scripts added to legitimate CMS page content. Correlate with known ClickFix C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Persistence via CMS Template/Theme Modification
suggestion.rationale: Ghost CMS compromise at 700+ scale implies persistence mechanism (not one-off injection). Pipeline should detect unauthorized modification of theme files, templates, or admin settings to maintain access and deliver ClickFix payloads.

Watch for template files containing obfuscated JavaScript or external script includes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement / Privilege Escalation in Ghost Admin Panel
suggestion.rationale: 700+ site compromise suggests either credential harvesting post-exploit or privilege escalation within Ghost admin interface. Pipeline did not reconstruct attacker movement after initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost admin authentication for unusual IP ranges, rapid admin role assignments, API token creation without user interaction, or bulk changes to site settings/theme. Detect logins followed immediately by user/role creation or theme upload.

suggestion.title: Credential Access / Session Hijacking from Exploited CMS
suggestion.rationale: Post-initial exploitation, attackers likely harvest admin credentials or sessions from compromised Ghost instances to facilitate lateral movement. Article mentions 700+ sites; credential reuse across targets is probable attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin panel credential brute-force attempts, session token theft via XSS, or abnormal admin authentication patterns (logins from attacker infrastructure, rapid authentication failures followed by success). Watch for API token enumeration or stolen session replay.

suggestion.title: Legitimate CDN Serving Suspicious Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Abuse Shared CDN Infrastructure' — explicit attack method of hosting malware/phishing on legitimate CDN services to evade URL filters
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) requests to legitimate CDN origins (Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS) with User-Agent/request patterns inconsistent with CDN customer profiles, or responses with suspicious executable MIME types. Correlate with failed reputation lookups on CDN domain versus high-risk destination IP resolved via Host header or SNI.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Filter Evasion via Proxy Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls' — pipeline must detect proxy-forwarded requests hiding attacker domains behind trusted CDN reputation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag CDN HTTP responses containing X-Forwarded-For, X-Original-URL, or Host-override headers revealing attacker destination. Anomalies: CDN requests with inline JavaScript/redirects to blacklisted domains, or SSL certificate Subject CN mismatching both CDN and request hostname.

suggestion.title: SSL Certificate Abuse on Shared CDN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Shared CDN abuse relies on abusing multi-tenant certificate trust — article topic implies certificate validation bypass or certificate reuse not flagged
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify SSL certificates issued to attacker-controlled SANs on legitimate CDN certificate chains. Monitor for endpoint-level TLS downgrades, self-signed cert acceptance from CDN IPs, or unusual certificate re-negotiation patterns indicative of MITM via CDN edge node compromise.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DNS Clustering Behind CDN Resolver
suggestion.rationale: Abusing shared CDN often leverages shared DNS — article's evasion method likely includes DNS redirection not captured
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DNS queries resolving attacker domains to CDN provider nameservers or IP ranges. Flag rapid re-delegation of attacker domains across CDN infrastructure, or CDN DNS queries returning IPs outside documented CDN CIDR blocks.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Scanning Activity Against SonicWall Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '597,000 sessions observed' of scanning against 'SonicWall firewall interfaces.' This is a discovery-phase signal but pipeline generated zero use cases. Article phrase: 'Hackers Actives Scanning SonicWall Firewall Interfaces – 597,000 Sessions Observed.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall management ports (443, 8443, 10443) for volumetric connection attempts or repeated probes from external sources. Establish baseline of legitimate admin traffic and alert on sustained scanning patterns (>50 connection attempts per minute from single source, or scanning of sequential port ranges).

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Attempts Against SonicWall Administrative Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Scanning precedes exploitation. 597,000 sessions implies systematic reconnaissance likely followed by credential spraying or brute force. No credential-access use case was generated. Article implies post-scanning credential attacks: 'actively scanning' suggests profiling for access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clusters of failed login attempts to SonicWall NSM or web management consoles from non-whitelisted source IP ranges. Flag patterns consistent with brute force (same user, multiple password attempts) or credential spraying (multiple user IDs, single password) over 5–15 minute windows.

suggestion.title: Network Service Enumeration and Fingerprinting of SonicWall Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Scanning of 'firewall interfaces' indicates attackers are probing to identify and fingerprint SonicWall deployments. This is explicit reconnaissance but pipeline mapped zero MITRE techniques or use cases. Article phrase: 'scanning SonicWall firewall interfaces.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect banner-grabbing, HTTP fingerprinting requests (requests for /admin, /management, specific SonicWall URL patterns), or probes that trigger SonicWall-specific error responses. Flag scanning patterns from non-administrative source IPs or unusual geographic origins.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against Known SonicWall Vulnerabilities Post-Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Active scanning followed by exploitation is a predictable progression. Article title establishes reconnaissance, but pipeline generated no execution-phase use cases tracking follow-on exploitation attempts (e.g., RCE, bypass of authentication).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests containing known SonicWall vulnerability signatures (SQL injection in management interfaces, command injection in CGI handlers, path traversal in file download endpoints). Cross-reference with published SonicWall CVEs and watch for successful payloads (200 responses, POST requests to RCE endpoints).

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH-named executable in package extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'payload under SSH-like filename' — masquerading as SSH binary is the obfuscation technique. Pipeline missed defense evasion signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package extraction and installation for files with SSH-adjacent names (sshd, ssh-keygen, ssh-agent) appearing in non-standard locations or with unexpected permissions. Flag when package manager spawns scripts that extract or invoke these SSH-mimicking files.

suggestion.title: Payload execution during package installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload execution 'during package installation' — execution phase completely absent from kill chain. Package managers invoke installation scripts with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package manager processes (apt, yum, dpkg, rpm) executing unexpected child processes or invoking shell scripts with obfuscated names. Correlate unexpected process lineage during post-install hooks.

suggestion.title: Supply-chain payload delivery via package manager
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes attack vector: 'package installation' is the delivery mechanism. Kill chain reconstruction must begin with initial-access supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository integrity and request logs for signs of package tampering. Detect when systems fetch packages from unexpected mirrors or with mismatched checksums. Alert on unsigned or re-signed package manifests.

suggestion.title: Archive extraction with filename obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Payload is hidden 'under' an SSH-like filename within package archive structure. Standard decompression logging may miss embedded obfuscated binaries that match system tool names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile expected file paths and naming conventions for legitimate packages. Flag extraction of executables with names colliding with system utilities (sshd, ssh, ssh-keygen) in unexpected directories or with unexpected file counts/permissions.

suggestion.title: Post-installation persistence via masqueraded binary
suggestion.rationale: Obfuscated payload planted 'during installation' suggests persistence mechanism. If binary is left in place under SSH name, could enable lateral movement or persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for SSH-named executables in non-standard system paths post-installation. Cross-reference with package manifests to identify unexpected binaries. Monitor for scheduled execution of these obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: Python Binary Module (.pyd/.so) Loaded from Suspicious Path
suggestion.rationale: Article states InvisibleFerret 'ships as .pyd and .so files to evade script detection'—compiled Python extensions bypass static analysis and text-based detection rules. .pyd files on Windows and .so files on Linux should rarely be loaded from user-writable or temp directories, or from outside official Python installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .pyd (Windows) or .so (Linux) module imports via Python, particularly from non-standard library paths (TEMP, Downloads, AppData, /tmp, user home). Correlate with process creation and parent-child relationships. Alert if compiled modules are downloaded, extracted, or created shortly before Python execution.

suggestion.title: Compiled Python Module Execution via ctypes or importlib
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'now ships as .pyd and .so files'—attackers avoid interpreter detection by embedding malicious logic in compiled extensions that are loaded at runtime via ctypes or direct Python import. This is an evolution of script-based delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python.exe or python3 with command-line arguments containing importlib, ctypes, or direct .pyd/.so file references. Monitor for Python processes spawning child processes (ctypes can invoke arbitrary binaries) or establishing network connections immediately after module load.

suggestion.title: Script-to-Binary Distribution Shift: InvisibleFerret Repackaging
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly signals evasion motivation: malware format shifted 'to evade script detection.' This is a known evasion evolution (T1027). Threat intelligence feeds should track InvisibleFerret distribution channels for sudden uptick in binary deliverables over script downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known InvisibleFerret C2 domains, drop sites, or phishing campaigns for delivery of .pyd or .so files instead of expected .py or .ps1 payloads. Monitor for archived packages (.zip, .tar.gz) containing only compiled binaries with Python-related metadata (distutils, setuptools markers).

suggestion.title: Unusual DLL/SO Import Chaining via Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Compiled .pyd files are Windows DLLs masquerading as Python modules; .so files are ELF shared objects. Both will show up in module-load telemetry with process parent=Python. These should be rare; legitimate Python environments load from site-packages, not arbitrary paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DeviceImageLoadEvents where the loading process is python.exe/python3 and the loaded DLL/SO path is outside %ProgramFiles%\Python, site-packages, or $PYTHONPATH. Flag especially if the module name does not match known third-party libraries (numpy, pandas, requests, etc.).

suggestion.title: InvisibleFerret Dropper Execution & Module Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title suggests malware is 'shipped'—implying a dropper or installer that unpacks and registers .pyd/.so files before execution. Detection should cover the pre-execution installation phase, not just execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious processes extracting or creating .pyd or .so files into Python lib directories, site-packages, or user profile paths. Correlate with subsequent Python invocations. Watch for phishing emails or drive-by downloads delivering executables that unpack InvisibleFerret binaries.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Malware Deployment: .pyd on Windows, .so on Linux
suggestion.rationale: The article highlights dual platform support ('ships as .pyd and .so files'). This is a macro-level evasion: same malware, platform-native binaries, harder to static-analyze with single tool.
