suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for coordinated artifact deployment across Windows and Linux in the same enterprise window (same timeframe, same user/asset group, related C2 infrastructure). Alert if the same threat actor distributes architecturally distinct binaries (.pyd vs .so) in a single campaign.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SQL Developer Installer Download from Non-Microsoft Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake SQL Developer Malware Installer' — threat vector is social-engineering users to download malicious .exe disguised as legitimate SQL tooling. Zero download-based detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe downloads matching 'SQL*Developer*', 'SQLServerDeveloper*', or 'SSDT*' patterns from domains outside Microsoft's CDN or known distribution partners. Cross-reference file hash against malware feeds. Monitor for execution from %TEMP% or %AppData% paths.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Search Result Click-Through to Malware Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'SEO Poisoning' — users deceived clicking search results. Pipeline missed initial-access detection spanning search referrer-chain analysis to landing-domain reputation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP Referer headers for navigation from major search engines directly to suspicious low-reputation domains. Alert on search keywords ('SQL Developer', 'SQL Server tools') resolving to newly registered or attacker-controlled IP ranges. Flag domains impersonating legitimate software vendors.

suggestion.title: Malware File Hash Detection — Fake SQL Developer Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific malware payload but pipeline extracted zero file hashes (MD5, SHA256) or file-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file hashes of suspicious SQL Developer installers against threat-intelligence feeds for Iranian APT infrastructure. Alert on process creation matching known malware signatures. Flag potentially stolen code-signing certificates used to sign payloads.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback Detection from Malware Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware execution naturally precedes command-and-control communication. Zero C2-phase detections generated despite clear attack-chain implication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from SQL Server or installer-spawned processes. Alert on DNS queries to known Iranian APT C2 domains. Establish behavioral baseline for expected SQL Server network traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Persistence Establishment via Registry or Service Creation
suggestion.rationale: Malware-as-installer pattern necessarily includes post-execution persistence. Pipeline mapped no persistence-phase techniques or detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service creation, scheduled-task installation, or registry Run-key modifications spawned from suspicious installer execution context. Flag unexpected SYSTEM-context process launches from temp or user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Masquerading as Legitimate SQL Server Tools
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector fundamentally relies on filename/metadata spoofing. Pipeline failed to map T1036 or generate masquerading-detection use case despite explicit article framing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables bearing SQL Server metadata (ProductName, CompanyName) with mismatched digital signatures, signing dates, or file origins inconsistent with Microsoft releases. Flag non-standard installation paths bearing SQL Server branding.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Module Execution via Suspicious DLL Loading
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'modular espionage ecosystem'—modular architecture requires dynamic DLL loading and child-process spawning as core execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes loading DLLs from temporary, user-writable, or non-system directories. Flag parent processes spawning coded children from %TEMP%, %AppData%, or obfuscated paths. Kazuar modular design manifests as unusual imageload sequences.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Browser and Email Stores
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'espionage ecosystem'—credential theft is defining behavior of espionage-class malware. No article body to confirm methods, but espionage malware universally targets credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser processes accessing browser credential databases (%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\Credentials), email client .pst files, or LSASS memory. Flag registry access patterns reading Browser\IntelliForms or cached login data.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Keys or Windows Services
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'operations' implies active command-and-control requiring boot-level persistence. Kazuar documented using Run keys and service installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKCU equivalents with entries pointing to temporary paths, packed binaries, or obfuscated command lines. Monitor WMI service creation with binary paths in non-standard locations.

suggestion.title: C&C Beaconing via HTTPS with Irregular Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'operations' requires active C&C. Kazuar uses encrypted HTTPS communication; detection requires behavioral analysis of connection timing and payload size.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS from non-browser processes to low-reputation or newly registered domains. Flag fixed-interval beaconing, consistent request sizes, or cipher-suite anomalies atypical for the source process.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via WMI Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'modular espionage ecosystem' implies multi-host presence. Kazuar spreads via WMI exploitation and remote execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wmic.exe or Win32_Process class instantiation targeting remote systems. Flag suspicious WMI arguments, remote IPC connections, and anomalous SMB/RPC traffic following WMI invocation.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Runtime Anti-Analysis Checks
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Evolves Into' suggests new evasion techniques. Espionage malware typically includes anti-debugging, anti-VM, and anti-sandbox logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IsDebuggerPresent API calls, GetSystemMetrics(SM_DEBUG) queries, WMI enumeration for VM artifacts, or suspicious registry probes for analysis tools. Flag packed/obfuscated code signatures.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploited'—this is the initial access vector. Pipeline extracted zero kill chain phases or IOCs for exploit attempts despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS for payloads indicative of parameter injection, path traversal, or file upload exploitation. Flag requests to known vulnerable LMS endpoints with non-standard parameters or binary/encoded payloads in POST bodies.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'BLUEBEAM Web Shell' as the deployed artifact; pipeline extracted no persistence indicators or IOCs for web shell presence despite this being the primary payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file uploads/creation of .php, .aspx, .jsp files in web-accessible directories (/uploads, /temp, /files) of LMS installation. Correlate with execution of these files via web server process; flag files with 'bluebeam' in name or containing common web shell signatures.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command Execution via LMS
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment (BLUEBEAM) implies command execution and C2 communication; pipeline surfaced zero execution or C2 detection patterns despite this being the direct post-exploitation objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by web server processes (apache, w3wp, nginx) or LMS application processes. Flag execution of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or scripting interpreters invoked with suspicious parameters or from web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Compromised LMS
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment necessarily implies command-and-control callbacks; pipeline generated no C2 detection use case or indicators despite this being the implicit threat actor objective post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from LMS server IP to non-business external IPs. Flag connections with GET/POST parameters containing Base64, hex-encoded commands, or response patterns consistent with shell protocol (command echo, output truncation).

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'RemotePE Memory-Only RAT' — pipeline missed core execution mechanic. Memory-only execution is the defining evasion characteristic and should trigger dedicated UC for suspicious process hollowing or reflection-based loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for indirect syscalls, VirtualAlloc→WriteProcessMemory→CreateRemoteThread chains, or unpacked code execution in lsass/svchost. Flag processes spawning unsigned/unattested child regions in memory without corresponding file on disk.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus RAT deployments consistently use obfuscated HTTP/HTTPS C2. Article describes 'deploys RemotePE...' implying active C2 infrastructure, but pipeline extracted no network IOCs or beacon patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST/GET patterns with suspiciously short user-agent strings, large request/response size asymmetry, or binary-encoded command structures in HTTPS payloads. Lazarus commonly uses obfuscated HTTP headers and certificate pinning to evade inspection.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Financial Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Target profile explicitly names 'financial and crypto firms' — strongly implies credential theft and browser/wallet harvesting. Pipeline generated no credential-access detections despite this being a standard Lazarus payload objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes injecting into or hooking browser processes (chrome, firefox, msedge) or accessing Windows Credential Manager vaults. Look for suspicious lsass child processes or ntdll patches that intercept credential APIs.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Proxies (LOLBIN) Chain
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RATs typically bootstrap via LOLBIN chains (powershell, wmic, rundll32) to avoid file-based signatures. Article's focus on memory-only execution implies this vector, but pipeline missed it entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell/cmd.exe spawning without associated scripts on disk, or wmic/rundll32 with encoded command-line arguments. Detect parent-child relationships where legitimate system binaries spawn unexpected children in temp directories.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Process Injection Timeline
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only malware inherently uses process injection to persist without disk writes. Article emphasizes 'memory-only' as evasion mechanism, but pipeline did not surface injection-specific detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: any process with handle to lsass/svchost + subsequent memory writes + missing parent executable. Flag VirtualAlloc in system processes followed by code execution outside normal code caves. Correlate with absence of corresponding .exe on disk.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Campaign Indicators (Email/Domain Patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output includes empty IOC dictionary despite CRIT severity and named threat actor. Even if full article was inaccessible, title keywords (Lazarus, RemotePE, finance, crypto) should trigger contextual IOC ingestion rules or fallback to known Lazarus C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference against known Lazarus phishing infrastructure (spear-phishing domains, sender spoofing patterns). Monitor for emails targeting finance/crypto sectors with RemotePE-adjacent file attachments (weaponized Office, archives with dual-use executables).

suggestion.title: LLM Prompt Injection / Jailbreak Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'jailbroken Gemini'—the attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface this as initial access technique requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM API calls for payloads with known jailbreak patterns ('ignore previous', 'pretend', 'system override'). Correlate with responses containing credentials, keys, or sensitive data that should be refused.

suggestion.title: Admin Credential Extraction via Compromised LLM
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states hacker 'steal admin credentials' via Gemini—direct credential access pattern pipeline should detect at LLM output layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag LLM responses containing plaintext admin passwords, API keys, tokens, or privilege-escalation paths. Alert if same session/IP then successfully authenticates with extracted credentials to backend systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Crypto Wallet Drainage Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly mentions 'drain crypto wallets'—exfiltration/impact phase. Pipeline should detect unusual wallet transaction volumes and destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large or rapid outbound transfers from enterprise custody wallets from new IPs or off-hours. Correlate with credential compromise. Monitor for sweep-to-exchange patterns indicating liquidation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using Stolen Admin Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromised admin credentials universally enable lateral movement—article title implies multi-system compromise across admin-credential-holding infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins with extracted admin credentials from unexpected geolocations. Monitor for immediate access to wallet-management or vault-administrative APIs post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Anomalous API Calls from LLM Service Account Context
suggestion.rationale: Jailbroken Gemini used to interact with backend APIs and exfiltrate data—article implies LLM session pivoted to command backend systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls from Gemini service account for abnormal endpoints (vault APIs, wallet-transfer endpoints, user provisioning). Flag repeated requests to credential-storage or asset-movement endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detection of Suspicious Package Installation from Compromised Public Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: malware 'spreads via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO.' Pipeline generated zero initial-access UC. Supply-chain compromise requires baseline detection of untrusted package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager commands (npm install, pip install, cargo add) and flag installations of packages not in organization whitelist, or from non-canonical registries. Correlate with unusual process spawning patterns and post-install file modification.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Hook Executing Code with Credential File Access
suggestion.rationale: Package installation triggers execution phases via setup scripts. Article specifies 'credential-stealing'—no UC for detecting install scripts reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, or accessing KUBECONFIG/GCP credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by package manager daemons (npm, pip, cargo) that open credential-related files or enumerate environment variables containing secrets (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GCP_*, KUBECONFIG, GitHub tokens). Flag if process tree is inconsistent with legitimate build operations.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials During or After Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware steals credentials; article headline emphasizes credential-stealing component. No UC detects post-theft exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure during package operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries or network connections initiated by package-manager child processes to non-whitelisted external domains. Flag if timing aligns with credential file access, or if process command-line contains credential values or file paths.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Namespace Confusion Attack: Installation of Suspiciously Named Packages
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often exploit name confusion (e.g., 'expresss' vs 'express'). Article implies malicious packages on legitimate registries; no UC for detecting lookalike package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package installation logs and flag package names with high edit distance to known legitimate libraries, or names containing common misspellings. Cross-reference installed versions against organization's pinned dependency list.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Package Registry Cache Poisoning or Hook Modification
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware often persists by modifying package manager config or hooks. Article implies ongoing credential theft; no UC covers persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to ~/.npm/, ~/.pip/, ~/.cargo/ config files, .npmrc, pip.conf, and npm/pip post-install hook directories. Flag unauthorized writes to these locations by non-package-manager processes.

suggestion.title: Detect termsrv.dll File Write or Replacement Events
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Modifies termsrv.dll' as primary attack. No detection use case generated despite this being the attack's core mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to C:\Windows\System32\termsrv.dll with timestamps outside normal Windows update windows, unsigned or revoked signatures, or file versions mismatched from expected baseline per OS version. Correlate with TerminalServices service restart events.

suggestion.title: Detect Concurrent Multiple RDP Session Logons
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack objective is 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions' but no UC detects the behavioral outcome of successful persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple simultaneous RDP session logon events (Security Event 4624, LogonType=10) for the same user account or multiple concurrent sessions from different source IPs within a short window. Flag sessions persisting abnormally long or appearing outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Detect TerminalServices Registry Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Enabling concurrent RDP sessions typically requires registry changes (fSingleSessionPerUser=0 or MaxConnectionsPerSession modifications). No UC for detecting registry tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\TerminalServices registry hive, specifically fSingleSessionPerUser, MaxConnectionsPerSession, or WinStationsDisabled values. Alert on changes outside normal update windows or by non-SYSTEM principals.

suggestion.title: Detect Unsigned or Version-Mismatched termsrv.dll
suggestion.rationale: APT DLL modification implies replacement with unsigned or spoofed version. Article implies tampering but no signature-based detection UC created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify termsrv.dll digital signature against Microsoft root CA and compare file version metadata against known-good baseline for each Windows OS version. Alert on missing/invalid signatures, mismatched file versions, or certificates from non-Microsoft CAs.

suggestion.title: Hunt for termsrv.dll Copies in Staging Directories
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector implies attacker staged modified DLL before deployment. No hunting use case for intermediate artefacts or staging locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for termsrv.dll files outside C:\Windows\System32, including copies in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, user Downloads, or obfuscated filenames. Correlate with file access logs to identify copy-to-System32 patterns.

suggestion.title: Correlate DLL Tampering with RDP Session Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Successful attack manifests as behavioral anomaly (multiple RDP sessions). No composite detection links DLL modification timing to subsequent RDP logon spikes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate termsrv.dll modification events with abnormal increase in RDP session creation (Event 4624 LogonType=10) or connection attempts in the following hours. Flag rapid logon/logoff cycles or connections from unusual source IPs to the same account.

suggestion.title: Telegram-based Credential Marketplace Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states cybercriminals 'use Telegram channels to sell verified bank and fintech mule accounts,' establishing Telegram as C2/coordination infrastructure. No traffic detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained Telegram client connections from corporate/banking segments paired with behavioral telemetry of account enumeration or credential validation. Detect encrypted channels with high message frequency, file transfers, or sticker usage (common obfuscation) correlating to known compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Fintech Account Verification Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed the 'verified' account verification step: 'sell verified bank and fintech mule accounts' indicates criminals are conducting account validation (phone, email, SMS OTP) in bulk. No behavioral detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential SIM swaps, OTP requests, or verification SMS receipts to numbers not linked historically. Detect coordinated verification of multiple accounts within 24h from shared IP ranges or device fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Mule Account Provisioning and Initial Transfers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sale of 'mule accounts' implying onboarding and fund transfer testing. Pipeline did not surface money movement or account activity anomalies post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly-verified mule accounts with zero historical transaction history receiving inbound transfers within hours of creation. Flag geographic velocity anomalies (account created in one country, first login from another). Monitor for rapid subsequent outbound transfers or inter-account consolidation.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Harvesting via Phishing to Banking Staff
suggestion.rationale: Mule accounts require either legitimate employee credentials or social engineering of banking staff. Article title implies widespread credential compromise but no phishing or credential-access detection chain was built.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing campaigns impersonating fintech/banking platforms with subsequent legitimate account login anomalies (impossible travel, new device, MFA bypass attempts). Flag credential submissions to lookalike phishing infrastructure coinciding with mule-account registration timestamps.

suggestion.title: Cross-border Mule Account Activity Network Signature
suggestion.rationale: Marketplace-driven account distribution implies accounts sold to multiple buyers across geographies. Pipeline did not suggest detection for distributed, low-volume transactions characteristic of money laundering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build risk profiles on mule accounts: detect clusters of accounts with matching setup patterns (creation date, device, IP) but divergent transaction destinations across high-risk jurisdictions. Correlate account metadata (email domain, phone prefix) to known fintech crime forums.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code OAuth Token Issuance
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Pipeline missed this token issuance anomaly—tokens granted to device that never performed MFA solve should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth device code grant flow completion where MFA was challenged and completed by user, but token is issued to attacker-controlled device. Look for device code auth from microsoft.com/devicelogin followed by token issuance with mismatched user agent or IP from phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'In some of the attacks, attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' No detection rule generated for unauthorized device registration following account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device registration events that occur immediately after (within 1-4 hours) device code authentication and token issuance, or from IP/geo mismatched to historical user pattern. Correlate device registration with mailbox access from same session token.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation for Defense Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments...attackers also...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Pipeline did not generate detection for suspicious inbox rule creation, a signature evasion tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rule creation (New-InboxRule via EWS/REST) that deletes, moves, or archives emails from common security domains (alerts@company, noreply@microsoft), or rules triggered by subject keywords matching phishing campaigns. Flag rules created via token-based auth shortly after compromise.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Device Code Portal Link
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector stated as 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers.' No detection rule for emails with microsoft.com/devicelogin or device code portal references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or similar device authorization portals sent in bulk from external domains. Correlate with user-agent strings and geoIP from device code acceptance to identify legitimate vs. phishing-origin codes.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie Capture via Proxy (Cookie Link Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cookie Link' attack mode: 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' No detection for proxy-based session theft or anomalous token usage post-capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth redirects or SSO flows through non-Microsoft hosts (via URL click logs, network proxy logs). Correlate with token usage: sessions created via unusual path should show anomalous access patterns (bulk mailbox read, unusual geo, rapid SaaS platform pivots) immediately after MFA completion.

suggestion.title: Rapid Cross-SaaS Platform Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes compromise grants 'full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms.' No detection for sudden multi-platform access surge from compromised token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user session accessing 3+ distinct SaaS platforms (M365, Salesforce, etc.) within 10 minutes of device code auth, especially from IPs mismatched to user history. Flag token re-use across multiple cloud tenants or applications in compressed timeframe.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation of CVE-2026-26980 affecting Ghost CMS; pipeline failed to generate any detection for this vulnerability despite it being the centerpiece of the threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS endpoints for POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable parameters (e.g., theme upload, admin API paths) that trigger 500 errors or unusual response codes. Track requests that bypass authentication or exploit version-detection weaknesses in Ghost < patched version.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Ghost Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Website hijacking for ClickFix delivery implies attacker account provisioning; article title states '700+ sites hijacked' but pipeline extracted no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ghost CMS admin user creation events (database INSERT or API POST to /ghost/api/admin/users) occurring after exploit patterns or from non-standard IPs. Correlate with authentication logs showing first login from attacker-controlled IP.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Payload Injection in HTTP Responses
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks used hijacked sites 'for ClickFix attacks'; no detection for malicious JavaScript or payload injection in served content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect outbound HTTP responses from compromised Ghost instances for ClickFix-associated script tags, known payload domains, or obfuscated JavaScript injected into blog post HTML. Monitor for DNS queries to known ClickFix infrastructure from affected site IPs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Ghost CMS Theme/Plugin Modification
suggestion.rationale: Website hijacking typically involves theme/plugin abuse for persistence; article mentions exploitation of 700+ sites but pipeline generated no detection for unauthorized code deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost theme/plugin directories for unauthorized file writes or replacement of legitimate templates. Alert on changes to theme index.hbs or package.json outside of scheduled updates, especially if followed by HTTP response injection or unexpected outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Version Detection & Vulnerability Probing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable Ghost instances before exploitation; article describes campaign targeting 700+ sites suggesting reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HEAD/GET requests to Ghost version-disclosure endpoints (e.g., /ghost/api/v3/clients/web, package.json) or diagnostic paths that leak version info. Correlate version-detection activity with subsequent CVE-2026-26980 exploitation attempts from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download from Shared CDN Edge Hostname
suggestion.rationale: Article title states abuse of 'shared CDN infrastructure' — attackers are abusing legitimate Cloudflare/Akamai/Fastly hostnames to deliver payloads. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for executable/script delivery via CDN paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binary/executable downloads (EXE, PS1, BAT, SH, DLL) served from hostnames matching shared CDN patterns (*-edge.*.* or known CDN providers). Alert when CDN IPs return Content-Disposition: attachment for suspicious MIME types.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Score Anomaly – Legitimate Domain to Malicious Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'bypass domain reputation security controls' by leveraging high-reputation CDN domains. No UC checks for mismatched reputation scores between domain and resolved IP or x509 issuer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when domain reputation scoring systems show high trust (Cloudflare/Fastly domain) but underlying infrastructure (resolved IP, x509 certificate issuer, WHOIS registrant) contains indicators of compromise or phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Beaconing to CDN Edge Node with Masqueraded Domain
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in 'bypass reputation controls' is C2 over HTTPS to CDN-hosted infrastructure. Article does not establish specific IOCs but should trigger C2 behavioral detection given the attack scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic, small-volume HTTPS requests to shared CDN hostnames with consistent intervals (beaconing). Flag User-Agent strings unusual for legitimate content delivery, or POST requests to static content paths.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL with Shared CDN Domain Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses legitimate CDN domains in phishing links to bypass URL reputation filters. Article describes this evasion but no email-based detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect URLs in email containing shared CDN domain names (e.g., `*.cloudflare.com`, `*.fastly.net`) pointing to attacker infrastructure via URL redirects, parameter injection, or subdomain takeover. Correlate with known phishing domains in redirect chain.

suggestion.title: Mass Firewall Interface Probing (SonicWall)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Actives Scanning SonicWall Firewall Interfaces' and observes '597,000 Sessions' — clear scanning campaign with massive volume signal. Pipeline missed the core reconnaissance activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to SonicWall default interface paths (e.g., /api/sonicos/auth) from unique source IPs over short time window. Threshold: >100 unique IPs in 1 hour targeting SonicWall device ports (443, 8443, 2222). Aggregate by target CIDR to identify mass scanning campaigns.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Credential Brute Force Detection
suggestion.rationale: Scanning 597K sessions implies probing for authentication. Article title 'Hackers Actives' suggests exploitation intent beyond passive reconnaissance — credential attacks highly probable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to SonicWall management interfaces. Alert on >10 failed logins from single source IP within 10 minutes, or distributed pattern: >50 failed attempts across ≥5 IPs to same SonicWall in <30 min window targeting default/service accounts.

suggestion.title: SonicWall Exploit Kit Traffic Pattern
suggestion.rationale: '597,000 Sessions Observed' suggests automated exploitation tooling. Pipeline should map CVEs in SonicWall (CVE-2021-20016, etc.) and detect corresponding POST/GET sequences against vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to known SonicWall vulnerability URIs (/api/webserver/, /api/sonicos/) with rapid 200/404 response patterns indicating version enumeration. Flag requests with unusual User-Agent or scripted request patterns (curl, python-requests). Baseline legitimate admin vs. scanner behavior.

suggestion.title: Geographic Anomaly – Firewall Scanning Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker campaign; likely originating from unexpected geographies or known malicious ASNs. Pipeline failed to correlate scanning source IPs with threat intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Map scanning sources to ASN/geography using enriched threat intel. Alert on scanning traffic from high-risk jurisdictions or known bulletproof hosting ASNs. Baseline normal admin access patterns by geography; flag deviations >50 unique IPs from single ASN targeting firewall in <24h.

suggestion.title: Malicious Postinstall Script Execution from Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'postinstall script executes automatically without warnings' and 'postinstall hooks in package managers (PHP/Composer and Node.js).' Pipeline generated no detection for this initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager postinstall hook invocations (npm install, composer install) that spawn unexpected child processes or network connections. Alert on child process spawning from npm/composer with curl or wget commands, especially to external GitHub or suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Curl with Disabled Certificate Verification in Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'TLS verification disabled' and shows attack pattern 'curl -sk' for downloading payloads. This is a critical evasion signature the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 'curl' or 'wget' execution with `-k`, `--insecure`, or `-sk` flags, especially in contexts involving package installation scripts or GitHub URLs. Correlate with child processes spawned from npm/composer/pip/composer contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH-Like Filename Creation in /tmp
suggestion.rationale: Article describes binary 'written to `/tmp/.sshd` (mimicking SSH daemon file)' and 'SSH-like naming conventions blend into system processes.' This is the signature persistence mechanism—completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in `/tmp/` matching patterns `/.sshd`, `/.ssh*`, `/.systemd*` or other dot-prefixed names mimicking system daemons. Cross-reference creation timing with package manager execution. Alert if file is subsequently marked executable and executed in background.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Modification via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'GitHub Actions workflow files weaponized for CI/CD pipeline execution' and 'Dependency Name: dependency_cache_sync' as malicious workflow dependency. Pipeline failed to surface CI/CD threat surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to `.github/workflows/` files that introduce new dependencies, especially those with names matching system utilities (`*_sync`, `*_cache`, `*_helper`). Alert on commits that add workflow steps executing curl/wget with disabled verification or calling binaries from /tmp or non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Background Process Execution with Redirected Error Streams
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Error messages suppressed to avoid detection' and shows execution pattern `/tmp/.sshd &`. Pipeline missed the defense-evasion pattern of background execution with output redirection (>&/dev/null).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution patterns combining background spawning (`&`) with stderr/stdout redirection (`>&/dev/null` or `2>/dev/null`), especially from scripts or unusual parent processes. Flag `/tmp/.*` binaries being executed in background from postinstall or GitHub Actions contexts.

suggestion.title: Python Extension Module (.pyd) Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references '.pyd and .so Files'—.pyd is Windows Python extension format used to evade script detection. No use cases generated to detect this execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python.exe or pythonw.exe loading or executing .pyd files from non-standard directories (excluding %PYTHONHOME%). Alert on .pyd files written to Temp, AppData, or user home folders, or loaded by processes without parent relationships to Python installations.

suggestion.title: Shared Object (.so) Library Loading on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Title references '.so Files'—Linux shared objects used for the same purpose. Pipeline generated no Linux-specific detection despite explicit call-out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dlopen() / ld.so calls for .so files loaded from /tmp, /var/tmp, or user-writable locations. Flag processes loading .so libraries that lack source code indicators or come from unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: Script Detection Evasion via Binary Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle emphasizes 'Evade Script Detection.' Pipeline failed to surface defense-evasion use case despite this being core attack vector—using compiled binary extensions to bypass script analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python/node/ruby process spawning with subsequent .pyd/.so/.pyx/.so file creation or execution in the same session. Alert on archive extraction (zip, tar, 7z) containing extension modules followed by script interpreter invocation within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malware Family: InvisibleFerret
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name appears in title but was not extracted as actor/malware family indicator. No IOC enrichment or historical baseline established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index and baseline indicators of compromise associated with InvisibleFerret (C2 domains, file hashes, delivery URLs, author metadata). Flag arrivals of .pyd/.so files matching historical InvisibleFerret signatures or delivery mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Malware Distribution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Shipping both .pyd (Windows) and .so (Linux) indicates deliberate cross-platform campaign. Pipeline generated no IOCs or techniques for this distribution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for delivery infrastructure (domains, IPs, file servers) hosting both Windows and Linux variants of the same malware. Alert on multi-OS payload arrays in single download requests or repository manifests.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Click-Through to Malicious Installer Download
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'SEO Poisoning to Deliver' as attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface detection for the initial-access mechanism—users deceived into downloading fake installer via search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect search queries for legitimate tools (SQL Developer, MySQL Workbench, etc.) followed by clicks to suspicious/newly-registered domains hosting malware. Correlate with executable downloads from non-vendor sources and subsequent process execution from user temp/download folders.

suggestion.title: Execution of Fake SQL Developer Installer with Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article core payload: 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer'. Pipeline provided zero execution-phase detections despite installer execution being the direct attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of installer executables (setup.exe, installer.exe, sqldev*.exe) spawned from browser processes, Downloads folder, or temp locations. Alert on parent-child anomalies (installer spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32). Cross-reference file hash against known malicious installer signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process and Payload Execution Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware installer would unpack or inject payload post-execution. No post-installation behavioral detection suggested despite 'malware' explicitly in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-installation of SQL Developer, monitor for unexpected child processes (command interpreters, WMIC, script interpreters), process hollowing attempts using legitimate tool names, or immediate network outbound connections to C2 infrastructure from installer working directory.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication and Data Exfiltration from SQL Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Iranian APT delivering malware to SQL developers suggests data theft/espionage objective. No command-and-control or exfiltration detections generated despite high severity classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS traffic from hosts executing the fake installer for connections to Iranian ASN ranges, newly-registered domains, or known Iranian APT C2 IPs. Alert on non-standard ports, suspicious DNS queries (DGA patterns), or certificate pinning bypasses indicating C2 tunneling.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Database Accounts and System Context
suggestion.rationale: SQL Developer targets have database credentials and system access. Article targets developers but pipeline surfaced no credential-access detection for likely post-compromise objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized LSASS access, SAM registry reads, or in-memory credential dumping post-malware execution. Alert on anomalous database authentication attempts, credential manager access from installer process context, or unusual privileged token impersonation on SQL Developer workstations.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Process Hiding and Behavioral Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated Iranian APT malware would employ evasion. Pipeline's zero kill-chain output suggests no consideration of malware self-hiding, parent-spoofing, or code obfuscation typical of APT-grade threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process-name spoofing (fake SQL Developer process disguising malware), unsigned executables in system paths, or process injection into legitimate Windows services post-installation. Monitor for anomalous file system activity (hidden files, alternate data streams, write-to-startup folders).

suggestion.title: Kazuar Modular Plugin/Component Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'modular espionage ecosystem'—describes staged plugin loading architecture; pipeline generated zero execution-phase detection for component delivery or DLL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious DLL loads and script execution from temporary locations or AppData. Monitor for parent process anomalies (e.g., System or WinLogon launching PowerShell/rundll32) associated with modular payload staging.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Modular espionage ecosystem implies persistent C2 communication channel; no use case for beacon detection, DNS/HTTP callback patterns, or C2 staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for periodic outbound connections on non-standard ports with encoded payloads, abnormal DNS query patterns (high-frequency subdomains, unusual TLDs), or repeated connection attempts to dynamic infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Data Staging and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Espionage-focused malware implies collection and exfiltration workflows; pipeline missed all exfiltration-phase detection for sensitive data handling or transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large sequential file read operations on sensitive directories (Documents, Desktop, AppData) followed by network transmission. Watch for file staging in %TEMP% or archive creation preceding network activity.

suggestion.title: Kazuar Registry-based Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Modular ecosystem requires persistence mechanism across reboots; no persistence-phase detection generated for Run/RunOnce registry modification or scheduled task abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to HKLM/HKCU Run, RunOnce, and WMI event subscription registry hives. Monitor for Task Scheduler event log entries (4698, 4702) associated with suspicious process parents or paths.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload to LMS Root Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'BLUEBEAM Web Shell' deployment—pipeline ignored persistence mechanism. Should detect file writes matching known web shell signatures or suspicious .aspx/.php/.jsp files in web-accessible directories post-KnowledgeDeliver exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file creation in web application root directories (especially .aspx, .php, .jsp, .jspx extensions) following HTTP 401/403 errors or POST requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS upload endpoints. Correlate with parent process spawned from w3wp.exe or equivalent web server process.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies zero-day in KnowledgeDeliver LMS—no detection for exploitation patterns. Pipeline missed initial-access phase entirely. Should detect requests to known vulnerable endpoints or anomalous POST payloads targeting the LMS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests with unusual POST/PUT/PATCH patterns to KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints (courseware upload, plugin install, configuration endpoints). Detect payloads containing shell commands, encoded scripts, or suspicious file extensions. Baseline against legitimate administrative traffic.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware family BLUEBEAM named in title but no execution detection. Should flag outbound C2 communication from web shell or suspicious command execution spawned from web server context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by w3wp.exe or apache/nginx with command-line arguments indicating shell execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from web server process to non-whitelisted IP ranges. Alert on DNS queries for known BLUEBEAM C2 domains (if available from threat feeds).

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP POST to LMS File Upload Handlers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation → shell deployment, implying malicious file upload mechanism. No detection for suspicious POST requests to upload endpoints with potential polyglot/disguised executable payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS upload endpoints (course materials, user avatars, plugins) containing double extensions (.aspx.jpg, .php.txt), null bytes, or MIME type mismatches. Flag requests with Content-Length anomalies or encoded payloads (base64, hex) embedded in multipart form data.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via LMS Administrative Override
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation likely bypasses authentication/authorization. Pipeline should detect attempts to create administrative accounts or modify role/permission objects in KnowledgeDeliver post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver LMS application logs for creation of new administrative users, role elevation events, or modifications to permission tables outside normal change windows. Correlate with unauthenticated or non-administrative source IP addresses. Detect shadow admin accounts or privilege grants to system service accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL/Module Injection into KnowledgeDeliver Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence may involve process injection or module loading. Pipeline ignored potential process-level defense evasion or code injection mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious module loads or remote thread creation targeting KnowledgeDeliver application processes (w3wp.exe, java.exe, etc.). Alert on unsigned or revoked DLL/module injection. Detect image loads from unusual paths (temp directories, %APPDATA%, SMB shares). Monitor process handle creation patterns consistent with process hollowing or DLL hijacking.

suggestion.title: Lazarus RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Execution via Unpacking
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'memory-only RAT' — malware loaded and executed directly in process memory without disk artifacts. Pipeline missed detection opportunity for in-memory code injection/unpacking patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process relationships where legitimate system processes (e.g., lsass, svchost) execute unpacking routines in memory. Alert on processes lacking on-disk image files or showing VirtualAlloc → VirtualProtect → CreateRemoteThread chains.

suggestion.title: Lazarus RemotePE C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT implies C2 communication from injected process. Article implies active callback infrastructure but pipeline extracted zero network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate outbound connections from financial services and crypto firm hosts. Flag unexpected outbound HTTPS to uncommon destination ports or IP geolocation anomalies; correlate with process execution of unusual system binary as initiator.

suggestion.title: Crypto/Financial Sector Supply Chain or Email Compromise Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'financial and crypto firms' — suggests targeted initial access vector (phishing, supply chain compromise, or watering hole). Pipeline missed identifying likely delivery mechanism and sector-specific IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with suspicious attachments or links sent to finance/crypto staff during business hours from external or compromised internal senders. Correlate attachment execution with immediate child processes that spawn unsigned binaries or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Tooling YARA/Hash Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific malware 'RemotePE' — expected to include file hashes, C2 domains, or YARA signatures. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for endpoint detection and response (EDR) tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest RemotePE hash signatures and domain IOCs into YARA rules and hash blocklists. Alert on file write followed by process execution with matching hash or behavioral signatures (unpacking, API hooking).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting or Session Theft in Financial Operations
suggestion.rationale: RAT on financial/crypto firm suggests credential theft or lateral movement to high-value accounts. Article likely describes post-exploitation discovery/collection phases but pipeline captured zero.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or rare processes reading HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings (credential storage) or accessing Credential Manager APIs. Flag interactive logons from previously unknown IP addresses to admin accounts post-RAT execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GenAI API Session Activity Before Credential Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attacker 'used Jailbroken Gemini'—implies adversary exploited safety constraints to request credential exfiltration. Should detect unusual GenAI session patterns (repeated tool calls, unusual token counts, rapid-fire API requests in short window).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GenAI sessions with abnormal request patterns (high variance in prompt length, repeated identical completions, multi-turn conversations focused on credential handling) immediately preceding account compromise. Establish baseline API call frequency per user and alert on 3σ+ spikes within 15 minutes of compromised admin account activity.

suggestion.title: Admin Credential Access from Unexpected Geolocation or Device
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Steal Admin Credentials'—pipeline should detect lateral movement post-credential-theft. Expected detection: admin account logins from new IP, device, or geolocation inconsistent with historical baseline, especially from Russia-attributed IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After credential compromise via GenAI exfiltration, attacker logs in with stolen admin credentials from foreign IP/device. Alert on: (1) successful admin sign-in from country/region or ASN not in past 90 days; (2) sign-in immediately after unusual GenAI activity detected above; (3) sign-in followed within 5min by crypto-wallet API calls or cloud-storage access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Crypto Wallet API Access or Blockchain Transaction Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Drain Crypto Wallets'—requires detection of wallet access, API token use, or blockchain transactions from compromised admin account. Article does not detail wallet platform; likely includes exchanges or self-custody platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative or service account initiating wallet transfers or API calls to crypto platforms: monitor for (1) authentication to crypto exchange API using admin credentials from anomalous IP; (2) large/repeated withdrawals from institutional wallet in short timespan; (3) new registered API keys or webhooks in wallet/exchange account immediately after compromised admin login.

suggestion.title: GenAI Jailbreak Attempt with Credential Exfiltration Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Jailbroken Gemini'—pipeline should alert on prompts attempting to bypass safety policies and solicit credentials, secrets, or sensitive data. Phrase: 'Jailbroken Gemini to Steal Admin Credentials' establishes intent to circumvent model guardrails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GenAI platform (Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude) conversation logs for prompt-injection or jailbreak attempts coupled with requests for credentials, API keys, or PII. Flag conversations containing: (1) adversarial suffixes or role-play scenarios designed to bypass safety filters; (2) requests for 'admin passwords', 'API tokens', 'authentication details'; (3) meta-instructions to ignore previous safety guidelines—escalate if followed by successful credential exfiltration within same session.

suggestion.title: Email Phishing Delivery of Malicious GenAI Links or Jailbreak Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly detail initial compromise vector, but credential theft via 'jailbroken' GenAI implies either: (a) attacker has direct access to GenAI platform, or (b) attacker phished admin into using attacker-controlled GenAI instance. Should detect phishing emails with GenAI links or prompt-injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing: (1) shortened URLs or base64-encoded GenAI platform links pointing to attacker-controlled instances or modified Gemini/Claude endpoints; (2) attachments or inline payloads containing jailbreak prompts or proof-of-concepts; (3) social engineering lures claiming 'new GenAI features', 'beta access', or 'admin credential verification' directed at high-value targets (admin, finance, crypto operations).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Sweep or Rapid Transaction Chain After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Drain Crypto Wallets'—implies mass liquidation or chain of transfers to launder stolen funds. Detection should track abnormal transaction volumes and velocity from institutional/admin-controlled wallet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, attacker rapidly transfers crypto from institutional wallet to external addresses. Alert on: (1) outbound transactions from admin-controlled wallet totaling >X% of balance in <1 hour; (2) cascade of small transfers designed to evade threshold alerts; (3) transfers to known-suspicious or newly-registered wallet addresses; (4) recipient addresses linked to Russian or OFAC-sanctioned exchange infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Compromised Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Supply Chain Attack Spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—malicious packages on these registries are the delivery mechanism. Pipeline generated no detection for installation of poisoned dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager invocations (npm install, pip install, cargo install) followed by unsigned or newly-registered package names. Alert on installs of packages with typosquatted or lookalike names in high-value projects.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Installed Malware Package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Credential-Stealing Malware'—the core payload. Pipeline should detect exfiltration of credentials post-installation (browser passwords, API keys, environment variables).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-installation, detect suspicious process spawning that reads credential stores (%APPDATA%, ~/.ssh, browser password DBs), or environment variable enumeration followed by HTTP POST to unexpected external domains.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Package Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing payload must exfiltrate data. Article does not name C2 infrastructure, but supply-chain malware typically phones home post-install. Pipeline missed command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS queries from process trees spawned by package manager, especially to newly-registered or recently-active domains with low reputation scores or non-standard TLDs.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Lookalike Package Name in Registry
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks commonly use name confusion (e.g., 'react-dom' vs 'react_dom'). Article mentions malware 'spreads via' registries but doesn't detail package names—pipeline should flag known typosquat IOCs if available.
log_sources: logs from npm API / PyPI logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package.json / requirements.txt / Cargo.toml dependencies against a registry of known-lookalike names. Alert on installs of packages with edit distance ≤2 from popular packages, or packages registered by unvetted authors shortly before compromise announcement.

suggestion.title: Malware Signature Detection in Downloaded Package Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'spreads'—should trigger file-based IOC matching (hashes, YARA signatures). Pipeline provided zero IOCs, so no signature-matching use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package cache directories (~/.npm, ~/.cache/pip, ~/.cargo) for files matching known malware hashes or YARA rules. Correlate with package manager process execution to detect installation of signed/unvetted code.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll'—a critical RDP system DLL. Any unauthorized modification to this file is highly suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write/modify events to termsrv.dll in System32. Legitimate updates arrive through Windows Update with valid signatures. Unauthorized modifications (unsigned, hash mismatch against known Windows versions, unexpected file sizes) indicate tampering to bypass RDP session limits.

suggestion.title: RDP MaxInstanceCount Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Enabling multiple concurrent RDP sessions requires modifying HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp\MaxInstanceCount. This is the explicit objective: 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to RDP session-limit registry keys (MaxInstanceCount, MaxIdleTime). Legitimate admins use Group Policy; attackers execute via cmd/PowerShell post-compromise. Baseline admin changes and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Concurrent RDP Session Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Once termsrv.dll is modified, adversaries exploit multiple RDP sessions for persistent lateral movement. Article title explicitly states 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-host baseline for concurrent RDP session counts (typically 1 for servers, 0-1 for workstations). Alert on anomalous increases or parallel sessions from unexpected users/IPs, especially correlated with termsrv.dll tampering.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL Load in RDP Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Modified termsrv.dll injection or sideload into svchost (RDP service) will show as unexpected DLL loads or IAT hooks within the RDP service process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor svchost.exe (TermService context) for unsigned or unexpected DLL loads from non-standard paths. Flag loads that violate Windows/SxS manifests. Correlate with termsrv.dll file tampering or RDP registry modifications.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Mismatched System DLL Execution
suggestion.rationale: termsrv.dll is Microsoft-signed. Modified versions carry invalid signatures or hashes mismatched against known Windows builds—direct indicator of DLL tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of critical RDP DLLs (termsrv.dll, tdisrv.dll, rdpcore.dll) with missing, revoked, or invalid code signatures, or file hashes mismatched against official Windows builds. High-confidence indicator of DLL tampering.

suggestion.title: RDP Service Restart Correlated with DLL Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Adversary must restart TermService to load modified termsrv.dll. Sequence of DLL modification + service restart = persistence installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file modifications to System32\termsrv.dll with subsequent TermService restarts. Legitimate restarts have admin context and occur during maintenance windows; flag sequences where unsigned/modified DLL precedes service restart.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Grant from Unusual Client or Location
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'abuses Microsoft's legitimate OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization grant flow' and 'Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Pipeline missed the detection of device code flow origination and token issuance anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code authentication grants (AAD audit event 'Initiate device authorization request') where the subsequent token redemption occurs from a different IP, geography, or client application than the device code was retrieved from. Particularly flag grants followed by immediate token use for bulk email access or folder enumeration.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation Following Suspicious Token-Based Login
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hackers...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Pipeline failed to connect OAuth-compromised sessions to subsequent mailbox manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation (New-InboxRule, Set-InboxRule) within 6 hours of a device code authentication approval or non-interactive login from unusual location. Flag rules that forward, delete, or move emails to secondary folders, particularly those masking high-risk keywords (password reset, verification, MFA, sign-in).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Registration in Azure/Entra Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Pipeline did not generate persistence detection for unauthorized device enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new Intune/Azure device enrollments (RegisteredDevice, EnrollmentProfile events) within 24 hours of a device code OAuth grant approval, especially without prior Windows Autopilot registration. Flag high-risk device types (unmanaged, mobile, virtual) registered by accounts with recent token-based authentication from unfamiliar locations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mailbox Delegation or Forwarding Post-Device-Code Auth
suggestion.rationale: Kali365's attack chain grants 'full access to their mailboxes' where attackers 'created malicious inbox rules' and later exfiltrate data. Delegation/forwarding rules are a primary persistence and collection mechanism not addressed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mailbox delegation changes (Add-MailboxPermission, Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfOf) and forwarding rules (Set-Mailbox -DeliverToMailboxAndForward, New-InboxRule with ForwardTo) within 12 hours of device code OAuth grant. Prioritize rules forwarding to external domains or newly-created distribution lists.

suggestion.title: Session Capture via Transparent Proxy / Adversary-in-the-Middle (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365's 'Cookie Link' mode: 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' This AitM pattern was not translated to detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful Azure AD/Office 365 logins followed immediately by unusual Certificate Authority (self-signed certs in proxy logs) or SSL/TLS renegotiation patterns. Correlate gateway logs showing HTTPS interception, unusual redirect chains before login completion, and authentication success despite proxy timeouts or session breaks.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Targeting Device Code Portal (microsoft.com/devicelogin)
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaigns 'primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, http://microsoft.com/devicelogin.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for phishing lure distribution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links or instructions directing to 'microsoft.com/devicelogin' or 'devicelogin.microsoftonline.com' especially if redirects through shortened URLs, encoded parameters, or attacker-controlled infrastructure. Cross-correlate recipients with subsequent device code OAuth approval events within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'CVE-2026-26980 Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites'. This is the vector initiating the entire attack chain and must be detectable at the moment of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PATCH requests to Ghost API endpoints (/ghost/api/*, /admin/api/*) with suspicious payloads, encoding evasion, or template injection patterns. Flag requests to Ghost installations from IPs not in baseline administrative ranges, especially with 40x responses immediately followed by 20x (indicating successful exploitation).

suggestion.title: Ghost Template/Theme File Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites were 'hijacked'—implies persistent malicious modification. Attackers must alter Handlebars templates to inject ClickFix payloads into rendered pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to Ghost theme files (*.hbs in /content/themes/) outside change-control windows. Monitor Ghost database for unexpected INSERT/UPDATE operations on the 'settings' table and 'mobiledoc' columns (where post/page content is stored). Detect inline script injection patterns in post_html field modifications.

suggestion.title: Injected Malicious JavaScript in Served Pages
suggestion.rationale: 700+ hijacked sites serving 'ClickFix Attacks' to users—ClickFix is a social engineering pop-up overlay. Malicious JavaScript must be injected into page responses to render the fake alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP responses from Ghost-hosted sites for inline <script> tags with obfuscated payloads, DOM manipulation targeting modal elements, or event listeners not in baseline. Flag responses with injected overlay divs, credential capture forms, or event handlers triggering external AJAX calls. Correlate with CSP violations on affected domains.

suggestion.title: Ghost Admin Account Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to gain RCE, attackers require persistent administrative access. Article's sustained hijacking of 700+ sites implies backdoor accounts were created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new user records in Ghost's 'users' table created during or immediately after CVE-2026-26980 exploitation attempts. Flag accounts with email addresses not matching expected organizational patterns, accounts created with elevated role (Owner/Editor) outside change windows, or multiple account creations from the same session.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DNS/Outbound Connections from Hijacked Ghost Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates ClickFix attacks—these typically exfiltrate credentials or fetch malware. Compromised sites must communicate with attacker C2 or credential-harvesting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS from Ghost server IPs (known from web hosting logs) for queries to attacker-controlled domains or uncommon TLDs not in baseline. Flag proxy logs showing POST requests from hijacked site IPs to credential-harvesting endpoints, data aggregators, or known malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate with ClickFix IOC feeds.

suggestion.title: Ghost Database Credential Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Persistent hijacking of 700+ sites likely requires attackers to harvest Ghost database credentials (API keys, hashed passwords) for lateral movement and long-term access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected SELECTs from Ghost 'users', 'api_keys', or 'settings' tables during exploitation windows. Monitor read access to Ghost config files (config.production.json) containing database credentials. Flag database backups accessed from non-administrative sessions immediately after CVE-2026-26980 exploitation detection.

suggestion.title: Shared CDN IP Infrastructure Abuse for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Abuse Shared CDN Infrastructure' establishes attackers are leveraging legitimate CDN networks for command and control or payload staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to shared CDN ASNs and IP ranges with command-and-control indicators (unusual ports, high-entropy encrypted tunneling, periodic heartbeat patterns). Cross-reference against known CDN operator ranges to isolate traffic deviating from normal content-delivery patterns.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Masquerading via CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls'—attackers inherit trust by hosting malicious content through shared CDN infrastructure, evading traditional domain-reputation blocklists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing or malware delivery originating from CDN IP ranges with high domain-reputation scores. Alert on payload detonation, credential form submission, or malware staging hosted on trusted CDN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Rapid Domain Registration on Compromised CDN Edge Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern implies registering many disposable domains pointing to shared CDN infrastructure to distribute phishing or payloads while bypassing reputation filtering. Article implies infrastructure compromise enabling this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly registered domains resolving to shared CDN infrastructure within 24–48 hours of registration. Correlate DNS resolution with HTTP User-Agent anomalies, certificate transparency logs, and WHOIS registrant metadata to identify bulk registration campaigns.

suggestion.title: SSH-Like Filename Creation During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'payload hidden under SSH-like filename during package installation.' Detection should surface files with SSH nomenclature (ssh, ssh.pub, authorized_keys, sshd, ssh-keygen variants) appearing in unexpected locations during apt/yum/dnf/rpm transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager processes (apt, rpm, yum, dpkg) and their child processes for unexpected file creation with SSH-related filenames. Alert on creation of files matching *(ssh|sshd|authorized_keys|ssh-keygen)* in non-standard SSH directories (/root/.ssh, /home/*/.ssh, /etc/ssh) during active package installation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Binary Execution Triggered by Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via packages typically execute hidden payloads during install phases via post-install scripts. Article describes 'payload' and 'installation,' implying code execution component absent from detection content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by package managers (apt, rpm, yum, dpkg) with unexpected parent-child relationships, unusual binary names, or execution from temporary/cache directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, package staging directories). Focus on shells, curl, wget, Python, Perl invoked without legitimate post-install script context.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Repository Evasion Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'hackers' and 'package installation'—implies compromised repository or malicious package upload. Pipeline should surface IOCs around package names, versions, repository signatures, or installer hashes for correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package manager queries to non-standard repositories, package installations with missing or invalid signatures, and downloads of package files with obfuscated or suspicious naming patterns. Correlate with known vulnerable/compromised package metadata.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Executable in System Binary Directory Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Hidden payload under 'SSH-like filename' suggests masquerading. Pipeline should detect files installed into /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /bin, /sbin that imitate SSH utilities but have non-standard properties (size, inode age, signature mismatch).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation in system binary directories matching SSH utility patterns during package transactions. Cross-reference against legitimate SSH binary hashes/signatures. Alert on execution of binary-named SSH utilities with unexpected parent processes or resource consumption.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .pyd/.so Binary Loaded by Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'ships as .pyd and .so files' to evade detection. No use case was generated to alert on unexpected binary extensions being loaded by Python interpreters or installed in non-standard library paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes (python.exe, python3) that load .pyd or .so files from user-writable directories, temp folders, or AppData. Baseline expected library paths and alert on deviations. Cross-reference file hashes against InvisibleFerret malware signatures.

suggestion.title: InvisibleFerret Malware Family Hash Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'InvisibleFerret' as a specific malware variant now distributed in binary form. No hash-based IOCs or file reputation lookups were suggested despite this being the primary identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain hash repository of known InvisibleFerret .pyd and .so samples. Alert on process execution or file creation events matching these hashes. Implement file signing validation to detect unsigned or revoked binaries masquerading as legitimate Python extensions.

suggestion.title: Binary Substitution for Script Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core technique: 'evade script detection' by shipping as compiled binaries instead. No detection UC addresses the behavioral pivot from script execution to binary extension loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile Python process behavior: sudden shift from script-based activity (importlib, ast module calls, code introspection) to direct binary/extension loading without corresponding legitimate library updates. Alert on anomalous ctypes/cffi usage to invoke compiled code.

suggestion.title: Script-to-Binary Conversion Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies conversion of script-based payloads into .pyd/.so form. No detection for build/compilation artifacts, Cython/pyinstaller/nuitka execution, or obfuscation tool invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of build tools (cython, py2exe, pyinstaller, nuitka) with suspicious output paths or naming conventions. Flag C compiler invocation (.cc, .cpp, clang, cl.exe) in contexts adjacent to Python source directories. Alert on temporary build artifacts in %APPDATA% or /tmp.

suggestion.title: Python Environment Discovery for Targeted Deployment
