suggestion.title: AI Model Jailbreak and Prompt Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article opens with 'jailbroken Gemini' as the primary attack vector: pipeline captured zero detections for prompt injection, model jailbreaking, or AI model abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI model API requests for injection patterns, system-prompt override attempts, role-play directives, or requests designed to generate restricted code (credential scrapers, wallet exploits). Baseline legitimate developer queries; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Admin Credential Exfiltration Post-AI Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'steal admin credentials' but pipeline generated zero credential-access detections: missing correlation between AI model interaction and subsequent credential access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin account login anomalies (unusual IPs, timing, MFA bypass) occurring within hours of jailbroken-AI API activity. Monitor for bulk credential exports, PAM access, or password manager queries from systems showing AI-abuse footprints.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Unauthorized Drain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly includes 'drain crypto wallets' as final impact, but zero use cases capture blockchain/wallet anomalies: missing exfiltration-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cryptocurrency transfers from compromised org wallets to unknown addresses, especially rapid liquidations or transfers to high-risk exchanges. Correlate with admin credential compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Malicious Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Jailbroken Gemini was used to steal credentials, implying code generation for credential harvesting: pipeline did not detect AI-assisted malware development or code-generation techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate AI model requests that generate executable payloads (Python credential scrapers, shell scripts, wallet interactions) with subsequent process execution on internal systems. Flag requests asking AI to generate 'credential theft,' 'wallet export,' or 'admin access' code.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Installation from Untrusted Checksum
suggestion.rationale: Article states credential-stealing malware spreads via npm, PyPI, CratesIO. Pipeline generated zero initial-access detections. Phrase: 'credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, pip install, cargo fetch for checksum mismatches, unsigned packages, or versions pulling from non-standard registries. Alert on package.json/requirements.txt modifications adding typosquatted or unusual dependencies in development/production builds.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Spawning Credential Harvesting Process
suggestion.rationale: Malware is explicitly credential-stealing. No T1555/T1056 detections generated for credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/pip/cargo child processes that read SSH keys, AWS credentials, .docker/config.json, git config, or environment variables (AWS_SECRET, GCP_CREDENTIALS). Correlate package install events with outbound connections to non-package-registry IPs within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution During Package Build
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware uses install hooks to execute code. Title says malware spreads via package managers—requires T1059 detection for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell spawned from package install (npm run, python setup.py, cargo build) with base64/hex-encoded arguments, eval, or exec calls. Alert on Node.js child processes with —allow-native-modules or —no-warnings flags during non-interactive CI/CD contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress Immediately Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing payload must exfiltrate. No command-and-control or exfiltration detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP from package install process to external IP ranges (non-CDN, non-package-repo). Flag connections to known credential broker domains, file-sharing services (pastebin, telegram, webhook), or C2 infrastructure within 10 minutes of npm/pip/cargo execution.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Tree Injection of Malicious Transitive Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often hide malware in transitive dependencies. No persistence or supply-chain-specific technique mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package lock files (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, Cargo.lock) for new transitive dependencies not declared in manifest. Alert when package manager downloads significantly more packages than declared. Track .git/config modifications to point to attacker-controlled forks.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Execution of Malicious Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often target automated build systems. No CI/CD-specific detection for supply chain abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected network calls or process spawning during CI/CD pipeline execution of package install steps. Correlate GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins build logs with outbound credential exfiltration or command-and-control callbacks.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Process RCE - Unexpected Child Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Execute Arbitrary Code'—code execution within 7-Zip context must spawn detectable child processes distinct from normal archive operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 7z.exe or 7zG.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or system utilities (wmic, reg, certutil, taskkill) without explicit user shell request. Flag extractions to temp/downloads followed by child process creation within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'New' vulnerabilities requiring patch remediation. Absence of version-tracking UCs leaves enterprises blind to deployment risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate 7-Zip binary versions (7z.exe file properties, registry HKCU/HKLM paths). Cross-reference detected versions against disclosed CVE fix dates. Report machines with vulnerable pre-patch versions.

suggestion.title: Archive Extraction - Forbidden Payload Types
suggestion.rationale: RCE via archive implies vulnerability in extraction or payload handling. Detections must distinguish normal archive ops from embedded exploit scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 7-Zip extraction to user-writable paths for execution artifacts (.exe, .dll, .vbs, .ps1, .scr). Baseline known-good extraction targets and alert on new paths. Correlate file-write events with process creation from extraction directory.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Cloud Atlas 'Modifies termsrv.dll'—the primary attack mechanism. This is a forensically detectable file-system artifact and should be detectable via hash mismatch or write-event monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to System32\termsrv.dll or hash deviations from baseline (obtained from clean Windows install images). Legitimate modifications only during patch deployment; alert on any process attempting to overwrite this critical RDP driver.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification Enabling Multiple RDP Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions'—this requires modification of HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\fSingleSessionPerUser (set to 0). Baseline behavior: locked at 1 (single session per user).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry value changes to fSingleSessionPerUser or Terminal Server\Licensing registry paths. Correlate with termsrv.dll modifications. Multiple concurrent sessions on same host is abnormal outside shared RDP farm environments.

suggestion.title: RDP Service Restart Following Payload Modification
suggestion.rationale: Modifying termsrv.dll requires service restart to load the modified driver. Detect correlation: file write to System32\termsrv.dll followed by RDP service stop/start within 5-minute window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Sysmon file-write events to termsrv.dll with taskkill.exe /IM svchost.exe or net stop termservice commands. Alert on RDP service restart initiated outside scheduled maintenance windows or deployment tools.

suggestion.title: Multiple Concurrent RDP Session Detection
suggestion.rationale: Post-modification, attacker gains ability to hold multiple interactive RDP sessions simultaneously—a lateral-movement advantage. Standard Windows policy allows 1 concurrent session per user; detect violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple simultaneous RDP logons (event ID 4624 type 10) to same target within short window. Alert if >1 user from same source IP or if concurrent RDP sessions exceed baseline for that host.

suggestion.title: Cloud Atlas C2 or Infrastructure Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes attacks to Cloud Atlas (aliases: MicroBanda, Karba). Threat intelligence should include known C2 IPs, domains, or ASNs associated with the group for network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Cloud Atlas infrastructure indicators from public OSINT (e.g., Shodan, DNS passive data, VirusTotal submissions). Alert on traffic to known Cloud Atlas C2 or hosting ASNs. Useful for retroactive hunting if termsrv.dll modification detected with no clear attacker source.

suggestion.title: Rapid Fintech Account Creation with Immediate Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article states criminals sell 'verified bank and fintech mule accounts,' implying batch creation and accelerated verification—operational prerequisite to inventory available for Telegram sale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag patterns: single IP/device creates 3+ accounts at same financial institution within 24 hours, followed by successful identity verification and account activation. Correlate with VPN/datacenter IP ranges and off-hours activity.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing or Phishing Against Bank/Fintech Platforms
suggestion.rationale: For accounts to be 'verified' and marketable, criminals must first compromise legitimate user credentials—phishing, credential stuffing, password spray, or insider theft are the only feasible paths to 'verified' status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for: failed login surges (10+) to financial institution accounts from datacenter/VPN IPs within hours, followed by successful login from same IP. Detect rapid testing of credential pairs (credential stuffing signature). Flag logins immediately post-phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Account Access to Telegram APIs from Financial Service IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Telegram as sales infrastructure; actors must access these channels to list/manage accounts or coordinate with buyers—observable as API calls or web access from compromised financial accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: outbound HTTPS connections from financial service authentication IPs to api.telegram.org or web.telegram.org, DNS queries for telegram.org originating from bank/fintech corporate networks, or rapid connection cycling to Telegram infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Multi-Account Takeover from Shared Command Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Mule account networks require centralized access; actors log into multiple distinct bank/fintech accounts from shared C2 or proxy infrastructure—detectable as temporal clustering of logins across unrelated accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful logins to 5+ distinct customer accounts at same financial institution from single IP/user agent within 2-hour window. Flag if logins occur outside business hours, from datacenter IPs, or precede unusual transaction activity by <30 min.

suggestion.title: Money Movement from Compromised Mule Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Mule accounts exist solely for money laundering; unusual transaction patterns (high velocity, new recipients, offshore transfers) distinct from legitimate user history indicate active abuse and layering phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: 3+ transfers from single account within 6 hours post-compromise, transfers to new/high-risk jurisdictions within 24h of account takeover, round-trip transfers (A→B→C→A within days), or transfer amounts in consistent increments (layering signature).

suggestion.title: Settings/Security Changes on Compromised Financial Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attackers securing stolen accounts immediately disable 2FA, change recovery email, alter phone numbers—observable account administration changes distinguish account takeover from legitimate user activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag within 30min of login: password change, 2FA removal/reset, recovery email substitution, or phone number modification on financial service accounts. Correlate with login from unusual geography/time.

suggestion.title: Device Code Redemption from Anomalous Geo or ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'generate a code, then trick targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page via phishing' — attacker-controlled device code redemption from foreign IP/ASN is high-signal indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code auth redemptions where IP geolocation is >500km from user's baseline, or ASN is non-corporate. Cross-correlate device code login timestamp with prior 24h MFA-satisfied logins from different geography. Flag if redemption IP does not match any user device IP from past 90 days.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation Within 15min of Device Code Token Redemption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states compromised accounts: 'created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity' — temporal correlation between OAuth device code token issuance and rule creation is definitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert CreateInboxRule or UpdateInboxRule events occurring ≤15 minutes after device_code_auth success. Flag rules with ForwardTo external domain, DeleteExistingRules=true, or conditions matching high-volume phishing patterns (from:* HasAttachments:true).

suggestion.title: Device Registration in Entra Post-Device Code Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network' — persistence indicator post-token compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device registration (Add-RegisteredDevice, RegisterDevice) initiated via OAuth tokens generated through device code flow within 1 hour prior. Alert if registering device name matches known IoT/printers (common device code targets per article).

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle via Cookie Link Proxy Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365 'Cookie Link' mode: 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing email URLs redirecting to attacker-controlled proxy domains mimicking microsoft.com/devicelogin. Correlate email click events with HTTPS requests to proxy infrastructure. Flag if same victims receive phishing email AND subsequent cookie/token exfil from proxy IP.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Usage from Attacker Location Post-Device Code Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges' — token usage from attacker infrastructure without re-authentication is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert OAuth refresh/access token usage originating from IP distinct from device code redemption location. Monitor for high-risk app access (Exchange, Teams, SharePoint) using device code-derived tokens. Flag token claims for device_code grant_type + app_id inconsistent with user's 90-day baseline.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Directing to Device Login Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365 initial vector: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or homoglyph variants (microsof.com, microsoft.co.uk). Cross-correlate email body social engineering pretext (account verification, security alert) with click-through → device code auth within 30 minutes. Flag if recipients are O365 users without prior Kali365 campaign exposure.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Ghost CMS vulnerability being actively exploited; pipeline extracted zero indicators or techniques. Must detect exploitation of CVE-2026-26980 at initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin endpoints (/ghost/api/admin/*) for authentication bypass payloads, version enumeration attempts, and HTTP requests containing known CVE-2026-26980 exploit signatures. Alert on POST/PUT requests with malformed JSON or parameter injection targeting Ghost API endpoints from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Admin Account Creation in Ghost CMS
suggestion.rationale: Site hijacking of 700+ instances requires persistence; pipeline mapped zero persistence techniques. Typical post-exploitation step is unauthorized privileged account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to Ghost /users endpoint creating new accounts with 'administrator' role immediately following successful CVE exploitation. Flag creation of admin accounts outside business hours or from anomalous source IPs with no prior legitimate admin activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Ghost Theme or Content Injection
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix attacks inject malicious redirects or ad-serving scripts into hijacked sites; article describes sites 'hijacked for ClickFix attacks' but pipeline produced zero impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost theme directories and post/page templates for unauthorized modifications post-exploitation. Alert on HTML/CSS/JS injection patterns, obfuscated scripts, or references to external ad-fraud/click-monetization domains. Flag unexpected <script> tags or document.location manipulations in static content.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Traffic and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix is explicitly named as the attack payload in the article title; pipeline extracted zero malware family IOCs or command-and-control indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised Ghost servers for outbound connections to known ClickFix infrastructure, ad-fraud networks, or click-monetization platforms. Alert on DNS queries from web servers to domains associated with ClickFix distribution or malicious ad networks; correlate with compromised site detection.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Web Shell Upload or Plugin Injection
suggestion.rationale: Ghost CMS extensibility via plugins/themes is probable post-exploitation persistence vector; pipeline produced zero execution or persistence techniques specific to CMS-based compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized Ghost plugin uploads or modifications to core plugin files post-exploitation. Monitor Ghost content-api calls attempting to install packages from untrusted sources. Alert on unexpected Node.js child process execution or file writes to Ghost plugin directories triggered by HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Anomalous encrypted traffic to shared CDN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Shared CDN Infrastructure'—pipeline missed the core detection vector. Attackers abuse legitimate CDNs (Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS CloudFront) to blend malicious traffic with benign requests. Need to detect when CDN traffic deviates from baseline patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical CDN traffic (volume, frequency, target destinations) per user/host. Alert on encrypted HTTPS connections to major shared CDNs exhibiting atypical patterns: sustained high-frequency C2-like beaconing, off-hours activity, or connections from hosts that rarely contact CDNs. Correlate with proxy decryption logs for payload inspection.

suggestion.title: Domain reputation bypass via CDN-hosted subdomains
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls'—pipeline failed to model the evasion technique of hosting payloads on CDN subdomains that inherit parent-domain trust scores. This is the primary attack vector described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS resolutions to atypical subdomains under major CDN provider zones (*.cloudflare.net, *.akamai.com). Cross-reference against known C2 IOCs and compare resolved IPs to legitimate CDN customer ranges. Alert when domain reputation checks are bypassed due to wildcard-certificate or parent-domain trust inheritance.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance DNS queries to CDN provider zones
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must discover and enumerate CDN provider infrastructure before exploiting it. Pipeline did not flag DNS reconnaissance as an initial-access signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or clustered DNS queries from internal hosts to shared CDN provider domains (queries to *.cloudflare.com, *.akamai.net, etc.). Distinguish from legitimate CDN customer lookups by alerting on queries to provider infrastructure zones rather than customer-specific subdomains.

suggestion.title: Certificate-based trust abuse via wildcard CDN SSL certificates
suggestion.rationale: Shared CDNs issue wildcard certificates; attackers exploit this to serve malicious content over HTTPS with inherited certificate legitimacy. Pipeline missed certificate-chain evasion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect TLS certificates from connections to CDN IP ranges. Alert when certificate subject is a wildcard (*.cdn-provider.com) but the requested domain differs significantly, or when certificate pinning/HPKP checks are bypassed. Correlate cert usage with known-malicious payload delivery signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Linux Payload' executing 'During Package Installation'—baseline package manager child processes and alert on unexpected shells, downloads, or network calls spawned from apt/yum/dpkg parent processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unexpected child process spawning from package managers or installation script interpreters. Flag bash/sh/python executed by apt, yum, dpkg, or dpkg postinst scripts. Baseline per environment; correlate with network connections or file writes to suspicious directories.

suggestion.title: SSH-Like Filename Masquerading in Non-Standard Locations
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is hiding payload 'Under SSH-Like Filename'—need detection for files named to impersonate SSH binaries (ssh, sshd, ssh-keygen, ssh_config, authorized_keys) or agent sockets created outside legitimate SSH directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation events matching SSH-related patterns (/ssh.*, /sshd, /ssh_config, /authorized_keys) outside /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /etc/ssh, /root/.ssh. Verify against package manifest; flag unexpected ownership, permissions, or embedded ELF headers.

suggestion.title: Package Installation Supply Chain Compromise IOC Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector during 'Package Installation'—pipeline should extract package names, versions, hashes, and installation command anomalies as IOCs; failing to do so is a critical gap for threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation events (apt history, yum logs, pip logs) with post-install file writes to /tmp, /var/tmp, hidden directories, or system paths; spike in network activity; child process execution. Baseline expected installer behavior per package; alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Hidden Payload Extraction and Execution from Temp/Cache Directories
suggestion.rationale: Payload is delivered during package installation—likely decompressed to /tmp or /var/cache—detection must catch file writes and execution from package-related temporary paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation followed by execution in /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/cache/apt, or similar directories. Flag executables created in cache with SSH-like names. Cross-reference with package installation timestamps; alert on orphaned processes post-install cleanup.

suggestion.title: System Utility Name Collision Detection (SSH Binary Impersonation)
suggestion.rationale: Filename obfuscation targeting SSH specifically suggests attacker aims to intercept SSH sessions or keys—detection should flag SSH-named files that hash/signature mismatch against legitimate package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain baseline hashes of all SSH-related binaries from legitimate packages. Alert on file creation matching SSH patterns where hash does not match baseline. Correlate with package version mismatch in package manager database; flag unsigned or repo-unsigned executables.

suggestion.title: Python Compiled Module (.pyd) Loading from Suspicious Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states malware 'ships as .pyd files' to evade script detection. This is the primary distribution mechanism; pipeline extracted zero execution-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on python.exe or python3 process loading .pyd modules from non-standard paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%, user home, UNC paths). Flag .pyd file creation immediately preceding Python process execution. Require valid publisher signature on .pyd files, alert on unsigned or unsigned-by-Microsoft variants.

suggestion.title: Linux Shared Object (.so) Module Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names .so files as InvisibleFerret's Linux evasion variant. Zero Linux-specific detection use cases generated despite clear platform attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .so file creation in /tmp, /var/tmp, or user home directories followed by dlopen() or LD_PRELOAD injection. Alert on ld.so activity loading .so modules unsigned or with timestamps misaligned to system package managers. Track mmap PROT_EXEC + PROT_WRITE on .so-backed memory regions.

suggestion.title: Compiled Binary Evasion Pattern (Script to Compiled Format)
suggestion.rationale: Article states goal: 'evade script detection.' This is core defense-evasion tactic. Kill-chain phase entirely absent from pipeline output—no defense_evasion phase reconstructed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of compiled binaries (.pyd, .so, .exe, .dll) with filename or archive metadata suggesting script-to-binary repackaging (script names, Python module conventions). Flag .pyd/.so delivery via email attachment or archive without legitimate publisher provenance. Correlate compilation timestamps with known malware build dates.

suggestion.title: InvisibleFerret Post-Load Behavioral Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Malware family explicitly named in title; no command-control or exfiltration detections generated. Post-execution activities of stager malware must be characterized once .pyd/.so module loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish network behavior baseline of Python interpreter after loading InvisibleFerret .pyd/.so modules: beaconing intervals, C2 port ranges, domain reputation. Monitor for child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash) originating from Python context post-module-load. Detect lateral-movement or credential-access primitives attributed to InvisibleFerret via code signatures or behavioral heuristics.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Domain + Installer Download Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'SEO Poisoning to Deliver Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer'—attacker injects malicious domains into search rankings, users click through, and download fake installer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of executable files claiming to be SQL Server setup from newly registered or spoofed domains (e.g., sql-developer[.]io, sqlserverdl[.]net) that rank in search results. Cross-reference file names/hashes against Microsoft's legitimate SQL Server distribution infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Installer Execution with Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer' execution. Installer spawn patterns will reveal malware behavior post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sqlserver setup.exe or installer-named binaries spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unexpected network connections. Establish baseline of legitimate SQL installer behavior (normal child processes, expected registry writes) and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Authenticode Verification: Unsigned or Forged SQL Installer
suggestion.rationale: Attackers mask malware as legitimate SQL Server installer. File signature verification will distinguish authentic Microsoft builds from masqueraded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for .exe files with 'SQL' in name or metadata but lacking valid Microsoft digital signature, or signed by non-Microsoft publisher. Alert on self-signed or outdated Authenticode timestamps.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration Pattern: SQL Keyword Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: SEO poisoning requires attacker-controlled domains to rank for 'SQL Server download' searches. Newly registered permutations and typosquats of legitimate software domains are detectable via DNS/WHOIS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for domains registered in last 30–90 days containing 'sql', 'server', 'developer', 'download' keywords alongside suspicious hosting or fast-flux behavior. Correlate registration ASNs/registrars with known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Command Execution (C2 Beacon)
suggestion.rationale: After installer runs, malware beacons to C2 or spawns interactive shells. Command execution from installer context will precede lateral movement or data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or cmd.exe spawned as child of SQL setup process followed by outbound connections to non-SQL-infrastructure IPs, file I/O to suspicious registries (persistence), or credential enumeration activity.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Baseline: Known SQL Installer Variants
suggestion.rationale: Once fake SQL installers are isolated, hash signatures become definitive detections for reuse across targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain catalog of known malicious SQL setup.exe / installer variants (MD5, SHA1, SHA256). Alert on any file execution matching these hashes, or on cryptographic similarity (SSDEEP/fuzzy hash) to known samples.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Shell Upload to LMS Document Root
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Deploy BLUEBEAM Web Shell'—web shell placement in accessible directories is the attack completion. No detection generated for this core payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file creation (*.php, *.aspx, *.jsp) in common LMS web-accessible paths (/uploads, /media, /public). Correlate with prior exploitation attempts. Web shells typically have small file size, embedded base64, or eval/exec functions.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Exploitation Attempt (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Zero-Day Exploited' in KnowledgeDeliver LMS. No detection crafted for exploitation of this public-facing application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints for injection patterns, null-byte sequences, directory traversal attempts, or unusual POST bodies. Baseline legitimate administrative paths and alert on suspicious parameter manipulation.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is explicitly named 'BLUEBEAM Web Shell.' No detection for command execution patterns or C2 beaconing from this malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution spawned from w3wp.exe or apache2 processes with suspicious command patterns (powershell -enc, cmd /c). Monitor HTTP request parameters for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `). Track outbound connections from web server processes to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: LMS Account Privilege Escalation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Web shell foothold typically leads to lateral movement and privilege escalation within the LMS. Article does not describe follow-on activity, but detection gap exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation after web shell placement: token impersonation, DLL injection into SYSTEM processes, or anomalous permission changes to LMS admin accounts. Correlate with prior web shell file creation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Connection from LMS Web Server
suggestion.rationale: BLUEBEAM likely establishes C2 communication (implied by 'Web Shell' functionality). Article mentions deployment but no detection for command-and-control beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound HTTPS/HTTP destinations from LMS server. Alert on new connections to non-educational, non-corporate ASNs, especially if to bulletproof hosters or known C2 infrastructure. Monitor DNS queries from web process for typosquatting or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Malware Signature - File Hash or Behavioral IOC Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'BLUEBEAM' as the deployed malware. No IOC hashes, domains, or behavioral signatures extracted for blocking or hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain BLUEBEAM hash repository (from threat intelligence feeds) and alert on file creation/execution matches. Monitor for behavioral IOCs: specific registry keys written by web shells, DLL injection patterns, or embedded user-agent strings specific to this family.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Process Injection & Memory Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'memory-only RAT' behavior—process injection is the core attack step. Title explicitly establishes this is the malware's distinguishing characteristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect indirect process creation (e.g., svchost, rundll32) spawning unusual parent processes or followed by suspicious child processes with minimal CLI args. Monitor for unsigned .NET assemblies injected into legitimate processes, or API calls to VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory from unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Callback Over Obfuscated HTTP/DNS
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE as a deployed RAT implies active command & control. Article references 'memory-only' which suggests encrypted or obfuscated C2 over common protocols to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual HTTP/DNS patterns from financial sector endpoints: frequent short-duration connections to unusual domains, DNS queries for uncommon TLDs, or HTTP POST/GET requests without User-Agent or with spoofed headers typical of Lazarus tooling.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Financial Targets
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'Financial and Crypto Firms'—implied collection phase. RemotePE RAT would harvest credentials from memory/registry to enable lateral movement and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mimikatz-like cmdline activity (lsass.exe access, sekurlsa commands), LSASS process dumping via Task Manager or rundll32, or registry queries to HKLM\SAM or credential stores. Alert on unusual powershell execution with Get-ItemProperty targeting Credential Manager.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials in Crypto/Finance Networks
suggestion.rationale: Financial and crypto targeting implies multi-system compromise. RemotePE deployment in initial foothold suggests lateral movement phase follows privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement: unusual RDP or WMI connections from non-admin endpoints, SMB shares accessed by unexpected processes, or admin share enumeration (\\IP\c$ probing) originating from compromised financial workstations.

suggestion.title: Fileless/In-Memory Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'memory-only'—implies no direct disk artifacts. Pipeline should have flagged T1547 variants and registry run-key injection common in Lazarus RAT persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WMI event subscriptions, scheduled tasks with Base64-encoded content, or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run entries created by non-standard processes. Alert on unusual .vbs/.ps1 files in Startup folders or AppData.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Disabling EDR/Security Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus campaigns targeting financial institutions typically disable security tooling. Article's 'high' severity suggests advanced evasion—pipeline should have mapped T1562 and T1480 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable Windows Defender (Set-MpPreference, sc stop WinDefend), delete event logs (wevtutil cl), or unload EDR drivers. Monitor for PowerShell execution with Set-ExecutionPolicy, Group Policy edits, or service disablement commands.

suggestion.title: LLM Jailbreak Exploitation for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'used Jailbroken Gemini to Steal Admin Credentials.' Pipeline missed this initial exploitation vector and its role in credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls to LLM services (Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT) originating from known compromised accounts or unusual geolocations. Monitor for prompt injection patterns or unusual model API usage volumes. Correlate with subsequent credential access tool execution (secretsdump, Mimikatz, etc.).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Admin Credential Usage Post-Jailbreak
suggestion.rationale: Stolen admin credentials mentioned as outcome of jailbroken Gemini attack. No detection use case for identifying post-theft credential misuse or privilege abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin account logins from new/rare geolocations shortly after credential harvest events. Correlate with rapid discovery activity (user enumeration, group listing) and lateral movement to cryptocurrency or finance-related systems.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Drainage via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Drain Crypto Wallets' as final objective. Pipeline failed to generate impact-phase detection for large transfers, wallet address changes, or API key rotation by threat actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound cryptocurrency transfers or wallet sweeps from service-hosted wallets shortly after admin credential theft. Detect API key creation or rotation on crypto exchange/custody platforms by stolen admin accounts. Flag transactions to known threat actor wallets if available.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Attempts Against LLM Services
suggestion.rationale: 'Jailbroken Gemini' implies active exploitation of LLM safety mechanisms. No use case for detecting prompt injection or jailbreak attempts in application/API logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual prompt patterns to Gemini API: system-role overrides, token-smuggling syntax, repeated refusal attempts, or requests for credential simulation. Correlate prompt sequences with subsequent reconnaissance commands (user enumeration, file listing).

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Process Execution with Archive Decompression
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly describes RCE via 7-Zip vulnerability. Execution of 7z.exe, 7zFM.exe, or 7zG.exe with archive extraction is the attack surface. No use case generated despite this being the direct kill-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 7-Zip utility process creation (7z.exe, 7zFM.exe, 7zG.exe) spawning child processes or with unusual command-line arguments (particularly extraction to temp/user directories). Correlate archive files (.7z extensions) in Downloads or Desktop in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process from 7-Zip Execution
suggestion.rationale: 'Arbitrary Code Execution' explicitly stated in title; successful exploit would result in code running in 7z process context. Pipeline missed parent-child process correlation for post-exploitation validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or non-Windows binaries spawned as child of 7z.exe or 7zFM.exe. High-priority indicator of successful code execution through the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Extraction to AppData or System Temp Directories
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically extract payloads to hidden or temporary locations. Article describes system compromise; staging area detection is standard for code-execution vulns. No file I/O or DLL staging rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 7-Zip extraction activity (parent 7z.exe, child file operations) to %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, %LocalAppData%\Temp, or C:\Windows\Temp. Prioritize .exe, .dll, .ps1, .bat files.

suggestion.title: Modified termsrv.dll File Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll'—DLL modification is the primary attack vector and should trigger file integrity or hash-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to %windir%\System32\termsrv.dll via integrity monitoring or hash-based detection. Alert on unexpected write events outside OS patching windows. Correlate with RDP service restart events (EventID 7036) and elevated process context.

suggestion.title: Concurrent RDP Session Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article objective explicitly stated as 'Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts'—represents behavioral departure from baseline single-session RDP usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EventID 4624 with LogonType 10 (RDP) occurring multiple times within short window for same user on same host, or simultaneous RDP sessions from different source IPs using same credentials. Baseline org-standard concurrent session limits and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: RDP Service Restart Correlated with DLL Modification
suggestion.rationale: Modifying termsrv.dll requires RDP service restart; article implies stop-modify-start operational sequence detectable via EventID 7036 correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EventID 7036 (TermService stopped) followed within 5 minutes by termsrv.dll file modification followed by service restart. Investigate source process—RDP service controlled by SYSTEM; user or script-initiated restarts warrant privilege escalation investigation.

suggestion.title: Terminal Server MaxInstanceCount Registry Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Enabling concurrent RDP sessions requires modification of MaxInstanceCount registry value; default is 1. Article objective directly implies this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\MaxInstanceCount for value increases above default (1). Legitimate changes from OS patching or GPO with SYSTEM privilege; flag user-mode or LOLBin process modifications as persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: Telegram Credential Trafficking Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Telegram Channels to Sell Verified Bank and Fintech Mule Accounts'—credential exfiltration and monetization pipeline should be detected at point of sale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns consistent with credential aggregation and sale: bulk account metadata transfer to Telegram bot APIs, repeated access to financial credential repositories followed by exfiltration to messaging platforms, or cryptocurrency payments correlated with credential disclosure.

suggestion.title: Bank Account Mule Registration Velocity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'verified' accounts being sold, implying rapid account creation and legitimation cycles. Multiple new bank account registrations from same IP/email/device within short timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag enrollment of multiple new fintech or bank accounts sharing infrastructure (IP, device, recovery email). Correlate with subsequent credential compromise patterns or velocity anomalies in account usage post-registration.

suggestion.title: Fintech Account Compromise via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'verified fintech mule accounts'—detection gap for post-compromise activity following purchase of stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login attempts followed by successful login from new geography/device with subsequent wire transfer activity or balance transfer commands. Track authentication method changes (MFA disable, recovery email updates) within hours of credential theft.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Payment for Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Title implies payment mechanism ('Sell')—article likely describes crypto transaction patterns funding credential purchases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for payment flows to known cryptocurrency exchanges or wallets correlated with credential posting activity. Cross-reference blockchain wallet addresses from dark-web credential paste sites with internal transaction logs.

suggestion.title: Telegram API/Bot Access for Credential Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Criminal infrastructure uses Telegram channels as operational platform—should detect API authentication, bot interactions, and message forwarding of credential material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Telegram API tokens, bot endpoints, or webhook callbacks in network traffic or process execution. Flag instances where bulk credential data (account numbers, SSNs, PINs) is encoded in HTTP POST payloads destined for Telegram gateway IPs or known botnet C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: OAuth Device Code Flow Spike from External Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it'—device code request initiation is the attacker's first action and a detectable log event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure authentication logs for device code flow initiation (grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code) from external/untrusted IP ranges targeting multiple user accounts. Baseline legitimate IoT/printer device enrollments to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Session Token Reuse from Device Code Grant Outside MFA Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access...without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Token is weaponized immediately after issuance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens bound to device code flows being used for interactive application access (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams) from geographically distant locations within minutes of token issuance. Flag non-interactive token usage patterns switching to interactive usage.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation Following Suspicious Device Code Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the campaigns...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity'—rules are created immediately post-compromise in the same session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rules created (especially delete/move/forward rules) by users who completed OAuth device code flow within prior 15 minutes. Baseline normal rule creation patterns per user to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: Device Registered in Entra ID Immediately After Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access'—device registration follows token theft and is logged in Azure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new device registrations (RegisteredNewDevice audit event) within 30 minutes of suspicious device code token usage. Flag devices with anomalous names, untrusted OS, or external registration IP.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Payload Directing to Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal' at http://microsoft.com/devicelogin—email vector precedes device code flow abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound emails containing links to http://microsoft.com/devicelogin or homograph/lookalike domains. Cross-reference recipients with users who subsequently completed device code authentication flows within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Session Proxying via Cookie Link Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link...proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA'—sessions routed through attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for M365 login success events followed by immediate token/session usage from different ASN or infrastructure provider. Detect outbound HTTPS proxy tunnels from user endpoints to non-corporate gateways during M365 login window.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: The article title explicitly names 'Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited' — this is the attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain phases despite this being the entire premise of the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for POST requests to admin endpoints, theme upload endpoints, or API calls consistent with CVE-2026-26980 exploitation patterns. Alert on successful admin account creation or template modification immediately following suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-Ghost Compromise
suggestion.rationale: 700+ sites hijacked implies successful exploitation → persistence mechanism. Article describes site takeover for ClickFix, requiring backend access maintenance. No persistence detection suggested despite clear attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file creation in Ghost theme directories (/content/themes/), unusual Ghost process spawning child shells, or unexpected HTTP requests to newly created endpoints serving credential harvesting or redirect payloads.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Scam Redirect Detection (Post-Hijack)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states sites hijacked 'for ClickFix Attacks' — the primary impact. Pipeline did not surface detection for malicious redirects or fake support overlays, which are the monetization mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 302/303 redirects from legitimate Ghost blog domains to known ClickFix support-scam domains, or injection of JavaScript overlays in Ghost response bodies that mimic OS pop-ups or browser warnings.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ghost Admin Account Enumeration & Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites requires administrative access post-exploitation. No detection for unusual auth patterns (brute force, credential stuffing, or token abuse) despite this being a logical post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed Ghost admin login attempts from unusual IP ranges, successful admin login immediately after exploitation indicators, or rapid creation of new admin users without corresponding legitimate invites.

suggestion.title: Ghost Core/Theme File Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 700+ sites hijacked — implies malicious code injection into theme files or core Ghost modules. No file integrity or code modification detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost /content/themes/, /core/, and /versions/ directories for unexpected file modifications (hash changes, timestamp anomalies). Alert on theme files being modified outside of expected deployment windows or by non-automated accounts.

suggestion.title: SNI/Host Header Mismatch in HTTPS Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Craft SNI requests pointing to trusted domains while routing actual payloads to attacker-controlled servers.' This is the core evasion technique and primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS connections where the SNI server name does not match the HTTP Host header or destination IP. High-reputation CDN SNI values routing to non-CDN IP space are strong signal of Underminr-class abuse.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Multiplexing to Multiple Destination IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'exploit HTTP/2 multiplexing to interleave malicious traffic with legitimate requests.' Single connection spawning traffic to unrelated IPs indicates abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 multiplexed streams within single connection; alert if streams route to IPs with disparate reputation or ASN ownership. Legitimate CDN traffic streams to same IP clusters; attack pattern shows divergence.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Registration on Shared CDN Providers
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Register domains with CDN providers that also host reputable websites' and cites 88M potentially-at-risk domains. Monitor domain registration patterns on Cloudflare, Akamai, AWS CloudFront, Fastly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new domain registrations pointing to shared CDN infrastructure where domain age <30 days and has no legitimate web content, historical backlinks, or DNS history. Cross-reference attacker-registered domain lists shared by CDN providers.

suggestion.title: Outbound Traffic to High-Reputation CDN Domains with Suspicious Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Security tools observe connections to high-reputation domains and allow traffic through'—detection must inspect content within CDN-masked traffic. Look for malware signatures or C2 patterns over Cloudflare/Akamai/AWS/Fastly domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Behavioral detection: high-reputation CDN domain accessed but request URI, User-Agent, or response payload matches known malware families, phishing infrastructure, or C2 beaconing. Use anomaly scoring on domain-reputation mismatch.

suggestion.title: CDN Tenant Isolation Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Review CDN tenant isolation configurations' as mitigation. Detect requests that appear to cross CDN customer boundaries or access unintended certificate/configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with Host/SNI pointing to tenant A but routing through CDN infrastructure configured for tenant B. Requests using shared IP hosting should have strict validation of HTTP Host header against certificate CN and SAN.

suggestion.title: Reputable Domain Access Spike from Single Source IP
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Monitor unusual traffic to high-reputation domains' as a detection method. Single source suddenly accessing dozens of CDN-hosted domains suggests Underminr reconnaissance or payload distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single source IP accessing >10 unique high-reputation CDN domains within 5-min window, especially if accompanied by non-standard ports, user agents, or request patterns. Baseline legitimate traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: SSH-Named Binary Execution from Package Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hide Linux Payload Under SSH-Like Filename During Package Installation.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this masquerading + execution combination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where executable name matches SSH tool patterns (ssh, sshd, ssh-keygen, ssh-keyscan, ssh-add, ssh-agent) but parent process is package manager (dpkg, rpm, apt, snap, pacman) or child originates from /tmp, /var/cache, or other staging paths typical of package extraction.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation Mimicking SSH Tools During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Core defense-evasion technique described: filename obfuscation using SSH-like names. No file-system detection rule created despite this being the primary attacker method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package installation directories (/opt, /usr/local, ~/.cache) for file-creation events where basename exactly matches SSH utilities but: (1) differs in size/hash from official OpenSSH, (2) lacks valid package signature, or (3) was installed outside vendor repositories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package with Undeclared Post-Install Payload
suggestion.rationale: Attack vehicle is compromised package installation. Article references payload embedded in package lifecycle but pipeline surfaced zero supply-chain initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate package manifests for file count, size, signature status, and post-install script length. Alert on deviations: packages from trusted repos suddenly containing SSH-named binaries absent from previous versions, or with post-install scripts executing unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: SSH-Named Executable Missing OpenSSH Package Provenance
suggestion.rationale: Attacker uses filename masquerading to evade pattern-matching defenses. No detection for SSH-named binaries lacking proper upstream cryptographic binding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For any binary matching SSH utility names on system, query dpkg -S / rpm -qf to confirm it belongs to openssh-client or openssh-server package. Flag any ssh/sshd/ssh-keygen outside these packages or with mismatched version/signature.

suggestion.title: Malicious Persistence via Package Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Payload installation described during package lifecycle implies persistence setup via init/systemd/cron. No persistence-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for systemd service creation in /etc/systemd/system and /usr/lib/systemd/system, cron job writes to /etc/cron.d, or /etc/init.d script creation during/immediately after installation of suspicious packages. Flag services that execute SSH-named binaries from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Package Post-Install Script Execution with Obfuscated Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Package post-install hooks (%post, dpkg triggers) invoke the malicious payload. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for hook-triggered commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation events with unexpected child process creation (esp. shells, interpreters, or binary execution). Alert if post-install script spawns processes with SSH-like names, unusual command-line arguments (C2 beacons, exfil), or connects to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Python Dynamic Module (.pyd) Execution from Non-Standard Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'ships as .pyd... files to evade script detection.' .pyd files are Windows Python compiled extensions; malware disguises code as fake modules to blend with legitimate imports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python.exe loads .pyd files from non-standard paths (temp, downloads, AppData, user profiles). Legitimate modules reside in Python site-packages or system directories. Flag .pyd files originating from archives, email, or user-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Linux Shared Object (.so) Loading via Script Interpreters
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '.so files' for Linux evasion. Shared objects loaded by Python, Perl, Ruby, or Node from unexpected paths indicate code obfuscation to bypass script-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .so files opened by script interpreter processes from /tmp, /var/tmp, home directories, or other writable paths. Legitimate shared objects load from /lib, /usr/lib, or application-specific directories. Flag provenance mismatches.

suggestion.title: Entropy and Signature Anomalies in Binary Extension Modules
suggestion.rationale: Malware uses 'compiled binary' formats to evade 'script detection.' Obfuscation indicators (high entropy, signature mismatches, suspicious naming) expose masqueraded malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .pyd/.so files with entropy >7.0, signatures not matching known-good library hashes, or names mimicking legitimate modules but originating from untrusted sources (email, web downloads, temp directories).

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning After Binary Extension Module Load
suggestion.rationale: If .pyd/.so extensions deliver payload execution, subsequent process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from the interpreter context indicates post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when script interpreter processes spawn child shells or command-line utilities after loading .pyd/.so files. Pattern (library_load → child_process) is indicative of code execution via compiled extension modules.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Search Result Click to Malicious Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Iranian APT Uses SEO Poisoning'—this is explicit T1598 (Social Engineering) initial access. No UC generated despite being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks from search engine result pages (referrer contains 'google.com/search', 'bing.com', 'yahoo.com') that redirect through known malware C2 domains or typosquatted software vendor sites. Correlate with first-seen domain registration dates (flag domains <30 days old impersonating popular dev tools).

suggestion.title: Suspicious SQL Developer Installer Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer'—this is T1204.002 and T1036.005 (masquerade). Pipeline missed the delivery+execution sequence entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on download and execution of .exe files with 'SQL', 'Developer', 'SSDT', or 'Server' in filename from non-Microsoft-signed sources. Cross-reference file hash against known malware reputation services. Flag if executable launched directly from Downloads/Temp directory within 5 minutes of download.

suggestion.title: File Masquerading as Legitimate SQL Server Installer
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: impersonating legitimate SQL Server developer tools (T1036.005). Pipeline produced no defense-evasion detections despite this being a centerpiece of the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables with filename patterns matching MS SQL Server/SSDT (e.g., 'SSMS*.exe', 'SQL*.exe', 'Developer*.exe') sourced from outside official Microsoft domains. Validate Microsoft authenticode signature; alert if missing or revoked. Check for binary compiled date mismatches (e.g., 2024 compile date but Windows file metadata shows 2015—signature spoofing indicator).

suggestion.title: Web Shell Process Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'BLUEBEAM Web Shell' deployed to LMS. Web shells execute as child processes of web server (iis, apache, php-fpm). This is the execution and persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned by w3wp.exe, httpd, or nginx with suspicious command-line arguments. Correlate with file creation in web-accessible paths (.aspx, .php, .jsp in web root).

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Followed by GET to Executable File in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment requires uploading malicious file. The phrase 'zero-day exploited to deploy BLUEBEAM' indicates initial file upload/write, then execution via web requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST to LMS endpoints followed by file creation with executable extension, then GET requests to that file. Detect multipart form data or encoded payloads in POST body targeting upload handlers.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Application Error Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day exploitation attempts will trigger application exceptions, auth failures, or SQL errors before successful code execution. Article phrase 'zero-day exploited' implies prior failed/successful exploit attempts in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden spike in KnowledgeDeliver HTTP 500 errors, authentication bypass attempts, or stack trace exceptions correlating with single source IP. Look for parameter injection signatures (SQLi, path traversal, template injection) in request logs.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command-and-Control Communication Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Deployed BLUEBEAM web shell must receive and execute commands. This occurs via anomalous HTTP request patterns to the shell file (special headers, encoded parameters, unusual verbs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to newly created executable files with suspicious parameters (cmd, shell, exec, payload). Flag requests with missing User-Agent, non-standard Accept headers, or command-like base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from Web Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Web shell must reach out to C2 infrastructure for command execution. Monitoring egress from web server processes is critical secondary detection after shell deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from w3wp.exe, httpd, or php-cgi processes to non-whitelisted destinations on non-standard ports. Correlate with persistence file creation timeline and request volume patterns.

suggestion.title: File Integrity Violation in LMS Web Directories
suggestion.rationale: Persistence requires BLUEBEAM file remain on disk in web-accessible location. FIM detects unauthorized additions to production code directories outside change windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/www/html, C:\inetpub\wwwroot, and LMS-specific web directories for file creation/modification with .php, .aspx, .jsp extensions or suspicious script content. Alert outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory-Only Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'memory-only RAT.' No detection use case was generated for unsigned/unattributed process execution without backing file on disk, despite this being the core delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution without a backing PE file on disk or with orphaned parent-child relationships between legitimate system processes and unsigned children. RemotePE likely uses process injection or direct memory instantiation; look for processes with memory write/execute patterns but no corresponding file-system activity or missing module mappings.

suggestion.title: Lazarus RemotePE C&C Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: RAT deployment inherently involves command-and-control communication. Article mentions RemotePE but no IOC extraction occurred, and no network-based detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound HTTPS or custom-protocol communication from financial/crypto-targeted hosts, particularly from processes not normally associated with network communication (Finance-sector EDPs, trading terminals, wallet software). Flag beaconing patterns with low-randomness inter-request intervals.

suggestion.title: Financial Sector Process Anomalies Preceding RAT Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting of 'Financial and Crypto Firms.' No detection use case maps Lazarus's reconnaissance or secondary-stage execution patterns in these environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous discovery activity on systems running financial software (Bloomberg terminals, trading platforms, crypto wallets/APIs): execution of whoami, net group, registry queries for credential stores, or enumeration of installed applications before RemotePE implant execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Gemini API Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Russian Hacker Used Jailbroken Gemini'—establishes Gemini as the attack vehicle. Pipeline missed this entirely. Should detect rapid/repeated API calls, unusual token volume, or geographic anomalies in Gemini access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gemini API calls from non-whitelisted IPs, excessive token consumption within short windows, or systematic probing of jailbreak payloads. Correlate with failed phishing attempts or credential theft.

suggestion.title: Admin Credential Exfiltration Post-LLM Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Steal Admin Credentials'—core attack objective. No detection proposed for credential access following Gemini compromise. Missing correlation between LLM abuse and credential loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin account credential access (new login, credential dump, password change) within minutes of anomalous Gemini API activity. Flag accounts accessing cryptographic material or exchange integrations immediately after suspected compromise.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Unauthorized Transfer
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Drain Crypto Wallets'—explicit impact phase. Pipeline generated zero detection for this financial theft, the article's primary outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-velocity outbound crypto transfers from organizational wallets/exchange accounts, especially to newly created or foreign wallets. Alert on transfers initiated by admin accounts outside business hours or geographies.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with LLM-Generated Characteristics
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies Gemini was used to craft phishing—likely initial compromise vector. Pipeline detected neither phishing delivery nor LLM-generated content artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with linguistic signatures of LLM generation: unusual grammatical precision, entropy anomalies, template-like phrasing, or prompt fragments. Cross-correlate with admin-targeted phishing campaigns and credential compromise timelines.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using Compromised Admin Credentials
suggestion.rationale: After credential theft ('Steal Admin Credentials'), attackers pivot to wallets. Pipeline missed detection for credential use and lateral movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag admin account logins from anomalous IPs/devices post-compromise, access to exchange/wallet infrastructure, or RDP/SSH sessions from external IPs using stolen credentials. Baseline legitimate admin workflows and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation with Embedded Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'credential-stealing malware' via package managers (npm, PyPI, CratesIO). Supply chain attacks inject execution during installation. No UC generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by package manager install operations (npm.exe, pip.exe, cargo.exe) for execution of scripts in package directories, especially .postinstall hooks or setup.py execution. Alert on child processes with network connections to external IPs immediately after installation or accessing credential stores (env vars, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Windows credential manager).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Package Manager Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'credential-stealing malware.' Malware in packages executes at install-time via hooks (npm postinstall, Python setup.py, Cargo build scripts). Missing detection for environment variable access or credential file reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package install scripts (run via interpreter spawned from npm/pip/cargo) accessing known credential paths: ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU, /etc/passwd, environment variables like AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN. Alert on reads + exfiltration network calls.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets npm, PyPI, and CratesIO—package repositories. No detection generated for unusual package versions, typosquatting, or suspicious package metadata/dependencies. Pipeline missed repository-level IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package dependency declarations (package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml) for references to newly-published or out-of-band versions; cross-check downloaded packages against known repo manifests. Alert on packages with suspicious post-install scripts (base64 encoding, curl/wget, code obfuscation in scripts). Flag packages with timestamps near known TrapDoor campaign dates.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware implies C2 exfiltration. Article doesn't provide C2 domains, but supply chain attacks consistently show command-and-control callbacks from installed code. Pipeline generated no network-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated by processes spawned from package managers (npm install, pip install, cargo build) to external IP addresses, especially non-standard ports (not 80, 443) or to IP reputation feeds (malware C2, botnet, data exfil). Baseline normal package manager traffic (CDNs, pypi.org) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Registry/Environment Poisoning via Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware often plants persistence or steals stored credentials. Title references 'spreads' implying distribution/persistence mechanisms. No detection for registry modifications, RC file manipulation, or shell profile hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect post-install script modifications to HKCU\Environment, ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.zshrc, or shell rc files coinciding with package installation. Alert on registry writes to RunOnce/Run by processes in package directories. Monitor for DLL/so/dylib placement in paths that package managers later search (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PATH modifications).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process from 7-Zip Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Execute Arbitrary Code and Compromise Systems'; RCE-via-archive exploitation flow is decompression → payload execution. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned as children of 7z.exe, 7zFM.exe, or 7zG.exe with command-line arguments, especially from temp directories or Downloads. Correlate parent process start time with archive modification time. Flag unsigned or low-prevalence child executables.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Archive Extraction to Suspicious Location
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payloads must be written to disk. Attack chain involves 'Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code' via crafted archives—detection should cover extraction to temp, system, or startup directories. Pipeline has no file-system detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 7-Zip extraction events to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Windows\System32, or StartUp folders. Baseline benign extraction patterns (e.g., user-initiated downloads) and flag bulk/recursive extractions or those from email clients or web browsers.

suggestion.title: Rapid Process Spawn Following Archive Activity
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation implies command execution immediately after archive processing. Article describes 'compromise' systems but pipeline captured zero behavioral linkage between archive handling and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create a sequence detector: 7-Zip file extraction event followed within 1-5 seconds by child process creation with high-risk command-line flags (cmd.exe, powershell.exe -NoP, rundll32, regsvcs). Deduplicate legitimate post-extraction workflows (e.g., installer self-extraction).

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Version Vulnerability Check
suggestion.rationale: Article is titled '[CRIT]' and discusses 'New 7-Zip Vulnerabilities'; should generate version-based inventory and patch-compliance detection. No version or CVE-linked detection rules were created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest installed 7-Zip versions from asset inventory (Registry, WMI, package managers). Flag instances below patched version (specific CVE versions from article, e.g., CVE-XXXX-XXXXX if disclosed in article). Send alert to patch management queue and risk registry.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Process Network Communication
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE execution may initiate C2 callbacks or data exfiltration. Article states 'Compromise Systems'—implies post-exploitation phases requiring network IOC detection. Pipeline generated no network-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal 7-Zip network behavior (typically none except version checks to 7-zip.org). Flag any outbound TCP/UDP from 7z.exe or descendant processes to external IPs or non-standard ports, especially post-extraction.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Modifies termsrv.dll to Enable Multiple RDP Sessions'—core attack vector. Pipeline produced zero detections for this named indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file modifications to System32\termsrv.dll or TermService-related DLLs outside Windows Update context. Compare against known-good Microsoft hash for current OS version. Alert on unsigned termsrv.dll or file writes to this path from non-System processes.

suggestion.title: Multiple Concurrent RDP Sessions Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article goal is enabling 'Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts'—Windows limits this by default. Exceeding baseline session count is direct evidence of the attack's objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal concurrent RDP session count per user per host. Alert when single user exceeds 2 concurrent RDP sessions or when multiple concurrent sessions originate from same source IP. Correlate with logon events to identify anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: RDP Session Limit Registry Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Enabling multiple RDP sessions requires disabling Windows session limits, typically via registry modifications (fSingleSessionPerUser, MaxInstanceCount). Article's technical objective implies this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\TermService\Parameters\* by non-trusted processes or outside change-control windows. Flag modifications to fSingleSessionPerUser (0→1), MaxInstanceCount, or MaxSessions. Combine with termsrv.dll modifications for high-confidence alert.
