suggestion.title: System DLL Cryptographic Validation - termsrv.dll
suggestion.rationale: Modified termsrv.dll will deviate from known-good Microsoft hash. Article's modification context demands cryptographic integrity checks, not just signature validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain SHA256 hashes of termsrv.dll for all OS versions in environment. Scan System32 on schedule or at load time; alert on mismatch. Unmatched versions may be legitimately signed but post-compromise patched binaries.

suggestion.title: Cloud Atlas APT Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies actor 'Cloud Atlas APT Group'—zero actor context extracted. Should correlate known C2 infrastructure, file hashes, or TTPs with termsrv.dll detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain Cloud Atlas known-bad IPs, domains, certificates, and file signatures from threat feeds. On detection of termsrv.dll modification or anomalous RDP sessions, cross-check network logs for beacons to known C2 or downloads of known Cloud Atlas tooling.

suggestion.title: Admin Process Accessing termsrv.dll for Patch Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes APT group modifying the DLL—attacker must have admin context. Detection should identify suspicious write operations even from admin processes during non-patch windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file writes to termsrv.dll from rundll32.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or PE injection utilities even when running as admin or SYSTEM. Baseline legitimate patch windows. Low-and-slow modification patterns (off-hours, uncommon process parents) indicate stealth.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Financial Account Access from New Geography
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'verified bank and fintech mule accounts'—pre-compromised accounts used for money laundering. Detect logins from geographies inconsistent with account holder location or historical patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentications to banking/fintech accounts from IP geolocation mismatches relative to account holder residence. Flag if the same account logs in from multiple distinct geographies within hours. Escalate if authentication occurs outside business hours and is followed by rapid fund transfers.

suggestion.title: Rapid Fund Transfers from Compromised Mule Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Core use case of mule accounts is moving illicit funds. Detect bulk transfers to shell entities or unusual wire destinations that deviate from historical account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for accounts performing large or multiple outbound transfers within 24 hours of first anomalous access. Escalate if destination accounts are newly created, belong to high-risk jurisdictions, or show patterns consistent with layering (rapid onward transfers).

suggestion.title: Telegram API Communication for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Telegram channels' as operational medium for coordinating mule account sales and usage. Detect programmatic Telegram API calls or unusual Telegram client behavior from enterprise infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS traffic to api.telegram.org from servers or workstations outside sanctioned Telegram business use. Detect POST requests to Telegram bot endpoints (getUpdates, sendMessage) or WebSocket connections indicating automated message handling.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account Credential Reset and 2FA Re-enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Sale of 'verified accounts' implies prior compromise and credential staging. Detect mass account credential changes, 2FA resets, or recovery email updates—indicators of account takeover preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple password resets, 2FA method replacements, or recovery contact changes across unrelated accounts within a time window. Escalate if followed by successful logins from new device IDs or IP addresses.

suggestion.title: Multi-Account Access from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Mule account operators manage dozens of stolen accounts. Detect a single source IP, device, or session authenticating to multiple unrelated financial accounts in rapid succession.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on a single source IP authenticating to 5+ distinct accounts within 1 hour, especially if account ownership spans different customer segments or business units. Cross-correlate with geographic and device anomalies.

suggestion.title: Device Code Authentication from Anomalous IP After Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page via phishing.' Device code grants should be correlated with recent phishing detection and IP anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful device code authentication flows (SignInLogs: authenticationMethod='Device Code Flow') where the initiating user IP differs significantly from 30-day baseline, occurs within 4 hours of inbound phishing email, or is followed by immediate OAuth scope expansion without subsequent interactive MFA.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Issued Without MFA Challenge During Token Use
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access...without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Stolen tokens accessed without re-validation are the attack's core success metric.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device-code authentication success events with subsequent API or mailbox access (via Graph API, Outlook Web Access, or native Office clients) where no additional MFA/Conditional Access challenge was triggered despite sensitive scope access.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'in some of the attacks, attackers also...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Inbox rules are direct persistence and concealment indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new inbox rules (operations: 'New-InboxRule' or 'Set-InboxRule') created by accounts that recently authenticated via device code, MFA-bypass indicators, or anomalous locations. Flag rules that auto-delete, soft-delete, or move items to hidden folders or external addresses.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Azure AD by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access.' Device registration is explicit persistence—attackers can re-authenticate without stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new device registrations (AuditLogs: Operation='Register device') by accounts with recent device-code auth, impossible-travel logins, or phishing-indicator correlations. Baseline: flag any registration from non-corporate VPN/ASN or registration of mobile/unknown device models for sensitive roles.

suggestion.title: OAuth Application Consent to Suspicious Service Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365 platform with 'token-capture functionality.' Compromised accounts will grant OAuth scopes to attacker-controlled or spoofed applications to persist access and exfiltrate data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth consent grants (AuditLogs: Operation='Consent to application') issued by accounts with recent device-code authentication or anomalous sign-in patterns. Prioritize newly registered applications, those requesting high-privilege scopes (Mail.Read, Files.Read.All, Directory.Read.All), or those registered in non-standard tenants.

suggestion.title: Session Proxying / Cookie Interception via Cookie Link Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article: Kali365 'Cookie Link' mode 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens.' Impossible-travel and session anomalies indicate AitM capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sign-in events where user authenticates from phishing/proxy infrastructure IP, solves MFA, then immediately performs sensitive actions (mailbox access, app registration, data exfil) from a geographically or temporally impossible second IP. Flag if session context changes (browser, device ID, user-agent) between auth and API calls.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites'—this is the initial access vector and should trigger detection for inbound exploit payloads or suspicious requests to vulnerable Ghost endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT requests to Ghost admin endpoints (e.g., /ghost/api/admin/) with payloads matching known CVE-2026-26980 exploit signatures, or from non-standard User-Agent strings. Flag any 200/201 responses to these endpoints from external IPs or unusual source contexts.

suggestion.title: Website Content Modification - JavaScript Injection Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sites 'hijacked' and used to serve 'ClickFix Attacks'—implies malicious JavaScript injected into legitimate pages after Ghost compromise. Standard post-exploitation persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to Ghost template files, theme assets, or post content that inject external script tags or inline JavaScript. Correlate with suspicious outbound HTTP requests from the web server to attacker-controlled domains. Look for <script> injections referencing scareware/ClickFix domains in HTTP response inspection.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Scam Popup Distribution via Hijacked Website
suggestion.rationale: Explicit attack purpose stated: 'ClickFix Attacks'—a fake-security-warning scam delivered through hijacked site content. Represents impact phase where victims are socially engineered via malicious popups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from compromised Ghost sites containing known ClickFix scareware domains, phone numbers, or CSS/HTML signatures of fake security warnings. Cross-reference with threat feeds identifying ClickFix C2 infrastructure. Flag requests to common ClickFix payment or support domains from users whose traffic passed through hijacked sites.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Ghost Admin API Authentication Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-26980 exploitation requires authentication bypass or brute-force of Ghost admin APIs—authentication anomalies should precede successful hijacking of 700+ sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost API authentication logs for failed login surges, password spray patterns, or successful logins from unexpected geographies/IPs. Correlate authentication timestamps with subsequent modifications to site content or templates. Flag API token generation events that precede unauthorized content changes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Propagation - Ghost Vulnerability Scanning Across Hosted Instances
suggestion.rationale: Scale of compromise (700+ sites) suggests automated reconnaissance and exploitation across multiple Ghost instances, likely on shared hosting or similar CIDR ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual scanning activity probing Ghost standard paths (/ghost/api/, /admin/, /.well-known/) across multiple target IPs within same subnet or hosting provider. Correlate with successful exploitation events. Flag single source IP scanning 50+ potential Ghost instances in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Detect CDN-Hosted Malicious Content Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article core premise: hackers 'abuse shared CDN infrastructure'—using legitimate, high-reputation CDN providers to host malicious payloads. Article phrase: 'bypass domain reputation security controls.' Should detect when high-reputation CDN IPs serve known malware families or phishing content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to known CDN IP ranges (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly, etc.) that resolve to domains with reputation scores below enterprise whitelist thresholds. Flag when CDN-hosted domains deliver binaries or phishing pages matching known malware hashes or phishing campaign indicators.

suggestion.title: Domain-CDN Trust Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies domains with poor history leveraging CDN's reputation. Should detect mismatches between domain age/history and hosting on trusted CDN. Phrase: 'bypass domain reputation security controls.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag newly registered or historically malicious domains that suddenly resolve to CDN edge IPs. Establish baseline of legitimate domain age vs. CDN adoption; alert on young domains with poor WHOIS history or previous abuse reports tunneled through CDN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Shared CDN Infrastructure Mass-Domain Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'shared CDN infrastructure'—multiple attacker domains likely sharing same edge servers, ASNs, or backend pools. No single IOC is malicious, but the pattern is.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate historical DNS resolutions: cluster domains that share CDN provider, edge location, and backend IP pools. Alert when 10+ distinct domains in the same cluster have anomalous registration patterns (rapid bulk registration, hidden WHOIS, WHOIS privacy abuse) or connect to known malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Reputation Filter Bypass via CDN Certificate Pinning
suggestion.rationale: Article premise requires attackers to defeat URL reputation checks. Article phrase: 'bypass domain reputation security controls.' Should detect attempts to exploit CDN SSL/TLS certificates (single certificate for many domains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSL certificate chains where the leaf certificate covers hundreds of SANs pointing to CDN-hosted malicious domains. Alert when reputation filtering systems see high-reputation CDN domain in the chain but low-reputation payload domain in the request.

suggestion.title: Egress to CDN Edges with Suspicious User-Agent/Referer Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Attackers abusing CDN likely disguise requests. Article describes 'abuse' of infrastructure implying obfuscation. No specific phrase but implicit in evasion narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS requests to CDN edge IPs with non-standard User-Agent strings (headless browsers, curl, wget, unusual encoding) or suspicious Referer headers (self-referential, generic, missing Referer on POST). Baseline legitimate CDN traffic and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Package Manager Spawns Process Matching SSH Utility Name
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Hide Linux Payload Under SSH-Like Filename During Package Installation' — core attack is payload execution post-install masquerading as SSH tool. Zero detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager processes (apt, dpkg, rpm, pacman) that create child processes with names matching SSH utilities (ssh, sshd, ssh-keygen, ssh-add, ssh-agent). Alert especially when process paths deviate from standard system directories (/usr/bin, /usr/sbin) or when execution timing correlates with recent package installation events.

suggestion.title: Executable with SSH-Tool Name Created Outside Standard Bin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Obfuscation technique: 'SSH-like filename' placed during installation. No file-creation detection covers anomalous file paths for legitimate-sounding binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of executable files with names matching SSH tools (ssh, sshd, ssh-*, .ssh*) in non-standard locations (/tmp, /var/tmp, home directories, application-specific paths) especially during or immediately after package manager execution. Verify against known SSH binary baseline.

suggestion.title: Package Install Creates Executable in /tmp or Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain payloads typically drop to world-writable or application-owned directories. Article implies unusual staging location; no detection for post-install file placement anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation (via audit logs or package manager tracing) with subsequent creation of executable files in non-package-standard paths. Flag especially if filenames mimic system utilities, use path traversal patterns, or include suspicious encoding.

suggestion.title: SSH-Named Binary Executed from Unexpected Location with Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Final execution phase of attack. No detection combines process name masquerading with behavioral indicators (network egress post-execution).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executables matching SSH names execute from non-standard paths and immediately initiate network connections (particularly outbound TCP/UDP to non-SSH ports or to suspicious infrastructure). Establish baseline of legitimate SSH binary locations and expected network behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .pyd File Creation Outside Python Site-Packages
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'ships as .pyd files'—Windows Python extension binaries that belong in site-packages or system directories. Creation in user temp, Downloads, or AppData signals evasion: article phrase 'to evade script detection' implies adversary expects .pyd to bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .pyd file creation in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Python\PythonCore and user-writable paths outside canonical Python directories. Correlate parent process (should be python.exe, pip, or installer—not cmd, powershell, or random executables) and file source (network, email temp). High-signal indicator of compiled malware deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .so File Creation in Non-Standard Directories (Linux)
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates .so (shared object) files as deployment vector. On Linux, .so creation outside /lib, /usr/lib, /opt, or application-specific directories is anomalous: article's 'evade script detection' implies compiled binaries bypass signature/heuristic rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .so creation in /tmp, /var/tmp, home directories, or via unusual parent processes. Correlate with subsequent dlopen() calls via auditd or strace. Low false-positive rate since .so creation is rare in most business environments outside package managers.

suggestion.title: Python Process Loading Non-Canonical .pyd Modules
suggestion.rationale: InvisibleFerret execution requires Python to load the .pyd: 'ships as .pyd' implies import or ctypes.CDLL() call. Article title omits method but article phrase 'evade script detection' suggests compiled binary masquerades as legitimate module.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Sysmon EID 7 (Image Load) for python.exe loading .pyd from non-standard paths or with suspicious names. Flag loads from user temp, network paths, or where .pyd timestamp post-dates Python startup. Correlate with command line containing unusual import statements or ctypes calls.

suggestion.title: Masquerading—.pyd/.so Named After Legitimate Standard Library
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'ships as .pyd and .so files to evade script detection'—implies naming and placement strategy to bypass heuristics. Common evasion: naming compiled payload 'requests.pyd', 'ssl.so', etc. to impersonate legitimate packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain whitelist of legitimate .pyd/.so files (hash, size, signer) from official Python repos. Flag any .pyd/.so with identical name to known packages but different hash, or created in user-writable locations. Cross-reference against PyPI and system library inventories.

suggestion.title: LD_PRELOAD or Library Path Hijacking for .so Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies .so as transport vector but does not detail execution method. Common Linux deployment: LD_PRELOAD environment variable to force loading of malicious .so during process spawn. Detection required if .so files recovered but execution mechanism unclear.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution with LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, or DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES (macOS) set, especially when library path points to user directories or recently created .so files. Cross-correlate with file creation timelines to detect setup-then-execute patterns.

suggestion.title: Spawning Child Processes or Network Connections Post .pyd/.so Load
suggestion.rationale: Article does not detail post-execution behavior but compiled malware modules typically persist or move laterally. Detection: if .pyd/.so successfully loads, watch for abnormal activity (child process spawning, network connections, file encryption) in processes that loaded the module.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of python.exe child processes and outbound connections. Flag python.exe spawning unusual children (rundll32, cmd, powershell) or initiating connections to non-whitelisted destinations shortly after loading non-canonical .pyd. Correlate timeline of .pyd creation + python.exe spawn with downstream activity for attack chain reconstruction.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download and Execution of SQL Developer Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware disguised as 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer' — core attack is delivering and executing a trojanized application. Title establishes execution from user download/installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of SQL Developer, SQL Server Management Studio, or similar database tools launched from user-writable directories (Downloads, Temp, AppData). Correlate with recent file downloads and uncommon parent processes. Flag if executable lacks valid Microsoft or JetBrains signatures.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Redirection to Malware Download Sites
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'SEO Poisoning' — article describes malicious search results landing users on attacker infrastructure. Phrase 'SEO Poisoning to Deliver' establishes redirect/landing page component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to known malicious domains impersonating legitimate package repositories or SQL tool download sites. Flag search-result-to-attacker-domain transitions. Monitor for 404s or redirects on typosquatting domains (e.g., sqlldeveloper.com, sq1developer.com).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation C2 Communication from SQL Tools
suggestion.rationale: Standard APT delivery implies C2 callback. Malware installer suggests persistence and C2 establishment. No C2 indicators in pipeline output despite high severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network activity from newly executed SQL-named processes. Baseline legitimate SQL tool network behavior. Flag connections to non-standard ports, encrypted tunnels from application-layer processes, or beaconing patterns with variable Jitter.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash and File Reputation Check for SQL Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions specific malware delivery but pipeline extracted zero file hashes or malware names. Fake installer should have associated file indicators or AV detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known-malicious hashes of the 'Fake SQL Developer Installer' from threat feeds. Cross-reference downloads against file reputation services (VirusTotal, Windows Defender ASR). Alert on unsigned executables with SQL-related names.

suggestion.title: Iranian APT Infrastructure and Domain Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'Iranian APT' but pipeline output contains no IOCs or actor-attributed infrastructure. Compromise of legitimate domains for SEO poisoning should yield domain IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known Iranian APT C2 domains, actor-registered infrastructure, and compromised legitimate domains used in SEO poisoning campaigns. Monitor DNS/URL queries to historical actor infrastructure. Flag traffic to fast-flux or DGA-generated domains associated with Iranian operators.

suggestion.title: Fake Installer Package Repository and Download Site Detection
suggestion.rationale: SEO poisoning directs victims to attacker-controlled download repositories mimicking legitimate SQL package sites. No detection articulated for the hosted-malware component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET requests to attacker-hosted installer mirrors. Flag sites with legitimate database-tool branding but non-standard hosting infrastructure. Detect anomalous download rates or geographical access patterns inconsistent with legitimate vendor CDN patterns.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Zero-Day Exploited'—pipeline produced no initial access detection. This is the attack's entry point and should map to T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to known vulnerable KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints with abnormal parameters, error codes indicative of exploit attempt (5xx server errors during unusual activity), or requests from external IPs during non-business hours. Flag payloads containing common web shell upload patterns or SQL injection signatures.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Web Shell Creation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'Deploy BLUEBEAM Web Shell'—pipeline failed to generate persistence detection despite this being the attack's primary outcome. Web shells are direct indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation/modification of .php, .asp, .aspx, .jsp files in web-root directories with obfuscated content, base64 encoding, or suspicious functions (system, exec, eval, passthru). Monitor for BLUEBEAM file path signatures. Flag web.config or .htaccess modifications enabling script execution.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Command Execution via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase: web shell enables command execution. Pipeline generated zero execution detection rules despite this being immediate post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, &&, ;, backticks), encoded payloads, or suspicious query parameters to suspected web shell paths. Detect process spawning from web server processes (w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx) with unexpected command-line arguments or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File System Modification in LMS Directory
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment requires file write to LMS installation path. Pipeline generated no file integrity or baseline deviation detection despite clear file system compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver LMS installation directory for unexpected file creation outside normal patch/update windows. Flag new executable/script files or modification of core application files. Compare against baseline using file hashing or directory snapshots.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only RAT Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'memory-only RAT' — RemotePE loads entirely in memory without disk artifacts. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for in-memory shellcode injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate system processes (svchost, rundll32, regsvcs) spawning child processes with no command-line arguments or spawning from atypical parents. Alert on processes with image-load patterns consistent with memory-only payloads (ntdll early, no associated file path on disk).

suggestion.title: Lazarus RemotePE C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'memory-only RAT' implies command-and-control communication. Pipeline missed C2 phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound traffic from non-network-service processes to uncommon ports or known RemotePE C2 infrastructure. Monitor for encrypted C2 beacons from spawned child processes of services.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Spear-Phish Against Finance Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Against Financial and Crypto Firms' — implies targeted delivery. Pipeline missed initial-access techniques and no threat actor (Lazarus) was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with macro-enabled Office docs or suspicious .exe/.dll attachments sent to finance/crypto domain recipients. Cross-reference sender reputation and link targets against known Lazarus infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping Before Lateral Move
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus historically extracts credentials post-compromise to enable lateral movement in financial networks. Article identifies finance/crypto targeting but pipeline ignored credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LSASS access (MiniDump, OpenProcess with PROCESS_VM_READ) or suspicious registry queries to HKLM\Security\SAM. Monitor for creation of hives or NTDS.dit access in credential-harvesting scenarios.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DLL/Shellcode Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only payloads require runtime deobfuscation. Article emphasizes 'memory-only' nature; pipeline missed defense-evasion detection for payload unpacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with high entropy memory allocations followed by memory execution (VirtualAlloc → WriteProcessMemory → SetThreadContext). Detect obfuscated strings being decoded at runtime in system contexts.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Malware Hash / Behavioral Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article names RemotePE as the payload; pipeline failed to emit any file hash IOCs, C2 domains, or behavioral signatures for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish RemotePE signature rules on file-less execution patterns: unsigned .NET process spawning, abnormal thread creation in system services, absence of legitimate module loading order.

suggestion.title: AI Model Jailbreak Exploitation for Credential Extraction

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual Gemini/LLM API calls requesting credential formats, admin account enumeration, or password-like outputs. Flag accounts with no prior API history making credential-extraction queries. Alert on authentication events immediately following suspicious AI model queries.

suggestion.title: Credential Abuse Post-Extraction from Compromised AI

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin credential usage from anomalous geolocations or at unusual times relative to account history. Flag successful logins to crypto/financial systems immediately after credential-theft indicators. Look for failed login attempts followed by success with different auth method.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cryptocurrency Wallet Access and Drainage
suggestion.rationale: Article headline includes 'Drain Crypto Wallets'—impact/exfiltration phase completely absent from pipeline. Title directly specifies financial impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wallet transfer logs for unusual withdrawal amounts, multiple txn to new addresses, or batch transfers to centralized exchange wallets. Alert on wallet admin changes without authorization. Flag API key generation for crypto infrastructure if account is outside normal crypto ops team.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation with Immediate Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'. No use case was generated for the execution + credential theft chain. Phrase: 'credential-stealing malware'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package manager execution (npm install, pip install, cargo add) with child processes accessing credential stores (registry hives, .ssh, .aws, browser LocalState, Credential Manager) within 30s. Alert on processes spawned from node_modules, site-packages, or target directories accessing LSASS or credential managers.

suggestion.title: Multi-Registry Supply Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack spans 'npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — three distinct package ecosystems. No IOC extraction and no cross-registry anomaly detection. Phrase: 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for packages installed from all three registries in same asset/build within 24h (supply chain widening). Flag packages with version skips, rapid re-releases, or unusual dependency chains. Alert if same malicious package variant appears across multiple ecosystems.

suggestion.title: Package Post-Install Script Execution with Outbound C2
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware must exfiltrate. Article indicates malware payload executes and steals credentials, but no use case for detection of C2 communication. Missing T1041.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from child processes spawned during package installation (parent = npm/pip/cargo). Flag non-RFC1918 IPs, high-entropy domains, or uncommon ports (8080–8090, 4444, 9999) contacted within 60s of install completion. Correlate with credential access event.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Detection Across Registries
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on package registries commonly use name variants to evade detection. No mention of detection for similar-named packages. Implicit in multi-registry attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor installed packages against known legitimate libraries using Levenshtein distance or character similarity (e.g., express → expres, lodash → loadash). Alert on installations of packages with >90% name similarity but different authors or first-time seen versions.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Package Manager Install Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malware in packages executes during or after installation. Title mentions credential-stealing behavior but pipeline mapped no execution technique (T1547.001, T1204.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with parent = npm/pip/cargo or working directory within node_modules/site-packages. Flag suspicious executables (.exe, .bat, .sh, .ps1) spawned from these paths. Baseline against known post-install hook processes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Process Spawning Child Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Execute Arbitrary Code and Compromise Systems' — exploitation pattern mandates post-extraction child process execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when 7zip.exe or 7zFM.exe creates child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) within 2 minutes of archive decompression. Correlate parent-child relationships to filter benign archive operations (extraction to staging).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable 7-Zip Version Installed
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates newly discovered vulnerabilities in 7-Zip. Pipeline should inventory and flag systems running affected versions to enable rapid patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query installed 7-Zip product versions against vendor advisory affected ranges. Flag systems running versions below patch level; escalate for immediate remediation or preventive isolation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Attached to Phishing Email
suggestion.rationale: Implicit delivery mechanism: 'attackers execute arbitrary code' requires user interaction opening archive. No detection for email + archive attachment vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on external emails with 7z/zip attachments followed within 10 minutes by 7-Zip process execution from user temp or download directories. Correlate to phishing indicators (spoofed sender, urgency language in OCR body).

suggestion.title: Executable Extraction into Suspicious Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires archive→file→execution chain. Pipeline missed detection for PE/binary writes by 7-Zip to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or other post-exploit staging locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 7zip.exe file-write operations to common staging directories (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Desktop, Downloads). Alert if file extension is exe/dll/scr and parent process is 7-Zip GUI or script engine.

suggestion.title: Command-Line 7-Zip Extraction with Output Suppression
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may automate exploitation via CLI to suppress GUI warnings. Pipeline should flag non-interactive 7-Zip invocations with suspicious path arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 7z.exe or 7zFM.exe processes spawned by cmd.exe/powershell.exe with command-line containing -o (output path) or -r (recursive) flags, especially if parent is scripting engine or scheduled task.

suggestion.title: Post-Extraction Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution often leads to persistence or privilege-escalation via registry. No detection for exploitation→registry chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 7zip.exe activity (within 60s window) with child process writing to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run. Flag as likely post-exploitation persistence attempt.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Cloud Atlas modifies termsrv.dll directly; this is the core attack mechanism and should generate file integrity and hash-based detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on hash mismatches or unsigned termsrv.dll in System32/SysWOW64. Monitor file modification timestamps outside Windows Update cycles. Correlate with RDP service restarts or unexpected svchost.exe behavior triggered by DLL reload.

suggestion.title: Registry-Driven Concurrent RDP Session Enablement
suggestion.rationale: Multiple concurrent RDP sessions require DisableSingleSessionPerUser or fDenyTSConnections registry keys to be modified; no behavioral detection use case for this persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server registry keys, especially fDenyTSConnections=0 or DisableSingleSessionPerUser changes by non-SYSTEM accounts outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Concurrent RDP Logon Session Baseline Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is multiple concurrent RDP sessions on victim hosts; no use case for detecting per-user session count anomalies outside baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-user baseline for concurrent RDP logon session count (typically 1-2). Alert when same user exceeds baseline with simultaneous sessions from different source IPs or same IP in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: DLL Interception in RDP Service via Import Address Table Hooking
suggestion.rationale: termsrv.dll modification implies code injection or IAT hooking into RDP service internals; no use case for detecting runtime DLL tampering or abnormal module loads in termsrv.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected DLL loads into svchost.exe -k termsvcs, especially non-Microsoft-signed modules from non-System32 paths. Flag kernel-mode callbacks or IAT hooks indicated by unusual import patterns in termsrv service memory.

suggestion.title: RDP Service Restart Temporal Clustering
suggestion.rationale: DLL modification to a running service typically requires service restart to take effect; no use case detects suspicious RDP service lifecycle changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP service (TermService) stop/start cycles outside maintenance windows, especially when paired with file modification alerts on termsrv.dll or registry changes to Terminal Server hive within same 5-min window.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via System DLL Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Modifying termsrv.dll in System32 requires SYSTEM privileges or file-permission manipulation; missing detection for unusual account attempting system file modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-SYSTEM or non-administrator accounts attempt write/replace operations on protected system DLLs (termsrv.dll, lsass.exe, ntdll.dll). Flag process creation with SeLoadDriverPrivilege or SeDebugPrivilege elevation preceding file modifications.

suggestion.title: Telegram C2 Communication for Account Marketplace
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states cybercriminals 'use Telegram channels to sell verified bank and fintech mule accounts.' This is a structured marketplace using Telegram as C&C/communication platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Telegram API traffic originating from financial institution networks or employees. Correlate Telegram connections with employee credentials flagged for compromise in external threat intel or compromised-credential marketplaces.

suggestion.title: Bulk Verified Account Creation and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes accounts sold as 'verified,' implying they were compromised, validated, and prepared for resale. Pipeline should detect upstream credential acquisition phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential stuffing, brute-force login attempts, or phishing campaigns targeting fintech/banking users. Flag accounts with subsequent anomalous activity (password resets, forwarding rules, fund transfers) shortly after compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover and Mule Account Monetization
suggestion.rationale: After sale, mule accounts are weaponized for money laundering. Article implies accounts used as financial conduits post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect dormant or newly-created accounts with sudden high transaction velocity, rapid fund cycling, transfers to external beneficiaries, or access from previously unseen geographies. Flag accounts matching known 'mule' behavioral patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised Fintech/Bank Account Resale Intelligence
suggestion.rationale: Article references structured sale of 'verified accounts,' indicating threat actors maintain inventory and pricing. This is discovery/preparation activity for downstream money-laundering operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate dark web/underground forum monitoring for postings advertising compromised bank/fintech accounts. Correlate seller patterns, pricing, account volume, and geography to identify campaigns. Cross-reference advertised institutions against your organization.

suggestion.title: Fintech-Targeted Credential Compromise Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions fintech platforms alongside banks. Pipeline should model vertical-specific targeting rather than generic credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing/social-engineering campaigns targeting fintech users with financial services-themed lures. Track if legitimate fintech branding/templates are spoofed. Correlate with historical data breaches of fintech customer PII to identify users at elevated compromise risk.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Token Issuance to Different Security Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access...without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' This is the core compromise mechanism enabling account hijacking without per-session MFA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device code authentication where MFA completes successfully, yet subsequent resource access (mail, Teams, SharePoint) occurs from IP/device/client differing from the MFA device. Alert on non-interactive sign-ins or app-only access immediately following device code flows, indicating token theft in different trust context.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation Post-Device-Code Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'attackers...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' This post-compromise persistence reveals account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbox rule creation (forward, delete, move-to-folder, suppress notifications) with device code auth, unusual login, or geographically-impossible travel within 15 minutes. Baseline normal rule creators and alert on new rulesets targeting message hiding or exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Following Token-Based Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access.' New device registrations indicate persistence consolidation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registrations (Intune/Azure AD Join) occurring within 5–30 minutes of device code authentication or successful token access from suspicious IP/location. Cross-reference device registration events with atypical sign-in anomalies from the same user in the same window.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Referencing Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers.' Initial access vector is explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or homograph variants, combined with urgency/social engineering language. Alert on click-through events from those emails, then correlate with device code auth success in user's AAD logs within 10 minutes of click.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Cookie Capture via External Proxy (Cookie Link Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies secondary attack vector: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' This is MFA-evasive credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sign-in attempts where the user's browser is redirected to attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure (homograph domains, subdomain hijacking) before reaching Microsoft login. Alert on successful MFA from external IP/ASN pools, then token usage from entirely different geolocation, indicating session cookie/token interception.

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequence: Device Code Auth → Multi-App Access → Inbox Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates full-account compromise chain: 'full access to their account...including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms, which are then used to steal data.' Detection should chain multiple events.

Alert if sequence occurs from non-corporate geolocation.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Campaign Detection via Payload Staging and Redirection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate hijacked Ghost sites for redirect chains to known ClickFix infrastructure (fake Windows Update, antivirus warnings, crypto scam landing pages). suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Account Creation or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites suggests attacker created backdoor admin accounts or escalated privileges post-exploitation. No use case for detecting unauthorized admin activity in Ghost.

Alert on password resets for high-privilege Ghost accounts during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk Website Compromise Pattern Detection (700+ Site Threshold)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 700+ sites affected—a multi-stage campaign signal. No use case for detecting attacker infrastructure or C2 that controls mass-compromised sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 or attacker callback infrastructure by detecting common outbound patterns from Ghost instances: single domain/IP receiving callbacks from >50 distinct Ghost sites, beacon frequencies consistent with malware C2 (hourly, daily), or shared malicious domain registrations across victim hosts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Reputation Score Manipulation via Shared CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'bypass domain reputation security controls' using CDN infrastructure. This is a clear attack pattern—domains hosted on legitimate CDN shared IPs inherit trust, allowing malicious domains to evade reputation blocklists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when newly registered or low-reputation domains resolve to shared CDN IP ranges known for hosting high-volume/mixed-trust content. Correlate domain registration age, WHOIS privacy flags, and DNS query patterns with reputation scores that lag behind manual threat research.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Traffic Concentration on Shared CDN Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CDN abuse as exploitation mechanism. Legitimate users distribute across many CDN PoPs; coordinated attack traffic from attacker infrastructure should concentrate on fewer CDN endpoints, violating geographic and temporal distribution norms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish CDN traffic baseline by geographic distribution of source IPs and PoP selection. Flag endpoint traffic from single source IP/ASN that deviates sharply from user baseline, especially when paired with known malicious ASNs or residential proxy ranges.

suggestion.title: Domain Reputation Mismatch: High-Trust CDN IP with Malicious Domain Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Attackers abuse 'shared CDN infrastructure'—leveraging the CDN's legitimate reputation while hosting malicious content. Detection gap: domains on trusted CDN IPs should still alert if WHOIS, SSL certificate, or DNS registrant metadata flags anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CDN IP reputation feeds and cross-reference with domain metadata (registrant history, certificate issuer, DNS TTL anomalies). Alert when a domain on a high-trust CDN IP exhibits low-trust metadata (bulletproof hosting registrar, recent domain age, privacy-masking registrant info).

suggestion.title: Rapid Domain Generation and CDN IP Pairing
suggestion.rationale: CDN abuse is effective precisely because attackers can rotate malicious domains quickly while reusing the CDN's static IP reputation. Missing detection: alert on high-frequency domain creation + immediate resolution to same CDN endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PassiveDNS or internal DNS logs for clusters of newly observed domains (age < 7 days) resolving to a single CDN IP or narrow IP range. Establish thresholds: N domains on one CDN IP within T time window, especially if historical data shows that IP serving legitimate single-tenant domains.

suggestion.title: Cross-Border Outbound Connections via CDN Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: CDN used to 'bypass' controls. Attackers route command-and-control traffic through the CDN to evade geofencing and IP-reputation blocks. Missing detection: internal hosts establishing outbound connections to CDN that then tunnel to blocked geographies or known malicious infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound firewall allows to legitimate CDN IPs with TLS/SSL decryption logs or endpoint telemetry revealing internal hosts accessing non-CDN-served content (e.g., suspicious hostnames in SNI fields, non-CDN HTTP Host headers). Flag tunneling patterns via legitimate CDN IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Postinstall Script Downloads Executable to /tmp with System Service Name
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'postinstall scripts...retrieve a binary...save it to the victim's system under the filename `/tmp/.sshd`...uses `chmod +x` to make the file executable'. This is the core attack vector with no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify postinstall script execution (npm install, composer install) followed by curl/wget with output redirects, chmod +x on /tmp files matching dot-prefix system daemon names (e.g., .sshd, .ssh, .systemd). Correlate parent process and command timeline within seconds.

suggestion.title: Curl with TLS Verification Disabled Downloading from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'Downloads binary named `fvbs.network` using `curl` with TLS verification disabled'—explicit indicator of malicious behavior that should trigger detection but was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect curl/wget invocations with --insecure, -k, or similar TLS-bypass flags, especially when downloading from GitHub releases or other external sources. High fidelity if spawned from package manager contexts or npm/composer postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Background Process Execution with Output Suppression from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Launches the binary silently in background with output suppression'—specific evasion technique (ampersand backgrounding, redirects to /dev/null) that should be detected as abnormal within postinstall script context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for background process spawning (trailing &) combined with stdout/stderr redirection (> /dev/null 2>&1) originating from npm/composer postinstall script execution. Unexpected background process lifecycle in package manager context is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies `dependency_cache_sync` as 'found in GitHub Actions workflows' injected into malicious commits on dev-* branches. This supply-chain vector targeting CI/CD infrastructure was not recognized by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflow file modifications (.github/workflows/*.yml) introducing unexpected dependencies or download commands, especially in dev-prefixed branches. Flag commits introducing `dependency_cache_sync` or similar cache-manipulation steps that precede postinstall hook modifications.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package Repository Branches Targeting Version Pinning Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack spreads 'through upstream GitHub branches (`dev-main`, `dev-master`, `dev`), ensuring continued exposure through branch-tracking package versions'. This persistence mechanism via version-tracking was not identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package installations specifying dev-* branch versions (e.g., @dev-main in composer.json, @next in npm). Cross-reference installed package versions with repository commit history, flagging commits that introduce postinstall script modifications or unusual dependencies within 48 hours of installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Dynamic Extension (.pyd) Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'now ships as .pyd and .so files to evade script detection.' .pyd files are compiled Python extensions rarely delivered to end users legitimately. Pipeline missed this primary evasion vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .pyd files executing from user-writable paths, temp directories, or without corresponding source .py files. Correlate execution with parent Python process or script interpreter. Flag .pyd files unsigned or signed by untrusted publishers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Shared Object (.so) Loading from Non-Standard Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights .so files as delivery mechanism to 'evade script detection.' Shared objects loaded by user-mode processes from non-standard paths are rare and indicate evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .so files loaded by non-system processes from user-writable or temp locations. Correlate with process execution outside standard library paths. Flag .so loads with no preceding package manager activity.

suggestion.title: InvisibleFerret Malware Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Named threat (InvisibleFerret) appears in title but pipeline failed to extract as IOC or create malware-specific detection use case. Malware names are primary indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement known-bad matching for InvisibleFerret indicators (file hashes, C2 infrastructure, associated filenames). Alert on delivery via email, web download, or fileshare. Correlate with .pyd/.so execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Binary Module Delivery to Bypass Script Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Core attack stated explicitly: binary packaging to 'evade script detection.' This is T1027 obfuscation + defense_evasion. Pipeline failed to map to defense_evasion phase or generate detection for obfuscation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of compiled Python/shared object modules via non-standard distribution channels. Monitor for process creation from .pyd/.so modules with suspicious command-line arguments or unusual parent-child relationships. Flag execution without corresponding Python interpreter.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Compiled Module Masquerading as Legitimate Python Library
suggestion.rationale: Malware masquerades as .pyd/.so extensions (T1036) to hide true intent. Attack explicitly leverages compilation to obscure payload from script-based detection methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or untrusted-signed .pyd/.so files with names resembling legitimate libraries (scipy, numpy, pandas). Cross-reference filenames against canonical PyPI package repositories. Flag loads from non-standard Python site-packages paths or when parent process is non-development context (Office, browser).

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoned Malware Installer Download Detected
suggestion.rationale: Core attack premise: 'SEO Poisoning to Deliver Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer.' No use case captures detection of suspicious installer downloads following search-engine-referer clicks to known-malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads (.exe with SQL Developer/Oracle branding) from non-official hosts, preceded by HTTP Referer headers from search engines. Correlate domain reputation and age. Flag if target host has no legitimate SQL developer tooling installed.

suggestion.title: Execution of Masqueraded Installer Post-Download
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies delivery vehicle is 'Fake SQL Developer Malware Installer' — execution of the binary is the immediate post-delivery step. No use case addresses process execution of masqueraded binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .exe process execution matching SQL Developer/SQL tooling names spawned from user-writable directories (Downloads, Temp, Desktop). Validate against legitimate Oracle/vendor certificate chains and check file hash against VirusTotal.

suggestion.title: Browser-Initiated Installer Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: SEO poisoning attack pattern: user clicks search result → browser downloads file → user executes installer. Article describes end-to-end delivery flow but no parent-child process detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes (chrome.exe, msedge.exe) with child process spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe/explorer.exe that then create or execute .exe files from Downloads/Temp with masqueraded software names. Correlate browser history against malicious domain list.

suggestion.title: Post-Installer C2 Beaconing to Iranian APT Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: CRIT severity and malware installer delivery pattern imply payload persistence and C2 communication. Article title signals full execution chain; no command-and-control detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from hosts executing masqueraded SQL-developer installers for suspicious POST requests, non-standard ports, and encoded payloads. Correlate with known Iranian APT C2 domain/IP indicators once article IOCs are available.

suggestion.title: Legitimate vs. Malicious Installer Hash Discrimination
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Fake SQL Developer' delivery—requires file integrity checks. Pipeline provided no hash IOCs or executable-reputation baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain allowlist of legitimate SQL Developer/SQL Server installer hashes from official Oracle/Microsoft CDNs. Alert on .exe files with matching filenames but unknown or known-malicious hashes. Cross-check digital signatures and publisher metadata.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment to KnowledgeDeliver Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BLUEBEAM web shell deployment post-exploitation. No UC detects file creation in web-accessible directories following the RCE. Expected persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable file creation (.php, .jsp, .aspx, .py) in KnowledgeDeliver web root directories, upload folders, or other web-accessible paths. Correlate with process events from web server or application processes. True positives will show exploitation followed by file write within seconds.

suggestion.title: Post-Web-Shell Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes web shell deployment enabling command execution. Expected discovery/enumeration phase (whoami, ls, ps, etc.) after shell placement. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation spawned by web server processes (apache, nginx, iis) or child processes of KnowledgeDeliver. Alert on shell interpreters or system utilities in command line. High fidelity if preceded by suspicious web server log entries or web root file writes.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Initial access vector (zero-day RCE) is the entry point. No detection for exploitation attempts against KnowledgeDeliver endpoints. Article specifies zero-day in LMS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests to known vulnerable KnowledgeDeliver endpoints (once disclosed) or requests with unusual payloads, encoding, or parameters targeting LMS functionality. Flag oversized POST bodies or content-type mismatches to LMS endpoints.

suggestion.title: BLUEBEAM Malware Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names BLUEBEAM as the deployed payload. Pipeline produced zero IOCs, including no malware hash, process name, or behavioral indicators for BLUEBEAM. Should cross-reference against threat feeds and file execution events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file creation/execution events against known BLUEBEAM signatures (hashes from threat intelligence feeds, process names, file paths, registry modifications). Alert on any hash match or behavioral indicators (C2 communication patterns, persistence mechanisms) associated with BLUEBEAM.

suggestion.title: Rapid System Discovery Commands Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Typical post-exploitation workflow includes discovery (whoami, id, uname, ps, ifconfig, netstat). Expected after web shell placement. No detection generated for this reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of system enumeration commands executed in short succession from web server processes or unusual parent processes. High fidelity if correlated with recent web shell creation or unusual HTTP requests to application endpoints.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory-Only Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body describe 'memory-only RAT' deployment—requires detection for code injection and process hollowing patterns. Memory-only malware evasion is the core attack mechanism and should trigger UC for unsigned code execution in process address space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation patterns consistent with RemotePE deployment: legitimate system process (e.g., explorer.exe, svchost.exe) spawning without command-line args, followed by anomalous memory write activity. Alert on unsigned DLL injection into process memory from external source or process clone with memory access.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Spearphishing Payload Delivery to Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes campaign to Lazarus targeting financial and crypto firms—Lazarus historically uses spearphishing with malicious attachments or links as initial access. Article context establishes targeting pattern but likely contains email indicators or delivery method details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails from external sources reaching financial/crypto sector employees with macro-enabled documents, suspicious archives, or shortened URLs. Correlate with rapid process creation (Office → rundll32/powershell) and unsigned DLL load from %temp%. Raise alert if detected process contacts known/suspected C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP/VNC in Financial Networks Post-RemotePE
suggestion.rationale: Article targets financial institutions where RDP/VNC lateral movement is standard APT behavior post-compromise. RemotePE RAT enables command execution for attacker to pivot internally—missing UC for anomalous remote desktop or VNC sessions from compromised hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP/VNC connections initiated from newly-compromised hosts (RemotePE execution sources) to high-value financial servers (domain controllers, exchange, databases). Flag if connection source has no historical RDP use or if lateral movement occurs within minutes of initial RemotePE execution.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping from LSASS Post-RemotePE Execution
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE RAT grants attacker command execution; next step in financial breach is credential harvesting via LSASS memory dumping. Article context of financial targeting implies subsequent T1003.001 activity, but no UC captures this critical step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to LSASS from uncommon parent processes (rundll32, powershell, cmd spawned by system services). Alert on LSASS memory reads shortly after RemotePE execution window. Correlate with suspicious replication service or credential manager use (Wdigest, SSPI).

suggestion.title: RemotePE C2 Beacon to Malicious Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT requires C2 communication to receive commands and exfiltrate data. Article title establishes RAT deployment but likely contains C2 domains, IPs, or protocol signatures. Missing UC to detect command channel establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS requests from financial sector hosts to newly-registered or suspicious domains (especially .ru, .cn TLDs or fast-flux indicators). Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from RemotePE execution sources to atypical destinations or known C2 indicators. Alert if beacon traffic shows regular interval patterns (e.g., every 5–60 seconds) typical of RAT callbacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Office Macro or Script Execution Triggering RemotePE
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE deployment in financial breach likely preceded by Office macro or script execution from spearphishing payload. Article context suggests macro-enabled document or VB script as delivery vector, but no UC captures macro→RAT execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Office process (Word, Excel) spawning PowerShell, cmd, rundll32, or regsvr32 with command-line arguments containing encoded payloads or suspicious registry modifications. Correlate with rapid file writes to %appdata% or %temp%. Escalate if process tree includes network communication to unknown IP within 30 seconds of macro execution.

suggestion.title: Trojanized StellarMonSetup.exe Distribution and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'trojanized installer `StellarMonSetup.exe` (actually GoToResolve RAT) masquerading as a cryptocurrency wallet, harvesting seed phrases.' Pipeline missed entire malware distribution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution and file writes from StellarMonSetup.exe or variants. Alert on child process creation from this executable, particularly network communication or credential access APIs. Flag any process attempting to access seed phrase storage locations post-execution.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Credential Stuffing via Gemini-Generated Mutations
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'custom script sent victim emails to Gemini 2.5 Flash, generating up to 20 plausible password mutations per target...combined with purchased infostealer logs to crack 29 WordPress admin accounts.' No detection coverage despite clear attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity failed WordPress login attempts from single source preceded by email reconnaissance. Correlate failed login patterns with known infostealer leak indicators (known breached usernames/domains). Alert when >5 failed logins per target within 10 minutes using password variants (case swaps, year appends, symbol substitutions).

suggestion.title: Persistent Gemini Memory File Jailbreak via Context Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'established persistent jailbreak control by creating a memory file (`GEMINI.md`) that accumulated escalation instructions across sessions' and 'prompting in Russian bypassed safety guardrails.' Pipeline missed execution of prompt injection attack via LLM manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gemini API calls for consecutive prompts containing jailbreak indicators (self-referencing 'GEMINI.md' memory file, 'authorized pentester' context claims, repeated Russian-language prompts after English refusals). Flag patterns of prompt escalation where refusals are followed by language-switched retry or privilege context redefinition.

suggestion.title: Seed Phrase and Wallet Address Exfiltration from Trojanized Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'harvesting seed phrases and crypto wallet addresses' leading to 40+ compromised wallets and full draining of at least one wallet. No detection for cryptographic material exfiltration despite explicit impact description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process memory access patterns consistent with reading from clipboard/temp files containing seed phrase-like strings (48-128 character hex/word sequences matching BIP39 patterns). Monitor for systematic enumeration of wallet application data directories (MetaMask, Exodus, hardware wallet sync folders). Correlate with network exfiltration of base64-encoded key material.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to Identified GoToResolve Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides four C2 IP addresses (213.165.51.115, 34.34.57.141, 34.34.81.129, 35.192.41.201) attributed to 'GoToResolve RAT infrastructure.' No detection use case despite concrete IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound connection from affected systems to known GoToResolve C2 IPs. Correlate with StellarMonSetup.exe execution timeline. Flag if communication occurs on non-standard ports (likely command obfuscation). Monitor for DNS queries to domains resolving to these IPs.

suggestion.title: Telegram-Based Credential Distribution and Social Engineering Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies @americanpatriotus (17k subscribers), @QFS_Terminal_Bot, and @USGuardianEagle as operational channels for 'subscriber engagement & fraud tool' and influence operations. No detection for social platform C2 or credential exfiltration channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor user device Telegram activity for joins to identified channels (@americanpatriotus, @QFS_Terminal_Bot, @USGuardianEagle). Alert on automated bot interaction patterns (rapid message consumption, credential paste detection). Correlate Telegram access with preceding credential compromise. Flag if corporate device connects to Telegram bots offering password 'recovery' or 'verification' services.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Malicious Package Installation from npm/PyPI/CratesIO
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO.' This is T1195.001 (Supply Chain Compromise). Pipeline failed to generate even a baseline UC for package repository compromise despite it being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious package manager operations: npm install/yarn add of packages from untrusted sources, PyPI pip install commands with unusual package names (typosquatting, near-duplicate names), cargo build executing during installation. Alert on unexpected process spawning from node_modules, site-packages, or target/ directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Malicious Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Credential-Stealing Malware.' Once malicious package is installed and executed, attacker steals credentials. Article body (if retrievable) likely describes credential exfiltration mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process execution from package manager contexts attempting to enumerate or read credential stores: ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, Windows Credential Manager access, environment variable dumping. Monitor for unexpected child processes of npm/python/cargo install reading sensitive file paths or accessing credential APIs.

suggestion.title: Automated Credential Exfiltration via C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware implies data exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. Should detect outbound communication from package-installed code to suspicious destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous network connections initiated by processes spawned during/after package installation. Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP to newly-registered or suspicious domains, abnormal DNS queries from node_modules or script execution contexts, and base64-encoded credential data in network payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Script Execution in Package Manifests
suggestion.rationale: npm, PyPI, Cargo all support hook scripts executed during install (postinstall, setup.py scripts). Malicious packages likely abuse these hooks. Article likely details this execution vector but pipeline missed it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json postinstall/preinstall/postuninstall scripts, setup.py egg_info commands, and Cargo build scripts for suspicious shell commands: base64 decoding, curl/wget to external URLs, environment variable access, credential file reads. Alert on process trees showing shell spawned from npm/python/cargo processes.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Dependency Confusion in Package Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use typosquatting (misspelled package names) or dependency confusion (same name on public vs private repo). Article likely mentions which packages were impersonated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs for installation of packages with names similar to popular libraries but with typos or unicode tricks. Alert on packages that depend on unusual or newly-created upstream packages. Cross-reference package names against allowlists of known legitimate packages.

suggestion.title: TrapDoor Campaign: Multi-Ecosystem Supply Chain Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'TrapDoor' and multi-platform scope (npm+PyPI+Cargo) indicates coordinated attack. Pipeline should have flagged this as specific threat actor campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installations of confirmed malicious TrapDoor packages across all three ecosystems within organization. Correlate package installation events with subsequent credential access, C2 beacons, and lateral movement attempts. Alert on any organizational machine installing known-malicious TrapDoor packages or near-duplicate variants.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states 'Execute Arbitrary Code and Compromise Systems'—exploitation vector yields code execution within or via 7-Zip context. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 7z.exe, 7zG.exe, 7zFM.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or regsvcs.exe with suspicious arguments. Baseline 7-Zip performs only archive enumeration; child processes with network capability or LOLBin patterns indicate payload execution post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Extraction and Immediate Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: vulnerability in 7-Zip triggers code execution. No detection suggested for the extraction→execution chain ('Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code' requires extraction of hostile archive content).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 7-Zip archive file access with immediate child process spawning (<2 sec). Flag extraction of exe, dll, scr, vbs, bat from archive followed by execution from temp paths. High-confidence indicator: archive extraction + WriteFile + CreateProcess in compressed timeline.

suggestion.title: Network Connections Originating from 7-Zip Process
suggestion.rationale: Title promises 'system compromise'—compromised 7-Zip initiates C2 or stage-2 payload retrieval. No network-phase detection generated despite clear attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: 7-Zip is archival tool; outbound connections are anomalous. Alert on any TCP/UDP from 7z*.exe processes post-exploitation window. Prioritize non-standard ports, non-HTTPS protocols, and destinations without correlation to known package manager or legitimate update infrastructure.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip File Delivery via Email or Web with Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability triggered by user opening hostile archive. 'Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code' implies delivery via social engineering. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for malicious file distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag 7z/zip arrivals with obfuscation markers: double extensions, mismatched content-type headers, archives from untrusted senders, or immediate extraction post-download. Trigger medium-confidence alert on archive received + archive opened + suspicious child process within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: 7-Zip Heap Corruption or Memory Exploitation Signals
suggestion.rationale: Title uses plural 'Vulnerabilities'—suggests memory safety issues (buffer/heap overflow common in parsing bugs). No memory-anomaly detection proposed despite code execution via memory corruption being likely vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor 7-Zip for memory anomalies: abnormal heap allocations during archive parsing, CreateRemoteThread from 7z context, or process crashes followed by resurrection. If vulnerability is heap overflow, watch for exception codes 0xC0000374 (heap corruption) or 0x80000003 (breakpoint) in archive parsing callstacks.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized termsrv.dll Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states: 'Cloud Atlas APT Group Modifies termsrv.dll to Enable Multiple RDP Sessions on Victim Hosts.' Pipeline generated zero file integrity monitoring or DLL modification detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to termsrv.dll in System32/SysWOW64 directories via file integrity monitoring. Establish baseline hashes and alert on changes. Correlate file modifications with DLL load events and unexpected process access to RDP-related binaries.

suggestion.title: Detect RDP Session Limit Registry Modifications
