suggestion.rationale: Enabling concurrent RDP sessions requires setting HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\fSingleUserSession to 0. Article describes this as core persistence mechanism but pipeline created no registry monitoring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to fSingleUserSession registry key and related RDP configuration registry paths. Baseline value should be 1 on production systems. Changes enabling concurrent sessions are anomalous and should trigger investigation.

suggestion.title: Detect Multiple Concurrent RDP Sessions from Single Source IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack purpose as 'enable multiple RDP sessions' (title, description). This lateral movement effect requires concurrent session detection but pipeline missed RDP session anomaly use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple simultaneous logon events (EventID 4624, Logon Type 10) from single source IP within time windows. Baseline legitimate concurrent RDP usage per user and alert on sustained deviation. Correlate with termsrv.dll and registry modifications.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Write Access to System DLL Files by Non-System Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Modifying a protected system DLL requires compromise of privileged context. Article indicates targeted modification of core RDP component but pipeline failed to create privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-SYSTEM/ADMIN accounts attempt write or execute access to protected system DLLs in System32. Termsrv.dll modifications by domain users are high-fidelity indicators. Correlate with prior exploitation or privilege escalation technique detections.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Injection into Terminal Server Services
suggestion.rationale: DLL modification implies code execution within RDP process context. Article focuses on termsrv.dll patching suggesting injection/hooking mechanism but pipeline generated no process injection detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious inter-process handles, memory access patterns, and unsigned DLL loads targeting termsrv.exe, svchost.exe hosting RDP services. Detect unusual API calls (WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread) originating from user processes targeting RDP services.

suggestion.title: Telegram C2 Channel Subscription and Message Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'cybercriminals use Telegram channels to sell'—Telegram channels are the explicit command and control infrastructure. Article describes active marketplace transactions over these channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Telegram API calls or telemetry showing subscription to channels with keyword patterns (account, verified, mule, bank, fintech, sale, buy, credentials). Correlate Telegram process execution with credential-handling processes (password managers, bank apps, email).

suggestion.title: Verified Account Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'verified bank and fintech mule accounts'—accounts are verified before sale, implying systematic credential collection and validation. No detection logic for bulk account compromise or verification testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential validation patterns: multiple failed logins from same IP followed by successful logins at odd hours; logins from datacenter/VPN IPs followed by account lockout resets; accounts with no prior activity suddenly logging in from geographic anomalies and then used for transfers.

suggestion.title: Mule Account Registration and Rapid Activation
suggestion.rationale: Accounts must be created and verified for sale. Article implies bulk account creation pipeline. No use case for detecting burst account registration or accounts with artificial sign-up patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag batch account creation from single IP/device; accounts registered with identical or pattern-matching PII; newly registered accounts bypassing MFA or step-up authentication; account setup followed immediately by credential export or API token generation.

suggestion.title: Money Mule Transaction Patterns via Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Mule accounts are used to 'move money' after purchase. Article phrase 'mule accounts' implies impact phase includes fund transfers. No detection for fraud execution via purchased accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accounts with zero transaction history executing multiple transfers to external accounts in short timeframes; transfers inconsistent with account holder profile; rapid fund movement after login from anomalous geography; account used for transfers then dormant for days.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Receipt Correlated with Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Marketplace implies payment in cryptocurrency. Article mentions 'sell'—payouts occur after account listing. No correlation between credential compromise timeline and blockchain payment settlement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on endpoints visiting cryptocurrency exchange sites (Coinbase, Kraken, Binance) within hours of Telegram C2 channel activity and credential access events. Flag inbound cryptocurrency transfers to exchange accounts owned by employees or devices linked to credential harvesting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code Authentication Flow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it on Microsoft's login page via phishing and social engineering' — device code flows where authenticating user differs from code requester is attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code flows where user completing authentication differs from device initiating request, multiple device codes generated per user in short windows, device code completions from IPs inconsistent with user baseline, or device code flows immediately preceding mailbox access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Inbox Rule Creation Following Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity' — explicit post-compromise persistence and defense evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbox rules created from unusual IPs, rules with deletion/hiding logic for incident response keywords, rules forwarding to external domains, or rule creation within minutes of suspicious authentication event.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Entra Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network' — indicates post-auth persistence and lateral movement enablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registrations outside normal IT provisioning, registrations from new geolocations, multiple device enrollments per user in 24 hours, or devices registered then immediately used for sign-in without typical onboarding activity.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OAuth Access Token Usage Post Device-Code Auth
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges' — attacker gains MFA-bypass token requiring behavioral anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens issued after device code flow used immediately by different IP/user agent, tokens accessing resources not in user's baseline, tokens used to perform administrative actions, or tokens active concurrently with user's legitimate sessions.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Targeting Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal' — initial access vector requiring email and web gateway detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails containing device code portal links (microsoft.com/devicelogin or lookalikes), user clicks from external email, portal visits preceded by phishing detection, or campaigns with device code lure language and urgency tactics.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie Capture via Attacker-Controlled Proxy (Cookie Link Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges' — man-in-the-middle attack requiring traffic pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication requests routed through unexpected proxies, SSL certificate mismatches on Microsoft domains, authenticated cookies appearing in non-Microsoft infrastructure logs, or session tokens captured by attacker IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 exploitation attempt against Ghost CMS endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 is being exploited. This is the initial compromise vector for 700+ sites; essential for detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to known Ghost CMS vulnerable endpoints with known CVE-2026-26980 exploit payloads. Look for POST requests to admin/API endpoints with unusual parameter patterns or SQL injection/template injection markers. Correlate with failed/successful web server responses indicating code execution.

suggestion.title: ClickFix malware process execution from Ghost site root
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites were hijacked 'for ClickFix attacks'—post-exploitation payload execution is the impact goal. Need detections for ClickFix process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix-related process names or parent-child relationships where web server processes (httpd, nginx, php-fpm) spawn powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or known ClickFix loader executables. Look for unusual process execution from web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Webshell or persistent backdoor installation on Ghost CMS
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites requires persistence mechanism beyond a single exploit. Should detect new web files created post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS installation directories for unexpected new .php, .js, or .hbs template files created after CVE exploitation timeframes. Correlate with web server access logs showing POST requests to content/themes/uploads directories followed by GET requests to newly created files from C2 IP ranges.

suggestion.title: C2 communication from compromised Ghost CMS instance
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix requires command-and-control communication. Article mentions hijacking sites 'for ClickFix attacks' implying active C2 channels from compromised instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound HTTPS/HTTP beaconing from web server process addresses to known ClickFix C2 domains or newly registered domains with Ghost-related reverse DNS. Look for beaconing intervals and suspicious User-Agent headers originating from web server contexts.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS admin account creation post-CVE exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining access to 700+ sites requires credential creation. Should detect new admin/privileged accounts created after exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin console logs and database audit trails for new user creation events with admin roles occurring after CVE-2026-26980 exploitation timestamps. Correlate with abnormal IP geolocation if available.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS theme/plugin file modification for payload injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hijacking—attackers must modify site content or infrastructure. Template/theme injection is common Ghost exploitation technique for persistent malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to Ghost theme files (content/themes/*.hbs) with timestamps correlated to CVE exploitation. Look for theme files writing to temp directories, adding iframe injection code, or spawning child processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious domain resolution to CDN IP with weak domain reputation
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls.' Attackers register malicious domains on legitimate CDN IPs (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly) to inherit IP reputation while domain itself is unknown/malicious. Detection gap: no use case flags domains with mismatched signals (whitelisted CDN IP + newly registered/malware-associated domain).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS resolution events: domain resolves to known CDN IP blocks (Cloudflare ASN 13335, Akamai, Fastly) where domain age is <30 days, reputation score is low/unknown (or flagged by threat feeds), but IP is whitelisted. Tune out legitimate CDN zones (CDN.example.com). Alert on: CDN IP + suspicious domain + no legitimate hostname pattern.

suggestion.title: Executable delivery from newly registered CDN-hosted domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery via CDN infrastructure. 'Abuse Shared CDN Infrastructure'—implies executables hosted on trusted IPs. No detection for EXE/DLL/PS1 downloads from CDN-hosted attacker domains. Phrase: attackers 'bypass' controls—implies successful payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on binary file downloads (EXE, DLL, MSI, PS1) from domains hosted on CDN IP ranges where domain age <30 days and user agent is non-standard (not Chrome auto-update, Windows Update, etc.). Baseline: CDNs primarily serve static content; executables are rare. Flag: executable + new CDN domain + suspicious user agent = likely malware staging.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing over whitelisted CDN-hosted domain
suggestion.rationale: Shared CDN infrastructure abuse enables C2 callbacks to succeed because IP reputation is good. Article: 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls'—implies reputation-based C2 filtering fails. No use case for periodic outbound HTTPS to newly registered CDN domains with C2 timing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect regular outbound HTTPS connections to domains hosted on CDN IPs where domain age <90 days and beacon timing is consistent (e.g., every 3600s, off-hours preference). Correlate: domain flagged malicious by sinkhole feeds, but traffic succeeds because CDN IP is globally whitelisted. Anomaly: low-entropy, low-volume periodic traffic to new CDN domain.

suggestion.title: Phishing landing page hosted on CDN to evade URL filtering
suggestion.rationale: CDN abuse enables phishing to bypass reputation checks. Article: 'Bypass Domain Reputation Security Controls'—phishing URLs on trusted CDN IPs are unblocked by legacy filters. No detection for phishing HTML/form submission patterns on newly registered CDN domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests to CDN-hosted domains (<30 days old) whose response contains phishing indicators: HTML forms with 'password', 'username', 'PIN' fields; action URLs pointing off-CDN to attacker infrastructure; CSS/markup spoofing legitimate brand (bank, payment processor, SSO provider). Correlate with email delivery: phishing URL in email → CDN IP → phishing HTML signature = confirmed attack chain.

suggestion.title: Bulk domain registration abuse on single CDN for threat campaign infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Shared CDN Infrastructure'—attacker registers multiple malicious domains on same CDN free/shared tier. Detection gap: no use case for bulk registration patterns or clustering of new domains on same CDN IP/ASN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk domain registration within 7-day window: 5+ domains registered to same email/registrar resolving to same CDN IP block or within 3 hops. Cross-reference parent CDN domain (whitelisted) against child domains (reputation unknown/malicious). Alert threshold: 5+ new domains on same CDN netblock in 7 days with no legitimate explanation (e.g., not a multi-tenant SaaS provider).

suggestion.title: Malware Masquerading as SSH Binary During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly cites 'SSH-like filename' obfuscation. Pipeline extracted zero defense-evasion detections despite this being the attack's signature technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of executable files during package manager execution (apt, yum, rpm) with names mimicking SSH binaries (/usr/bin/ssh*, /usr/sbin/sshd*) or SSH config tools. Validate against legitimate SSH package file manifests; unexpected creations indicate masquerading.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Attack occurs 'during package installation'—T1195 supply-chain vector. Pipeline identified zero initial-access phase despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager retrieval and installation (apt-get install, yum install) followed by execution of unexpected child processes or creation of binaries in system paths. Cross-reference package SHA256 against legitimate repository manifests for tampering detection.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Persistence via Masqueraded System Binary
suggestion.rationale: Payload hidden under SSH filename likely persists across reboots if placed in startup locations or system directories. Pipeline missed persistence phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file placement in SSH/system startup contexts (/etc/ssh, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /etc/rc.d equivalents) immediately following package manager completion. Alert if file signature or metadata diverges from known SSH binaries.

suggestion.title: Execution via Package Manager Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates payload executes during installation—T1204 user-driven execution via package scripts. Pipeline found no execution techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from dpkg/rpm post-install script contexts, especially network-related activity (curl, wget, nc) or shell execution. Correlate with SSH-like filenames created in same process tree.

suggestion.title: Python .pyd Extension Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware now 'ships as .pyd' files to evade detection. .pyd files are compiled Python extensions on Windows that execute arbitrary code; no use case was generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python.exe, python3) loading or importing .pyd files from user-writable or suspicious directories. Monitor for .pyd files created or modified in site-packages, temp dirs, or AppData. Flag unsigned .pyd binaries or those with suspicious compilation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Linux .so Shared Object Loading via Python
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies .so files (shared object libraries) as the Linux equivalent distribution mechanism; no Linux-side detection was generated. .so files loaded by Python can execute native code while evading script-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .so file creation in Python lib directories, /tmp, or user home directories. Alert on dlopen/ld.so.1 syscalls loading .so files from non-standard paths. Flag Python processes spawning child processes immediately after .so import (indicator of native code execution).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Compiled Binary Module Import
suggestion.rationale: Core evasion stated explicitly: malware uses compiled binaries to 'evade script detection'. This is T1027 (Obfuscated Files). No use case addresses detection of suspicious compiled module characteristics (entropy, age, signing, parent process context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect recently-created compiled modules (.pyd, .so) with mismatched timestamps (compilation date >> creation date). Flag modules signed by untrusted issuers or unsigned entirely. Alert on compiled modules imported by processes not associated with legitimate development/package management.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python ctypes/ImportLib Usage
suggestion.rationale: Compiled .pyd/.so loading typically occurs via Python's ctypes, importlib, or ctypes.CDLL. Article does not mention delivery method, but no detection covers the programmatic import of compiled extensions from suspicious sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python scripts or interpreter arguments containing ctypes.CDLL, importlib, or direct .pyd/.so path references. Alert on import statements resolved to non-standard directories. Flag temporary Python scripts that immediately import compiled modules and then delete themselves.

suggestion.title: Detect downloads from fake software distribution sites (SQL Developer)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Users downloading from the fake site received a weaponized installer' from getsqldeveloper[.]com, the initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process executing downloads from getsqldeveloper[.]com or lookalike SQL Developer domains. Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for search results redirecting to unregistered vendor sites mimicking Oracle branding.

suggestion.title: Detect MiniFast backdoor IOC file hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 26+ SHA256 hashes for MiniFast samples. Hash-based detection is direct: '10fd541674adadfbba99b54280f7e59732746faf2b10ce68521866f737f1e46d' and similar known malware variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, execution, or transfer involving any MiniFast SHA256 hashes. Monitor for child processes spawned by sql-installer executables with suspicious command-line parameters.

suggestion.title: Monitor for AppDomain hijacking exploitation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states MiniFast exploits '.NET runtime loads application configuration files' to execute silently. This requires registry/config manipulation: 'AppDomain hijacking' is the explicit technique described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious writes to registry keys controlling AppDomain configuration (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NET Framework\policy, application config files modified outside Visual Studio). Monitor for unsigned/anomalous DLL injection into system-level processes.

suggestion.title: Detect scheduled task persistence from weaponized installers
suggestion.rationale: Article defense recommendation: 'Security teams should monitor for unexpected scheduled task changes,' indicating persistent backdoor uses scheduled tasks for execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scheduled task creation by suspicious SQL Developer installer processes or from SYSTEM context with hidden triggers. Monitor for tasks pointing to AppData, Temp, or obfuscated executable paths.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP C2 communication with Chrome User-Agent spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies MiniFast uses 'HTTP-based C2 communication with Chrome User-Agent spoofing' to blend with legitimate traffic. Monitor for this specific evasion signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes (DLLs, installers, rundll32) issuing HTTP requests with Chrome User-Agent string. Correlate with C2 domain IOCs (business-startup[.]org, ramiltonsfinance[.]com) and flag anomalous HTTP patterns from system processes.

suggestion.title: Monitor for SEO poisoning site access via search engines
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Achieved top rankings on Bing and DuckDuckGo for target search terms'—users finding fake site via search. Detect when corporate endpoints query and visit these poisoned search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS/HTTP access to getsqldeveloper[.]com, business-startup[.]org, and related infrastructure. Flag any user performing SQL Developer searches followed by navigation to non-Oracle domains within 10 minutes. Monitor for Bing/DuckDuckGo search referrers to these malicious sites.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Artifact Detection - BLUEBEAM Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BLUEBEAM web shell deployment via LMS zero-day exploit ('exploited to deploy BLUEBEAM Web Shell'). Zero detection rules generated despite clear post-exploitation artifact risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for web shell file write operations to web-accessible directories (e.g., /var/www, DocumentRoot) immediately following LMS process execution. Correlate with parent processes spawned from web server context (apache, nginx) executing interpreters (php, asp, jsp). BLUEBEAM signatures: look for shell-like script artifacts or suspicious encoded payloads in newly created web-accessible files.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies KnowledgeDeliver LMS as zero-day vector ('KnowledgeDeliver LMS Zero-Day'). No detection rule for exploit attempts against this product-specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request patterns to KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints for malformed payloads, path traversal attempts, or deserialization attacks. Flag requests with suspicious parameter encoding or unusually long POST bodies to admin/configuration endpoints. Correlate with subsequent out-of-band callbacks or file system modifications in LMS directories.

suggestion.title: Post-Web-Shell Execution - Child Process Spawning from Web Context
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment implies subsequent code execution for lateral movement or data exfiltration. Article does not detail post-shell actions, but detection gap exists for child process spawning from web server parents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) spawn non-standard children (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, curl, wget, nc). Baseline expected children by environment. Cross-reference with web server access logs to identify triggering HTTP requests. High-priority if spawned children attempt network communication or file system writes outside DocumentRoot.

suggestion.title: RemotePE RAT Process Execution from Script/Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'memory-only RAT' deployment—core evasion technique that bypasses file-based detection. Pipeline must detect scriptlet/inline code execution patterns typical of fileless malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned PowerShell/CScript/WScript processes spawning without corresponding script files on disk, or command-line execution of memory-resident payloads. Monitor for process creation with unusual parent chains (e.g., Office → Rundll32 → memory payload) combined with post-execution deletion or lack of on-disk artifacts.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Communication to RemotePE Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: RAT campaigns require C2 heartbeats and command delivery. Article's 'memory-only' design implies persistent command-and-control beaconing must be detected in network telemetry without relying on dropped malware files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from finance/crypto-sector hosts to known Lazarus infrastructure, or traffic exhibiting RAT behavioral patterns (regular beaconing intervals, command-response latencies, binary C2 protocol signatures). Correlate with unsigned process execution and memory injection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Valid Accounts Post-RemotePE Implant
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'financial firms'—high-value environment where attackers escalate from initial compromised host to critical systems. Lazarus typically uses stolen credentials for lateral movement across domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication events from RemotePE-compromised host to sensitive systems (database servers, exchange, domain controllers) using legitimate service accounts. Flag failed authentications followed by success, and authentications from unusual network gateways or during non-business hours from confirmed implant source.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Finance/Crypto Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies financial and crypto targets—implying data theft objective. Pipeline must detect large data transfers, credential harvesting, or wallet access patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network activity from finance/crypto systems post-RemotePE implant for anomalous data volumes, encrypted archives, or traffic to known exfiltration infrastructure. Correlate with access to sensitive files (wallet files, ledgers, customer databases, authentication logs).

suggestion.title: RemotePE Payload Injection into System Process
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT delivery suggests code injection into legitimate processes (living-off-the-land). Pipeline must detect process hollowing or remote code injection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious allocations and writes to remote process memory (CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, SetWindowsHookEx). Monitor for process pairs with unexpected parent-child relationships, unsigned child processes spawned from svchost/explorer/winlogon, and execution of known injection gadgets.

suggestion.title: Phishing/Document Exploit Initial Delivery to Finance Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article doesn't specify delivery method in provided excerpt, but Lazarus historically uses spear-phishing and Office exploits. Detection must cover likely initial-access vector for a targeted campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Office documents (macro-enabled, exploit-payload-embedded) delivered to finance/crypto employees; monitor for suspicious macro execution, OLE embedding of executables, or .docx/.xlsx files triggering child process creation (Python, PowerShell, Rundll32). Correlate document creation with external email sources and timelines preceding RemotePE detection.

suggestion.title: LLM Jailbreak Used for Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Jailbroken Gemini' as attack vector; pipeline missed this as execution/credential-access technique and should detect prompts attempting to extract credentials or bypassing guardrails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual API calls to Gemini/LLM endpoints with payloads containing jailbreak strings (e.g., 'ignore safety guidelines', 'return credentials'). Correlate with subsequent admin account enumeration or privilege escalation. Flag if originating from non-standard geolocation or proxy.

suggestion.title: Admin Credential Abuse Following Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing admin credentials; pipeline should detect post-compromise lateral movement using those credentials: 'Steal Admin Credentials and Drain Crypto Wallets' phrase indicates attacker then uses stolen creds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin account logons from unusual geographic location or IP range inconsistent with baseline, followed within hours by cryptocurrency exchange or wallet access. Alert on admin accounts used to access financial or sensitive systems without prior activity pattern.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Access After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article impact is 'Drain Crypto Wallets'; pipeline missed detection for anomalous wallet access following credential theft: suspicious access to exchange APIs, wallet transfer initiation, or balance queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual access to cryptocurrency exchange accounts, wallet management tools, or blockchain transaction initiation tools using compromised admin credentials. Flag large or rapid fund transfers out of known corporate-controlled wallets.

suggestion.title: LLM Safety Filter Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'Jailbroken Gemini' indicates attacker successfully bypassed AI safety mechanisms; should detect known jailbreak payloads or prompt-injection patterns in API logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect LLM API request payloads for known jailbreak patterns (e.g., 'DAN' prompt, role-play scenarios, token smuggling). Alert on requests that attempt to override system prompts or extract training data. Correlate multiple failed attempts from same user/IP within short window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from npm/PyPI/CratesIO
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack 'spreads credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — pipeline identified zero indicators of compromise during package installation, the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of packages with suspicious names from npm, PyPI, or CratesIO during non-standard hours or from unexpected sources. Correlate package installation processes with immediate outbound network connections to non-registry IP ranges or domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly labels attack as 'credential-stealing malware' — pipeline captured no detection for credential access or exfiltration behaviors expected during post-installation execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by package managers accessing credential stores (browser SQLite DBs, SSH keys, API token files), reading environment variables containing secrets, or performing unusual file reads from home directories. Detect subsequent network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack spreads 'via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — pipeline should detect indicators of malicious package registration such as name squatting, typosquatting, or compromised legitimate packages with unusual version jumps or metadata changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package manager API logs and registry metadata for rapid version releases, unusual dependency chains, new accounts uploading to popular packages, or packages with names similar to widely-used libraries.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware spreading via package managers — pipeline identified no execution-phase detections for setup scripts, post-install hooks, or build-time code execution typical of supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell or interpreter execution triggered during package installation (npm install, pip install, cargo build). Flag commands that access environment, modify shell initialization files, or reach external URLs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing attack may persist across developer machines and internal infrastructure — pipeline missed detection for lateral movement from developer workstations to internal assets using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential exfiltration timing with subsequent authentication attempts from non-standard geolocations or times. Flag lateral movement using credentials harvested at specific package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: SaaS Platform Unauthorized Access - Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article describes April 8, 2026 breach: 'unauthorized third party gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' in Salesforce environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce logins from new geographies, VPN/proxy ranges, credential stuffing patterns (rapid failures before success), and service account API token generation outside maintenance windows. Flag authentication attempts preceded by abnormal MFA failure rates.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Query and Export Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stolen over 600,000 records containing corporate data' from Salesforce; pipeline missed collection phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual volume of Salesforce API calls querying franchisee document repositories, bulk report exports, or mass field-level access. Alert on export activity during off-hours or by service accounts with no historical export patterns.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Customer PII Exfiltration from Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration of 'names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses' of '185,300 people' in a '9.4GB archive' via dark web.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass data transfers from Salesforce to external cloud storage or unknown destinations. Flag creation of large encrypted archives containing customer demographic fields. Monitor egress traffic volume anomalies from document repositories.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Dark Web Leak Site Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility' and 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay ransom.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web forums, ransomware leak-site aggregators, and ShinyHunters' known domains for appearance of '7-Eleven,' '7-11,' or franchisee data sale advertisements. Alert on extortion forum posts threatening public data release.

suggestion.title: Franchisee Document Repository Suspicious Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies breach 'limited to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' containing PII of 185k individuals; pipeline missed document-repository collection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor franchisee document store access for queries targeting demographic fields (name, DOB, email, phone, address) in bulk. Flag single-session retrieval of >50k documents. Detect archival or compression of franchisee folders by privileged or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Vulnerability Exploitation Post-Announcement
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CERT-In is recommending 12-hour patching for internet-facing flaws, implying active in-the-wild exploitation. Pipeline should flag monitoring for exploitation attempts within patching window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 401/403 → 200 transitions, SQL injection patterns, RCE payloads, or proof-of-concept exploitation signatures against known internet-facing services within 12 hours of patch release.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Reconnaissance and Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'AI-assisted attacks.' Pipeline should detect automated reconnaissance patterns consistent with LLM-driven enumeration (high-volume fuzzing, intelligent path traversal, parameter discovery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag anomalous User-Agent patterns (ChatGPT, Claude, API clients), high-frequency parameter fuzzing from single source, or linguistic patterns in request payloads suggesting LLM-generated queries.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Evasion or Rollback
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies defenders rushing to patch. Pipeline should detect attackers attempting to block, delay, or reverse patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on termination of patching services, modification of update configurations, or suspicious process activity coinciding with patch installation windows.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Service Exposure Increase
suggestion.rationale: CERT-In advisory on internet-facing flaws implies discovery phase targeting. Should detect newly exposed or misconfigured services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new internet-routable resources, security group/firewall rule changes opening ports 80/443/22/3306/5432, or service exposure outside trusted networks.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer Record Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance.' Must detect unusually large customer/CPNI record extraction operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk Salesforce export/deploy operations targeting customer object fields beyond baseline operational volumes, especially executed by non-standard service accounts or from unusual origins. Focus on customer name, phone, address, CPNI, and plan-info field access.

suggestion.title: Entra Account Compromise Post-Voice Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Detect post-vishing Entra compromise signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Entra accounts with MFA rejection/bypass followed by successful login from unexpected geography, or API calls (esp. to cloud SaaS) within hours of failed MFA. Baseline normal SSO patterns per role and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Single Credential Access to Multiple Distinct SaaS Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers use one compromised SSO to access 'Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox, and many others.' Detect lateral movement across SaaS via stolen credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single user or service principal accesses 5+ distinct unrelated SaaS platforms within 24 hours, especially if access deviates from baseline role. Correlate across Okta, Entra, and platform audit logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized OAuth Token Generation for Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: ShinyHunters 'breaching numerous integration companies to steal OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances.' Detect unauthorized token creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth token generation outside standard integration provisioning workflows, or tokens created by accounts not documented as integration owners. Monitor for token reuse across unusual IPs or user agents.

suggestion.title: CPNI Data Extraction by Non-Authorized Roles
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'customer proprietary network information (CPNI) data' exfiltrated. Detect inappropriate access to telecom customer protection data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on queries or exports of CPNI fields (phone type, plan info, service details) by accounts lacking documented telecom-ops or support justification. Baseline permitted CPNI access by role and detect outliers.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Export Exfiltration to External Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: data 'stolen' and posted to 'ShinyHunters data leak site.' Detect intentional exfiltration of bulk export to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large Salesforce export volume in audit logs with outbound transfers to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains. Monitor for bulk API retrieval (e.g., SOQL queries exporting millions of records) followed by data staging to attacker-controlled cloud storage or paste sites.

suggestion.title: Custom Linux Malware Execution on Edge Router via Spawned Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'custom Linux implant' deployment to edge routers. Execution of the malware binary or dropper is a critical detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual process spawning on edge routers, particularly non-standard binaries in /tmp, /var, or writable device-specific directories. Monitor for processes with minimal command-line arguments, parent processes that are legitimate services (sshd, cron, httpd), or binaries with recently-modified timestamps.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Linux Service or Scheduled Task Creation
suggestion.rationale: Custom implants on Linux devices require sustained presence mechanism. Article context implies long-dwell compromise on edge routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of /etc/systemd/system services, /etc/cron.d entries, or init scripts with non-standard names or pointing to unusual paths. Flag any service restarts immediately after creation or persistence entries that trigger C2-like outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Edge Router Remote Code Execution or Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Initial compromise vector for edge routers typically involves T1190 (public-facing application exploit) or T1133 (external remote services abuse).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing exploitation payloads, SQLi, command injection patterns, or known edge router CVE exploits targeting management interfaces. Monitor for successful authentication from geographically anomalous sources or multiple failed login attempts followed by success from same IP.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Edge Router to External IP
suggestion.rationale: Deployed custom Linux implant requires external command and control channel for operator interaction and secondary payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag consistent outbound connections from edge router to non-RFC1918 destinations, especially to China-linked ASN ranges or on non-standard ports (8080, 443, 9000, 10000). Monitor for DNS queries immediately before C2 connections or resolution of newly-registered domains with short TTLs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Edge Router to Internal Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article targets edge routers (network perimeter devices). Attackers will pivot to internal network via lateral movement from compromised perimeter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound SSH (port 22), Telnet (23), or RDP (3389) connections from edge router to internal IP ranges. Monitor for port scanning or OS fingerprinting patterns originating from edge router, or unusual tool deployment (scp, rsync, wget) to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Binary or Script Transfer to Edge Router
suggestion.rationale: Deployment of 'custom Linux implant' requires tool transfer mechanism. Article implies binary or script-based malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation in edge router directories with executable permissions, especially binaries transferred via wget, curl, scp, or HTTP PUT. Monitor for files created with no corresponding package manager event or unexpected size/entropy characteristics.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from cPanel User to Root via LiteSpeed Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be abused by any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' Core privilege escalation vector with root outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent is cPanel-related daemon (cpanel, cpsrvd, or /usr/local/cpanel/* child processes) and offspring executes with uid=0 or SYSTEM privileges. Correlate spawning from LiteSpeed plugin paths.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution with Root Privileges from cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' via the plugin interface. Script interpreters spawning from plugin context with root should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash, sh, perl, python spawning from /usr/local/cpanel/plugins/litespeed/* or similar plugin directories with root privileges. Include command-line keyword detection for script file loading or arbitrary argument passing.

suggestion.title: HTTP Exploitation Attempts Against cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin'—indicating web-facing interface. T1190 applies to initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel/Apache/Nginx logs for POST/GET to LiteSpeed plugin endpoints with abnormal parameters, encoding patterns, or error cascades indicating exploitation attempts. Flag repeated 40x/50x responses from /plugins/litespeed paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Asset Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation with federal patch due 2026-05-29 demands immediate asset exposure hunt. Article mentions 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference cPanel installations in asset inventory against LiteSpeed plugin version detection. Flag any version <[patched] as exploitable until confirmed patched. Prioritize publicly exposed cPanel instances.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attempt Against Drupal Database Abstraction Layer
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests' and 'Imperva has observed over 15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites.' No detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal endpoints (e.g., /admin, /api, /search) containing SQL syntax markers (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comment sequences) without prior successful authentication. Correlate request patterns with PostgreSQL error logs showing syntax errors in unexpected transactions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Followed by SQL Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the vulnerability is 'exploitable without authentication,' a key attack precursor. No UC addresses auth-bypass + injection chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where failed Drupal authentication attempts (HTTP 401/403) are immediately followed by requests containing SQL syntax or URL-encoded injection payloads from the same source IP, indicating exploitation of the auth-bypass flaw.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-SQL Injection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can potentially lead to information disclosure, privilege escalation, and even remote code execution.' No use case for detecting post-exploitation privilege escalation activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting SQL injection attempts against Drupal, monitor for database user privilege changes, sudoers file modifications, or process execution with elevated privileges (e.g., www-data/apache running as root or executing /bin/bash with UID 0) within 5 minutes of injection activity.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Attempt via Drupal SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names RCE as potential impact ('remote code execution') but pipeline generated no detection for post-injection code execution attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe) directly from Drupal web server processes (apache/www-data/nginx) or database processes (postgres/mysql) following successful SQL injection, especially commands accessing /tmp, /var/tmp, or touching suspicious files.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Drupal SQL Injection Information Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'information disclosure' as a direct impact of successful exploitation. No detection UC for data enumeration or exfiltration post-injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound connections or DNS queries from Drupal server immediately following SQL injection attempts, especially to non-whitelisted external IPs or DNS names, combined with database query logs showing SELECT statements on sensitive tables (users, passwords, sensitive_data).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Drupal Version Detection (CVE-2026-9082)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Shadowserver now tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations' indicating version fingerprinting is possible. No UC for identifying vulnerable Drupal versions in use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Drupal instances by Server header fingerprinting or /admin/config endpoint responses. Match version strings against CVE-2026-9082 affected versions. Alert on instances missing patches or lacking recent /core/CHANGELOG.txt version markers post-remediation date (May 27, 2026).

suggestion.title: XWiki Path Traversal via ssx/jsx Resource Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'It's possible to get access and read configuration files by using URLs such as `http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg`.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite explicit exploitation pathway documented. HTTP requests to vulnerable endpoints with traversal patterns (leading `/`, `/../`, `..%2f`) must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web logs for GET/POST requests to `/bin/ssx/` or `/bin/jsx/` endpoints containing `resource=` query parameters with leading slashes or `/../` sequences. Alert on requests attempting to access WEB-INF, configuration files, or parent directory traversals. Correlate with XWiki versions prior to 16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, or 18.0.0-rc-1.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Exposure via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability allows 'read[ing] configuration files' and provides example accessing `WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg`. Pipeline missed detection for successful configuration file reads, which would manifest as 200-level HTTP responses to traversal requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify successful configuration file reads by correlating ssx/jsx endpoint requests containing path traversal patterns with HTTP 200 responses. Flag requests that include xwiki.cfg, properties, configuration, credentials, or secrets patterns in the resource parameter.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable XWiki Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit patch boundaries: 'patched in 18.0.0-rc-1, 17.10.3, 17.4.9, 16.10.17.' Pipeline should generate version-matching hunt for affected versions to surface vulnerable asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for XWiki installations running versions prior to: 16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, or 18.0.0-rc-1. Cross-reference with web server logs showing ssx/jsx endpoint activity. Prioritize Tomcat instances as article specifies 'can apparently be reproduced on Tomcat instances.'

suggestion.title: XWiki Unauthenticated XAR Import via REST Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Direct attack vector stated: 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks'—this is exploitation, not reconnaissance
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /wikis/* endpoints lacking valid auth headers (missing session tokens, API keys, Authorization header). Monitor multipart requests containing XAR files from unauthenticated sources. Alert on HTTP 200/201 responses indicating successful document import without prior authenticated session.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-33137 Vulnerable XWiki Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions and patches: 16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1—critical for asset inventory matching
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for XWiki instances with versions prior to the patched releases. Cross-reference instance IPs with public scanning data (Shodan, Censys) for external exposure. Prioritize instances also reachable on port 80/443.

suggestion.title: Bulk Wiki Document Creation Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Stated impact: 'allowing an unauthenticated attacker to create or update documents in the target wiki'—document injection is the attack outcome
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wiki audit logs for document create/update events with no corresponding authenticated user session or REST API token. Flag rapid document creation patterns (>5 docs/minute). Correlate creation timestamps with external network events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub API Authentication Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions' — implies auth mechanism compromise or credential abuse. Pipeline should surface detections for abnormal login/API token patterns even without full incident details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts to GitHub Actions API from unusual IP geolocation or device, or successful login followed by Actions workflow creation/execution from non-standard clients. Monitor for token compromise indicators (multiple failed MFA, reused tokens across regions, actions from revoked/suspended accounts).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Unauthorized Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Denying Access to Actions' — attackers may be attempting to run malicious CI/CD workflows on compromised accounts. Detect unauthorized workflow launches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution logs for workflows triggered outside normal business hours, from unfamiliar users/IPs, or workflows that modify repository secrets, branch protections, or deploy credentials. Flag new workflows added to repositories without standard code review.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-26980 as the primary exploitation vector: 'Hackers Exploit Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Ghost CMS endpoints with exploitation payloads, unusual parameters, or known vulnerability signatures. Flag 5xx error responses followed by evidence of command execution. Correlate with subsequent file writes or process spawning from web service context.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Process Execution and File Creation
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix identified as the deployed payload: 'Poison 700 Websites With ClickFix Malware.' Core execution indicator for the 700-site compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ClickFix process creation by name or hash. Monitor for file drops to temporary directories, web roots, or system paths. Detect network callbacks or behavioral signatures (registry modifications, enumeration) associated with ClickFix.

suggestion.title: Web Service RCE: Shell Spawning from Ghost Node Process
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploitation results in remote code execution. Article describes poisoning 700 sites, implying successful post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: High-fidelity: Ghost Node process or web server spawning cmd.exe, powershell, bash, or sh. Flag unusual parent-child process relationships where web service is parent of shell interpreters—strong RCE indicator.

suggestion.title: Web Content Poisoning: Malicious File Modification in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states 700 websites 'poisoned.' This implies malware-induced modification of web content or injection of malicious scripts into web-accessible files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of HTML, JS, PHP files in web-accessible directories from unexpected users or processes. Implement file integrity monitoring on web roots. Correlate file modification timestamps with exploitation attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: Distributed Ghost CMS Compromise Pattern: Mass Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: 700 websites compromised in one campaign; this scale suggests coordinated mass exploitation or supply-chain attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ClickFix detections, RCE indicators, or suspicious web file modifications across multiple hosts within narrow time window. Detect mass scanning for Ghost instances. Alert on similar compromise signatures (file hashes, process names, network patterns) appearing on 10+ servers simultaneously.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Scanning Against Ghost Admin Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires discovering vulnerable Ghost instances and probing admin endpoints. Should detect scanning and exploitation attempts against Ghost infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple requests to Ghost /admin or /api endpoints with exploit payloads. Flag abnormal User-Agents, rapid-fire requests, or unusual parameters. Alert on successful admin access from suspicious source IPs, especially followed by RCE or file-write events.

suggestion.title: Detect Phishing Email Delivery of MiniFast/MiniJunk
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Phishing' as deployment vector; no phishing-related UC was generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with suspicious sender reputation, malware-bearing attachments, or drive-by-download links matching known malicious domains. Flag messages targeting high-value verticals (government, energy, finance) from Iranian ASNs or spoofed government domains.

suggestion.title: Detect SEO Poisoning Campaign Directing to Malware
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'SEO Poisoning' as deployment vector; no initial-access UC for SEO campaigns generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate search-engine referrer logs with suspicious landing domains or IP ranges. Alert on high-volume requests from search queries targeting legitimate software/updates that resolve to hosting infrastructure known for malware delivery.

suggestion.title: Detect MiniFast Malware Execution Indicators
suggestion.rationale: MiniFast is named in title but no execution or behavioral detection UC was produced for this malware family
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for MiniFast indicators: specific process signatures, registry modifications, file writes, or DLL injection patterns. Compare against samples from phishing-delivery artifacts; correlate with secondary payload delivery or C2 beacons.

suggestion.title: Detect MiniJunk V2 Post-Exploitation Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk V2 named in title but no C2 communication or command-execution UC generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MiniJunk V2-specific beacon signatures, C2 domain patterns, or non-standard protocols. Correlate process execution (MiniFast dropper) with subsequent network callbacks to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Iranian Threat Actor Infrastructure Registration
suggestion.rationale: No infrastructure or attacker-attribution UC; actor attribution implied by 'Iranian Hackers' in title but not surfaced
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly registered domains or ASN changes with known Iranian registrar patterns, payment methods, and WHOIS obfuscation techniques. Cross-reference against phishing-delivery domains and SEO-poisoning landing pages.

suggestion.title: Detect ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-5426)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Threat actors obtained the machine key and used it in ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution.' This is the exploit vector—ViewState validation failures or MAC exceptions must be surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ASP.NET ViewState deserialization exceptions, MAC validation failures, or suspicious __VIEWSTATE parameters in POST requests. Flag unauthenticated access to .aspx endpoints immediately before RCE indicators. Monitor for large or obfuscated ViewState payloads from external sources.

suggestion.title: Detect Godzilla Web Shell .NET In-Memory Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Mandiant says the threat actor deployed the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam).' In-memory shell must be caught via process/assembly anomalies from w3wp.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on System.Net assemblies or reflection-based code execution loaded by w3wp.exe. Monitor for uncommon .NET namespaces (System.Reflection, System.Management) instantiated in web contexts. Detect AMSI/CLR telemetry showing dynamic code compilation or assembly loading from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized JavaScript Modification in Web Application Root
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This allowed them to modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin and to load a malicious script from a domain under the attacker's control.' File-based persistence via application assets is persistent and auditable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected CREATE or MODIFY events on .js files in web root directories. Establish content baseline and alert on additions of prompt()/alert() functions referencing security plugins. Cross-correlate with failed authentication logs or user complaints about unusual prompts.

suggestion.title: Detect Fake Installer Distribution via Compromised LMS
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the malicious code on the platform convinced users to download a fake installer, which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon, essentially planting a backdoor.' Installers served from unexpected application endpoints are detectable via HTTP transaction analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable files (.exe, .msi, .dll) served by KnowledgeDeliver or similar LMS endpoints to end-user clients. Monitor for HTTP responses containing installers from new/unexpected URI paths. Flag installer downloads triggered by JavaScript alerts or user-initiated browser downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Cobalt Strike Beacon Deployment and C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The payload was encrypted using a key that used the name of the compromised organization, which indicated that the threat actor prepared this payload specifically for the targeted organization.' Organization-specific encoding is a signature of targeted campaign—beacon callbacks are highly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Cobalt Strike-like HTTPS traffic patterns (known beacon IPs, SSL cert serials). Monitor for DNS lookups of attacker-controlled domains referenced in JavaScript injections. Detect base64-encoded POST payloads from user machines to external IPs on port 443 or non-standard HTTPS ports.

suggestion.title: Detect Hardcoded Machine Key Compromise and Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file provided by the vendor. This configuration file contained hardcoded machineKey values used by the ASP.NET framework.' Once a shared key is exposed, its use in multiple organizations is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate machine key usage per deployment. Alert if the same machine key is detected signing ViewState in multiple unrelated customer environments (indicates key compromise). Monitor for ViewState validation errors from sources unable to obtain the legitimate key.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Command and Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly deploys 'Cobalt Strike' — industry-standard C2 framework requiring network-based detection for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cobalt Strike beacons establish encrypted C2 over HTTPS or DNS using known callback patterns and signatures. Monitor for connections to non-standard ports (50050, 7001, 8080, etc.), JA3/JARM fingerprint matches, or DNS queries with suspicious subdomains from compromised web servers.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Malware Loader Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Deploy Godzilla' payload. Godzilla is a known webshell loader deployed post-exploitation for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Godzilla executes through scripting interpreters (PowerShell, cmd.exe) or in-memory injection. Detect anomalous child processes spawned from web application parent processes (w3wp.exe, tomcat) launching shell interpreters with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title states '[CRIT] KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited' — establishes initial compromise vector via public-facing application vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Attackers exploit unpatched KnowledgeDeliver LMS to achieve code execution. Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable LMS endpoints, unusual query parameters, file uploads to web directories, or error-code patterns preceding shell creation.

suggestion.title: Executable File Creation from Web Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'flaw exploited to deploy' indicates post-exploitation file-drop activity from compromised web tier to disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After achieving code execution on LMS, attackers stage malware binaries. Monitor for .exe, .dll, .ps1 file creation in IIS/application directories or ProgramData with timestamps correlating to anomalous web application process execution.

suggestion.title: Detect MFA Prompt Flooding — High-Frequency Authentications
suggestion.rationale: Article core scenario: 'attacker floods user's authentication app with push notifications until user approves one out of annoyance.' Requires detection of >N prompts in <M seconds per user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user account receives more than 3 MFA authentication prompts within 60 seconds, or >5 within 300 seconds, particularly if the user does not successfully authenticate on the first or second attempt. Filter for geographic or device anomalies alongside prompt bursts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Device Enrollment Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'enrolled their own devices for MFA to maintain persistence' after initial compromise. Detection must catch device registration under compromised credential context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account compromise indicators (impossible travel, password changes, risky sign-in) with new device enrollment on the same account within ±2 hours. Flag registrations from untrusted or never-before-seen device models or OS versions.

suggestion.title: Detect MFA Bypass via Prompt Fatigue Followed by Admin Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-prompt-bombing sequence: 'attacker had VPN access as employee. They then escalated to administrative privileges.' Should link successful auth after fatigue pattern to rapid privilege elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting a MFA prompt flood that results in successful authentication, baseline the account's privilege elevation attempts over next 4 hours. Alert if account attempts to grant itself admin rights, add to domain admin groups, or request Kerberos TGS for high-privilege services.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious MFA Approvals from Unexpected Geographies
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions attack pairs with 'vishing call' and attackers trigger prompts from unfamiliar locations. Real Cisco breach involved attacker accessing personal Google account followed by corporate MFA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MFA approvals from IP addresses in geographic regions the user has never authenticated from, or from VPN exit nodes known to be attacker-controlled. Correlate with same-session login failures or unusual network paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Credential Compromise Before MFA Fatigue Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'push bombing cannot happen without valid credentials. The attacker needs your real username and password before the attack can begin.' Prerequisite is often brute force or credential stuffing; detection must catch compromise *before* bombing begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts that spike for a single account (>10 failures in 10 minutes) followed by a successful login from the same or related source IP. Escalate if the success is then followed within 300 seconds by MFA prompt activity.

suggestion.title: Detect VPN Access Immediately Post-MFA Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Cisco case: post-MFA-fatigue, attacker immediately accessed 'VPN as the employee' and progressed to Citrix and domain controllers. Link auth success to privileged network access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN authentication success for an account that experienced MFA prompt anomalies (fatigue pattern or device enrollment) within the preceding 24 hours, particularly if VPN session is followed by RDP/SSH to domain controllers, Citrix gateways, or administrative subnets.

suggestion.title: Defender Automatic Device Isolation Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'When a device in your organization is suspected to be compromised, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can automatically isolate the device.' Pipeline missed this event as a detection anchor—isolation events themselves are indicators of suspected compromise and should be ingested, logged, and monitored for patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MDE logs for automatic device isolation events. Correlate isolation triggers with suspicious process execution, network connections, or credential access patterns in the hours preceding isolation to confirm compromise vector.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Attempts Post-Device Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes isolation 'limit[s] attacker lateral movement.' Defensive UC: detect when isolated devices continue receiving lateral movement probes, SMB enumeration, or authentication attempts from other network segments—indicating attacker persistence despite containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After device isolation event, monitor for inbound network reconnaissance (ARP scans, NetBIOS probes, SMB port scans) and failed authentication attempts targeting the isolated host. Isolation failure or short TTL may indicate attacker escalating against containment.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Propagation Attempt Detection Post-Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article states isolation prevents 'ransomware propagation.' UC: detect when isolated devices (suspected ransomware-infected) attempt to execute encryption routines, write to network shares, or enumerate additional targets post-isolation—indicating active malware despite containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor isolated device for suspicious file operations (mass file extension changes, encryption-like process behavior), network share enumeration, or lateral spread attempts. High-confidence indicator that isolation was triggered by live ransomware, not false positive.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Attempt from Isolated Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article cites prevention of 'data exfiltration' as isolation benefit. UC: detect when isolated (compromised) endpoints attempt data staging, compression, or egress despite network isolation—indicating attacker racing to exfil before containment tightens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor isolated device for archive creation (ZIP, RAR), compression utilities, or bulk file read operations targeting sensitive paths (C:\Users\*\Documents, database directories). Correlate with failed outbound connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Automatic User Account Isolation in Hands-on-Keyboard Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Defender for Endpoint could also isolate compromised user accounts as part of automatic attack disruption to block lateral movement in hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks.' UC: detect account isolation events and monitor for post-isolation persistence attempts using that account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account isolation events with logon failures, privilege escalation attempts, or service enumeration in preceding 24h. High-confidence signal of operator hands-on-keyboard activity before containment.

suggestion.title: Automated Device Isolation Triggered
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Microsoft Defender 'automatically isolates compromised devices'—a high-confidence containment signal. Pipeline produced zero use cases; this is the primary detection outcome described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Defender isolation events (device quarantine/network segmentation initiated). Correlate isolation triggers with preceding suspicious process activity (encryption loops, system enumeration) within the 5–15 min window before isolation decision.

suggestion.title: High-Volume File Encryption Activity Pre-Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware's core behavior (T1486) must precede isolation detection. Article emphasizes stopping 'ransomware spread'—detecting encryption patterns before isolation confirms early kill-chain point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes creating encrypted files at scale (>100 files/min with entropy >7.5) targeting user directories, shared drives, or backup mounts. Correlate with unusual parent process chains or system binary abuse.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Pre-Encryption Discovery & Preparation
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware typically performs reconnaissance before encryption (file/directory discovery, permission enumeration). Article's isolation feature detects the end state; detection should cover earlier behavioral stages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of discovery utilities (dir, fsutil, wmic) or direct API calls (FindFirstFile loops, OpenFile with successive path queries) targeting user/system directories, followed by permission enumeration attempts within same session.

suggestion.title: Service Termination or System Shutdown Post-Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware frequently stops security services or forces reboots. Article's isolation feature responds to compromise; detection should cover common post-encryption cleanup behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution (net.exe, sc.exe, wmic.exe) targeting antivirus/backup services or shutdown/reboot commands from user processes. Trigger on failed stop attempts or suspicious command-line patterns (/y, /f flags).

suggestion.title: Network Isolation Enforcement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Defender 'isolates' devices—network segment changes or firewall rule enforcement are expected. Detection should capture the containment mechanism itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden drop in outbound connection success or appearance of new network isolation rules applied to a device. Correlate with preceding ransomware IOC matches or Defender isolation events.

suggestion.title: Mass File Rename or Extension Modification (Ransomware Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Many ransomware variants rename encrypted files with threat-specific extensions (.locked, .encrypted, .{UUID}, etc). Article's isolation detects the device; detection should identify the file-level signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batch file renames targeting >50 files with unusual extensions, or overwriting of file metadata (timestamps, sizes increasing uniformly). Correlate extension patterns with known ransomware families.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'DLL Side-Loading' as primary attack method. Pipeline extracted zero detection use cases despite this being the defining technique of the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate Windows executables (e.g., rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe) loading unusual DLL files from non-standard paths or with suspicious naming patterns. Flag cases where a legitimate executable's directory contains a malicious DLL with same/similar name, indicating side-loading attempt.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
