suggestion.rationale: Article targets '9 countries' indicating multi-stage espionage operations requiring reconnaissance and lateral movement, but pipeline surfaced no use cases for discovery/lateral movement phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal user enumeration commands (net user, dsquery), network share enumeration, and credential access attempts following DLL side-loading execution, consistent with espionage campaign lateral movement.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Side-Loaded Malware
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns require command-and-control communications, but no network-based detection use cases were generated for malware callbacks or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from processes spawned by DLL side-loading, especially to newly registered domains or IPs not in organizational allow-lists. Correlate with historical MuddyWater C2 infrastructure patterns.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry/Startup Locations Post-DLL Execution
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country espionage campaign requires persistence mechanisms beyond initial execution. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detections despite campaign scope suggesting long-dwell objectives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or Startup folder additions immediately following DLL side-loading execution, indicating persistence installation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Delivery of Side-Loading Package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes espionage campaign targeting 9 countries; MuddyWater historically uses phishing. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for phishing vectors delivering the side-loading executable+DLL pair.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with suspicious .zip or archive attachments containing paired legitimate.exe + malicious.dll files with similar naming, especially to government/defense sector recipients in targeted countries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Lineage from Legitimate Windows Binary
suggestion.rationale: DLL side-loading execution creates unusual parent-child relationships (legit exe → injected/side-loaded DLL → suspicious child processes). Pipeline extracted zero behavioral detections despite this being the core attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build whitelist of expected child processes for known Windows binaries (calc.exe, notepad.exe, etc.). Alert on deviations where legitimate executable spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network tools—high indicator of DLL side-loading exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Angular Language Service Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerabilities in Angular extension 'enable RCE attacks'—should detect unexpected VSCode/IDE extension installations or modifications, particularly targeting language service tooling
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation or update of VSCode/IDE extensions with 'Angular', 'language-service', or 'language-server' in metadata, especially from non-official publishers or unsigned sources. Establish baseline of legitimate Angular development tools per user/team.

suggestion.title: Shell Execution from Language Service Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability implies arbitrary code execution in extension context; detect when language-service or IDE extension processes spawn shell interpreters or system commands
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe, language-server.exe, or VSCode child processes spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash with suspicious arguments (encoded payloads, network callbacks, file exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Extension Process Outbound Network Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malicious RCE extension likely establishes C2; detect IDE extension processes making unexpected outbound connections to non-standard ports or unapproved domains
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected network destinations of Angular Language Service (npm.org, github.com, official CDNs). Flag extension processes connecting to non-Microsoft/non-npm ASNs, port 8080/8888, or dynamic/residential IP space.

suggestion.title: Language Service Binary or Manifest Modification
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploited through extension manifest or entry-point injection; detect unauthorized writes to extension directories or config files
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to .js/.json files in VSCode extensions folder (e.g., %APPDATA%\Code\extensions\*), especially main.js, package.json, or compiled entry points outside normal update windows.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Extension Version Running
suggestion.rationale: Article cites specific vulnerabilities; should identify installed extensions matching vulnerable version signatures mentioned in CVE advisories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse VSCode extension manifests for version strings and cross-reference against published CVE databases for Angular Language Service. Flag presence of known-vulnerable versions in use.

suggestion.title: RDP Lateral Movement to Critical Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Uses RDP Access' as primary attack vector. RDP is foundational to the attack chain but no detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connections (port 3389) to critical hosts from unusual source IPs, especially outside business hours. Flag failed logins followed by success with different credentials. Correlation with credential compromise events strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Remote Admin Tools' used for 'stealthy persistence' but no detection for tool deployment or execution was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known remote admin tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, ConnectWise, etc.) from unexpected processes or locations. Monitor for suspicious service installations, registry persistence mechanisms, or scheduled task creation that would enable tool persistence.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Post-RDP Compromise
suggestion.rationale: RDP compromise typically precedes credential harvesting to enable lateral movement. Article describes stealthy persistence but credential harvesting mechanisms were not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LSASS access patterns, credential manager queries, or suspicious use of credential dumping tools (mimikatz, ProcDump). Correlate with RDP session events to identify post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Service or Scheduled Task Creation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Persistence via remote admin tools typically leverages services or scheduled tasks. Article states 'persistence' as core attack goal but detection mechanism for persistence hooks is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new service creation or scheduled task registration with network connectivity, especially post-RDP compromise. Flag tasks executing from unusual paths or with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Admin Tool Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'stealthy' persistence which implies evasion techniques. No detection logic addresses obfuscation or hiding of admin tool presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process injection into legitimate processes, masquerading of tool executables, disabled Windows Defender, or Log deletion. Correlate file system writes to unusual locations with process execution from the same parent.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP to Internal Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: RDP compromise is stated as the entry vector; lateral movement to domain infrastructure and critical systems is implicit in persistence strategy but no horizontal movement detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multi-hop RDP chains (RDP from external → internal server → critical asset). Flag RDP to servers with administrative roles accessed by non-admin accounts or from atypical source ASNs.

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Program Loading and Kernel Hook Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'eBPF Rootkit' as a delivery component. eBPF programs are loaded via bpftool, syscall(BPF), or writes to /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/ and /sys/kernel/bpf/. Detection must intercept these privileged operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bpftool invocations, bpf syscalls, or file writes to /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/{kprobe,uprobe}_events and /sys/kernel/bpf/. Flag processes loading .bpf.o or .o files into kernel. Correlate eBPF loads with subsequent defense-evasion activity (process hiding, network socket hijacking).

suggestion.title: Fileless Process Execution: Spawning Without Disk Binary Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'fileless execution' as core technique. Process spawned without preceding file-system access to a legitimate binary on disk. Detection via process ancestry anomalies: execve() syscalls without preceding open() of the target binary from parent process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child process creation where parent initiates exec without opening a binary file first. In audit logs, detect execve() syscalls not preceded by open() or stat() of the executable path. Alert when shell or interpreter spawns with memory-only ancestry (injected loader parent).

suggestion.title: Shell Command Execution with Encoded Payloads from Memory Context
suggestion.rationale: Fileless delivery often chains to /bin/bash or /bin/sh with inline code. 'bash -c' with base64/hex-encoded payloads, or shell invocation from non-standard parents (interpreters, loaders) indicate fileless post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash/sh -c arguments containing base64, hex, URL encoding, or compression markers. Alert when shell inherits from interpreters (perl, python, ruby) or memory loaders. Flag command lines >500 chars with obfuscation patterns. Baseline legitimate dev tool usage to reduce FPs.

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Compromise: Suspicious IDE, Git, or Build Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'targets developers.' Unusual child processes from IDEs (VSCode, PyCharm), git operations (clone/push from attacker repos), npm/pip/Maven executing shell code, or build scripts downloading untrusted binaries indicate supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE processes spawning shells, compilers, or curl/wget. Detect git operations pulling from non-whitelisted origins or unsigned commits. Flag npm/pip/Maven invoking shell interpreters or executing external scripts. Alert on download of binaries into dev directories from non-standard sources.

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Beaconing from Unexpected Processes
suggestion.rationale: Quasar is a Remote Access Tool; article must describe C2 callbacks. Detect outbound TCP/UDP connections from fileless or memory-loaded processes to external IPs, especially on high ports or repeating patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for which processes legitimately initiate outbound connections. Flag non-service processes (shells, interpreters, build tools) establishing TCP sessions to external IPs. Alert on periodic beaconing (connection every N seconds/minutes). Monitor for DNS queries to dynamic or newly-registered C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Kernel Syscall Interception via kprobe/uprobe: Hiding Processes and Network Sockets
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkit hides attacker artifacts by intercepting syscalls. Detection requires monitoring /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/ for kprobe and uprobe installation targeting getdents64, connect, sendto, or process listing syscalls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/kprobe_events or uprobe_events with patterns targeting process enumeration or network syscalls. Monitor enable_kprobes toggles in tracing control. Flag attempts to access /proc/[pid]/trace_pipe or /sys/kernel/debug/bpf/ after suspicious privilege gain.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DDoS Traffic Volume Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses 'AI DDoS Attacks' and 'smarter' attack vectors. Pipeline should extract detection logic for abnormal traffic volume spikes, especially multi-vector attacks. Title phrase 'New AI DDoS Attacks' establishes this as core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden sustained traffic spikes from distributed sources exceeding baseline thresholds. Alert on multi-vector attack patterns (UDP floods, SYN floods, application-layer attacks) within compressed timeframes. Correlate with botnet command-and-control signaling if available.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: AI-powered DDoS requires orchestration; article's framing suggests coordinated attack infrastructure. Pipeline should extract indicators of C2 communication used to direct DDoS traffic. Missing kill-chain 'command and control' entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify beaconing patterns to known C2 infrastructure. Look for regular interval callbacks, encoded/obfuscated DNS queries, or unusual port activity from compromised hosts. Correlate timing of C2 communication with DDoS traffic initiation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Vulnerability Scanning Preceding DDoS
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated ('smarter') AI-driven attacks typically include reconnaissance. Article's emphasis on AI suggests adaptive targeting. Pipeline missed initial-access and discovery phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning, web service enumeration, and vulnerability research traffic to target assets in days/hours before DDoS launch. Detect scripted reconnaissance tools and automated scanning signatures.

suggestion.title: Botnet Infection / Initial Compromise Vector
suggestion.rationale: DDoS requires infected bots; article focuses on 'how to fight back' against sophisticated attacks, implying attacker methodology includes compromise phase. Pipeline extracted no initial-access techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify delivery mechanisms for botnet malware (phishing, watering holes, exploit kits). Correlate malware installation artifacts with subsequent DDoS-related outbound connections and C2 signaling.

suggestion.title: Adaptive DDoS Evasion of Mitigation Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes attacks are 'smarter'—implying evasion of defenses. AI suggests adversary adapting to mitigation. No defense-evasion techniques extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid attack-pattern variation: shifting target ports, changing payload signatures, switching between attack vectors mid-stream. Alert on failure of static blocklists and signature-based mitigation, indicating adaptive adversary.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation or Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks targeting developers pivot through package managers and build artifacts; title explicitly identifies 'developer machines' as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected package manager executions (npm install, pip install, apt-get) from non-standard user contexts or with unusual source repositories. Flag installations of packages with typos similar to legitimate libraries (typosquatting) or packages updated within hours of first detection.

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines often hold SSH keys, API tokens, and repo credentials; article focuses on machines as attack targets, implying credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation of common credential dumping tools (secretsdump, pass-the-hash utilities, ssh-keygen read operations) or unusual file access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube directories outside normal IDE/tool operations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Commits or Code Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev machines enable malicious commits; article positions machines as strategic targets for code manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Git push/commit operations from dev machines with unusual author metadata, commits to protected/main branches outside normal workflows, or Git operations using credentials different from usual developer accounts.

suggestion.title: Build Pipeline or IDE Process Chain Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Developer machine compromise extends to build artifacts; unusual process execution chains in IDEs (VSCode, JetBrains) or build tools (gradle, maven, make) indicate post-compromise actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag IDE or build tool processes spawning shell interpreters, curl/wget operations, or rundll32 calls. Detect base64-encoded commands in IDE terminal history or build logs.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Tool Installation or Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Dev machines are entry points; compromises manifest as persistence via modified package managers, build caches, or developer tool configurations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to .npmrc, .bashrc, .zshrc, Maven settings.xml, or Gradle properties files outside package manager updates. Monitor for new entries in PATH environment or symlink creation pointing to suspicious build tool paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code OAuth Flow Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the core attack: 'abusing OAuth device code authentication to steal session tokens' and 'trick targets into entering [codes] on Microsoft's login page.' This is the foundational technique requiring SOC detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous device code authentication patterns: multiple failed device code authorizations from single user within short window, rapid-fire device code requests, device codes approved from geographically impossible locations, or successful device code authentications immediately followed by anomalous API calls (bulk mail read, rule creation, device enumeration).

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rule Creation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article documents that compromised accounts had 'malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' This is explicit defense evasion activity following initial access and should trigger alerts as anomalous for typical user behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation within hours of device code authentication anomalies, especially rules that delete/move/suppress emails, rules created via PowerShell or API, or rules matching known evasion signatures (domain-based filtering, keyword suppression, forwarding to external addresses).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Azure AD
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Device registration post-compromise enables persistence and evasion of device-based Conditional Access policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device registration events with device code authentication anomalies, unusual sign-in patterns, or mailbox operations. Flag bulk device registration to single user, registration of unusual OS types from geographically impossible locations, or registration within hours of credential compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Targeting Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article documents Kali365 campaigns sent 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal.' Catching phishing at the email gateway prevents the entire attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin, especially combined with urgency language, Microsoft spoofing, or requests to verify identity. Flag phishing templates matching known Kali365 campaign characteristics and emails requesting device code authorization.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Abuse After Device Code Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Detection of token misuse is critical for containing the breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for OAuth token issuance from device code flows followed within minutes by mailbox enumeration, folder operations, forwarding rule creation, or bulk API calls. Detect tokens used from impossible geolocations or by applications not baseline for the user.

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle via Session Proxying (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kali365's second attack mode 'Cookie Link' that 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' Represents session hijacking without stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication sessions with unusual geographic routing patterns, TLS interception indicators on trusted endpoints, or legitimate logins immediately followed by account access from geographically impossible distance (suggesting session was captured and replayed from attacker infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation via HTTP POST
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies CVE-2026-26980 as the attack vector affecting 700+ sites. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite high severity and specificity of the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ghost CMS admin API endpoints (/ghost/api/admin/, /admin/) for payloads characteristic of CVE-2026-26980 exploitation. Flag POST/PUT requests with crafted parameters bypassing authentication, originating from non-whitelisted networks, or containing Base64-encoded payloads targeting CMS core files.

suggestion.title: Website Defacement and Content Injection for ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hijacking of 700+ sites specifically to deploy ClickFix attacks, indicating content-level compromise. Pipeline should surface detection patterns for website defacement and malicious script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected modifications to web-served files (HTML, JavaScript, PHP) in Ghost CMS directories, injection of script tags referencing ClickFix infrastructure domains into web responses, and sudden increases in outbound HTTP redirects to unknown destinations from web server processes.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Admin Account Creation in Ghost CMS
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of 700+ sites implies persistence mechanism; attackers would create administrative accounts to maintain access. Article context of coordinated campaign suggests account manipulation as post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS database for unexpected user creation via API endpoints, detect new admin/Editor tier accounts created outside change windows, correlate with timestamps of CVE exploitation attempts, and flag account creation from IP addresses distinct from legitimate administrative networks.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from Web Server to ClickFix Domains
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked sites serving ClickFix payloads implies web servers must communicate with attacker infrastructure for malware staging or callback. Article states sites hijacked 'for ClickFix attacks' but pipeline identified zero C2 detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and outbound HTTPS connections from web application processes (w3wp.exe, php-cgi, node) to known ClickFix malware distribution domains. Correlate web server WHOIS queries on newly registered domains with subsequent outbound connections from the same process.

suggestion.title: Rapid Bulk File Modification in Ghost CMS Root
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites in coordinated fashion implies automated or scripted bulk modification of site content. Article phrase 'hijack 700+ sites' indicates mass compromise requiring batch modification detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by Ghost CMS or web server services creating/modifying multiple HTML or JavaScript files in rapid succession. Alert on command-line execution of file write/append commands (sed, printf, echo) from w3wp or httpd processes, particularly targeting theme or template directories.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only RAT Execution via Indirect Command Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'memory-only RAT' deployment; suggests fileless execution pattern typical of advanced APTs. No UC generated despite this being a primary detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for indirect command execution (WMI, scheduled tasks, or parent-child process anomalies) where the parent is a benign system process (LSASS, svchost, explorer) and child invokes cmd/powershell with minimal command-line artifacts or living-off-the-land binaries. Correlate with subsequent network beaconing.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beacon Detection (RemotePE Family)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'RemotePE' RAT and Lazarus as threat actor; standard APT pattern includes C2 communication but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or network detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS traffic from financial sector endpoints to known or suspected RemotePE C2 infrastructure. Look for beaconing intervals, unusual port/protocol combinations, or certificate anomalies associated with Lazarus historical infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Process Injection via Suspended Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RATs typically use process injection (T1055) to evade disk forensics. Article abstract suggests this mechanism but zero detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with suspicious combinations: CREATE_SUSPENDED flag usage, immediate thread manipulation via CreateRemoteThread, and execution from process with unusual privilege context (services.exe, NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM). Correlate with parent process that lacks legitimate reason for code injection.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency/Financial Endpoint Targeting via Network Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'financial and crypto firms' but no detection for sector-specific targeting patterns or lateral movement within these environments was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor financial sector endpoints for suspicious network egress to non-whitelisted destinations, particularly traffic from key workstations (trading systems, wallet nodes, exchange admin workstations). Flag unusual data volume exfiltration or access to sensitive systems (database servers, key management appliances).

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from PyPI/npm/CratesIO
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Spreads Credential-Stealing Malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — pipeline missed detection of suspicious package installs across all three major package repositories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of packages from npm, PyPI, or CratesIO that match known malicious package names. Correlate with unexpected package manager executions (pip install, npm install, cargo add) on systems without developer context. Flag package installations followed by suspicious credential-access patterns within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft Post-Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware payload explicitly described as 'credential-stealing' — no detection built for credential access behaviors triggered by package code execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawned from package manager (pip.exe, npm.exe, node.exe, cargo.exe) accessing Windows credential stores (HKLM\Security\SAM, credential.sqlite, .aws/credentials), browser password managers (Chrome/Firefox profile dirs), or calling credential enumeration APIs. Alert on unexpected API calls to OS credential APIs from package manager child processes.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Package Manager Processes
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware inherently exfiltrates stolen credentials to C2 — pipeline failed to suggest detection of network beaconing from package manager or package-spawned child processes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections originating from package manager processes (python.exe, node.exe, cargo.exe, ruby.exe) or their child processes to unusual IPs/domains. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains initiated by package execution. Alert on HTTPS connections to non-standard C2 IPs from these processes, especially those with suspicious TLS certificates or self-signed certs.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest / Repository Upload Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Title states attack 'spreads via' multiple repositories — implies package was uploaded to official repos; no detection for suspicious package versions, metadata, or upload patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor official package repository APIs and logs for: new package versions with sudden popularity spikes, packages with unexpected dependency graphs (adding unrelated crypto/network libs), version bumps with large binary size increases, or uploads from newly registered accounts. Flag packages with obfuscated code (minified JS, compiled binaries in unexpected languages).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution from Package Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing payload must execute during installation — no detection for setup.py/package.json build/install script execution or obfuscated code patterns typical of supply chain malware
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell, cmd.exe, or shell spawned with base64-encoded arguments during package installation. Track child processes of pip.exe, npm install, or cargo processes that execute cmd, powershell, or bash with encoded payloads. Flag any use of certutil.exe, System.Net.ServicePointManager, or network API calls from package install contexts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository Package Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Multi-repository attack suggests typosquatting or name confusion strategy — no detection for similar-named packages across npm/PyPI/CratesIO that could indicate coordinated supply chain operation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package names across all three registries looking for: common typosquats (single-character substitutions, vowel swaps), packages with similar names across repos uploaded within same timeframe, and packages maintained by newly created accounts or low-reputation publishers. Cross-reference against known legitimate package ecosystems.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Record Export Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen over 600,000 records containing corporate data and personally identifiable information' from Salesforce. 600k+ record export in a single event is detectable as exfiltration anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce API for bulk export operations (SOQL queries with high record counts, Reports/Data Export APIs) from non-service accounts. Establish baseline for franchisee document access volume and alert on 10x+ anomalies, especially outside business hours or from new IP/user context.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Account Compromise - Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized third party gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems' and 'breaching 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment.' ShinyHunters specializes in Salesforce targeting, implying credential theft or social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Salesforce logins from new geolocation/IP, disabled MFA on admin accounts, permission elevation on dormant service accounts, and API token generation by non-service principals. Correlate with phishing emails targeting Salesforce users in the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: PII Collection and Structured Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed the data of 185,300 people, including names, dates of birth, unique email addresses, phone numbers, and physical addresses' constitutes bulk PII extraction detectable by DLP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy DLP rules detecting correlated PII field exports (name + DOB + email + phone + address in single query/file). Monitor for structured data transfers matching franchisee document schema. Establish baseline for document store access and flag bulk downloads.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Extortion Group Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility for the attack on April 17' and 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay a ransom.' Threat actor name and extortion pattern missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference incident date (April 8 breach, April 17 claim) with ShinyHunters IOC feeds and leak site monitoring. Alert on extortion emails from known ShinyHunters addresses. Correlate with public announcements on ShinyHunters' dark web properties.

suggestion.title: Multi-Victim Salesforce Campaign Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 15+ ShinyHunters victims in past year: 'European Commission, Vimeo, Zara, MANGO, McGraw-Hill, ADT, Medtronic, PornHub, Rockstar Games, Match Group, Cisco, Google.' Coordinated Salesforce targeting campaign pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create incident correlation rule: if your org uses Salesforce and is in a vertical hit by ShinyHunters (retail, SaaS, enterprise, media), escalate monitoring for anomalous account activity and phishing in April-May 2026 timeframe. Cross-reference breach victim list against supply chain and partner ecosystem.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unpatched Internet-Facing Services (12h Window)
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Patching for Internet-Facing Flaws' — pipeline missed detection logic for rapid exploitation post-disclosure or during vulnerability window before remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to known-vulnerable public-facing services (web servers, VPNs, RDP) from external sources within 12 hours of CVE publication. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or HTTP error codes (e.g., 400-range) indicating exploitation probing.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Reconnaissance and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly invokes 'AI-Assisted Attacks' — pipeline failed to map offensive AI tooling (automated scanning, vulnerability discovery acceleration) to reconnaissance/discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify non-human reconnaissance patterns: mass scanning across ports/services, rapid probing of multiple endpoints, or statistically anomalous HTTP User-Agent strings associated with automated AI scanning frameworks or LLM-based enumeration tools.

suggestion.title: CERT-In Advisory Correlation and Zero-Day Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CERT-In advisories typically reference specific CVE identifiers and affected vendors — pipeline extracted zero IOCs, suggesting failure to map advisory references to CVE database or vendor patch releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CERT-In published CVE list with internal patch management and vulnerability scanner logs. Alert on systems running vulnerable versions of applications referenced in advisory, especially those internet-facing or with public exposure.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Attack - Entra Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' but pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting post-compromise account activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Entra ID logins from unusual geographic locations, IP ranges, or device types within 24 hours following social engineering attempts. Monitor for MFA changes, password resets, or conditional access policy modifications on user accounts targeted by external phone calls.

suggestion.title: Bulk Salesforce Data Export - Customer Records Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat actors 'export[ing] millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance' but pipeline provided no detection for bulk record exports or suspicious API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk Salesforce data exports exceeding 10K records per transaction, exports to new custom reports, or large-scale API calls using field selectors for customer contact data (names, emails, phone numbers). Correlate with newly-compromised account access patterns.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Misuse - Cross-SaaS API Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions threat actors stealing 'OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances' and reports targeting 'Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox' via compromised SSO, but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API bearer token/OAuth token usage from residential IPs, VPN endpoints, or geographies inconsistent with user baseline. Alert on service account tokens used for bulk data operations or accessed immediately after employee credential compromise events.

suggestion.title: Entra Account Lateral Movement Across SaaS Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes extortion group methodology: 'after gaining access to a corporate SSO account, threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications' and lists 7+ target systems, but pipeline generated no lateral movement detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single Entra credential accessing 5+ distinct SaaS platforms (Salesforce, M365, Google Workspace, etc.) within 1-hour window, especially from non-corporate device or unrecognized IP. Flag BPO/contractor account activity suddenly querying customer data systems.

suggestion.title: Customer Data Collection - PII Field Export Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies stolen data includes 'customer names, email addresses, addresses, phone numbers, phone type, plan information, CPNI data' and 'customer support ticket data', but no use case detects suspicious bulk PII queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce queries exporting customer contact fields (name, email, phone, address) in bulk, use of default reports to extract full customer datasets, or API calls with field selectors including PII. Escalate if performed by newly-compromised account or from external IP.

suggestion.title: BPO/Contractor Account Compromise - Social Engineering Target Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article notes extortion group 'target[s] employees and BPO agents' Microsoft Entra, Okta, and Google SSO accounts' as primary social engineering vectors, but pipeline generated no use case for monitoring contractor credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline BPO/contractor account behavior and alert on deviations: new IP logins, access to non-assigned customer tenants, API calls to Salesforce, or password resets within hours of employee reports of credential-harvesting phone calls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on Edge Router Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Custom Linux Implant' deployed to routers; no execution detection generated despite this being core attack indicator. Should detect shell spawning, interpreter invocation, or unexpected commands on production router devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor edge routers for unexpected shell invocation (bash, sh, ash) from network daemons, unusual command-line arguments suggesting script staging, or process execution from non-standard paths. Correlate with failed initial-access attempts.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation on Linux Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes maintaining access via 'custom implant' on SE Asian routers; no persistence UC generated. Linux routers use cron, systemd units, or rc.local—attackers would abuse these for re-execution across reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized crontab entries, systemd service creation in /etc/systemd, /lib/systemd, or /etc/init.d modifications. Flag suspicious restart policies, ExecStartPost/Pre with encoded payloads, or service files with root privilege re-execution.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Compromised Edge Routers
suggestion.rationale: Custom implant requires C2 maintenance; article implies persistent control over SE Asian edge infrastructure but no C2 detection UC provided. This is critical for identifying active post-compromise operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from router IPs to suspicious ASNs (bulletproof hosters, Tencent, Alibaba), frequent DNS lookups to newly registered or fast-flux domains, or traffic on atypical ports (8080, 443, 8888) with beaconing periodicity patterns.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Application Exploitation on Router Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article cites targeting SE Asian edge infrastructure, implying internet-exposed devices; likely initial vector is default credentials, CVE-based RCE, or CGI injection. No exploitation detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor router management HTTP/HTTPS endpoints for SQL injection attempts, CGI parameter fuzzing, malformed requests with encoded payloads typical of router RCE exploits, or successful authentication from non-administrative source IPs/geolocations.

suggestion.title: Firmware or Configuration Tampering on Edge Router Devices
suggestion.rationale: Edge routers are prime targets for supply-chain or persistence mechanisms. Article implies implant 'deployment' but no detection for unauthorized firmware changes, config exports, or management credential modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected firmware uploads, configuration backups, or SSH key generation on routers. Detect unauthorized access to privileged management ports (22, 23, 8022) from external source IPs, or changes to firewall ACLs that whitelist suspicious command-and-control ranges.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Data Exfiltration via Compromised Router Position
suggestion.rationale: Article targets SE Asian infrastructure suggesting lateral movement and intelligence collection. Compromised routers enable monitoring of all transiting data; no exfiltration detection UC provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusually large data volumes or sustained transfers originating from or transiting through compromised edge router. Flag traffic to known Chinese threat infrastructure, egress outside business hours, or protocols unexpected in router telemetry (SSH tunnels, reverse shells).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Detection via Vulnerability Scan Results
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48172 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. This is the primary detection vector for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any asset reporting positive match for CVE-2026-48172 in vulnerability scanner output or CMDB. Prioritize unpatched LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin instances facing the internet. Cross-reference against patch compliance logs with due date 2026-05-29.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Execution with Root Privileges from cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — this is the core post-exploitation activity that must be detected once vuln is exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script execution (shell, perl, python, bash) originating from cPanel processes or cPanel user context (UID < 1000) where EUID or process elevation results in root (0) privileges. Baseline expected cPanel maintenance scripts and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Local User to Root via cPanel Plugin Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — privilege escalation is the core technical mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation events where source is a cPanel user account (typically UID 10000+) and target privilege is root (UID 0). Alert on sudo/sudoedit abuse, SUID execution, or setuid binaries invoked from cPanel plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Anomalous cPanel Plugin File Access or Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin' — detect abuse of the plugin interface itself, not just downstream effects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file modifications or execution within cPanel plugin directories (typically /usr/local/cpanel/plugins or /home/*/cPanel_modules). Alert on cPanel plugin invocation with unusual arguments, POST requests to plugin endpoints from non-trusted sources, or plugin execution outside normal administrative windows.

suggestion.title: Valid Account Exploitation: Unauthorized cPanel User Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be abused by any cPanel user account' — this is account-based exploitation, not credential theft, distinct from typical lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate cPanel user login activity with subsequent privilege escalation or system-level actions. Alert when legitimate cPanel user accounts trigger root-level operations outside expected workflows. Monitor for bulk or batch execution from single user accounts that normally perform interactive work.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance or Data Access via Root Shell
suggestion.rationale: Once root is achieved via arbitrary script execution, attacker capability expands dramatically. Article's 'root privileges' statement implies full system compromise is possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting root script execution, hunt for follow-up reconnaissance: enumeration of /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, AWS credentials, SSH keys, database configs. Flag execution of common recon tools (whoami, id, uname, cat /etc/hosts, nmap, curl to cloud metadata endpoints) in root context within 5 minutes of exploitation timestamp.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE-2026-9082 SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'without authentication, allowing attackers to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests.' 15,000+ attempts detected in May alone. No SQL injection detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal installations (identified by URI patterns or web server fingerprinting) for HTTP requests containing SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comment sequences) in query parameters, POST bodies, or headers targeting database abstraction layer endpoints. Baseline against known benign Drupal query patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution on Drupal Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Successful exploitation can potentially lead to information disclosure, privilege escalation, and even remote code execution.' No RCE detection generated despite this explicitly being a possible outcome of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SQL injection exploitation indicators with subsequent suspicious process execution on Drupal web server (w3wp.exe, apache2, php-fpm): shell spawning, script interpreters, encoded command execution, or network connections from web application context.

suggestion.title: Database Privilege Escalation Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites privilege escalation as outcome. No detection for elevated database access patterns or role changes following exploitation of database abstraction layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs and database connection patterns on Drupal servers for: database user/role elevation, privilege grants to web application service accounts, or lateral movement from web tier to database tier credentials after SQL injection time windows.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Data via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'information disclosure' as exploitation outcome. Imperva observed attacks targeting Gaming and Financial Services (50% of attacks). No data exfiltration detection mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual database query volume or data transfer patterns from Drupal PostgreSQL instances post-exploitation window. Flag egress of sensitive schema tables (users, credentials, payment data) via SQL queries or large uncompressed database exports over HTTPS/DNS tunneling.

suggestion.title: Drupal Installation Vulnerability Assessment & Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Shadowserver now tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online, most of them from North America (272) and Europe (273).' Asset discovery and patch status monitoring is foundational for this threat class but no detection or inventory use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for publicly accessible Drupal instances via fingerprinting (HTTP headers X-Drupal-Cache, CHANGELOG.txt, specific URI patterns). Correlate with vulnerability databases to flag instances running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-9082. Alert on unpatched assets in high-risk sectors (financial, government, gaming).

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Drupal Installation Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions coordinated targeting of 6,000 sites across 65 countries with sector focus. No reconnaissance/scanning detection for attackers enumerating Drupal versions or endpoints prior to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanner/bot activity targeting known Drupal enumeration endpoints (CHANGELOG.txt, /admin, /user/login, REST API paths) at scale or from suspicious ASNs. Flag repeated requests to non-existent Drupal paths from single source attempting version detection or functionality mapping.

suggestion.title: HTTP Path Traversal — XWiki ssx/jsx resources Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'path traversal via resources parameter in ssx and jsx endpoints when using leading slash' with PoC URL demonstrating /../../WEB-INF/ traversal. Zero use cases generated despite this detailed attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/POST requests to /bin/ssx/ or /bin/jsx/ endpoints with 'resource=' parameter containing leading forward slash followed by path-traversal sequences (../, ..). Flag requests where resource value would escape intended directory scope.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Exfiltration Attempt — XWiki WEB-INF
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'read configuration files' and specifically names WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg as accessible target. This signals discovery/collection phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing 'WEB-INF' in path or resource parameter, combined with XWiki-identifying User-Agent or endpoint. Correlate against vulnerable version ranges (< 18.0.0-rc-1, < 17.10.3, < 17.4.9, < 16.10.17).

suggestion.title: XWiki Platform Vulnerable Version Exposure — CVE-2026-23734
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt. Zero use cases generated; standard vulnerability-asset correlation was omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset/vulnerability systems for XWiki Platform instances running versions 18.0.0 before rc-1, 17.10.x before 17.10.3, 17.4.x before 17.4.9, or 16.10.x before 16.10.17. Identify externally accessible instances via port 8080/443 scans or reverse-DNS resolution.

suggestion.title: Minify Parameter Bypass — XWiki ssx/jsx Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: PoC URL includes 'minify=false' parameter: 'resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false'. This suggests attackers disable compression to exfiltrate readable config. Detection should trigger on parameter combinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to ssx/jsx endpoints with minify=false AND resource parameter containing path traversal or leading slash. This parameter combination reduces likelihood of benign traffic.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-33137 XWiki Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-33137 in 'Indicators of Compromise (high-fidelity only)' section. Pipeline must identify vulnerable XWiki versions (pre-16.10.17, pre-17.4.9, pre-17.10.3, pre-18.0.1) before patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory against vulnerable XWiki version ranges (16.x <16.10.17, 17.0-17.3.x, 17.4.0-17.4.8, 17.5-17.9.x, 17.10.0-17.10.2, 18.0.0, 18.1.0-beta/rc). Prioritize systems with internet exposure or in untrusted network zones.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated REST XAR Import to /wikis/{wikiName}
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding states 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks.' This is the direct attack vector requiring hunt for REST calls lacking prior authentication tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to /wikis/{wikiName} or /wikis/.*/rest endpoints on XWiki instances where source IP has no corresponding authenticated session within 5-minute lookback or lacks valid auth headers (Authorization, JSESSIONID).

suggestion.title: XAR Archive Upload or Import Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability allows attackers to 'create or update documents in the target wiki' via XAR import. XAR file uploads, especially from unauthenticated sources, are abnormal and directly indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uploads of .xar or .jar files containing XWiki archives to /upload or /import endpoints; correlate with unauthenticated session logs. Flag file creation events in XWiki document directories (spaces/) immediately following XAR receipt.

suggestion.title: Bulk or Anomalous Document Creation in XWiki
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful exploitation manifests as unauthorized 'create or update documents.' Abnormal document proliferation outside normal user workflows signals exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for rapid document creation events (>10 docs in 5 minutes) or creation from service accounts/unauthenticated sessions in XWiki audit logs. Correlate with absence of corresponding user UI login events or API authentication headers.

suggestion.title: File Hash IOC: Exploit Artifact (SHA1 4b7b95b79256...)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides SHA1 4b7b95b79256374d487e9ece1dc48f527966990f in 'Indicators of Compromise' section. This hash must be hunted on endpoints to detect exploit payload or malicious XAR archive presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search endpoint file systems and memory for files matching SHA1 hash 4b7b95b79256374d487e9ece1dc48f527966990f. Check temp directories, download folders, and web application upload directories where XAR payloads might be staged.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Auth Failures - Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions'—indicates elevated auth failure rates. Pipeline ignored this clear observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions API endpoints (actions.github.com) for abnormal spike in 401/403 responses or auth token rejections. Correlate with GitHub status page updates. Look for sustained elevation in failed authentication attempts that diverges from baseline within 5-minute windows.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Disruption - Orphaned Workflow Runs
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes Actions being inaccessible. Pipeline should detect failed workflow executions or queued-but-unexecuted jobs during service incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows stuck in 'queued' or 'waiting_for_runner' state for >30 minutes with concurrent auth errors. Track dependency failures in multi-job workflows tied to GitHub infrastructure status changes.

suggestion.title: Token Compromise During Service Degradation
suggestion.rationale: When GitHub auth is down or degraded, users may resort to alternative authentication methods or token reuse. Article context strongly implies credential-handling risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PAT (Personal Access Token) or OIDC token generation, usage, or validation anomalies during reported GitHub outage windows. Flag tokens created just before or during incident as high-risk if later used in unusual ways.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Risk - Unvetted Dependency Updates During GitHub Downtime
suggestion.rationale: If Actions cannot validate code or CI checks fail, attackers may inject malicious dependencies. Article phrase 'Denying Access to Actions' implies CI gates are offline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package uploads (npm, PyPI, etc.) or dependency merges that bypass GitHub Actions checks or occur when workflow runners report connectivity loss. Correlate with incident timeline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised GitHub Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: If GitHub's own auth backend is compromised (suggested by service-wide auth failures), attackers gain access to service accounts with broad permissions across hosted repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication from GitHub service accounts (bot identities, automation accounts) to other cloud platforms (Azure, AWS) or internal systems during or immediately after GitHub auth incident. Track permissions changes on those accounts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Unrestricted Token Generation During Incident
suggestion.rationale: Service degradation or broken auth validation could allow attackers to generate high-privilege tokens without normal MFA/audit controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any token creation (PAT, OIDC, SSH keys) with org-wide or repo-admin scope during incident window where normal validation was known to be offline. Cross-check against expected CI/CD service accounts.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 as the vector used to compromise 700 websites. Pipeline produced zero kill chain phases; T1190 exploitation should be detectable via anomalous HTTP request patterns to Ghost CMS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/PUT requests to Ghost CMS admin endpoints or known vulnerable API paths with unusual payloads or rapid scanning patterns. Correlate with Ghost CMS version detection to identify in-scope targets.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states websites were 'poisoned' with ClickFix malware. No detection rule generated despite named malware family commonly using HTML injections, fake browser update popups, and script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ClickFix indicators: suspicious JavaScript execution from web server processes, creation of fake browser update files, registry modifications associated with ClickFix payload delivery, and command-line execution patterns matching known ClickFix downloaders.

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawning Suspicious Children Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful CVE-2026-26980 exploitation would allow arbitrary code execution. Pipeline did not suggest detection for unexpected child processes spawned by Ghost/web server processes (apache, nginx, node).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes from Ghost CMS/Node.js service accounts. Alert on spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, curl, wget, or unusual interpreters from web server parent processes, especially if accompanied by network egress.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation or Privilege Escalation in Compromised CMS
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation activity following CVE-2026-26980 compromise would typically include persistence via admin account creation. Article mentions 'poisoned' websites but pipeline generated no detection for account manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin API calls for user creation, role elevation, or authentication bypass patterns. Detect unusual database modifications creating new admin accounts or modifying permission tables.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation in Web Root Directories
suggestion.rationale: Website poisoning implies injected files. Pipeline missed detection for suspicious file writes to web-served directories post-CVE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate file creation patterns in Ghost CMS content/theme directories. Alert on executable file extensions (.exe, .dll, .php, .jsp, .aspx) or suspicious script files (encoded JavaScript, obfuscated shells) created outside normal deployment windows in web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Executable or Script Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Deploy MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 via Phishing' as delivery mechanism, yet pipeline generated zero detection use cases for phishing campaigns or email-borne malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email attachments with executable content (.exe, .com, .scr) or suspicious script files (.ps1, .vbs, .js) originating from external senders. Correlate attachment hashes against known MiniFast/MiniJunk samples. Monitor for immediate process execution following user interaction with these attachments.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning and Redirect Chain to Malware Download
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'SEO Poisoning' as attack vector—no detection use case was generated for malicious search result redirection or landing page reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on newly registered or compromised domains appearing in search engine results. Detect redirect chains landing on attacker infrastructure. Alert on users navigating to domains hosting malware downloads immediately after search activity.

suggestion.title: MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware family names are core indicators but pipeline surfaced zero execution-phase detections. No behavioral patterns, process trees, or file I/O signatures mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process spawning from browser or email client processes. Look for parent-child process chains showing script interpreter (powershell, cmd, cscript) execution following user interaction. Monitor for injection into legitimate system processes or unusual file creation in AppData/Temp.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting and Browser Credential Store Access
suggestion.rationale: MiniFast and MiniJunk are infostealer families historically targeting credentials; pipeline did not map T1555 or credential_access phase despite malware names implying credential theft capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when malware processes access browser credential stores (%APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, Firefox profiles) or attempt to dump LSASS memory. Monitor for unusual registry access to Windows credential managers. Correlate file access patterns with known credential exfiltration TTPs.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: All-in-one malware like MiniFast and MiniJunk require C2 beaconing; pipeline generated zero detection use cases for command-and-control or exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with base64-encoded or encrypted payloads to attacker-controlled domains. Monitor for DNS queries to known malicious infrastructure or fast-flux domains. Alert on sustained outbound connections from infected endpoints carrying telemetry (system info, credentials, browser data).

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Malware Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: No persistence phase UCs generated despite Iranian APT campaigns typically establishing foothold via registry modifications, scheduled tasks, or startup folders post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to Run/RunOnce registry keys or creation of scheduled tasks by non-standard processes. Alert on .lnk files in Startup folder or additions to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\Load. Correlate timing with malware execution.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization RCE via Hardcoded Machine Key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes threat actors using 'hardcoded machine key' to 'sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution'—core detection gap given this is the root exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ASP.NET applications for anomalous ViewState parameters in HTTP requests, particularly POST operations to .aspx pages. Inspect base64-decoded ViewState for unexpected serialization objects; correlate with IIS worker process (w3wp.exe) spawning unusual child processes. Alert on ViewState validation failures in ASP.NET logs paired with process creation.

suggestion.title: Godzilla In-Memory Web Shell Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '.NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)'—an in-memory persistence mechanism that requires specific behavioral signatures not covered by standard web shell rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious compilation and loading of .NET assemblies into IIS worker process memory. Look for csc.exe or roslyn compilation invoked from w3wp.exe context, or .NET reflection APIs used to dynamically load unsigned/suspicious assemblies. Monitor for IIS responding to HTTP requests with command output patterns consistent with web shell interaction.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Web Application Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat actor modifying 'application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin'—a distinct attack phase requiring file-integrity and script-analysis detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to .js files within web application directories (esp. wwwroot, application root). Alert on JavaScript files containing code that constructs download prompts or references external attacker-controlled domains. Cross-reference modified JS with known application baselines.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Delivery via Fake Software Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious script 'convinced users to download a fake installer,' which deployed 'Cobalt Strike beacon'—requires detection for both social-engineering delivery and beacon C2 traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious .exe or .msi downloads from web server contexts; inspect for beacon signatures (DNS beaconing, HTTPS C2 patterns, malleable C2 indicators). Correlate download events with user interaction logs showing 'security plugin' or 'authentication' prompts. Monitor for Cobalt Strike HTTP/DNS fingerprints and known beacon domains.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation and File System Access Expansion Post-Web Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'executed commands to escalate their control over the web server's file system'—a post-exploitation detection gap for lateral movement from IIS context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution spawning from IIS worker process context (w3wp.exe child processes) that attempt filesystem access beyond the web application directory. Alert on command-line invocations of privilege escalation utilities (whoami, ipconfig, systeminfo, net.exe) from web server context. Correlate with abnormal file access patterns in sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver-Specific CVE-2026-5426 Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CVE-2026-5426 as affecting 'installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026' with 'standardized web.config file'—version and configuration-specific detection is required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create signature for KnowledgeDeliver pre-Feb-24-2026 installations by fingerprinting web.config version/content hash. Monitor for HTTP requests to KnowledgeDeliver endpoints with ViewState parameters; correlate with known machine-key values if accessible. Alert on exploitation attempts if web.config has not been updated post-Feb-24-2026.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited'—this is the named initial access vector. Pipeline failed to generate any detection use case for exploitation attempts against this identified vulnerable application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints for anomalous HTTP requests with suspicious payloads, known vulnerability scanner signatures, or URI patterns consistent with exploitation. Flag successful file uploads or script injections to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Godzilla' was deployed post-exploitation. This known webshell should trigger detection via file creation in web directories, process spawning from web services, or command-line activity. Pipeline generated no UC despite unambiguous mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious script files (PHP, ASPX, JSP) written to web directories with Godzilla-associated naming patterns or obfuscation. Flag process creation where web service accounts spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash with unusual parameters.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Command and Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names Cobalt Strike as the deployed C2 framework. This tool has distinctive network signatures (JA3 fingerprints, TLS certificate patterns, beacon intervals) and should have generated a dedicated UC. Pipeline missed this despite explicit reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Cobalt Strike C2 beaconing via known JA3 signatures, suspicious HTTPS certificate patterns, periodic small-payload traffic consistent with beacon check-ins, or communication to known CS infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Web Service Process Spawning System Command Shells
suggestion.rationale: LMS compromise followed by Godzilla webshell deployment implies web-to-shell execution. This behavioral pattern is central to the described attack chain but pipeline did not generate a detection use case for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where web service accounts (w3wp.exe, apache, nginx, tomcat) spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh. Escalate detections with suspicious arguments or execution from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Multiple MFA Push Notifications in Short Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: MFA prompt bombing inherently floods users with repeated authentication challenges to overwhelm decision-making. Title emphasizes this tactic; requires detection of anomalous MFA challenge volume within minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when same user account receives >3 MFA push notifications or TOTP requests within 5 minutes. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and cross-reference with user communication to identify social engineering success. Establish baseline per user to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Approved MFA Following Multiple Rejections
suggestion.rationale: Core bombing tactic: attacker floods user until they approve out of frustration or confusion. Pattern of rejected-then-approved challenges is distinctive of compromise via this method, not accidental re-auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful MFA approval within same session after 2+ denied/expired challenges. Score higher if temporal clustering is tight (<2 min between reject and approve). Cross-validate against user's device history and typical approval latency.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Triggering MFA Challenges
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain begins with valid credential acquisition (phishing, breach). Successful password submission followed by downstream MFA activity indicates attacker has progressed to second-factor manipulation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume login attempts (10+ in 15 min) from non-residential IPs or impossible-travel locations with successful password validation and immediate MFA challenge issuance to recipient. Indicates automated credential spray reaching second factor.

suggestion.title: Geographic Mismatch Between Initial Login and MFA Approval
suggestion.rationale: Bomber is remote; legitimate user may be geographically distant from attacker. Detecting IP location delta between initial sign-in and MFA approval surfaces potential user duress or successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events where initial password-validation IP and MFA-approval IP are >500 km apart with impossible travel time between events. Weight alert higher if MFA approval IP matches known malicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Recipient with Subsequent MFA Bombing
suggestion.rationale: Title implies MFA failure stems from prior compromise; pipeline must trace from email vector. Users who clicked phishing links should be monitored for downstream MFA anomalies within 24 hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Join email click data (malicious URL recipient) with high-volume MFA challenges and successful approval to same user account within 24 hours. Indicates compromised credential use on legitimate account post-phishing.

suggestion.title: Successful Account Access Post-MFA Bombardment
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is account takeover; successful login after sustained MFA activity, followed by anomalous post-auth behavior, confirms compromise. Required to measure impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login completion after MFA bombardment (>3 challenges, ≥1 approval) when followed within 30 minutes by unusual account activities (new device, impossible travel, privilege changes, forwarding rule creation, data export).

suggestion.title: Rapid Multi-Host File Encryption Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Stop Ransomware Spread' and 'Isolates Compromised Devices'—implies detection of file encryption as the attack step that triggers isolation. Pipeline missed this core ransomware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bursts of file creation/modification with encryption-like extensions (.locked, .encrypted, .ransom variants) or mass overwrites of user document directories within a short time window on a single device. Correlate with process creation for known ransomware families or suspicious script execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Network Shares Pre-Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions preventing 'Ransomware Spread'—implies lateral propagation to network shares or adjacent hosts. Pipeline failed to surface lateral movement detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual read-then-write patterns across network shares, or processes accessing multiple hosts sequentially to execute payloads. Flag high-volume share enumeration from a single source followed by file writes to those shares.

suggestion.title: Device Isolation Trigger - High Entropy File Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Automatically Isolates Compromised Devices'—the isolation decision must be based on detection signals. Pipeline should model what signals justify isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes encrypting files at scale (e.g., >100 files/min in system or user directories), particularly when combined with parent process indicators of malware (renamed system binaries, script interpreters with obfuscation, unsigned executables). These signals trigger automated isolation.

suggestion.title: Defensive - Ransomware-Adjacent Process Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title discusses response to 'Compromised Devices'—implies the article may describe attack chains leading to ransomware execution. Pipeline produced no detection for command execution, process manipulation, or malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscated PowerShell/cmd execution, script interpreters with packed/unsigned parents, or processes spawning from Office/browser contexts without user interaction. These precede ransomware payloads and warrant heightened isolation readiness.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable and Suspicious DLL Pair
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'DLL Side-Loading' in title and campaign overview. This is the primary attack mechanism and requires detection of legitimate executables loading DLLs from non-standard paths or with suspicious attributes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate Windows executables (e.g., rundll32, explorer, svchost, legitimate third-party apps) loading DLLs from user-writable directories, %AppData%, %Temp%, or paths inconsistent with the executable's installation directory. Flag unsigned or recently-created DLLs loaded by legitimately-signed processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Drops in System Paths by MuddyWater Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: DLL side-loading campaigns typically stage both the legitimate executable and malicious DLL in the same directory. Article mentions 'espionage campaign' requiring reconnaissance and staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation of executable + DLL pairs in unexpected locations (downloads, %Temp%, email attachment extraction paths). Baseline known-good pairs and alert on anomalous combinations, especially if the DLL hash is previously unseen.

suggestion.title: Process Execution with Command-Line Indicators of DLL Sideload Staging
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater often uses common delivery mechanisms such as compressed archives or scripts that extract both components. Missing coverage for extraction and execution workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for archive extraction tools (7-Zip, WinRAR, tar, expand.exe) or script interpreters (powershell, cmd, cscript) followed within seconds by legitimate process execution from non-standard paths, particularly in user-controlled directories.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Compromised Process or Service Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns typically establish persistence. Article states 'espionage campaign' with no indication of one-shot attacks; persistence mechanisms should be covered.
