suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to run, runonce, or service registry keys by processes that loaded suspicious DLLs. Alert on additions of legitimate executables as service binaries pointing to non-standard paths or with encoded/obfuscated ImagePath values.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater-Attributed Infrastructure Network Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies threat actor (MuddyWater). No mention of extracted C2 domains, IPs, or known infrastructure. Network-based detection should correlate with threat-actor TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound network connections from processes that loaded suspicious DLLs against known or newly identified MuddyWater C2 infrastructure. Flag HTTP User-Agent strings or certificate issuer anomalies consistent with MuddyWater malware families.

suggestion.title: Espionage Payload Communication via Sideloaded Process
suggestion.rationale: Campaign is explicitly espionage-focused, implying data exfiltration. Pipeline missed detection of communication from processes post-DLL injection suggesting data theft workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected network connections (DNS queries, HTTP POST, HTTPS) originating from legitimate-looking executables that were previously flagged as sideload vectors, particularly to non-standard ports or with high volume of data transfer.

suggestion.title: Angular Language Service Extension Install or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes extension-based attack vector ('Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities'). Pipeline should detect installation of malicious or unsigned extensions, manifest tampering, or extension permission changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of extension manifests, unexpected extension directory writes, or unsigned extension registration. Alert on extension installs from non-standard sources or with admin privileges.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution from Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'RCE Attacks' in title. Pipeline failed to surface execution pattern detection for code execution originating from extension sandboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from extension runtime (e.g., node.exe, chrome.exe with extension UIDs), particularly with suspicious command lines (PowerShell, cmd.exe, script interpreters). Flag unexpected outbound network connections from extension process contexts.

suggestion.title: Extension Manifest or Code Injection/Tampering
suggestion.rationale: RCE via extension requires either malicious manifest or code injection into extension files. Article body truncation prevents specific vector identification, but this is standard attack path against extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected writes to extension installation directories (/Extensions/, .vscode/extensions, chrome://extensions paths). Alert on base64-encoded or obfuscated content appearing in extension files, or file modifications followed by immediate process execution.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Extension Auto-Load or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: RCE via extension likely includes persistence mechanism. Pipeline should map extension-based persistence to MITRE T1547.004 or equivalent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of extension autoload registries or manifest files with run/autoStart directives. Flag extensions added to startup directories or extension load lists modified outside of official IDE/browser management.

suggestion.title: Successful RDP Logon from External IP to High-Value Host
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RDP as entry vector: 'RDP Access' — core attack initiation mechanism requiring baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful RDP logons (EventID 4624, Logon Type 10) to assets without prior RDP activity, especially from external IPs or after failed brute-force attempts. Baseline normal RDP access and flag deviations by user, source IP, and time-of-day.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Execution Post-RDP Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'Remote Admin Tools for Stealthy Persistence' — second stage of attack chain requiring process execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful RDP logon with child process execution of psexec.exe, wmic.exe, or winrs.exe within 30 minutes. Flag when these tools run with SYSTEM or unexpected service account privileges, especially targeting multiple destination hosts.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Activity Following RDP + Admin Tool Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'NightSpire Ransomware' as payload — impact phase detection critical for blocking encryption before mass file encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity file modifications (>1000 files/min) with consistent extension rewriting (.nsp, .nightspire, or attacker-specific) originating from process trees rooted in RDP session or spawned by remote admin tools. Correlate with executable creation in temp directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Brute-Force Against RDP Service
suggestion.rationale: RDP persistence implies credential compromise; article does not mention initial exploit, suggesting credential attack as likely entry method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of failed RDP logon attempts (EventID 4625, >10 failures within 5 minutes) targeting specific accounts from single source IP. Correlate with successful logon from same source immediately following brute-force termination.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task or Service Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Stealthy Persistence' — indicates re-entry mechanism beyond initial RDP session, requiring dormant persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service creation (sc.exe, New-Service) or scheduled task registration (schtasks, Register-ScheduledTask) executed from RDP context, especially those running as SYSTEM without corresponding user context. Look for persistence artifacts pointing to attacker-controlled payloads in temp or public shares.

suggestion.title: Shadow Account Creation for RDP Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: RDP 'stealthy' access sustained over time requires hidden account; article does not exclude account-based persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect local user account creation (EventID 4720) followed by addition to Remote Desktop Users group, especially when created outside normal provisioning windows. Flag accounts with administrative group membership created after incident start time.

suggestion.title: Fileless Code Execution on Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fileless Execution' as core capability; pipeline produced zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation or memory-region modification without corresponding file I/O on disk. Alert on mmap/mprotect syscalls followed by code execution in non-standard regions (heap, /dev/shm).

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Loading and Kernel Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'eBPF Rootkit'; pipeline extracted zero rootkit or privilege-escalation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bpf() syscalls loading programs into kernel space, particularly from unprivileged processes. Alert on kernel hook attachment (kprobes, tracepoints) from suspicious source processes.

suggestion.title: Developer-Targeted Initial Access for Quasar RAT
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Targets Developers'; article describes targeted delivery mechanism. Zero initial-access use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for developers executing files from suspicious origins or clicking malicious links. Correlate email metadata with unusual interpreter spawning (Python, Node, Go launching rare child processes).

suggestion.title: Quasar RAT Command-and-Control Communication Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: As a RAT, Quasar must establish C2 communication for command issuance. Zero C2 detection use cases in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile outbound connections from developer workstations to suspicious infrastructure. Monitor for periodic beaconing patterns to known or suspected Quasar C2 domains/IPs; flag unusual encryption or tunneling.

suggestion.title: System Discovery and Reconnaissance via eBPF Sniffing
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkits are leveraged for stealthy system reconnaissance and data collection. Article implies post-exploitation activity. Pipeline missed discovery-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eBPF programs that attach to networking or process-tracing hooks to exfiltrate system metadata, environment variables, or network data. Alert on anomalous kernel-to-userspace data flows.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Rootkit-Hidden Processes
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkits hide malicious processes from standard enumeration tools. Article explicitly mentions rootkit capability. Zero defense-evasion detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare process listings between kernel-level queries (proc parsing) and userspace tools (/bin/ps, top). Flag discrepancies indicating rootkit-level DKOM. Monitor vfs/syscall hook modifications.

suggestion.title: Volumetric DDoS Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'New AI DDoS Attacks'—volumetric component is implicit in any DDoS discussion. Webinar framing 'Learn How to Fight Back' indicates defensive detection is primary scope yet zero DDoS-specific use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained traffic increase from >10 distributed sources targeting single asset, rate exceeding baseline by 5x+ over 5-minute window. Correlate with time-of-day and legitimate traffic patterns to reduce noise from legitimate spikes.

suggestion.title: Application-Layer DDoS Detection (HTTP Flood / Slowloris)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attacks are 'smarter'—AI optimization implies attacks move beyond simple volumetric patterns to application-layer exploitation. This nuance was entirely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid incomplete HTTP requests, slow request completion times, excessive connection holding, or requests with malformed headers from single/clustered IPs. Flag when request-per-connection ratio deviates >3σ from baseline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Egress to Known Botnet / DDoS-as-a-Service Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: AI DDoS campaigns require command-and-control coordination or botnet enrollment. No C2 or orchestration patterns extracted despite 'new' attack methodology implying novel infrastructure may be in use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections to known botnet C2 domains, DDoS-for-hire platforms, or previously-unobserved infrastructure associated with AI-augmented attack groups. Flag rare destination ports (non-80, 443) and beaconing patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Manager Install from Unusual Source
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses developer machines as primary targets; supply chain compromise typically begins with trojanized package installation (npm, pip, rubygems). Pipeline should detect installations from non-standard repositories or unusual version transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager invocations (npm install, pip install, gem install, cargo build) with suspicious flags (--registry, --index-url, environment variable overrides). Correlate with unusual child processes or network connections to non-standard repositories. Flag version downgrades or version pins to old/unpatched releases.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Git Credentials and SSH Keys
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines store authentication materials (git config, SSH keys in ~/.ssh, API tokens in env). Article implies attackers target these to pivot supply chain; detect reads/copies of credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access to .ssh/*, .git/config, ~/.netrc, .aws/credentials, or shell profile files (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc) by non-git/non-ssh processes. Flag exfiltration of these files via curl/wget/SCP to external hosts. Monitor for base64-encoded credential data in process arguments.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Git Hooks and Shell Profile Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses developer machines as persistent beachheads; attackers establish persistence via git hooks (pre-commit, post-commit), shell profiles (.bashrc, .zshenv), or IDE startup scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected writes to .git/hooks/*, ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.bash_profile, or IDE config directories (.vscode/settings.json, .idea/workspace.xml). Flag execution of shell profiles or hook scripts by non-shell processes. Monitor for suspicious sourcing of external scripts within login/shell initialization.

suggestion.title: Source Code Exfiltration via Archive or Copy Utilities
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes supply chain attacks targeting code; successful compromise leads to IP theft. Detect bulk exfiltration of source code repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on tar/zip/7z invocations over ~10 MB targeting source directories (~/.git, src/, node_modules). Flag curl/wget/scp/sftp operations exfiltrating archives or individual source files to external hosts. Monitor for unusual compression tool execution from IDE or shell processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IDE Plugin or Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploit IDEs (VSCode, JetBrains) to implant backdoors or steal credentials via malicious extensions. Article should surface this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin/extension directories for suspicious installs (.vscode/extensions, .gradle/caches, .m2/repository). Flag network requests from IDE processes to untrusted CDNs. Detect unsigned or self-signed extensions. Alert on IDE processes spawning shells or making outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Git Configuration or Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Compromised developer machines enable attackers to modify git remote URLs, inject malicious commits, or pivot via git credentials to other repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 'git config' invocations modifying user/global config, especially credential.helper, core.sshCommand, or remote URLs. Flag commits signed by unknown keys or with unusual authorship metadata. Monitor for git operations from non-interactive processes or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Initialization Failure on 15+ Character Hostname
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Windows Server 2016 Domain Controller May Fail with 15-Character Hostname'—this is an operational failure that triggers impact phase and should be detectable via DC event logs or system initialization monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Server 2016 Domain Controller services failing to initialize or entering error states immediately after boot when hostname length exceeds 14 characters. Correlate hostname configuration against NetBIOS/FQDN length limits. Alert on repeated DC service restarts or startup failures in event logs.

suggestion.title: Hostname Configuration Validation for Domain Controller Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a constraint ('15-character hostname') that affects DC viability—detection should baseline valid hostname patterns for DCs in Active Directory to identify non-compliant configurations that may cause silent failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all Domain Controller hostnames in Active Directory and alert on any DC object with a NetBIOS name >15 characters or FQDN components that conflict with DC initialization requirements. Generate inventory of at-risk systems before service failure.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal' — campaigns should be detected by outbound emails containing http://microsoft.com/devicelogin or similar device auth URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound phishing emails that contain or redirect to device authorization flow portals (microsoft.com/devicelogin, similar patterns). High fidelity signals: sender not from trusted domain, URL shortener abuse, urgency/social engineering lures, no legitimate business context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code OAuth Authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token' — device code authorizations followed immediately by token issuance and high-risk actions (mass email access, cloud app access) from new/anomalous clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device code OAuth grants with subsequent token usage showing account access from geographically impossible locations or unusual client applications. Flag if device code auth + MFA completion + immediate cross-tenant or external app access within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rules Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity' — detection for inbox rule creation by anomalous sessions or devices should trigger on rules with forwarding/deletion patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rule creation within 1-4 hours of successful OAuth token auth via device code, especially rules that forward/delete/move mail or target sensitive keywords. Baseline user's historical rule creation behavior; anomalies merit escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Azure/Entra
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access' — device enrollment events from compromised accounts should correlate with phishing/device code auth timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registration/enrollment (Intune, Azure AD join, Windows Hello enrollment) by accounts that recently completed device-code OAuth flows or triggered phishing alerts. Flag if registration occurs outside business hours or from untrusted IPs.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie Capture via Cookie Link AitM
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens' — detection for impossible travel, token replay, or session access from attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful logins (MFA passed) with near-simultaneous failed login attempts or token usage from geographically impossible origin, or detect session cookies presented from out-of-band infrastructure. Baseline user login patterns and flag anomalous browser/client user agents.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant or Cloud SaaS Access Post-Device-Code Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat actors now have full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms' — token reuse against federated apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for OAuth tokens issued via device code flow being reused to access downstream cloud SaaS (Salesforce, Slack, etc.). Alert if MFA-passing token auth + same session token used against non-Microsoft apps, especially within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states CVE-2026-26980 as exploit vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or kill-chain mapping for initial access. Should detect abnormal HTTP requests to Ghost endpoints matching known POC patterns or error responses indicative of exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS web servers for HTTP POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Alert on requests with suspicious User-Agent strings, script injection payloads, or from non-standard source IPs. Correlate web server 4xx responses with subsequent authentication anomalies within 1-2 hours.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Payload Injection into Ghost Templates
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 700+ sites hijacked 'for ClickFix attacks'—execution phase must involve script/payload delivery. Pipeline created no detection for malicious code injection or defacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to Ghost theme files, metadata, or post content containing obfuscated JavaScript, iframe tags, or external script references to known ClickFix C2 domains. Monitor HTTP response headers and content for injected redirect headers or malicious <script> tags in responses from compromised blogs.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Web Shell Persistence in Ghost Root
suggestion.rationale: Title states site 'hijack' implying persistent access; pipeline did not surface persistence detection. Web shells are standard post-exploitation persistence in CMS compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost content directory and theme folders for unexpected PHP, JSP, or executable uploads post-CVE timestamp. Alert on web server access logs showing requests to newly created files in content root. Cross-reference file timestamps with detected exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Ghost Admin Account Creation Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining 700+ compromised sites requires credential persistence; pipeline did not create detection for backdoor accounts. Article phrase 'hijack' implies attacker maintenance access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost API logs and database activity logs for creation of new admin or staff-level user accounts within hours of detected CVE exploitation. Flag accounts created with mismatched timestamps, generic names (admin2, test), or from non-internal IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Compromised Ghost Sites Serving Malicious Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites exploited 'for ClickFix attacks'—impact phase involves serving malware. No detection for traffic redirection or malicious content serving from hijacked domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected HTTP 301/302 responses from known legitimate Ghost blog domains to suspicious or phishing-infrastructure destinations. Monitor DNS queries from web servers to unknown destinations. Flag unexpected meta-refresh tags or window.location JavaScript in page responses.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Ghost CMS Database or Config Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites at scale likely involves database tampering for backdoor persistence or payload staging. Pipeline did not surface database-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost database for INSERT/UPDATE operations on users, posts, or settings tables outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on new row additions to user tables with high-privilege roles and timestamps matching exploitation timeline. Track modifications to Ghost config files for C2 callback infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only Code Execution via Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'memory-only RAT' — requires detection of code execution without disk artifacts. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning where image path mismatches payload in memory, or legitimate system process (System, csrss, svchost) spawning with suspicious command-line arguments. Monitor for WriteProcessMemory and CreateRemoteThread APIs targeting system services.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Malware Execution Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'RemotePE' as deployed malware; no IOC or execution signature extracted despite this being primary technical indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish signatures for RemotePE process behavior: known process names, command-line patterns, registry keys, API call sequences, and mutex artifacts. Correlate with C2 beacon indicators.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beacon and Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT necessitates C2 communication; Lazarus has documented beacon signatures and network behaviors. Article omits C2-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from compromised endpoints to known or suspected Lazarus C2 infrastructure. Detect beacon traffic patterns: regular HTTP POST/GET callbacks, non-standard ports, encrypted payloads, and size/timing anomalies.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing Detection for Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only deployment typically uses process hollowing into legitimate processes; article describes this evasion pattern without corresponding defense-evasion use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process anomalies: legitimate system process (explorer.exe, svchost.exe) spawning child with inconsistent subsystem or command-line. Flag hollow processes via image load mismatches or empty image path fields.

suggestion.title: Phishing-Based Initial Access for Lazarus
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus' primary initial-access TTP is spear-phishing and watering holes against financial/crypto sectors (article target). Pipeline generated no initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macro-enabled Office documents, HWP exploits, archived executables, and suspicious script downloads arriving via email to finance/crypto company domains. Track macro execution and living-off-the-land binary abuse following email interaction.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from npm/PyPI/Crates.io
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies supply-chain attack 'spreads credential-stealing malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—no detection UC exists for package manager install activity tied to known-malicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of package install commands (npm install, pip install, cargo build) targeting known-compromised package names. Correlate against live feed of flagged packages from npm/PyPI/Crates registries. Flag when install succeeds from non-standard mirrors or with unusual post-install script execution.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Malicious Package Post-Install Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload is 'credential-stealing malware'—supply-chain vector uses post-install hooks to steal credentials at package load time. No UC for detecting credential APIs (process.env, .aws/credentials, ~/.ssh, browser storage) being read during package setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/python/rust post-install or setup scripts reading credential stores: /home/*/.ssh/*, /home/*/.aws/*, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Credentials, browser profile directories. Alert on credential-access APIs (getenv, open() on credential paths) during package installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DNS/HTTP from Package Manager Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware payload must exfiltrate to attacker C2—article title indicates multi-platform campaign but no detection for anomalous network activity initiated by npm/pip/cargo processes or child processes spawned during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by package manager processes (node, python, rustc) or their child processes during install/build phases. Flag domains with low reputation, newly registered, or known C2 sinkhole infrastructure. Cross-reference against passive DNS for patterns.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Package Name Variation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks commonly use name-squatting (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'lodash-utils'). Article states TrapDoor spreads 'via npm, PyPI'—detection should identify package installs where names are visually similar to legitimate high-dependency packages or recently created variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package installs where package name is Levenshtein-distance close to known legitimate packages (e.g., one character substitution, swapped letters). Alert on first-time installs of packages created <30 days ago that depend on only recent/new packages or have unusual network footprint.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Process Spawning from Package Manager Installation
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware in post-install hooks will spawn child processes (curl, wget, powershell, bash) to exfiltrate or download payloads. Article describes multi-platform campaign—no detection for unexpected child process spawning from npm/pip/cargo parent contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package manager processes (or their children: node.js, python, cargo) spawn non-standard children: shell interpreters (bash, cmd.exe, powershell), network utilities (curl, wget, nc), or archive tools (zip, tar) during install phase. Baseline legitimate post-install activities per popular packages.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Internet-Facing Vulnerabilities (Disclosure-to-Patch Window)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Internet-Facing Flaws Amid AI-Assisted Attacks' + '12-Hour Patching' establishes a vulnerability disclosure-to-patch gap as the attack surface. Pipeline produced no use case for T1190 or post-disclosure exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability disclosure timestamps with abnormal traffic spikes to affected internet-facing services. Alert on HTTP requests containing exploitation signatures (SQLi, RCE payloads, path traversal) within 24 hours of CVE publication and before patch deployment.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Malware Payload Generation and Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'AI-Assisted Attacks'. Pipeline should have created detections for LLM-generated polyglot payloads, obfuscated command chains, and novel evasion patterns that bypass static signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor command-line invocations for high entropy arguments, unusual whitespace/encoding patterns, dynamic content generation (base64 -d, certutil), and chained utility abuse. Flag PowerShell/cmd execution with variable substitution or loop-based payload construction.

suggestion.title: Automated Vulnerability Scanning of Public Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in 'Internet-Facing Flaws' threat model: attackers enumerate targets before exploitation. Pipeline missed T1595/T1592 (Active Scanning, Gather Victim Network Information).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect systematic port/service enumeration from external sources against internet-facing hosts. Alert on tools (nmap, masscan, nessus User-Agents) or unusual request patterns to common vulnerability-bearing ports (80,443,3389,22) from single source IPs.

suggestion.title: Rapid Iterative Exploitation During Patch Window
suggestion.rationale: The 12-hour window is mentioned as critical context. Pipeline should detect repeated exploitation attempts/failures as attackers iterate—characteristic of AI-assisted fuzzing/automation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In the 12-hour window post-disclosure: alert on ≥5 distinct payload variations against the same endpoint from same source IP, high HTTP error rates (4xx/5xx spikes), or repeated request patterns with modified parameter encoding.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing (Vishing) Targeting Employee SSO Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' No use case for detecting vishing attempts or suspicious inbound calls preceding authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag employee reports of unsolicited calls requesting credential validation. Correlate inbound calls (marked high-risk via phone system logs) with Entra logins from new device/location within 4 hours. Alert if login follows call report and originates outside normal work hours or geography.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra Account Takeover via Credential Stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised Entra account used for downstream SaaS access. Should detect credential reuse/brute-force patterns preceding successful login from abnormal source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ failed Entra login attempts for same user account across different IPs within 1 hour, followed by successful login. Flag successful logins with impossible-travel distance or from high-risk countries if not corporate VPN.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Theft and Unauthorized SaaS API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealing OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances.' Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized OAuth consent grants or token issuance from compromised account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Entra for new OAuth app consents granted by high-risk accounts or during off-hours. Alert on Salesforce API authentication using tokens issued >30 days prior with zero subsequent legitimate use.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Export of Customer PII and CPNI
suggestion.rationale: Article: '40 million records containing the personal information of consumer and business customers' stolen from Salesforce. No detection for bulk data extraction from CRM by non-sales-ops accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk API exports (Bulk API, REST export) retrieving >10k Contact/Account records. Correlation check: is exporting user in customer-service/sales role? Flag exports containing CPNI fields by non-compliance teams.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Unrelated SaaS Platforms from Single SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'access to export millions...from the company's Salesforce instance...after gaining access...threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as...Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe...' Single compromised identity accessing >5 SaaS is behaviorally abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track single user accessing 5+ distinct SaaS applications within 24 hours when historical baseline is ≤2. Flag if apps are in different business units (e.g., Finance + Operations + HR). Cross-check against RBAC: is user entitled to all accessed apps?

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Data Staging and Exfiltration via Compromised SaaS Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen data is then used to extort the company by threatening to leak the data if a ransom is not paid.' Implies bulk data movement from Salesforce to attacker-controlled staging or leak site.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large Salesforce export volumes (>1GB per day) with suspicious network egress (uploads to free file-hosting, unknown S3 buckets, or Tor exit nodes). Alert if export occurs from account with no prior export history.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Linux Process Execution on Edge Router Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'custom Linux implant' deployment; no use case generated for detecting unusual process spawning or script execution on network edge devices targeting router OS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or non-OEM binaries spawned on Cisco, Fortinet, Juniper, or Huawei edge routers. Flag bash/sh process creation from non-standard paths or with suspicious command-line arguments. Establish process baseline for each router model to detect anomalous child process chains.

suggestion.title: Router-to-External C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'custom Linux implant' which necessarily implies command-and-control communication; no detection use case for outbound C2 traffic from compromised edge router.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate edge router NetFlow/firewall logs for outbound connections to non-whitelisted external IPs on non-standard ports (avoid 53, 80, 443 if possible). Alert on encrypted TLS sessions from router management interface IPs to suspicious ASNs or bulletproof hosting providers. Establish baseline of expected router update/NTP destinations.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation on Network Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: 'Custom Linux implant' implies persistence; article does not detail mechanisms but pipeline missed establishing detection for cron jobs, init.d modifications, or firmware rootkits on routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unauthorized modifications to /etc/cron.d, /etc/init.d, or equivalent persistence paths on routers. Monitor for new user accounts created on router management interfaces. Detect firmware flash operations outside maintenance windows. Alert on modifications to SSH authorized_keys or sudoers files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Edge Router
suggestion.rationale: Southeast Asian edge routers are network chokepoints; article implies router compromise but pipeline generated no detection for downstream lateral movement or internal reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate internal traffic flows originating from compromised router IP for lateral scanning (sequential connection attempts to internal subnets). Flag DNS queries for internal infrastructure from router. Detect SMB/RDP/SSH connection attempts from router to internal hosts outside normal maintenance schedules.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Router Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Edge router compromise typically involves configuration tampering (ACL bypass, route injection, traffic interception); pipeline missed this critical persistence and evasion vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any configuration changes to ACLs, static routes, or traffic mirroring outside approved change windows. Flag modifications to logging settings that reduce visibility. Detect insertion of new user accounts in router config. Compare running config MD5 checksums against baseline to detect unauthorized modifications.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Vulnerability Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin' — requires asset inventory hunt to identify installed plugin versions and patch status. Template reference confirms standard approach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search package managers and file system paths for LiteSpeed cPanel plugin installation. Cross-reference against known vulnerable version ranges to identify unpatched hosts. Alert on plugin version < [patched version per LiteSpeed advisory].

suggestion.title: cPanel User to Root Privilege Escalation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — direct privilege escalation from unprivileged user context. Requires behavioral detection of execution lineage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning with root UID where parent process is cPanel user context or cPanel daemon (cpanel, cpsrvd). Flag script execution (bash, sh, perl, python) spawned with uid=0 from cpanel user session.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution Detection in cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — detection gap for script execution anomalies originating from cPanel plugin code paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script interpreter invocation (bash, sh, perl, python, etc.) spawned from LiteSpeed cPanel plugin directories with root privileges. Monitor for unexpected child processes spawning from cpanel daemon with no corresponding legitimate cPanel operations.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin Directory Modification or Injection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation often involves writing malicious code to plugin paths or leveraging plugin file write permissions. Article indicates plugin is 'exposed,' suggesting possible file-write attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteSpeed and cPanel plugin directories for unauthorized file creation, modification, or permission changes. Flag unexpected writes to plugin configuration or script directories; correlate against legitimate cPanel/LiteSpeed update processes.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection via HTTP Plugin Interface
suggestion.rationale: Plugin 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin' — exploitation likely traverses HTTP interface. Web log analysis for malicious payloads or unexpected plugin parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel plugin interface endpoints for exploitation patterns: unusual parameter values, script injection attempts, path traversal, or base64-encoded payloads in plugin request paths. Correlate HTTP 200 responses with suspicious cPanel user API calls to privilege-escalation parameters.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt - Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests' and Imperva detected '15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites' — direct detection gap for known active exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/POST requests to Drupal installations containing SQL injection signatures in database API calls. Focus on unauthenticated requests targeting database abstraction endpoints with quote injection, UNION-based payloads, or time-delay patterns. Alert on geographic clustering of requests from same ASN/IP range.

suggestion.title: Drupal Patch Status & Vulnerability Assessment Gap
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver identified 'nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online, most of them from North America (272) and Europe (273)' — pipeline should flag inventory gaps on endpoints not running patched Drupal versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate asset inventory (CMDB, Nessus, Qualys) against known Drupal version banners captured in HTTP headers or vulnerability scanners. Flag servers running Drupal versions prior to CVE-2026-9082 patch. Alert when unpatched instances are accessible from internet-facing WAF logs or public scanning engine hits.

suggestion.title: Post-SQL Injection Privilege Escalation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploitation 'can potentially lead to information disclosure, privilege escalation, and even remote code execution' — missing detection for privilege escalation activity following successful SQL injection against Drupal DB.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post SQL injection success, monitor for unusual database user privilege grants, role additions, or CREATE USER commands within PostgreSQL audit logs. Cross-correlate with successful exploitation time windows derived from WAF/web logs. Alert on unexpected system account elevation post-web request.

suggestion.title: Drupal RCE Indicator Post SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states successful exploitation can 'lead to...remote code execution' — missing detection for code execution payloads or shell access immediately following SQL injection exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or PHP/script interpreter invocation on Drupal web server immediately after detected SQL injection attempts. Flag unusual process spawns from web service accounts (apache, www-data, drupal user). Alert on web shell file creation in Drupal directories (/sites/default/files, /modules).

suggestion.title: Sector-Targeted Drupal Exploitation by Geographic Region
suggestion.rationale: Imperva observed 'Attacks are primarily targeting Gaming and Financial Services sites so far, at collectively almost 50% of all attacks' across 65 countries — missing threat-hunting use case for sector/geography correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Drupal-specific HTTP requests by source geography and target sector. Alert on anomalous spike in SQL injection attempts from specific ASNs/regions targeting Gaming or Financial Services Drupal instances. Correlate with Shadowserver/GreyNoise threat intelligence feeds for known vulnerable Drupal scanner activity.

suggestion.title: Drupal Information Disclosure via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Successful exploitation can potentially lead to information disclosure' — missing detection for data exfiltration patterns via SQL injection (database schema enumeration, credential table access).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs for UNION-based injection queries selecting from user, password, or credential-related tables. Alert on large result sets returned via HTTP response (byte count anomaly) following SQL injection patterns. Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS exfiltration of credential hashes or sensitive schemas.

suggestion.title: Path traversal in XWiki ssx/jsx endpoints via resource parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation: 'URLs such as `http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false`'. Pattern is clear and testable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to XWiki ssx or jsx endpoints containing resource parameters with leading slashes and directory traversal sequences (../ or ..\). Look for patterns like `resource=/..` or `resource=/../` in GET/POST parameters.

suggestion.title: XWiki configuration file access via path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article states objective: 'get access and read configuration files' such as 'xwiki.cfg'. This is the post-exploitation activity that should trigger security alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful HTTP responses (200/301/302) from XWiki ssx/jsx endpoints when path traversal patterns are present in resource parameter. Watch for access to sensitive files (xwiki.cfg, web.xml, etc.) via path traversal.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory - XWiki platform instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-23734
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable versions (pre-18.0.0-rc-1, pre-17.10.3, pre-17.4.9, pre-16.10.17). This enables proactive asset inventory hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify XWiki instances via application fingerprinting or asset databases. Cross-reference against patched versions (18.0.0-rc-1+, 17.10.3+, 17.4.9+, 16.10.17+). Flag any instances running earlier versions as exposed.

suggestion.title: XWiki ssx/jsx endpoint discovery via HTTP enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation requires identifying vulnerable endpoints. Article specifies `ssx` and `jsx` endpoints—reconnaissance activity should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP requests to `/bin/ssx/` and `/bin/jsx/` endpoints with varying resource parameters, especially when followed by successful 200 responses. Pattern suggests automated reconnaissance or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure - XWiki CVE-2026-33137 Vulnerable Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article lists vulnerable versions (prior to 16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1) and patched versions explicitly. Pipeline failed to generate 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt from article's recommended hunts section.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan asset inventory for XWiki installations running versions prior to patched releases. Flag instances as vulnerable to unauthenticated XAR import via POST /wikis/{wikiName}.

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection - XWiki Exploit/Payload SHA1
suggestion.rationale: SHA1 4b7b95b79256374d487e9ece1dc48f527966990f explicitly provided in article IOCs section. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and generated zero hash-based hunts despite article recommending 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoints for file and process hash matches against the provided SHA1. Detect exploit/payload delivery, staging, or execution via hash-based file monitoring.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated REST API Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states POST /wikis/{wikiName} 'executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks'. This direct attack vector was not reconstructed in kill-chain or converted to detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /wikis/* endpoints for absent or invalid authentication headers. Alert on requests lacking valid session tokens or authentication credentials that succeed (2xx response) in importing or modifying content.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Wiki Document Creation/Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or update documents in the target wiki'. This persistence/impact indicator was entirely missed by pipeline despite being the tangible outcome of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect document creation or bulk modification events lacking authenticated user context. Alert on REST API-initiated document changes without valid session tokens or from untrusted IP sources, particularly rapid bulk modifications.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Authentication Failure Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions'—direct signal of auth rejection surge. Pipeline omitted obvious detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike in 401/403 HTTP responses from api.github.com targeting Actions endpoints. Correlate workflow failure timestamps with auth error timestamps. Raise alert if >30% of authenticated Actions requests fail within 5-min window.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Validation Failure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'Authentication Issues Denying Access' suggests systematic token/credential rejection. Could indicate compromised validation logic, revocation service failure, or active attack on auth layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Elevated rates of valid credentials being rejected (auth token validation failures). Monitor for sudden drop in successful token refresh operations or systematic rejection of bearer tokens with no corresponding account lockout/suspension.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Execution Halt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies Actions denied, implying CI/CD pipeline halt. Actionable for supply-chain risk and build-integrity detection; phrase 'Denying Access to Actions' directly establishes scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect org-wide or enterprise-scope drop in GitHub Actions workflow completion rate. Alert when >50% of queued Actions runs fail with authentication-class errors in single 10-min window. Scope by repository/org to distinguish target-specific compromise from platform-wide outage.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 affecting Ghost CMS; no detection rule was generated despite this being the vector for the 700-site compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for HTTP requests targeting known CVE-2026-26980 exploit endpoints (authentication bypass, SSRF, or file upload paths). Correlate with Ghost version strings in logs to identify vulnerable instances (< patched version). Look for POST requests to admin/auth endpoints or unusual ghost admin activity from non-admin sources.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies ClickFix as the payload delivered via poisoned websites; no detection logic was provided for identifying deployment or execution of this malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix malware signatures in HTTP responses from known-compromised domains (if IOCs are recovered). Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript payloads serving .js files with suspicious names. Correlate user click events to domains serving ClickFix with subsequent endpoint compromise or credential theft.

suggestion.title: Website Content Injection and Malicious HTML/JS Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'poisoning 700 websites' with malware, implying content modification; no use case for detecting injected scripts or modified site content was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server responses for anomalous script tags, base64-encoded payloads, or suspicious domains in injected iframes. Compare response bodies to baseline content signatures. Flag Ghost CMS instances serving significantly modified page content post-compromise or sudden inclusion of external JS sources.

suggestion.title: Unusual Ghost CMS Admin Activity and Unauthorized User Creation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of CVE-2026-26980 in Ghost would likely lead to admin account creation or privilege escalation; no detection for post-exploitation admin activity was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost application logs for new admin user creation events, especially during unusual hours or from unexpected IP ranges. Detect failed login attempts followed by success from non-standard user agents. Flag API token generation for service accounts immediately after CVE exploitation timeframe.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with MiniFast/MiniJunk Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Iranian Hackers Deploy MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 via Phishing' — initial access vector must be monitored. Pipeline extracted no phishing-related detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails containing MiniFast or MiniJunk v2 payloads (file hashes, signatures) or emails with suspicious macros/scripts from untrusted senders. Correlate with phishing-reporting and MUA logs for attachment execution.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Link Click and Redirect Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'SEO Poisoning' as attack vector but no detection UC for this abuse vector. Pipeline missed infrastructure reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks on SEO-poisoned search results that redirect through suspicious domain chains. Flag high-entropy or typosquat domains mimicking legitimate vendors. Correlate with TLD-age and domain-registration-to-campaign-date metrics.

suggestion.title: MiniFast Malware Process Execution and Behavior
suggestion.rationale: MiniFast is named explicitly as the primary payload but pipeline created no malware execution or C2 communication detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MiniFast process spawning from user-accessible paths (temp dirs, Downloads), followed by suspicious script-interpreter or WMI activity. Monitor for C2 beaconing to known attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: MiniJunk V2 Malware Installation and Registry Persistence

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MiniJunk v2 installer execution and subsequent registry modifications to Run/RunOnce/Winlogon keys. Flag suspicious service creation or scheduled task registration paired with malware file hashes.

suggestion.title: Iranian APT Infrastructure Reconnaissance (Domain/IP Pivots)
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes campaign to 'Iranian Hackers' but no IOC extraction or infrastructure pivoting logic visible. Pipeline should surface attacker-controlled domains and C2 servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify attacker infrastructure through WHOIS/DNS pivots on known Iranian APT registration patterns (resellers, name servers). Alert on user connections to newly-identified campaign domains before public disclosure.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization with Known Hardcoded Machine Key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'obtained the machine key and used it in ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads' via 'identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys across multiple customer deployments' in web.config. Pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for __VIEWSTATE parameters in HTTP requests to ASP.NET applications signed with known hardcoded machine keys from KnowledgeDeliver deployments. Detect crafted ViewState payloads via MAC validation failure or gadget chain signatures in deserialization stacks. Alert on ViewState modification attempts without corresponding valid user session.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Web Shell (.NET In-Memory) Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)' as deployed post-exploitation. No detection use case or IOC produced. Pipeline missed named malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET process (w3wp.exe, aspnet_wp.exe) loading CLR assemblies from suspicious paths or in-memory regions. Monitor for network connections initiated from w3wp.exe to external C2 domains. Correlate with HttpModule registration in IIS logs or suspicious AppDomain.CreateInstance() calls.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Injection via Compromised Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code on the platform convinced users to download a fake installer which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon.' Pipeline generated no detection for client-side payload delivery or Cobalt Strike IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious installer executables downloaded from web server after JavaScript modification. Monitor for Cobalt Strike-typical child processes (rundll32, regsvcs, mshta) spawned from installer parent. Detect Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic (HTTPS with known beaconing patterns) initiated from client machines that accessed the compromised web portal.

suggestion.title: JavaScript File Modification in Web Application Directory Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes post-exploitation: 'threat actor executed commands to escalate control... modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin.' Pipeline missed this file tampering indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to .js files in web application directories (especially in wwwroot or inetpub) by processes running under IIS app pool identity. Alert on new inline script injection containing 'security authentication plugin' keywords or external <script> src= loading from attacker-controlled domains. Correlate with web shell process execution.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded ASP.NET Machine Key Detection in web.config
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: 'KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file... contained hardcoded machineKey values.' No configuration scanning detection generated for this preventative control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan deployed web.config files for hardcoded machineKey elements matching known KnowledgeDeliver defaults or samples shared in public disclosures. Flag any ASP.NET application using non-cryptographically unique machine keys. Prioritize KnowledgeDeliver instances running on versions prior to Feb. 24, 2026.

suggestion.title: Suspicious External Script Loading from Injected JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker 'loaded a malicious script from a domain under the attacker's control' via modified app JavaScript. No network-based or DOM-based detection use case was generated for external script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to domains loading JavaScript from non-whitelisted sources initiated by legitimate web application URLs. Alert on DNS requests to suspicious domains referenced in injected JavaScript. Detect script.src changes or eval() execution with external URLs in web application context.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited'; no use case captured the initial compromise vector. Pipeline should detect attempts to exploit known or zero-day flaws in the LMS application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to KnowledgeDeliver LMS endpoints with suspicious parameter values, unusual encoded payloads, or directory traversal patterns. Correlate with subsequent outbound connections or process spawning to detect post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Malware Beacon Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Godzilla as deployed payload but pipeline extracted no IOCs or C2 detection logic. Godzilla is a webshell variant that establishes command channels; detection should focus on characteristic C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with atypical User-Agent headers, suspicious Content-Type mismatches, or encoded command parameters. Look for persistent POST beacons to web-accessible paths from compromised LMS server or web process spawning child shells.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to surface use cases for Cobalt Strike despite being named in title. Cobalt Strike beacons are high-confidence IOCs with known network signatures, encryption patterns, and process injection behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection into legitimate applications (e.g., rundll32, svchost), suspicious network connections on non-standard ports, HTTPS traffic with mismatched certificates or DNS queries to known Cobalt Strike infrastructure domains. Watch for parent-child process relationships violating expected binary execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Code Execution via LMS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware deployment post-exploitation but pipeline did not map execution techniques. Focus on the transition from vulnerability exploitation to arbitrary code execution on the web server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of shell or scripting processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) as children of the web server application process or LMS-related services. Correlate with suspicious working directories or command-line arguments suggesting script/payload execution.

suggestion.title: Multiple MFA Prompts to Single User
suggestion.rationale: Article title and threat name establish that attackers bombard users with repeated MFA approval requests to achieve fatigue/acceptance. No UC generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user receives >3 MFA prompts from distinct IP addresses or geographic locations within 5 minutes. Filter out legitimate MFA re-sends from help desk. Correlate with successful login immediately after prompt storm.

suggestion.title: Successful Login After Rejected MFA Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Bombed users eventually approve; pipeline missed the success-after-bombardment pattern. Title implies users eventually capitulate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful login immediately following ≥2 failed MFA challenges from the same user within 2 minutes. Flag accounts with approved MFA after >1 rejection in the same session. Correlate with IP reputation data.

suggestion.title: Atypical MFA Approval Geographic Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Prompt-bombing often originates from attacker-controlled sessions; approved MFA from unexpected geography signals compromise. Article context implies location anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when MFA approval IP geolocation differs significantly from recent user baselines or differs from the login attempt IP. Flag impossible-travel scenarios (login attempt IP + MFA approval IP within seconds, >500km apart).

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequential Login Attempts to Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Attackers retry logins quickly with captured credentials while bombing MFA. Article subject matter implies sustained access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 login attempts to the same account from ≥2 distinct source IPs within 10 minutes. Exclude known automation and service accounts. Correlate failures + MFA challenge timing.

suggestion.title: User Report of Unexpected MFA Prompts
suggestion.rationale: Victims recognizing the attack surface in helpdesk tickets, incident reports, or security surveys—pipeline should map user awareness signals. Article implies user frustration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest helpdesk tickets, Slack security reports, and email-to-SOC containing phrases like 'MFA prompt,' 'approval I didn't send,' 'phone wouldn't stop.' Aggregate by user and alert tier-1 for account takeover investigation within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: MFA Provider Abuse Notifications
suggestion.rationale: Okta, Duo, Azure AD, etc. emit abuse alerts when threshold of prompts triggered from same account. Pipeline should surface provider-native signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MFA provider logs and webhooks for 'suspicious activity detected,' 'unusual prompt volume,' or 'fraud alert' events. Ingest directly into SIEM and trigger immediate account review and forced re-auth.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Activity Before Automatic Isolation Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states feature is designed to 'thwart attackers' attempts to move laterally across the network'—implies lateral movement precedes isolation. Detection should catch the activity that triggers isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral movement tool execution (PsExec, WinRM, remote RDP, WMI) and lateral tool transfer prior to DeviceIsolationEvent. Correlate failed login attempts, service creations, and SMB traffic to non-standard administrative shares within a short time window before isolation occurs.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration Attempts Pre-Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'data exfiltration' as a risk the isolation feature prevents—implies successful detection of exfiltration activity triggers isolation. Need detection for exfiltration activity before containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk network data transfer to external/untrusted IP ranges, especially SMB/RDP/WinRM outbound or archive creation followed by transfer. Include cloud-to-external exfiltration patterns (unusual OneDrive/SharePoint downloads by compromised service account).

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware Execution Pre-Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article states feature prevents 'ransomware propagation'—suggests Defender detects encryption/ransom activity before isolation. Need behavioral detection of encryption operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file rename/extension change operations, encryption-tool execution (7z, RAR, OpenSSL for legitimate tools being abused), mass write operations to user directories, and ransom note file creation (e.g., README.txt, DECRYPT.txt patterns).

suggestion.title: Detect Account Compromise Leading to Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'account isolation' feature to 'block lateral movement in hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks'—implies detection of compromised account activity precedes account-level isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed login attempts from unusual locations followed by successful login, unusual process execution under compromised account (especially SYSTEM/LSASS access), and credential dumping tool execution. Correlate with subsequent isolation/account disable events.

suggestion.title: Monitor Endpoint Isolation Event Frequency for Attack Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes automatic isolation as operational response. Cluster of isolation events across multiple endpoints within time window indicates coordinated compromise or exploit campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate DeviceIsolationEvent (or equivalent Defender event) across fleet. Alert on >3 automatic isolations within 1 hour or >5 within 4 hours to the same domain/tenant, suggesting mass compromise or widespread vulnerability exploitation.

suggestion.title: Ransomware File Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article centered on stopping 'ransomware spread'—encryption is definitive attack signature. Missing detection for mass file modification patterns, extension proliferation, registry hive manipulation that precedes isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file creation/modification across multiple directories by single process, unusual extension changes, high-rate WriteFile operations, or registry access patterns (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet) consistent with ransomware initialization and encryption routines.

suggestion.title: Device Network Isolation Event Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'automatically isolates compromised devices.' Pipeline missed detection for isolation trigger events themselves—network segmentation, connectivity drops, Defender quarantine flags correlating with prior suspicious activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MDE device isolation events and correlate with preceding anomalies. Detect sudden drops in outbound connections, network adapter state changes, Windows Defender ATP isolation flags, or firewall rule modifications triggered by threat detection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Attempts Pre-Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stop ransomware spread'—lateral movement precedes isolation. Pipeline missed detection for SMB enumeration, credential harvesting, lateral tool spawning (PsExec, WMI), and admin share access indicative of ransomware lateral propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement precursors before isolation triggers: unusual SMB traffic patterns from infected device, suspicious credential access/enumeration, lateral tool execution (PsExec cmdline patterns), IPC$ or ADMIN$ enumeration, or WMI lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Behavior Triggering Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Defender's automatic isolation is triggered by threat detection logic—pipeline must model detection for process behaviors that activate it. Missing UC for command execution, privilege escalation, or cryptographic operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process anomalies preceding isolation: high file handle creation rates, suspicious parent-child relationships (system.exe spawning cmd.exe), base64-encoded PowerShell/cmd commands, unusual privilege escalation attempts, or crypto library loading and entropy device access patterns.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Windows Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'DLL Side-Loading' as primary attack technique. Pipeline failed to create detection for T1574.001 despite it being the campaign's defining characteristic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect legitimate, signed Windows executables (svchost.exe, rundll32.exe, etc.) in unusual directories or loading unsigned/unexpected DLLs from the same path. Correlate with dropped binary timestamps and code signing mismatches. MuddyWater typically side-loads via spear-phished Office documents that extract the legitimate EXE and malicious DLL to %TEMP%.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater Spear-Phishing with Office Macro or Exploit Attachment
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater's primary delivery mechanism is spear-phishing with weaponized Office documents. Article title indicates campaign targeted 9 countries, consistent with email-based initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office application spawning suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) or unusual file drops to %TEMP% or %APPDATA%. Detect execution of documents with embedded macros or exploits followed by binary file extraction in the same directory.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Spear-Phishing or OSINT Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Espionage-focused APT campaigns require credential access. MuddyWater characteristically performs OSINT before phishing. No detection use case generated despite campaign targeting multiple countries implying credential theft phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on credential prompt dialogs spawned from Office applications or suspicious processes. Monitor for multiple failed login attempts post-spear-phishing email receipt. Correlate with user-reported phishing emails and suspicious attachments in logs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SMB and Windows Admin Shares
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 9 countries' networks (implies enterprise infrastructure). No lateral movement detections generated. MuddyWater typically moves laterally post-compromise via C$ and ADMIN$ shares.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows admin share access (\\hostname\C$, \\hostname\ADMIN$) from non-administrative user accounts or hosts. Monitor for copy operations (copy, xcopy, robocopy) moving executables or DLLs across systems in the same network segment.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater C2 Communication Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns require command-and-control. No C2 detection patterns created. MuddyWater uses custom HTTP/HTTPS C2 with specific header and URI patterns (varies by campaign).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate beaconing to known or suspected MuddyWater C2 infrastructure. Monitor for HTTP requests with MuddyWater-characteristic User-Agent strings and encoded payload exfiltration. Alert on DNS queries to known C2 domains or anomalous domain registration patterns matching MuddyWater's naming conventions.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task or Registry Run-Key Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Persistence mechanism not surfaced. MuddyWater uses scheduled tasks (schtasks.exe) and registry Run keys for maintaining access in espionage operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect schtasks.exe or New-ScheduledTask PowerShell calls creating tasks with suspicious triggers or payloads pointing to %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or network shares. Monitor registry modifications to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or user-level Run keys with non-standard binary paths or filenames.

suggestion.title: Angular Language Service Extension Loaded from Unexpected Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Angular Language Service Extension' as attack surface; pipeline should detect unauthorized or suspicious extension installations and loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Angular Language Service extension files (.crx, .vsix) instantiated from non-standard paths (%APPDATA%\Code\extensions, user temp directories) or loaded by code.exe with unsigned/mismatched manifest signatures.

suggestion.title: Command Shell Execution from Extension Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly claims 'RCE Attacks'; should detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned from extension runtimes or with module dependencies to extension directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe child processes with parent code.exe or extension node.js runtime; focus on obfuscated arguments, encoded payloads, or LOLBin chains (certutil, mshta, regsvcs).

suggestion.title: Extension Registry or Manifest Persistence Configuration
suggestion.rationale: RCE post-exploitation requires persistence mechanism; should detect registry writes or extension config modifications enabling auto-load or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSCode or .vscode-settings.json / extensions.json for suspicious trusted-extensions lists, disabled sandbox flags, or extension auto-start settings.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Extension Installation or Download
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'vulnerabilities enable RCE' implies attacker must first deliver malicious extension; should detect installation from command-line or non-marketplace sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 'code --install-extension' invocations with non-official marketplace URLs; monitor for curl/wget downloads of .vsix files from external or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Modified Extension Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise or local modification; unsigned packages are deviation from secure extension model and precursor to RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .vsix/.crx extraction or execution with missing or invalid digital signatures; detect obfuscated JavaScript/TypeScript in extension manifests or version downgrades to vulnerable releases.

suggestion.title: RDP Session Establishment from New/Modified Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'RDP Access...for Stealthy Persistence.' RDP combined with account manipulation is classic persistence vector; pipeline entirely missed this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account creation/modification events (4720, 4738) with RDP authentication success (4624) within 24 hours. Alert on RDP sessions from accounts added to Remote Desktop Users group. Flag RDP logons outside normal business hours from rare source IPs to newly created accounts.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Execution Following RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: Title cites 'Remote Admin Tools' as persistence mechanism; no detection coverage for tool execution or C2 delivery via these tools post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of PsExec, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ConnectWise, or RMM agents spawned by cmd.exe/PowerShell within 2 hours of RDP session establishment. Monitor for process command lines containing remote execution flags (-d, -s, -i). Alert on unsigned binaries in System32 or AppData matching remote admin tool signatures.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence Post-RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: 'Stealthy persistence' descriptor implies living-off-the-land techniques. Scheduled tasks are standard post-RDP persistence mechanism not addressed despite clear persistence focus.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TaskScheduler creation events (4698, 4699) within 6 hours of RDP session spike. Detect tasks executing under SYSTEM context with hidden attributes or binary paths in temp directories. Correlate task creation with network egress to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Service Installation for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Remote admin tools and ransomware persistence rely on service-level execution (T1543.003). Article's emphasis on 'stealthy' suggests service-based C2; pipeline ignored this execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service creation (4697) with binary paths pointing to temp, Downloads, or AppData locations. Monitor for service modifications immediately after RDP session. Detect services executing unsigned binaries or spawning unusual child processes (cmd, PowerShell).

suggestion.title: RDP Brute Force Targeting Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: RDP stated as initial access vector. Credential access via brute force is prerequisite for RDP persistence but entirely absent from kill-chain reconstruction.
