suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 15+ failed RDP logons (4625) against single target within 1 hour. Alert on successful logon (4624) to service account or admin account from rare external IP after failed attempt spike. Correlate with account lockouts (4740) and credential exposure in threat feeds.

suggestion.title: WMI Command Execution for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Remote admin tools frequently invoke WMI for process execution and persistence. Pipeline failed to identify WMI-based command execution despite T1047 applicability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wmiprvse.exe spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell with suspicious command lines. Monitor for WMI process creation (ProcessCreate events) with encoded or obfuscated arguments. Alert on wmic.exe execution from non-admin parent processes or during night hours.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Module Loading Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'eBPF Rootkit'; pipeline generated zero detections. eBPF rootkits persist at kernel level and must be surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eBPF program loading via bpf() syscalls (BPF_PROG_LOAD, BPF_PROG_RUN), suspicious eBPF tooling (bpftool, llvm toolchain), or kernel probe attachment (kprobes/tracepoints). Baseline legitimate eBPF use (Falco, BCC, tcpdump eBPF), alert on anomalous sources or obfuscated programs.

suggestion.title: Fileless Malware Execution via Memory Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Fileless Execution'; pipeline missed entirely. Fileless payloads reside only in process memory, leaving no on-disk artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned without corresponding on-disk image file. Detect ptrace/mmap for code injection (PTRACE_POKETEXT), /proc/<pid>/maps showing executable non-file-backed memory, and process forking from interpreters (bash, python, perl) with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Developer-Targeted Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Targets Developers'; pipeline missed initial_access phase. Developer targeting implies social engineering or supply-chain vectors (phishing, fake tools, package compromise).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for dev-specific malware delivery: suspicious git clones/commits, npm/pip installs from untrusted repos, fake IDE plugins, GitHub Actions abuse, and phishing targeting development teams or open-source maintainers.

suggestion.title: RAT Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Quasar is a RAT family; RATs require C2 channels. Pipeline generated no C2 communication detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from anomalous processes to rare/newly-registered domains or bulletproof hosters on non-standard ports. Alert on encrypted tunnel setup (SSL/TLS) from non-network tools, DNS-over-HTTPS anomalies, and periodic beaconing patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Fileless RAT likely executes from legitimate process context (shell, interpreter, debugger); pipeline missed execution anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate children of development tools (bash, python, node, ruby, gdb). Alert on unusual children: shells spawning network utilities (curl, nc), interpreters creating sockets, interpreters forking privileged processes, suspicious environment variable injection.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Level Process/File Hiding Indicators
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkit enables hiding at kernel level; article describes kernel persistence. Pipeline did not suggest behavioral detection of hiding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inconsistency between kernel audit logs and process enumeration: operations logged but processes absent in 'ps/pgrep', open ports visible in auditd but missing from 'netstat/ss', file operations on inodes unreachable via 'stat/lstat'. Correlate auditd with osquery process/socket enumeration.

suggestion.title: DDoS Traffic Spike with Anomalous Protocol Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'smarter' AI DDoS attacks; conventional DDoS detection should monitor for volumetric and protocol-based anomalies. Article does not provide specific IoCs but DDoS narrative demands impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound traffic spike >5 SD above baseline with unusual protocol ratio (e.g., disproportionate UDP, ICMP, or SYN-flood packets). Cross-correlate with regional/sectoral threat intel to confirm DDoS intent vs. legitimate spike.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DDoS-as-a-Service or Botnet C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: AI-driven DDoS implies coordinated botnet or managed attack infrastructure. Article likely discusses attack automation or tooling, but pipeline extracted no C2 domains or malware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for beaconing patterns, DNS queries to known DDoS-for-hire or botnet C2 domains, and anomalous outbound connections matching DDoS attack timings. Correlate with attack onset time.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance for DDoS Target Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: AI-optimized attacks would benefit from prior scanning/enumeration of target infrastructure. Title references 'smarter' attacks suggesting reconnaissance phase, but pipeline captured no discovery techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scans, HTTP OPTIONS requests, or ICMP sweeps originating from unusual or distributed sources in the 24-48 hours preceding DDoS event onset. Look for fingerprinting of mitigation appliances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH/Git Credential Access from Developer Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article topic: developer machines as primary supply-chain targets. Implicit focus on credential compromise to access repos/CI systems. No detection generated for .ssh key extraction or credential store access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads/copies of ~/.ssh, ~/.netrc, ~/.aws/credentials, or Keychain/credential-store binaries from non-developer processes. Alert on batch exports of authentication material or suspicious parent-child process chains reading credential files.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Typosquatted Dependency Installation via Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: dev machines targeted for supply-chain poisoning. Realistic attack vector is malicious npm/pip/maven packages. Pipeline missed detection for suspicious package manager commands or dependency graph anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/pip/gradle install commands pulling from non-standard registries, packages with similar names to known libraries, or installations without matching lock-file entries. Flag unsigned packages or those with revoked digital signatures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Commit or Code Push Activity
suggestion.rationale: Developer machine compromise directly enables repository poisoning. Article context implies code repository access as attack objective. No UC for detecting unauthorized git push/commit from dev environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git commands (push, commit) from developer machines using compromised SSH keys or with commits authored by unrecognized identities. Alert on unexpected repository branches being created or code reaching main/production branches outside normal workflow.

suggestion.title: Build Script or Gradle/Maven Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Build environments on dev machines are direct supply-chain injection vectors. Article addresses dev machines as entry points; no detection for build.gradle, pom.xml, or package.json script modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized writes to build configuration files or build-hook directories. Flag execution of unusual binaries or network calls during build phases. Monitor for build artifacts signed by unexpected identities or compiled outside standard CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: IDE extensions running on dev machines with full project access are high-leverage persistence mechanism. Article topic: dev machines; no detection for plugin installation or IDE process spawning unusual child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor installation of unsigned or third-party IDE extensions. Alert on IDE processes spawning shells, network tools, or git commands with unexpected parameters. Detect extensions modifying git hooks or SSH configurations.

suggestion.title: Git Hook Injection for Build Poisoning or Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev machines enable git hook modification to execute malware on every commit/push. Article implies repository-level compromise from dev machines; no UC for detecting pre-commit/post-commit hook tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized creation or modification of .git/hooks files. Alert on git hooks that execute binaries, network commands, or modify build artifacts. Monitor for hooks executed with unexpected privileges or spawning child processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Domain Controllers with Hostname Length ≥15 Characters
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '15-Character Hostname' as failure condition. Configuration auditing for hostname compliance is a foundational detection for this issue class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all domain controllers and flag any where hostname length is ≥15 characters. Correlate with unexpected restarts, LDAP failures, or replication errors. Baseline current hostnames and alert on changes approaching the threshold.

suggestion.title: Monitor Domain Controller Restarts Following Hostname Changes
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in article: remediation of 15+ character hostnames may require restart. Detection should correlate AD changes with system restart events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on System event 1074 or unexpected shutdown (6006) on Windows Server 2016 DCs where a hostname change was logged in the previous 24 hours. Flag cascading failures if replication partners report sync failures post-restart.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Replication Health Baseline for Windows Server 2016
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim is DC failure; replication and LDAP availability are primary failure indicators. Detection should establish and monitor baseline service health.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline LDAP response latency and replication sync time for Windows Server 2016 DCs. Alert if replication partners report failures or LDAP queries exceed SLA. Cross-reference with known 15+ character hostnames to triage.

suggestion.title: Device Code Authentication from Anomalous Source IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'trick targets into entering' device codes on Microsoft's portal and 'once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token.' Core credential access vector with no detection mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag device code authentication requests originating from IPs with no historical login pattern, rapid sequential device code flows from same source, or device code completion immediately following phishing campaign send times. Alert on device code MFA completion where user context is unavailable (headless/non-interactive).

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation Post-OAuth Token Grant
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Explicit post-compromise defense evasion tactic requiring detection after suspicious OAuth events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation within 24 hours of suspicious device code authentication or anomalous OAuth token usage. Correlate with rules that move messages to archive, delete categories, or forward externally. Monitor for rules set by account owner but originating from new device/geolocation.

suggestion.title: Device Registration in Entra Following OAuth Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Persistence via infrastructure modification post-initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new device registrations to Intune or Entra within 12-48 hours of suspicious OAuth token creation. Prioritize registrations from new geographic regions, atypical device types, or unusual OS/browser combinations inconsistent with user baseline.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Usage via AitM Proxy Infrastructure (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cookie Link' mode that 'proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens.' Tokens exfiltrated via AitM require detection on usage anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens used from IP geolocations inconsistent with user profile. Flag simultaneous token usage from geographically distant IPs within 5-minute windows. Monitor for tokens granted via device code that are then used with non-standard user agents or from known proxy/datacenter ASNs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Mailbox Data Access and Exfiltration Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieved 'full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account' and 'to their mailboxes, where they created malicious inbox rules.' Post-OAuth account takeover collection behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-scale mailbox searches, message export operations, or folder-level access following device code authentication. Flag patterns: rapid folder traversal, accessing mail from years past, accessing shared mailboxes not in user's normal scope, or attachment downloads to new external IP.

suggestion.title: PhaaS Platform Intelligence: Kali365, EvilTokens, Tycoon2FA Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Kali365 distributed 'via Telegram channels for cybercriminals' and references related services (EvilTokens, Tycoon2FA). Threat intel gap: no tracking of PhaaS platform artifacts, reseller networks, or common lure templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish IOCs for Telegram channels/groups advertising Kali365, EvilTokens, and Tycoon2FA. Track phishing lure samples, login proxy endpoints, and reseller onboarding pages associated with these services. Cross-correlate email subjects/sender domains in device-code phishing campaigns to identify shared templates or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 and states 700+ sites were exploited. No UC exists to detect exploitation of this public vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for HTTP POST/PUT requests to admin API endpoints combined with known CVE-2026-26980 payload patterns. Correlate with unusual account creation or permission elevation in Ghost admin logs within minutes of the request.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Injection via CMS Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks were used to 'hijack 700+ sites for ClickFix attacks,' indicating content injection of ClickFix payloads. No UC detects this post-exploitation content manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Ghost CMS posts or pages modified outside normal admin hours with injected JavaScript matching known ClickFix patterns (fake system alerts, call-to-action overlays, obfuscated payloads). Cross-reference with time of CVE-2026-26980 exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation on Ghost Instances
suggestion.rationale: Ghost CMS hijacking for persistent ClickFix campaigns implies attackers created admin accounts for long-term access. No UC detects unauthorized admin provisioning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin_users table for new high-privilege accounts created outside normal business windows or from IPs inconsistent with site owner. Flag if creation follows CVE-2026-26980 exploitation within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references CVE-2026-26980 exploitation. Organizations need inventory-based detection of affected Ghost CMS versions to prioritize patching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all internet-exposed Ghost CMS instances for versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-26980 (exact range not provided in article but should be extracted). Alert on unpatched instances within 7 days of exploit disclosure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Between Ghost Instances via Shared Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: 700+ compromised Ghost sites suggests possible attacker movement across multiple instances using shared credentials, databases, or plugin repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ghost CMS admin logins across multiple domains from identical IP/user-agent within 1-hour window. Flag bulk plugin installations to multiple Ghost instances from attacker-controlled package sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from Ghost Admin Panels
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 700+ sites for ClickFix campaigns implies attackers accessed site data, credentials, or analytics. No UC detects exfiltration patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk exports of Ghost CMS posts, subscribers, or settings data via admin API. Flag unusual data downloads followed by new external C2 connections or plugin installations that beacon out of band.

suggestion.title: DPAPI-based Loader Decryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DPAPILoader decrypts and loads RemotePELoader from disk using the Windows Data Protection API (DPAPI)' — direct indicator of the first-stage loader execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes invoking CAPI/CryptUnprotectData or DPAPI decrypt operations followed by rundll32/regsvcs/regasm loading. Look for parent process launching legitimate-looking processes that subsequently decrypt and execute second-stage payloads.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Remote Loader Beacon Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RemotePELoader beacons to a C2 server and waits until it receives the next stage: RemotePE' — the C2 communication pattern is the pivotal second-stage execution point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for beaconing patterns from previously-staged processes (svchost, rundll32, regsvcs). Flag outbound connections with cryptographic/encoded payloads, irregular intervals, or use of legitimate services (HTTPS, DNS) as covert channels.

suggestion.title: Telegram-based Social Engineering Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attack chain leverages social engineering, particularly via Telegram and fraudulent scheduling platforms, to compromise employees' — direct initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for employees accessing Telegram Web clients, desktop clients, or fraudulent scheduling platforms (spoofed Calendly, Outlook, Google Calendar clones). Correlate with subsequent downloads of documents, executables, or staged files.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only Malware Execution without Disk Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'RemotePE, a RAT executed entirely in memory and never written to disk, leaving no filesystem artifacts' — the core evasion technique distinguishing this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process hollowing, process injection, or reflective DLL loading via parent-child process relationships and memory attributes. Flag legitimate processes (svchost, winlogon) spawning child processes with unusual memory I/O patterns or allocated virtual memory not tied to loaded DLLs.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion via Environmental Keying
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware toolset includes 'environmental keying' — technique to evade sandboxes and EDR analysis by checking system properties before executing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes querying system metadata (registry keys, WMI classes, system time, hardware IDs, domain membership, process listings) immediately after launch but before operational execution. Correlate with known anti-analysis patterns.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange / DeFi Platform Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies targets as 'trading and DeFi organizations' with $577M stolen; prior campaigns (DeFi sector Sept 2025) indicate sector-specific targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag reconnaissance traffic toward DeFi platforms, crypto exchanges, and wallet infrastructure. Monitor for employee credential harvesting from DeFi/exchange authentication systems. Correlate legitimate access logs with unusual wallet API queries or fund movement events.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—multiple package repositories compromised. Pipeline failed to generate detection for suspicious or anomalous package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of packages from npm, PyPI, or CratesIO repositories with known malicious checksums, or packages published by newly-created or compromised accounts. Monitor package manager processes (npm, pip, cargo) spawning unusual child processes immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Credential-Stealing Malware'—core payload is credential exfiltration. Pipeline missed detection for in-memory credential scraping, API key/token access, or environment variable enumeration during package initialization scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager or package-launched processes invoking credential storage APIs (.aws/credentials, .ssh, keychain, environment variables), or processes reading common credential file paths and exfiltrating data over network connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Build/Package-Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Malware must exfiltrate stolen credentials. Article implies C2 communication but pipeline extracted no detection for data exfiltration. Build environments installing malicious packages should be monitored for unexpected outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS connections initiated by npm, pip, or cargo processes to non-standard domains (not package repositories, not official CDNs). Correlate with credential-access signals (API keys in memory, .aws access).

suggestion.title: Package Installation with Altered or Missing Checksum Verification
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often exploit weak package integrity checks. Article mentions three repositories—pipeline should flag installations without checksum verification or with checksum mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package downloads where integrity verification is bypassed (--no-verify flags, missing lockfile enforcement) or where installed package checksums do not match published hashes in repository metadata.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Execution Context During Package Build/Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Malware payload runs during install-time hooks (preinstall, postinstall, setup.py). Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation or elevated execution during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager processes spawning children with elevated privileges, accessing sensitive directories, or invoking shell interpreters with encoded/obfuscated arguments during package installation phases.

suggestion.title: Mass Package Publication by Newly-Registered or Compromised Maintainer Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'spreads via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—suggests attacker controls or spoofs maintainer identities. Pipeline should detect rapid package uploads from unusual accounts or account takeovers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repository API activity (npm publish, PyPI upload, cargo publish) from newly-created accounts, accounts with no prior publish history, or geographic/IP anomalies inconsistent with maintainer baseline. Correlate with package names similar to legitimate libraries.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Record Export Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stolen over 600,000 records' from Salesforce. No detection logic exists for volumetric data exfiltration via API bulk operations or report exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single Salesforce export jobs that process >50K records where user has no prior bulk export activity. Correlate exports with failed MFA attempts in prior 24h or logins from new geographies. Baseline normal export patterns per org and flag 10x+ deviation.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Initial Access via Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthorized third party gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems' used for storing franchisee documents, indicating credential theft or exploitation without technical vectors specified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Salesforce logins followed immediately by anomalous API activity (bulk query, content export) without intervening UI navigation. Flag logins after 3+ failed MFA attempts in prior hour, or successful logins from impossible-travel distances.

suggestion.title: Data Breach Ransom Timeline Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents ShinyHunters' explicit extortion timeline: April 17 breach claim, May 1 notification, May 26 public leak. No detection UC correlates data exfil events to threat actor ransom communications or dark web leak site postings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large Salesforce exports with ransom note appearances on ShinyHunters leak site or dark web dumps. Alert when corporate data appears on known extortion actor sites within 72 hours of detected exfil anomalies. Cross-reference customer domains against threat actor leak manifests.

suggestion.title: Franchisee Document Store Unauthorized Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies breach limited to 'systems used to store franchisee documents.' No detection for sequential document access or repository traversal anomalies targeting sensitive stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce Libraries, Content stores, and file shares for bulk sequential folder listing or >50 document downloads in <10 min by single user. Alert on access to franchisee document collections by service accounts or APIs with unexpected user-agents.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Salesforce Customer Targeting Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ShinyHunters 'targeting Salesforce customers for the past year' and lists 20+ victims (Cisco, Google, Match Group, McGraw-Hill, ADT, Rockstar, Vimeo, Zara). Pipeline did not surface actor attribution or campaign correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain ShinyHunters target list correlation. Alert Salesforce customers on any detected large data export when ShinyHunters campaign activity is observed (leak site updates, public claims, victim announcements). Cross-check new data breach notifications against ShinyHunters' public victim claims within 30-day windows.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts on Unpatched Internet-Facing Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames 'Internet-Facing Flaws' and urgency of patching—implies active in-the-wild exploitation. Title directly references the threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Internet-facing web services (IIS, Apache, nginx) for exploitation signatures: unusual HTTP verbs or content-types to application endpoints, encoded payloads in headers/parameters, SQLi syntax, remote code execution artifacts (shell spawning, process creation from web service context), and abnormal response sizes indicating successful compromise.

suggestion.title: AI-Driven Automated Vulnerability Scanning and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls out 'AI-Assisted Attacks'—indicates high-velocity, automated scanning. AI tools typically enumerate and assess targets at machine speed across ranges, not manual reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid, sequential probes to diverse non-existent paths/endpoints from single source IP, concurrent version enumeration requests (banner-grab patterns, User-Agent version sniffing), or requests matching known AI-powered scanner tool signatures (unusual User-Agents, probe sequencing). Establish baseline for legitimate assessment activity; alert on anomalous scale/pattern.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Initial compromise via Internet-facing flaw (T1190) will transition to discovery and lateral movement. Detection must account for pivots from web-service process context to internal network reconnaissance or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application processes (w3wp.exe, httpd, nginx) for spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe, executing discovery commands (whoami, ipconfig, net view, net user), initiating outbound SMB/RDP/WinRM to internal IPs, or loading suspicious modules. Alert on process parent mismatch: unexpected parentage of system tools.

suggestion.title: Patch Application Compliance Monitoring Against Mandated SLA
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 12-hour patching mandate from CERT-In—defenders must verify compliance across fleet. Systems not patched within window remain exploitable and represent detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch compliance 13+ hours post-advisory date (May 27, 2026 + 12h baseline). Identify Internet-facing hosts that have not installed the specified security patch. Correlate with network exposure scans or previous vulnerability scans to confirm continued risk. Alert on Internet-exposed unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Indicators of Breach Following Internet-Facing Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 12-hour urgency window presupposes existing active exploitation in the wild. Defenders need hunt queries to detect post-compromise forensics: file writes, registry modifications, lateral movement artifacts, data staging indicative of compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creation/modification in web root directories (wwwroot, htdocs, webroot) outside normal deployment windows, suspicious registry modifications (Run keys, startup folder persistence), file exfiltration patterns (large data volume to external IPs immediately post-compromise), or process execution outside web service identity context.

suggestion.title: Known Exploit PoC or Framework Traffic Patterns for AI-Assisted Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions AI-assisted attacks. Modern AI exploitation frameworks have identifiable command/control patterns, tool-specific network signatures, and behavioral markers distinct from manual penetration testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of known AI-powered vulnerability assessment tools (Shodan API queries, Censys integration patterns, automated exploit framework traffic) and alert on anomalous usage from internal networks or mass external scanning infrastructure. Monitor for C2 beaconing from compromised internet-facing assets.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Campaign Targeting Cloud SSO Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Vishing is the entry point; no detection UC was generated for this initial access method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSO account logins from unexpected geolocations or device enrollments following voice communication indicators. Flag accounts with rapid failed-then-successful login patterns consistent with credential guessing post-vishing.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Customer Record Export by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'used this access to export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance.' This core attack step—bulk data extraction—has no corresponding detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume Salesforce API calls (Reports.query, queryMore, describe calls) from accounts without baseline export history. Correlate with login anomalies within same session.

suggestion.title: BPO/Third-Party Provider SSO Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters' documented campaign: 'targeting employees and BPO agents' Microsoft Entra, Okta, and Google SSO accounts.' BPO compromise is a stated attack pattern but no BPO-specific detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSO logins originating from known BPO/third-party provider IP ranges or user agents accessing sensitive customer data repositories outside their historical scope.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Reuse for Salesforce API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors stealing... OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances.' Token-based lateral movement bypasses MFA on credential re-entry; no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth tokens used from multiple geographic locations within short timeframes, or tokens generating API calls inconsistent with user's baseline (e.g., bulk exports from background service accounts).

suggestion.title: Cross-SaaS Data Exfiltration by Single Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters' pattern: 'steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox.' Simultaneous multi-SaaS access is distinctive and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate data export/download events across 3+ SaaS platforms by the same user within 24-hour window, especially when account exhibits prior credential compromise signals (unusual location, time-of-day shift, new device).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on Edge Router Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'custom Linux implant' targeting edge routers. Pipeline missed all execution-phase detections. Implant must spawn processes to function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning on network edge devices (routers, firewalls). Custom implants execute shell commands or binary payloads; detect in-memory execution, unsigned binaries in system paths, or processes with suspicious parent-child relationships on low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Edge Router Public-Facing Application Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title references targeting 'edge routers'—indicates T1190 exploitation of admin interface, web service, or known CVE. Pipeline failed to surface initial access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor edge device admin interfaces for exploitation payloads: SQLi patterns, RCE encoding markers (base64, double-encoding), command separators. Alert on HTTP requests that precede unexpected process execution or file creation on the same device.

suggestion.title: Linux Implant Persistence via Systemd or Cron
suggestion.rationale: Custom implant requires persistence mechanism. No T1543/T1547 detections suggested. Article phrase 'custom Linux implant' implies intentional long-term presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/systemd/system, /etc/cron.d, and /lib/systemd/system-sleep for new or modified entries. Alert on services/cron jobs with suspicious binaries, obfuscated commands, or pointing to world-writable directories. Cross-reference against inventory of expected router management processes.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Compromised Router
suggestion.rationale: Implant implies command and control. Custom malware typically beacons to attacker infrastructure. Article context (APT activity) confirms C2 phase. Pipeline suggested zero C2 detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish egress baselines for edge routers (should be highly restricted). Alert on connections to rare ASNs, dynamic DNS providers, or geolocations inconsistent with business operations. Monitor for DNS tunneling patterns, repeatedly failed connections to multiple IPs, or connection attempts on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Edge Router to Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: Compromised edge router is a beachhead for internal network access. Article targets 'Southeast Asian' organizations—implies multi-stage attack. Zero lateral-movement detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal connections originating from edge device IPs to internal subnets or sensitive hosts. Detect SSH connection attempts to multiple internal IPs, SMB/RDP enumeration, or file transfers from edge device to internal endpoints using tools like `scp` or `curl`.

suggestion.title: Malware Discovery via File Hash and Yara Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific malware artifact ('custom Linux implant'). Pipeline should generate detection rules based on behavioral IOCs even if full sample not yet available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Linux process logs with file creation events to identify implant delivery and execution. Alert on file creation in /tmp, /dev/shm, or startup directories immediately following web traffic anomalies. Monitor for curl/wget commands downloading binaries followed by chmod +x and execution.

suggestion.title: Detect cPanel User Privilege Escalation to Root via LiteSpeed Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — direct privilege escalation path from unprivileged user to root requiring detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cPanel user-context processes executing commands with uid=0 or effective_uid=0. Alert on script execution originating from cPanel plugin code paths where caller_uid != 0 but target_uid == 0. High-fidelity signal: non-root cPanel user spawning shell with root EUID.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary Script Execution from cPanel Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — execution phase requires detection for script launch with elevated context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or interpreter invocations with arguments passed from LiteSpeed cPanel plugin source (e.g., stack traces, process parent-child relationships). Alert on bash -c or similar interpreter invocation where parent process name or binary path contains 'litespeed' or 'cpanel'.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation of cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin (CVE-2026-48172)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin' with T1190 mapping — initial exploit attempt against exposed plugin requires network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to cPanel plugin endpoints for LiteSpeed module exploitation patterns. Alert on POST requests to plugin URLs from non-admin cPanel user contexts (user_role != admin). Baseline expected plugin access patterns and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Inventory and Alert on Vulnerable LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Version
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates rapid remediation by 2026-05-29 — asset discovery and version matching is prerequisite for patch due-date enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all cPanel instances for installed LiteSpeed plugin and extract version. Match against vulnerability database for CVE-2026-48172. Generate inventory report with patch status (patched/unpatched) and alert on any unpatched instance past due date 2026-05-29.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection - Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'SQL injection vulnerability in the Drupal content management system...exploited without authentication, allowing attackers to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests.' Imperva documented 15,000+ attack attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal database abstraction API endpoints for SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, DROP, ALTER, EXEC) in parameters. Correlate with PostgreSQL slow-query logs for injected syntax. Alert on requests without User authentication header reaching data API paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Drupal Exploitation Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'can be exploited without authentication'—distinguishes from credential-based attacks. Over 6,000 targeted sites suggests scanning+exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate unauthenticated requests to Drupal public paths. Flag spike in 401/403 sequences immediately followed by database API calls from external subnets. Alert on requests with SQL syntax in POST body to /user/login or /install paths (common Drupal endpoints).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Privilege Escalation Post-SQL-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'successful exploitation can potentially lead to...privilege escalation, and even remote code execution.' SQL injection on database abstraction API enables direct privilege escalation in PostgreSQL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL GRANT/ALTER ROLE/CREATE ROLE commands issued in same session as atypical SELECT queries. Flag elevation of database user privileges within 60 seconds of web server error logs (500 errors during exploitation attempts). Alert on postgres system table modifications.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SQL Injection - Gaming & Financial Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attacks are primarily targeting Gaming and Financial Services sites so far, at collectively almost 50% of all attacks.' Information disclosure is explicit exploitation outcome. Shadowserver tracked 670 unpatched instances indicating data at risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for data volume egress from PostgreSQL server. Alert on unusual outbound data to external IPs within 2 hours of SQL injection attempts. Monitor for DNS tunneling (DNSEXFIL patterns), HTTPS POST to suspicious domains, or raw TCP to non-standard ports from database host.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Post-RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can potentially lead to...remote code execution.' SQL injection to RCE to persistence is standard kill chain—web shell deployment is typical next step on Drupal servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new .php, .phtml, .jsp, .aspx files written to web-accessible directories (/sites/default/files, /var/www/html) within exploitation window. Correlate file creation with HTTP 200 responses to unusual paths. Alert on child process execution from web server process spawning bash/cmd.

suggestion.title: Automated Scanning for Unpatched Drupal Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Shadowserver now tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online.' Reconnaissance phase—attackers fingerprinting Drupal versions and scanning for vulnerable targets. 'Over 15,000 attack attempts' implies coordinated scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Drupal fingerprinting paths (/admin, /user/login, /sites/all/modules, /CHANGELOG.txt) from single external IP across 50+ internal targets in <30 minutes. Flag User-Agent strings matching bot scanners. Alert on responses revealing Drupal version in Server headers or page footers to external sources.

suggestion.title: XWiki ssx/jsx path traversal exploitation with resource parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly demonstrates attack: 'URLs such as http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false'. No detection generated for this endpoint/parameter combination despite being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to /bin/ssx or /bin/jsx endpoints with 'resource=' parameter containing leading slash and directory traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, ..%2f). Alert on any successful (HTTP 200) traversal of WEB-INF paths.

suggestion.title: XWiki WEB-INF configuration file exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'get access and read configuration files' and explicitly names WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg as accessible target. No detection for successful access to sensitive configuration directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses for requests to WEB-INF/ paths, particularly xwiki.cfg, web.xml, or other config files. Correlate response size and content-type (should be text/plain if config file); flag JSON/HTML responses as indicator of error pages hiding traversal failure.

suggestion.title: Sequential path traversal fuzzing against XWiki endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation would typically be preceded by reconnaissance; article describes specific payload but adversaries would test multiple traversal sequences. No detection for fuzzing behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of HTTP 404/403 responses followed by 200 on ssx/jsx endpoints from same source IP, indicating path traversal payload iteration. Threshold: 5+ failed attempts within 5 minutes preceding successful request.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to XWiki /wikis Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks.' Pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite severity assessment claiming 2 fired.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated POST requests to /wikis/{wikiName} patterns on internet-facing XWiki instances. Alert on successful responses (200/201/204) lacking valid auth tokens, session cookies, or auth headers. Flag bulk or repetitive requests suggesting automated XAR payload delivery.

suggestion.title: XAR Archive Ingestion via REST
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes XAR import as the attack vector—'XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks'—but pipeline generated zero detection for archive import operations or multipart uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with XAR-related MIME types or multipart form data containing .xar file uploads to /wikis endpoints. Monitor XWiki application logs for document import events initiated via REST without prior admin session context.

suggestion.title: Document Lifecycle Events Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or update documents in the target wiki' unauthenticated. No detection use case exists for unauthorized document manipulation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on XWiki PageSavedEvent or DocumentUpdatedEvent entries where audit logs show no matching authentication event or where the API caller IP has no prior admin login history. Flag bulk document creation in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable XWiki Version Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides patched versions (16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1). Pipeline claimed 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' in recommended hunts but generated zero use case output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory for XWiki Platform instances with unpatched versions: any <16.10.17, 17.4.x <17.4.9, 17.10.x <17.10.3, 18.0.x <18.0.1. Prioritize internet-accessible hosts or those in untrusted network zones.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Authentication Failure Rate Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions'—this demands detection of abnormal 401/403 response rates, failed token validation, and cascading auth failures across GitHub API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for GitHub API authentication failures (401/403 HTTP responses) per user/IP cohort. Alert on 5–10× elevation over 15–60 minute windows. Correlate with GitHub status page and API degradation announcements to discriminate legitimate outages from attack-driven denials.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) Usage Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Authentication crises often mask or enable token theft. Detection must identify tokens used from novel geographies, IPs, or times inconsistent with user baseline behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for PAT/OAuth token activity. Flag tokens suddenly used from new country/city, midnight hours, or via CI/CD systems not previously associated with the token. Correlate with account risk signals.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Execution Failure Cascade During Auth Window
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'Denying Access to Actions' indicates workflow execution was blocked. Detection should identify sudden workflow failure rate elevation, unauthorized job cancellations, or execution queues that timeout during auth failure periods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track GitHub Actions workflow execution logs for spike in failures, timeouts, or cancellations. Correlate timing with authentication API error windows. Flag anomalous actor identity or repository targets triggering failures.

suggestion.title: Distributed Brute Force or Credential Spray Against GitHub Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Authentication outages may be cover for or result of active compromise attempts. Detection should identify repeated failed login/token validation attempts from distributed or single-source IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed GitHub authentication attempts grouped by source IP. Alert on >5 failures per minute per IP (brute force) or >3 unique target accounts per IP per 10 minutes (spray). Exclude known CI/CD systems and internal IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via GitHub OAuth App Permission Grants During Auth Failure
suggestion.rationale: Auth outages or compromises may enable or mask installation of rogue OAuth applications. Detection should flag unusual OAuth app authorization grants, especially with 'repo', 'workflow', or 'admin' scopes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for OAuth application authorization events. Alert on apps requesting elevated scopes (workflow, repo, admin), especially from IP ranges or user agents not associated with developer activity, or during auth failure windows.

suggestion.title: Secret Scanning and Commit Access During GitHub Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: If authentication issues enabled unauthorized repository access, detection must surface attempts to exfiltrate secrets, clone large repositories, or push commits during the incident window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub audit logs for unusual git clone/push/pull activity (large data transfers, unusual repository targets) with authentication failure windows. Flag anonymous or service-account commits. Monitor for secret detection bypass or disable.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Hackers Exploit Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980'; pipeline failed to surface any initial-access detection despite clear vulnerability targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to Ghost CMS admin endpoints with payloads matching known CVE-2026-26980 exploit patterns. Look for unusual HTTP response codes (20x followed by 4xx/5xx) or request timing anomalies in unauthenticated admin panel requests.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware JavaScript Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Poison 700 Websites With ClickFix Malware'; ClickFix is a known JavaScript-based malware distributor, yet no detection rule for JavaScript injection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual <script> tag injections in website responses, particularly obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads. Monitor for modifications to static web resources (HTML templates, footer injections) that reference external JavaScript sources not in site configuration.

suggestion.title: Website Content Integrity Anomaly - Malware Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '700 Websites' being 'poisoned'; this is persistent malware injection requiring website content modification, yet no file-integrity or content-drift detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to website root, .htaccess, or CMS theme/plugin files. Cross-reference file modification timestamps against CMS update logs; unauthorized changes post-exploit indicate injection. Monitor for unexpected external requests originating from web server processes.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Compromised CMS - Visitor Download Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'Poisons 700 Websites'; implied impact is malware delivery to visitors, yet no detection for the downstream victim infection vector was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web visits to known-compromised domains (700 Ghost CMS sites) with unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe) or file downloads in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%. Alert on users visiting Ghost CMS sites followed by unknown executable downloads within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Panel Unauthorized Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article references exploitation of CVE-2026-26980; successful exploits typically require post-breach admin manipulation, yet no authentication anomaly detection for CMS admin access was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS authentication logs for rapid login attempts using default credentials, password spray patterns, or successful logins from IP ranges not in baseline. Alert on admin account creation or privilege escalation immediately post-vulnerability exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 Malware Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states Iranian actors use 'phishing' as primary initial access method. No email-based detection logic was surfaced despite this being explicitly named attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails containing attachments with names/hashes matching known MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 samples, or emails linking to malicious URLs. Look for process execution chains spawned by email attachment detonation (Office macros, PDF exploits) leading to outbound C2 traffic.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Campaign Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'SEO poisoning' as deployment vector. No detection use case for poisoned search engine results, compromised domains, or malicious landing pages was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolutions and HTTP requests to domains or subdomains known to host SEO-poisoned results. Monitor for unusual patterns in web traffic to low-reputation domains coinciding with malware hash execution.

suggestion.title: MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 Process Execution and Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: No behavioral detection for malware execution itself was generated. Article describes active malware families requiring process-level and registry-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation and registry modifications consistent with MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 malware behavior profiles. Cross-reference file hashes against known samples; alert on unsigned executables or DLLs with suspicious parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from MiniFast/MiniJunk V2
suggestion.rationale: No network-based C2 detection was proposed despite malware implying external command infrastructure. Article describes deployed malware families requiring C2 communication monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections from compromised endpoints to known or suspected C2 infrastructure. Correlate process execution of MiniFast/MiniJunk variants with unusual external communication patterns, especially to known Iranian hosting providers or bulletproof hosts.

suggestion.title: Email Header Analysis for Phishing Campaign Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article's phishing vector implies email-based reconnaissance. No use case for header analysis, sender reputation, or SPF/DKIM failures was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze email headers for spoofed or compromised sender domains, SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, and reply-to field mismatches. Flag campaigns with consistent sender patterns matching known Iranian APT infrastructure.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes ViewState deserialization attacks: 'ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution.' This is the core exploitation mechanism and requires detection at HTTP parameter level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ASP.NET applications receiving ViewState parameters with anomalously large payloads or unusual Base64 patterns. Flag requests where ViewState contains deserialization gadgets (ysoserial signatures). Correlate with machine key entropy in web.config files across deployments.

suggestion.title: Godzilla In-Memory Web Shell Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names Godzilla (aka BlueBeam) as the deployed web shell: '.NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla.' Requires detection of in-memory shell behavior and ASP.NET handler anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious ASP.NET child processes (w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe without direct HTTP handler mapping). Monitor for .NET reflection/Assembly.Load calls in ASP.NET worker process. Alert on HTTP requests to unknown .ashx or .asmx endpoints with command-like parameters.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Machine Key Exploitation Across Multi-Tenant Deployments
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys across multiple customer deployments.' Requires detection of shared cryptographic material and its misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory web.config files across ASP.NET deployments; alert if machineKey validation keys are identical across customer instances. Monitor for external attempts to craft ViewState using known hardcoded keys. Flag any machine key exfiltration (e.g., unauthorized access to web.config).

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection into ASP.NET Application Files for Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Attack step: 'modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a "security authentication plugin".' This requires detection of unauthorized JS modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write operations to .js files in web application directories by processes outside expected deployment pipelines. Alert on inline <script> tags added to application JS files post-deployment. Correlate with HTTP GET requests for those JS files followed by unusual user downloads.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Installation via Fake Installer Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Final payload delivery: 'malicious code on the platform convinced users to download a fake installer, which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon.' Requires endpoint detection of Cobalt Strike execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unknown .exe/.msi from user Downloads folder immediately after browser activity. Monitor for Cobalt Strike beacon signatures: suspicious rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe, or regasm.exe execution with network beaconing. Alert on process injection into web browsers or svchost.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Payload Customization Per Targeted Organization
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'payload was encrypted using a key that used the name of the compromised organization, which indicated that the threat actor prepared this payload specifically for the targeted organization.' Suggests targeted, pre-staged campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify staged payloads with organization-specific encryption keys or metadata. Monitor for command-line arguments containing organization names used as cryptographic material. Correlate payload properties (size, entropy, timestamps) with known threat-actor staging infrastructure.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Remote Code Execution Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited'—this is initial-access. No detection generated for web application vulnerability exploitation or post-exploitation indicators on LMS servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver LMS web endpoints for exploitation attempts: unusual HTTP POST payloads to admin interfaces, error pages following suspicious parameter injection, and file uploads to non-standard directories. Correlate failed HTTP requests with subsequent webshell creation.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Creation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deploy Godzilla'—a known webshell/backdoor. Pipeline generated no execution or file-write detections for webshell deployment post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious .php, .aspx, or .jsp files created in web-accessible directories immediately after LMS exploitation attempts. Detect execution of web shells through unusual child processes spawned by web server processes (IIS, Apache, Nginx) and suspicious command-line activity from web server accounts.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Deploy...Cobalt Strike'—a primary C2 framework. Zero C2-related detections despite this being explicitly stated in the threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cobalt Strike beacon callbacks: HTTPS traffic with characteristic TLS fingerprints, DNS A-record lookups followed by HTTPS to non-standard ports, and HTTP(S) requests with DGA-like domain patterns or C2-associated User-Agent strings. Alert on reverse-shell processes spawned by web server processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised LMS via Webshell or C2
suggestion.rationale: Godzilla and Cobalt Strike enable lateral movement and persistence. Article's title implies multi-host compromise but no discovery/movement use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious network connections from compromised LMS server to internal systems (SMB shares, RDP, WinRM). Detect lateral-movement tools deployed via Godzilla shell or Cobalt Strike: psexec variants, admin$ share writes, and pass-the-hash or Kerberos relay attacks.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation (Scheduled Tasks, Registry, Services)
suggestion.rationale: Cobalt Strike and Godzilla attacks typically establish persistence. Article mentions deployment but no persistence-detection use cases are present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks, registry run keys, or Windows services by web-server or SYSTEM processes on LMS hosts. Alert on suspicious service binaries that execute web-based payloads or spawn reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Lateral Movement Between Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames threat: 'isolates compromised devices to stop ransomware spread'—lateral propagation is the core threat model Defender targets, but pipeline generated no detection use case for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution and file operations indicative of malware attempting to propagate to network-accessible systems. Flag suspicious shares access, lateral tool execution (psexec, wmic, PowerShell remoting), and payload staging on remote systems by processes spawned from initially compromised device.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption and Mass Extension Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware impact ('stop ransomware spread')—implying encryption is the payload, but no detection use case for encryption behavior was extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity file writes with extension modification patterns (.enc, .locked, .ransom, etc.), bulk renames across folders, or suspicious cryptographic API calls by non-system processes. Correlation with high file modification rates within short time windows indicates ransomware encryption activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning Ransomware Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article implies execution and propagation chain but no detection for the initial ransomware execution or parent-child process relationships was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual parent-child process relationships indicating ransomware execution, especially processes spawning from user-accessible vectors (Office macros, scripts, email-delivered executables) that subsequently attempt lateral movement or file encryption operations.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly identifies DLL side-loading as the campaign vector; pipeline produced zero UCs. Legitimate utilities (rundll32, msiexec, explorer) loading unsigned/unexpected DLLs from writable directories is the canonical attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on signed executables loading DLLs from %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, user Desktop, or other non-system paths. Baseline expected DLL loads per executable; flag deviations. Correlate DLL path with executable parent process to detect DLL preloading abuse.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Delivery of DLL Side-Loading Pairs
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaign targeting 9 countries; typical MuddyWater delivery involves email-attached archives containing paired executables and malicious DLLs. No initial_access UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email delivery of .zip/.rar archives containing both .exe and .dll in the same container. Flag when archive is extracted to user Downloads/Desktop, then .exe is immediately executed. Cross-reference with known MuddyWater C2 signatures post-execution.

suggestion.title: Account Enumeration via LDAP/Net Commands Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country espionage campaigns require reconnaissance of target networks; article mentions targeting 9 countries but no discovery/enumeration UC exists. Pipe text suggests institutional targeting (e.g., gov/defense sectors).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-DLL side-loading execution, monitor for elevated discovery: net.exe /domain, dsquery.exe for account/group enumeration, Get-ADUser/Get-ADGroup PowerShell calls, or LDAP queries to domain controller. Correlate execution context (child of injected process) with discovery commands.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Process Injection from DLL-Loaded Context
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country espionage campaign inherently requires lateral movement; DLL side-loading enables code execution context for process injection. No lateral_movement UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious parent-child relationships where unsigned/injected processes spawn system utilities (svchost, lsass, explorer spawning cmd/PowerShell). Flag when parent PID is inconsistent with process name. Correlate with prior DLL side-loading indicator on same host.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Compromised Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Espionage implies command & control and data exfiltration; no exfiltration or command_and_control UC present. Article implies persistent access model across 9 countries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-DLL side-loading execution, monitor for repetitive outbound connections (beaconing) to non-standard ports, unknown ASNs, or domains registered recently. Alert on encrypted tunnels originating from process tree containing side-loaded DLL execution. Correlate DNS queries with known MuddyWater C2 registrars.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Clipboard/Memory Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Espionage operations require credential access for lateral movement and data access. DLL side-loading enables user-mode code execution for credential scraping, but no credential_access UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned from DLL side-loading context querying HKEY_CURRENT_USER registry hives (credential storage), accessing lsass.exe memory, or monitoring clipboard. Flag LSASS_ACCESS events from unexpected parents. Correlate with failed/successful logon spikes on same or adjacent hosts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Angular Language Service Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes extension name as attack vector—'Multiple Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities.' Pipeline should have detected extension installation from untrusted sources as initial access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VSCode/IDE extension installation events for Angular Language Service Extension variants from non-official marketplace sources, unsigned extensions, or unusual install paths. Alert on rapid multi-extension installations or install attempts from internal forums/malicious URIs.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from Extension Host Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'RCE Attacks'—vulnerability must spawn arbitrary processes. Missing execution-phase UC despite this being the core attack mechanism described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (PowerShell, cmd, bash, curl, wget) spawned by VSCode extension host with suspicious command lines, %TEMP% binary execution, or obfuscated arguments. Flag unexpected interpreter activity or network tool execution from extension context.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Communication from Extension Process
suggestion.rationale: 'RCE Attacks' implies command & control and exfiltration capability. Zero network-based detection coverage despite extension RCE being a known C2 vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from IDE/VSCode processes to non-standard ports, newly-registered domains, or known-malicious IPs. Flag DNS queries from extension processes with anomalous TTLs or frequency patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access to Developer Credentials and Source Code
suggestion.rationale: RCE on developer machine enables lateral movement to enterprise infrastructure. Title establishes impact scope as 'Enable RCE'—collection of git credentials, SSH keys, and source code is implicit threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unexpected reads of .git, .ssh, .env, cloud credential files, and source repositories from extension processes. Alert on batch enumeration of files in developer directories or exfiltration of SSH/API tokens via process environment inspection.

suggestion.title: Registry/Persistence Modification by Extension Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE persistence establishment via extension manifest/config modification or auto-start registry keys. Pipeline produced zero persistence-phase coverage despite extension-based attacks commonly establishing footholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to VSCode extension config/manifest files, extension data directories, or auto-start registry hives (Run, RunOnce) initiated by extension host. Flag suspicious scheduled tasks created from extension context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Extension Token Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: If extension runs with elevated IDE privileges, detect pivot to system-level operations. Title scope 'Enable RCE Attacks' implies full code execution capability unconstrained by user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token impersonation, CreateProcessAsUser calls, or elevation attempts originating from extension host process. Alert on SYSTEM-context process creation initiated by user-level extension threads.

suggestion.title: RDP Brute Force and Successful Logon Clustering
suggestion.rationale: 'RDP Access' explicitly stated in title as attack vector; article body mentions RDP as entry mechanism but no detection generated for T1133.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of failed RDP logon attempts (EventID 4625) from external IPs followed by successful logon (EventID 4624) to administrative accounts. Correlate with logon time anomalies and non-standard RDP ports. Flag source IPs with no prior authentication history.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Execution (PsExec, WMI, WinRM) Post-RDP
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Remote Admin Tools' but pipeline generated zero detections for T1021 lateral movement or post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on psexec.exe, wmic.exe, or winrs.exe with remote targeting parameters (\\hostname, -node:) executed within 1 hour of successful RDP logon. Correlate with service creation events (T1543.003) and process parent-child chains indicating non-standard execution context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Account Creation and Privilege Escalation via RDP Session
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Stealthy Persistence' implying credential/account-based mechanisms; no persistence detection for T1098 or T1136 was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new local or domain account creation (EventID 4720/4722) within minutes of RDP session. Flag accounts with system-mimicking names (e.g., 'sysadmin', 'backup_svc'). Alert on addition of new accounts to sensitive groups (Administrators, Remote Desktop Users) via EventID 4728/4732.

suggestion.title: File Encryption Bulk Activity and Ransom Note Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'NightSpire Ransomware' explicitly but zero detection for encryption impact (T1486) or ransom note deployment was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file writes across multiple directories in compressed timeframe, particularly .nightspire or uncommon extensions. Alert on creation of ransom note files (readme.txt, RECOVERY_KEY.txt, note.html) in root system directories. Flag processes with low reputation scores encrypting >1000 files in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: RDP Registry and Firewall Rule Persistence Modification
suggestion.rationale: 'Stealthy Persistence' via RDP requires sustained access; pipeline missed detections for T1547 or firewall modification (T1562.004) hardening RDP exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server registry keys enabling fDenyTSConnections=0 or disabling NLA. Alert on new inbound firewall rules (netsh advfirewall) permitting port 3389 from non-corporate ranges or ANY protocol. Monitor for deletion of RDP audit event logging (T1562.001).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP Chaining to Secondary Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article implies multi-host RDP-based persistence but no detection for T1021.001 chaining or internal network pivot detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP connections from internal server A to server B to server C within compressed time window, especially if servers lack prior communication patterns. Alert on RDP logons from compromised internal assets to critical infrastructure (domain controllers, backup servers). Flag RDP use from non-standard user accounts (service accounts, administrative accounts outside normal hours).

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Installation via bpf() Syscall
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'eBPF Rootkit' as a core capability, yet zero detection use case was generated. eBPF program loading is a novel kernel-level persistence mechanism rarely seen in production workloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor bpf() syscalls with BPF_PROG_LOAD and BPF_PROG_ATTACH flags. Alert on unsigned or obfuscated eBPF bytecode loaded by non-kernel processes. Correlate LLVM/clang invocations on production systems with subsequent eBPF operations.

suggestion.title: Fileless Execution via Process Injection or Memory Mapping
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly mentions 'fileless execution' as a primary evasion mechanism, but pipeline generated no detection for in-memory code execution, mmap + mprotect patterns, or direct syscall execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mmap/mprotect syscall sequences with PROT_EXEC flags. Alert on parent-child process anomalies where interpreters (bash, perl) spawn from non-standard parents (systemd, cron, network services). Monitor for direct executable memory writes followed by execution.

suggestion.title: RAT Command-and-Control Beaconing and Reverse Shell Detection
suggestion.rationale: Quasar is identified as a RAT (Remote Access Trojan), implying C2 callbacks and interactive shell access. Pipeline generated no detection for outbound C2, reverse shells, or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from developer workstations to rare ports (8888, 9999, high-numbered ports). Detect /bin/bash or /bin/sh spawning network connections. Alert on large POST requests with binary payloads or connections to unregistered/recently registered domains.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential and SSH Key Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'developers'; pipeline missed detection for ~/.ssh enumeration, git credential theft, IDE session hijacking, or source code repository access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.bashrc, and IDE config directories. Alert on tools like 'find', 'cat', or 'tar' enumerating developer home directories. Detect unauthorized git clone/push operations or SSH key generation outside normal workflows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Module or eBPF Bytecode Compilation on Production Systems
suggestion.rationale: eBPF requires kernel headers and compiler toolchain. Legitimate prod systems rarely invoke clang/LLVM to compile kernel-level code. Pipeline missed this strong privilege-escalation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clang, llvm-*, or bpftool execution on systems without a baseline dev environment. Monitor for #include <linux/bpf.h> file reads. Correlate compilation with subsequent bpf() syscalls or kernel ring buffer access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Manager Execution with Atypical Registry or Flags
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes 'developer machines' as supply chain attack target. Package manager abuse (npm, pip, cargo) is standard vector. Phrase: 'developer machines are now the number one target.'
