suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/pip/cargo/gem install with --no-verify, --force, --unsafe-perm flags or pointing to non-standard registries. Monitor for package installs from accounts with no recent package history.

suggestion.title: Git Configuration or Shell Profile Modification Post-Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on developers require persistence hooks in development environment. Developer machines imply git/shell automation as persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected writes to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.gitconfig, git hooks directories, or PATH modifications. Correlate with recent package installations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Git Credential Extraction or Remote Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines store high-value secrets (git tokens, ssh keys, credentials). Supply chain attack article positions developers as targets; source code repository access is primary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of .ssh/id_rsa, .git/config, git credential storage, or environment variable dumping (ssh-keyscan, git config --list-all). Flag credential helper invocations outside normal git push/pull flows.

suggestion.title: IDE Plugin or Editor Extension Installation from Unknown Source
suggestion.rationale: Developer machine compromise pathway through trusted tools. IDE plugins execute with full developer environment access and source code visibility—critical attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code plugins directory, JetBrains plugin cache, Vim plugin managers for installations outside official marketplaces. Flag unsigned or newly-created developer accounts installing extensions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Build Artifact or CI/CD Pipeline Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack impact flows through build system. Article's focus on 'developer machines' implies compromise cascades to build outputs and deployed artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, build.gradle, pom.xml outside expected deployment windows. Flag build tool invocations with suspicious arguments (curl to external URLs, compression to network paths).

suggestion.title: Process Spawning from Package Manager or Node Modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute code at install/runtime. Developer machine as attack target implies post-compromise execution occurs during normal development workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution originating from node_modules/, site-packages/, vendor/, or .gem directories, especially network calls to external domains or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Code Authentication Flow Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code' sent to targets. Device code flows are legitimate but rare in normal operations. Should detect when device auth codes are generated but tokens aren't issued from expected device types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authentication requests where the authorization device differs from the device that consumes the token, or where code is generated multiple times in short windows targeting different users.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'attackers also created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity' after gaining account access. Inbox rules post-compromise are a defense evasion and persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation events shortly after OAuth token issuance or unusual authentication events, especially rules with forwarding, deletion, or hiding conditions that weren't previously present.

suggestion.title: Device Registration in M365 Environment Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Device registration is persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registration events that occur in close temporal proximity to suspicious OAuth token usage, unusual interactive sign-ins, or inbox rule modifications.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Bypass of Multi-Factor Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Token theft bypasses MFA entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth access token creation where MFA was satisfied for user A but token is used from different IP/device/geolocation as user A, or tokens are used immediately without interactive user activity.

suggestion.title: Cookie/Session Token Harvesting via AitM (Cookie Link Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cookie Link' mode: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic where authenticated session cookies are transmitted to attacker infrastructure, or identify login portals that require token/cookie submission followed by redirect to legitimate Microsoft services.

suggestion.title: Authentication Transfer Between Disparate Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends: 'block authentication transfer policies that allow authentication sessions to move between devices.' This implies attackers move authenticated sessions post-device-code attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when an authenticated session (indicated by refresh token or device context) is used on a second device within hours, especially if first device shows no interactive usage after authentication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation of Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 as the attack vector. Pipeline should flag POST/PUT requests to Ghost admin endpoints, authentication bypass attempts, or requests to known vulnerable Ghost API paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Ghost CMS admin endpoints (/ghost/api/) with unusual methods or payloads. Flag rapid authentication failures followed by successful shell.* or content injection attempts. Track POST requests to vulnerable Ghost endpoints associated with CVE-2026-26980.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Injection into Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites were 'hijacked' for 'ClickFix attacks,' indicating malicious script injection into legitimate site content. Pipeline should detect unexpected JavaScript or iframe injection into static assets or HTML responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded or obfuscated JavaScript appended to HTML files or injected into web template directories. Alert on unexpected modifications to index.html, header includes, or footer template files in Ghost content directories. Flag responses containing ClickFix-associated domains or JavaScript deobfuscation signatures.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After compromising sites via CVE-2026-26980, attackers modified content for ClickFix distribution. Should detect file writes or database updates injecting malicious payloads into published content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost content and template directories for unexpected file modifications outside of standard deployment windows. Track database writes to post content, metadata, or footer injection points. Alert on bulk modifications affecting >50 articles within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Authentication Anomaly - Admin Session Abuse
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-26980 exploitation likely involves session hijacking or privilege escalation. Should detect unusual admin portal login patterns, geographically impossible logins, or token/session reuse anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed /ghost/api/admin/authentication attempts from single IP followed by successful admin login. Flag admin sessions from IPs or User-Agents inconsistent with historical behavior. Detect unusual API token generation or unusually long session durations.

suggestion.title: ClickFix C2 Communication from Compromised Sites
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix is a malware family that executes in users' browsers and likely communicates with attacker-controlled C2. Should detect outbound HTTPS connections from compromised Ghost servers to ClickFix C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS connections from Ghost server IP ranges to known ClickFix C2 domains or IP ranges. Alert on bulk data exfiltration via HTTPS tunnels to suspicious destinations. Detect DNS queries for ClickFix-related domain patterns (e.g., registrant history, domain age, SSL certificate anomalies).

suggestion.title: Bulk Site Content Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '700+ sites' were hijacked. A detection rule should flag when a single compromise enables rapid modification of multiple downstream victim sites or when framework vulnerabilities affect site batches simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate file modification events across Ghost installations sharing infrastructure or CMS version. Alert when >10 unique websites within the same IP range or managed service undergo content modification within 1-hour window. Correlate with CVE-2026-26980 exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory-Only Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references RemotePE as a memory-only RAT — no file-based artifacts expected. Pipeline should detect injection into legitimate processes and in-memory payload execution signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unusual process injection patterns (CreateRemoteThread, NtWriteVirtualMemory) into system processes (svchost, lsass, explorer). Memory-resident RATs often avoid disk writes; detect via suspicious memory allocations with execute permissions, followed by parent-child process relationships that mismatch file system artifacts.

suggestion.title: Lazarus C2 Beaconing (RemotePE Profile)
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE is identified as memory-only RAT; persistent C2 communication is essential to the attack. Pipeline should surface inbound/outbound C2 patterns specific to Lazarus infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic beacons to hardcoded C2 addresses; RemotePE typically uses HTTP/HTTPS with obfuscated payloads. Watch for anomalous DNS queries and HTTP headers that deviate from normal application patterns in targeted financial/crypto environments.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping via RemotePE RAT
suggestion.rationale: Article targets financial and crypto firms—implying credential access is core objective. RATs typically inject into lsass or use inline credential dumping; pipeline should detect these post-execution behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mimikatz-like patterns (NTLM hashing, token theft) post-RemotePE execution. Financial targets suggest targeted credential exfiltration; look for suspicious lsass access, unusual authentication failures followed by successful logins, and abnormal network egress of credential-sized payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RemotePE in Financial Networks
suggestion.rationale: RAT deployed against financial sector typically enables horizontal propagation. Article does not mention initial vector; assume post-compromise lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In financial networks, RemotePE RAT likely spreads via SMB/RDP to critical systems (trading platforms, payment gateways, wallets). Detect lateral movement via unusual admin share access, credential reuse across systems, and process creation events on target servers that map to RAT execution signatures.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Financial Data Post-RAT Infection
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus targeting crypto/financial firms inherently aims to steal credentials, keys, or transaction data. Pipeline should surface bulk data exfiltration indicators correlated with RemotePE presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data staging operations (clipboard capture, screen recording) and encrypted egress tunnels post-RemotePE infection. Financial/crypto firms show anomalous outbound traffic patterns (large HTTPS transfers) and suspicious file access to wallets, trading databases, or credential stores.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Phishing/Spear-Phishing Delivery (RemotePE Initial Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article omits initial access vector but Lazarus historically uses spear-phishing. Pipeline should reverse-engineer delivery if IOCs (domains, sender addresses, URLs) are available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for phishing emails with RemotePE dropper attachments (Office macros, ISO files, LNK) or malicious URLs to financial/crypto sector targets. Detect Office application spawning suspicious child processes (PowerShell, cmd), ISO mounting, or executable extraction patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious package manager invocation and child-process execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'spreads via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO'—implies code execution occurs during dependency install. Pipeline must detect npm install, pip install, cargo add events followed by anomalous child-process spawns or file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/pip/cargo/mix commands that spawn child processes (bash, sh, powershell) or access credential stores. Baseline should exclude known benign setup scripts and flag execution outside development hours or from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Credential enumeration and exfiltration post-package-install
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly names 'Credential-Stealing Malware'—core payload behavior. Pipeline must detect post-install attempts to read ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Internet Account Manager, or invoke credential-dumping patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by package managers that enumerate or read credential files, access browser storage (Chrome SQLite, Firefox profiles), query Windows credential manager APIs, or construct base64-encoded payloads for exfil.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from development environment post-package-install
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware requires exfil channel; article implies 'TrapDoor' includes C2 behavior. Pipeline should detect anomalous external connections from build-tool child processes to non-allowlisted infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TCP/UDP outbound from npm, pip, cargo child-processes to IPs outside known CDN/mirror ranges, particularly to residential ASNs or newly-registered domains. Check for DNS queries to suspicious subdomains immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted or lookalike package installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via registries commonly use name spoofing (e.g., 'leftpad' vs 'left-pad', 'request' vs 'request-promise'). Article does not name packages explicitly, but typosquatting is standard TrapDoor-class attack delivery. Pipeline should flag installs of packages with high Levenshtein distance from legitimate names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a known-good package database (most-downloaded npm/PyPI/Cargo packages) and alert on install of package names differing by ≤2 edits or sourced from new/low-reputation maintainers. Flag installs from non-CI/non-standard dev user accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious lifecycle hook execution in setup.py, package.json, or Cargo.toml
suggestion.rationale: Modern package managers execute setup scripts (postinstall, preinstall, build, prepare hooks in npm; postinstall in pip; build.rs in Cargo). Malware likely hides payload in these hooks. Article implies execution at install-time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and alert on shell/Python/Rust execution originating from node_modules/.bin, site-packages, or .cargo directories. Flag scripts that invoke curl/wget to external URLs, write to /tmp or user home, or attempt process isolation bypass (sudo, RunAs).

suggestion.title: Mass exfiltration of source code and build artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated supply-chain malware often exfils source + credentials together. While article headline focuses on credential theft, source-code theft is standard secondary payload in supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file copies from source directories (~/projects, /src) to staging directories (~/Downloads, /tmp) immediately post-package-install. Correlate with outbound network traffic to C2; alert on tarball/zip creation + remote upload in same session.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Org Unauthorized Access – Credential Compromise or API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cybercriminals claimed to have stolen over 600,000 records containing corporate data and personally identifiable information after breaching 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment.' Explicit Salesforce breach; likely credential theft or OAuth token abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce API audit logs for anomalous service-account token creation, bulk exports via Data Loader or REST API, and authentication from non-corporate IP ranges or Tor. Alert on disabled MFA accounts re-enabled post-breach, or password changes on dormant franchisee service accounts. Correlate with timestamps after April 8, 2026.

suggestion.title: Bulk Collection – Franchisee Document Store Mass Read
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' and 'stolen over 600,000 records.' Indicates centralized document repository accessed in bulk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or recursive file enumeration targeting franchisee document shares (SMB, SharePoint, cloud storage) within 24–48-hour window. Alert on archive creation (ZIP/TAR/GZ) of >100MB containing mixed PII field names (email, phone, DOB, address) from least-privileged or service accounts. Flag read operations from API or non-interactive sessions.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration – Dark Web Leak Site Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'They then leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site.' Explicit exfiltration of 9.4GB to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic for uploads >500MB to newly-registered, Tor-exit-proxied, or bulletproof-hosting-provider domains. Flag HTTPS/SSH uploads of archives containing PII. Correlate with prior credential-compromise timeline (April 8) and detect uploads from dormant or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Leak Site Data Dump – ShinyHunters Monitor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the company refused to pay a ransom' and ShinyHunters 'leaked a 9.4GB archive…on their dark web leak site.' Extortion-gang operational activity post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ShinyHunters-linked dark web leak portals (via onion-scraper feeds or threat-intel subscriptions) for 7-Eleven or parent-company data announcements. Alert on ransom notes referencing 7-Eleven assets or 186k/600k record counts. Correlate dump-site activity with breach timeline and leaked-data schema against internal asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Franchisee Account Compromise – Lateral Movement to Restricted Shares
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'systems used to store franchisee documents' were breached; attackers moved from Salesforce to document stores. Suggests franchisee account misuse or credential-stuffing on subsidiary systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline franchisee account access (login times, document types, request volume, source IPs). Alert when franchisee credentials access non-franchisee-owned systems (corporate-only document shares, parent-company repos, HR systems). Flag logins from VPN/Tor-exit nodes or non-standard client user-agents.

suggestion.title: Ransom Note and Extortion Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'company refused to pay a ransom to have the stolen data returned and destroyed' and 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility.' Direct extortion attempt is documented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for inbound emails, chat messages, or ticket submissions from attacker-controlled addresses (often free email, remailers, or compromised corporate accounts) claiming data theft and demanding payment. Correlate sender IP, domain registration date, and email header anomalies with known ShinyHunters infrastructure. Flag high-entropy subject lines or impersonation of legitimate executives requesting wire-transfer confirmations.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Internet-Facing Service via Known Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes 'Internet-Facing Flaws' as primary attack vector with 12-hour urgency window. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for this critical phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching known exploit payloads or vulnerability scanner signatures targeting web applications, followed by successful response codes (200, 302) from previously failing endpoints. Correlate rapid sequential attempts across multiple targets with geographically distributed or proxy-masked source IPs.

suggestion.title: AI-Optimized Exploitation Attempt Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifically mentions 'AI-Assisted Attacks,' implying novel attack sequencing or high-volume coordinated attempts, yet pipeline surfaced no behavioral detections for this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous attack patterns: non-standard User-Agent strings combined with rapid endpoint enumeration, unusual payload encoding/obfuscation, or exploitation attempts that deviate from known public PoCs. Flag clusters of similar requests from disparate sources suggesting centralized attack orchestration.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor Persistence on Patched Service
suggestion.rationale: Urgent patching window implies active exploitation in the wild. Post-compromise, attackers establish persistence via web shells or code injection—standard follow-up after successful initial access not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file writes to web-accessible directories (e.g., /var/www, wwwroot) immediately post-patch, new .php/.asp/.jsp files with low entropy names, or modifications to existing application files. Alert on unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash) spawned from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unpatched System Detection via Service Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes identifying systems vulnerable to 'Internet-Facing Flaws.' Defensive coverage should include proactive scanning detection to catch unpatched assets before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound scans probing for specific vulnerable service versions, banner grabbing against web ports, or vulnerability scanner traffic (e.g., Shodan, Censys signatures). Flag patterns matching known automated reconnaissance tools used to inventory unpatched Internet-exposed services.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Targeting Corporate SSO Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'ShinyHunters claimed they breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Core initial access vector not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual incoming calls to corporate numbers followed by failed/successful SSO logins within 2 hours. Monitor for employee reports of unsolicited calls requesting credential verification. Correlate voicemail transcripts referencing urgent account access requests with subsequent authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra OAuth Token Abuse for SaaS Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After gaining access to a corporate SSO account, the threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox.' Describes T1550.001 exploitation but no detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Entra accounts issuing OAuth tokens for multiple SaaS applications (4+) within 24 hours post-compromise. Flag token issuance from geographically impossible locations or after failed login attempts. Alert on tokens used to access data export APIs in previously-unaccessed systems.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer Record Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat actors used this access to export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance.' A 40-million-record extraction is detectable but unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk export operations (reports.export, data loader, API batches) exceeding 50K records from single compromised account. Flag exports of PII-containing fields by accounts without historical data export patterns. Correlate with Entra token issuance and cross-reference export destination (external URLs, cloud storage).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Multi-Application Access Pattern from Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article lists theft from Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox—7+ SaaS apps accessed in parallel from one compromised identity. No use case detects this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts accessing 5+ distinct SaaS applications within 12 hours of a login anomaly (new location, device, time-of-day outlier). Prioritize detection when accessed apps include data repositories (Salesforce, Slack, Dropbox, SharePoint). Correlate with OAuth token issuance and unusual API activity.

suggestion.title: Support Ticket System Bulk Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat actor also claims to have stolen customer support ticket data.' No detection use case for unauthorized bulk access to support systems containing sensitive customer interactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor support platform for accounts querying >5K tickets outside normal departmental scope, bulk exports of ticket data, or ticket system API access from compromised SSO tokens. Alert on data exported to external email domains or cloud storage endpoints.

suggestion.title: Data Breach Extortion Site Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters publishing stolen data on public leak site. Detection of organization asset/employee reconnaissance of known leak sites during incident response window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal IP access to known ShinyHunters/extortion group leak sites (passive monitoring during incident window). Correlate with incident investigation timeline. Track external reconnaissance of leak site IPs/domains that may indicate attacker infrastructure scanning or ransom negotiation activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on Edge Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'custom Linux implant' deployed to routers. Execution of unknown processes, shell invocations, or binary downloads on edge appliances should be detectable, yet pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases. Phrase: 'Custom Linux Implant.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning, shell script execution, or binary writes to /tmp, /var, or /opt on edge routers. Flag invoking processes with non-standard parent processes or execution from unprivileged service accounts on perimeter appliances.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistence on Edge Routers (Cron/Systemd)
suggestion.rationale: Implant implies persistent presence requiring cron jobs, systemd units, or init scripts. Article does not detail persistence mechanism, but persistent compromise of routers cannot occur without such mechanisms. No persistence-phase use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation, modification, or deletion of cron jobs, systemd unit files, or /etc/init.d scripts on edge routers. Alert on unexpected scheduled tasks, new system services, or boot-start registrations on perimeter devices.

suggestion.title: Edge Router Outbound C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Implant requires command-and-control channel to attacker infrastructure. Title indicates 'China-linked' campaign, suggesting C2 to Chinese ASNs or known APT infrastructure. Pipeline generated zero C2-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline edge router outbound traffic to known internal/business destinations. Alert on sustained or periodic connections to undocumented external IPs, non-standard ports, or geolocation inconsistent with regional operations. Flag encrypted tunnels or port non-standard protocols originating from router management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Edge Router Management Interface Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting 'Southeast Asian edge routers,' implying initial compromise via vulnerability or weak credentials on management plane (SSH, HTTP, SNMP). No initial-access detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor edge router management ports (22/SSH, 80/HTTP, 443/HTTPS, 161/SNMP, manufacturer-specific) for failed authentication spikes, malformed protocol requests, or known exploitation signatures. Alert on credential stuffing patterns or successful access from unusual geographies.

suggestion.title: Edge Router Configuration Checksum Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Implant installation requires filesystem or bootloader modifications on router. No defense-evasion or file-integrity use case was generated to detect unauthorized config/binary changes on perimeter appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline checksums of critical edge router binaries (/sbin, /bin, /lib, bootloader, config files). Alert on divergence from baseline, unexpected new files in sensitive paths, or config exports that differ from known-good snapshots.

suggestion.title: cPanel Web Interface Exploitation Attempt (CVE-2026-48172)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin'—the attack vector is the public-facing web interface. Pipeline did not surface initial-access detection for this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel web server logs for POST requests to vulnerable plugin endpoints, particularly from non-administrative user sessions. Correlate timing with subsequent privilege escalation events. Alert on request patterns deviating from baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Local User to Root Privilege Escalation via cPanel Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'any cPanel user account...execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—privilege escalation from user to root is the core attack. Pipeline missed this execution and escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-root cPanel user processes spawning shell/script interpreters (bash, perl, python, sh) that subsequently obtain or execute with root permissions. Look for setuid/setgid abuse, sudo calls, or privilege elevation API invocations initiated from cPanel user context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous cPanel User Privilege Escalation Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'any cPanel user account' can trigger the flaw—requires detection of privilege escalation from low-privilege users. Pipeline should map this account-based attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline which cPanel user accounts typically execute administrative-level scripts or trigger privilege escalation; alert on deviations. Correlate cPanel user login events with root-level activity within 60 seconds. Monitor for failed escalation attempts preceding successful ones.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Vulnerability Scan Coverage and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal due date 2026-05-29. Pipeline should operationalize the CVE for vulnerability inventory and patch-deadline tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CVE-2026-48172 against vulnerability scanner output and asset database. Identify all LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin installations. Flag as critical if not patched before 2026-05-29 deadline. Correlate unpatched assets with web access logs for exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests'—core attack vector. 15,000+ attacks observed, indicating active reconnaissance and exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal database abstraction API endpoints for SQL injection payloads: single-quote escaping, UNION SELECT syntax, stacked queries (semicolon delimiters), and comment sequences (-- or /**/). Baseline against legitimate Drupal query patterns and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Unauthenticated SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Successful exploitation can potentially lead to...privilege escalation'—explicit post-SQL-injection lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SQL injection attempts against Drupal with subsequent privilege escalation events in OS/database logs. Flag admin account creation or role elevation from web application process context without corresponding legitimate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Webshell Persistence Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'can potentially lead to...remote code execution'—implicit second-stage payload delivery. Imperva/active exploitation data suggests threat actors are reaching RCE; monitor for deployment artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of executable files (PHP, JSP, ASP) in Drupal webroot directories following SQL injection exploitation attempts. Flag process execution from unexpected web-server child processes (e.g., bash/cmd spawned by Apache/Nginx).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass: Successful Admin Access Without Logon Events
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'can be exploited without authentication'—attackers bypass Drupal auth entirely via SQL. Monitor for admin sessions with no preceding authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Drupal admin actions (config changes, user creation, module installation) without matching user authentication events in OS or application logs. Cross-correlate session tokens with logon events to identify token forgery/bypass.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Database Enumeration and Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 15,000+ active exploitations; threat actors will perform reconnaissance post-injection. Article describes 'information disclosure'—queries for system information.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SQL queries for INFORMATION_SCHEMA enumeration, table listing (SELECT * FROM pg_tables), user enumeration (SELECT * FROM pg_user), and column discovery post-SQL-injection. Flag repetitive data structure queries from single source IP within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Unpatched System Inventory and Exposure Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Shadowserver now tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online'—asset hygiene is the primary defense. Patch deadline is May 27; detect non-compliant systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internet-facing Drupal instances for Drupal version and patch status. Alert on instances running vulnerable Drupal versions (pre-patch for CVE-2026-9082) via banner grabbing, plugin detection, or known version fingerprints. Flag continued exposure after May 27 deadline for federal agencies.

suggestion.title: XWiki ssx/jsx path traversal exploitation via leading-slash resource parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'URLs such as `http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false`'. This is the core attack — http.request.uri contains /bin/ssx or /bin/jsx with resource parameter starting with / or containing ../ traversal sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET/POST requests to endpoints matching /bin/(ssx|jsx)/* where the resource parameter begins with '/' or contains '../' path traversal. XWiki legitimate requests use relative resource paths without leading slashes. Track per-source-IP request volume to detect scanning.

suggestion.title: XWiki WEB-INF configuration file access via path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It's possible to get access and read configuration files' with explicit example targeting WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg. Successful exploitation yields 200 OK responses on sensitive config access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to ssx/jsx endpoints with resource parameters targeting /WEB-INF/*, config files, or web root escape sequences that result in HTTP 200 status. Correlate successful collection attempts (200 responses) with prior exploitation attempts from same source.

suggestion.title: XWiki minify=false obfuscation bypass in path traversal requests
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates: 'resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false'. The minify=false flag explicitly disables output minification, a defense-evasion technique to obfuscate payloads, mirroring T1027 obfuscation evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ssx/jsx requests where minify=false is combined with suspicious resource parameters (leading /, ../, or WEB-INF paths). This combination signals intentional payload obfuscation bypass rather than legitimate client behavior.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated XAR Import Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks.' Article explicitly recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /wikis/{wikiName} endpoint without prior user authentication. Monitor for XAR file uploads from unauthenticated or external-origin sessions. Correlate with document creation events in XWiki audit logs from non-admin contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Document Creation or Update in XWiki
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'allowing an unauthenticated attacker to create or update documents in the target wiki.' Requires detection of unauthorized persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor XWiki document creation/modification events with null or missing authentication tokens. Flag bulk document mutations within short time windows. Cross-reference document changelog against known admin accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-33137 Asset Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' hunt in recon phase to identify vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect probes or banner grabs targeting /wikis/ endpoints on XWiki instances running versions 16.10.0-16.10.16, 17.4.0-17.4.8, 17.10.0-17.10.2, or 18.0.0. Correlate POST requests to /wikis/{wikiName} with lack of auth headers from scanner IP patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Bulk Authentication Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions.' Pipeline should detect sudden spikes in auth rejections against GitHub Actions API/webhook endpoints. Establishes T1110 (Brute Force) or T1021 (Remote Services) patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained burst of 401/403 HTTP responses from github.com/api/v3/actions endpoints. Baseline: <5 failures/min per org; alert if sustained >50/min for >5 min. Filter: exclude known CI/CD token rotation events and documented maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Denied Access to GitHub Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'Denying Access to Actions'—direct evidence of T1531 (Account Access Removal) or authorization failure. Pipeline missed mapping to access control disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for sudden spike in 'repo_access_denied' or 'action_run_denied' events. Correlate with user IP changes, new device fingerprints, or geolocation anomalies. Alert if >10 distinct repos affected within 5-min window.

suggestion.title: Service Availability Incident – GitHub API Endpoint Unavailability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GitHub Down'—pipeline failed to map to T1498 (Denial of Service) or T1526 (Enumerate Cloud Resources). Impact phase tactics for SaaS platform outages are fundamental detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden loss of reachability to github.com (ping/HTTP GET failures from multiple vantage points). Correlate with error logs showing 5xx or timeout responses. Baseline uptime >99.9%; alert if >0.1% of requests fail for >2 min.

suggestion.title: PAT (Personal Access Token) Validation Failures
suggestion.rationale: Authentication issues suggest token/credential validation bypass or revocation. Article does not detail if tokens were invalidated, leaked, or misconfigured—but pipeline should have generated speculative UC for T1078.004 (Cloud Accounts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid-fire token validation failures (Bearer token rejections) in GitHub API logs. Baseline: <1 invalid-token error per user/hour; alert if single user triggers >5 rejections in 1 min or >50 across org in 5 min.

suggestion.title: OAuth/SSO Provider Connectivity Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Authentication failures could stem from upstream OAuth/SAML provider failure (T1556 - Modify Authentication Process). Pipeline failed to enumerate credential chain dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If GitHub uses federated identity, detect failures at OAuth provider integration points (e.g., Azure AD, Okta). Alert on: (1) OAuth token endpoint 5xx errors, (2) SAML assertion validation timeouts, (3) mismatched user/group claims.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Workflow Trigger Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies GitHub Actions; pipeline should detect T1204.003 (User Execution - Malicious Link) or T1059.001 (PowerShell) if workflows themselves are compromised or hijacked during the outage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor workflow execution logs for: (1) jobs triggered from unusual source repos, (2) base64-encoded scripts in workflow YAML, (3) unexpected use_secrets directives. Alert if >3 abnormal executions per workflow in 10 min.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-26980 as the attack vector; no detection use case exists despite 700 confirmed compromises. Article: 'Hackers Exploit Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS endpoints for exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-26980. Correlate HTTP POST/PUT requests to Ghost admin APIs with authentication bypass or code injection payloads. Flag unusual version-specific paths or error responses indicative of exploitation probing.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Delivery from Compromised Websites
suggestion.rationale: Article states '700 Websites poisoned with ClickFix Malware' but pipeline extracted no malware-delivery detection logic. This is execution-layer activity affecting end-users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script injection or malicious redirects on known-compromised Ghost CMS sites serving ClickFix payloads. Monitor for unusual HTTP 302/meta-refresh responses, JavaScript beaconing to command-and-control domains, and file downloads matching ClickFix signatures post-visit to affected domains.

suggestion.title: Website Defacement and Content Injection Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'poisoning' websites—content modification is impact-layer indicator. Pipeline missed this detection gap entirely.
log_sources: Git audit logs (if Ghost uses git-based content)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost content database and published file modifications for unauthorized inserts of malware delivery scripts, iframes, or redirects. Alert on mass changes across multiple posts/pages in short time window. Correlate with failed login attempts or privilege escalation in Ghost admin logs.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Authentication Bypass or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attackers gained admin access (ability to modify 700 sites' content); no detection UC for initial access control weakness. Required precursor to website poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins from anomalous IPs post-CVE-2026-26980 exploitation, privilege escalation to admin role immediately after failed auth attempts, or API tokens created outside normal admin workflows. Flag rapid content modification API calls by freshly-created service accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Between Compromised Ghost Instances
suggestion.rationale: 700 websites compromised suggests either mass hosting-account takeover or shared infrastructure abuse. Article implies coordination across multiple targets—no detection for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Ghost instances on same hosting provider being compromised within short time windows. Correlate Ghost API tokens, SSH keys, or database credentials shared across instances. Alert on bulk password reset operations affecting multiple WordPress/Ghost admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes successful exploitation of CVE-2026-26980 but pipeline missed detection for the likely code-execution phase that enabled malware deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost server logs for PHP/Node.js code execution anomalies post-exploitation: unexpected child processes, file writes to web-accessible directories, or reverse-shell outbound connections. Correlate with CVE-2026-26980 exploitation indicators in IDS/WAF logs.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Deploy MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 via Phishing'—this is the primary attack vector and demands detection for malware payloads in email attachments or links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails containing file hashes, domains, or behavioral signatures associated with MiniFast or MiniJunk V2. Correlate phishing detection rules with known payload indicators. Alert on user interaction with suspicious links/attachments that trigger malware detonation.

suggestion.title: SEO poisoning infrastructure detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'SEO Poisoning' as deployment vector—attackers compromise search results to redirect victims to malware distribution sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track clicks on suspicious domains masquerading as legitimate software/documents via poisoned search results. Monitor for redirects through URL shorteners or CDNs that ultimately serve malware payloads. Identify domains with typosquatting patterns targeting common search terms.

suggestion.title: MiniFast malware execution and C2 communication
suggestion.rationale: MiniFast is deployed as the attack payload but pipeline provided no execution or C2 detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MiniFast execution via process creation events, file writes to suspicious directories, or known file hashes. Monitor network traffic for C2 beacons to known command-and-control infrastructure. Alert on suspicious child processes spawned from initial phishing payload.

suggestion.title: MiniJunk V2 malware execution and behavioral signatures
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk V2 is the second malware deployed but requires separate detection signature—likely distinct C2, execution method, or persistence behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MiniJunk V2 file hashes, command-line arguments, registry modifications for persistence, and obfuscation patterns. Correlate with known C2 domains/IPs used by this variant. Alert on process hollowing or code injection techniques associated with this malware family.

suggestion.title: Iranian threat actor campaign infrastructure correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes attacks to 'Iranian Hackers' but pipeline failed to surface threat actor name, aliases, or historical IOC correlation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference malware samples, C2 domains, and registrant information against known Iranian APT groups (e.g., APT33, APT34, MuddyWater, etc.). Flag infrastructure sharing historical patterns: WHOIS privacy services, bulletproof hosters, shared SSL certificates, or autonomous system usage typical of Iranian threat actors.

suggestion.title: Payload download and execution from phishing redirects
suggestion.rationale: Phishing + SEO poisoning chains require detection of secondary download stages after user clicks malicious link—payload staging is implicit in 'via Phishing and SEO Poisoning' but unmapped to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect secondary payload downloads (MSI, EXE, scripts, Office macros) following clicks on phishing URLs or SEO-poisoned search results. Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned immediately after download completion. Alert on unsigned executables or double-extension files (e.g., .pdf.exe).

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution'—the core exploitation technique. No detection present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to .aspx endpoints with __VIEWSTATE parameter >4KB or containing serialized .NET object gadget patterns. Alert on ViewState validation failures in IIS logs. Flag requests where ViewState MAC validates against known hardcoded machine keys (CVE-2026-5426 specific key hash).

suggestion.title: Godzilla In-Memory Web Shell Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'deployed the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla' with no corresponding detection. Godzilla has been used in similar ASP.NET attacks since August 2024.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect w3wp.exe or aspnet_wp.exe loading unexpected .NET assemblies or executing inline compilation (System.CodeDom, System.Reflection.Emit). Monitor for unusual HTTP requests routed through web worker processes spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell, or w3wp establishing outbound HTTPS connections.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection in Web Portal Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat actor 'modified an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin.' No detection for web application file tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification to .js/.aspx files in web application directories outside scheduled deployments or by service accounts. Flag JavaScript containing external iframe loads, window.open to unfamiliar domains, or prompt dialogs requesting installation of authentication plugins.

suggestion.title: Staged Malware Download via Fake Installer Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious script 'convinced users to download a fake installer, which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon.' No UC for second-stage payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable/MSI downloads from KnowledgeDeliver portal with unusually large file sizes (padded fakes) or mismatched signatures. Monitor browser→installer→system process chains (rundll32.exe, regsvcs.exe spawned from temporary directories). Alert on process injection from installer executables.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded ASP.NET Machine Key Detection in Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys across multiple customer deployments' and 'hardcoded machineKey values' as the vulnerability root cause. No detection for exposed or default keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan web.config files for machineKey entries matching known vendor defaults or deployer-common patterns. Alert if identical machineKey exists across multiple servers. Flag web.config readable by non-admin accounts or exposed via backup files (.bak, .old).

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Execution Post-Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'payload was encrypted using a key that used the name of the compromised organization' and Cobalt Strike beacon delivered via fake installer. No detection for post-exploitation C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rundll32.exe or regsvcs.exe spawned from installer executables in temp directories. Monitor for DNS/HTTPS beaconing to newly registered domains from user-tier processes. Flag process injection and parent-child chains matching Cobalt Strike staging patterns (installer→cmd→rundll32).

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes LMS vulnerability being exploited; article body was truncated but should contain exploit payloads or web shell indicators. Pipeline generated zero detections for initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver endpoints for abnormal POST/PUT requests to course upload, user import, or plugin endpoints; flag requests containing encoded payloads, shell metacharacters, or non-standard content-types. Correlate with subsequent process creation events.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title names Godzilla as deployed payload but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Godzilla is a known ASP.NET webshell family with distinctive command structure and in-memory backdoor capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Godzilla variants via HTTP POST parameter patterns (typically 'z', 'cmd'), Base64-encoded payload markers, and ASP.NET process spawning (aspnet_wp.exe, w3wp.exe) with suspicious parent/child relationships. Monitor for unusual System.Diagnostics.Process or Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal API calls in IIS worker processes.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Injection and C2
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states Cobalt Strike deployment but pipeline generated zero indicators. Standard Cobalt Strike post-exploitation includes reflective DLL injection, beacon configuration, and HTTPS C2 beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike beacons via HTTPS traffic anomalies: JA3 SSL fingerprints matching known Cobalt Strike configurations, abnormal certificate issuer patterns, or traffic to known infrastructure. Correlate with rundll32.exe/svchost.exe spawning from unusual parents or executing DLLs from temporary directories.

suggestion.title: LMS Course/Content Upload for Payload Staging
suggestion.rationale: LMS flaws typically exploited via upload mechanisms; article title indicates vulnerability exists but pipeline extracted no upload-based indicators or file hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver uploads for non-course MIME types (executable, archive, script) in document libraries; detect executable uploads masquerading as course content; flag failed validations followed by successful execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Cobalt Strike Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Cobalt Strike post-compromise implies privilege escalation and lateral movement but pipeline generated zero techniques for discovery, enumeration, or lateral movement phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike lateral movement via elevated command execution (runas, psexec patterns), scheduled task creation for persistence, and winrm/psremoting over unusual ports. Correlate with unusual credential submission events and process creation from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequential MFA Prompts to Single User
suggestion.rationale: MFA prompt bombing specifically involves overwhelming a user with multiple authentication prompts—the core attack vector. Article title states 'Why Your Second Factor Isn't Saving You,' implying the attack defeats MFA by volume/timing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >5 MFA prompts sent to the same user_id within 10 minutes without corresponding sign-in completion. Filter for legitimate bulk-approval scenarios (user manually dismissing) vs. adversary-triggered prompt floods. Baseline per organization and user role.

suggestion.title: MFA Prompt Approved After Recent Denial or Cancellation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploit user fatigue by spamming prompts until the victim accidentally approves one out of confusion or to stop notifications. Attack sequence: deny, deny, approve within seconds = indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MFA approval within 30 seconds of a prior MFA denial/cancellation for the same user and authentication method. Correlate with risk score (unusual location, impossible travel, new device). High-confidence positive indicator of prompt-bombing acceptance.

suggestion.title: MFA Challenge Approvals from Geographically Impossible Locations
suggestion.rationale: Prompt bombing attacks often originate from attacker infrastructure in a different geography than the legitimate user's recent activity. User in London denies prompt, attacker approves from Singapore 5 seconds later = sign of multi-location attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Calculate time delta between initial sign-in attempt and MFA approval, derive implied travel speed using geolocation from request IPs. Flag approvals requiring >900 km/h implied travel (impossible without aircraft). Correlate with user's last-known location.

suggestion.title: MFA Prompt Storm from Anomalous Device or IP
suggestion.rationale: Attackers sometimes trigger MFA prompts via automated tools or stolen cookies before the victim's legitimate device attempts sign-in. Flood of prompts to registered device(s) followed by approval from unregistered IP = hostile pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA challenges initiated from IP/device not in user's recent authentication history, especially if followed by rapid approval-attempt sequences. Cross-reference with threat intelligence for attacker infrastructure or open proxies.

suggestion.title: Successful Sign-In Post-MFA Prompt Bombardment
suggestion.rationale: The end goal of prompt bombing is account takeover. Successful sign-in immediately after a high-velocity MFA prompt sequence = compromise indicator, especially if followed by lateral movement or data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication with prior 30-60 minute window of >3 MFA prompts. Enrich with post-auth activity: new token issuance, API calls from unusual clients, email forwarding rules, or lateral access attempts. Escalate if secondary indicators present.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed MFA Attempts Before Successful Approval
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate users rarely cancel/fail MFA repeatedly then approve. Adversary-driven pattern: many failed attempts (user ignoring attacker prompts) + eventual approval (user fatigued or attacker guesses correctly).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >3 MFA failures followed by approval within 15 minutes for the same user+auth method. Weight higher if failures and approval originate from different IPs or if approval happens at unusual hours (outside user's baseline window).

suggestion.title: DLL side-loading attempt via unsigned binary execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names DLL side-loading as the attack vector; no detection use case was generated despite this being a primary technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned/untrusted executable loading legitimate-named DLLs from suspicious paths (typically application directories not system32). Flag processes loading older/patched versions of system DLLs before legitimate system process execution.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater command-and-control pattern detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates espionage campaign with C2 activity, yet no IOCs or detection patterns for C2 communication were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to known or suspected MuddyWater C2 domains; monitor for HTTP/HTTPS beaconing from compromised endpoints to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Known MuddyWater C2 indicators should trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: Multi-country targeting and lateral movement indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies campaign targeting 9 countries, but pipeline generated no geographic-scope detection logic or cross-border IOC correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on logon events from unusual geographic origins relative to normal user/asset behavior; correlate failed/successful authentication attempts across multiple devices within a short timeframe suggesting compromise spread.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution via Compromised Angular Language Service Extension
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'RCE Attacks' yet pipeline generated zero execution detections. Article phrase: 'Multiple Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities Enable RCE Attacks'—RCE is the stated impact vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python) spawned by Angular Language Service host or extension process. Alert on execution of binaries or scripts from user extension directories that deviate from baseline development workflows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Angular Language Service Extension Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: RCE requires malicious extension delivery/installation. Title signals 'Multiple Vulnerabilities' implying varied attack paths; no detection addresses initial extension install or loading phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation of Angular-related extensions from non-official sources, unsigned extensions, or those from recently-created or low-reputation publishers. Correlate install events with subsequent suspicious process activity in extension context.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Privilege Escalation from Extension Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes RCE but does not specify privilege level. Extension vulnerabilities commonly chain to system-level execution; no privilege-escalation detection generated despite threat scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected process creation from extension host with subsequent token elevation, UAC bypass attempts, or high-integrity process spawning. Flag if extension process transitions from user-context to SYSTEM or ADMIN privileges.

suggestion.title: RDP Access from External IP with Subsequent Service Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'NightSpire Ransomware Uses RDP Access'—primary initial access vector requires detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP connection (port 3389, 3390, or variants) from non-whitelisted external IP to internal Windows host, followed within 60 minutes by suspicious process execution (psexec, WinRM, or service installation) from the same source. Flag weak-credential or brute-force patterns preceding successful logon.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Installation and Persistence Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Remote Admin Tools for Stealthy Persistence'—these tools maintain attacker foothold between sessions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution or file creation of common remote admin tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Ammyy Admin, Chrome RDP, etc.) from system paths or temp directories post-RDP compromise. Alert on registry Run/RunOnce keys or scheduled tasks configured to auto-start these tools.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption by NightSpire Ransomware
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware payload indicated by title—impact phase involves systematic file encryption across multiple extensions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag high-velocity file modifications (>500 files/minute) across multiple extensions (doc, xls, pdf, jpg, etc.) within user-accessible shares. Alert on ransom note creation or file rename patterns. Correlate with memory indicators of encryption (high CPU, unusual API sequences like CryptEncrypt).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP Chaining and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Persistent RDP access enables multi-stage lateral movement; attackers harvest credentials for privilege escalation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP daisy-chaining: successful logons from a compromised internal host to other internal hosts. Alert on credential dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump, secretsdump) executed post-RDP access. Flag failed RDP login storms followed by successful access using harvested credentials.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: RDP Port Masking and Firewall Rule Injection
suggestion.rationale: 'Stealthy Persistence' suggests attackers modify network/host configuration to evade detection and maintain access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to RDP service (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server): port changes, NLA bypass, or security layer disabling. Alert on netsh/PowerShell firewall rule additions opening RDP ports from unexpected subnets. Flag deletion or suspension of network monitoring tools.

suggestion.title: Windows Event Log Suppression and Forensic Artifact Wiping
suggestion.rationale: Stealthy campaigns clear logs post-compromise; ransomware actors eliminate traces before encryption to prevent forensic recovery
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wevtutil.exe or PowerShell Clear-EventLog execution targeting Security, System, or Application logs. Monitor for suspicious Event ID 104 (log cleared) without corresponding administrative task logging. Flag deletion of MFT, $Journal, and VSS snapshots via vssadmin or diskshadow.

suggestion.title: Fileless Code Execution via Memory-Resident Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Fileless Execution' as a primary attack mechanism, yet no detection use case covers in-memory code execution or absence of child process spawning from traditional executable locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution (e.g., shell interpreters, language runtimes) that lack corresponding mapped executable files on disk, or processes spawning without a parent-child relationship to on-disk binaries. Flag suspicious mmap/mprotect syscalls preceding code execution in developer tools.

suggestion.title: eBPF Program Loading and Kernel Hook Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly highlights 'eBPF Rootkit' as persistence/evasion mechanism. eBPF program attachment requires specific syscalls (bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD), bpf(BPF_MAP_CREATE), bpf(BPF_RAW_TRACEPOINT_OPEN)) that are detectable at syscall level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bpf() syscalls with BPF_PROG_LOAD or BPF_PROG_ATTACH operations originating from unprivileged processes or non-standard kernel monitoring tools. Correlate with elevated privilege acquire events immediately preceding.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Process Ancestry and Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Targets Developers' as the attack surface. Detection should focus on legitimate dev tools (IDEs, build systems, package managers) exhibiting anomalous behavior: spawning shells, making network connections to non-standard ports, or executing downloaded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by developers' common tools (gcc, python, npm, go, cargo, java) that are shell interpreters, curl/wget, or unsigned binaries. Correlate with network connections to non-standard C2 ports or uncommon ASNs from developer machines.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Kernel Exploit or Systemd Timer Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkit deployment typically requires root; title implies fileless execution, suggesting exploit or privilege escalation vector not covered. Should detect suspicious systemd timer creation, sudo abuse, or kernel module loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of systemd timer files in /etc/systemd/system or /usr/lib/systemd/system by non-root users, or unexpected sudo invocations from application contexts. Monitor auditd for privilege transitions preceding eBPF syscalls.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Dynamically Decoded Payload Execution in Developer Environments
suggestion.rationale: Fileless execution pattern typically involves base64/hex decoding, reflection, or dynamic library loading. Should detect shell commands containing decode chains, eval() patterns, or direct syscall invocation from interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell commands (bash, sh, zsh) containing base64/xxd/od decode piped to interpreter, or Python/Perl/Ruby one-liners with eval/exec. Flag processes executing code from environment variables, pipes, or process substitution without intermediate file artifacts.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon Activity from Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: RAT requires command-and-control communication. No use case addresses periodic outbound connections from dev tools or suspicious DNS queries for attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections on unusual ports (8080, 8443, 4444, custom ranges) from developer tools or new processes spawned by them. Flag DNS queries for newly registered domains from dev machines, or connections to IP space associated with known RAT infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from Unofficial Registries
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit developer dependency installation workflows. Article addresses why developer machines are targets—malicious packages are the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm, pip, nuget, maven installs for typosquatted package names (off-by-one character similarity to legitimate libraries), packages from non-canonical registries, or installs with explicit '--registry' flags pointing to attacker infrastructure. Alert on packages with zero download history or suspicious creation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Build Tool Execution with Network I/O
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines run build/CI processes. Compromised build tools or injected build steps represent execution mechanism for distributing malicious artifacts into supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag build tools (msbuild, gradle, make, bazel) spawning curl/wget/powershell for artifact download, writing to unexpected directories, or executing unsigned code. Alert on build processes with outbound network connections to non-business infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines store SSH keys, API tokens, cloud credentials, git credentials—all high-value targets. Credential theft enables lateral movement and persistence in supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.kube directories. Flag tools reading git credential helpers, npm token files, or environment variable enumeration. Alert on batch credential copying or exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Commits/Code Injection to Repository
suggestion.rationale: Once developer machine is compromised, attacker injects malicious code into source repository to poison the supply chain at origin. This is the persistence/impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git commits from compromised developer accounts outside normal working hours, unusual author metadata, commits that modify build files or add unexpected dependencies, or code changes introducing known malware patterns. Alert on disabled branch protection rules right before suspicious commits.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Developer Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromised developer credentials (especially with elevated access) enable lateral movement to internal infrastructure, private repositories, CI/CD systems, and cloud environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate login/API activity from developer machine source IP, then same user account accessing from non-developer infrastructure or unusual geographies. Alert on git operations (push/pull) from unexpected IP addresses, cloud resource access using dev credentials, or VPN/bastion access patterns.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Code or Credentials from Dev Machine
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exfiltrate proprietary code, private keys, or credentials from compromised developer machines to enable future attacks or sale on dark markets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large outbound data transfers from dev machines to non-business IPs, especially at off-hours. Flag connections to known malware C2 infrastructure. Monitor for compression of source directories, credential file transfers, or unusual DNS queries followed by data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Code Authorization Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors initiate the device authorization process themselves to generate a code, then trick targets into entering it'—core attack vector absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure AD device code flow authorization attempts, especially those followed by immediate API calls from anomalous IPs or followed by token reuse outside the claimed device context. Alert on high-velocity device code requests from single source.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Registration in Microsoft Entra
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access'—persistence mechanism requiring continuous monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registrations within 24 hours of suspicious OAuth token activity or device code flows. Flag registrations occurring outside business hours or from non-standard device types.

suggestion.title: Malicious Inbox Rules Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity'—exfiltration concealment indicator absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rules forwarding to external domains, deleting sensitive emails (HR/Finance keywords), or suppressing read receipts. Flag rules created within 12 hours of failed/succeeded MFA or device registration events.

suggestion.title: Attacker-in-the-Middle via Cookie Link Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mode 2: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens'—distinct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify logins where successful MFA is followed by subsequent actions (email access, Teams use, SharePoint queries) from different IP/user-agent within 30 minutes. Correlate with known proxy/CDN IP ranges indicating AitM interception.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Containing Device Code Portal Links
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'campaigns primarily targeted Microsoft 365 environments using phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal'—initial access detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails containing links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or obfuscated variants thereof. Alert on mass phishing campaigns with urgency-based pretexts (security alert, account review, consent request) leading to device code portal.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Usage Bypassing MFA Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access...without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges'—MFA bypass abuse pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OAuth token usage where token was issued via device code flow; alert if subsequent sensitive operations (rule creation, device admin elevation, app consent grants) bypass conditional access policies that normally require MFA.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 as exploitation vector for mass hijacking. No initial-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Ghost CMS instances matching known CVE-2026-26980 exploit payloads or vulnerable endpoints. Monitor for POST requests with parameter injection, unusual Content-Type headers, or script encoding patterns in versions prior to patch date.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Persistence via Backdoor/Shell
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sites 'hijacked' — implies persistence mechanism. No persistence-phase detection provided by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected files in Ghost content directories, anomalous Ghost database modifications, unauthorized admin user creation, or suspicious scheduled tasks on Ghost hosts. Baseline legitimate Ghost file hashes and detect deviations.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions sites hijacked 'for ClickFix Attacks' — requires detection of injected malicious content. Pipeline missed impact/delivery phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP responses from identified compromised Ghost sites containing ClickFix indicators: injected iframe elements, obfuscated JavaScript serving fake security warnings, fake browser notification prompts, or redirect chains to external domains.

suggestion.title: Mass Ghost CMS Compromise Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 700+ sites hijacked in coordinated campaign. No use case for detecting clusters of compromised instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ghost instances with identical injected content signatures, unusual cert issuance patterns, or synchronized infrastructure changes. Flag rapid clusters of Ghost version downgrades or simultaneous admin panel access from attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Process Injection into System Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RemotePE as 'memory-only RAT'—implicit indicator of in-process execution without disk artifacts. Requires detection of code injection into svchost, lsass, or other privileged processes. Article phrase: 'memory-only RAT'.
