suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious DLL loading into system processes; monitor for VirtualAlloc followed by WriteProcessMemory patterns; alert on process creation with mismatched parent-child relationships indicating injection.

suggestion.title: Lazarus-Attributed Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: RAT deployment inherently requires C2 channel; article specifies threat actor as Lazarus, implying known or attributable infrastructure. No IOCs returned despite 'Lazarus Deploys' in title. Requires network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to known Lazarus-attributed C2 domains/IPs; alert on non-standard ports from financial/crypto hosts; detect encrypted traffic patterns consistent with RAT beaconing.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Keylogging or Input Capture
suggestion.rationale: Financial and crypto firm targeting indicates credential theft motivation. Memory-only RAT designed for persistence and credential harvesting in sensitive environments. No detection built for capture mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious API calls (GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx, GetKeyboardState); detect unusual hook installation; alert on credential manager access or LSA secret dumps.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Targeting of financial and crypto firms indicates data exfiltration objective. Memory-only execution suggests data is processed and moved without visible staging. Should detect bulk data reads from sensitive locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large sequential file reads from wallet directories, trade databases, or credential stores; monitor for data compression followed immediately by network transmission; alert on unusual outbound data volumes from finance-tier hosts.

suggestion.title: LOLBAS Execution for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT with crypto/finance targeting likely requires lateral movement across secure network segments. Article does not describe initial compromise vector; assume use of legitimate tools to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abuse of psexec, wmic, or rundll32 for remote execution; detect unusual parent-child process chains (e.g., explorer.exe spawning powershell); alert on SMB traffic associated with lateral movement tools.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Command Execution and Script Loading
suggestion.rationale: No mention of delivery mechanism in article, but financial sector targeting and memory-only profile suggest living-off-the-land tactics. PowerShell is standard vector for Lazarus in financial attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell ScriptBlock logging; detect obfuscated command lines; alert on reflective DLL injection via PowerShell; flag base64-encoded payloads and string escaping patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Public Registries
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates attack 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — malware delivered through package installation. No detection logic for unusual or newly-created packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of npm install, pip install, or cargo install commands followed by child process spawning with suspicious command-line patterns or network connections. Flag installations from newly-created or low-reputation packages in public registries.

suggestion.title: Credential Access Post-Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing malware' — malware payload should harvest credentials after execution. Pipeline missed credential-access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection, LSASS access, or browser process manipulation originating from child processes spawned by package managers. Monitor for keylogging APIs, credential dumping utilities, or suspicious registry access to cached credentials post-installation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Package-Spawned Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware requires exfiltration or C2 callback. Title mentions malware distribution but no IOCs or C2 domains extracted. No detection for command-and-control communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline outbound connections from package manager processes and child processes. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains or IP connections to non-standard ports initiated by child processes spawned within 60 seconds of package installation.

suggestion.title: Multi-Registry Package Manager Supply Chain Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' as three simultaneous attack vectors. Pipeline should correlate cross-registry compromise signals and flag coordinated poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create alert for detection of similar malware signatures or command-and-control infrastructure detected across multiple package manager ecosystems within same timeframe. Flag package versions with identical embedded payloads published to npm AND PyPI AND CratesIO.

suggestion.title: Package Installation Triggering Unexpected Subprocess Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain payload requires execution step. Package managers normally only download/extract. Any subprocess spawning from install process is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any child process spawned by npm, pip, cargo, or their child processes during package installation phase. Baseline legitimate post-install hooks and flag deviations. Focus on spawns of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, curl, wget.

suggestion.title: Modification of Package Dependencies or Lock Files
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often achieve persistence by modifying dependency specifications. No detection for package.json, requirements.txt, or Cargo.toml tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to package manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, setup.py) outside of developer IDEs/git commits. Detect file write events from non-standard processes modifying dependency specs.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Export by Unauthorized Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'breached 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment' and 'stolen over 600,000 records...after breaching 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment.' No detection rule exists to catch mass record exports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk export operations (BulkDataLoadJobStateChange, BulkDataLoadJob) originating from non-standard user, IP, or time window. Correlate with >50k record exports or >500MB data size. Baseline normal franchisee data export patterns first to avoid FP on legitimate operations.

suggestion.title: Salesforce User Credential Compromise - Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attackers moved from 'certain 7-Eleven systems' to Salesforce environment, indicating credential harvesting or session hijacking: 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems...later [breached] 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce login from IP addresses or user agents inconsistent with historical baselines for that user. Flag logins immediately before or during bulk export operations. Alert on concurrent logins from same user in different geographic regions within short time window.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Registration and Data Publication by ShinyHunters
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay a ransom.' Network and DNS telemetry should capture infrastructure creation and data posting activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known ShinyHunters leak site infrastructure and Tor exit nodes. Alert on internal hosts establishing connections to known ShinyHunters infrastructure post-compromise. Monitor threat intelligence feeds for 7-Eleven or franchisee-related mentions on ShinyHunters public leak site or chat channels.

suggestion.title: Initial Access - Trusted Relationship Exploitation or Credential Compromise to 7-Eleven Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' on April 8 provides initial foothold before Salesforce breach. Vector unclear but likely T1199 or T1078.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication anomalies to 7-Eleven franchisee document storage system: logins from unusual IPs, times, or user roles. Detect credential stuffing or spraying against known Salesforce admin accounts. Baseline normal franchisee system access patterns; alert on deviations preceding April 8, 2026.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Extortion Communication - Threat Actor Contact
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility for the attack on April 17' and 'company refused to pay a ransom.' Email, dark web communication, or threat notification should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on receipt of emails from known ShinyHunters contact addresses or domains. Monitor dark web for mentions of 7-Eleven company name or executives combined with 'ransom' or 'payment' terms. Alert on suspicious domains registered post-breach with company name in registrant or WHOIS.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Aura Campaign - Targeted SaaS Account Compromise Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers for the past year...Salesforce Aura data theft attacks.' Specific campaign targeting pattern that should alert on similar Salesforce customer breaches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce orgs where shared login credentials appear in breaches. Detect Salesforce API token creation in bulk (>5 per hour) or token usage from non-standard clients. Monitor for authentication service enumeration (T1087) in Salesforce followed by bulk record queries.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Internet-Facing Vulnerable Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly centers on 'Internet-Facing Flaws' and 12-hour patching urgency. Should detect scanning/enumeration and exploitation attempts against exposed services before patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual connection attempts to known-vulnerable service ports (web servers, RDP, SSH on non-standard ports). Correlate inbound exploit signatures or suspicious HTTP User-Agents with rapid-fire requests spanning multiple destinations in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Vulnerability Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'AI-Assisted Attacks.' Should detect automated scanning patterns consistent with LLM-driven reconnaissance probing for internet-facing asset inventory and vulnerability discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag high-volume, pattern-varied HTTP requests from single source IPs with LLM-characteristic request spacing/timing (consistent intervals, diverse payloads, minimal delay between probes). Detect enumeration of common web paths (/admin, /debug, /.git) at scale.

suggestion.title: Rapid Patch/Update Deployment Failures or Delays
suggestion.rationale: CERT-In recommends 12-hour patching SLA. Should monitor for systems that fail to apply security patches within SLA windows or that remain unpatched post-advisory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch deployment events and cross-reference against vulnerability advisories. Alert when internet-facing assets remain unpatched >12 hours post-CERT-In advisory. Correlate with failed update logs or rollback events.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Polymorphic Exploit Payloads
suggestion.rationale: AI-assisted attacks imply adaptive/polymorphic evasion. Should detect exploit attempts using randomized or obfuscated payloads to evade signature-based defenses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDS alerts for exploit attempts with non-deterministic payloads (XOR encoding variations, randomized shellcode, polyglot executables). Detect encoding/obfuscation patterns within HTTP POST bodies targeting known-vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Vishing Attack Against Employee Identity Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' No detection proposed for inbound vishing or post-vishing account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PBX/telephony logs indicating inbound call to employee + Entra sign-in from new device/geography within 30 minutes. Alert on Entra account showing: (1) first successful sign-in after 18:00 local time, (2) high-risk sign-in without MFA enforcement, (3) immediate password reset or MFA re-registration post-vishing window. Flag repeated vishing patterns: same caller ID targeting multiple employees.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Customer Record Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors used this access to export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance.' No UC for detecting mass CRM data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce for single user/API token exporting >5K records in 1-hour window or running bulk-export reports containing full customer datasets (names, emails, phone, address fields). Baseline typical export volume per role; alert >10x baseline. Correlate with first-time or unusual IP/device access to Salesforce within 2 hours of Entra compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Detect SaaS Lateral Movement from Single Compromised SSO Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After gaining access to a corporate SSO account, the threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox, and many others.' Pipeline missed multi-SaaS access pattern from single compromised identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create SaaS access baselines by user role. Alert if single user account accesses >4 distinct SaaS platforms (Salesforce, Slack, Google Workspace, SAP, Adobe) within 60 minutes, especially if user role typically accesses <2 SaaS applications. Correlate with Entra risk signal (unusual sign-in) and OAuth token grants to unfamiliar apps.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration of Customer Support Ticket Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actor also claims to have stolen customer support ticket data.' Second exfiltration vector (support platform) not represented in any detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor support ticketing system for bulk ticket retrieval via API or UI export by single user in <1 hour window. Alert on non-support-agent roles accessing tickets or retrieval of customer PII patterns (email, phone, address fields) at scale. Baseline typical ticket access per agent; flag >500% baseline deviation.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Leak Site Upload by Extortion Group
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions ShinyHunters posting Charter on 'ShinyHunters data leak site' with threat to release if ransom not paid. No detection proposed for data appearing on known breach forums or leak sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor known ShinyHunters and general data leak sites (manual or via threat intelligence feeds) for mention of organization name, customer record datasets, or Salesforce instance indicators. Correlate timing: 40M customer record collection ~April 1, public leak listing shortly after. Alert SOC on detection and cross-reference with internal exfiltration timeline.

suggestion.title: Detect Extortion Threat Communication from Threat Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters extorting Charter...threatened to leak stolen data unless a ransom is paid' and 'ShinyHunters claimed to BleepingComputer that they breached Charter.' Pipeline missed communications/threat notifications as impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if Security/IR team receives unsolicited communications (email, contact form, messaging platform) from threat actors claiming breach and demanding ransom. Capture all metadata: sender domain, routing, attachments (proof-of-data evidence). Cross-reference claimed stolen records/access method with recent Entra and SaaS audit anomalies. Escalate to senior IR and executive leadership immediately.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Binary Execution or Shell Spawning on Edge Router
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'custom Linux implant' deployed—implies malware execution. Should detect anomalous process spawning on router hardware (Cisco ASR, Juniper MX, Fortinet, etc.), especially shell interpreters or unsigned binaries from /tmp or memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Edge routers have minimal legitimate process creation. Flag any /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or /bin/ash spawning from non-root accounts or unusual parent processes. Detect binary execution from /tmp, /dev/shm, or memory-resident code. Baseline vendor-signed processes and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Module or Init.d Persistence on Router
suggestion.rationale: Custom Linux implant requires persistence mechanism. Article implies long-term compromise—detect modifications to /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, /lib/modules, or cron jobs establishing backdoor callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to boot-time execution paths and scheduled task configs on router appliances. Unexpected .so/.ko files in /lib/modules or new entries in /etc/cron.d are high-fidelity indicators. Baseline vendor-installed modules and alert on additions post-deployment.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Router to Suspicious Destination
suggestion.rationale: Implant requires command-and-control channel. Article implies external callbacks—detect encrypted or obfuscated outbound connections from router management interfaces to non-RFC1918 addresses on non-standard ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline router egress (NTP, DNS, syslog). Flag TLS connections on 443/8443/custom ports to rare or newly-seen external IPs. Detect high-entropy encrypted traffic or DNS queries for infrastructure domains from router IP ranges. Use reputation scoring and volume anomalies.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Public Edge Router Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly targets 'edge routers'—implies exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities (RCE, auth bypass, or supply-chain compromise). Should detect exploit attempts or anomalous access to router admin interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to router management ports (443, 8080, 8443) for known CVE payloads (RCE patterns, overflow signatures, SQLi). Flag failed auth followed by successful access to same router within minutes. Detect requests without proper authentication headers to default admin URIs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Backup or Credential Extraction from Router
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-router compromise in Southeast Asia, implying lateral movement or data harvesting. Should detect bulk config exports, running-config reads, or credential dumps from routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 'show running-config' or 'show startup-config' commands outside scheduled backups. Flag SFTP/SCP transfers of .bin, .cfg, .conf files from router to external or atypical IPs. Detect Netconf/YANG bulk queries or SSH command sequences that enumerate device state.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Asset Exposure — LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references template substitution with this CVE. Canonical detection for CISA KEV entries with federal remediation deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match CVE-2026-48172 against vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory. Flag all LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin instances, prioritizing those unpatched before federal due date 2026-05-29. Correlate with exposed cPanel service ports (2083/2087/2086).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unprivileged cPanel User to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be abused by any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—directly describes the privilege escalation attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unprivileged cPanel user processes (UID > 1000) spawning root-level child processes (UID 0). Detect invocations of sudo/su from cPanel context without legitimate privilege escalation chain. Flag anomalous privilege transitions from cPanel user to root.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution as Root from cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—the actual operational exploitation payload distinct from the escalation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for script interpreters (bash, sh, perl, python) executing with root privileges (UID 0) where parent process or execution lineage traces to cPanel user session. Flag unexpected root-level script execution patterns that deviate from normal cPanel operations.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attacks Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Imperva has observed over 15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites' actively exploiting CVE-2026-9082. Real-time detection of these in-flight attacks is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal installations for SQL injection payloads in query parameters and POST bodies targeting the database abstraction API. Alert on UNION-based, time-based, and boolean-based SQLi signatures: SELECT, --, /*, UNION, SLEEP(), BENCHMARK() and URL-encoded variants (%27, %23, %2F).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Drupal Version Detection and Asset Inventory Gap Closure
suggestion.rationale: Shadowserver identifies 'nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online,' mostly in North America (272) and Europe (273). Version fingerprinting via HTTP headers is the fastest remediation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query HTTP responses from Drupal instances for X-Generator header, meta generator tags, CHANGELOG.txt exposure, or UPGRADE.txt disclosures revealing version strings pre-dating the CVE-2026-9082 patch. Cross-reference with CISA KEV timeline and patch release dates to identify unpatched exposures.

suggestion.title: Post-SQLi Privilege Escalation via Rapid Drupal User/Role Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article warns exploitation can lead to 'privilege escalation.' Detect anomalous user role changes correlating with SQL injection activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate detected SQL injection attempts with subsequent modifications to drupal.users_roles, drupal.users (admin flag), and drupal.role tables. Flag rapid admin account creation (>1 per minute following SQLi attempts) or permission elevation to admin role from non-admin user context.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SQL Injection Database Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns of 'information disclosure' as exploitation impact. SQL injection enables arbitrary SELECT queries on sensitive Drupal and business tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for unusual SELECT statements from Drupal application context targeting users, passwords, secrets, or custom business data tables. Flag enumeration patterns: LIMIT with incrementing offsets, wildcards in WHERE clauses, repeated failed queries probing table existence via error messages.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL Injection via Web Shell Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can potentially lead to remote code execution.' Detect .php/.sh file creation in Drupal writable paths or shell command execution from web context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After SQL injection detection, monitor for .php, .phtml, .sh file creation in Drupal-controlled directories (sites/default/files, modules/, themes/, var/lib/drupal/). Also detect process spawning from web server UID (www-data, apache, nginx) with shell invocation (bash -c, sh -i, nc reverse shell patterns).

suggestion.title: Vertical-Targeted Drupal Exploitation in Gaming and Financial Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attacks are primarily targeting Gaming and Financial Services sites so far, at collectively almost 50% of all attacks.' Priority-tier these verticals in detection tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Lower alert thresholds for SQL injection detection rules on Drupal instances tagged to Gaming and Financial Services business units. Correlate attack source IPs with hosting provider reputation feeds (bullet-proof hosters, bulletproof proxies) and add geographic/ASN context to identify organized campaign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: XWiki ssx/jsx Path Traversal Parameter Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'XWiki Platform has path traversal via resources parameter in ssx and jsx endpoints when using leading slash'—pipeline should detect GET/POST requests to /bin/ssx or /bin/jsx endpoints where the resource parameter contains directory traversal sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to XWiki ssx or jsx endpoints (/bin/ssx/*, /bin/jsx/*) where the 'resource' URL parameter contains directory traversal sequences: ../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f, or leading /.. patterns. Prioritize requests targeting protected paths like WEB-INF.

suggestion.title: XWiki Configuration File Disclosure via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article provides concrete exploitation proof-of-concept: 'http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false'—specific detection should identify attempts to read sensitive XWiki configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to XWiki ssx/jsx endpoints with resource parameters pointing to xwiki.cfg, xwiki.properties, or WEB-INF/* paths. Flag successful HTTP 200/302 responses as likely configuration file disclosure.

suggestion.title: XWiki Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions: '18.0.0-rc-1, 17.10.3, 17.4.9, 16.10.17'—any version below these thresholds remains vulnerable. Pipeline should identify and inventory vulnerable instances via banner disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XWiki HTTP responses leaking version information in headers, footers, or admin endpoints. Flag versions lower than the patched releases (16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.0-rc-1) as CVE-2026-23734 exposure.

suggestion.title: Directory Traversal in Web Application Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism relies on directory traversal sequences: 'resource=/../../WEB-INF/'—generic detection should catch similar patterns across web applications to identify broader exploitation campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests where URL parameters contain directory traversal patterns (../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f) combined with attempts to access protected directories (/WEB-INF, /etc, /config, /windows). Correlate across endpoints and applications.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated POST to /wikis/{wikiName} Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks' — primary attack vector but no use case generated despite clear initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to /wikis/{wikiName} or /wikis/* endpoints where authentication headers are missing, invalid, or expired. Flag requests containing binary payloads (XAR archives) or multipart form data from external/untrusted sources. Baseline legitimate API consumers to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: XWiki Vulnerable Version Detection (CVE-2026-33137)
suggestion.rationale: Article's own 'Recommended hunts' section references 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' template but pipeline generated zero use cases; vulnerable versions explicitly listed (16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1 patch thresholds).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference XWiki instance version discovery (via web fingerprinting, version response headers, or banner grabbing) against vulnerable patch versions. Alert on 16.x, 17.x, or 18.x instances below specified patch levels. Prioritize internet-facing assets.

suggestion.title: File Hash IOC Match: SHA1 4b7b95b79256374d487e9ece1dc48f527966990f
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'Recommended hunts' section explicitly lists 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' template with SHA1 marked 'high-fidelity' but pipeline IOC extraction output is empty; this template-based detection should have auto-generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alerts on file hash matches (SHA1: 4b7b95b79256374d487e9ece1dc48f527966990f) across all endpoints. Correlate file presence/transfer with XWiki process execution or HTTP POST requests to /wikis/ endpoints. Flag as delivery/execution of CVE-2026-33137 XAR payload.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Document Creation/Modification in XWiki
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'allowing an unauthenticated attacker to create or update documents in the target wiki' — execution/impact phase but no use case captures unauthorized document operations despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor XWiki application/database audit logs for document creation or modification events with missing, invalid, or NULL user authentication context. Correlate with preceding POST /wikis/{wikiName} requests lacking valid session tokens. Flag document property changes and new page creation from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Elevated Authentication Failure Rate - GitHub Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Authentication Issues Denying Access.' Pipeline generated zero UCs for auth failure spikes despite this being the core impact signal: 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline GitHub authentication failure rate per organizational tenant. Alert on deviation >3σ above normal within 15-min window. Correlate failure codes (401, 403, invalid_token) with scope of affected users/services to distinguish service-wide outage from targeted attack.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions CI/CD Execution Denial Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Denying Access to Actions'—GitHub Actions is the CI/CD platform. Pipeline failed to generate detection for widespread action execution failures. Phrase 'Authentication Issues Denying Access to Actions' directly establishes this gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow runs for systematic auth-related failure patterns (workflow.runs.conclusion=failure + auth error in logs). Alert on spike in failed OIDC token validations or actions/checkout failures correlated across multiple repositories within same time window.

suggestion.title: Service Availability Loss - GitHub API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title 'GitHub Down' signals availability impact. Pipeline generated no availability-focused detection despite high severity. Phrase 'GitHub Down' establishes need for service health monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API endpoint response codes (api.github.com, actions.github.com) for sustained elevation in 401/403/5xx responses. Alert when percentage of failed auth-related requests (401/403) exceeds 10% of baseline for ≥5 min. Cross-reference with GitHub status page for validation.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token / PAT Revocation or Invalidation Event
suggestion.rationale: Authentication denial could stem from token mass revocation or invalidation. Article does not specify root cause ('Authentication Issues') but token lifecycle events are critical detection gap for auth failures.
log_sources: GitHub personal access token audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass token revocation events or unexpected token expiration patterns in GitHub token audit logs. Track applications/users attempting API calls with invalidated PATs/OAuth tokens. Correlate token invalidation timestamps with auth failure spikes.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980'; pipeline extracted zero vulnerability or exploitation indicators despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS instances for HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoints with payloads consistent with CVE-2026-26980 exploitation. Flag POST requests to admin API with authentication bypasses or malformed parameters. Alert on 401/403 spikes followed by successful admin API calls from same source.

suggestion.title: Malicious Theme/Template Injection in Ghost CMS
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'poison 700 websites' indicates code implantation at scale; no persistence or injection use case generated despite clear post-exploitation code placement requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/modification in /content/themes/ directories outside scheduled maintenance. Flag theme files containing base64-encoded payloads, obfuscated JavaScript, or external domain references. Alert on template files with non-standard Handlebars syntax or suspicious eval() calls.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Distribution via Compromised Ghost Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ClickFix Malware'; pipeline extracted zero malware family indicators, delivery mechanisms, or payload signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix-pattern browser notification abuse: injected code requesting notification permissions, fake browser update prompts, or redirect chains to malware distribution sites. Monitor for injected script tags pointing to known ClickFix C2 or dropper infrastructure. Alert on HTML pages with notification-abuse JavaScript variants.

suggestion.title: Bulk Ghost CMS Vulnerability Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain required identifying 700+ vulnerable Ghost instances; no reconnaissance phase mapped despite implied scanning/enumeration step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk requests to Ghost fingerprinting endpoints (e.g., /ghost/api/v3/admin/version, sitemap.xml, robots.txt) from single or closely-timed IPs. Alert on high-volume requests to Ghost administrative paths with low success rates. Correlate IP geolocation data with known mass-scanning infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Credential Compromise or API Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale code injection requires valid admin access or token theft; phrase 'poison' suggests in-situ modification rather than defacement. Pipeline missed credential or session abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost admin login logs for successful authentications from unusual geographies or newly-seen IPs. Detect API tokens with 'admin' scope generated outside normal business windows. Alert on modifications to theme/settings via API without matching UI session logs. Flag password resets or token regenerations during exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Detection: MiniFast/MiniJunk Lures
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'phishing' as delivery vector ('Iranian Hackers Deploy MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 via Phishing and SEO Poisoning'). Zero phishing-related detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound emails with MiniFast or MiniJunk malware signatures, suspicious attachment types from external senders, or links redirecting to malware distribution infrastructure. Correlate with proxy logs for click-through patterns to malicious pages.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Attack Landing Page Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'SEO Poisoning' as explicit initial vector but zero web-based phishing/malware hosting detections present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS requests originating from search-engine referrers to newly-registered or compromised domains. Correlate high-ranked search results with subsequent malware execution indicators on requesting endpoints.

suggestion.title: MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malware families explicitly named in title but no process-execution, file-write, or behavioral detections generated for payload deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation matching MiniFast/MiniJunk behavioral signatures, unusual spawning from Downloads or TEMP directories, or parent-child process anomalies following email/browser interaction.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Dropper-to-Payload Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Two distinct malware names indicate multi-stage delivery but no behavioral correlation for staged execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser/document-handler spawning system executables with network beaconing to attacker infrastructure within 10-minute window. Flag TEMP file creation followed by execution.

suggestion.title: C2 Domain/IP Communication for MiniFast/MiniJunk Families
suggestion.rationale: Implication that deployed malware requires C2 infrastructure ('Deploy') but zero command-and-control detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network flows for known MiniFast/MiniJunk C2 servers. Alert on periodic beaconing, anomalous port usage, or encrypted tunneling from user endpoints.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'used it in ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution' using hardcoded machine keys—core attack vector at initial access requiring HTTP request-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ASP.NET applications for HTTP POST requests with suspicious __VIEWSTATE parameters (unusually large, nested object structures, known gadget chains). Alert on requests containing base64-encoded .NET serialized objects sent to .aspx handlers. Correlate with application exceptions referencing ObjectStateFormatter deserialization failures or VIEWSTATE signature validation errors.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Web Shell In-Memory Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actor deployed '.NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)' after RCE—requires detection of web shell execution patterns and memory-resident malware in IIS worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning from w3wp.exe (ASP.NET worker) initiating cmd.exe or powershell.exe with command-line arguments. Monitor for suspicious .NET reflection APIs (System.Reflection.Emit) invoked from w3wp memory. Alert on HTTP POST requests to .aspx endpoints that result in immediate command execution followed by HTTP 200 responses containing command output.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Injection into Web Application Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin'—requires file modification detection on web server for defense evasion and social engineering setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application directories for unexpected modifications to .js, .html, .css, .aspx files, especially those introducing new script tags, external loads, or user interaction prompts. Alert on file writes to web-accessible paths by w3wp.exe with content containing suspicious keywords: 'plugin', 'download', 'authenticate', 'security update'.

suggestion.title: Fake Installer Distribution from Compromised Web Property
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious JavaScript convinced users to 'download a fake installer, which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon'—requires detection of social engineering payloads and atypical executable downloads from internal web properties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users receiving system security or plugin update prompts from internal web properties (KnowledgeDeliver LMS). Alert on .exe downloads from web application servers to user endpoints, especially with filenames suggesting installers or security tools. Correlate downloads with HTTP response timestamps matching JavaScript modification indicators.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states fake installer payload infected machines 'with a Cobalt Strike beacon, essentially planting a backdoor' with organization-specific encryption—requires endpoint and network detection of beacon execution and C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cobalt Strike beacon indicators: rundll32.exe with .tmp/.scr files, suspicious memory injections into svchost.exe or explorer.exe, HTTP POST requests with unusual User-Agent strings and suspicious URIs (/submit, /download). Alert on DNS requests from user endpoints to attacker-controlled domains paired with HTTPS traffic on non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 50050).

suggestion.title: Hardcoded ASP.NET Machine Key Exposure in web.config
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys across multiple customer deployments' in 'standardized web.config file provided by the vendor'—requires proactive detection of exposed cryptographic keys before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan ASP.NET web.config files for hardcoded machineKey elements containing fixed validationKey and decryptionKey attributes. Alert on identical machine key values across multiple deployments or systems (indicating shared pre-shared keys). Cross-reference with KnowledgeDeliver deployment versions and patch status against CVE-2026-5426 (vulnerable before Feb 24, 2026).

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited'—this is initial-access phase. Pipeline found no UC to detect exploitation of the LMS vulnerability itself, despite this being the entry point for the entire chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LMS application logs for exploitation patterns typical of RCE vulnerabilities (e.g., suspicious query parameters, path traversal attempts, script injection in course materials). Correlate with HTTP 500 errors and subsequent suspicious process spawning from web service accounts. Focus on CVE patterns reported for KnowledgeDeliver versions in use.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Staging and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'Godzilla' specifically—a known webshell—yet pipeline extracted zero IOCs or execution detection logic. Article describes direct deployment post-exploitation, requiring execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Godzilla webshell staging via file write events from IIS/Apache worker processes to unexpected directories (webroot subdirs, temp folders). Look for process execution chains spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe from web service accounts (w3wp.exe, apache2, httpd). Correlate POST requests with unusual Content-Length values or multipart uploads to user-accessible LMS directories.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Deployment from LMS Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Cobalt Strike' as the second payload deployed. Pipeline found no detection use case for beacon execution, despite this being the command-and-control phase critical for persistence and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cobalt Strike beacon C2 traffic via network indicators: unusual outbound connections from web service processes, HTTPS/HTTP POST beacons with JARM fingerprints matching known Cobalt Strike profiles, or suspicious DNS queries from compromised LMS servers. Monitor for beacon-typical process injection patterns (rundll32, svchost spawning from web contexts). Flag DNS requests for known C2 domains associated with Cobalt Strike infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised LMS to Adjacent Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'deployment' of both Godzilla and Cobalt Strike post-exploitation, implying lateral movement potential from the LMS to internal infrastructure. Pipeline extracted no detection use cases for this phase despite high likelihood in education/enterprise LMS environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RPC traffic originating from LMS server IP to internal file servers, domain controllers, or classroom infrastructure. Detect pass-the-hash or NTLM relay attempts where credentials from LMS compromise are used to authenticate to adjacent systems. Flag lateral movement tools (psexec, wmiexec, smbexec) spawned from LMS-context processes.

suggestion.title: LMS Service Account Privilege Escalation or Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation scenarios typically require persistence beyond initial shell. Article does not specify persistence mechanism, but pipeline should have flagged detection logic for scheduled tasks, registry autoruns, or privilege escalation from LMS service account context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious scheduled task creation executed under LMS service account (e.g., w3wp.exe spawning schtasks.exe). Monitor registry for new run keys, startup folders, or WMI event subscriptions written by web service accounts. Flag UAC bypass attempts or token impersonation from LMS context to establish persistence.

suggestion.title: Multiple MFA Push Notifications in Short Timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'MFA Prompt Bombing' directly indicates attackers trigger repeated push notifications to exhaust user resistance. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts receiving >5 MFA push notifications within 60 seconds, particularly if from distinct geographies or device fingerprints. Correlate with subsequent successful MFA accept after flood. Alert on pattern: many rejections followed by unexpected approval.

suggestion.title: MFA Accept Following Repeated Failed Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Prompt-bombing attacks succeed when user accepts after fatigue; article premise is 'second factor isn't saving you' — directly implies successful auth post-bombing. No use case detected this acceptance-after-bombardment pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA push acceptance events immediately following 3+ rejected push attempts within 2 minutes. Baseline normal rejection rates per user; alert on deviations >2σ. Cross-reference with IP geolocation changes or impossible travel.

suggestion.title: Credential-Based Authentication Without Prior Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article context: attackers use MFA bombing after obtaining valid credentials via phishing/credential stuffing, then exploit user fatigue. Pipeline missed detection of the prerequisite: login attempts with valid credentials from anomalous context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful password authentication from IP/geography not associated with user baseline, immediately followed by MFA challenge (precondition for bombing). Alert on valid-credential login success before MFA step if attacker has phished credentials.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel Before MFA Bombing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often compromise credentials from one region, then trigger login from another to initiate MFA prompt sequence. Article doesn't explicitly state this but is implicit in attack flow. Zero use cases covered geolocation-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sign-in activity from IP address geographically inconsistent with user's recent login location, followed within 30 seconds by MFA challenge initiation. Flag as high-risk if origin IP is VPN/proxy or datacenter-hosted.

suggestion.title: MFA Method Downgrade or Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Prompt-bombing article title implies MFA 'isn't saving you' — suggests attackers may pivot to alternate MFA bypasses if push bombing fails (SMS fallback, email fallback). No detection for method-switching patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid MFA method switching within single authentication session: push notification rejected, then immediate fallback to SMS or email code. Alert if user's registered MFA methods are modified seconds before failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Bulk MFA Push Notifications Across User Population
suggestion.rationale: Campaign-level prompt-bombing attacks may target multiple users simultaneously using compromised credential list. Pipeline produced zero corpus-level or tenant-level detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate MFA push rejection counts across tenant. Alert if rejection rate across all users exceeds baseline by >3σ within 15-min window (indicates coordinated bombing campaign). Cross-reference source IP addresses for clustering.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Network Share Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Defender isolation is designed to 'limit attacker lateral movement.' This is the primary adversary behavior being defended. Detection should trigger before auto-isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify compromised endpoints executing lateral movement via SMB, WMI, or RDP by monitoring for suspicious credential usage across hosts, unexpected administrative share access (C$, IPC$, ADMIN$), or remote process execution from low-privilege contexts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via High-Volume Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'prevent impacts such as data exfiltration' as a key threat scenario. Early detection is needed before isolation containment activates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal egress patterns: large data transfers to external/non-whitelisted IPs, bulk reads of sensitive file repositories followed by network transmission, or access to cloud storage APIs from compromised hosts deviating from baseline.

suggestion.title: Ransomware File Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'prevent impacts such as ransomware propagation' as a primary defense goal. Detection should identify ransomware before it spreads via lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify mass file modification activity with encryption indicators: sudden appearance of new file extensions, high-frequency file rewrites in user directories, process behavior indicating cryptographic operations, or file-rename patterns consistent with encryption.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Network Share Enumeration and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Stop Ransomware Spread'—implies discussion of lateral movement mechanisms. Ransomware propagation via SMB/network shares (T1570, T1021.002) is the primary attack step that precedes device isolation triggers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential enumeration of network shares from a single host (\\*\IPC$, \\*\C$) followed by write attempts. Correlate with process creation showing legitimate tools (net.exe, wmic) or suspicious parent-child chains launching batch/PowerShell scripts.

suggestion.title: Mass File Encryption Activity (Ransomware Impact)
suggestion.rationale: 'Ransomware Spread' in title presupposes encryption execution phase (T1486). This is the observable that would trigger Defender's isolation mechanism described in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-velocity file operations (>100 writes/sec) where parent process is atypical for the directory (e.g., explorer.exe, svchost.exe writing to user data). Flag extension changes or multiple rewrites of the same file in <5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Device Isolation Triggered by Ransomware Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Core article feature: 'automatically isolates compromised devices.' Pipeline should detect the isolation event itself as high-signal indicator that MDE threat detection succeeded and containment initiated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any MDE device isolation event. Cross-reference isolation timestamp with preceding 10 minutes of DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceFileEvents for ransomware behavior (encryption, lateral movement tools, credential access).

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Process Parent
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Uses DLL Side-Loading'; standard MuddyWater tradecraft involves T1574.002 to execute malicious payloads without EDR detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LoadDLL events where a legitimate Windows binary (e.g., rundll32.exe, msiexec.exe, explorer.exe) loads a DLL from an atypical directory (AppData, Temp, Downloads, or subdirectories of System32 excluded from standard Windows installation). Alert on DLL imports from parent processes not whitelisted. Correlate with process command-line arguments that do not match expected usage patterns for that binary.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of 9-Country Targeting Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting '9 Countries'; campaign planning requires initial access vector establishment and network infrastructure setup specific to geographies or sectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for patterns of spear-phishing emails or social-engineering probes targeting organizations in the identified countries. Monitor for clusters of initial compromises within 48-72 hours preceding DLL execution, suggesting coordinated campaign timing. Flag email attachments with dual extensions (e.g., .pdf.exe) or embedded executables arriving in waves to multiple geographies.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Startup Folder or Registry Run Keys Following DLL Execution
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater campaigns consistently establish persistence after initial execution; DLL side-loading is typically stage-1 payload, followed by registry or filesystem hardening (T1547.001, T1547.009, T1547.014).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 5-10 minutes of suspicious DLL load from T1574.002 pattern, monitor for HKLM or HKCU registry writes to Run, RunOnce, Startup, or ShellExecute keys. Correlate file creation events in Startup folders (user or all-users) with the parent process from initial DLL side-load. Alert on scheduled task creation via schtasks.exe or TaskScheduler following execution.

suggestion.title: Command & Control via HTTP POST to Dynamically Generated Subdomains
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater's post-exploitation payloads use domain generation algorithms (DGA) or fast-flux infrastructure; espionage campaigns require exfiltration channels matching targeting profile (9 countries).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries from processes spawned by or loading DLLs in unusual locations, querying newly registered domains or subdomains under legitimate-looking parent domains. Flag HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with user-agent strings matching legacy Windows versions (e.g., WinHTTP/1.1 or custom agents without browser signatures). Correlate failed DNS resolutions followed by successful resolution to dynamically-allocated IPs within same ASN.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Compression Before Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaign against government/diplomatic targets requires collection and staging; MuddyWater historically uses rar.exe or 7zip for compression before C2 upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of compression utilities (7z.exe, rar.exe, winrar.exe, zip.exe) launched by or descended from processes that previously loaded DLLs from T1574.002 pattern. Flag archive creation in Temp, AppData, or user-accessible directories. Alert on parent process being system services (svchost.exe, spoolsv.exe, etc.) spawning compression tools—strong indicator of post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Credential Harvesting from Lsass or SAM Hives
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country targeting across government/diplomatic sectors implies credential access for horizontal movement; MuddyWater payload typically includes lsass dumping or SAM registry exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of procdump.exe, taskmgr.exe with debug flags, or rundll32.exe invoking ntdsutil.dll/samlib.dll against lsass.exe or system processes. Flag registry exports of HKLM\\SAM or HKLM\\Security via reg.exe or PowerShell registry snapshots. Alert on access to %systemroot%\\repair\\sam or volume shadow copies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Angular Language Service Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes extension-based RCE attack vector; no detection rule for extension install/activation patterns. Cannot cite specific phrase as article body is corrupted, but premise is implicit in 'Multiple Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code or development environment logs for unexpected Angular Language Service extension installation, activation, or version changes. Flag installations from non-official sources or with unsigned/untrusted publishers.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Angular Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly claims 'Enable RCE Attacks'; no detection rule for post-infection execution pattern. Kill chain must cover the exploitation/execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) from VS Code extension worker processes or from angular-language-service related binaries with unusual parent/child relationships.

suggestion.title: Malicious Angular Extension Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies command execution; no detection rule for command-line patterns or payloads injected via extension. Article body missing but title guarantees this attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual command-line arguments passed to processes spawned by Angular Language Service extension, including obfuscated PowerShell, encoded payloads, or network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious RDP Logon Volume and Geographic Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states ransomware 'uses RDP access'—initial-access vector that must be detected via brute-force patterns, non-standard hours, or geographic impossibilities
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP logon failures (Event 4625) exceeding threshold within 10-minute window, especially on port 3389. Alert on successful RDP logons from impossible geolocation deltas or outside business hours. Correlate failed attempts immediately preceding successful logon as brute-force success indicator.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Process Execution and File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'remote admin tools'—TeamViewer, AnyDesk, ConnectWise, and Splashtop processes are persistence mechanism; detect installation and spawning
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on execution of TeamViewer.exe, AnyDesk.exe, ConnectWise-labeled binaries, or Splashtop processes from %Temp%, AppData, or user Download folder. Detect file drops to ProgramFiles or ProgramData matching remote-tool signatures. Monitor for registry writes to HKLM\Run or scheduled-task creation linking to these tools.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence Modification for RDP or Backdoor Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stealthy persistence'—ransomware establishes auto-start via registry Run keys or scheduled tasks to survive reboot and ensure remote-tool survival
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKCU equivalents, or scheduled-task creation via schtasks.exe/WMI, especially when the targeted executable resides in non-standard path or is unsigned. Correlate registry writes with prior RDP logon or remote-tool installation.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Ransomware Encryption File Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is 'ransomware'—encryption phase exhibits sustained mass file writes, unusual extension changes (.encrypted, .locked, .nightspire), and rapid file open/write/close cycles
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process writing >1000 files in <5 minutes across \\* network shares or local drives. Flag file extension changes to known ransomware extensions or unknown extensions preceded by encryption-like permissions changes. Correlate with parent process svchost, rundll32, or explorer spawned from unusual working directory.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP Session Chaining
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates RDP access paired with remote tools—classic pattern for multi-stage lateral movement; detect sequential RDP logons host-to-host within internal network
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP logon where both source and destination are internal IPs, especially if source IP shows no prior RDP activity. Alert on source IP performing RDP logon to host A, then host A performing RDP to host B within 10 minutes. Correlate with remote-admin-tool execution on intermediate host.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: RDP Port or Firewall Rule Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'stealthy persistence'—attacker modifies RDP port (non-standard), disables Windows Defender, or removes firewall rules blocking inbound RDP to evade detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\PortNumber (non-3389 value). Alert on execution of netsh firewall delete rule or powershell Remove-NetFirewallRule targeting inbound RDP. Flag registry deletions of Windows Defender exclusions or DisableAntiSpyware = 1 writes.

suggestion.title: Fileless Scripting Engine Execution from Network Source
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'fileless execution.' Should detect shell/interpreter spawning without corresponding script files on disk or with suspicious parent processes typical of RAT payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh/python/perl spawned without a .sh/.py file reference in working directory or command line. Correlate with unexpected parents (curl, wget, mail, cron). Look for interpreters reading stdin from network sockets or /dev/tcp redirects.

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit BPF_PROG_LOAD via bpf() Syscall
suggestion.rationale: Title specifically names 'eBPF rootkit' as core capability. Should detect bpf() syscalls with BPF_PROG_LOAD operations attempting to install kernel-level hooks for persistence and evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on bpf() syscall with cmd=BPF_PROG_LOAD from unexpected processes. Look for attachment to kprobes on security functions (sys_execve, sys_open, sys_connect) or overwriting audit/security module entries. Cross-reference against kernel module load logs.

suggestion.title: RAT C2 Callback Detection via Process Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: RAT inherently requires command-and-control communication. Fileless delivery implies in-memory C2 logic triggering outbound connections from dev tools or system binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from bash/sh/python/curl/wget to non-standard ports (non-80/443) with no historical baseline. Alert on DNS queries to newly registered domains followed immediately by connection. Correlate with suspicious process lineage.

suggestion.title: SSH Key and API Token Exfiltration from Developer Homes
suggestion.rationale: Article targets developers, implying credential harvesting. Should detect reads/exfiltration of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, .env files, .docker/config.json, git credentials, or IDE token files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes (especially non-standard ones) reading from ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/*, or .env files in developer workspaces. Flag bulk reads across multiple credential paths in short timeframe. Cross-reference with network egress.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged Process Capability Elevation via eBPF
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkit allows privilege escalation and access bypass without traditional sudo/setuid. Should detect capabilities being granted to unprivileged processes after eBPF operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with uid < 1000 making bpf() syscalls or inheriting elevated capabilities/file descriptors post-eBPF load. Detect eBPF filters attached to security-critical syscalls (execve, connect, open) that could suppress audit logging.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Memory Region Writes via ptrace or /proc/mem
suggestion.rationale: Fileless execution often involves code injection into running processes. Should detect ptrace() or direct /proc/[pid]/mem writes from unexpected parents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ptrace(PTRACE_POKETEXT/PTRACE_SETREGS) or open(/proc/[pid]/mem) from processes without standard parent relationships. Correlate anomalous memory writes with subsequent unusual child process creation or network activity.

suggestion.title: DDoS Traffic Spike Detection via Network Volume Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'new AI DDoS attacks are smarter'—implies volumetric or behavioral anomalies. Pipeline generated no detection for abnormal traffic volume despite this being the core impact signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound traffic spikes exceeding 3-sigma of 30-day rolling mean, especially from distributed /24 CIDR blocks or from AS-paths not in historical baseline. Correlate with dropped packet counts and high RTT variance indicating congestion.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vector DDoS Attack Coordination (L3/L7 Hybrid)
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'smarter' attacks—implies adaptive/multi-stage tactics beyond single-vector floods. No UC generated for coordinated attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on temporal clustering of network-layer (SYN/UDP) floods concurrent with application-layer (HTTP/DNS) abuse from different source populations, suggesting command-orchestrated botnet activity.

suggestion.title: AI-Optimized Attack Pattern Recognition (Behavioral Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly invokes 'AI' making attacks 'smarter'—implies adversary is adapting payload/timing in real-time. Pipeline generated nothing on adaptive attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect entropy shifts in attack packet headers (TTL variation, window-size distribution, User-Agent diversity) and timing (inter-request intervals showing non-random patterns inconsistent with legit user behavior).

suggestion.title: Botnet Command & Control Beacon (Infrastructure Reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: DDoS campaigns require command infrastructure. Title context suggests organized attack campaign. Pipeline generated zero IOCs for botnet C2 or infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic DNS lookups to algorithmically-generated domains (DGA), fast-flux patterns, or connections to known botnet C2 IP ranges. Correlate with outbound traffic on non-standard ports (TCP 6667, 8080, 443 anomalies).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Non-Standard Repository
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines executing package install commands (npm, pip, cargo) are central to supply-chain compromise. Article premise is that dev machines are #1 target; installing packages is the mechanism attackers use to inject malicious code into the software supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager CLIs (npm, pip, pip3, cargo, apt) for installations from non-whitelisted registries, untrusted sources, or with unusual flags (--force, --unsafe-perm, --no-verify). Correlate with DNS/network telemetry to detect install commands pointing to suspicious hosts or typosquatted package names.

suggestion.title: SSH Private Key or Git Credential Access and Movement
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines hold unencrypted SSH keys and git credentials in ~/.ssh and ~/.git directories. Article frames dev machines as targets—stealing credentials grants attackers commit/push access to repositories, enabling code poisoning downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reads on ~/.ssh (private keys) and ~/.git/config (stored credentials). Flag scp, rsync, or network exfiltration of .ssh or .git directories. Alert on git credential invocations followed by network outbound connection, or git credential-store writes outside normal developer workflow.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized IDE Plugin or Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: IDEs are dev machine attack surface. Malicious IDE extensions can inject code into builds, exfiltrate credentials, or modify sources transparently. Article positions dev machines as primary target; plugins are persistent, trusted-context execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin installation directories (VS Code extensions folder, JetBrains plugins dir) for writes from unexpected processes or installer scripts. Flag plugin installs followed by unusual child processes or network calls. Baseline known-good plugins and alert on new/unsigned additions.

suggestion.title: Build Tool or Compiler Replacement or Hash Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Attackers target build pipelines on dev machines to inject malware at compile time. Article highlights dev machines as supply-chain weak point; compromising gcc, clang, javac, etc. poisons all downstream builds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain cryptographic signatures or hashes of build-tool binaries (/usr/bin/gcc, /usr/bin/clang, maven, gradle, cmake). Alert on file modifications, version downgrades, or unexpected child processes spawned by build tools. Monitor build tool binary execution from unusual parent processes or with suspicious arguments.

suggestion.title: Source Code Repository Cloned to Suspicious Location or with Unusual Flags
suggestion.rationale: Dev machines clone from internal repositories. Attackers may clone repos to exfiltrate source code or inject code via hooks. Article's supply-chain angle implies attacker goal is source code access or code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git clone / git fetch commands for unusual destination paths (outside standard workspace directories), bulk clones of multiple repos, or clones followed by immediate archive/compression. Flag clones with credentials embedded in URLs or from non-standard git servers. Correlate with lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Development Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Dev machines store API keys, tokens, and credentials in shell config files (.bashrc, .zshrc, env files). Article frames dev machine compromise as enabling downstream supply-chain attack; exfiltrating credentials unlocks repository, artifact, and build-infrastructure access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution of cat, grep, env, or printenv targeting shell configuration files, .env files, or AWS credential files. Flag exfiltration via scp, curl POST, or base64 encoding of credential-bearing files. Alert on credential exposure in process command-lines or environment-variable reads by non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Directing to Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers.' Core initial access vector for the campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with links to microsoft.com/devicelogin or variations targeting the device code portal. Correlate mass phishing campaigns with subsequent device code authorization events in same tenant/user context. Flag emails from external domains impersonating Microsoft infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Successful OAuth Device Code Grant with MFA Bypass Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Core credential access, the MFA bypass is the persistence value.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful device code authorization flows where the device is not registered to the user, or from foreign geolocations. Detect device code grants followed immediately by multi-application sign-ins without subsequent MFA prompts (MFA-bypass signature). Alert on bulk device code authorizations within 1-hour windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Outlook Inbox Rules Post-Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'In some of the attacks, attackers also...created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Direct persistence and defense-evasion tactic following token theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rule creation within 4 hours of device code authorization or suspicious sign-in. Flag rules that forward/redirect to external addresses, delete messages by criteria, or suppress notifications. Correlate rule creation with compromised session timeline and user baseline deviation.

suggestion.title: Unrecognized Device Registration in Azure AD/Entra Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Lateral movement and persistence through device trust relationships.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor device registration events for new enrollments within 2 hours of device code grant or suspicious sign-in activity. Alert on registrations from foreign geolocations or non-BYOD device types. Correlate new device registrations with subsequent conditional-access policy violations or unusual resource access patterns.

suggestion.title: Token-Based Access to SaaS Platforms Post Device Code Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat actors now have full access to all applications the user normally has access to via their single-sign-on account, including Microsoft 365, Salesforce, or any other cloud SaaS platforms.' Attacker pivots from email access to broader SaaS compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate OAuth tokens obtained via device code flow with subsequent logins to SaaS platforms (Salesforce, Slack, GitHub, etc.). Detect access to applications outside user baseline. Alert on impossible travel between Office 365 sign-in and SaaS platform access (different IPs/geolocations in short timeframe).

suggestion.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Cookie/Token Capture via Phishing Proxy (Cookie Link)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' Alternative attack mode with lower friction than device code in some scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication requests routing through attacker-controlled proxy infrastructure before Microsoft endpoints. Identify suspicious SSL/TLS negotiation patterns, certificate pinning violations, or known phishing proxy IP ranges. Implement Conditional Access policies to block cross-device auth transfers and restrict device code flows to corporate networks only.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Post-Exploitation Content Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 700+ hijacked Ghost sites; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or techniques for persistence. Hijacked sites require malicious template/theme injection to serve ClickFix popups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS admin API calls (`/admin/api/posts/`, `/admin/api/themes/`) for unauthorized POST/PUT operations by non-admin service accounts. Alert on rapid bulk modifications to post bodies or theme files, especially containing JavaScript obfuscation patterns or references to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Popup Delivery via Web Content Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions ClickFix attacks; no detection use case addresses the malicious popup execution or JavaScript injection mechanism used to trick site visitors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript payloads in HTTP responses containing ClickFix signatures: modal overlays with fake error icons, button elements with `onclick` handlers executing shell commands, or base64-encoded PowerShell execution patterns. Alert on unusual JavaScript file modifications to served web content.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Authentication Bypass or Credential Reuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: 700+ sites hijacked implies either bulk exploitation of a known auth bypass, credential stuffing, or privileged account compromise. Pipeline generated no detection for anomalous admin access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual login patterns to Ghost `/admin/` endpoints: logins from non-US geoIPs (if org is US-based), non-standard User-Agent headers, rapid-fire auth attempts from single IP across multiple domains, or login success followed immediately by POST to API endpoints that historically generate auth errors.

suggestion.title: Malicious Redirect Chain from Compromised Ghost Sites to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix attacks redirect victims to attacker-controlled domains for payload delivery. Article title implies 700+ redirect infrastructure but pipeline extracted zero C2 or redirect domain IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP redirects (301/302) from legitimate Ghost blog domains to suspicious external domains. Alert on patterns: known-good domain → typosquat/lookalike domain, or legitimate domain → IP-based redirect, or rapid redirect chain modifications on same domain within short time window.

suggestion.title: RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Execution via Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'memory-only RAT'—core evasion tactic. Pipeline generated zero execution detections despite this being primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process misalignment (e.g., Office/system process spawning suspicious unsigned child) with no corresponding PE file on disk. Monitor for VirtualAlloc→WriteProcessMemory→CreateRemoteThread chains from legitimate processes.

suggestion.title: Lazarus Phishing Delivery to Financial Sector
suggestion.rationale: RemotePE deployment against 'Financial and Crypto Firms' implies phishing precursor. Pipeline surface no initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect macro-enabled Office documents from external email; alert on DDE/VBA execution chains following attachment open. Correlate user-clicked phishing with downstream RemotePE indicators.

suggestion.title: Financial Data Staging & Exfiltration Post-Compromise
