suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware in supply chain typically targets application secrets stored in environment variables and dotenv files. Article implies broad credential theft — detection should specifically catch reads of .env files and environment variable access during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file read events of .env, .bashrc, .profile, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, and environment variable dumps (env, Get-ChildItem Env:, printenv) occurring within 10 seconds of npm/pip/cargo child process spawn, especially when followed by outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious URL Redirect from Chatbot Service
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users' — indicates initial access through chatbot compromised or manipulated to serve malicious links. No detection use case proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI chatbot recommendation logs for unusual or obfuscated URLs. Baseline expected domains and alert on deviations. Correlate chatbot-served URLs with subsequent user clicks and network connections to cryptocurrency infrastructure or unknown domains.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Execution Post-Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article states users are redirected to 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — malware must be executed on victim machines. No detection for malware execution or process anomaly was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cryptomining binaries (xmrig, monero variants, etc.) or suspicious processes with cryptocurrency pool connections. Look for process execution from browser temp folders or AppData shortly after suspicious URL clicks.

suggestion.title: Sustained High CPU/GPU Utilization After Web Activity
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking inherently consumes system resources. Article describes users being redirected to execute mining code. No resource anomaly detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user web activity (chatbot interaction + suspicious redirect) with sustained elevated CPU/GPU usage from background processes. Flag when resource spikes coincide with execution of unsigned or unsigned-but-legitimate binaries from unusual paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Pool Connection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking malware must communicate with mining pools. Article implies victims connect to attacker infrastructure. No C2/mining pool detection use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from user endpoints to known cryptocurrency mining pool IP ranges and domains (stratum, getwork protocol, monero-pool, etc.). Correlate with process execution of potential miners from suspicious paths.

suggestion.title: BIND 9 Vulnerable Process Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Resolvers and Authoritative Servers' exposed to 'Remote Exploits' — requires process monitoring for vulnerable BIND 9 versions running on name servers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BIND 9 process (named or bind) running on systems known to host DNS infrastructure. Correlate process start with version checks against published vulnerability advisories. Alert on versions matching vulnerable ranges in BIND 9 CVE disclosures.

suggestion.title: DNS Authority Query Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Authoritative servers are attack target — successful exploitation may manifest as unusual DNS responses, zone transfer attempts, or query patterns diverging from baseline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal DNS query patterns for authoritative name servers. Detect spikes in AXFR requests (zone transfers), queries for non-existent records, or responses with abnormal TTLs that may indicate compromise or DoS.

suggestion.title: BIND 9 Process Restart or Crash Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Remote exploits against DNS software often trigger process crashes or restart loops; article indicates active remote exploitation risk
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid BIND 9 (named) process termination and restart cycles within 5-minute windows on DNS infrastructure servers. Correlate with error logs indicating segmentation faults, out-of-memory conditions, or unexpected exits.

suggestion.title: DNS Resolver Response Poisoning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Compromised resolvers may inject malicious DNS responses; article identifies 'Resolvers' as attack surface, enabling potential DNS hijacking or traffic redirection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS responses from internal resolvers for CNAME/A record responses pointing to unexpected IPs not in IPAM. Compare resolver responses against authoritative sources for known domains; flag mismatches indicating potential cache poisoning.

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to BIND 9 Service Ports from Unusual Sources
suggestion.rationale: Remote exploits imply network-reachable BIND 9 instances; detect reconnaissance or exploitation attempts to port 53 (DNS) and potential control-plane ports from untrusted networks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound traffic to port 53 from external networks or suspicious internal subnets targeting systems running BIND 9. Correlate with IDS signatures for known BIND 9 exploit payloads (CVE-specific PoCs if available).

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection - cPanel LiteSpeed Redis Function Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability in 'lsws.redisAble function' enables 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' No detection logic provided for this core attack vector despite active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel JSON API audit logs and web server logs for HTTP requests containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' originating from external or unprivileged sources. Correlate with root-privilege process spawning events within 1-5 seconds. Any match indicates direct CVE-2026-48172 exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Forensic IOC Detection - Suspicious Redis Function Calls in cPanel Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit forensic command: grep -rE 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/ as detection signature. Pipeline did not surface this log pattern as an IOC despite being the primary detection method recommended by vendor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs for pattern 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble'. Extract and alert on source IPs. Cross-reference against authorized administrative IP allowlist; flag unexpected sources. Check system audit logs on matched timestamps for post-exploitation lateral movement or persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Plugin Inventory - LiteSpeed cPanel Versions v2.3-v2.4.4
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'vulnerability is being actively exploited' in 'all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4.' Pipeline did not extract or flag software version ranges despite CISA mandate to patch within 4 days.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query cPanel/WHM plugin directory and package managers to enumerate LiteSpeed plugin versions installed. Flag any installation within v2.3–v2.4.4 range for immediate alert and patch scheduling per CISA BOD 22-01 compliance. Feed results to vulnerability management system with critical priority.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Behavior - Root Process Spawning from cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers gain 'arbitrary scripts with root privileges,' meaning root-level processes spawn from cPanel context. No behavioral detection logic provided despite this being the execution phase indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is cPanel/WHM plugin (or lsws.redisAble-related process) and child process UID is 0 (root). Capture command-line and script content. Particularly sensitive to /bin/bash, /bin/sh, perl, python spawned with root after cPanel unauthenticated request.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution - cPanel Plugin Public Interface Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'remote attackers with no privileges' exploit plugin, contradicting assumption that cPanel requires authentication. No RCE-focused detection provided despite this being the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs on cPanel ports (typically 2082, 2083) for requests to unauthenticated JSON API endpoints containing Redis-related parameters. Alert on GET/POST to cpanel_jsonapi endpoints with no valid session cookie or auth header followed by execution-class HTTP response codes. Correlate with process audit events.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting and Homoglyph Package Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware abusing npm, PyPI, and OpenVSX; supply-chain attacks on package repos classically employ name-spoofing as initial-access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository APIs for new registrations with high string similarity to popular packages (Levenshtein distance ≤2, homoglyphs). Flag registrations by freshly-created accounts, then correlate with rapid-install attempts and unusual publisher geo.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Spawned by Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware distributed via packages executes upon install; detect non-standard child processes spawned by npm/pip or setup-script execution workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install, pip install, or postinstall scripts spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl/wget making network connections. Baseline normal package behavior per package name; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from Package Code or Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Developer-targeting malware steals SSH keys and API tokens; article's malware targets developers, which typically involves reading ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, and credential environment variables during or after install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of credential files (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.m2, .kube/config) or access to env-var strings matching credential patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET) during package install or import.

suggestion.title: Repository Account Compromise: Anomalous Package Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes abuse of GitHub, npm, PyPI, and OpenVSX; accounts must be compromised or tokens stolen to upload malicious packages; detect account takeover patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on account logins from new geo/IP followed by package uploads, rapid version bumps in same session, or package-upload + immediate deletion (test-and-exfiltrate pattern). Monitor for API token usage outside CI/CD time windows.

suggestion.title: Dependency-Chain Attack: Anomalous Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages may declare unused or obfuscated dependencies to pivot into other systems; flag dependency anomalies as persistence or second-stage-payload mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag packages with declared dependencies never imported in source, new-account dependencies, or transitive chains including multiple newly-registered packages. Alert on packages declaring heavy network/crypto imports inconsistent with package purpose.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm definition modification — suspicious Java payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text' but pipeline missed explicit detection for algorithm *modification* events. Core attack vector is algorithm replacement, not just process spawning. Article states: 'An authenticated user...can exploit this to achieve RCE via algorithm evaluation engine.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PUT/PATCH operations to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* where request body contains suspicious Java keywords (Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder, System.getRuntime, /bin/sh). Correlate with successful 200/204 responses and subsequent process spawning.

suggestion.title: ChangeMissionDatabase privilege grant or assumption — unauthenticated algorithm injection prep
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' as precondition. Pipeline missed detection of privilege escalation or lateral privilege assumption attempts targeting this role. Quoted: 'An authenticated user with the `ChangeMissionDatabase` privilege can exploit this.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect role/permission assignments granting ChangeMissionDatabase or algorithm-write privileges via API calls, LDAP modifications, or config changes. Especially alert on privilege grants to service accounts or non-human identities.

suggestion.title: Janino expression engine error/exception during algorithm evaluation
suggestion.rationale: Janino is the attack surface. Failed or malformed injections will produce compilation/runtime exceptions. Pipeline missed detection of abnormal JVM exception patterns tied to algorithm evaluation. Article highlights Janino as the vulnerable component but no exception-based hunt exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs or JVM error streams for Janino compilation failures, ClassCastException, InvocationTargetException, or java.lang.Runtime access denials during algorithm evaluation. High frequency of Janino errors followed by process spawn = exploitation.

suggestion.title: Authentication token/session hijacking to Yamcs API — unauthorized algorithm endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Delivery phase assumes an authenticated session. Pipeline did not suggest detection for session abuse or token theft used to modify algorithms. Article implies attacker must be 'authenticated' but method of obtaining creds is not detailed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication-to-exploitation time skew: successful login from unusual location/device, followed within minutes by algorithm PATCH requests from the same session token. Flag if session reuse across disparate source IPs.

suggestion.title: JVM crash or unplanned termination following algorithm execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payloads may destabilize the Yamcs JVM (memory exhaustion, infinite loops, or direct JVM termination). Pipeline missed impact detection. Article says RCE achieved but not whether attacks leave detectable fault signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected yamcs or java process exit codes, elevated exception rates in logs between algorithm PATCH and process termination, or rapid restart loops in process creation events. Correlate with suspicious algorithm modifications in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Account Suspension or Platform Ban
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Nightmare-Eclipse' as a Windows exploit researcher subject to GitHub + GitLab suspensions. No actor name or account-action event was extracted. Pipeline should flag platform bans as leading indicators of infrastructure disruption and potential tool/payload redistribution to alternate channels. Phrase: 'GitLab Suspends Windows Exploit Researcher Nightmare-Eclipse After GitHub Ban'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account suspensions, DMCA takedowns, or repository deletions targeting known exploit researchers and malware authors across development platforms. Track creation of new accounts, repos, or domains immediately post-suspension as potential evasion (re-registration, mirror sites). Correlate with malware artifact availability.

suggestion.title: Phishing links hosted on or redirected through Google legitimate domains
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Abuse Trusted Google Domains to Hide Phishing Links From Email Gateways'—the core attack is pivoting through Google's trusted infrastructure. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or detection logic for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing hyperlinks that resolve through or redirect from Google domains (docs.google.com, sheets.google.com, drive.google.com, etc.) but ultimately terminate at non-Google hostnames, especially those with low reputation or high-risk TLDs. Correlate click events with final destination classification.

suggestion.title: Email gateway bypass via legitimate domain redirect chains
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes evasion of email security controls—phishing links bypass gateways by using Google's whitelist status. No defense evasion techniques or gateway-specific detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateway allow-lists and proxy policies for redirect patterns: legitimate Google domain URLs that are initially scanned as safe but contain embedded or deferred redirects to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Alert on redirect-chain depth exceeding 2 hops from initial click.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Google Workspace features abused for phishing (forms, surveys, shortened URLs)
suggestion.rationale: Title and threat profile (hiding links from email gateways) suggest attackers likely abuse Google Forms, Surveys, or URL shorteners (goo.gl, etc.). No mention of abuse of specific Google Workspace primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with links to Google Forms, Google Surveys, or Google's URL shortening services that request credential entry or contain embedded phishing elements. Correlate with user responses to forms that request out-of-band credential submission.

suggestion.title: Unusual geographic or temporal patterns in Google domain link distribution
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns using trusted domains often follow targeting patterns. Pipeline did not generate any behavioral or campaign-based detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the volume and geographic distribution of unique Google domain links in inbound email. Alert when a specific Google domain or redirect pattern appears in >N emails within a T-minute window, or targets a specific department or business unit disproportionately.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WhatsApp Session Creation on iOS 16 Device
suggestion.rationale: Title states '0-Click Account Takeover'—attacker gains authenticated session without user action. Detection must flag session creation from new device/IP in absence of credential entry or MFA challenge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when WhatsApp account (phone-based identity) shows new session from previously unseen device fingerprint or geographic region within minutes of last legitimate activity, especially if no password reset or 2FA verification ceremony is logged. 0-click means session bypasses standard auth.

suggestion.title: iOS Memory Corruption Exploit Targeting WhatsApp Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies '0-Click' on iOS 16—implies memory safety bug or privilege escalation exploit in WhatsApp or iOS kernel. Detection should correlate device crash telemetry with subsequent unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag iOS 16 devices running vulnerable WhatsApp version with abnormal WhatsApp process terminations (crash logs indicating heap/buffer corruption) immediately followed by session creation from attacker-controlled IP. Cross-correlate version inventory with disclosed exploit scope.

suggestion.title: Bulk Message Transmission from Compromised WhatsApp Account
suggestion.rationale: Post-takeover, attacker controls account and can abuse contact list for phishing/lateral movement. Title implies full account control is achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid message volume spike to new/external recipients from WhatsApp account following session anomaly. Flag if target recipients are corporate domains, admin accounts, or finance/HR personnel. Baseline legitimate user's typical message cadence and recipient distribution.

suggestion.title: Contact List Exfiltration from Compromised WhatsApp
suggestion.rationale: With account control, attacker gains access to full contact list and encrypted message history. This supports further social engineering or targeting. '0-Click' takeover grants full account capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on full contact list download or bulk contact enumeration immediately after unauthorized session creation. Monitor for export/sync of contacts to external storage or API calls requesting entire contact database rather than interactive retrieval.

suggestion.title: Salesforce massive data export to external recipient
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stole over 600,000 records' and 'leaked a 9.4GB archive'. Bulk export of this scale from Salesforce would generate specific audit logs and unusual query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce for unusually large query results, API calls exporting >100k records, or SOQL queries spanning sensitive objects executed by service accounts or recently-provisioned users. Alert on downloads/exports >1GB in 24hr window or Salesforce to external IP transfers.

suggestion.title: Salesforce account compromise—anomalous auth and API activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized third party gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems' on April 8. Most probable vector is compromised credentials, session hijacking, or weak MFA controls on Salesforce service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Salesforce logins from unexpected geolocation or ISP on April 7-8, 2026. Alert on API authentication via bearer tokens from new/suspicious sources. Monitor for disabled MFA or password resets on service/admin accounts in 48hr before April 8.

suggestion.title: Extortion demand and ransom communication detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility...April 17' and 'leaked a 9.4GB archive...after the company refused to pay a ransom'. Ransom communications are standard in extortion attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email and messaging for extortion demands naming 7-Eleven breach, payment instructions, or dark web URLs. Detect communications referencing specific exfil artifacts (9.4GB, 600k records, franchisee documents). Track ransom wallet addresses and payment attempts.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters dark web leak site data publication tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site'. Pipeline should surface ShinyHunters infrastructure and track new victim postings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor known ShinyHunters leak domain(s) for new victim postings, file sizes, record counts, and metadata. Cross-reference Have I Been Pwned data dumps with Salesforce customer lists to identify additional likely victims. Alert on ShinyHunters infrastructure registration or new subdomains.

suggestion.title: Franchisee document repository access by non-authorized users
suggestion.rationale: Article: breach 'limited to certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents'. Should detect unusual access patterns to sensitive business document repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access to Salesforce Files or document objects containing franchisee data by users lacking historical read permissions. Detect bulk folder enumeration, recursive file listing, or >100 document downloads in <1hr by service accounts or unfamiliar user accounts.

suggestion.title: Breach notification delay vs. discovery—SLA violation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: Compromise discovered April 8, claimed April 17, but notification issued May 1—23-day disclosure delay. Should correlate incident timeline against regulatory/contractual notification requirements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag breaches where time-to-notification exceeds 30/60-day SLA. Cross-reference Have I Been Pwned records against 7-Eleven's May 1 disclosure date to validate completeness. Alert if threat actor publishes breach on leak site before victim notification.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BTMOB 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to gain elevated permissions and grant itself further system access without additional user interaction.' This is a core persistence and privilege escalation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected accessibility service permission grants after APK installation. Alert on accessibility service configurations enabling input capture or device control capabilities. Track processes/apps requesting accessibility permissions and subsequent elevated actions.

suggestion.title: Phishing to Fake App Store Redirection Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Operators send victims to phishing websites that pose as streaming services, cryptocurrency mining platforms... victims are pushed toward fake app stores that mimic legitimate repositories.' This is the initial delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phishing URLs impersonating streaming services, crypto platforms, or government agencies (e.g., Argentina tax/customs). Detect redirects to fake app store domains. Correlate with regional phishing campaigns targeting specific countries.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Installation from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'victims are pushed toward fake app stores that mimic legitimate repositories and prompt them to install a malicious APK.' Track APK installations outside official Google Play.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installation events originating from non-Google Play sources. Flag installation of known malicious APKs matching ESET signatures (Android/Spy.Agent.EED, EIJ, EIK). Alert on rapid successive APK installations indicating testing/variation.

suggestion.title: Rapid Malware Variant Generation via MaaS Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'As new variants can be generated quickly, defenders should expect rapid payload turnover rather than a stable set of threats.' BTMOB APK builder enables easy payload customization. 'Cyble's report... noted roughly 15 samples of BTMOB v2.5 had been spotted... in a mere two or so weeks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect polymorphic/variant APKs with similar behavioral signatures but different file hashes. Monitor for APK families exhibiting high variant turnover rates (15+ variants in 2 weeks suggests MaaS tool). Use yara rules or fuzzy hashing to group variants.

suggestion.title: Regional Phishing Lure Customization
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bad actors have also been spotted tailoring their lures to specific regions' and example provided: 'campaigns that spread BTMOB while impersonating Argentina's tax and customs authorities.' Indicates organized, localized social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing campaigns by impersonated entity (tax authority, banking app, streaming service) and target region. Flag government agency impersonation attempts (especially tax/customs offices). Alert on lure customization patterns matching known regional targets.

suggestion.title: Remote Data Exfiltration via Android RAT
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrate a range of sensitive data, capture screenshots and record activity on the device, and ultimately take remote control of it.' Describes collection and exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected data transfers from mobile devices following APK installation. Track screenshot/screen recording API calls correlated with unknown network connections. Detect command-and-control communication patterns consistent with remote access trojans.

suggestion.title: Detect Voice Phishing Attack Leading to Entra Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' This is the initial access vector and should trigger detection on post-compromise account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Entra account sign-in events from unusual geographic regions, impossible travel scenarios, or user-agents inconsistent with the user's baseline immediately following known social engineering campaigns. Correlate with high-risk authentication signals.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass Salesforce Data Export from Single Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance' (40 million records claimed). An export of this scale is anomalous and should trigger exfiltration alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk export operations (Data Export, Reports export, bulk API calls) targeting customer records that exceed the user's historical baseline by orders of magnitude. Flag exports by accounts that do not typically perform bulk exports.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Across Disconnected SaaS Platforms via Compromised SSO Account
suggestion.rationale: Article documents ShinyHunters' broader pattern: 'After gaining access to a corporate SSO account, the threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox.' A single compromised SSO account accessing multiple unrelated SaaS applications is a lateral movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for a single user account authenticating to 3+ disparate SaaS platforms (Salesforce, Slack, SAP, Zendesk, etc.) within a 2-hour window, especially if the access pattern deviates from the user's historical behavior or role.

suggestion.title: Detect OAuth Token Theft and Misuse for Salesforce Access
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'threat actors breaching numerous integration companies to steal OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances.' OAuth token compromise enables account takeover and should trigger detection on token reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Salesforce API access authenticated with OAuth tokens from IP addresses, geographic locations, or user-agents inconsistent with the integrating application's known infrastructure. Alert on token reuse across multiple Salesforce instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Extortion Threat Communications from Threat Actor Leak Site
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the impact: 'ShinyHunters...threatened to leak stolen data unless a ransom is paid.' Ransom notes, leak-site notifications, or extortion emails should be detected and escalated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound emails containing links to data leak sites (especially ShinyHunters domains), extortion language, ransom amounts, or references to recently stolen data. Correlate with recent credential compromise or data export alerts for context.

suggestion.title: Detect Targeting of BPO Agent SSO Accounts by Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'conducting widespread social engineering campaigns that target employees and BPO agents' Microsoft Entra, Okta, and Google SSO accounts.' BPO agents often have elevated SaaS access; their compromise is a high-value target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish alerts for anomalous authentication patterns on BPO agent accounts, including sign-ins from unusual geographies, device types, or times outside business hours. Baseline BPO agent access patterns separately from standard employees.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-48172 and recommends substituting this CVE into asset-exposure hunt templates. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-48172 detections in LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin deployments. Alert on hosts failing remediation by federal due date 2026-05-29. Correlate scanner findings with live cPanel service telemetry to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: cPanel Non-Root User Escalation to Root Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be abused by any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—this is the attack's privilege escalation phase, completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process or command execution with root/uid=0 initiated by unprivileged cPanel user accounts. Flag script interpreters (bash, sh, perl, python) spawned from cPanel user context with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution from cPanel Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' via 'user-end cPanel plugin'—execution phase undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script interpreter spawning (bash, sh, python) with root privileges originating from cPanel plugin paths or triggered by cPanel user sessions. Raise alert on uncommon script names or exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: HTTP SQLi Injection Patterns Targeting Drupal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'triggered via specially crafted requests' and is SQL injection. No detection use case was generated despite this being the primary attack vector for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for SQL injection metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, DROP, etc.) in request parameters targeting Drupal application paths (sites/default, admin, modules). Correlate with 5xx error responses or unusual response latencies indicating query execution. Alert on unauthenticated requests to admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Drupal Admin/Sensitive Resources
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'can be exploited without authentication,' yet pipeline missed this as a direct IOA. Requests accessing admin endpoints without prior session/login events are exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Drupal admin paths (/admin, /user/login, /admin/config) from source IPs with no prior successful authentication event in the session or authentication log. Flag requests with SQLi-like payloads in request URI or body.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Anomalous Queries Following Web Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'successful exploitation can potentially lead to information disclosure...and remote code execution' via SQL injection. Pipeline did not suggest correlating malicious HTTP to backend database queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests with SQLi signatures to PostgreSQL query logs (via audit/pgaudit). Alert on UNION-based queries, stacked queries, or time-delay injections executed within 100ms of suspicious HTTP requests. Flag queries attempting to access system tables (pg_users, information_schema).

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Web Shell Placement Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes RCE as possible outcome ('even remote code execution'). Pipeline failed to suggest detection for the persistence mechanism attackers would establish after database compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal web directories (sites/default/files, modules, themes) for file creation or modification immediately following HTTP SQLi attempts. Alert on PHP/shell file writes from web server process. Correlate with process execution of newly written files or outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from PostgreSQL Post-SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'information disclosure' as explicit impact and reports 15,000+ attack attempts. Pipeline missed detection for the data extraction phase following successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers from Drupal web server or PostgreSQL process to external IPs, especially to known C2 or hosting infrastructure. Correlate with prior HTTP SQLi activity. Alert on unusual connection protocols or port usage from database processes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation in PostgreSQL Following Successful SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'privilege escalation' as a consequence of successful exploitation. Pipeline did not generate post-exploitation privilege elevation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs for role/user permission changes (ALTER USER ... WITH SUPERUSER) or group membership modifications following SQLi-like queries. Alert on escalation from web server user context to database admin role.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ScreenConnect remote access from external networks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'abusing ScreenConnect'—direct evidence of attacker-controlled remote session abuse for deployment of mining payloads. This is the execution/persistence hinge in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect process (scservice.exe, ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe) accepting inbound connections from non-corporate geolocation or IP ranges, especially correlated with abnormal child processes (e.g., powershell.exe, csc.exe). Baseline expected users and IPs; deviation = suspicious.

suggestion.title: GPU miner process execution via .NET utilities
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states malware 'abusing...Microsoft .NET utilities' to launch mining. .NET tools (csc.exe, regsvcs.exe, msbuild.exe) are common LOLBin vectors for executing hidden payloads. GPU mining binary should be tracked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect csc.exe, msbuild.exe, regsvcs.exe with command-line arguments indicating inline C# compilation or assembly loading; child processes mining xmrig, nbminer, or hashcat with GPU flags (-gpu-platform, -U, -d). High GPU utilization anomaly post-execution.

suggestion.title: Poisoned search result landing page detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifically cites 'poisoned search results' as initial access. Attacker-controlled landing pages must be identified and blocked to prevent initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web traffic logs to known search-result-poisoning domains or landing pages serving ScreenConnect installers or scripts. Flag if user visits a domain (e.g., fakesite.com posing as legit software) followed within minutes by ScreenConnect process creation and/or PowerShell execution.

suggestion.title: Abnormal elevated GPU utilization and mining pool traffic
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking is the explicit impact phase. GPU resource hijacking must be surfaced. Mining pool connections (e.g., to Monero pools) and sustained high GPU load are smoking guns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained GPU utilization >80% for >30 min outside scheduled workload windows. Correlate with egress traffic to known crypto-mining pools (Monero, XMR, stratum protocols on ports 3333, 6666, 14444, etc.). Baseline expected GPU usage per endpoint; anomalies = alert.

suggestion.title: AI chatbot malicious URL injection detection
suggestion.rationale: Article description notes 'malicious sites also surfaced through AI chatbots.' This is an additional initial-access vector distinct from search-poisoning; chatbots may be hosting or recommending compromised URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads or navigation to malicious domains initiated from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or similar AI interfaces (referrer or context indicates LLM). Cross-reference downloaded files against known malware hashes or suspicious signatures.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect installer downloads from suspicious sources
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow includes attacker-delivered ScreenConnect installation, likely bundled or obfuscated. File downloads and execution signatures are critical IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect binaries or MSI packages downloaded from non-standard sources (temp folders, script-served URLs, cloud storage shares). Verify signatures; flag unsigned or revoked certs. Correlate with parent process (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, msiexec.exe) spawning install.

suggestion.title: XWiki - XAR import execution in application audit log
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'executes a XAR import' but no UC captures application-level XAR import events. XWiki audit trail should log import operations with actor identity; anomalous imports from anonymous/unexpected sources is high-fidelity indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor XWiki audit logs for XAR import events (ImportAction or similar) initiated by unauthenticated or anonymous users. Establish baseline of legitimate scheduled imports; flag imports from unexpected IP ranges, high volume in compressed timeframe, or imports of packages containing suspicious document names or system-level modifications.

suggestion.title: XWiki - wiki document creation spike from unauthenticated source
suggestion.rationale: Article impact: 'create or update documents in the target wiki' but pipeline produced zero hunts for document creation anomalies. Successful exploitation would manifest as document creation burst from single IP without authenticated user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline document creation rate per wiki namespace. Alert on >10 documents created within 5-minute window from single unauthenticated IP or session. Include document type in alert; flag creation of system/configuration documents (space descriptors, macros) as higher severity than user content.

suggestion.title: XWiki - asset inventory: unpatched instance detection via banner/version
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions (16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1). Pipeline missed asset-driven hunt to identify vulnerable versions in enterprise inventory. Missing recon-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and active scans for XWiki instances. Extract version from Server header, X-Powered-By, or /bin/view/Main/ page analysis. Flag versions 16.x <16.10.17, 17.x <17.4.9, 17.10.x <17.10.3, 18.0.x <18.0.1 as vulnerable. Correlate with outbound scanner activity from threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: XWiki REST /rest/wikis endpoint - unauthenticated access to privileged operations
suggestion.rationale: Root cause: 'without performing any authentication or authorization checks'. Pipeline missed detection of auth bypass on REST endpoints by flagging requests lacking valid session tokens or auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference /rest/wikis/* POST requests against active session store. Flag requests where Authorization header is absent, malformed, or references expired/invalid tokens. Compare caller's typical operation profile (time of day, IP range, request frequency); unauthenticated calls to privileged endpoints warrant immediate escalation.

suggestion.title: XWiki - XAR archive content in HTTP request/response
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'XAR import' but no UC inspects request/response payloads for XAR artifacts (MIME type, file signatures, XML manifests). Network-layer detection possible if inspection tools available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to /rest/wikis/* for Content-Type headers indicating archive formats (application/zip, application/x-xar) or XML manifest patterns (META-INF/manifest.xml). Alert on responses containing XAR import success indicators or error messages revealing wiki state. Correlate with subsequent document creation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Phishing email with MiniFast/MiniJunk malware attachment or link
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'phishing' as delivery vector; MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 are the payloads. Pipeline missed initial access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails containing attachments or URLs matching known MiniFast/MiniJunk signatures or behavioral patterns. Detect email gateways flagging suspicious Farsi/Iranian-locale phishing campaigns targeting users in critical sectors. Alert on execution of unknown executables from email temp/download folders correlating to phishing click timestamps.

suggestion.title: SEO-poisoned malicious domain serving MiniFast/MiniJunk
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'SEO poisoning' as primary delivery mechanism. Pipeline produced no domain IOCs and no detection for compromised/poisoned search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains known to serve SEO-poisoned results or recently registered domains mimicking legitimate vendors. Flag web proxies and firewalls for unexpected redirects from search engine results to attacker infrastructure. Monitor for anomalous user navigation patterns (search → suspicious domain → malware download).

suggestion.title: MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 process execution with command-line obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Malware family names given but no execution signature or behavioral detection. Article does not specify execution technique; pipeline should flag common patterns for Iranian APT malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent processes tied to email clients, browsers, or download managers. Detect execution of MiniFast/MiniJunk variants by file hash, authenticode signers, or behavioral IO patterns (e.g., registry queries, DLL injection, parent-child process relationships). Flag execution with non-English locales or from %TEMP% directories.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing from MiniFast/MiniJunk to Iranian-controlled infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Iranian malware families typically establish C2 post-execution; none of the pipeline output addresses command-and-control detection, domain/IP sinkholing, or traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish DNS sinkhole entries and firewall rules for known MiniFast/MiniJunk C2 domains (if available from intelligence). Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from infected hosts to Iran-based ASNs or newly registered domains with short WHOIS privacy expiration windows. Detect anomalous traffic patterns outside business hours or to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage malware loading mechanism (dropper/loader pattern)
suggestion.rationale: MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 naming suggests at least two distinct malware families; phishing + SEO poisoning pattern indicates two-stage delivery (dropper → payload). Pipeline provided no staging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process chains indicative of dropper execution followed by secondary payload. Detect file writes to %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, or %PROGRAMDATA% followed by immediate execution. Flag HTTP/FTP requests to attacker C2 originating from initial malware process, indicating secondary-stage staging.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization with Hardcoded Machine Keys
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'obtained the machine key and used it in ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution' — core exploitation mechanism requiring explicit detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ViewState payloads with abnormal deserialization patterns or signed using known compromised machine keys. Alert on failed ViewState validation followed by process execution. Track suspicious HTTP requests with encrypted ViewState targeting aspx endpoints.

suggestion.title: Godzilla In-Memory .NET Web Shell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)' as the deployed malware but pipeline surfaced no detection hypothesis for this named family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Godzilla/BlueBeam signatures in w3wp.exe process memory and child process creation. Detect unusual CLR assembly loading within IIS worker processes. Monitor for dynamically compiled HTTP handlers injected into ASP.NET application domains.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection into Web Application Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'modify[ed] an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a "security authentication plugin"' — file-level modification with social-engineering payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized writes to JavaScript files in web application root directories. Detect embedded download or plugin installation prompts in static content. Correlate file modifications with web access logs showing injected code served to users.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Installation via Fake Installer Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious JavaScript 'convinced users to download a fake installer, which led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon, essentially planting a backdoor' — end-to-end attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious executable downloads from web application contexts masquerading as security tools or installers. Monitor for Cobalt Strike beacon process signatures and C2 communication patterns. Alert on msiexec.exe execution from unusual parents following user downloads.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Keys in Vendor-Supplied Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file...containing hardcoded machineKey values' — supply-chain weakness enabling at-scale exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan vendor-supplied web.config and configuration files for hardcoded cryptographic material matching known vulnerable patterns or CVE-2026-5426 indicators. Alert if machineKey values are identical across multiple deployments or match public disclosures.

suggestion.title: Organization-Specific Encrypted Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'The payload was encrypted using a key that used the name of the compromised organization, which indicated that the threat actor prepared this payload specifically for the targeted organization' — targeted attack with custom encryption keying.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for encrypted or obfuscated payloads containing organizational identifiers in encryption material or metadata. Detect Cobalt Strike staging servers or beacon payloads customized to specific target organizations. Flag highly tailored malware with organization-embedded keys.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Cobalt Strike as deployed payload. 'Deploy Godzilla and Cobalt Strike' indicates post-compromise C2 establishment but zero use cases capture beacon callbacks, DNS queries, or HTTP POST patterns typical of Cobalt Strike HTTPS traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Cobalt Strike beacon indicators: HTTPS POST requests with malleable C2 profiles, DNS TXT record queries, suspicious USERAGENT patterns (e.g., 'Mozilla/5.0' with unusual entropy), and communication to known CS infrastructure. Focus on LMS admin/teacher accounts initiating outbound connections immediately post-exploit.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Godzilla' as second payload deployed. Godzilla is a JSP/PHP/ASPX webshell commonly used for post-compromise persistence. Pipeline fails to propose detection for webshell execution or its characteristic C2 beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Godzilla webshell installation in KnowledgeDeliver upload directories (e.g., /uploads/, /tmp/, /var/www/html/). Monitor for: (1) unusual .jsp/.php/.aspx file uploads in web roots, (2) POST requests with obfuscated payloads (base64, gzip), (3) specific header patterns (X-Forwarded-For, special cookies) typical of Godzilla C2 traffic.

suggestion.title: KnowledgeDeliver LMS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article asserts 'KnowledgeDeliver LMS Flaw Exploited' but pipeline extracts zero initial-access indicators. No detection rule for HTTP 40x/50x patterns, error-based SQLi, or path traversal attempts against known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /admin/, /course/, /file download paths).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver web server logs for exploitation patterns: unusual URI paths, error-based SQL injection signatures, path traversal attempts (../, ..\), oversized payloads in POST bodies, or unexpected request methods (PUT, DELETE). Baseline normal LMS traffic and alert on anomalies in file-download and admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of web application (LMS) typically follows with code execution in wwwroot or webapp process context. Pipeline misses process-execution detection for spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or reverse shells from IIS/Apache/Tomcat processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when web server processes (w3wp.exe, apache2, tomcat) spawn child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh. Include parent-child anomaly detection for processes writing to suspicious paths or invoking network tools (curl, wget, nc). Scope to post-deployment timeframes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: LMS exploitation often targets privileged accounts (admin teachers, course creators) for lateral movement. Article does not detail this, but no use case captures admin-account abuse post-exploitation (e.g., unusual login locations, privilege escalation within LMS).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LMS authentication logs post-exploitation timestamp. Flag admin-role accounts logging in from new geographies, non-business hours, or with subsequent privilege-escalation attempts (course creation, role grants, user additions). Cross-reference with failed login attempts preceding successful admin sessions.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via LMS Content or User Records
suggestion.rationale: Educational LMS systems host sensitive data (student records, course materials, instructor contact info). Article title omits exfiltration detail, but post-compromise scenarios commonly include bulk data access. Zero detection rules for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LMS database query logs and file-access patterns for bulk downloads: large sequential course enrollments, all-users queries, CSV/JSON export requests to non-standard recipients, or repeated access to student credential/PII fields. Alert on unexpected email/FTP/cloud uploads containing course or user data.

suggestion.title: MFA Challenge Flooding Within Short Window
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'MFA Prompt Bombing' directly indicates attacker-driven repeated MFA challenges to exhaust user resistance. This is the initiation phase of the attack and should trigger alerts on 5+ failed MFA attempts per user within 5 minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spike in rejected/pending MFA authentication attempts from same user over short time window, particularly when followed by eventual approval. Correlate with preceding failed signin attempts using valid credentials. Alert if approval originates from device/location not seen in user baseline within 30 days.

suggestion.title: Post-Fatigue-Attack Session with Suspicious Activity
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker forces MFA approval via bombing, they gain session access. Article framing 'Your Second Factor Isn't Saving You' implies successful compromise post-MFA. Should detect sessions immediately following bombing pattern with abnormal behavior (mailbox access, sensitive group queries, forwarding rule creation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirmed MFA bombing pattern + approval, detect abnormal activity in same session: bulk mailbox reads, inbox rules addition, app/service principal token requests, AAD directory queries, or permission grants—especially from atypical device/IP.

suggestion.title: Credential Validation Spray Before Bombing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must have valid email + password before attempting MFA bombing. Missing detection for credential enumeration or validation testing phase that precedes the bombing attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect low-velocity failed signin attempts (1-3 per hour) using valid email addresses but invalid passwords across multiple users, followed days later by focused MFA bombing on a subset of those accounts—suggests credential validation then targeted attack.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Session After MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article's premise is MFA failure to stop account takeover. Post-compromise, attacker moves to high-value targets. Missing detection for lateral movement behavior unique to MFA-bypassed scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-MFA-approval session attempts resource access outside user's typical patterns: accessing shared mailboxes, resource mailboxes with calendar access, or accessing other users' OneDrive at unusual hours or in bulk.

suggestion.title: Endpoint Automatic Isolation Triggered by Defender
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Compromised endpoints that are automatically isolated are disconnected from the network to reduce the risk of further impact'—this isolation event is a high-fidelity detection signal that should trigger SOC monitoring and orchestration workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on endpoints placed into automatic isolation by Defender for Endpoint. Correlate isolation timestamp with preceding suspicious process execution, failed credential attempts, and lateral movement network events to understand what triggered containment and inform response.

suggestion.title: User Account Isolation by Defender Attack Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Defender for Endpoint could also isolate compromised user accounts as part of automatic attack disruption to block lateral movement in hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks'—account isolation is a containment signal requiring response tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user accounts placed into isolation by Defender AAD risk detection engine. Correlate with preceding risky sign-ins, impossible travel alerts, and anomalous token usage patterns to validate isolation appropriateness.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Behavior Pre-Isolation Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes isolation is designed to 'limit attacker lateral movement'—hunt for the lateral movement techniques that trigger automatic isolation on production endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious lateral movement patterns including multiple failed login attempts, RDP/WinRM connection attempts to non-standard targets, scheduled task creation across multiple systems, and remote service installation that would trigger automatic attack disruption.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration Pre-Isolation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states isolation prevents 'impacts such as data exfiltration'—create detection for the data access and transfer patterns that precede isolation on compromised endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bulk file reads from sensitive directories (temp staging), archive creation (7z, rar, zip), mass network uploads to cloud storage, or external FTP/HTTP uploads that would be detected and trigger automatic isolation.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption Activity Triggering Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists preventing 'ransomware propagation' as isolation goal—create detection for the file encryption and lateral spread patterns characteristic of ransomware that Defender would catch and isolate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass file encryption (high-volume transformation to .locked, .crypt, or ransom note creation), simultaneous encryption across network shares, and lateral encryption attempts post-compromise that would trigger automatic isolation.

suggestion.title: Device Release from Isolation Audit and Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'devices can also be released from containment at any time by security operators'—lack of logging, unauthorized releases, or premature releases could indicate incident response failures or possible attacker evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device releases from isolation without documented remediation completion, releases by unauthorized operators, or releases within minutes of isolation. Track release justifications and correlate with subsequent suspicious activity to validate remediation effectiveness.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Application Launch
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'DLL Side-Loading' as primary technique; no detection use cases were generated for this signature attack pattern despite Severity: high classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of legitimate signed executables (e.g., Windows tools, Adobe, Office) from non-standard directories or followed immediately by unusual DLL file creation/load events in the same directory. Flag when legitimate .exe spawns and loads a non-Microsoft or unsigned DLL from the same parent directory.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via DLL Side-Loading Preparation
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater campaigns typically combine DLL side-loading with registry-based persistence for reliability; article context suggests espionage requiring sustained access, yet no registry IOCs or detection were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run registry paths coinciding with DLL file writes to system folders or application directories. Alert when unsigned or unsigned-by-Microsoft DLLs are registered as service dependencies.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation for DLL Side-Loading Execution
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns typically use scheduled tasks for persistent execution; article mentions targeting 9 countries (multi-stage delivery likely), yet no persistence mechanisms were identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scheduled task creation via schtasks.exe or Task Scheduler APIs that execute legitimate Windows binaries (rundll32, msiexec, regsvr32) pointing to unusual UNC paths, temporary directories, or user-writable locations—common wrappers for DLL side-loading payloads.

suggestion.title: Unsigned DLL Loading from Temp / AppData Directories
suggestion.rationale: DLL side-loading depends on placing malicious DLLs alongside legitimate executables; article specifies DLL side-loading as attack vector, yet no file-system detection pattern was created for DLL staging or loading from non-standard paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL file creation in %TEMP%, %AppData%, user home directories, or application root directories followed within seconds by a legitimate Windows executable launching from the same location. Correlate file creation, load, and process spawn events. Exclude known software vendors.

suggestion.title: C2 Traffic from DLL Side-Loading Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes espionage campaign (implies data exfiltration and command-and-control); no IOCs for command-and-control infrastructure, network beacons, or DNS queries from potentially compromised hosts were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections (ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443, 53) originating from processes launched via DLL side-loading (identified via DeviceImageLoadEvents + unsigned DLL) to external IPs or newly-registered domains. Flag HTTP POST/PUT requests with suspicious User-Agent strings or without standard Accept headers.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater Malware Family Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names MuddyWater as threat actor; no actor-specific IOCs (file names, registry keys, C2 domains, or file paths) associated with known MuddyWater tooling (e.g., RegSvcs, ClearScript, Powerstats) were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or script loading matching known MuddyWater indicators: RegSvcs.exe spawning child processes, PowerShell execution of obfuscated scripts referencing Win32 APIs, or registry key access to HKCU\Software\AppDataLow. Cross-reference with published MuddyWater IOC feeds (e.g., CISA, Dragos, Mandiant).

suggestion.title: Language Service Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Enable RCE Attacks'—arbitrary code execution via extension requires launching child processes. Article phrase 'Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities Enable RCE' establishes code execution is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Language Service processes (angular-language-service, language-service runner) spawn unexpected child processes, especially PowerShell, cmd.exe, or script interpreters. RCE post-exploitation typically begins with arbitrary process execution in the compromised context.

suggestion.title: Angular Extension Malicious Installation or Load
suggestion.rationale: Title 'Extension Vulnerabilities' and RCE suggest attack vector is a malicious or compromised extension. Article directly addresses Angular Language Service Extension as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized or suspicious Angular Language Service extension installations in VS Code or other IDEs. Monitor extension directory for unexpected .vsix files, registry keys tracking extensions, or unsigned/obfuscated extension manifests.

suggestion.title: Network Outbound from Language Service Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE implies attacker gains command and control; article establishes 'Enable RCE Attacks' as outcome. Post-compromise C2 callbacks are typical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound network connections initiated by Language Service processes to non-standard ports or domains. Extension RCE commonly establishes C2 or data exfil channels.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File I/O from Language Service Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE execution in extension context would allow file read/write outside normal IDE boundaries. 'Enable RCE' implies broad file system access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Language Service process reading/writing files outside standard workspace/extension directories, especially source code repos, config files, or .ssh / credential stores.

suggestion.title: Rapid Extension Version or Package Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Multiple vulnerabilities suggest version-dependent exploits. Attacker may force downgrade to vulnerable version. Article explicitly mentions 'Multiple Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/package manager commands and extension version manifests for unexpected downgrades or pinning of Angular Language Service to older vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation from Developer Workstation
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes developer machines as supply chain attack entry points; malicious dependency injection is the core mechanic. Pipeline captured nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/pip/nuget install commands with unusual flags (--unsafe-perm, scripts disabled) or targeting non-standard registries. Correlate with out-of-band network connections to attacker-controlled artifact hosts or typosquatting domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Home Directories
suggestion.rationale: Compromised developer machines yield SSH keys, Git tokens, and API credentials for downstream supply chain pivots—core attack motivation per article theme.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for batch file access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git-credentials, and OS credential stores from process contexts not normally accessing them. Flag archive/exfiltration of these paths.

suggestion.title: Build Artifact Poisoning via Compromised Developer Account
suggestion.rationale: Once dev machine compromised, attacker commits malicious code to repositories or modifies CI/CD outputs before deployment—the actual supply chain compromise step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected commits/PRs from developer accounts outside normal hours, unusual commit times relative to user timezone, or source-code changes in CI/build scripts without code-review approval.

suggestion.title: Rogue IDE Plugin or Build Tool Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers compromise Visual Studio, IntelliJIDEA plugins, or build tools (Make, Gradle, Maven) as persistence/backdoor mechanism on developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or attacker-signed plugin installation in IDE plugin directories. Detect suspicious auto-execution of build tools or IDE startup hooks calling out to external C2.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Developer Machine to Repository Server
suggestion.rationale: Article implies developer machines are pivot points; attackers lateral-move to Git servers, artifact registries, and CI/CD systems to achieve supply-chain reach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to Git/artifact/deployment systems from developer workstation IPs using developer credentials outside business hours or from unexpected geographies. Flag service-account usage from non-infrastructure machines.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting and Dependency Confusion Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use malicious packages with typo names (e.g., @angular → @angulr) or exploit private package version conflicts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package downloads from unexpected registries, mismatched package hashes, or installation of packages with names Levenshtein-close to legitimate libraries. Alert on public-registry queries from build systems expecting private repos.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Software Download from AI Chatbot Recommendation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'users querying AI chatbots for software download recommendations being presented with links to attacker-controlled domains within generated responses.' No use case generated for this initial delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads initiated via browser processes following LLM-driven queries (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude contexts). Correlate download domains against known malware hashes and lookalike domains for legitimate utilities. Alert on downloads of executables matching fake software naming conventions (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite, PDFgear) from non-vendor domains.

suggestion.title: GPU Cryptomining Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'secretly mines cryptocurrency using victims' GPUs, causing performance issues and hardware damage.' No detection case for cryptomining workload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of processes with high GPU utilization spawned from temporary directories or downloads folder. Correlate process execution with sustained CUDA/OpenCL API calls. Monitor for unsigned or recently-created executables calling GPU libraries. Alert on processes initiating connections to known cryptomining pool domains (stratum+tcp://, mining.*, pool.*) or wallet addresses.

suggestion.title: Execution of Fake Utility Software from Suspicious Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific impersonated utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear, Display Driver Uninstaller) sourced from attacker domains. No detection case for execution of these lookalike binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate utility execution paths and publishers. Alert on execution of CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite, PDFgear, or Display Driver Uninstaller from non-standard locations (Downloads, AppData, %TEMP%) or unsigned/mismatched digital signatures. Flag process parents from browser processes or shells that indicate user-initiated execution of downloaded files.

suggestion.title: GPU-Impersonating Software Download Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'users who own high-performance GPUs.' Article specifies fake software targeting GPU-owners via chatbot recommendations. No use case for detection of this targeting pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users downloading GPU-related utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, GPU monitoring, GPU drivers) from suspicious domains following LLM interactions. Cross-reference download history with AI search/chatbot logs (if available). Alert on multiple users in same environment downloading fake GPU utility variants within short timeframe, suggesting targeted campaign or lateral spread.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning Domain Reputation Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'SEO poisoning, pushing malicious sites to the top results.' No IOC ingestion or domain reputation check triggered for attacker-controlled sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user visits to newly-registered or recently-compromised domains impersonating legitimate software vendors. Correlate with SEO ranking spikes for software-related keywords. Flag domains hosting fake utilities (especially CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor variants) if they lack SSL certificate history, exhibit certificate pinning anomalies, or resolve from bulletproof hosting providers.

suggestion.title: LLM-Driven Malicious Recommendation Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'crafting prompts that trick AI chatbots into recommending the same infected links.' No detection hypothesis for prompt injection or LLM output poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM request/response pairs for injection patterns (unusual syntax, repeated keywords, adversarial prompts requesting specific domain recommendations). Flag LLM outputs containing links to newly-registered domains, non-vendor hosting, or domains flagged for malware. Correlate suspicious LLM responses with subsequent user downloads from those domains. Alert on chatbot outputs recommending downloads outside official vendor sites.

suggestion.title: BadHost Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers can exploit BadHost'—the core attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary threat. Article phrase: 'Attackers Can Exploit BadHost'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests matching BadHost exploit signatures (specific parameter injection, malformed headers, or known CVE payloads). Monitor for 4xx errors followed by 200 responses to admin/sensitive paths within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive AI Agent Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states goal is to 'access sensitive AI Agent Server endpoints'—direct objective. Pipeline missed generating endpoint-access detection. Article phrase: 'Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication to /agent/*, /api/internal/*, or /model/* endpoints from external/untrusted sources. Baseline per-endpoint access patterns; flag requests outside business hours or from anomalous geolocations.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from Compromised AI Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Access to 'sensitive' endpoints implies data exposure risk; no exfiltration detection generated despite high severity designation. Attack impact is data theft from AI infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent endpoints for sustained data transfer volume anomalies (>5x baseline), bulk model/config downloads, or transfers to non-whitelisted external IPs. Alert on credential material (API keys, tokens) in request/response bodies.

suggestion.title: Password Spraying Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' to weak password selection. Attackers enumerate weak credentials at scale across user populations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts targeting different user accounts from single source IP within compressed time window (e.g., 30 failed logins to 20+ users in 10 minutes). Correlate spray attempts that immediately precede successful logins to identify compromise patterns.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Reuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'breach password protection' checking against '5.4 billion known breached credentials' and cites Verizon DBIR: 'stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches'. Attackers systematically test public breach-dump credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication attempts using credentials known to exist in public breach databases or credential dumps. Raise alert severity if successful login is followed within minutes by privilege escalation, role assignment changes, or sensitive resource access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous AD Password Reset Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article advocates 'self-service password resets' to reduce friction and helpdesk load. Attackers may abuse reset mechanisms for account takeover or persistence; monitor reset chains and identity-validation bypass patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password reset frequency anomalies: >3 resets per user per day, resets by dormant accounts, or resets from unusual geolocations. Flag cascading resets (Account A resets, then immediately Account B resets with same source IP).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-48172 as 'actively being exploited' and provides grep detection pattern. Pipeline extracted nothing. Article: 'This vulnerability is being actively exploited, and poses a risk for all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel logs and HTTP request logs for patterns containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' or requests targeting the lsws.redisAble function. Correlate with unauthenticated or low-privilege source IPs. Alert on any match, especially from external sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Configuration Manipulation via cPanel API
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability stems from 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features' in lsws.redisAble function. Should detect abnormal cPanel API calls attempting Redis manipulation. Article: 'vulnerability is related to the mishandling of Redis enable/disable features and was found in the lsws.redisAble function.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cPanel API calls or function invocations referencing Redis enable/disable operations, particularly from IP addresses not in administrator whitelist or with session tokens indicating non-admin context. Focus on lsws.redisAble function calls.

suggestion.title: Root-level Script Execution in cPanel Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack outcome: 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' Should detect unexpected elevated-privilege script execution.
