suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on java process with yamcs/org.yamcs in command line spawning bash, sh, dash, zsh, nc, ncat, socat, python, or perl. Parent-child relationship between Java and shell is the critical signal.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell via /dev/tcp from Yamcs process tree
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation: 'Reverse-shell /dev/tcp file descriptor from Yamcs java process tree' as distinct C2 indicator. Quote: ProcessCommandLine checking for '/dev/tcp/' or '/dev/udp/'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash/sh/zsh spawned with /dev/tcp/[IP]/[PORT] or /dev/udp/ in the command line where parent is Java or grandparent is Java with yamcs-related process names. Extract remote IP and port for C2 attribution.

suggestion.title: Yamcs default guest user with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'In Yamcs's default configuration (no security.yaml), the built-in guest user [can exploit this].' This is the privilege-escalation / initial-access vector that the pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication as 'guest' or default accounts to Yamcs, followed by PATCH requests to MdbOverrideApi endpoints. Flag instances where security.yaml is absent or guest privilege is not restricted.

suggestion.title: Nashorn ClassFilter bypass via ScriptEngine instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Root cause from article: 'ScriptEngine used to evaluate user-supplied algorithm text... constructed without a ClassFilter'. This is the vulnerability mechanism — detection should cover missing security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Yamcs server logs for Nashorn ScriptEngine instantiation or algorithm evaluation errors. Flag any eval() or script execution from untrusted algorithm definitions. Also check for presence of ClassFilter in Yamcs config; absence is a vulnerability signal.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Container Image Pull Without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'exposes private container images without authentication'—core attack path is unauthenticated registry access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry (Docker, OCI, Gitea) for pull/fetch operations to private image repositories where the request lacks valid Bearer token, OAuth session, or authentication headers. Flag successful 200/201 responses to private namespace pulls from unauthenticated clients.

suggestion.title: Gitea API Token/Session Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism likely involves session/token validation bypass in Gitea API endpoints handling container manifest access—'without authentication' suggests auth check is skipped or fooled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Gitea `/v2/` (Docker Registry API v2) or container manifest endpoints that lack `Authorization` header or contain malformed/expired tokens, yet receive 200 OK responses. Track requests from IPs without prior valid authentication events.

suggestion.title: Mass Container Image Enumeration Against Private Gitea Registry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability disclosure likely enables attackers to enumerate private image tags/versions without auth—'exposes' implies discoverability, not just download access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential requests to Gitea container registry tag/manifest listing endpoints (e.g., `/v2/<namespace>/<repo>/tags/list`, `/catalog`) from single source IP within short time window, especially if unauthenticated or from non-whitelisted CIDR. Flag if requests probe multiple private namespaces.

suggestion.title: Gitea Container Registry Requests from External/Unexpected Networks
suggestion.rationale: Private container images are typically pulled only by authorized CI/CD systems or internal container orchestrators—unsolicited external registry pulls are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of IPs/ASNs pulling from private Gitea registries; alert on image pull requests originating from non-whitelisted external networks or suspicious geolocations. Correlate with auth bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Gitea Webhook or Deploy Token Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability leaks webhook URLs, deploy tokens, or integration secrets stored in Gitea, attackers gain persistent registry access—common side-effect of auth-bypass bugs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea admin/settings logs for enumeration of webhooks, deploy keys, or token settings by non-admin accounts or during suspected vulnerability exploitation windows. Alert on disclosure of secrets in HTTP request logs or error messages.

suggestion.title: Gitea Version-Specific Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Once CVE version range is disclosed, exploitation attempts will target specific Gitea versions via manifest endpoint anomalies—should detect pre/post-patch behavior deltas.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After CVE disclosure, monitor Gitea server logs for requests matching known exploitation signatures (e.g., path traversal in manifest fetch, parameter injection in auth checks). Correlate with Gitea version in Server headers; alert if vulnerable versions respond to bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code/OpenVSX Extension Installation and Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article states extensions 'stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' and 'planted dozens of dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update.' Dormancy + update-triggered execution is a critical attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension directory writes followed by process spawn only after restart or package update event. Flag unsigned extensions or those with network egress in child processes immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Enumeration and Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies extensions 'stole cryptocurrency wallets'—requires file system enumeration of wallet storage (.ethereum, .solana, browser extension storage) and credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by IDE extensions opening wallet files in standard cryptocurrency storage paths. Correlate file reads with Base64 encoding/compression operations and subsequent C2 beacon.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain-based C2 Polling and Address Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions'—process must query Solana RPC, decode Base64 memo fields, then connect to extracted IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes connecting to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com), performing Base64 decode operations, then initiating connections to previously-unseen IPs. Correlate decoded values against known blockchain transactions.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT C2 Configuration Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys, leveraging a global decentralized network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-BitTorrent applications initiating DHT protocol queries (UDP to standard or non-standard DHT ports) with hardcoded infohash patterns, followed by connections to derived peer IPs.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar API for C2 Dead-Drop Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' Legitimate calendar access + Base64 decoding of event titles is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated Google Calendar API calls by non-browser/non-native-calendar processes, especially with simultaneous Base64 decoding of returned event title strings and subsequent C2-like network connections.

suggestion.title: Post-Takedown Sinkhole Detection (164.92.88.210)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides sinkhole IP: 'all machines compromised in a Glassworm attack are beaconing to the IP address 164.92.88[.]210 operated by CrowdStrike.' Direct IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Any outbound traffic to 164.92.88.210 indicates active Glassworm compromise. Minimal expected false positives. Investigate originating process for credential theft, wallet enumeration, or extension persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool/Library Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies supply chain attack against developers. Pipeline missed UC for detecting compromised dependency injection or malicious package distribution—core to supply chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package managers (npm, pip, NuGet, Maven) for unexpected or unsigned package versions, suspicious metadata (mismatched author, sudden popularity spike), and installation activity outside normal development windows. Correlate with known-malicious hashes or supply-chain threat feeds.

suggestion.title: GlassWorm Malware Behavioral Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names specific malware 'GlassWorm.' Pipeline failed to ingest malware name or propose signature-based detection around known GlassWorm indicators (process execution, memory artifacts, file writes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create process execution rules for known GlassWorm process names, command-line patterns, parent-child relationships (e.g., development tools spawning obfuscated PowerShell/cmd). Monitor for suspicious memory injection or DLL loading chains typical of malware delivery.

suggestion.title: C2 Infrastructure Connectivity After Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'infrastructure takedown'—strongly implies command-and-control disruption. Pipeline missed UC for detecting outbound C2 traffic from compromised developer systems to known GlassWorm C2 domains/IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and network logs for developer machines resolving or connecting to previously-observed GlassWorm C2 infrastructure, proxy/redirector domains, or DGA-generated destinations. Correlate with takedown announcements for IOC lists.

suggestion.title: Developer Workstation Behavioral Anomaly Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware targeting developers typically exhibits lateral movement, credential harvesting, or source-code exfiltration patterns. Pipeline generated no UCs for these post-execution behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unusual file access patterns on developer machines (mass enumeration of .sln, .cs, .git, credentials files). Monitor for unusual data transfers to external IPs, especially during off-hours or before infrastructure takedown notification. Cross-reference with source-control audit logs for unauthorized clone/download activity.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Phishing Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Grandoreiro Malware campaigns'; banking trojans historically use spearphishing with attachments as primary delivery mechanism
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious email attachments with obfuscated extensions, Office documents spawning non-Office child processes, or recent executables opened within minutes of email arrival. Alert on macro-enabled documents originating from external senders.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Credential Harvesting from Browser/Wallet Storage
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro specifically targets banking and financial credentials; malware must access stored passwords and cached session data
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection into explorer.exe, svchost, or browser processes. Detect enumeration of Registry credential storage (HKLM\SAM, credential manager vault) or suspicious access to AppData browser folders containing cached credentials.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro C2 Communication Over Encrypted Channels
suggestion.rationale: Malware campaigns establish persistent command-and-control; Grandoreiro known for obfuscated HTTPS C2 beaconing
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows hosts establishing recurring outbound HTTPS connections to recently registered domains, non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 8888), or IPs with poor reputation. Alert on unusual TLS certificate details or mismatched SNI/certificate CN pairs.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Android APK Installation Outside App Store
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'BTMOB RAT Campaigns Target Android Users'; RATs delivered as malicious unsigned APKs sideloaded onto devices
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of APK files from non-standard sources (USB, SMS-delivered links, third-party app stores). Alert on APKs with obfuscated package names or those requesting dangerous permission sets (camera, contacts, location) immediately upon installation.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Remote Code Execution via Device Admin Abuse
suggestion.rationale: RATs require elevated privileges; BTMOB known for exploiting Accessibility Services and Device Admin permissions for unrestricted command execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for applications requesting Accessibility Services or Device Admin privileges post-installation. Detect Accessibility Service access patterns inconsistent with app function (e.g., messaging app accessing device admin). Alert on keystroke interception or UI automation abuse.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Data Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Title states campaign targets users; RATs exfiltrate SMS, call logs, contacts, and installed app lists to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound network traffic from newly installed applications, especially to suspicious C2 domains. Detect large data transfers containing SMS content, contact databases, or app inventory data to foreign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Prompt Abuse — Malware Recommendation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Abuse AI Chatbot Recommendations to Push Malicious Software Download Links' — pipeline failed to propose detection for compromised or manipulated chatbot outputs recommending malware. Requires monitoring chatbot response quality and correlation with known malware domains/URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag chatbot interactions where AI response text contains URLs/domains flagged in malware intel feeds, file-hash recommendations, or executable download prompts. Correlate with subsequent user downloads and execution on same endpoint within 1h window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download Post-Chatbot Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes end-user downloading malware from chatbot-recommended links. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection tying download events to prior chatbot API calls or web activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe, .msi, .zip downloads initiated within 2 minutes of chatbot interaction, especially from unfamiliar or newly registered domains. Cross-reference with web proxy logs for referrer chain showing chatbot service → malware host.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot API Token/Auth Abuse — Malicious Injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack surfaces that chatbots can be abused to emit malware links. Pipeline should flag prompt-injection payloads or unauthorized API calls altering chatbot output toward adversarial goals, especially if source IP/auth context changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous API calls to chatbot endpoints (rate spike, unusual auth tokens, non-standard prompt parameters). Flag responses containing shellcode, base64-encoded executables, or URLs to known malware-hosting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Malicious Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes '22 versions of npm RAT' distributed via npm. Supply-chain attack on package management is the entry vector. Title: 'Hackers Push 22 Versions of npm RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / yarn add commands for installation of known malicious package names. Cross-reference installed package versions against threat intel feeds. Detect installations from non-standard registries or with suspicious metadata flags.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process from Node.js Runtime
suggestion.rationale: npm RAT executes arbitrary code upon installation/require. Article describes malware with 'wallet theft and persistent backdoor' implying code execution. Standard RAT behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.js or npm spawn unusual child processes (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, curl). RAT payloads typically initiate C2 callbacks or persistence mechanisms immediately after unpacking.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Registration via Startup/Init Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'persistent backdoor.' npm RAT must survive reboots—likely via startup scripts, registry run keys, or systemd/launchd entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKCU/HKLM Run/RunOnce, ~/.bashrc, /etc/init.d, or ~/.config/systemd following npm package installation. Monitor for scheduled tasks or cron jobs created by node processes.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet File Access from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Wallet Theft.' RAT must enumerate and exfiltrate wallet files (MetaMask extensions, hardware wallet pairing files, private key stores).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.js process accessing wallet-related directories (~/.ethereum, ~/.solana, ~/.metamask, AppData/MetaMask). Monitor for file reads of .json keystore files, .seed, or .key extensions by Node.js child processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Network Communication from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: npm RAT requires command-and-control channel. Article describes backdoor implying persistent C2 callbacks for commands/data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline expected npm/Node.js network destinations (registries, CDNs). Alert on DNS queries or TCP/443 connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains from node processes. Cross-reference resolved IPs against C2 threat feeds.

suggestion.title: npm Module Obfuscation and Anti-Analysis Patterns
suggestion.rationale: RAT developers typically obfuscate code to evade static analysis. Article describes '22 versions' suggesting intentional polymorph/obfuscation strategy to bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with minified/obfuscated main entry points, suspicious eval() calls, or base64-encoded payloads. Detect dynamic require() chains or heavy use of Buffer operations in package.json scripts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Claude Installer Execution from Non-Standard Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers distributing fake ChatGPT and Claude installers. Legitimate installer execution should be from browser downloads or vendor domains only. Detection: 'Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers to Deploy'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of any executable containing ChatGPT or Claude in the filename originating from non-vendor directories (Desktop, Downloads, Temp), unsigned or with mismatched publisher certificates, or downloading from non-canonical domains.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Backdoor IOC Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names DinDoor as the deployed backdoor. Pipeline should extract malware signatures, file hashes, and C2 endpoints. Article states: 'Deploy DinDoor Backdoor'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of any process matching known DinDoor signatures, spawning child processes with persistence mechanisms, or injecting into legitimate processes to establish backdoor foothold.

suggestion.title: Installer Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers will have different file hashes than official releases. Pipeline should correlate downloaded installer hashes against official vendor repositories. Indicates: 'Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any downloaded executable claiming to be ChatGPT or Claude installer where the SHA256 hash does not match official OpenAI or Anthropic release checksums published on vendor sites.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Software Distribution Domain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers must be hosted on attacker-controlled or compromised domains. Article indicates distribution channel attack: 'Hackers Use Fake... Installers'. Pipeline should identify typosquatting or lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user downloads of executables from domains that closely resemble official ChatGPT or Claude vendor domains (typosquatting, homograph attacks), or WHOIS-registered within the last 90 days with registrants matching previous malware distribution infrastructure.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Once deployed, DinDoor must establish C2. Article confirms backdoor deployment but pipeline extracted no network IOCs or C2 indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/TCP connections from processes spawned by fake installer executables to known DinDoor C2 IP addresses or domains, or unusual DNS queries matching DinDoor DNS sinkhole patterns.

suggestion.title: Installer Masquerading Detection via Code Signing Chain
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers impersonate legitimate software. Real ChatGPT/Claude installers carry valid code signatures from OpenAI/Anthropic. Detection: 'Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of binaries claiming ChatGPT or Claude identity but lacking valid digital signatures from OpenAI, Inc. or Anthropic, PBC., or bearing signatures from untrusted certificate authorities.

suggestion.title: Banking Trojan Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies Grandoreiro malware being deployed to target banks; pipeline must detect file execution of known banking trojan samples and families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of Grandoreiro samples via hash signatures, yara rules, or behavioral patterns (suspicious process spawning from temp folders, parent-child relationships indicative of malware staging). Alert on mstsc.exe or svchost.exe spawning from unlikely paths or with suspicious cmdline args.

suggestion.title: Credential Overlay Attack on Banking Applications
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans targeting 'Portuguese banks' implies overlay/hook attacks to intercept credentials; article describes credential-stealing campaign but pipeline generated no detection for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect overlay windows created on top of banking app processes (Accessibility API abuse, window hooks, or DLL injection into banking app). Look for suspicious DLL loading into legitimate banking client processes, or accessibility features being programmatically enabled to capture input.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Injection into System Services
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans commonly inject into svchost.exe or similar legitimate processes for stealth and persistence; article mentions Latin American targeting but provides no detection for process-hollowing or injection techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual LoadLibrary/VirtualAllocEx/WriteProcessMemory chains targeting system services or long-running processes. Monitor for svchost.exe or services.exe spawning child processes or accessing unusual network resources.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beacon Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro as a remote-access banking trojan requires C2 communication; article describes active campaign but pipeline did not identify C2 infrastructure or callback patterns to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic to known Grandoreiro C2 domains (if IOCs published). Detect beaconing patterns: regular periodic connections to suspicious domains, unusual User-Agent headers, traffic to domains with freshly registered whois or bulletproof hosting providers.

suggestion.title: System Enumeration and Profiling by Banking Malware
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans profile victim systems before credential theft; article describes targeted campaigns requiring victim fingerprinting but no detection for reconnaissance queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid WMI/registry queries for system info (processor, memory, OS version), running processes, and installed security software. Look for suspicious systeminfo.exe, tasklist.exe, or wmic.exe execution from unusual parents (malware processes).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Keys or Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans require persistence across reboots; article implies ongoing campaign but no detection for persistence mechanisms typical of Grandoreiro.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious HKCU/HKLM\Run registry writes, particularly from temporary or user-writable paths. Detect Task Scheduler event creation for .exe or .vbs payloads with suspicious triggers or hidden attributes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Token Access from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes tokens are 'stolen'—pipeline missed credential access phase entirely. Must detect: development tool processes reading .env files, environment variables, or credential stores containing API keys or bearer tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when IDE or build-tool processes access files matching patterns: .env, .aws/credentials, .config/*/token, HOME/.anthropic, or read environment variables containing 'OPENAI_API_KEY|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|TOKEN'. Correlate with unexpected child processes or network IOCs.

suggestion.title: Legitimate-Looking UI Process with Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes social engineering vector—'legitimate-looking'—pipeline missed defense evasion and execution entirely. Must detect: processes impersonating known tools executing unusual sub-processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes named or parented by 'Codex', 'Remote-UI', or mimicking VSCode/JetBrains IDEs, especially when launching curl/wget/Python with Base64-encoded payloads or spawning shell to exfiltrate credential data. Check for mismatched process signing or unusual directory placement.

suggestion.title: Outbound Token Exfiltration to Unknown C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes tokens being 'stolen'—requires exfiltration detection. Pipeline provided no IOCs and no network-based use cases. Expected: detection of token-serialized traffic to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect development-tool processes initiating HTTPS POST requests with JSON or Base64-encoded payloads to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Signature: POST bodies containing patterns matching 'sk-', 'bearer', 'token=', or similar credential markers from non-standard ports (8888, 9000, 5000).

suggestion.title: Malware Package Supply Chain—Fake Development Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Title references specific 'Codex Remote UI' variant; article likely describes npm/pip package masquerading as legitimate tool. Pipeline extracted zero supply-chain IOCs—missing entire initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of suspicious packages with names similar to legitimate tools (codex, remote-ui, vscode-*, jetbrains-*). Flag typo-squatting patterns. Alert when package install scripts execute with elevated privileges or modify environment/proxy settings. Cross-reference against known malicious package registries.

suggestion.title: Batch Enumeration of Token Files in User Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies systematic token collection ('your AI tokens' plural); pipeline missed collection phase and associated file-enumeration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, recursive file-system enumeration targeting ~/.config, ~/.env, .openai, .anthropic directories or globbing patterns matching *.key, *.token, *.pem within short time windows (< 10s), especially from child processes of development tools.

suggestion.title: npm package installation with suspicious post-install scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'malicious npm package'—such packages typically abuse post-install lifecycle scripts to execute code during installation. No detection hypothesis was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe spawning child processes (powershell, cmd, curl, git) immediately during or after install operations. Flag spawned processes accessing environment variables or writing to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or user home directories outside expected artifact locations.

suggestion.title: Directory enumeration from npm package context
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'stole files from Claude AI User Directory'—implies discovery and enumeration of target directories. No detection for recursive directory listing or file enumeration from npm-spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm-spawned processes calling dir/ls with recursive flags (-R, -r) or PowerShell Get-ChildItem -Recurse on user home directories, particularly ~/.claude, ~/.ssh, or ~/Documents. Correlate with subsequent file read operations.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via GitHub API from suspicious context
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'via GitHub'—implies use of GitHub as exfiltration vector or C2 endpoint. Pipeline must detect unauthorized GitHub API calls, repository creation, or file uploads from npm or user process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS POST/PUT requests to api.github.com from unexpected processes (npm spawned tasks, node scripts). Flag requests creating repositories, uploading files, or pushing content from processes running in temp/npm_cache context. Correlate with prior file read operations on user directories.

suggestion.title: Claude configuration/credential access from third-party process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting 'Claude AI User Directory'—likely contains configuration, API keys, or session tokens. No detection for unauthorized access to ~/.claude or similar from npm-managed packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation from npm (node.exe, npm.exe spawned children) reading .claude directory, claude.json, api_keys, or similar credential stores. Include parent process chain to identify package context.

suggestion.title: Supply chain compromise: malicious npm package publication
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim is a 'malicious npm package'—indicates T1195.001 supply-chain attack vector. Pipeline must flag package metadata: registration date, initial downloads, version jump patterns, unusual collaborators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for packages with new maintainers, unusual version bumps, or rapid download spikes targeting security/AI tools categories. Cross-reference against typosquatting lists and maintainer reputation. Flag packages with obfuscated post-install scripts or Base64-encoded payloads in package.json.

suggestion.title: Anomalous environment variable exfiltration from npm context
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package likely harvested $HOME, $USER, $GITHUB_TOKEN or similar environment context before exfiltrating files. No detection for env var reads/exports from npm-spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe and node.exe child processes for access to environment variable tables or /proc/[pid]/environ on Linux. Flag subsequent file writes or network calls appending env values. Include parent process and npm package name in alerts.

suggestion.title: Detect Code Injection into Amazon App from Unauthorized Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states app 'hijacking Amazon App to inject affiliate codes.' This requires runtime code injection; pipeline generated zero detection for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inter-process code injection targeting com.amazon.venezia: WriteProcessMemory, library loading from non-standard paths, or ptrace syscalls from preinstalled app processes. Alert on unsigned code sections injected into Amazon process memory.

suggestion.title: Detect Preinstalled Malware App via Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'preinstalled app found on Motorola phones'—textbook T1199. Pipeline failed to map this initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all system/preinstalled apps on Motorola devices; alert on unsigned or unusual system-level app installations. Cross-reference against known legitimate Motorola-signed packages. Flag any preinstalled app with elevated permissions targeting Amazon infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Amazon App Outbound Connections to Non-Amazon Affiliate Domains
suggestion.rationale: Affiliate code injection implies exfiltration to affiliate tracking networks or payment redirectors. No detection for unauthorized egress from Amazon app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and HTTP requests originated from Amazon app process; alert on connections to affiliate networks, URL shorteners, or non-Amazon CDN domains. Flag outbound requests containing injected affiliate parameters or tracking codes.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized File Modification of Amazon Application Package
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking implies runtime patching or file-level modification of app resources. Article mentions persistence against specific app—no file integrity detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to /data/app/com.amazon.venezia/* or app package directory from processes not signed by Amazon or Google. Alert on modification of app binary, DEX, or configuration files from preinstalled app context.

suggestion.title: Detect Library Injection or Runtime Hooking in Amazon Process Space
suggestion.rationale: Code injection into running app likely via LD_PRELOAD or native library interposition. Article's hijacking mechanism implies hooking—no evasion technique detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected .so or .odex library loads into Amazon app, especially from /system/lib, /data/local, or preinstalled app directories. Monitor LD_PRELOAD and equivalent environment variable tampering.

suggestion.title: Detect Affiliate Code Parameter Injection in Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat is 'inject affiliate codes'—requires traffic interception and mutation. No behavioral detection for modified HTTP parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Amazon app HTTP requests (referrer, affiliate parameters, cookies). Alert on unexpected affiliate IDs, parameter mutations, or redirects injected into Amazon traffic. Correlate with known affiliate tracking domains.

suggestion.title: Android App Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Lets Attackers Remotely Control Android Devices'—implies distribution vector; malware delivery to devices requires sideload or non-Play Store installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installation events outside Google Play Store. Detect PM install commands and sideload file staging. Flag APKs with missing or suspicious signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Beaconing from Android Application
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'remotely control' capability—requires persistent outbound command channel to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from suspicious app processes to non-standard ports. Flag periodic beaconing patterns, callbacks to newly-registered domains, or known C2 IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Excessive or Suspicious Permission Grants to Android App
suggestion.rationale: Remote control implies harvesting device data and controlling device functions—requires requesting and obtaining permissions for camera, microphone, contacts, location, storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APKs requesting dangerous permission clusters (CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO + READ_CONTACTS + READ_SMS + LOCATION + WRITE_EXTERNAL). Cross-check against legitimate Play Store baseline.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Suspicious App Process
suggestion.rationale: Remote control malware must steal device data; article implies capability to collect and transmit sensitive information (contacts, messages, files, device ID).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app processes reading sensitive databases (/data/data/*/databases) or accessing ContactsProvider followed by large outbound transfers. Detect unusual data volumes to C2.

suggestion.title: Execution of System Commands via Malicious App
suggestion.rationale: Remote control requires executing arbitrary commands on the device; article's 'control' capability implies shell or binary execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect app processes spawning shell (sh/bash) or invoking system binaries. Monitor Runtime.exec() calls; flag unexpected process ancestry (app → shell executable).

suggestion.title: BTMOB Malware Family Indicators of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: No malware-specific IOCs extracted despite article being about named malware family BTMOB; should have captured package names, hashes, URLs, C2 domains from article content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once article parsed for BTMOB-specific indicators: create signatures for BTMOB package names, known APK hashes, C2 domains, and persistence receivers. Monitor for BTMOB process execution and file writes to app data directories.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Data Exfiltration Preceding Ransom Demand
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords 'cyber extortion economy' and 'data theft' indicate exfiltration is the attack precursor. Article explicitly describes data theft as the foundation of extortion leverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers to external storage (S3, Mega, file.io) or direct exports using CLI tools (rclone, aws-cli, gsutil). Correlate volume and timing with subsequent ransom communication on public forums or Telegram.

suggestion.title: Ransom Negotiation via Telegram Bot or Channel
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly cite 'Telegram' as communication platform; extortion economy depends on negotiation infrastructure separate from C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS to Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org, gateway.telegram.org) from non-standard business contexts. Detect new Telegram bot tokens created or used for mass notification patterns post-incident.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Partner Targeting for Data Amplification
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'supply chain'; extortion actors increase pressure and data value by simultaneously compromising vendors, customers, or partners of primary target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate compromise timelines of supply chain partners (via VPN logs, directory services, supplier portal access). Detect fishing or credential stuffing targeting contractor networks within 1-2 weeks of primary target compromise.

suggestion.title: Frontier AI-Powered Data Annotation for Leak Publication
suggestion.rationale: Keywords mention 'Frontier AI'; extortion economy now uses large language models to analyze, summarize, and contextualize stolen data before public leak to maximize ransom pressure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls to LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude) with stolen datasets as context. Monitor for batch inference patterns on recently exfiltrated database tables, followed by leak site publication.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Recommendation Links to Malicious Download Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'users querying AI chatbots for software download recommendations were presented with links to attacker-controlled domains within generated responses.' No detection for this poisoning vector exists in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when users click links from AI chatbot responses that resolve to domains in threat intel feeds (150+ identified malicious domains). Flag URLs in chatbot transcripts that match patterns of malware distribution infrastructure. Monitor for click-through events from LLM outputs to previously-unvisited domains with low reputation scores.

suggestion.title: Execution of Fake System Utility Impersonators (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, PDFgear, etc.)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names impersonated utilities: 'CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, and PDFgear' — but pipeline missed masquerading detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of processes named or disguised as common GPU-utility software (CrystalDiskInfo.exe, HWMonitor.exe, etc.) from unusual paths, especially if launched after recent downloads from suspicious domains. Check file signatures and publisher metadata — legitimate utilities are signed; malicious variants typically are not.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Software Execution (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three mining families: 'gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI' — direct impact/payload indicators that should trigger alerts but appear nowhere in detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or DLL loading matching known miner process names/signatures (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI, or common variants). Escalate if launched from temporary directories, from ZIP extractions, or by system utilities masquerading as legitimate software. Cross-correlate with network traffic to known mining pool infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ZIP Archive Extraction and Miner Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the download instead retrieves a malicious ZIP archive hosted on campaign-linked subdomains' containing mining payloads — extraction and staging behavior is critical detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP extraction to temporary or user writable locations followed immediately by execution of miner processes, or execution of suspicious binaries with names matching legitimate utilities. Correlate on timestamp: recent download + ZIP extract + miner execution within seconds is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect and .NET Utility Abuse for Cryptojacking
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'abusing ScreenConnect and Microsoft .NET utilities' but pipeline extracted no defense-evasion or persistence detection logic around these pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ScreenConnect (legitimate RMM) or legitimate .NET tools (csc.exe, InstallUtil.exe, regasm.exe) are used to stage, compile, or execute cryptominers. Flag unusual .NET assembly execution, DLL loading from temp directories, or process trees where ScreenConnect spawns unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GPU Utilization Spike Without User Activity
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets high-performance GPU systems; resource hijacking (T1496) should be detected via performance baselines, but no infrastructure or endpoint behavior detection exists in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline GPU and CPU utilization per user/system. Alert when sustained GPU load >80% occurs during off-hours or without corresponding user process activity (idle desktop, no active game/rendering app). Cross-reference with process execution history to identify mining software.

suggestion.title: Detect BadHost Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Attackers Can Exploit BadHost to Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints' — exploitation is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero rules for detecting exploit attempts against known BadHost paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests containing BadHost exploit patterns, command injection payloads, or known CVE PoC signatures targeting /agent, /endpoint, or /api paths. Flag requests from external networks or unusual source IPs to these sensitive URIs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Access to Protected AI Agent Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Impact described as access to 'Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints' — successful exploitation grants unauthorized endpoint access. Zero rules generated for detecting this post-exploitation state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 200/201 HTTP responses to protected /agent/*, /model/*, or /service/* endpoints originating from non-whitelisted IPs or lacking required authentication tokens. Correlate successful access with subsequent lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect Agent Capability and Model Discovery Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Once endpoint access is gained, attackers enumerate agent capabilities and available models. Standard post-compromise discovery behavior not detected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency sequential requests to agent metadata endpoints (/capabilities, /models, /endpoints, /health) within short time windows following successful authentication, especially from previously-unseen principals.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Spray Attacks Against Active Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency'—the threat is named directly yet no detection UC was suggested for this common attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts (Event 4625 / logon failure) against distinct user accounts originating from a single source IP within a short time window (5–10 minutes). Filter out expected service accounts and noise. Flag when failed-login count exceeds threshold (e.g., >5 unique users in 10 minutes).

suggestion.title: Detect Accounts Attempting to Use Compromised Passwords
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses breach-password protection: 'continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials'—organizations need to detect when users attempt logon with credentials flagged in breach databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful logon events (Event 4624) with identity data enriched against known-breach password lists. Flag accounts that successfully authenticate after their credentials appeared in a breach database, especially if they had not previously changed that password.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Active Directory Password Policy Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses policy changes ('tying expiration periods to password length'); adversaries often modify AD password policies to persist, evade, or lower security. Pipeline should have flagged defense-evasion scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Directory Service event logs (Event 5136 Object Modified, 5137 DirectoryService Object Created) for unauthorized changes to password policy GPOs or default domain policy password settings. Alert on modifications to MinPasswordLength, MaxPasswordAge, ComplexityEnabled, or PasswordHistoryCount from non-approved admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Self-Service Password Reset Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends self-service resets with MFA: 'verifying identity through MFA or other authentication methods.' Attackers often abuse password reset flows to gain account access; absence of detection use case is a gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset request logs for multiple failed reset attempts against the same account (credential stuffing), resets from geographically impossible locations within seconds, or repeated resets outside business hours. Flag when MFA bypass or invalid token submission is logged.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Reuse Across Enterprise Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'are likely to repeat it across other systems simply because remembering dozens of credentials isn't realistic'—credential reuse is a stated threat, yet no detection for reused passwords was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication events across different systems (AD, email, VPN, web apps) with the same username. Detect when the same account authenticates in rapid succession across multiple services with identical or similar credential patterns, indicating reused passwords that could indicate compromised credentials are in use.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated cPanel API Exploitation - Redis Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' parameter allowing 'remote attackers with no privileges' to trigger the vulnerability. Direct attack vector requiring no authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel web logs for HTTP requests containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble', especially from external IPs or sources without prior authentication context. Successful responses (HTTP 200) from unauthenticated sources indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation enables 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—a critical privilege boundary violation from unprivileged web context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with UID 0 (root) spawned from cPanel web service processes running under unprivileged UIDs. Flag arbitrary script execution (bash, perl, python) inconsistent with routine cPanel operations.

suggestion.title: Detection via Provided cPanel Log Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exploitation detection command: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/'—direct log signature for attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs for entries containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble'. Correlate source IPs against whitelist and alert on external/unauthenticated sources. Implement the recommended investigation step: block invalid IPs and examine system logs for actions by detected IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Log Examination and Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs', indicating attackers access and review cPanel logs post-compromise to cover tracks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file access (read/write/delete) to /var/cpanel/logs or /usr/local/cpanel/logs from cPanel processes or web workers outside normal administrative workflows. Monitor for log rotation anomalies or file size reductions indicating tampering.

suggestion.title: Version Fingerprinting of Vulnerable cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects 'user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4'. Attackers must enumerate version before exploitation; banner grabbing and version probes are prerequisite reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance: banner grabbing attempts, requests to cPanel diagnostic endpoints, or version-disclosure probes. Correlate version detection attempts with subsequent cpanel_jsonapi_func exploitation attempts within narrow time windows (< 1 hour).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised cPanel Root Context
suggestion.rationale: Root privilege execution grants attacker complete host control. Subsequent lateral movement to customer databases, other internal systems, or data exfiltration is expected post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting CVE-2026-48172 exploitation, monitor cPanel server for unexpected outbound SSH, RDP, or database connections from root context. Alert on mass file transfers, credential dumping tools, or reconnaissance commands executed with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Version Published to Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product...published to the npm registry'—need detection of unexpected package metadata changes, version jumps, or registry anomalies under the TanStack identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for CVE-2026-45321-related TanStack package versions; flag versions with unexpected checksums, unusual metadata changes, or rapid re-publishing. Cross-reference against known good versions in version manifests.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Malware Process Behavior Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing malware' delivered via the package—execution phase must show registry/credential-store access anomalies after npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawned from node.js or npm child processes attempting to access HKLM\SAM, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, or credential manager APIs within 60s of npm install of CVE-2026-45321 package.

suggestion.title: Trusted npm Account Identity Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware 'published under a trusted identity'—indicates account compromise or impersonation; detection should flag atypical publishing activity from known vendor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm publish events from TanStack canonical accounts with unusual geographic origin, IP, timestamp, or velocity; correlate with GitHub Actions logs for unexpected CI runs publishing to registry.

suggestion.title: npm Package Dependency Resolver Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Detection of the initial delivery vector—organizations installing CVE-2026-45321 will see unusual package resolution or version lock-file mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm or yarn resolves TanStack package to versions matching CVE-2026-45321 fingerprint; validate against package-lock.json or yarn.lock integrity and compare checksum against npmjs.com metadata.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials from npm Malware
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials are stolen (article: 'credential-stealing malware'), expect follow-on lateral movement or persistence using harvested credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential theft signals (registry/API access) with downstream authentication anomalies: failed logins with harvested passwords, unexpected RDP/WinRM sessions, or service account usage spikes within 5min–2hr of malware execution window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48027 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and sets Federal due date 2026-06-10. This is the canonical first detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Nx Console installations matching CVE-2026-48027. Prioritize hosts updated between publication date and Federal due date. Cross-reference with asset patch-compliance metrics.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Supply Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'a malicious version of Nx Console to be published.' This is T1195 supply-chain compromise, not just public-facing app exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console extension installation/updates. Flag installations from untrusted sources, versions with mismatched hashes, or rapid version changes. Correlate install timestamps against malicious version release window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Multiple Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory' — direct credential access attack is primary attacker objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned from Nx Console context accessing browser credential stores, OS vaults, SSH keys, or cached authentication tokens in sequence. Short time-to-complete and high-entropy access pattern indicate automated harvesting.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Retrieval and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — network retrieval and execution of obfuscated code are distinct kill-chain steps requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx Console for unexpected network connections retrieving packed/obfuscated binaries or scripts. Correlate with child process execution, especially powershell, cmd, or bash spawned with suspicious argument patterns.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Processes from Nx Console
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension executes fetched payload as child process. Article does not name process names, but behavioral execution context is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from Nx Console executable or installation directory with elevated privileges, obfuscated command lines, or script-interpreter invocations (cmd, powershell, bash, python).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Credential Use Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: After credentials harvested, attacker likely uses them for lateral movement or persistence. Article establishes credential theft as primary payload objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-harvesting timeline (detected above) with subsequent authentication anomalies: logins from new geolocations, impossible travel, unusual service principal activity, or RDP/SSH connections using harvested secrets.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Asset Hunt: Daemon Tools Lite Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Daemon Tools Lite' as the vulnerable product with 'Federal patch due: 2026-05-30'—enterprises must enumerate all instances before remediation deadline. Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Daemon Tools Lite installations across endpoints and filter for unpatched/vulnerable versions. Correlate software inventory against CVE-2026-8398 patch status to surface high-risk assets requiring urgent remediation before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Patch Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal 2026-05-30 due date creates temporal urgency and audit/compliance liability. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—must track remediation progress and flag missed deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track CVE-2026-8398 status across fleet pre- and post-remediation. Alert on hosts showing 'vulnerable' status after patch deployment attempts. Flag any unpatched instances at deadline threshold (2026-05-29 EOD) for escalation.

suggestion.title: Continuous High-Frequency API Probing from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' Defenders need to detect this baseline anomaly behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high-rate API requests from single source IP targeting multiple endpoints or object IDs within short time window. Baseline normal API request patterns per app, alert on >3σ deviation in request frequency or endpoint diversity per source.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Exploitation — Unauthorized Cross-User/Cross-Tenant Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage' and notes 'User A should not be able to read user B's invoice' — this is a key exploitation pattern requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests where authenticated user attempts to access resources scoped to a different user ID, tenant ID, or account context. Track authorization check failures followed by successful data returns. Correlate request patterns showing systematic ID/tenant enumeration.

suggestion.title: API Object Enumeration — Sequential Identifier Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'structural reasoning about how API objects relate to identities' and 'probe, observe, reason, escalate, validate' — attackers enumerate valid object/user relationships through iteration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of API requests with rapidly incrementing or systematically-varied user IDs, tenant IDs, or resource identifiers from single source. Flag when >20 sequential numeric IDs are requested in <5 minute window with >80% 404/403 response ratio (indicating enumeration rather than legitimate access).

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation Pattern — Sequential Vulnerability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path' — defenders should correlate successive exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed authorization probes, auth bypass attempts, or injection payloads from same source in sequence within 10-minute window. Flag when pattern transitions from reconnaissance (enumeration, info-gathering) to exploitation (payload injection, privilege escalation attempts) without expected session reset.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempt — Failed Auth Followed by Successful Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as context-dependent vulnerabilities requiring detection. Authentication bypass patterns precede unauthorized data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect temporal proximity between failed authentication attempts and subsequent successful API calls using same or forged credentials. Flag when failed login is immediately followed (within 1 minute) by successful authenticated API call with same user agent/source IP but different auth token or header manipulation indicators.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Leakage Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'cross-tenant data leakage' as a key vulnerability. Defenders need behavioral detection for multi-tenant boundary violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In multi-tenant applications, detect users accessing API resources or data objects belonging to different tenant contexts. Flag requests where tenant_id in request path/params differs from authenticated user's tenant_id. Correlate with data egress patterns (large response payloads, bulk export API calls).

suggestion.title: Phishing emails impersonating IT support targeting law firms
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails from newly registered or typosquatted IT support domain variants sent to law firm/legal org employees. Correlate with whois registration age <30 days and typosquat patterns (e.g., 'it-helpdesk-portal.local' vs 'ithelpdesk-portal.local'). High confidence if followed by credential-phishing or callback instructions.

suggestion.title: Remote desktop session access following IT support impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' after phishing or phone contact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP/remote access tool initiations (mstsc.exe, TeamViewer, AnyDesk, etc.) by users who were recently targeted by phishing (matching email sender domain from 24h prior). Escalate if session originates from external IP and user has no history of remote work.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB/external drive connections on corporate systems
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers' as attack vector when in-person access is gained: 'malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for USB device connections followed by large-volume file access/copying to removable media within 10 minutes. Alert especially on: (1) devices connected outside business hours, (2) connections on systems with prior remote access sessions, (3) bulk transfers of sensitive file types (*.docx, *.pdf, *.xlsx from /Legal, /Financials shares).

suggestion.title: Callback phishing and phone-based social engineering targeting employees
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and references 'callback phishing' campaigns from May 2025 FBI notification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound phishing emails mentioning 'IT support callback required' with phone logs showing calls to law firm employees in the same 2-hour window. Flag campaigns where phishing email domain + caller ID both impersonate IT. Review voicemail transcripts for remote access requests.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via remote access tools or removable media post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes SRG 'exfiltrate data, usually through legitimate remote access tools or by sending an individual in-person to the victim company's location' and threats to 'sell or post it on their leak site.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk data transfers via remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk uploads >500MB) or simultaneous file reads from sensitive directories with USB device connection. Combine with user activity anomalies: rare remote tool execution, off-hours activity, legal/financial file access.

suggestion.title: Physical presence of unauthorized individuals claiming IT support
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags as indicator: 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' when 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference physical security badge logs with IT department roster. Alert on badge entries from unregistered/external users who claim IT affiliation. Escalate if coincident with failed VPN access attempts, phishing campaigns, or after-hours facility access. Coordinate with security team on badge verification.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Bulk Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '300+ fake domains' — clear infrastructure setup signal. No detection for coordinated domain registration clusters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify 50+ domains sharing registrar, nameserver, or IP space registered within 48-72 hour windows. Cross-reference against phishing keyword patterns (FIFA, World, Cup, tickets, login, official).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets fans with fake domains — implicit typosquatting of legitimate sports properties. No behavioral detection for user navigation to lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks to domains with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known FIFA/sports sites, combined with recent registration (<30 days) and absence of security indicators (HSTS, valid SSL chain, brand trust seals).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious Domain Link
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign described as targeting fans — implication of email-based delivery. Pipeline has no email IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with URLs pointing to domains <30 days old, unregistered/suspicious registrars, or matching FIFA/sports keywords. Flag messages failing DMARC/SPF alignment.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form on Phishing Domain
suggestion.rationale: Fake domains imply landing pages collecting credentials. Article context missing from extraction, but phishing infrastructure strongly suggests credential collection phase (T1589.002).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST to phishing domain IPs for credential-like parameters (password, email, account, token, pin). Correlate source IPs against VPN/proxy services and geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: DNS Query Spike to Newly-Registered Domains
suggestion.rationale: 300+ domains suggests bulk infrastructure testing and user traffic. No pattern for anomalous DNS query volume to low-reputation/young domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single hosts or user cohorts generating >10 DNS queries to distinct domains all registered <14 days prior within 5-minute window. Baseline against legitimate sports fan behavior during World Cup events.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm modification with embedded Java compilation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text' and 'ChangeMissionDatabase privilege.' Missing detection for suspicious Java code (Runtime.getRuntime, ProcessBuilder, reflection APIs) in algorithm API payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP PATCH/POST payloads to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoints for keywords Runtime, ProcessBuilder, getRuntime, Method.invoke, Class.forName, or ObjectInputStream. Spike in requests with Java source code in body during off-hours or from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Yamcs privilege escalation to ChangeMissionDatabase role
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege.' No hunt for privilege grants or role assumption detected. This is a critical prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs API logs (or auth system logs if integrated) for role grants, policy attachments, or privilege escalations to ChangeMissionDatabase. Correlate with subsequent algorithm modifications.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm configuration file tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'algorithm text' stored in configuration. Detecting modifications to algorithm definition files (e.g., MDB config files, YAML, XML) could catch disk-side exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of files matching Yamcs MDB paths (typically under /etc/yamcs/ or similar) or algorithm definition files (.algo, .mdb extensions) for unexpected writes by non-admin users or system services spawning editors.

suggestion.title: Yamcs server JVM log collection for Janino compilation errors
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Janino expression engine. Compilation failures or exceptions in JVM logs (catalina.out, Yamcs logs) would indicate exploitation attempts or failed payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Yamcs JVM/application logs for 'Janino', 'CompileException', 'SyntaxError' in algorithm compilation context, or unusually high exception rates during algorithm evaluation. Baseline normal compilation failures and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or low-privilege access to Yamcs algorithm API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authenticated user,' implying baseline should be restricted. Missing detection for API calls to algorithm endpoints from unexpected source IPs, users, or auth contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Yamcs admin accounts and networks accessing /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoints. Alert on requests from new/unexpected sources, service accounts, or anonymous sessions.

suggestion.title: Janino expression engine abuse via API introspection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'user-controlled algorithm text' compiled dynamically. Janino allows reflection; missing hunt for attempts to invoke reflection, bytecode manipulation, or system-level APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request bodies to algorithm endpoints for keywords: 'invoke', 'reflect', 'getMethod', 'getDeclaredMethod', 'newInstance', 'defineClass', 'BytecodeProvider'. Correlate with subsequent child process spawning.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Renderer Property-Access Gadget Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article payload `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}{{r|inspect}}` followed by `r.context.scopes`, `r.liquid.parser`, `r.liquid.options.fs` shows attacker probing renderer object graph. This is the gadget-chain setup before RCE. Detection should trigger on suspicious property-access patterns in template AST or filter evaluation logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiquidJS renders template with filter chain accessing internal objects (context, parser, options). Monitor template AST for valueOf, constructor, prototype, or multi-level property access on render-context objects. Flag templates containing 'r.liquid.' or 'r.context.' property traversal.

suggestion.title: Prototype Pollution via __proto__ Assignment in LiquidJS Templates
suggestion.rationale: Payload includes `assign __proto__` which is prototype-pollution precondition. Article text confirms '__proto__' and 'constructor' are gadget-chain components ('assign __proto__'). Direct detection of __proto__ assignment in template filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inbound HTTP requests containing template syntax with __proto__, constructor, or prototype keywords. Search for: 'assign __proto__', '__proto__:', 'constructor.prototype', escaped variants ('%5F%5F', '%70%72%6F%74%6F'). High precision; low FP.

suggestion.title: Node Module Import Chaining from LiquidJS Context
suggestion.rationale: Article shows `getBuiltinModule` and `child_process` as post-gadget targets. Attacker chains prototype-pollution → module loader access → child_process spawn. Detection focuses on Node.js require/import of dangerous modules from web-context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.exe or web process (node, w3wp) calls require('child_process') or similar module-load followed by execSync/spawn within same process lifetime. Correlate module-load timing with inbound HTTP request timestamps to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Suspicious /etc/passwd or System-Config Access via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: Article use-case UC_10_1 detects /etc/passwd modification but is wrongly phased. Correct detection: any filesystem access to sensitive OS files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /root/.ssh) by Node.js or IIS process following LiquidJS SSTI indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File open/read events for /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh or Windows equivalents (SAM, SECURITY hive) initiated by node.exe, w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe. Correlate timing with LiquidJS HTTP requests. Exclude legitimate package-scan operations.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Template with Circular Reference Inspection
suggestion.rationale: Attack entry-point: `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}{{r|inspect}}` reveals circular references in rendering context. An attacker first probes renderer structure to enumerate gadgets. Detection: Templates containing `valueOf` filter or `inspect` on simple assignments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Template syntax containing 'valueOf' filter or 'inspect' function on single-token assignments (e.g., {%assign X=1|valueOf%}). Low severity alone but high precision for reconnaissance phase; correlate with subsequent payloads for full attack chain.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Outbound Connection from Node.js Process Post-LiquidJS RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE via template injection and child-process spawning, but missing detection for post-exploitation behavior: attacker likely establishes reverse shell or C2 callback. Detection should catch outbound connections from spawned shell process with Node parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound network connection initiated by cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with parent process node.exe or w3wp.exe within seconds of process creation. Flag connections to non-standard ports or private IP ranges from web-tier servers.

suggestion.title: Yamcs guest/default user accessing ChangeMissionDatabase API
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In Yamcs's default configuration (no `security.yaml`), the built-in `guest` user…' This indicates default users have dangerous privilege. UC should detect first-time or anomalous guest-user API calls to MdbOverrideApi, or privilege escalation from guest to admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests from guest or anonymous users to /api/mdb-overrides/* endpoints, or sudden elevation of guest-user role from read-only to ChangeMissionDatabase. Baseline: guest users should rarely touch API endpoints; any access is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm override enumeration / failed-then-successful pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes user-supplied algorithm evaluation in MdbOverrideApi. Attackers likely enumerate or test payloads before deploying RCE. UC should detect: multiple PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* in short window, with varying request bodies or response codes (failures followed by success).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* from same source within 60 seconds, or pattern of HTTP 400/500 responses followed by 200 OK from same user. This indicates payload testing or algorithm probing.

suggestion.title: Nashorn alternative RCE patterns (indirect class loading, compat mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Nashorn ScriptEngine without ClassFilter, enabling Java.type exploitation. But Nashorn has alternate RCE vectors: load('nashorn:mozilla_compat'), importPackage(java.lang), indirect Class.forName. UC_2_2 catches direct Java.type but misses obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH/POST requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* containing: load('nashorn:mozilla_compat'), importPackage(java.), Class.forName, or var statements assigning Java.type results. Flag as high-confidence if paired with shell-spawning in UC_2_3.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE credential/config access from Yamcs process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE on 'Yamcs server'. After shell execution (UC_2_3), attacker will exfiltrate credentials, SSH keys, security.yaml, or database configs. UC should correlate Java process with file access to sensitive paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java process (parent=Yamcs, identified by command-line args 'yamcs' or 'org.yamcs') reading files: ~/.ssh/*, security.yaml, yamcs.properties, *.key, *.pem, or database config paths within 30 seconds of shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from compromised Yamcs server
suggestion.rationale: Yamcs is satellite/telemetry control software, implying integration with larger infrastructure. Post-RCE, attacker will pivot to adjacent systems. UC should detect outbound scanning, credential-stuffing, or remote-access attempts from Yamcs host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SSH, RDP, WinRM, or HTTP scanning initiated from Yamcs server IP to internal network ranges post-compromise. Correlate timing with successful exploitation (UC_2_2 + UC_2_3).

suggestion.title: Malicious algorithm persistence / mission-database backdoor
