Flag apps with legitimate signer certificate but suspicious behavior profile or undocumented permissions.

suggestion.title: Affiliate Code Injection Domain Requests from System UID
suggestion.rationale: Malware must contact C2/tracking infrastructure to resolve affiliate redirect domains or fetch injection payloads. System process making requests to non-standard domains reveals injection infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP connections from system UID (< 10000) to affiliate tracking/shortener domains (*.amazon-oa.com, tracking.amazon.*, bitly, etc.). Cross-reference resolved IPs against known affiliate injection campaigns. Alert on anomalous outbound HTTPS to non-Amazon infrastructure from preinstalled app.

suggestion.title: Detect Automated Data Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes data theft as the foundation of the extortion economy: 'explores trends in data theft and extortion, outlining key strategies.' No use cases capture detection of bulk data movement or staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag high-volume outbound transfers to unrecognized cloud storage, archive sites, or attacker-associated IP ranges, especially from user endpoints with large file aggregation patterns in the hours prior.

suggestion.title: Monitor Telegram Bot and Extortion Channel Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Telegram as infrastructure for the extortion economy. Pipeline missed detection of C2 or negotiation channels: 'supply chain, Telegram' keywords present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS queries, TLS handshakes, or HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Telegram bot endpoints associated with named threat actors, especially when originating from corporate gateways or compromised internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltrated Data Posting on Threat Actor Leak Sites
suggestion.rationale: Extortion model requires actors to publish stolen data; article discusses the 'evolving cyber extortion economy' but pipeline generated no impact-phase detection. Leak site posts by ShinyHunters, Bling Libra, etc. are final proof of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference external threat intelligence feeds, dark web monitors, and leak site aggregators to detect when an organization's name, domain, or employee credentials appear on known extortion actors' data leak portals.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack Pattern Detection via Vendor Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article calls out 'supply chain' as a vector. Pipeline missed use case for detecting when attackers compromise vendors or suppliers to gain access to multiple downstream organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual authentication patterns from third-party vendor accounts, phishing campaigns targeting vendor staff, or anomalous file access/sharing from vendor-associated identities with permissions to multiple business units.

suggestion.title: Frontier AI Model Abuse for Extortion Payload Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle explicitly mentions 'as frontier AI models advance.' Pipeline failed to surface detection for AI-generated malware, phishing, or ransom note sophistication as a new tactical shift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with extremely polished, contextually coherent ransom demands or phishing payloads; detect process execution chains that invoke LLM APIs or contain markers of AI-generated code payloads; correlate with known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: FortiClient Code Execution via Vulnerable Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states FortiClient 'Code Execution Vulnerability Exploited' — no detection use case for vulnerable client versions attempting exploit patterns or patched version enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child processes spawned by FortiClient (fcagent.exe, forticlient.exe) or unexpected network communication from FortiClient to external infrastructure. Alert on versions known to be vulnerable unless patched.

suggestion.title: EKZ Malware Process Execution and C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions EKZ malware deployment but pipeline extracted no payload indicators or execution signatures. 'Deploy EKZ Malware' phrase establishes executable ingestion and execution step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect EKZ malware process creation, file writes to temp/startup folders, registry persistence mechanisms, and suspicious parent-child relationships following FortiClient process termination or injection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Endpoint via FortiClient Credentials
suggestion.rationale: FortiClient often stores VPN/network credentials. Exploitation could lead to lateral movement; article implies post-compromise activity but pipeline identified no credential-access or lateral-movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous VPN authentication patterns or outbound network connections from the compromised FortiClient host to internal resources shortly after infection timestamp.

suggestion.title: EKZ C2 Communication and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'deployment' implies C2 setup; no use case for detecting command-and-control traffic or data exfiltration signatures specific to EKZ family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS traffic from EKZ-infected hosts to known or suspected C2 domains/IPs. Monitor for beaconing patterns (regular callback intervals).

suggestion.title: Cannot recommend without article content
suggestion.rationale: Article body provided is exclusively CSS font-face definitions. No actual narrative content, threat descriptions, attack steps, or security recommendations are readable. The title '[HIGH] 3 SOC Steps that Shut Down Incident Risks Early' implies defensive controls or detection guidance, but specific techniques cannot be mapped without the actual text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unable to formulate hypothesis without article content.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Suspicious Domain Recommendations Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites'—the chatbot becomes the delivery mechanism. Pipeline missed this primary attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot API response logs and recommendation outputs for anomalous URLs. Flag recommendations to newly registered domains, domains with malware reputation, or domains not previously recommended. Correlate timing and recommendation frequency across user cohorts to identify coordinated poisoning.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Process Execution on Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployed via redirect is explicitly cryptojacking; article does not specify the post-infection detection method for mining processes or resource abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect crypto-mining binaries (xmrig, ethminer, cryptonight variants) by process name, command line, and file hash. Correlate sustained CPU/GPU spike (>70% for >5min) with unexpected process launch. Monitor outbound connections from mining process to known pool IPs and C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Redirect Chain to Malware Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow is Chatbot → Redirect → Malware Site. No UC generated for detecting the redirect chains themselves that bridge user click to payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP/HTTPS redirect chains (≥3 hops) originating from chatbot recommendation domains. Flag chains terminating in newly registered, low-reputation, or malware-category domains. Alert on redirect chains that bypass corporate URL filters or reputation engines.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Chatbot Model Output or Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Chatbot recommendations are poisoned—either via model compromise, prompt injection, or service-layer tampering. Pipeline did not surface detection for malicious inference patterns or model hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot inference logs for: (1) statistically unusual recommendation outputs vs. baseline, (2) clustering of malicious URLs in single session, (3) recommendations to domains not in historical training data, (4) injection keywords or payloads in user inputs preceding malicious recommendations.

suggestion.title: Malware Infrastructure Domain DNS Resolution Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'cryptojacking malware sites' (plural). Pipeline should identify and IOC-track those domains; no domain/IP extraction occurred despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS query logs for known malware distribution domains mentioned in campaign reporting. Detect bulk DNS queries to newly registered domains sharing naming patterns (typosquats, TLD variants). Monitor passive DNS for recent registrations matching attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Service API Compromise or Authorization Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Root-cause detection gap: pipeline did not identify upstream compromise signals (API credential theft, unauthorized service access, configuration injection) enabling recommendation poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls with unusual authentication patterns, cross-region/IP access to chatbot endpoints, bulk recommendation-output modifications, or API token reuse. Correlate with timing of poisoning campaign launch and user-session anomalies.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed AD Logins—Password Spraying Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' to use weak passwords. Describes T1110.003 attack class attacking AD accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on source IP generating 10+ failed AD logon attempts to distinct user accounts within 5 minutes, where all failures share the same or similar password (if observable via auth failure codes). Filter for on-premises AD and exclude known password-reset tools.

suggestion.title: Password Reset Using Known-Breached Credential
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials' and Verizon stat: 'stolen credentials involved in 44.7% of breaches.' Maps to T1110.004 (Credential Stuffing) or offline reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag AD password-change events where new password matches entries in known-breach databases (HIBP or internal correlations). Correlate with preceding failed logon attempts from unfamiliar location/IP to detect credential-stuffing recovery.

suggestion.title: Predictable Password Incremental Change
suggestion.rationale: Article describes user workaround: 'minimal tweaks, changing a few characters' and predictable patterns like 'Password!2026.' Enables T1110.001 (Password Guessing) when attacker has old password.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect password-change events where Levenshtein distance between old and new password is <3, or new password appends/prepends single characters to old, or increments year/sequence numbers. Alert if user had high failed-logon rate prior to reset.

suggestion.title: Same Credential Used Across Multiple Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article: users 'repeat [passwords] across other systems simply because remembering dozens of credentials isn't realistic.' Enables lateral movement when credentials from one system compromise another.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of accounts legitimately using same credentials across multiple systems (service accounts, shared roles). Alert on deviation: same UPN + password hash (or same authentication principal) authenticating to unexpected systems, applications, or geographies in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Detect cPanel redisAble API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs' and 'If this command results in any output, we recommend you examine the IPs.' Direct log pattern for exploitation attempts already provided; pipeline ignored it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search cPanel logs for cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble invocations, especially from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with Redis enable/disable configuration changes. Establish baseline of legitimate admin IPs and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation via Redis Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'incorrect privilege assignment weakness that enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' This is the core attack—unauthorized to root in a single step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution or API calls where unprivileged user context triggers root-level actions in cPanel plugin functions. Look for redisAble function invocations followed by high-privilege operations without intermediate sudo or authentication.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'vulnerability is being actively exploited, and poses a risk for all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4.' Version range critical for scope assessment but pipeline generated no inventory-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for cPanel LiteSpeed plugin versions v2.3 through v2.4.4. Cross-reference with patched versions (post-v2.4.5 implied). Alert on unpatched systems in production, especially federal or critical infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution Post-Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables remote attackers...to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' This is the impact phase; detection should monitor for unexpected script execution in privileged context post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate cPanel plugin API activity (especially redisAble) with subsequent child process creation or script execution running as root. Look for anomalous script sources or encoding (Base64, hex) suggesting obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Redis Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features.' Attempts to modify Redis settings without explicit admin action should trigger alerts, especially if initiated via plugin API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Redis configuration files for unexpected enable/disable state changes. Alert if Redis config modifications occur without corresponding authorized administrative actions in cPanel logs within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation — TanStack Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious versions of the product... published to the npm registry.' Pipeline must hunt for installation of compromised TanStack packages; developers installing from npm is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or npm.exe spawning from package.json in development environments. Cross-reference installed package versions against CISA advisory timeline (published 2026-05-27). Look for npm install/update commands targeting TanStack in the ~72hr window before remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from npm Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'credential-stealing malware under a trusted identity.' Once malicious package executes, look for credential harvesting artifacts (environment variable reads, .bash_history theft, AWS credential access, browser storage).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After TanStack installation, hunt for node/npm child processes reading sensitive files (.aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa, browser local storage). Correlate with outbound HTTP/HTTPS to non-standard destinations from development machines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'malicious versions... publish credential-stealing malware.' Compromised npm packages execute arbitrary code on installation or first require(). Detect unusual process spawning from node_modules directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process parent path containing 'node_modules' that spawns children other than expected node/npm child processes (e.g., powershell.exe, cmd.exe, python.exe spawned from node_modules/.bin/). High fidelity if spawned process is unsigned or unsigned by TanStack.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Audit — TanStack Package Publish Events
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'malicious versions... published to the npm registry.' External detection: query npm audit logs or use npm security advisories API to flag when TanStack package metadata changes or new versions published in the advisory window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subscribe to npm publish events for TanStack packages. Flag any version releases between 2026-05-27 (article publish) and 2026-06-10 (patch deadline). Cross-reference against official TanStack release notes. Any unattested release is candidate for supply-chain compromise.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Credential Exfiltration Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing malware.' Post-infection, expect lateral movement prep: SSH keys copied, git credentials harvested, .env files read, cloud credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For machines with recent TanStack npm installs, hunt for file read access to .ssh/, .aws/, .git/config, .env, browser cookie stores, and /etc/passwd. Correlate with unexpected HTTPS/DNS to external IP space 10+ minutes post-installation.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Hash Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'malicious versions... published.' EDR/DevOps platforms can verify installed package hashes against npm registry. A mismatch is a red flag for local tampering or man-in-the-middle compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare hash of installed TanStack package against npm registry official hash. Alert if hash mismatch, missing signature, or package-lock.json does not match installed version. High-priority if timestamp of installed package precedes official npm publish time.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Disk and Memory via Nx Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload 'could harvest credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory' — core malicious behavior, must be detectable via suspicious file/registry access patterns and LSASS/credential-manager process interactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console or node.exe child processes reading credential storage paths (%APPDATA%\*\Login Data, %USERPROFILE%\.aws, %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Vault) and accessing LSASS or credential-manager process memory. Flag child process spawns post-payload fetch with high entitlement requests.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Obfuscated Payload Download and Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromised extension 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — detectable as post-installation network beaconing from IDE process + suspicious local staging/deobfuscation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound HTTPS/DNS from Nx Console process or node.exe children to non-standard domains. Correlate with subsequent base64-decode or gzip-expand cmdlet invocations. Flag PowerShell/cmd children spawned within 2 minutes post-download; monitor for in-memory execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Nx Console Extension Installation from Non-Official Source
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector: 'malicious version of Nx Console to be published'. Installation events and manifest integrity mismatches are detectable. Article does not specify whether installed from official marketplace or sideloaded.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .vscode/extensions, IDE plugin registries, and npm cache for Nx Console extension installation. Flag installations outside official marketplace. Track extension.json manifest for version mismatches (reported version vs. actual binary hash). Alert on unsigned or self-signed extension manifests.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Nx Console Version Inventory (CISA KEV Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active wild exploitation and federal patch deadline 2026-06-10. Standard required hunt for all Nx Console installations, versions, and patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all endpoints with Nx Console installed (global and per-user). Flag any version < fixed version (unspecified in article). Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results against inventory for false negatives. Prioritize high-risk users (developers, DevOps, cloud infrastructure teams).

suggestion.title: Abnormal Child Process Spawning from Nx Console Extension Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Credential harvesting payloads typically spawn cmd/PowerShell/certutil for credential dump operations. Article states payload executes locally — process tree anomalies are high-fidelity signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes of Nx Console extension (node.exe, electron.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe, or credential-dumping tools. Flag parent-child process pairs with mismatched user contexts or unexpected working directories. Alert on network-connected child processes.

suggestion.title: Registry/File System Writes to Credential Storage Locations by Nx Process
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'fetched...obfuscated payload' that 'could harvest' — sophisticated variants may exfiltrate *and* persist credentials locally. File/registry write patterns to browser/SSH/cloud config directories are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nx-sourced process writes to %APPDATA%\..., %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, %USERPROFILE%\.aws directories, or HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer credential cache keys. High specificity if correlated with prior credential-read activity.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Daemon Tools Lite Inventory by CVE-2026-8398
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with reference to '_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure' template, and states 'CVE-2026-8398 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline generated no use case despite direct guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for installed Daemon Tools Lite instances and cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-8398. Identify systems running vulnerable versions and prioritize systems with internet exposure. Alert on instances not patched by federal deadline 2026-05-30.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Vulnerability Scanner Match and Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-8398 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the primary detection method and notes federal due date 2026-05-30. Pipeline failed to generate this critical detection despite direct recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when any vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.) detects CVE-2026-8398. Correlate findings with process execution and network logs for potential exploitation attempts. Track remediation progress against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Process Execution and Child Process Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'embedded malicious code' with high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability, implying post-infection detection is necessary beyond asset inventory. Pipeline generated no behavioral or post-compromise detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish process baseline for legitimate Daemon Tools executables (dtimg.exe, daemon.exe). Alert on unexpected child process spawning, particularly suspicious executables, command-line activity, or network connections that deviate from known-good behavior.

suggestion.title: High-Volume API Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed.' Describes systematic reconnaissance: 'recon, probe, observe, reason, escalate, validate.' Detect rapid sequential API discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency requests to API endpoints with varying path segments, query parameters, or identifiers within short windows. Detect systematic testing of non-existent endpoints, admin paths, or version enumeration (v1/, v2/, etc.). Alert on sources making requests to 100+ unique API paths in <5 min.

suggestion.title: Authorization Bypass via Cross-Tenant Object Access Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage, authentication bypasses' as context-dependent flaws detected via 'authorization probes guided by structural reasoning about how API objects relate to identities.' Detect users accessing resources outside their tenant/permission scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests where tenant_id, user_id, or account_id in the API path/payload differs from the authenticated context. Flag repeated parameter enumeration attempts (incrementing IDs: /users/123, /users/124, /users/125) followed by successful access. Alert on 403→200 status transitions on the same resource endpoint after parameter modification.

suggestion.title: Chained Multi-Step Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path' — invisible to heuristic tools. Detect sequences of attacks combining lower-severity findings into high-impact outcomes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate distinct security events in sequence within same session/source: e.g., info disclosure (resource enumeration) → authentication attempt → privilege escalation → data access. Alert when individual steps would be low-severity but sequence indicates exploitation. Example: user enumeration → password spray → BOLA exploitation in <30 min.

suggestion.title: API Schema & Structure Inference via Error Response Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pentesting motion of 'probe, observe, reason' applied to APIs. Attackers map API structure through error messages and behavioral differences to guide subsequent attacks. Detect systematic error-driven reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify sources sending requests designed to extract API metadata: intentionally malformed payloads to trigger verbose error responses, testing HTTP methods (OPTIONS, HEAD, TRACE), directory fuzzing, or comparing response times/sizes to infer resource existence. Alert on sources with high ratio of 400/404/405 responses followed by successful API access.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Intent-Behavior Gap Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'the vulnerability lives in the gap between intended behavior and actual behavior' — authentication bypasses are undetectable by signatures. Detect state-manipulation that circumvents auth intent without violating heuristic rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for auth state inconsistencies: sessions claiming elevated privileges without corresponding SSO/MFA events, successful requests immediately after failed authentication, password reset flows granting access without re-authentication, or token manipulation that shouldn't grant privilege escalation. Detect race conditions between auth checks and protected operations.

suggestion.title: Continuous Unauthorized Vulnerability Scanning Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: defenders must scan 'on a schedule' to keep pace; attackers scan 'continuously at machine speed.' Detect ongoing automated scanning/pentesting activity outside authorized security testing windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify persistent automated scanners probing production: correlation of requests matching scanner signatures (Burp, OWASP ZAP, Nikto), requests at regular intervals from same source, payloads testing known vulns (SQLi, XSS, injection), or User-Agent headers of automated tools. Alert on high-volume low-and-slow scanning outside authorized pentest windows.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Impersonating Internal IT Support
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' Initial access vector via credential and access harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with sender domain external to organization but display name matching internal IT/support aliases. Elevated confidence if email requests user to call back, verify credentials, or enable remote access. Correlate with subsequent RDP logon attempts or VPN access within 2 hours of email open.

suggestion.title: RDP Access Grant Following Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' Execution phase where attacker pivots from social engineering to remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP logons (EventCode 4624, LogonType=10) from external/non-corporate IP addresses within 30 minutes of phishing email recipient activity. Alert on RDP sessions paired with unusual process creation (file copying, data staging tools) or session duration >2 hours for first-time login.

suggestion.title: USB/External Drive Insertion Followed by Bulk Data Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'By going to the victim's location in person, the malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.' Collection phase via removable media exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for USB/external storage device connection events followed within 5 minutes by high-volume file copy operations (robocopy, xcopy, cp -r) targeting removable drives or unfamiliar mount points. Alert on bulk copy of files from restricted directories (C:\Users, program files, database locations).

suggestion.title: Unescorted Individual Claiming IT Access at Physical Location
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies indicator: 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers.' Physical social engineering attack preventing remote-only detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate badge/door access logs against IT ticket system to identify individuals accessing secure areas without corresponding service orders. Alert on discrepancies between claimed IT visit and logged tickets, especially for floor locations housing sensitive data or critical systems.

suggestion.title: Extortion Ransom Email with Data Leak Threat
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees.' Post-compromise extortion communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails from external senders containing keywords 'ransom', 'leak', 'pay', 'deadline', 'public disclosure', 'site' paired with financial demands and threat language. Alert if multiple recipients within same organization receive similar messages within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: DNS/Web Queries to Typosquatted IT Portal Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Infrastructure reconnaissance and phishing preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS requests and HTTP traffic to domains with character substitutions matching known organizational IT support portals (e.g., 'supp0rt' vs 'support', 'helpdesk1' vs 'helpdesk'). Alert on newly registered domains (<14 days old) with these patterns, especially if WHOIS registrant is anonymous or foreign proxy.

suggestion.title: Bulk Lookalike Domain Registration - GHOST STADIUM Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article title states '300+ fake domains' targeting FIFA fans. Pipeline extracted zero domains. Bulk registration of typosquatted/homoglyph domains is the core attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration patterns for clusters of visually-similar domains registered within short time windows, particularly those mimicking legitimate sports/betting properties. Correlate against known GHOST STADIUM campaign indicators (domain registrant info, nameserver clustering, SSL cert issuer patterns).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Form Submission
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting 'FIFA World Cup fans' implies credential capture via fake login/account pages on the 300+ domains. Pipeline missed credential_access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains with form field names matching FIFA/sports betting login patterns (username, password, email, phone). Correlate source IPs posting to multiple GHOST STADIUM domains within same session.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Distribution - GHOST STADIUM Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates phishing campaign; email is implied attack vector but zero email IOCs or detection logic generated. No coverage of T1566.002 (Phishing via Spearphishing Link).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on emails with URLs resolving to GHOST STADIUM domains. Flag emails with FIFA/World Cup urgency language (urgent ticket purchase, account verification required, limited availability). Correlate with domain registration timestamps to catch early campaign waves.

suggestion.title: DNS Typosquatting Detection - Sports Betting/World Cup Properties
suggestion.rationale: 300+ domains implies heavy use of character-substitution and domain-typosquatting (e.g., 'fifa' → 'fífa', 'tickets' → 'tickts'). Pipeline did not identify T1583.001 as acquisition technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries for Levenshtein-distance similarities to known FIFA, World Cup, Ticketmaster, and betting site domains. Flag registrations with Damerau-Levenshtein distance ≤2 from legitimate brands. Correlate WHOIS registrant data to identify shared infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Cluster Attribution - GHOST STADIUM Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Campaign has explicit name ('GHOST STADIUM') but was not surfaced for tracking. Bulk malicious domain registration warrants campaign-level attribution and tracking framework.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build campaign signature around shared WHOIS registrant details, nameserver hosting, SSL certificate issuers, and IP space clustering. Alert on new domain registrations matching GHOST STADIUM fingerprint (e.g., registrant email patterns, hosting infrastructure, domains registered in rapid succession).

suggestion.title: Java Reflection/Runtime API Injection in Yamcs Algorithm Definitions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states engine 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text without enforcing a secure sandbox.' Exploitation payload must contain Runtime.exec() or ProcessBuilder bytecode. Detection gap: no hunt for actual malicious code patterns in algorithm definitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Yamcs MDB for algorithm definition modifications containing Java reflection keywords (java.lang.Runtime, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, getRuntime, exec, newInstance, Method.invoke). Cross-reference source IP and user against approved algorithm maintainers. Correlation with UC_33_5 (PATCH events) strengthens confidence.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized ChangeMissionDatabase Privilege Assignment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this.' Detection gap: no hunt for privilege-escalation attempts or anomalous privilege assignment. Attackers must either compromise existing privileged account or escalate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new users/accounts being granted ChangeMissionDatabase privilege outside change-management windows. Alert on privilege escalation attempts to this role from lower-privilege accounts. Correlate with unusual login times/IPs for affected accounts.

suggestion.title: Yamcs JVM Compilation Errors / Janino Exception Spikes
suggestion.rationale: Janino compilation of malicious bytecode triggers exceptions. Article references 'Janino Expression Engine'—failed/malformed payloads generate compilation errors in application logs. Detection gap: no hunt for elevated exception rates or specific Janino compilation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs for spikes in org.codehaus.janino.CompileException or java.lang.ClassFormatError. Baseline normal exception rates; alert on 5x+ increase. Correlate with concurrent algorithm modification attempts (UC_33_5) to identify payload development testing phase.

suggestion.title: Yamcs Algorithm Modification from Out-of-Band Users/Sources
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires ChangeMissionDatabase role, but legitimate algorithm modifications originate from known, approved users and IP ranges. Detection gap: no hunt for OOB modifications signaling account compromise or insider threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain list of authorized algorithm editors. Hunt for algorithm modifications from users not on list, from IPs outside corporate ranges, or during off-hours. Correlate with failed authentication attempts preceding successful modification (lateral movement post-compromise scenario).

suggestion.title: Yamcs Process Resource Anomalies During Algorithm Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious bytecode compilation and execution induces measurable CPU/memory pressure on JVM. Article describes compilation of untrusted expressions—successful exploitation causes detectable performance degradation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal CPU/memory for Yamcs JVM. Alert on sustained >80% CPU or >70% memory for Yamcs process correlating with concurrent algorithm modification API calls (PATCH /api/mdb/*/algorithms/*). False-positive threshold: legitimate batch algorithm execution typically <60% sustained CPU.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS SSTI gadget tokens in inbound HTTP (UC_11_2)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_11_2 with Splunk SPL detecting `1|valueOf`, `r.context.scopes`, `r.liquid.parser`, `__proto__`, `child_process` in HTTP URLs, and Defender KQL for DeviceNetworkEvents matching these patterns. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for LiquidJS template injection signatures: filter chains like 1|valueOf that leak context objects, and property traversal (via __proto__ or direct chaining) accessing dangerous modules like child_process and fs.

suggestion.title: Node.js web process spawning shell (UC_11_3)
suggestion.rationale: Article defines UC_11_3: shell process (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh) spawned by node.exe, w3wp.exe, or iisnode.exe parent. This is the post-exploitation signature when gadget chains successfully achieve code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell processes spawned from Node.js-based web process parents. RCE via LiquidJS template gadget chains typically result in immediate shell spawning from the template evaluation context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious filesystem access from Node.js template context (UC_11_1)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies UC_11_1: filesystem modifications (create/modify) on /etc/passwd initiated from node processes. Indicates post-RCE reconnaissance or impact phase accessing host configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor filesystem create/modify events on sensitive files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh) when initiated from Node.js processes. Template RCE exploitation chains often include immediate reconnaissance gathering.

suggestion.title: Multi-step gadget chain: Node.js module access from template filters
suggestion.rationale: Article details exploit flow: `1|valueOf` → context.scopes → liquid.options.fs and context traversal → getBuiltinModule → child_process/fs module access. This specific multi-step gadget pattern is not captured by the three listed hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect filter chains accessing Node.js built-in modules: patterns combining getBuiltinModule calls, __proto__ traversal, or require() statements within template evaluation contexts, ultimately targeting child_process, fs, or os modules.

suggestion.title: Yamcs ChangeMissionDatabase privilege abuse or lateral privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'user with the `ChangeMissionDatabase` privilege' can exploit; missing detection for privilege escalation or privilege-based abuse. No UC monitors for unusual use of database-modification privileges or attempts to elevate to this role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to MdbOverrideApi endpoints originating from non-privileged service accounts, or spike in ChangeMissionDatabase API calls from guest/service accounts. Correlate with web logs showing PATCH requests from unexpected or suspicious user identities.

suggestion.title: Mission Database algorithm validation bypass or suspicious algorithm content
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'algorithm text in MdbOverrideApi.updateAlgorithm'; missing detection for the algorithm content itself. Current UCs detect the HTTP request structure but not the payload anomalies (Java.type, getRuntime etc. in algorithm scripts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* where request body contains obfuscated or encoded Java class references, or unusual algorithm syntax mixing JavaScript with Java reflection patterns. Monitor Yamcs application logs for algorithm evaluation errors or exceptions during script parsing.

suggestion.title: Yamcs default guest account exploitation or failed authentication bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'In Yamcs's default configuration (no `security.yaml`), the built-in `guest` user' is vulnerable; no UC detects guest account usage or default-credential exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and alert on non-standard or no-authentication PATCH requests to MdbOverrideApi when security.yaml is absent or default auth is detected. Flag any HTTP requests using guest credentials (or no credentials) to sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: Yamcs configuration file tampering (security.yaml, algorithm definitions)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enabled by missing security.yaml config; no UC monitors for creation, modification, or deletion of Yamcs configuration or database definition files on disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileCreated, FileModified, or FileDeleted events on Yamcs configuration directories (typically /etc/yamcs, ~/.yamcs, or relative config paths), especially changes to security.yaml, algorithm definitions, or mission database files that occur during or shortly after anomalous web activity.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from Yamcs mission database post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE leading to arbitrary code execution but does not cover post-exploitation data theft. If attacker gains shell access, likely next step is data exfiltration of telemetry/mission data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate reverse-shell establishment (UC_3_4) with subsequent large data transfers from the Yamcs host to remote IP:port pairs. Monitor for file-read operations on Yamcs database directories (e.g., **/mdb/**, **/data/**) followed by socket writes or curl/wget processes spawned from the Java process tree.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API authentication event with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege assignment or abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker must possess 'ChangeMissionDatabase' privilege to override algorithm logic. Initial access phase requires either credential compromise or unauthorized privilege grant. Pipeline omitted initial-access and privilege-related detections entirely. Article phrase: 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this by overriding the algorithm…'
log_sources: application logs from Yamcs auth subsystem
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor successful Yamcs API authentication from unexpected source IPs, unusual time-of-day, or service accounts. Track assignments or escalations of ChangeMissionDatabase role/privilege. Correlate with prior failed login attempts or password-spray indicators. Yamcs logs or proxy logs will show POST to /api/auth/* or /api/login endpoints followed by algorithm-modification activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized or suspicious algorithm code modification via REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack via PATCH to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* endpoint. Pipeline generated UC_2_4 for payload content (java.lang.Runtime) but not for the request method/endpoint anomaly itself. Detect baseline deviation: which users/IPs typically PATCH algorithms, and flag outliers. Article phrase: 'overriding the algorithm logic within the Mission Database (MDB) during real-time operation'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* endpoints, especially those containing Jython/Python keywords (import, class, def, java.lang). Baseline normal algorithm-modification frequency, user population, and request payload size. Flag requests with embedded shell commands, file I/O, or network I/O even if obfuscated. Correlate endpoint hits with absence of prior web-based algorithm-design activity.

suggestion.title: Jython ScriptEngine or JSR-223 exception logging anomalies post-patch
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is in 'script evaluation engine for Python algorithms' using 'Jython (via the JSR-223 ScriptEngine API)'. Failed or malformed Jython compilation may emit stack traces or compilation errors to Yamcs logs. Detect exception patterns that suggest payload testing or syntax violations. Article phrase: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text using Jython (via the JSR-223 ScriptEngine API)'
log_sources: Yamcs ScriptEngine or AlgorithmManager component logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs component logs (AlgorithmManager, ScriptEngine subsystem) for exception types: javax.script.ScriptException, CompilationException, java.lang.ClassNotFoundException (if payload attempts to load unexpected classes). A burst of failed script-compilation errors followed by a successful algorithm patch is suspicious. Track stack traces mentioning java.lang.Runtime, java.io.*, or java.net.* to identify intrusion attempts.

suggestion.title: Yamcs process token/session anomaly: ChangeMissionDatabase privilege escalation via API
suggestion.rationale: Even if attacker starts with lower privilege, they may exploit token-handling vulnerabilities to escalate to ChangeMissionDatabase. Article implies privilege is prerequisite; detect how privilege is obtained if not legitimately assigned. Article phrase: 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege…' (but does not specify how a non-privileged user obtains this).
log_sources: API gateway logs with privilege context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track API tokens or session IDs that perform algorithm-modification operations (PATCH /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*) without ChangeMissionDatabase privilege in the originating auth claim/JWT. If token elevation is detected between two requests, flag as privilege-escalation attempt. Correlate with API responses (403 Forbidden initially, then 200 OK after escalation probe).

suggestion.title: Yamcs restart, shutdown, or system-state anomaly post-exploitation (defense evasion / persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Article does not describe persistence mechanisms, but successful RCE via Jython may allow attacker to modify configuration, inject startup hooks, or tamper with Yamcs restart behavior. Detect unexpected service restarts, configuration changes, or JVM arguments being modified. Critical gap: no persistence/defense-evasion hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Yamcs service restarts (e.g., ServiceStarted events within hours of failed algorithm-patch attempts, or without IT ticket correlation). Monitor Yamcs config files (yamcs.yaml, startup scripts) for unauthorized modifications. Track JVM command-line changes, especially additions of -Xbootclasspath, -javaagent, or custom classpath entries that could inject malicious code on startup.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Registry API Access
suggestion.rationale: Title states vulnerability 'exposes private container images without authentication'—pipeline must detect HTTP requests to /v2/ or registry endpoints lacking Authorization headers or valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET requests to container registry API endpoints (/v2/, /api/v2/) from sources without prior authentication context. Flag requests missing standard Docker/registry auth headers (WWW-Authenticate challenge responses followed by Authorization: Bearer tokens).

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Private Container Image Manifests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exposure of 'private' images—implies attacker can list/enumerate images and fetch manifests without credentials. Pipeline should detect discovery of registry contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated GET requests to /v2/<image>/manifests/<tag> or /v2/_catalog endpoints from single source without auth context. Threshold: >5 distinct manifest requests in 5min window or enumeration of >10 image names from unauthenticated session.

suggestion.title: Bulk Private Container Image Downloads via Unauthenticated Registry
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows access to private images—exfiltration phase involves layer downloads. Article phrase 'exposes private container images' indicates data extraction risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to /v2/<image>/blobs/sha256:<hash> (layer downloads) or full image pulls from unauthenticated source. Baseline: flag >50 MB of layer data or >3 distinct images downloaded in single session without valid pull credentials.

suggestion.title: Missing Docker Registry Authentication Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is authentication bypass at Gitea registry endpoint. Pipeline should detect requests that should require auth but receive successful responses (200/206 instead of 401/403).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry HTTP responses: flag 200/206 responses to protected registry paths (/v2/, /blobs/, /manifests/) when request headers lack Authorization field or contain invalid tokens. Compare against baseline of authenticated request patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Developer Extension Installation from Supply Chain Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions' and later 'GitHub repositories and npm packages' as primary attack surface. No detection for suspicious development tool installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution from extension managers (code.exe, npm.exe) and IDE update mechanisms for installations from newly-registered or spoofed package sources. Flag rapid sequential package/extension installations from single process. Alert on file writes to extension directories combined with credential file access shortly after.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Peer Network Querying for C2 Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys' — a decentralized C2 channel with no traditional sinkhole point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections on DHT ports (6881-6889, 1234-6969 ranges) from non-BitTorrent client processes. Detect DNS queries for BitTorrent tracker domains. Flag development tool processes (npm, node, code) making peer-network discovery calls. Correlate multiple failed DHT queries followed by fallback to secondary C2 channels.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar API Abuse for C2 Dead-Drop Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths' — legitimate SaaS service exploitation as C2 delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Calendar API calls from headless or non-interactive processes. Flag events with Base64-encoded or URL-like patterns in title/description fields. Establish baseline of legitimate calendar API usage and alert on deviations. Monitor for repeated queries to same calendar accounts from non-human principals.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain Transaction Monitoring for Encoded C2 Addresses
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop' — blockchain-based C2 requiring network-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS connections to Solana RPC endpoints (api.solana.com, spc.solana.com) from non-financial/development tools. Flag repeated queries to same wallet addresses or accounts. Detect memo field parsing patterns in network traffic. Correlate blockchain lookups with subsequent command execution or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Dormant Malicious Extension Activation on Version Update
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update' — behavioral persistence requiring post-update execution profiling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning within 60 seconds following VS Code or extension update completion. Track modifications to extension manifest files or activation event bindings during updates. Alert on extension processes with elevated privileges or network access post-activation.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential and Wallet Exfiltration by Infected Extensions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies extensions 'stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' — indicating multi-vector credential harvesting requiring file-access and process monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code.exe, npm.exe, or extension processes accessing .ssh directories, .gitconfig, .netrc, or wallet app-data paths. Flag file reads >100KB from credential directories. Detect base64-encoded credential material in process memory or temporary files. Alert on credential access followed by outbound connections to C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: GlassWorm targets 'developer supply chain attack infrastructure'—this implies malicious package or artifact injection into build systems, repositories, or package managers. No UC generated despite being core to the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories, artifact storage, and build automation for suspicious uploads or modifications to developer-facing packages. Flag unsigned or anomalously-signed artifacts. Alert on repository credentials used from atypical IPs or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution in Developer Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: A 'malware takedown' implies executable payloads deployed to developer machines. Title explicitly names 'GlassWorm Malware' but no execution-focused UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of process spawned from build directories, package cache, or Git repositories with parent processes being package managers, build tools (Maven, npm, Gradle), or interpreters. Look for unsigned executables launched from cache or temp directories.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Developer Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Takedown 'disrupts infrastructure'—implies C2 beaconing. Article explicitly discusses infrastructure takedown yet no network-based UC for C2 callback detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from developer machines to non-standard ports and domains. Flag encrypted outbound connections from build agents and development workstations to known or suspected malware C2 indicators. Detect repeated failed DNS queries for malware domains on remediation lists.

suggestion.title: Compromise of Build Tool Credentials and Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often pivot to credential theft from developer environments. 'Developer supply chain' context implies credential access, but no UC for harvesting build tokens, SSH keys, or repository credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized reads of SSH keys, .git credentials, API tokens, or build automation config files. Alert on suspicious command-line usage of git clone/push with hardcoded credentials. Monitor for exfiltration of .ssh and .netrc files or environment variable dumps.

suggestion.title: GlassWorm Malware Artifact and Hash Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero IOCs—no file hashes, filenames, or network indicators despite 'GlassWorm Malware' being explicitly named. Hash-based detection is foundational for malware response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish a baseline of known GlassWorm malware file hashes, process names, and code signing certificates. Alert on any process execution or file creation matching GlassWorm-associated indicators. Flag masquerading attempts (e.g., executables impersonating legitimate developer tools).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Supply Chain Artifact Modification
suggestion.rationale: Takedown implies long-running malicious infrastructure. Supply chain attacks often establish persistence through modified build outputs or dependencies. No UC captures persistence in supply chain context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistence mechanisms in build artifacts: modified DLLs/libraries, compromised startup scripts, or injected hooks in build tool configurations. Alert on unexpected system service registration originating from build directories or package installations.

suggestion.title: Malicious DLL Side-Loading via Utility ZIP Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'archive includes the legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded when launching the benign binary.' Clear delivery mechanism with no corresponding detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ZIP archives containing legitimate system utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear, DisplayDriverUninstaller) paired with unsigned DLLs. Alert when these utilities load DLLs from temporary directories or non-standard paths immediately after extraction.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect C2 Installation via MSIExec from Utility Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'msiexec.exe to install vcredist_x64.dll, which is a package installer for the ScreenConnect remote access tool.' C2 establishment pattern not captured as detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect msiexec.exe spawned from legitimate utility processes installing ScreenConnect components (vcredist_x64.dll). Flag unexpected ScreenConnect.exe process execution with network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing into Microsoft-Signed .NET Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'process hollowing into a legitimate .NET binary signed by Microsoft: InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe.' Core evasion technique with no detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspected process hollowing into Microsoft-signed .NET binaries spawning unusual child processes, loading suspicious modules, or executing without expected command-line arguments. Correlate SimpleRunPE.exe or RuntimeHost.exe file creation with subsequent hollowing attempts.

suggestion.title: Six Persistence Mechanisms via Hidden Folder and Autostart Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'SimpleRunPE.exe that copies itself as RuntimeHost.exe into a folder hidden in Explorer' and 'six persistence mechanisms across multiple Windows autostart locations.' Multi-persistence pattern entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when suspicious binaries establish multiple persistence mechanisms across Run/RunOnce registry keys, Startup directories, WMI event subscriptions, and scheduled tasks. Flag creation of hidden folders or file attribute modifications alongside persistence registry writes.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Modification of Windows Defender Exclusion List
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'malware also invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender.' Defense-evasion action not translated to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell for Add-MpPreference or Set-MpPreference cmdlets modifying exclusion lists, particularly when spawned from ScreenConnect, msiexec, or other suspicious parents. Alert on -EncodedCommand or -NoProfile execution patterns.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Module Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes: 'mining modules is downloaded and executed. The supported mining programs are gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI.' Impact phase and suspicious download pattern not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of known GPU mining tools (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI) from external or attacker-controlled domains. Monitor for unexpected GPU utilization spikes and mining-pool communication patterns following process-hollowing or persistence establishment.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan: Credential Harvesting & C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly positions Grandoreiro as a campaign malware targeting Windows users; no detection logic provided despite clear Windows-focused threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Grandoreiro typically establishes persistence via registry modifications and scheduled tasks, then beacons to C2 servers. Look for suspicious PowerShell execution spawning from system processes, followed by registry writes to Run keys, correlated with outbound HTTPS or HTTP POST traffic to dynamically resolved domains.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT: Remote Access Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies BTMOB RAT as a parallel campaign threat; no behavioral or network signatures captured despite RAT's inherent command-and-control signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: BTMOB RAT typically establishes bidirectional communication with attacker-controlled servers to execute arbitrary code, enumerate processes, and interact with registry. Detect via anomalous process spawning (cmd.exe, PowerShell children from unsigned executables), registry enumeration loops, and outbound connections to non-standard ports from legitimate service processes.

suggestion.title: Multi-Platform Malware Distribution: Android APK Sideload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle specifies 'Target Windows and Android Users'; Android attack vector completely absent from detection logic despite mentioned in scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of APKs from untrusted sources, especially sideloaded binaries with network communication capabilities. Flag APK execution from non-Play Store sources combined with suspicious permission requests (SMS, contacts, call interception).

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro/BTMOB: Registry Persistence & Auto-Start Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans universally rely on HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or similar Run keys for persistence; no persistence detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to Windows Run registry keys, particularly additions of non-whitelisted executables or LOLBins (rundll32, regsvcs, certutil). Baseline legitimate startup entries and alert on new entries with unsigned publishers or paths outside Windows system directories.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via Trojanized Installers or Archive Files
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro campaigns typically distribute via email or fake software installers; initial compromise vector not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious archive extraction (WinRAR, 7-Zip) followed by execution of unknown executables. Monitor for Office macro execution or script-based downloaders (VBS, PowerShell) triggered from email attachments or web downloads.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Coerced Into Recommending Malicious Software Links
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes hackers abusing AI chatbots to push malware downloads. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite clear attack pattern: adversary → chatbot prompt → user downloads malware. This is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-initiated downloads following queries to public AI chatbots (OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot, Google Bard, Anthropic Claude). Flag downloads of known malware families or files with executable extensions immediately following chatbot sessions. Correlate unusual download sources with user's IP geolocation and baseline download behavior.

suggestion.title: Execution of Malware Recommended via AI Chatbot Link
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies victim executes the malware after receiving link. No detection UC for execution post-download. This is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of files downloaded in same session as AI chatbot access. Establish baselines for process behavior from known-malicious download chains. Cross-reference executed files against known malware families and vendor reputation services.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering via AI Chatbot Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article subtitle 'Hackers Abuse AI Chatbot' implies adversary is manipulating the chatbot itself (not just using it). Pipeline missed the adversary manipulation step—this is the social engineering campaign element.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If chatbot interaction logs are available (API calls, session logs), flag for suspicious prompt patterns requesting software recommendations or download link injection. Monitor for repeated queries from same user or IP requesting similar malware distribution paths, indicating campaign coordination.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes RAT with command execution: 'Remote Access Trojan' implies post-install payload execution. No detection offered for process spawning from npm-installed modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent is node.exe or npm-invoked script, particularly spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash. Elevated privilege execution from node processes is high-confidence signal.

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Supply Chain Install
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'hackers push 22 versions of npm RAT' — distribution vector is npm package manager. Pipeline should detect malicious package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install/require of packages with typosquatting indicators, unusual names, or from new publishers. Correlate with network egress to uncommon destinations within 5 minutes of install.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor via npm Module Boot Hook
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'persistent backdoor' — pipeline failed to map persistence mechanisms. npm modules can hook into node startup and process initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to .npmrc, package.json scripts (preinstall, postinstall, prepare, poststart), or npm global modules loading unusual executables. Monitor for node.js processes with suspicious environment variables or module paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet File Access from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'wallet theft' capability. No detection provided for file access patterns targeting wallet software or key material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag node.exe or child processes accessing known wallet software directories (~/.ethereum, ~/.bitcoin, ~/AppData/Roaming/Exodus, etc.) or reading .key/.pem/.json files in user home directories.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from npm Module
suggestion.rationale: RAT definition requires command-and-control. Article does not surface detection for suspicious DNS/HTTP egress from npm-spawned processes to non-standard ports or domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe initiating TLS/SSL connections to recently-registered domains, IPs with high ASN diversity, or known C2 infrastructure. High-entropy hostnames or numeric-only subdomains from npm context is suspicious.

suggestion.title: npm Package with Obfuscated or Eval Code
suggestion.rationale: 22 variants of RAT suggests polymorphism or obfuscation. Pipeline should flag npm packages with common evasion patterns (eval, base64 strings, hidden scripts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Yara/content scan npm package tarballs for eval(), Function constructors, base64-encoded payloads, or minified code with suspicious entropy. Flag packages where main entry point is obfuscated or calls require() with dynamic paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Claude Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes fake installers as delivery mechanism: 'Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers to Deploy DinDoor Backdoor'. No UC was generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of ChatGPT or Claude installer binaries from non-official download locations (temp dirs, Downloads, uncommon paths). Establish whitelist of legitimate installer hashes/signatures and alert on mismatches or unsigned executables claiming to be official installers.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Backdoor Process Behavior and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'DinDoor Backdoor' deployment but pipeline extracted zero malware family IOCs or behavioral signatures. Backdoor execution and persistence mechanisms must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DinDoor process signatures, registry modifications for persistence (Run keys, services, schedulers), and service/driver creation patterns associated with backdoor installation. Correlate installer execution with subsequent registry modifications within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Revoked Installer Certificate Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers imply unsigned or stolen certificates. Pipeline generated no signature/code-signing use cases despite this being a primary anti-analysis and trust-abuse tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of binaries with names matching legitimate software (ChatGPT, Claude) but lacking valid signatures, bearing revoked certificates, or signed by unrecognized publishers. High-confidence signal when installer name + invalid signature occurs.

suggestion.title: Installer Child Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious installers typically spawn unexpected child processes (payload decryption, persistence setup). No use case captured this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate child processes spawned by official ChatGPT/Claude installers. Alert on deviations: unusual cmd.exe, PowerShell, or system binary execution originating from installer parent process.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Malware Execution via Phishing Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Hackers Use Grandoreiro Malware' — typical delivery vector is phishing emails with malicious Office/script attachments. No execution detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution (Office macro runners, script interpreters, rundll32, wscript) originating from email temp folders or spawned by email client processes, followed by child process anomalies or DLL injection.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Banking App Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Portuguese Banks and Latin American Companies' — Grandoreiro's signature technique is injecting into banking applications for credential interception. No credential harvesting detection present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned DLL injection into banking applications (edge.exe, chrome.exe, iexplore.exe, banking app processes) followed by API calls for window enumeration, text capture, or clipboard monitoring.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beaconing for Grandoreiro
suggestion.rationale: Active campaign requires C2 communication to exfiltrate stolen credentials and banking data. Pipeline identified no C2 infrastructure or communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted HTTPS/HTTP beacons to unknown domains with regular intervals, POST requests with suspicious encoded payloads, or DNS queries to newly registered or malicious C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Screen Capture and Keystroke Logging
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro collects screen captures and keystroke logs to harvest OTP and credentials during online banking sessions. No collection-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes with elevated screen capture API calls (BitBlt, GetDC) or keyboard hooking (SetWindowsHookEx), particularly when hooked into banking/browser processes and communicating to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Token Exfiltration from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is token theft—'Steals Your AI Tokens'—but pipeline generated zero UCs for detecting unauthorized access or movement of credential material. Should detect unusual egress of API keys/bearer tokens from development environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for environment variable exfiltration (OPENAI_API_KEY, similar patterns) in process arguments or network traffic. Correlate high-entropy strings matching API token patterns sent to non-whitelisted external IPs. Flag simultaneous token creation and immediate egress from dev tool processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation or Extension Load from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'legitimate-looking Codex Remote UI'—social engineering aspect of supply chain compromise. Pipeline missed detection for installation of trojanized packages, VS Code extension loads from non-official stores, or executable launches from suspicious paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/PyPI install commands with package names matching known malicious variants. Flag VS Code extension installations via manual .vsix loads or registry/config-file modifications. Detect child process execution from extension cache or plugin directories with suspicious command-line patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Token Usage: Stolen Credentials Used from Unexpected Context
suggestion.rationale: Once tokens are stolen, attacker will use them for downstream API calls. Article emphasizes credential theft but pipeline did not suggest detection for misuse post-compromise (e.g., OpenAI API calls from attacker IP, unusual geolocation, API consumption spike).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls using compromised tokens from geographic regions, IP ranges, or time-of-day patterns inconsistent with legitimate developer workflow. Trigger on token usage within minutes of installation of suspicious extension (time-to-abuse). Correlate token ID with process that exfiltrated it.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Remote UI or Extension Communication with Unregistered Domains
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'Remote UI'—likely C2 callback or data exfiltration endpoint. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or network-based detections despite clear implication of attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS traffic from development tool processes to low-reputation, newly-registered, or DGA-like domains. suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Embedded Malicious Code'—this indicates trojanized legitimate software. Pipeline generated no hash-based integrity detection despite supply-chain compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline hash values for legitimate Daemon Tools Lite binaries from vendor. Alert on process execution of Daemon Tools with file hashes deviating from known-good baseline, indicating modified or counterfeit copies.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Post-Compromise Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability' but provides no behavioral detection use case. Embedded malware implies post-exploitation C2 or data exfiltration activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous network connections, child process spawning, or privilege escalation originating from Daemon Tools Lite processes. Baseline legitimate application behavior and alert on deviations consistent with malware payload execution.

suggestion.title: Repeated API Authorization Probe Failures (BOLA/IDOR Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names BOLA/IDOR as exploitable context-dependent vulnerabilities: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage, authentication bypasses.' Defenders must detect systematic authorization enumeration via repeated probes with varying user/tenant IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints accepting user/tenant ID parameters for rapid sequential requests returning 403/401 with differing ID values. Flag 10+ authorization failures within 60 seconds from single source as IDOR enumeration attempt.

suggestion.title: Continuous Automated API Endpoint Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes threat model: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed.' Defenders should detect systematic, high-volume API path enumeration consistent with automated DAST/pentesting tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify single source generating requests to large number of non-existent/uncommon API endpoints within short window, or User-Agent strings matching pentesting frameworks (Burp Suite, ZAP, OWASP variants).

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'cross-tenant data leakage' as concrete exploitable vulnerability. Defenders must detect access requests crossing tenant/org boundaries, especially via direct ID substitution in URLs/parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated requests accessing resources assigned to different customer organization/tenant than requester's home tenant, particularly when tenant context modified via URL parameter or payload substitution.
