suggestion.title: Chained Exploit Sequence Correlations (Multi-Step Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker objective: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' Single low-severity events are noise; logical exploit chains across 1-2 hours indicate coordinated attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user/session activity detecting sequence: resource enumeration → failed privilege check → credential modification → resource access, all within 120 minutes. Escalate if sequence shows logical progression toward critical asset.

suggestion.title: API Injection Payload Testing (DAST Probing Signature)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DAST methodology: 'throws payloads at a running application or API and observes responses: error messages, time delays, behavioral differences.' Defenders should recognize structured injection probe sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential requests to same endpoint with deliberate injection payloads (SQL syntax, timing operators, XXE, template injection markers) followed by response-time measurement, within <5 minute window from single source.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Testing Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'authentication bypasses' as key context-dependent vulnerability class requiring detection. Defenders must flag abnormal auth manipulation patterns distinct from credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormal authentication patterns: repeated auth requests with header manipulation (Authorization variants, bearer token mutations), session fixation techniques, or token replay within short window from single source/IP.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing / Fake IT Support Solicitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states SRG 'either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' — foundational attack vector requiring email content and phone number discovery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails containing phone numbers and urgent IT support pretext (helpdesk, technical issue, account verification). Correlate email delivery to organization with incoming calls from numbers matching phishing message content. Flag emails impersonating legitimate IT domain variants.

suggestion.title: RDP Access Initiated After Phishing / Social Engineering Pretext
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' — attackers weaponize employee-granted RDP after successful phoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connections (mstsc.exe, Remote Desktop) initiated by non-IT employees or from unusual source IPs shortly after callback phishing emails sent to organization. Detect RDP client invocations from user accounts that rarely initiate remote sessions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB / External Drive Connection to Corporate Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and 'stealing data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives' — physical exfiltration vector requiring device monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on USB/external drive connections to corporate computers, especially outside business hours or from workstations accessed via RDP or following phishing indicators. Correlate with reports of unauthorized individuals in secured areas or physical badge access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted IT Support Domain Registration and Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns' — domain infrastructure for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and web proxy logs for visits to known typosquatted domain patterns (single-character swaps, omitted characters, different TLDs of legitimate IT support domains). Flag registration of new domains matching law firm or financial services org names with IT support keywords.

suggestion.title: Unidentified Individuals Claiming IT Support / Physical Intrusion Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers, as possible indicators of an SRG attack' — physical attack surface requiring security coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Coordinate badge system and physical security with SOC. Alert on badge access attempts by unknown IDs or guests claiming IT affiliation, lack of proper credentials, or absence from IT directory. Correlate with concurrent network anomalies or phishing reports.

suggestion.title: Post-Exfiltration Extortion / Ransom Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients' — post-breach impact phase requiring communications monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ransom/extortion emails mentioning data theft, leak threats, or sale of stolen data. Monitor for bulk calls to employee/client contact lists from unknown phone numbers referencing security breaches or data exposure. Correlate with reports of prior phishing or RDP compromise.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection — FIFA/World Cup Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes phishing campaign targeting FIFA fans. 'GHOST STADIUM Phishing Campaign Targets FIFA World Cup Fans' — pipeline must detect inbound emails leveraging tournament-related lures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails containing FIFA, World Cup, tournament, ticket-related keywords with embedded links or reply-to addresses belonging to newly registered or sinkholed domains. Correlate sender domain reputation and DKIM/SPF alignment against official FIFA registrant IPs.

suggestion.title: Fake Domain Access — FIFA Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: '300+ Fake Domains' — requires network layer detection of user access to domains impersonating FIFA entities. Proxy and DNS logs must flag FIFA-themed domains registered within 30 days or hosting compromised content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains with FIFA/World Cup keywords not in official WHOIS registrant database or IP whitelist. Trigger on first-access to newly registered domains matching phishing pattern infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Fake Domain
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign targets fans — implies credential harvesting via fake login pages on those 300+ domains. Must detect successful credential entry to attacker-controlled form endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to domains flagged as phishing infrastructure containing form data patterns matching email, password, 2FA code fields. Correlate with user context to identify victims before account abuse.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise Post-Phishing — Login Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Victims of credential-harvesting phishing show abnormal account activity: impossible travel, new device logins, inbox rule creation within hours of phishing email detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting phishing email, alert if same user's account logs in from new IP/geolocation within 24h, creates inbox rules, enables SMTP relay, or modifies forwarding addresses. Chain events to phishing receipt time.

suggestion.title: MFA Enrollment After Phishing — Attacker Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated phishing campaigns harvesting credentials + SMS/app tokens enable attacker-driven MFA re-enrollment for persistent backdoor access. Must surface anomalous MFA configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MFA method registration changes (new phone, new app, new email) on accounts within 12 hours of detected phishing email targeting that user or domain. Correlate with impossible-travel logins from new device.

suggestion.title: GHOST STADIUM Infrastructure — Domain/IP Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Campaign is named 'GHOST STADIUM' with 300+ domains — threat intel must correlate shared hosting, registrars, certificate issuers, and nameservers to identify full attacker infrastructure beyond enumerated IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Pivot on GHOST STADIUM-attributed domains to identify common nameserver, registrar, IP geolocation clusters. Use SSL/TLS certificate CN/SAN overlap to uncover additional campaign domains. Build YARA rules on domain patterns.

suggestion.title: Java code-execution patterns in Yamcs algorithm PATCH/POST request bodies
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists in 'user-controlled algorithm text' evaluated by Janino. Should detect Java Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder, reflection APIs, or Process-related class instantiation in payloads to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH or POST request to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoint containing Java code execution APIs (Runtime.getRuntime, ProcessBuilder, java.lang.Process) in request body indicates Janino expression engine exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Yamcs authentication followed by privilege elevation to ChangeMissionDatabase role
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this.' Privilege escalation to this specific role is a critical prerequisite detectable in audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Yamcs user account granted or elevated to ChangeMissionDatabase privilege shortly after authentication, particularly from service/automation accounts, indicates privilege escalation for RCE setup.

suggestion.title: Failed Janino compilation errors followed by successful algorithm update and child process spawn
suggestion.rationale: Attacker would likely probe the algorithm evaluation endpoint with malformed payloads. Pattern of failed compilations followed by success and OS process spawning indicates iterative exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Multiple failed PATCH/POST requests to algorithm endpoints (Janino compilation errors in logs) from single source within short window, followed by successful request and shell child process, indicates active exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP reconnaissance on Yamcs /api/mdb/algorithms endpoint paths
suggestion.rationale: Attacker performs discovery of algorithm endpoints before exploitation. Repeated OPTIONS, HEAD, or high rate of 404 responses on algorithm paths precedes PATCH with malicious payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Repeated OPTIONS/HEAD requests or 404 responses on /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* paths followed by PATCH request with code payload indicates endpoint enumeration and exploitation.

suggestion.title: Yamcs MdbOverrideApi PATCH with Java reflection RCE payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies '/api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/*' as vulnerable endpoint and lists RCE payloads ('Java.type', 'java.lang.Runtime', 'ProcessBuilder') used to bypass Nashorn ClassFilter restriction. Represents initial exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* containing Java reflection/execution patterns (Java.type, java.lang.Runtime, ProcessBuilder, getRuntime). Correlate with HTTP 200-204 responses and subsequent child process spawning within java parent.

suggestion.title: Java parent spawning shell child from Yamcs process tree
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Nashorn Runtime.exec' spawning shells as post-exploitation behavior. Pipeline missed detection for java parent process with 'yamcs' or 'org.yamcs' in cmdline spawning bash/sh/zsh/nc/ncat/socat children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process 'java' with command line matching '*yamcs*' or '*org.yamcs*' or '*yamcs-core*' spawning child process names matching sh, bash, dash, zsh, nc, ncat, socat, python, python3, perl, ruby.

suggestion.title: Shell executing /dev/tcp file descriptor redirect from Yamcs JVM
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '/dev/tcp/' redirection pattern as C2 mechanism. Quote: 'Reverse-shell /dev/tcp file descriptor from Yamcs java process tree'. Pipeline failed to detect this specific Unix shell reverse-shell technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Command line containing '/dev/tcp/' or '/dev/udp/' executed by bash/sh/dash/zsh process where parent is java or yamcs-related. Extract reverse host and port from regex `/dev/(?:tcp|udp)/([^/]+)/(\d+)` for C2 enrichment.

suggestion.title: MdbOverrideApi calls from ChangeMissionDatabase-privileged accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' can trigger exploitation. Pipeline missed application-level audit detection using privilege gating. Enumeration of this privilege group provides baseline for anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Yamcs application logs recording MdbOverrideApi.updateAlgorithm invocations from accounts holding ChangeMissionDatabase privilege. Flag: calls from default 'guest' account or privilege escalation preceding the API call.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm override via API — privilege abuse (ChangeMissionDatabase)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires `ChangeMissionDatabase` privilege. No UC detects privilege abuse or detection of this privilege being exercised. Article: 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs REST API logs for authenticated requests from accounts with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege who then modify algorithm definitions via PATCH /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*. Baseline legitimate algorithm authors and alert on outliers or after-hours modifications.

suggestion.title: Jython/JSR-223 script engine invocation from Yamcs JVM
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability uses 'Jython' and 'JSR-223 ScriptEngine API' to dynamically compile and evaluate algorithm text. No UC directly detects Jython script compilation or class-loading patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt JVM process arguments, stack traces, or JVM debug/instrumentation logs for invocations of javax.script.ScriptEngine, jython.* class references, or Algorithm*.compile patterns from Yamcs runtime. Baseline normal algorithm evaluation and alert on unusual script patterns.

suggestion.title: Yamcs REST API unauthenticated access or session escalation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires authentication but no detection covers scenario where attacker gains initial valid Yamcs session through credential compromise, weak auth, or session fixation prior to algorithm injection. Article: 'authenticated user' but does not discuss how that authentication is obtained.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed Yamcs API authentication attempts followed by successful login from same source within short window (credential guessing). Monitor for API authentication from non-corporate IP ranges or off-hours.

suggestion.title: Yamcs configuration or mission database file modification
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits algorithm definition override in the mission database. No UC monitors for filesystem or database modification of Yamcs config/algorithm files outside of expected change-control processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of Yamcs algorithm definition files (typically XML or YAML in MDB directory) by non-authorized service accounts. Pair with version-control commit history to detect out-of-band modifications.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Registry Image Pull
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication'—the core attack is direct retrieval of container images from Gitea registry without valid bearer token or credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Gitea container registry endpoints (/v2/, /api/v1/packages) that lack Authorization headers or bearer tokens, or return 200 OK to unauthenticated HEAD/GET manifest requests. Establish baseline of valid pull operations and flag anomalous registry access from unknown source IPs or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Gitea Registry API Authentication Bypass via Path Traversal or Missing Auth Check
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'without Authentication' access; likely mechanism is missing authorization gate on registry endpoints. Article phrase directly states unauthenticated access is possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea application logs and API gateway logs for requests to /api/v1/packages/container or similar registry endpoints returning success (200/202) with missing or invalid Authorization header. Correlate with failed authentication attempts in preceding request logs to establish baseline of normal vs. exploitation traffic.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Container Image Manifest Download from Private Gitea Registry
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is the ability to download image manifests and blobs from Gitea's container registry without credentials. Article emphasizes 'Private Container Images' being exposed.
log_sources: S3 bucket access logs (if blobs stored in cloud)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful GET requests to Gitea registry blob storage endpoints (/v2/<image>/blobs/sha256:<hash>) and manifest endpoints (/v2/<image>/manifests/<tag>) from clients with no recorded authentication session. Flag bulk manifest/blob downloads from single source IP or time spike in registry access volume.

suggestion.title: Container Image Repository Enumeration via Unauthenticated Gitea Registry API
suggestion.rationale: If authentication is missing, attackers can enumerate all available private repositories via listing endpoints. Article describes 'exposes' which implies discovery of private assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated requests to Gitea registry enumeration endpoints (/api/v1/packages, /v2/catalog if implemented) that succeed. Flag sequential requests listing repository names, tags, or metadata from single source without prior valid authentication.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exposed Private Container Image Credentials or Content
suggestion.rationale: Private container images may embed credentials, deploy keys, or sensitive configuration. Exposure enables downstream compromise. This is the impact pathway from the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-incident: correlate container images downloaded via unauthenticated registry with secrets leaked or misconfigurations in downstream systems. Monitor for authentication attempts using credentials sourced from image layers (ENV vars, config files). Flag image content that should have been redacted (API keys, tokens, SSH keys) in pull operations.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain-Encoded C2 Server Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop' — direct C2 communication channel that should trigger detection on blockchain RPC queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor developer workstations for unexpected connections to Solana blockchain RPC endpoints (node.solana.com, public RPC services) or Base64-decoded data in network traffic pointing to blockchain addresses. Correlate with known GlasswormRAT process signatures.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Network Queries for C2 Configuration Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys' — peer-to-peer C2 fallback using decentralized network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BitTorrent DHT port 6881-6889 or uTP traffic originating from VS Code, npm/Node processes, or developer tools. Flag hardcoded DHT key queries or unusual peer count in DHT announcements.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Abuse for Dead-Drop C2 Path Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths' — abuse of legitimate SaaS for command delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Calendar API calls (create, list, update events) from atypical processes or outside business hours. Decode event titles for Base64 strings containing IP addresses or domain paths. Alert on API access from developer workstations outside normal calendar automation patterns.

suggestion.title: Dormant Malicious Extension Activation on Update Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Glassworm operators planted dozens of dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update' — persistence via staged payload activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code and OpenVSX extension directory for extensions with delayed execution or update hooks. Flag extensions where code activation timestamp differs significantly from installation timestamp. Correlate extension updates with process spawning from .vscode or .extensionData directories.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Store and Cryptocurrency Wallet Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware 'stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' — credential harvesting from privileged development environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file/registry access to credential stores (.ssh, .aws, .docker, MetaMask/Exodus wallet directories, browser credential storage) from unexpected processes. Flag access to git credentials, npm tokens, and SSH key files within seconds of process launch.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Modification in GitHub/npm Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Later attack waves extended to GitHub repositories and npm packages, with one campaign in March impacting more than 400 software artifacts' — upstream compromise of development artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository commit events and npm package publish events for accounts with abnormal activity patterns (new committers, unusual hours, bulk uploads). Flag packages with dependency additions to unknown registries or sudden behavioral changes in version diffs.

suggestion.title: GlassWorm malware execution or sample detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'GlassWorm Malware'—canonical malware family signature should trigger hash-based, filename, process behavior, or memory-artifact detection use cases. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known GlassWorm samples via file hash (MD5/SHA256), process name patterns, or suspicious parent-child relationships. Monitor for unsigned or anomalously-signed binaries with GlassWorm indicators (e.g., strings, imports, code sections). Flag process launches from user-writable or temp directories combined with network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Supply chain package or dependency injection—developer artifact compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Developer Supply Chain Attack Infrastructure'—indicates malicious package, dependency, or artifact repository compromise. No use cases generated for detecting suspicious dependency resolution, package manifest tampering, or repository anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package managers (npm, pip, NuGet, Maven) for installation or updates of packages with zero or suspiciously-low historical usage. Detect downloads from malicious or newly-registered artifact repositories. Flag build systems pulling dependencies from non-canonical sources or via unverified TLS certificates.

suggestion.title: Developer build/CI pipeline infrastructure compromise—unusual execution context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'disrupted developer supply chain attack infrastructure'—implies hosted infrastructure (CI/CD, build servers, artifact repos) was compromised. No detection for anomalous build job execution, unexpected credential usage in build context, or exfiltration from CI logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API tokens, SSH keys, or build credentials being accessed from unusual network sources or outside normal CI/CD windows. Flag build jobs with unexpected third-party service integrations or credential exfiltration patterns. Monitor for environment variable access to secrets in non-standard build contexts.

suggestion.title: C2 communication or callback from compromised developer infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Takedown language implies active malware infrastructure (C2 servers, exfil endpoints). No detection use cases for outbound communication, DNS resolution patterns, or network callbacks consistent with malware command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or HTTP requests from build servers to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Flag encrypted outbound traffic (HTTPS/DNS-over-HTTPS) to IPs not in allow-list, especially from CI/CD infrastructure. Alert on unusual port usage (high ephemeral ranges) or beaconing patterns from dev infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious code injection into published artifacts or build outputs
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack targeting developers implies injected code in downstream artifacts (binaries, libraries, containers). Article mentions 'disrupts infrastructure'—suggests code tampering. No detection for artifact integrity checks or unexpected binary modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect published artifacts (DLLs, EXEs, container images, JAR files) with unexpected code sections, unsigned sections, or mismatched file hashes vs. published checksums. Monitor artifact build pipelines for injection of unexpected dependencies or build steps. Flag container image layers with suspicious payloads or modification timestamps.

suggestion.title: Takedown/Law enforcement infrastructure seizure indicators—IOC invalidation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Takedown'—implies law enforcement or hosting provider action. No detection to identify when known-bad infrastructure becomes unavailable, sinkholed, or associated with law enforcement notices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS resolution of known C2 domains for sudden IP changes, NXDOMAIN responses, or sinkhole IPs (e.g., known LE infrastructure). Alert if malware beacons abruptly cease despite no local remediation. Cross-reference takedown announcements with observed IOCs in your logs to date exposures and attack window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious msiexec.exe installing ScreenConnect remote access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the malicious DLL 'uses msiexec.exe to install vcredist_x64.dll, which is a package installer for the ScreenConnect remote access tool.' This is the persistence gateway.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor msiexec.exe spawning vcredist or ScreenConnect-related installations, especially from non-standard paths or following suspicious DLL loads. Legitimate ScreenConnect deployment is managed; sudden installation from user directories or temporary locations is anomalous. Correlate with parent process chain from archive extraction.

suggestion.title: Process hollowing into Microsoft-signed .NET binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article names explicit targets: 'process hollowing into a legitimate .NET binary signed by Microsoft: InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe.' Lists 7 hollow vectors explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect these 7 Microsoft-signed .NET tools spawning unexpected child processes, making unusual network connections, or exhibiting memory/handle patterns inconsistent with legitimate build/system operations. Monitor for image loads from uncommon directories or suspicious argument patterns that deviate from expected tool invocation.

suggestion.title: PowerShell adding malware to Windows Defender exclusion list
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware also invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender.' Direct defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell execution of Add-MpPreference or Set-MpPreference with -ExclusionPath or -ExclusionProcess parameters, especially when parent process is ScreenConnect, a .NET binary, or unexpected script host. Legitimate exclusions are deployed via SCCM/Intune; ad-hoc PowerShell calls are suspicious.

suggestion.title: GPU mining tool execution (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies final impact payload: 'one of three mining modules is downloaded and executed...gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI, all of them designed to use graphics processing units.' Clear compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection on presence/execution of gminer.exe, lolminer.exe, or SRBMiner processes. Monitor for sustained GPU resource consumption anomalies. These tools are not legitimate in enterprise environments. Correlate execution with parent process chain from hollowed .NET binary or ScreenConnect session.

suggestion.title: DLL side-loading attack on system utility executables
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial compromise: archive contains 'legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded.' Targets CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extraction/execution of these 6 utility names from archive formats or temporary directories followed by unusual DLL loads from the same path. Flag unsigned or mislocated DLLs loaded by these utilities. Track network retrieval from gleeze[.]com subdomains or similar archive-hosting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Virtual machine and analysis tool detection enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'checks the environment for virtual machines and a set of 40 process names corresponding to analysis tools. If any are identified, the malware terminates its execution.' Sandbox evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process enumeration loops checking for debugger, hypervisor, and analysis tool artifacts (WinDbg, IDA, Wireshark, ProcessMonitor, etc.). Watch for rapid registry queries to VM detection hives. Unexpected process termination immediately after such checks indicates active evasion.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Process Execution & DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers Grandoreiro as a 'malware' targeting 'Windows and Android users'—a banking trojan known for process injection and DLL loading as execution mechanisms. No process-execution detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious DLL injection or side-loading associated with Grandoreiro execution, such as process creation with injected memory mapped regions or DLLs loaded from non-standard paths. Monitor for LoadImage/CreateRemoteThread patterns indicative of banking trojans establishing code execution.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'BTMOB RAT' as a Remote Access Trojan—RATs inherently establish C2 communication as their primary function. No network-based C2 detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from compromised endpoints to known BTMOB C2 servers, anomalous DNS queries to suspicious domains, and persistent outbound connections from non-whitelisted executables. BTMOB RAT typically beacons on a fixed schedule.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Credential Theft & Banking Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is a 'banking' trojan (per title)—banking trojans universally steal credentials and perform browser/session interception. No credential-access detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect keylogging or screen capture processes spawned by Grandoreiro payloads, monitor for uncommon browser extensions or browser-process children, and alert on unusual login patterns (simultaneous logins from different geos, failed auth spikes preceding successful logins).

suggestion.title: Multi-Platform Malware Delivery (Windows→Android Cross-Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states both 'Windows and Android' are targeted in the same campaign—suggesting either delivery chains that compromise one platform to pivot to another, or coordinated parallel campaigns. No cross-platform delivery detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malicious APK downloads or Android app installs from compromised Windows hosts, or browser-based credential harvesting that feeds Android device compromise. Look for characteristic delivery infrastructure (URLs, domains) that serve both Windows EXE and Android APK payloads.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Detection (Registry/Scheduler)
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans like Grandoreiro and RATs like BTMOB establish persistence to maintain long-term access. Article describes 'campaigns'—implying sustained presence. No persistence detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Registry modifications in Run/RunOnce keys, WMI event subscriptions, or scheduled tasks creating executables. Grandoreiro and BTMOB variants commonly establish persistence via Registry hives or Task Scheduler entries pointing to unusual directories.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Code Obfuscation & Living-Off-The-Land
suggestion.rationale: Modern banking trojans and RATs employ obfuscation and LOLBin techniques to evade detection. Article describes 'campaigns'—suggesting adversaries are operational and employing known evasion tactics. No evasion-focused detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscated PowerShell scripts, suspicious usage of msiexec/rundll32/regsvcs to execute malicious payloads, and process trees with suspicious parent-child relationships. Monitor for unsigned or low-signature-trust executables spawning LOLBin processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Non-Standard Registry or Force Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 22 malicious npm RAT package versions as initial attack vector. 'Hackers push 22 versions' indicates multi-variant distribution campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm.exe or npm.cmd spawning with install/add arguments using --force, --save-dev, or registry URLs outside trusted mirrors (not registry.npmjs.org). Correlate with child processes and immediate registry or file modifications.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Executing Obfuscated or Dynamically-Constructed Code
suggestion.rationale: Persistent backdoor installed at package installation time via postinstall.js scripts. Malicious npm packages obfuscate payloads using Base64, eval(), or code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe child processes from npm cache directories (AppData\Roaming\npm-cache) executing postinstall.js with high string entropy, Base64 decode patterns, eval() calls, or dynamically invoked PowerShell commands. Alert on any child process spawning from postinstall context.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Key or Scheduled Task from npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'persistent backdoor'—npm malware achieves persistence via HKCU Run keys, Startup folders, or scheduled tasks created during postinstall execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reg.exe or PowerShell.exe registry writes to HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or schtasks.exe invocations immediately following npm package installation. High-confidence if paired with obfuscated postinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Browser Profile and Wallet Extension Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'wallet theft'—npm RAT accesses cryptocurrency wallets (MetaMask, Web3) and browser credentials stored in Chrome/Edge profiles or extension localStorage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or npm-spawned processes accessing browser data directories (AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, AppData\Roaming\wallet extension paths). Alert on code attempting to enumerate or read wallet private keys, localStorage, or clipboard in npm package context.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Beaconing from npm-Installed Backdoor Process
suggestion.rationale: Persistent backdoor and wallet theft require exfiltration channel—npm malware must maintain C2 connectivity for attacker commands and credential/wallet data upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS or DNS from node.exe processes to non-standard domains (excluding npmjs.com, github.com, cdn registries). Flag POST requests with Base64/encrypted payloads, unusual User-Agent headers, or periodic beaconing patterns from npm-spawned child processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MSI Execution Followed by PowerShell/Deno Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'MSI installer file...executes via Windows' native installation tool. The MSI file subsequently drops a CMD file and PowerShell script...[then] installs the Deno JavaScript runtime through standard Windows package managers (Scoop and WinGet).' This chaining of MSI → PowerShell → Deno is the hallmark of this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MSI execution (via msiexec.exe or Windows Installer service) that is followed within minutes by PowerShell or CMD spawning package managers (scoop.exe, winget.exe) with arguments installing Deno or similar runtime. Correlate parent-child relationships and execution timelines to identify chaining behavior consistent with automated malware installation.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Run Key Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'establishes persistence by creating Windows registry run keys, ensuring reactivation on system restart.' This is a direct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKLM equivalent, especially when the value data points to PowerShell, CMD, or newly installed runtimes (Deno paths), or when run keys are created by MSI installers or package managers in abnormal execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft Pattern: Multiple Cryptocurrency Wallet API/Extension Access
suggestion.rationale: Article details DinDoor 'Targets over 50 crypto wallet extensions and software wallets including Atomic Wallet, Exodus, and Electrum' and 'Steals information from browsers.' Multiple rapid accesses to known wallet software is a collection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single process or process chain accessing multiple known cryptocurrency wallet application files, browser extension directories, or wallet-related registry keys in succession. Correlate with screen capture or clipboard operations and unusual network egress to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Deno Process Execution and Network Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article states DinDoor is deployed by 'Deno JavaScript runtime...fetches and executes the DinDoor backdoor directly from attacker-controlled servers.' Legitimate Deno usage is rare; execution fetching and running remote code is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Deno process creation with command-line arguments indicating script download or execution from external URLs, particularly to non-standard ports or domains not in approved allowlists. Correlate with parent process being PowerShell, package managers, or MSI installation tools.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Edge Hidden Process Screen Streaming via P2P
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Uses hidden Microsoft Edge browser processes to stream live video feeds via peer-to-peer connections.' Hidden Edge spawned by unusual parent processes is highly suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for msedge.exe spawned by processes other than the normal user session (e.g., system services, package managers, Deno, PowerShell) with command-line flags indicative of headless or hidden operation. Correlate with P2P network traffic (STUN, ICE, WebRTC) to non-standard peers.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Known DinDoor C2 Domains and Associated IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists eight C2 domains (claudescript[.]top, ms-telemetry-gateway-us[.]com, etc.) and five IP addresses explicitly. Any network egress to these should be flagged immediately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create indicator-based detection rule for DNS requests or network connections (any protocol, any port) to the C2 domains: claudescript[.]top, ms-telemetry-gateway-us[.]com, dakatawebstick[.]com, ashpaltlonpro[.]com, agilemast3r[.]duckdns[.]org, geralnewlong[.]com, hngfbgfbfb[.]cyou, logicalnewrestore[.]com, or to IPs 23.227.196.107, 45.137.99.121, 31.57.129.23, 66.78.40.107, 193.233.198.132.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Email Delivery via Phishing Attachments
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Use Grandoreiro Malware to Target' indicating delivery mechanism; pipeline extracted zero delivery-phase IOCs. Grandoreiro campaigns typically begin with phishing emails containing Office macros or malicious scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with suspicious Office attachments (especially .docm, .xlsm) sent to Portuguese banking institutions and Latin American companies. Alert when Office applications spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32 after attachment execution. Correlate sender reputation, attachment sandboxing results, and macro behavior.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Process Injection and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware deployed to targets but pipeline failed to establish execution phase. Banking trojans like Grandoreiro inject into legitimate processes to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection patterns: Office applications (WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE) creating child processes with unsigned DLLs or suspicious memory writes. Monitor for execution of living-off-the-land binaries (certutil, mshta, rundll32) with parameters indicative of code execution. Alert on uncommon process trees originating from email delivery.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Credential Harvesting from Banking Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Portuguese banks specifically; Grandoreiro's primary function is credential and banking form theft, but no credential-access use cases were generated despite being central to this malware's purpose.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for keylogging hooks or API interception targeting banking applications (online banking portals, banking software). Alert on registry modifications enabling browser extensions in Chrome/Firefox/Edge. Detect unusual access patterns to browser credential stores, Credential Manager vaults, or Windows SSO tokens from suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans require persistent C2 for command execution and data exfiltration. Article describes active campaigns but pipeline generated zero network-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate banking application traffic from Portuguese and Latin American financial endpoints. Alert on anomalous outbound connections from Office-spawned child processes to non-standard ports or domains. Correlate C2 infrastructure from threat feeds with observed network patterns; flag encrypted HTTPS traffic with unusual certificate issuers or self-signed certs.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration of Banking Credentials and Customer Records
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting of Portuguese banks and Latin American companies indicating data theft motive; no exfiltration use cases generated despite being Grandoreiro's end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file reads from user profile directories, registry credential stores, and browser cache/cookies. Alert on unusual archive creation (RAR, ZIP) of banking or customer data files. Detect exfiltration of collected data over C2 channel or to public cloud storage. Correlate suspicious process execution with large outbound data transfer volumes.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Remote UI Application Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI'—indicates initial compromise vector is a fake or compromised installer/executable masquerading as legitimate software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned or suspicious-signed executables with names resembling 'codex', 'remote-ui', or similar Remote Desktop software variants from user download/temp paths. Correlate parent process (browser/explorer) with child executable spawning network connections to non-CDN destinations.

suggestion.title: API Token/Credential Harvesting from Local Stores
suggestion.rationale: Attack payload is token theft: article states 'Steals Your AI Tokens'—malware must locate and exfiltrate credentials from environment variables, dotfiles, config files, or browser extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading credential files (.env, .aws/credentials, .ssh/config, ~/.openai, browser credential stores) or dumping environment variables. Flag unexpected child processes of Remote UI applications accessing PII/secret material in batch reads.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of API Credentials to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malware purpose is token theft; credentials must be sent to attacker: 'Steals Your AI Tokens' implies C2 communication or DNS exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound POST/PUT requests from suspicious processes containing base64-encoded or plaintext API token patterns (sk-*, ghp_*, pat_, key=). Flag DNS queries to newly-registered or suspicious domains from Remote UI process context. Monitor for bulk credential staging in memory before network send.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Token Usage Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once tokens are exfiltrated, attacker will consume stolen credentials for cost/resource exploitation: expected follow-on to token theft is anomalous API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline API usage per user (geography, time-of-day, model/endpoint, request rate). Alert on: (1) API calls from non-standard geolocations, (2) requests outside business hours, (3) sudden cost spike, (4) requests to experimental/private models, (5) disabled MFA accounts suddenly active, (6) token reuse on new IPs within short window.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Delivery of Malicious Installer
suggestion.rationale: Malware is described as 'Legitimate-Looking'—social engineering is primary delivery mechanism, likely via phishing, fake vendor site, or trojanized download link.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails or messages linking to suspicious domains mimicking 'codex', 'remote-ui', or legitimate vendor branding. Flag newly-registered domains (< 30 days) with vendor-lookalike names. Monitor for user downloads of EXE/MSI/ZIP from non-vendor domains matching malware naming convention.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Process Spoofing or Living-off-the-Land Execution
suggestion.rationale: Legitimacy claim ('Legitimate-Looking') suggests evasion tactics: process naming spoofing or use of Windows built-ins (PowerShell, certutil, bitsadmin) to execute/stage malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process trees where Remote UI spawns unusual built-in tools (powershell.exe -enc, certutil, wget, curl) for credential access or C2 communication. Detect parent-child mismatches (e.g., svchost.exe spawning explorer.exe spawning Remote UI). Flag unsigned Remote UI executables loaded from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Post-Install Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious npm package triggering code execution during install—article title states 'malicious npm package' implying package.json postinstall/preinstall scripts or bin entry points. Pipeline provided no execution detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node executing unexpected child processes during package install. Look for npm.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget with suspicious arguments (exfil patterns, GitHub URLs, base64 encoding). Correlate install time with unexpected process activity in user temp or home directories.

suggestion.title: File Collection from Claude AI User Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'stole files from Claude AI user directory'—indicates systematic file enumeration and reading from ~/.claude or similar. Pipeline missed collection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unusual file reads from Claude user directory (e.g., C:\Users\*\.claude\*, ~/.claude/*). Correlate with npm/node process context, especially reading config, credentials, or session files. Flag reads followed immediately by network events (exfil).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to GitHub via npm Package Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title states exfil 'via GitHub'—implies HTTPS requests to github.com/raw or GitHub API. Pipeline did not capture command-and-control or exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes making HTTPS requests to github.com with unusual patterns: API calls to user repos, raw content delivery, or gist creation. Flag base64/encoded payloads in request bodies or POST requests to GitHub that correlate with recent npm installs and file collection activity.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Attack: Typosquatting or Namespace Confusion on npm Registry
suggestion.rationale: Malicious package on npm indicates either typosquatting, compromise of legitimate package, or namespace confusion. Title does not provide package name—pipeline should have extracted it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require logs for packages similar to popular libraries (Levenshtein distance analysis). Correlate with first-seen timestamp on registry, low download counts, or newly registered accounts. Flag installs followed by unexpected privileged process spawning or directory access.

suggestion.title: Claude AI Configuration/Credential Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Stealing from 'Claude AI user directory' implies sensitive config, API keys, session tokens, or workspace metadata. Pipeline missed credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads of Claude config files (settings.json, .env, credentials, auth tokens) by npm/node processes. Flag when sensitive file reads are followed by process execution of curl/wget or file encoding (base64, tar, zip) operations within the same process lineage.

suggestion.title: npm Package: Obfuscated or Minified Malicious Code Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages typically use obfuscation, minification, or encoded payloads in package.json scripts or bundled code. Pipeline provided no code-based indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze npm package.json for suspicious postinstall/preinstall/prepare scripts: base64 encoding, array notation string concatenation, unusual URL patterns, GitHub gist/raw references. Flag packages where install script is disproportionately large or unrelated to declared functionality.

suggestion.title: Bulk data exfiltration to external infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article core subject is cyber extortion economy, which depends on data theft. Keywords include 'extortion' but pipeline generated zero use cases for collection/exfiltration phases typical of extortion campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data volumes (>100 MB) transferred to external cloud storage, attacker infrastructure, or atypical geographic destinations outside business hours. Flag creation of staged archives (.7z, .rar, .zip) in user temp directories or cloud sync folders immediately prior to network exfil.

suggestion.title: Extortion demand delivery via Telegram Bot API
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'Telegram' as communication channel in extortion operations. Pipeline missed command-and-control detection for automated ransom-demand delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS lookups and TLS connections to api.telegram.org, particularly bot.telegram.org endpoints, from compromised user accounts or cloud instances. Flag POST requests containing JSON with 'sendMessage' or 'sendDocument' methods indicating automated message delivery.

suggestion.title: Ransom note deployment across file shares
suggestion.rationale: Extortion campaigns stage ransom notes (DECRYPT_ME.txt, README.txt) to victim systems; article discusses extortion tactics but pipeline captured no impact-phase detection for file creation, desktop changes, or victim notification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of files matching ransom-note patterns (README.*, DECRYPT.*, HELP*.txt) across 50+ directories or SMB shares in short time window. Monitor for registry modifications to wallpaper/screensaver hives; alert on bulk email/SMS dispatch from internal systems.

suggestion.title: Threat-actor leak site reconnaissance from internal endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article covers extortion marketplace economy but pipeline missed detection of reconnaissance activity targeting known extortion leak sites (ShinyHunters, Scattered LAPSUS$ portals) from breach-affected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and proxy logs for connections to known extortion gang leak portals and darkweb marketplace mirrors. Flag any internal user/system agent making repeated HTTP HEAD/GET requests to these sites, especially post-detection window.

suggestion.title: Supply-chain target enumeration in Active Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'supply chain' attacks used by extortion groups for initial compromise; no use case detects reconnaissance of vendor/partner accounts or systems prior to lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual LDAP queries filtering for supplier/partner domains or 'vendor' user descriptions from compromised service accounts. Flag password spray attempts against supplier-linked email domains or successful logins followed by immediate lateral movement to shared cloud infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Threat-actor operational security leak (OSINT harvesting)
suggestion.rationale: Extortion groups operate leak sites and Telegram channels to advertise victims; pipeline should flag reconnaissance of group operational infrastructure (Telegram channels, public victim lists) indicating threat maturity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated DNS/TLS lookups to known Telegram vanity channels associated with Bling Libra, Hazy Scorpius, ShinyHunters (e.g., @group_name_leaks). Alert on automated scraping patterns (user-agent anomalies) against threat-actor darkweb leak sites.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Critical Notepad++ Vulnerabilities Allow Attackers to Execute Arbitrary Code'—execution phase demands immediate detection for child processes spawned by notepad++.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on notepad++.exe spawning unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wmic.exe, curl.exe, net.exe). Establish baseline of legitimate plugin-related process spawning; flag anomalous command-line arguments or system utilities as code execution signal.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Unauthorized Plugin File Creation
suggestion.rationale: Code execution in text editors typically abuses plugin loading mechanisms. 'Critical' severity suggests active exploitation—require detection of malicious plugin files written to extension directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification in Notepad++ plugin directories (plugins/, plugins/installed/, plugins/NppPlugins/) from unexpected parent processes. Alert on DLL/executable files appearing outside normal vendor update windows.

suggestion.title: Notepad++ Binary Tampering via File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability exploitation often culminates in binary replacement or code injection to ensure persistence and repeated execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to notepad++.exe binary, unexpected DLL loads into Notepad++ address space (esp. unsigned/revoked certs), or file writes to installation directory from non-installer processes.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS RCE Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Code Execution Vulnerability Exploited'—core attack vector must be detected at delivery/exploitation stage before malware execution occurs. Pipeline missed initial access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to known FortiClient EMS endpoints (e.g., /api/v2/ endpoints) with unusual payloads, or unexpected execution of EMS child processes with suspicious cmdline parameters indicating code injection or template injection exploitation.

suggestion.title: EKZ Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deploy EKZ Malware'—this is the payload phase. Pipeline generated zero use cases for malware execution or file indicators despite this being the visible impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EKZ malware file creation, process execution, or module loads. If malware hashes are disclosed, prioritize hash-based detections; if not, behavioral detections should capture suspicious DLL injections or process hollowing from compromised EMS process.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Privilege Escalation or SYSTEM-Context Execution
suggestion.rationale: EMS vulnerability likely executes in high-privilege context (SYSTEM or administrative). Pipeline missed privilege escalation phase that would enable lateral movement or malware persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation under FortiClient EMS or related services executing child processes with elevated integrity levels, or writing to HKLM registry/startup locations. Token duplication or impersonation activity from EMS context is suspicious.

suggestion.title: EKZ Malware Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Deployed malware must establish C2 to receive commands or exfiltrate. Pipeline had no detection coverage for outbound infrastructure communication, a mandatory phase post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from EKZ malware process to known C2 infrastructure. If domains/IPs are disclosed, use them; otherwise, flag uncommon protocols (binary C2 on port 443, DNS exfiltration) or geographically anomalous destinations from newly infected EMS host.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiClient EMS
suggestion.rationale: EMS runs in network-trusted position and manages multiple endpoints. Article does not detail lateral movement but threat model implies post-exploitation pivot risk. Pipeline missed this critical secondary phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor EMS process or child processes for unexpected lateral connection attempts (e.g., SMB, WinRM, RDP) to other hosts. Flag pass-the-hash or credential relay from EMS host context, or remote execution of EKZ malware on secondary systems.

suggestion.title: Persistence via EKZ Malware (Registry/Scheduled Task)
suggestion.rationale: No persistence indicators extracted despite active exploitation for malware deployment—attacker must ensure EKZ survives reboots. Pipeline missed this phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on EKZ malware writing to Run keys (HKCU/HKLM), creating scheduled tasks, or registering WMI event subscriptions under EMS context. Monitor for new startup items appearing post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Execution from Recruitment-Themed Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets crypto firms via fake recruiter lures and macOS malware. Pipeline missed detection for initial payload execution from social engineering. 'Fake Recruiter Lures' combined with 'macOS Malware' implies weaponized attachments or archives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution (fork, spawn, or open) initiated from recently extracted or mounted archives with HR/recruitment-themed names. Focus on bash, zsh, or native macOS interpreters spawning unusual child processes immediately after archive mount events.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Recruiter Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly uses 'fake recruiter lures' targeting crypto firm employees. No detection use case for credential capture phishing or fake HR platforms mentioned in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication attempts from external recruitment platform domains not in allowlist, or from IPs geolocation inconsistent with recruiter origin. Monitor for credential submissions to domains with HR/recruitment keywords registered recently (< 90 days).

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent / Launch Daemon Installation from Crypto-Firm User
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware in targeted crypto campaign implies persistence mechanism. Pipeline extracted no persistence-phase detections despite malware being core to attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to ~/.LaunchAgents/, /Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons with source process being shell interpreter or archive extraction utility. Correlate with preceding network connections to attacker infrastructure or suspicious downloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Crypto Exchange / Wallet Infrastructure from Compromised Employee
suggestion.rationale: JINX-0164 targets cryptocurrency firms; no detection for lateral movement to high-value crypto assets, exchange wallets, or signing infrastructure post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP, SSH, or API calls from compromised employee endpoint to internal cryptocurrency infrastructure (exchange nodes, cold wallet signing servers, HSM management interfaces). Baseline normal access patterns per user role; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to Non-US C2 from Crypto Firm Network
suggestion.rationale: Cryptocurrency firms are high-value targets for theft. Pipeline generated no collection/exfiltration detections despite this being likely objective for JINX-0164 campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual egress volume or protocol usage to non-US ASNs from crypto firm endpoints, particularly from employee machines that executed the recruitment-themed malware. Flag exfiltration of wallet metadata, transaction logs, or customer databases.

suggestion.title: macOS Dylib Hijacking or Code Injection from Malware Dropper
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware delivery implies post-execution persistence/evasion (dylib injection, process hollowing). Title states malware but pipeline surfaced no evasion techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of .dylib files in non-standard locations, or dyld environment variable modifications. Correlate with process execution events showing unexpected library loads or code signing bypass indicators.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Zero-Day Exploitation Post-Public Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Public Release of Zero-Day Details Before Vendor Coordination'—indicates exploit code or functional PoC is likely public and attackers have actionable attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal process execution, network connections, or file writes on Microsoft products matching the disclosed zero-day vector. Correlate with public exploit release timeline. Look for obfuscated PowerShell, DLL injection, or memory-corruption signatures if RCE.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Microsoft Software Exploitation in Pre-Patch Window
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes vulnerability 'Before Vendor Coordination'—indicates a window where patches do not yet exist and all Microsoft instances are vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network/email ingress patterns targeting known-vulnerable Microsoft product versions during the pre-patch disclosure window. Flag any process spawning or command execution on affected products absent corresponding patch evidence.

suggestion.title: Correlation: Exploit PoC Public Release and Immediate Attack Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of public release—implies community detection logic should trigger on disclosed zero-day timelines and correlate with attack telemetry spikes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate public vulnerability disclosure events (CVE/PoC release) with process execution, network anomalies, or suspicious auth events on vulnerable systems. Spike detection in 6–72 hours post-public-release window.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading: Legitimate EXE + Malicious DLL Archive Pair
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the core technique: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' Archives contain paired legitimate executable (HLS Installer.874.exe) + unsigned DLL. No use case detects this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archives extracted in user directories containing both a legitimate Windows executable and unsigned DLL with suspicious size. Alert when extracted EXE executes immediately after extraction, especially from temp/Downloads. Flag when the DLL is loaded from archive extraction path into system process.

suggestion.title: Fake Plugin/Browser Update Prompts Leading to Archive Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial access: 'player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update' and fake browser crash page, driving downloads from 'urush1bar4[.]online'. This primary infection vector has no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archive downloads from non-legitimized update domains (outside Microsoft, Adobe, Google official repositories). Correlate browser page context (video player, streaming site) with EXE/ZIP downloads. Alert on downloads from .online domains during media playback sessions.

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner / XMRig Process Execution from Temp/Archive Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies payload: 'miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Malware names SilentCryptoMiner and XMRig appear in article metadata, but no use case detects miner spawn or resource indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution with command-line patterns matching XMRig or SilentCryptoMiner variants (pool URIs, wallet addresses, thread counts) spawned from user temp/downloads. Monitor for sustained high CPU consumption by child processes of extracted executables.

suggestion.title: RAT Module Beaconing and Remote Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'gained a RAT module' but provides no use case for C2 detection, command execution, or exfiltration indicators associated with remote access trojans.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound network connections from child processes of extracted EXEs to unusual ports or previously uncontacted IPs. Alert on periodic beaconing patterns (interval-based HTTP/HTTPS requests, binary protocol signatures) from temp-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Persistence Establishment via DLL Injection into System Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device,' but no use case covers registry modification, autorun keys, or DLL injection hooks created by the malicious DLL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKCU variants for new entries created by processes spawned from user directories. Detect unexpected DLL loads into svchost, explorer, or system processes from non-system32 paths.

suggestion.title: Multi-Year Campaign: Cross-Domain Infrastructure Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article ties current activity to 'previous campaigns' involving pirated digital libraries, with domain migration from 'file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu' to 'urush1bar4[.]online.' No use case tracks domain infrastructure patterns or campaign continuity indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries and network connections to .online TLDs hosting malware archives with previous .ru/.top piracy site activity. Flag organizations with historical connections to file[.]ipfs domains now connecting to urush1bar4[.]online or similar dynamic infra.

suggestion.title: SBI YONO App Deactivation Phishing SMS Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly describes 'Scammers are Sending Fake Messages Claiming Your YONO App Will be Deactivated.' Pipeline generated zero UC; this is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMS messages to SBI customers claiming immediate app deactivation, containing suspicious shortened URLs or callback numbers. Flag messages originating from non-official SBI shortcodes or claiming urgent action required to 'reactivate' the YONO app. Correlate with downstream phishing-page visits and credential entry attempts.

suggestion.title: Phishing Page Credential Harvesting from SBI YONO Deactivation Lures
suggestion.rationale: The scam inherently requires victims to be redirected to a fake login/OTP-entry page. Article states scammers send messages; the logical next step is credential harvesting, yet no UC captures the landing-page detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTP POST requests to domains mimicking SBI YONO (typosquats, lookalikes) originating from users who received the phishing SMS within the prior 15 minutes. Flag pages that prompt for OTP, password, or debit-card details under the guise of app reactivation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Events Post-Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Credential-theft phishing campaigns are followed by account-compromise attempts (login from new device, balance checks, fund transfers). Pipeline captured no detection for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-harvest phishing URLs with unusual SBI account login activity: login from new IP/device, multiple failed login attempts, followed by successful login and high-risk transactions (fund transfer, balance inquiry). Flag accounts accessed within 2–4 hours of the phishing-message timestamp.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Distribution via YONO App-Deactivation Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Fake-deactivation messages often include links to sideload or install fake banking apps. Article title hints at app compromise ('YONO App Will be Deactivated'), yet pipeline found no UC for malicious-app detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of APKs/apps from non-official app stores claiming to be 'YONO' or 'SBI Mobile Banking' following phishing-message receipt. Flag apps with suspicious permissions (SMS read, call interception, credential storage), and correlate installation with credential-entry events or unusual account activity.

suggestion.title: SBI Domain Typosquatting and Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Every phishing campaign requires attacker-controlled domains or redirect infrastructure. Article mentions fake messages but pipeline extracted zero IOCs, including no domains, shortened URLs, or hosting details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify typosquat domains registering 'YONO,' 'SBI-YONO,' or variants; correlate with SSL certificates issued in the campaign window. Flag DNS queries from Indian IP ranges and phishing-SMS recipients. Monitor WHOIS, registrant changes, and IP geolocation to attribute to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: IT Support Impersonation Email Targeting Law Firms
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'IT Support Impersonation Attacks' as primary vector; pipeline generated zero detections for phishing/pretexting campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails spoofing internal IT support, help desk, or security teams requesting immediate credential verification, MFA resets, or account confirmation. Flag urgency language (locked account, security incident, verify now) and URLs directing to credential-capture domains or lookalike authentication pages.

suggestion.title: Help Desk System Abuse for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Impersonation campaigns typically pivot to help desk exploitation for password resets; pipeline missed internal detection opportunity for unusual reset requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor help desk and identity systems for MFA bypass requests, credential resets, or account unlocks initiated by external or unfamiliar internal addresses outside change windows; cross-reference with email impersonation attempts.

suggestion.title: Silent Ransom Group Campaign Indicator Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor name 'Silent Ransom Group' provided in title; pipeline failed to surface actor name or correlate with public threat intelligence on infrastructure, domains, or malware hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enrich all initial-access detections with threat intelligence on Silent Ransom Group known sender domains, spoofed law-firm subdomains, C2 infrastructure, and associated malware indicators if available from public advisories.

suggestion.title: Law Firm Sector-Targeted Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies law firms as target sector; indicates reconnaissance and vertical targeting requiring sector-aware alerting that pipeline did not generate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect campaigns with law-firm context (references to legal processes, attorney language, spoofed law-firm domains, bar association branding) combined with credential-harvest redirects or malware delivery.

suggestion.title: Veeam Service Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Privilege Escalation Attacks' via Veeam—core attack vector. No rule generated. Veeam backup processes should be monitored for token elevation and unprivileged-to-privileged transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Veeam backup service processes (veeam*.exe, VeeamBrokerSvc, VeeamNotificationSvc) spawning child processes with SYSTEM or high-integrity tokens. Flag repeated elevation prompt failures or token requests via Veeam threads to administrative resources.

suggestion.title: Veeam Credential Dumping and SAM Access
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation vulnerabilities in backup software enable credential theft—article implies multi-stage attack. Pipeline missed credential_access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by Veeam services accessing SAM registry hives, LSASS memory, or executing credential dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump). Monitor Veeam database and config file reads for sensitive credential material.

suggestion.title: Access Token Manipulation via Veeam Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation typically leverages token manipulation (T1134). Not captured. Veeam services run in privileged contexts and may allow token duplication or impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Veeam service processes creating handle duplications with elevated privileges, or spawning child processes with mismatched integrity levels. Flag OpenProcessToken or DuplicateToken API calls originating from Veeam backup service threads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Software Recommendation URLs in LLM Outputs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'users querying AI chatbots for software download recommendations were presented with links to attacker-controlled domains within generated responses.' Pipeline missed the LLM injection vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM API responses and user-facing chatbot outputs for domain recommendations that match newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Flag responses recommending download links for legitimate software (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear) from non-official sources.

suggestion.title: Trojanized System Utility Downloads from Suspicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Campaign 'impersonates legitimate system utilities' and 'targets users who own high-performance GPUs.' Need detection for downloads of signed-looking but malicious binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of executables matching known legitimate software names (CrystalDiskInfo.exe, HWMonitor.exe, FurMark.exe, etc.) from domains not matching official publisher domains. Cross-reference against Windows Update and official vendor sites.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Process Execution and GPU Utilization Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states campaign's goal is 'cryptocurrency mining' and 'GPU mining value.' Once infected, systems exhibit characteristic mining behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known cryptomining binaries (xmrig, monero-miner, etc.) or unsigned processes spawning GPU-intensive child processes. Correlate with sustained GPU utilization >80% for >30 minutes on non-gaming systems. Monitor for process names masquerading as system utilities.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Tool Installation Post-Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers [gain] persistent remote access through abused ScreenConnect deployments' as secondary payload. ScreenConnect execution is post-exploitation persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ScreenConnect (ConnectWise) process execution following recent suspicious software downloads. Alert on ScreenConnect service installation or unsigned ScreenConnect binary execution. Monitor for ScreenConnect network beaconing to attacker-controlled relay servers.

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoned Malicious Domain Cluster Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'SEO poisoning' as technique to surface malicious download sites. Domains impersonating legitimate software publishers appear in search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clusters of newly-registered domains with typosquatting variations or subdomain layouts mimicking legitimate software vendors (e.g., 'crystaldiskinfo-official.com', 'hwmonitor.net'). Correlate domains with malware hosting infrastructure and track which systems resolved/visited them.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GPU-Targeted System Reconnaissance
