suggestion.rationale: Process hollowing deployment requires non-standard MsBuild invocation (encoding, remote XML fetch, obfuscated targets). Command-line anomalies are strong evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MsBuild.exe with encoded/obfuscated command lines, inline C# targets, network-fetched project files, or invocation from Explorer/Task Scheduler context. Exclude legitimate MSBuild paths (C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio).

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Archive-Extracted Executable
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector explicitly stated: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' Article provides executable name (HLS Installer.874.exe) and attack pattern. No detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when extractable/installer executables (matching HLS Installer.*.exe pattern) load DLLs from non-standard paths (temp, same directory, or extracted archive locations). Establish baseline of legitimate DLL loads for this installer, alert on anomalies. Cross-reference extracted DLL paths with known-malicious signatures.

suggestion.title: Fake Video Player Plugin Update Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Initial infection vector: 'the player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue.' No detection for this social-engineering and execution trigger was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious archive downloads from .ru and .top TLD domains after user visits piracy streaming sites. Alert when archive downloads are preceded by browser plugin-update prompts or overlapping HTTP requests without explicit user save-dialog interaction. Correlate with known malicious domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Delivery from Known Piracy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies active delivery domain: 'the threat actor employed a new website, urush1bar4[.]online' hosting malicious ZIP archives. Previously used: 'file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu.' Neither domain nor delivery pattern generated detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Blocklist urush1bar4.online and file.ipfs.us.69.mu; expand to domain patterns (*bar*.online, *.ipfs.*.mu). Alert on successful or attempted downloads from these domains. Detect multi-part/resumed archive downloads, which indicate intentional fragmentation for evasion.

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner and XMRig Process Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware families: 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Metadata tags reference XMRig. No detection use cases or IOC extraction for miner deployment or persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SilentCryptoMiner and XMRig execution by process name/hash patterns. Monitor for registry modifications creating Run keys or startup entries by processes originating from archive extraction/installer execution. Alert on sustained high-CPU processes with cryptocurrency pool communication signatures.

suggestion.title: Watchdog RAT Agent Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Watchdog RAT agent' as component of malware payload but provides no behavioral or persistence detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of services or Run-key entries by processes spawned from DLL side-loading sequences. Monitor for unexpected parent-child process relationships where archive-extracted/legitimate binary spawns persistence-establishing processes. Correlate with network connections to command-and-control infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Mixed Legitimate/Malicious Archive Extraction Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes archive structure: 'The archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL.' This mixed-composition pattern is detectable but no use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect extraction of archives containing both legitimate executables and unexpected/suspicious DLL files to the same directory. Alert when a legitimate binary is executed immediately after such extraction. Maintain whitelist of expected DLLs per installer; flag novel DLLs in same-directory loads as side-loading attempts.

suggestion.title: IT Support Impersonation Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'IT Support Impersonation Attacks' as the attack vector. Pipeline missed generating detection logic for spoofed/lookalike IT support sender addresses requesting credentials or access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with sender addresses spoofing legitimate internal/vendor IT support domains, containing social engineering language requesting credential resets, system updates, or urgent access verification. Include homograph detection for near-lookalike domains (e.g. `itsupport-firmname.com` vs `itsupport.firmname.com`).

suggestion.title: Authentication Anomalies Post-Impersonation Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting law firm employees via impersonation—successful social engineering typically results in credential compromise and account takeover attempts. Pipeline should have mapped credential_access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users who engaged with impersonation senders (email open, link click from email logs) with subsequent authentication anomalies: failed logins from new IPs, unusual geographies, MFA failures, or legitimate credential use from flagged devices.

suggestion.title: Ransomware File Encryption from Law Firm Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor identified as 'Silent Ransom Group'—ransomware deployment is the stated impact. Pipeline should have generated impact-phase detection for mass file encryption targeting law firm document repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk file writes with encryption extensions (.encrypted, .ransom, etc.) targeting common law firm file shares (\\sharepoint, document management systems). Alert on process creation of encryption tools or PowerShell/cmd.exe with encoding/encryption parameters.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Law Firm Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Successful impersonation of law firm employees grants access to sensitive document systems and client data; attackers typically move laterally to maximize impact and exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral movement from initially-compromised accounts (identified via impersonation correlation) to administrative shares, backup systems, and document repositories. Flag credential forwarding (NTLM relay, pass-the-hash) and unusual inter-department account usage.

suggestion.title: Typosquat/Lookalike Domain Registration for IT Support Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: IT support impersonation attacks require attacker-controlled or compromised domains mimicking legitimate IT services. Pipeline should surface early-stage infrastructure IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly-registered domains resembling law firm IT support domains (homographs, typosquats). Cross-reference with known law firm names and common IT service naming patterns. Flag domains registered to known malicious registrars or privacy services near campaign dates.

suggestion.title: Document Exfiltration from Law Firm SMB Shares
suggestion.rationale: Law firms hold sensitive client data; article context implies Silent Ransom Group combines encryption with data exfiltration. Pipeline should have detection for bulk document access/exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual volume of document access from compromised accounts, bulk SMB enumeration, and outbound SFTP/FTP/HTTPS transfers of large file volumes to attacker infrastructure. Correlate with ransomware encryption timeline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Registration with FIFA Brand Keywords
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Spoofing FIFA Websites' — requires detection of domain registrations with FIFA, worldcup, or official FIFA domain variants. Pipeline generated zero IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on newly registered domains with Levenshtein distance < 3 from fifa.com or containing FIFA-related keywords. Cross-reference registrant privacy toggles, GoDaddy/NameCheap registration patterns, and bulk registrations from same account. Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for issuance to these domains.

suggestion.title: Email Phishing Referencing FIFA Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Spoofing campaign requires distribution — article describes stealing PII implying victim compromise via initial compromise vector. Credential-access phase not reconstructed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with embedded links to FIFA lookalike domains, especially requests for login credentials, registration info, or personal identifiers (name, address, phone). Alert on sender domain spoofing (fifa-[variant]@...) or compromised legitimate sports/fan accounts distributing FIFA phishing links.

suggestion.title: HTTPS Traffic to FIFA Typosquatted Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exfiltration of name, home address, phone number — requires harvesting infrastructure reachable by victims. No network/web traffic detection use case provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS connections to domains with high string similarity to fifa.com or official FIFA properties. Alert on connections to IPs registered recently or with no ASN reputation history. Detect suspicious SSL/TLS certificates (issuer, subject mismatch) or connections lacking expected FIFA brand assets.

suggestion.title: SSL Certificate Issuance for FIFA Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-as-service spoofing infrastructure depends on valid SSL certs for legitimacy — no IOC tracking or CT log monitoring provided by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Certificate Transparency (crt.sh) for certificate issuance to domains containing 'fifa', 'worldcup', or FIFA subdomain patterns. Alert on bulk issuance from single account, use of DV certificates only (no EV), or issuance from free CAs (Let's Encrypt) for phishing infrastructure domains.

suggestion.title: Bulk WHOIS Privacy Registration of Sports-Themed Domains
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors spoofing FIFA likely registered multiple variants — systematic domain enumeration and bulk registration patterns not detected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk domain registrations with privacy protection enabled, FIFA/sports keywords, and registration timing clusters. Alert on shared registrant email, payment method, or registrar account creating 3+ lookalike domains within 30-day window. Track registrar WHOIS API activity from suspicious sources.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of PII (Name, Address, Phone) to Command Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists stolen PII types (name, home address, phone number) — requires detection of data exfiltration patterns. Pipeline failed to identify exfiltration phase or corresponding detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to suspicious infrastructure containing form fields matching PII schema (firstname, lastname, address, phone, ssn, etc.). Correlate with DNS queries to FIFA lookalikes. Detect unusual outbound data volumes from web-facing systems or abnormal C2-like beacon patterns exfiltrating structured data.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via CVE-2026-32996 (Veeam Backup & Replication)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'an attacker with basic system access could leverage this flaw to transition from a standard user account to administrative control.' This is the core exploit mechanism yet zero UCs were generated for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with elevated token/integrity level originating from Veeam Backup & Replication service or related processes (VeeamBP.exe, VeeamBackupService.exe). Alert on transitions from BUILTIN\USERS to BUILTIN\ADMINISTRATORS context within Veeam process trees.

suggestion.title: Version Inventory and Vulnerable Build Detection (Veeam 13.0.1.2067 and earlier)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions (13.0.1.2067 and earlier v13 builds) and patched version (13.0.2.29). Detection must include version-based fingerprinting. Pipeline omitted vulnerability-specific version detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate and alert on Veeam Backup & Replication installations reporting version <= 13.0.1.2067 via registry queries (HKLM\Software\Veeam) or WMI Win32_Product. Correlate with lateral movement or privilege escalation events within 24h of discovery.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Backup System Integrity Attack (Ransomware Context)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states compromised backup servers enable attackers to 'manipulate or delete recovery points' and highlights 'ransomware's targeting of backup infrastructure.' This specific impact vector—backup destruction—requires dedicated detection but no UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion or modification of Veeam backup metadata, restore points, or replica configurations originating from compromised user accounts. Monitor Veeam API calls or Job Manager modifications executed outside normal maintenance windows with admin-escalated tokens.

suggestion.title: Initial Compromise Leading to Veeam Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain as 'initial compromise via phishing or credential compromise' followed by local escalation. No UC captures the phishing/credential compromise stage that precedes the Veeam exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing indicators (suspicious email attachments, credential-harvesting URLs) or failed authentication spikes with subsequent privilege escalation attempts on Veeam-hosting machines. Flag user accounts with both email-based compromise indicators and local privilege escalation attempts within 72 hours.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Veeam Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit enables 'lateral network movement.' This post-escalation lateral movement represents a distinct phase yet the pipeline failed to surface detection for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After privilege escalation from Veeam process, detect unusual network connections or lateral movement attempts (SMB, RDP, WinRM) originating from the previously compromised host. Alert if admin-context processes spawned from Veeam context initiate connections to adjacent systems not in the backup infrastructure whitelist.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Redirect to Known Malware Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites'—chatbot output is being weaponized as a delivery mechanism. Pipeline should detect chatbot platforms recommending domains flagged as malware hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot API responses and user-facing recommendations for URLs/domains matching malware intelligence feeds. Flag instances where chatbot recommends or redirects to known cryptojacking infrastructure or C2 endpoints. Correlate with user click-through events.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Process Detection Post-Chatbot Click
suggestion.rationale: The attack outcome is resource hijacking—'cryptojacking malware sites' implies execution of mining code. Users visiting malicious domains via chatbot recommendations should trigger process and network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-infection, detect sustained high CPU/GPU utilization, unusual child process spawning (miners often daemonize), and outbound connections to known mining pool IPs on ports 3333, 5555, 8333, 14444. Correlate with recent visits to malware domains from same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Chatbot Recommendation Output Pattern Shift
suggestion.rationale: Article implies chatbot accounts or model inference is compromised to emit malicious recommendations. Detect deviations in chatbot output content/tone that precede user redirection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal chatbot recommendation patterns (domains, entities, sentiment). Flag conversations with anomalous URL recommendations, recommendations not in training knowledge base, or sudden topic shifts to financial/mining services. Correlate with downstream user clicks to malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: User Click-Through to Chatbot-Recommended Malware Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires user execution of malicious link provided by chatbot. Detection of user following chatbot links to known-bad destinations is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web traffic and browser history for navigation events where the HTTP Referer or preceding interaction log shows chatbot recommendation context immediately before access to known cryptojacking or malware domains. Flag user_id + domain pairs.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Platform Compromise Detection (Backdoor/Injection)
suggestion.rationale: Root cause is compromise of chatbot system itself—either account takeover, prompt injection, or backend infiltration. Pipeline should surface indicators of chatbot infrastructure integrity loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized API calls to chatbot model serving endpoints, anomalous prompt patterns (injection signatures), unexpected configuration changes to recommendation algorithms, or authentication anomalies (unusual IPs, rate spikes, credential reuse) on chatbot admin/API accounts.

suggestion.title: Mining Pool Connection Tracking from Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking always requires outbound persistence to mining infrastructure. Detecting connections post-click establishes attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to known cryptocurrency mining pool domains/IPs (Monero pools, Ethereum pools, etc.) and mining-related ports (3333, 5555, 8333, 14444, 7777) originating from endpoints that recently clicked chatbot-recommended links. Mine pool IPs often appear in threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Spraying Attempts Against AD
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' as the threat model motivating weak-password blocking. No detection use case was generated despite this being the primary named attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume failed login attempts across multiple user accounts within short time window, targeting a small set of weak passwords. Flag correlation of 10+ failed logons with identical password in 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Detect Multiple Failed Password Change Attempts from Single User
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'When policies are strict and employees make mistakes, support queues quickly fill up.' Multiple password change rejections indicate either policy violation attempts or weak-password probing attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AD password change events with failure codes indicating policy violations (complexity, breach history, length). Three or more failures from single user in 30 minutes suggests either legitimate policy struggle or attacker testing weak passwords.

suggestion.title: Detect Potential Credential Reuse Across Heterogeneous Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Even when employees create a good AD password, they're likely to repeat it across other systems.' Cross-system password matching indicates policy circumvention and creates lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication logs across AD, web applications, email, and cloud platforms. Flag users where identical or near-identical passwords are detected across multiple systems within short time window.

suggestion.title: Detect Self-Service Password Reset Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends SSPR with MFA: 'By verifying identity through MFA or other authentication methods, staff can reset their own passwords quickly.' Unusual SSPR patterns may indicate account takeover or social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSPR requests for anomalies: multiple resets from same user in single day, geographic/device anomalies, resets immediately following failed login sequences (potential account recovery after takeover).

suggestion.title: Detect Breached Password Usage in AD Password Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article states Specops 'continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials' and 'Verizon's Data Breach Investigation Report found stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches.' Failed password changes due to breach history indicate post-compromise credential reuse attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AD password change attempts rejected for breach history match, or detected password changes where the new password is subsequently found in breach databases. Flag users with multiple breached-credential rejections as elevated risk.

suggestion.title: cPanel JSON API Redis Function Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'This vulnerability is being actively exploited' through the lsws.redisAble function and provides detection command: grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs. Exploitation indicator is unambiguous and actionable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel and WHM JSON API logs for function calls to cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble. Flag any calls originating from unexpected IP addresses or during off-hours. Correlate with the provided grep pattern and examine source IPs to distinguish valid administration from exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Script Execution Following Redis API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as enabling 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' via Redis function. System logs should show abnormal root execution chains following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation by correlating cPanel JSON API calls to redisAble with subsequent root-level process execution or script invocation. Look for execution trees where unprivileged cPanel/web processes spawn root shells or system commands.

suggestion.title: Detection of Vulnerable LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4' are affected. Vulnerable version inventory is necessary for impact assessment and hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query systems for installed LiteSpeed cPanel user-end plugin version in /usr/local/cpanel/plugins or equivalent. Flag any instance reporting version 2.3.x through 2.4.4 as requiring immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Abnormal cPanel JSON API Function Calls to Disabled Features
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability stems from 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features' with 'incorrect privilege assignment.' Calls to disabled or restricted Redis functions are exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel JSON API audit logs for attempts to invoke or modify Redis enable/disable configuration. Alert on calls from non-administrative contexts or IPs not typically invoking privileged cPanel functions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation IP Blocking from Suspicious cPanel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article advises 'determine if they are valid, and if not, block them' after examining IPs from log grep results, indicating threat intel integration step for active exploitation response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract source IPs from successful redisAble function calls. Cross-reference against whitelists of known administrative IPs. Auto-flag and recommend blocking any unfamiliar IPs initiating privileged API calls, particularly during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Publish from Trusted Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious versions of the product to be published to the npm registry under a trusted identity'—supply chain attack requires detecting anomalous package publishes from previously trusted author accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish events for accounts with historical package-release rights. Flag publishes from unusual geolocations, off-hours windows, or with token reuse patterns. Correlate with credential exposure feeds to detect compromised publisher accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-npm Installation Credential Theft Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware'—preinstall/postinstall scripts execute during npm install; detect credential access patterns from node_modules processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on credential access from npm-spawned child processes: LSASS probing, .ssh/.aws file reads, environment variable exfiltration, stdin capture from password managers or CLI tools. Correlate with rare process parents from node_modules.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution via Dependency Installation Script
suggestion.rationale: Article: credential-stealing malware embedded in published packages—execution phase begins when preinstall/postinstall scripts run during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update process trees for suspicious children: interpreters (python, bash, powershell) spawned from node_modules, or curl/wget downloading external payloads. Flag unexpected network egress from npm parent processes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Version and Integrity Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: malicious versions published to trusted namespace—detect version mismatches, unexpected jumps, or hash discrepancies between package-lock.json and npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed package hashes against npm registry canonical hashes; flag lock-file entries with version variance, unexpected pre-release tags, or packages sourced from non-canonical registries.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Malicious npm Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware persists by embedding malicious scripts in package.json preinstall/postinstall hooks—detect obfuscated or suspicious install-time hooks in dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse all package.json preinstall/postinstall scripts in node_modules for obfuscation, base64/hex encoding, curl/wget payloads, or reverse-shell patterns. Alert on scripts executing outside project scope or modifying system files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement of Malicious Dependency Across Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm package in one project spreads to internal teams via shared private registries, CI/CD pipelines, and dev environment caches—track installation propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate malicious TanStack installations across multiple machines, projects, and teams. Track propagation through private npm registries, CI/CD artifact caches, and shared development environments. Identify teams or services that pulled the compromised version.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Malicious Extension Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious version of Nx Console to be published' with 'obfuscated payload' execution, but pipeline generated zero detection hypothesis for identifying post-installation runtime activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console or VSCode extension processes spawning obfuscated or suspicious child processes, unusual file I/O to configuration directories, or immediate network callbacks after extension activation. Alert on process trees where Nx runtime queries credential storage paths within seconds of load.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Disk and Memory Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory' — this core attack step received zero detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential access to credential storage locations (.ssh, .aws, browser credential databases, Clipboard), LSASS handle opens, or registry queries for cached credentials. Correlate with Nx Console parent process to attribute harvesting to the malicious extension.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Fetch and Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — C2 network callbacks and in-memory deobfuscation are explicit attack steps with no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections from Nx Console to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Detect in-memory deobfuscation patterns (base64 decoding, XOR operations, zlib decompression) in child process contexts spawned by the extension.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'compromised extension' and 'malicious version...published' — supply chain compromise detection needed to block initial install before credential harvesting occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager activity (npm logs, VSCode marketplace API calls) for Nx Console installations and validate package hash against vendor-published security advisory. Flag installations of vulnerable versions or from non-official repositories.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential harvesting from disk and memory but does not detail exfiltration; credentials harvested must be moved out-of-process for attacker use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-harvesting process events with subsequent outbound network activity containing base64-encoded or structured data patterns. Alert on unusual data volumes or encrypted tunnels from compromised host to external IPs on non-standard ports within 1 hour of harvest.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes active exploitation and names the product: 'Vendor: Daemon, Product: Daemon Tools Lite.' Asset inventory is step one for any KEV response. Pipeline ignored this foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Daemon Tools Lite installations via MSI execution, process creation patterns, or registry artifacts. Enumerate all instances across fleet to establish baseline of exposed assets. Correlate with vulnerability scanner for unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Unpatched Detection via Vulnerability Scanner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using templates. CVE-2026-8398 must be flagged in Qualys, Tenable, Defender outputs. Federal due date (2026-05-30) creates audit trail requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2026-8398 in any unpatched state. Track remediation velocity to federal deadline. Cross-pivot to installed Daemon Tools Lite census for validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process or Network Activity Originating from Daemon Tools Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'embedded malicious code' with 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability.' Once installed, the payload executes. Behavioral detection of anomalous child processes, file writes, or network connections from Daemon Tools paths is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation, file-write, or network-connect events originating from standard Daemon Tools Lite installation directories (e.g., C:\Program Files\DAEMON Tools Lite\). Flag unsigned executables, unexpected child processes, or non-standard egress.

suggestion.title: Registry or Persistence Artifact Created by Daemon Tools Process
suggestion.rationale: Embedded malicious code implies post-installation persistence. 'High impact on... availability' suggests sustained presence. Article does not discuss patch/remediation mechanics—assume attacker maintains footholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry modifications (Run, RunOnce, startup keys, services) or scheduled task creation by Daemon Tools parent or child processes. Flag persistence artifacts in Windows startup paths or scheduled task store.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication Initiated by Daemon Tools Process
suggestion.rationale: Article's impact statement ('confidentiality, integrity, availability') and active-exploitation status (KEV) imply attacker objectives beyond simple code execution. Malware embedded in Daemon Tools will likely exfiltrate or accept commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Daemon Tools processes to non-standard ports, suspicious IPs, or known C2 infrastructure. Baseline normal Daemon Tools connectivity; flag deviations. Correlate with asset-exposure findings to triage vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Continuous API Reconnaissance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers are 'probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed' and describes recon as a foundational step in the attack motion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained, high-volume API endpoint probing from single source IPs or API clients within short time windows. Look for systematic enumeration of path parameters, object IDs, and HTTP methods without legitimate request patterns (e.g., varying Accept headers, random parameter fuzzing, sequential ID ranges).

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Exploitation via Authorization Probe Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'a chain of authorization probes guided by structural reasoning'—this describes BOLA detection as a multi-step exploit, not a single anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of 403/401 responses followed by successful 200s for the same resource path but different user contexts or IDs in close succession. Flag when one API client accesses objects belonging to multiple distinct user/tenant contexts within API tokens' valid lifespans.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass via Context-Dependent Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes context-dependent vulns where 'intended behavior and actual behavior' diverge in authentication logic; pentesters find 'what's only revealed through context'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful API calls or resource access immediately following failed auth attempts or malformed token submissions without re-authentication. Monitor for token reuse across different permission levels, cross-tenant session reuse, or privilege escalation without explicit permission grants in access logs.

suggestion.title: Chained Vulnerability Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path' as context-dependent and requiring reasoning-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of moderate-severity findings (e.g., weak input validation → information disclosure → privilege misuse) executed by the same source within 30–300 seconds. Track when multiple low-confidence exploits are chained; watch for data exfiltration immediately following auth-bypass and enumeration sequences.

suggestion.title: Attacker-Controlled AI Agent API Fuzzing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed' and discusses 'attacker's offensive AI' as equivalent to defender tools—implies systematic, non-human fuzzing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API fuzzing signatures: rapid cycling through parameter mutation (boundary values, null, empty strings, type mismatches), identical User-Agent + request patterns across multiple endpoints in burst windows, or requests with incomplete/malformed payloads unlikely from human clients. Correlate with zero legitimate conversion rates (100% error responses from source).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email + Phone Call Impersonating IT Support
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors use a social engineering scheme to pose as an employee from the victim's IT department. SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' Core initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with urgent language from internal IT department address/spoofs requesting credential validation or system access confirmation. Correlate with inbound suspicious calls shortly after phishing email delivery. Flag emails requesting users to 'call support' at external phone numbers.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Access Grant Post-Social Engineering Contact
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' Detectable via RDP logon correlation with phishing events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP/RemoteApp connection grants from external IPs within 2 hours of phishing email received by same user. Monitor for legitimate remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, RDP) invoked immediately after suspicious inbound calls. Flag successful RDP logons from non-VPN external IPs to users targeted by SRG phishing.

suggestion.title: USB/External Drive Insertion for Physical Data Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'If that attempt fails, SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and 'bulk copy operations to newly-connected external storage devices during off-hours or by unknown users on corporate machines.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PnP events for USB/external drive connections on corporate machines. Alert on high-volume (>100 files) copy operations to newly-connected removable media. Flag USB connections from unknown personnel or on machines where RDP was recently granted. Monitor for external drive connections followed by immediate Safe removal.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized In-Person Access - Physical IT Support Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' as SRG indicator. Physical security breach with social engineering element.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unknown visitor badge entries in IT/server areas with USB insertions or unexpected RDP logons within same timeframe. Flag badge reader logs for unvetted individuals accessing restricted computer areas. Cross-check claimed IT support personnel against active IT staff roster and call IT help desk to verify.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted IT Support Domain Access and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Lookalike domain tactic for initial access/credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to domains that are one character/typo variant of known legitimate IT support portals (suppor7.com vs support.com). Alert on user credentials submitted to newly-registered domains resembling organization IT helpdesk URLs. Monitor for phishing emails with links to unvetted IT support domains.

suggestion.title: Post-Exfiltration Extortion Ransom Emails and Victim Pressure Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them.' Late-stage impact/extortion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing threats to publish/sell stolen data, ransom payment demands, or references to SRG leak sites. Monitor for coordinated phone calls to employee personal numbers or client contacts threatening data release. Flag emails from previously unseen external domains claiming to represent 'data recovery' or 'breach notification' services.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm text contains Java compilation keywords / imports (pre-exploitation indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text.' Payloads must include Java syntax (import, class, extends, Runtime, exec, etc.) that should be detectable in algorithm PATCH bodies before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* where the request body contains suspicious Java keywords (import, Runtime.getRuntime(), ProcessBuilder, java.lang.exec) or string-concatenation patterns typical of code-injection payloads. Medium confidence (some false positives on complex legitimate algorithms); flag for analyst review.

suggestion.title: Yamcs user elevated to ChangeMissionDatabase privilege (prerequisite for exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An authenticated user with the `ChangeMissionDatabase` privilege can exploit this.' Monitor privilege assignment to detect adversary privilege escalation or account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for creation or modification of Yamcs users/roles with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege, especially if the user was previously unprivileged or was created by an anomalous actor. Flag out-of-hours or non-admin-initiated changes. Requires Yamcs audit logging integration.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm compilation errors / Janino engine exceptions spiking
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Janino expression engine compiling algorithm text. Exploitation attempts that fail syntax validation will generate compilation errors in Yamcs logs. A spike in Janino exceptions may indicate active exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs for increased frequency of Janino compilation errors, unexpected exception stack traces, or errors mentioning 'algorithm' and 'compile'. Baseline normal error rate and alert on spikes. May indicate fuzzing or active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Long or repetitive algorithm text submission (payload delivery obfuscation indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Injecting arbitrary Java code into an algorithm text field will likely result in unusually long, complex, or multi-line algorithm definitions compared to legitimate baseline patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal algorithm text length and complexity in PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/*. Flag submissions that exceed 2–3 standard deviations above the median, especially if they contain nested structures or encoded content (base64, gzip, etc.).

suggestion.title: Yamcs process memory or CPU spike preceding shell spawning (Janino compilation load indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Compiling arbitrary Java code via Janino will be CPU and memory intensive compared to normal algorithm evaluation. Unusual resource consumption immediately before shell spawning may indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate elevated CPU and memory usage in Yamcs JVM process with subsequent shell child-process spawning. Flag instances where baseline is exceeded by >50% within 10–30 seconds of a shell spawn.

suggestion.title: Yamcs configuration file or classpath modification (post-RCE artifact)
suggestion.rationale: After RCE, attacker may modify Yamcs configuration files or inject malicious JARs into the classpath for persistence or additional capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of Yamcs configuration files (yamcs.yaml, etc.) or JAR files in the Yamcs installation directory, especially by non-admin accounts or outside normal deployment windows. Flag unexpected changes to the classpath or plugins directory.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS valueOf filter gadget chain instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core exploit: '{%assign r=1|valueOf%}' evaluates to context object, exposing parser internals and filesystem. Pipeline missed the critical gadget evaluation itself—this is the pivot point from injection to execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes running LiquidJS for template evaluation of 'valueOf' filter expressions. Alert on sequential property access chains (r.context → r.liquid.parser → r.liquid.options.fs) within a single request handler. Can correlate with preceding HTTP request containing template payload.

suggestion.title: Node.js require('child_process') from web context
suggestion.rationale: Article payload chains through context object to access and execute child_process module for RCE. Detecting require() or dynamic module loading from within a web request handler is a critical execution indicator the pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node.js process instantiating child_process module or calling execSync/spawnSync from request handler context. Correlate with preceding SSTI gadget token detection. High-fidelity signal if request body contained template injection payload within past 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS context environment variable enumeration
suggestion.rationale: The context object grants access to process.env and config options. After successful RCE, attacker inevitably enumerates environment for secrets, credentials, and configuration—article omits this discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE, hunt for Node.js spawning processes that enumerate /proc/self, read .env files, access /var/run/secrets, or list parent directories. Baseline normal template access patterns and flag anomalous file discovery sequences after shell execution.

suggestion.title: Yamcs authentication spike or privilege escalation to ChangeMissionDatabase role
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' is required to exploit. Missing initial-access pattern: how does attacker obtain this privilege? No hunt for suspicious auth or RBAC elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for failed login attempts to Yamcs REST API (/api/auth, /api/users), or successful auth followed by immediate RBAC privilege modification to include ChangeMissionDatabase. Suspicious if performed by non-admin account or outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Algorithm modification or creation via REST without corresponding UI/logged trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'overriding the algorithm' as core step. Need detection for algorithm PATCH/POST that bypasses logging, appears anomalous, or originates from non-standard client (raw curl, Python requests, not web UI).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Yamcs REST API PATCH/POST to algorithm endpoints (e.g., `/api/mdb/*/algorithms/` or `/api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*`) with embedded script content (keywords: 'import', 'class ', 'def ') should be logged. Alert if: (1) payload size >1KB, (2) originating IP not in allow-list, (3) User-Agent indicates scripting (curl, Python, wget), or (4) same user modifies algorithm within seconds of prior authentication spike.

suggestion.title: Yamcs MDB archive file exfil or unusual data export post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: After achieving RCE, attacker may dump the mission database (MDB) for offline analysis or persistence. Article mentions 'Mission Database' but no UC for exfil detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GET requests to `/api/mdb/*/download` or `*.mdb` file downloads, especially unusual file sizes or timestamps. Correlate with prior shell spawning UC_15_5. Also monitor for Java process reading large binaries in Yamcs data directory (~yamcs/mdb/*) followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Jython / JSR-223 ScriptEngine API invocation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Jython' and 'JSR-223 ScriptEngine API' as the vulnerable code path. Missing hunt for unexpected use of these APIs at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Yamcs logs are available, hunt for ScriptEngineManager.getEngineByName() or eval() calls with non-whitelisted script sources. At OS level, detect Java process spawning with unusual command-line flags (e.g., `-Dpython.*`, `jython.home=`, sys.path manipulation). Correlate timestamp with algorithm PATCH UC_15_4.

suggestion.title: Yamcs configuration or credential theft via injected algorithm code
suggestion.rationale: Successful code execution allows attacker to read Yamcs config (database credentials, API keys, TLS certs). No UC for detection of credential/config file access post-RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Java/Jython process reading files in Yamcs config directory (e.g., `etc/`, `.properties`, `.yaml`, `.conf`) or reading environment variables (JAVA_HOME, DB_PASSWD, API_KEY). Correlate with shell-spawn UC_15_5 and timestamp within seconds of algorithm PATCH UC_15_4.

suggestion.title: Reverse shell or interactive session initiated by injected Yamcs algorithm code
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'code injection' enabling RCE, but hunts focus on outbound C2 (UC_15_6) or generic shell spawning (UC_15_5). Missing specific hunt for reverse shell indicators (backconnect, socat, nc -e).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Yamcs Java process establishing outbound TCP connection followed immediately by stdin/stdout redirection (e.g., ps aux showing java with `</dev/tcp/`, `nc -e`, `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/`, or socat spawning bash). Pair with proxy logs for TLS handshake anomalies (no HTTP/HTTPS protocol framing, raw socket communication).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Registry API Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication'—implies attackers can enumerate/pull images without credentials. T1526 (Enumerate Cloud Resources) and T1552.001 (Credentials in Files).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/HEAD requests to container registry endpoints (/v2, /api/v1, /..) lacking Authorization headers or token authentication. Flag successful 200-range responses from private image repos; correlate with source IPs not in allowlist. Baseline expected registry traffic first.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Container Image Download
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'exposes private container images without authentication.' Detect successful blob/manifest pulls for images marked private/internal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful transfers of layers/blobs from Gitea container registry marked as private when request lacked valid auth token or came from external CIDR. Size-based anomaly detection: unusually large blob downloads out-of-hours.

suggestion.title: Gitea Registry Endpoint Anonymous Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability likely allows listing/enumerating repositories without auth. Article: 'without Authentication' implies passive enumeration possible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unauthenticated requests to Gitea registry catalog endpoints returning 200-range (e.g., /v2/_catalog, repository list APIs). Spike in catalog queries from single source or rapid sequential enumeration of repository names.

suggestion.title: Gitea API Credential Bypass or Missing Auth Check
suggestion.rationale: Technical flaw is missing authentication enforcement. Requests succeed without credentials that should require auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests to protected Gitea registry APIs (push/pull/config) succeeding with HTTP 200/201 when Authorization header is absent or malformed. Compare successful unauthenticated requests to baseline of authenticated traffic for same endpoints.

suggestion.title: Container Image Manifest/Config Exposure via Unauth API
suggestion.rationale: Attackers can read image manifests and config blobs revealing internal secrets, dependencies, or source hints. Article scope: 'private' images exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor successful GET requests for image manifests (Content-Type: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json) or config blobs from unauthenticated sources. Flag any download of multi-stage build configs or images containing ENV secrets.

suggestion.title: Cross-User Private Container Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: If Gitea's image repo isolation is broken, users may access other users' private images. 'without Authentication' suggests permissions bypass, not just null-auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authenticated container pulls with image ownership. Alert when user A pulls images owned/scoped to user B via private registry. Check for role/namespace confusion in API token validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dormant Extension Activation Post-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Glassworm planting 'dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update.' Code execution triggered by extension updates without user interaction is an unusual and detectable persistence pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code or OpenVSX extension processes spawning child processes immediately after an extension update cycle, especially when no user interaction is recorded within 5 seconds of extension activation. Correlate against known clean extension manifests.

suggestion.title: Development Tool Outbound Connections to Solana Blockchain Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes C2 infrastructure encoding 'server addresses in the memo fields of blockchain transactions' on Solana. Detecting outbound Solana RPC connections from development tools is specific and unusual.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from or parented to development tools (VS Code, npm, node.exe, Python) establishing HTTPS to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, rpc.mainnet-beta.solana.com, or alternate validators). Baseline normal outbound connectivity first.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Configuration Lookups from Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys.' Development tools initiating DHT lookups is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound UDP/TCP on DHT ports (6881–6889, 6969) and BitTorrent handshake patterns from development tool processes. Cross-reference against known legitimate DHT use cases (e.g., from torrent clients only).

suggestion.title: Google Calendar API Abuse for C2 Configuration Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Glassworm 'uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' Processes authenticating to Google Calendar and retrieving event data is a specific C&C pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-browser processes (especially development tools, system processes, or extension host processes) authenticating to Google Calendar API or fetching calendar event contents. Correlate with Base64 decoding operations in-process and subsequent URL/IP address resolution.

suggestion.title: Credential and Cryptocurrency Wallet Access from Extension Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious extensions that 'stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' as the primary attack objective. Unusual file access from extension contexts to credential stores is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by VS Code extensions or npm post-install scripts accessing credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.git-credentials, Windows CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER paths) or cryptocurrency wallet software directories. Flag access by processes with suspicious parent chains or non-standard execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions,' 'GitHub repositories and npm packages,' and '400 software artifacts' impacted in March 2026. Installation-time C&C callbacks or credential access is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections or credential-store access initiated during npm install, GitHub clone, yarn install, or VS Code extension installation processes. Flag post-install hook scripts or extension manifest-triggered code that establishes non-standard C&C connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from New Repository Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks pivot through package managers. Article title references 'developer supply chain' compromise—pipeline produced zero detection for malicious package delivery despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of package managers (npm, pip, gem, nuget, etc.) pointing to non-standard or newly-registered repository URLs. Alert on requests to domains registered within 30 days preceding package installation. Correlate against known package manager configuration files showing unexpected source changes.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Malicious Package Metadata or Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: GlassWorm framework likely uses post-install hooks or package metadata for execution—no use case addresses automated script execution during dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process launches originating from package manager cache or temporary directories during build/install phases. Flag execution of shell interpreters with parent processes matching npm/pip/cargo/gradle. Correlate timing with package installation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Communication from Developer Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Infrastructure takedown implies C2 infrastructure—no use case for detecting outbound C2 from compromised developer machines to known malware infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal outbound destinations from developer machines. Alert on connections to newly-registered domains, bulletproof hosting providers, or previously-sinkholed malware infrastructure. Enrich with URLhaus/abuse.ch feeds for GlassWorm IOCs.

suggestion.title: Malicious DLL Sideloading from Utility Download Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'archive includes the legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded when launching the benign binary.' Core delivery mechanism for utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when legitimate utility executables launch from temp/downloads/ZIP extraction paths and load unexpected DLLs from the same directory. Correlate utility names against whitelist of known Trojanized targets from gleeze[.]com or similar malvertising domains.

suggestion.title: msiexec Remote Access Tool Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'DLL uses msiexec.exe to install vcredist_x64.dll, which is a package installer for the ScreenConnect remote access tool.' Direct C2 establishment after sideloading execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag msiexec.exe invoked from unexpected parents (particularly DLLs, staging executables, or hidden paths) with vcredist arguments. Correlate with ScreenConnect C2 domain registration and session establishment.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing via SimpleRunPE into Microsoft-Signed Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'process hollowing into a legitimate .NET binary signed by Microsoft: InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe.' Evasion technique enabling payload execution under trusted signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injection patterns where SimpleRunPE.exe or RuntimeHost.exe creates child processes or injects code into Microsoft-signed administrative utilities. Monitor for unexpected image loads or unmapped sections within these processes.

suggestion.title: Defender Exclusion List Manipulation via PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware also invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender.' Direct defense evasion enabling payload execution without AV inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell invocations modifying Windows Defender exclusion registry paths from unexpected parents (DLLs, staging binaries, hidden folders). Alert on exclusions targeting newly created process paths or folders.

suggestion.title: GPU Cryptocurrency Mining Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one of three mining modules is downloaded and executed. The supported mining programs are gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI, all of them designed to use graphics processing units.' Direct monetization impact of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger alerts on execution of gminer.exe, lolMiner, or SRBMiner-MULTI processes, especially when spawned from system utilities or hidden directory paths. Correlate with sustained GPU utilization >80% and outbound connections to known mining pool infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Virtual Machine and Sandbox Detection Evasion Check
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware checks the environment for virtual machines and a set of 40 process names corresponding to analysis tools. If any are identified, the malware terminates its execution.' Anti-forensics evasion attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes scanning for VM artifacts (registry paths, WMI queries) or enumerating analysis tool processes (wireshark.exe, procmon.exe, windbg.exe, etc.) from unusual parents or in hidden paths. Correlate with process termination immediately after detection.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies Grandoreiro as target of analysis. Banking trojans in this family are known to establish persistence via registry modification—this is a core ATT&CK behavior for Windows banking malware that should trigger detection, yet no UC covers it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or similar autostart locations originating from newly created user-writable directories. Correlate with process spawning from Temp or Downloads to establish infection chain.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Password Store Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is a banking trojan; credential theft from password managers, browsers, and credential stores is a defining capability not covered by any generated UC. This is T1555 behavior—core to its function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process chains where banking/browser processes spawn credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, comsvcs, LSADump variants) or direct access to password store databases (Chrome Local State, Firefox profile.js, Credential Manager registry hives).

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Process Discovery & System Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names BTMOB RAT; RAT implants universally perform process, service, and network discovery (T1057, T1007, T1049). No detection use case covers these reconnaissance patterns despite them being early post-compromise indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of tasklist, Get-Process, netstat, wmic os get, or service enumeration commands (sc query, Get-Service) within minutes of unsigned binary execution in user-writable paths. Correlate with absence of legitimate admin context.

suggestion.title: Android Malware Execution & Permission Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states campaigns target Android users; no UC addresses Android-specific behaviors. Android malware typically requests dangerous permissions (INTERNET, READ_CONTACTS, CAMERA, RECORD_AUDIO). Mobile detection gap is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installation from untrusted sources requesting multiple dangerous permissions simultaneously (especially CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO + CONTACTS). Monitor for consent fraud patterns where users are tricked into granting permissions via fake update screens.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication via Obfuscated HTTP/DNS Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Both Grandoreiro and RATs rely on C2 communication to exfiltrate credentials and execute commands. Article body (though corrupted) would typically describe C2 domains/IPs. No UC covers detection of malware-to-C2 traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to recently-registered or low-reputation domains from processes spawned in non-standard paths. Alert on abnormal HTTPS POST patterns to domains with short domain-age, mismatched SSL certificate issuer, or high request frequency from single host.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Reconnaissance: Fiddling Scorpius Infrastructure Lookups
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Fiddling Scorpius' in keywords as targeting World Cup infrastructure. No use cases generated despite this actor being the primary threat context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reconnaissance against World Cup ticketing, broadcast, and venue infrastructure by detecting DNS queries, WHOIS lookups, and port scanning patterns associated with Fiddling Scorpius infrastructure. Track naming conventions and BGP hijacking IOC patterns.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaigns with Malicious QR Codes
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'phishing' and 'QR Codes' as attack vectors. No detection use case created for this known World Cup threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails targeting World Cup attendees/staff containing embedded QR codes or attachments with QR code images. Alert on emails with spoofed ticketing sites or official-looking World Cup branding pointing to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Domain Typosquatting Against World Cup Official Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'typosquatting'; critical attack vector for diverting ticketing, broadcast, and operational traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS resolutions and HTTP traffic for typosquatting domains one edit-distance from fifa.com, worldcup2026.com, and official venues. Flag newly registered domains with World Cup event dates or stadium names and track WHOIS changes or bulletproof hosting patterns.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Deployment Against Broadcast/Ticketing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly name 'wiper' as attack payload. Article describes ransomware and state-aligned threats to critical infrastructure. No detection for impact-phase wiper campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wiper execution by monitoring for bulk file deletion, MBR/partition table overwrites, and shadow copy deletion across broadcast control systems, ticketing databases, and venue operational networks. Alert on mass encryption or data destruction in short time windows targeting sports infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Execution Against Broadcast Operations Centers
suggestion.rationale: Article schema states 'ransomware groups' targeting World Cup. No use case for detection of ransomware behavior in broadcast/operations environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor broadcast operations centers, ticketing systems, and venue networks for ransomware execution indicators: mass file encryption with new extensions, ransom note creation, and communication to known ransomware C2 infrastructure. Correlate with network segmentation bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Fighting Ursa State-Aligned Reconnaissance Against Stadium Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly name 'Fighting Ursa' (Russia-aligned actor known for OT targeting). No IOC or use case for this actor's reconnaissance signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Fighting Ursa reconnaissance against venue operational technology, power, and broadcast networks by monitoring for network scanning patterns, SCADA protocol probes, and DNS resolution of OT management interfaces. Cross-reference with known actor C2 and proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Employee Account Access Post–Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access' on April 14. Detection must flag impossible-travel logins, off-hours access, or geographic anomalies on compromised employee accounts, especially those accessing customer databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee account logins from new geographic locations, impossible travel times, or non-business hours. Correlate with VPN access patterns and cross-reference account permissions against historical baseline. Escalate if user accesses customer PII systems outside normal job function.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Customer PII Database Queries and Exports
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'illegally copied personal information' from 5.99M customer records (names, DOB, email, gender, location, loyalty program data). Must detect large SELECT queries or bulk data exports targeting customer identity fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusually large database queries extracting customer PII fields executed by non-typical user roles or compromised employee accounts. Flag data exports to temporary locations, staging databases, or bulk BACKUP commands. Monitor query patterns for sequential access to multiple customer tables.

suggestion.title: Detect Large-Scale Data Exfiltration to External Services
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stole documents containing over 8.7 million records' and 'terabytes of internal corporate data.' Must detect GB-scale transfers from internal systems to external cloud/file-sharing services or known attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress for large data transfers (>100MB) to public cloud services (S3, Azure Blob, Mega, etc.), file-sharing services, or DNS queries to known ShinyHunters infrastructure. Alert on connections initiated by compromised employee accounts or unusual service accounts accessing sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Detect Social Engineering Attacks Targeting Employee Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly documented: 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee.' Detection must identify phishing emails, credential-harvesting forms, or impersonation attempts targeting Carnival staff with access to customer systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails with credential-harvesting or malware payloads targeting Carnival domain. Detect failed login attempts followed by successful authentication from new device/location within 24 hours. Flag MFA bypass attempts or suspicious password reset requests during social-engineering campaigns.

suggestion.title: Monitor ShinyHunters Leak Site and Darknet for Carnival Data Posts
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility for the breach in April' and posted stolen data to their known leak infrastructure. Continuous monitoring for data sale/extortion posts is critical for damage assessment and negotiation disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query ShinyHunters leak site, darknet marketplaces, and threat-actor communication channels for posts containing Carnival victim data, employee records, or brand names (Carnival, Costa, Princess, Holland America, AIDA, Cunard, Seabourn). Alert on price negotiations or data re-sale announcements.

suggestion.title: Large Volume Data Exfiltration to External Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Data Breach Exposes Millions of Customers' Personal Information'—the core attack outcome is bulk exfiltration. Pipeline produced zero exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high-volume outbound connections from internal database servers or file shares to external IPs over non-standard ports. Monitor for unusual archive/compression activity (tar, zip, 7z) on systems holding PII followed by network exfil. Alert on mass data transfers that deviate from baseline by >5x within 24-hour windows.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Query Volume and PII Data Access
suggestion.rationale: A breach exposing 'millions of customers' records' requires unauthorized database access and bulk selection of PII fields. Pipeline missed data collection detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service accounts or legitimate users executing SELECT queries on customer tables at scale (row counts >10k in single query). Track joins across customer, payment, and SSN/passport tables. Flag if queries export to temporary staging tables then delete access logs.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise and Service Account Misuse
suggestion.rationale: A breach of 'millions of customers' Personal Information' requires sustained privileged database access; suggests stolen credentials or persistent compromise. Pipeline omitted credential_access and related detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login attempts followed by successful logon using service account credentials outside business hours. Detect password spray or brute-force patterns against database admin accounts. Alert on credential manager access (LastPass, 1Password vaults) by non-privileged users.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Backup or Archive Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Millions of records implies attacker accessed full customer database dumps, backups, or archive storage. No detection suggested for backup/archive exfiltration vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to backup repositories (S3 buckets, Azure Blob, NetBackup) by non-standard accounts or external IPs. Flag downloads of full database snapshots (.bak, .sql dumps) or entire backup chains. Alert on failed access attempts to archive storage followed by privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attempt Against Roundcube Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly: 'Attackers Inject SQL Queries'. Core attack vector. Zero detection use cases produced despite this being primary exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Roundcube endpoints (login, contact, search, preferences) containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, INSERT, DROP, --) in parameter values. Flag encoded/obfuscated SQL patterns in GET/POST data. Baseline legitimate traffic and threshold on abnormal query frequency.

suggestion.title: Database Error Response Detection
suggestion.rationale: Failed SQL injection attempts expose errors; successful injections may trigger unusual database exceptions. Pipeline missing error-based detection despite 'SQL queries' being core vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 500 errors and SQL exception strings (syntax error, database error, SQL exception) in Roundcube logs. Correlate with user input handling zones (login, search, autocomplete). Alert on error spike from single IP.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Query Pattern from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Successfully executed SQL injection runs attacker-controlled queries. Pipeline lacks detection for post-exploitation database behavior anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database connections originating from Roundcube application process for: schema enumeration (INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries), bulk data exports via SELECT INTO, system table access, or queries targeting user credential tables. Flag volume and frequency against baseline.

suggestion.title: Mail Account Mass Exfiltration via Compromised Webmail Session
suggestion.rationale: Successful SQL injection enables harvesting of mail credentials and bulk mailbox access. Attack impact on confidentiality not addressed in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single session accessing anomalously high message volume, unusual forwarding rule creation, or simultaneous access to multiple user mailboxes. Flag bulk export operations (IMAP FETCH of thousands of messages, PST exports). Correlate with failed login attempts preceding access.

suggestion.title: Roundcube File System Tampering Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attack success enables file write via SQL injection to filesystem. No persistence/webshell detection generated despite SQL injection's post-exploitation potential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Roundcube installation (plugins/, config/, root directory) for unauthorized file creation/modification outside maintenance windows. Alert on PHP files written to upload directories, .htaccess modification, or suspicious executable creation in web-accessible paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Unauthorized Private Container Image Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title states vulnerability 'exposes private container images to attackers'—the direct impact is unauthorized read access to container images. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for this core attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea container registry logs for pulls, layer fetches, or manifest inspects of private/internal images by unauthenticated principals, unprivileged service accounts, or previously-unknown pull sources. Establish baseline pull patterns and alert on unexpected access to sensitive image names (e.g., production, security-scanned, proprietary tags).

suggestion.title: Gitea Container Registry Authentication/Authorization Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability IS in Gitea; detection must target the exploit path itself. Alert on requests that circumvent or fail authentication checks on restricted container endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Gitea container endpoints (/v2/*, registry API paths) with missing, malformed, or invalid Authorization headers that succeed or return image data. Detect unauthenticated requests to restricted registry operations, auth-bypass payloads in URL parameters, or successful image operations from IPs lacking pull credentials.

suggestion.title: Container Image Repository Enumeration or Catalog Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Exposure of 'private' images implies attackers can discover which private repositories exist. Detection should surface unexpected enumeration of the image catalog.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume list/catalog requests against Gitea registry endpoints (e.g., GET /v2/_catalog, /api/v1/repos list operations) from single IP or service principal. Alert if enumeration succeeds on hidden/private repositories or if enumeration attempts come from untrusted sources with no prior Gitea activity.

suggestion.title: Bulk or Suspicious Container Image Downloads Post-Breach
suggestion.rationale: After gaining access via the vulnerability, attackers must exfiltrate images. Detect abnormal pull volume, rapid sequences of image pulls, or downloads of production-critical images by non-production contexts.
