suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid or bulk pulls of private container images (>5 unique image layers in <5 minutes), pulls of high-value images (base OS, security-critical services) by accounts/IPs without historical pull activity, pulls followed by off-site re-hosting, or unusually large data transfers to container registries outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: DNS Query to Suspicious Domain Resolved via Shared CDN Edge IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attackers abusing shared CDN edge IPs to 'bypass protective DNS filtering.' Pipeline missed basic detection for DNS queries resolving to abuse-pattern domains on legitimate CDN IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries where response IP belongs to known CDN provider (Akamai, Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront ranges) AND target domain matches newly registered, phishing, or malware-associated domain lists. Correlate DNS filtering bypass attempts with subsequent HTTP/HTTPS requests to confirm payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Rapid Domain Rotation Within Single CDN Edge IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers using shared CDN infrastructure; attackers typically rotate domains rapidly to evade blocking while keeping IP static. Pipeline did not identify this temporal attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within a 24-hour window, detect >N unique domains resolving to the same CDN edge IP address. Filter out legitimate high-volume CDN services (bulk CDN customers) via exception list. Escalate if domains have low reputation scores or short TTLs.

suggestion.title: HTTP/S Traffic to CDN Edge IP with Suspicious TLS SNI Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Attackers abuse shared CDN IPs by hosting malicious content alongside legitimate services. Article describes this abuse pattern; pipeline should have suggested detection for TLS SNI divergence from CDN's primary hostname.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS connections to known CDN IP ranges where TLS SNI hostname does NOT match the IP's reverse DNS or documented CDN hostname pattern. Correlate with malware/phishing domain indicators to confirm abuse.

suggestion.title: Comparative DNS Filtering Evasion Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article's core premise is DNS filters are bypassed via CDN. Pipeline should surface detection for attempts to reach blocklisted domains via CDN IPs where the domain itself would be blocked by name-based filtering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare DNS query logs against internal or external blocklist. Alert when a queried domain appears on blocklist but resolution succeeded via CDN IP, indicating blocklist evasion. Flag if same user/host retries immediately after initial block.

suggestion.title: Legitimate CDN IP Whitelist Abuse via Payload Inspection Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article implies organizations allow CDN traffic by IP due to whitelist policies. Pipeline should recommend detection for abuse of overly-permissive CDN allowlisting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On whitelisted CDN IP traffic, apply layer-7 inspection (if permitted by policy) to detect malware signatures, C2 beacons, or data exfiltration patterns masked as legitimate CDN traffic. Alert on anomalous binary, obfuscated, or encrypted payloads within CDN flows.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Malware Execution from Suspicious Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'JS Malware Infrastructure.' Pipeline generated zero detection rules for JavaScript execution patterns despite clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect instances of JavaScript interpreters (cscript.exe, wscript.exe, node.exe, browsers) executing .js files or inline scripts with obfuscation markers or downloaded from untrusted sources. Correlate execution with network artifacts indicating communication to known malicious hosting providers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Connections to Malicious Hosting Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH as malware hosts. Pipeline should have created network-layer detection for connections to these providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS resolution and TCP/UDP connections to infrastructure owned or operated by GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH ASNs/IP ranges. Correlate with endpoint activity (process execution, file write) to identify potential malware download or callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript File Download and Execution Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hackers hosting malware on infrastructure; typical delivery involves downloading .js files. Pipeline missed detection of download-to-execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of file download events (.js, .jse, .vbs, .ps1 written to temp directories) immediately followed by execution via script interpreters. Prioritize downloads from non-standard sources or downloaded via HTTP without HTTPS certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Delivery of JavaScript Malware via Email or Web Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'hackers use infrastructure to host JS malware'; article likely describes delivery mechanism (phishing or redirect chains). No use cases generated for spearphishing or web-based delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with .js attachments or links to GHOSTYNETWORKS/OMEGATECH infrastructure. Flag URL clicks leading to these providers, especially if followed by script execution. Correlate with user behavior (unusual download locations, execution context).

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Employee Targeted by Fake Recruiter Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Fake Recruiter Lures' as attack vector against crypto firms—this is initial-access phishing that should trigger detection for emails from fake recruiter domains, LinkedIn connection requests with interview scheduling, or attachment-based payloads. Article establishes this is the primary social-engineering hook.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails or messages impersonating recruiters with domain typosquats of major recruiting firms or spoofed internal domains targeting cryptocurrency sector employees. Alert on suspicious LinkedIn outreach with interview scheduling links or file downloads from newly-created domains referencing cryptocurrency or hiring keywords.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from User Download or Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'macOS Malware'—the payload delivery mechanism. Should detect execution of unsigned binaries, script execution from Downloads folder, or .dmg/.pkg installation from temporary directories following fake recruiter engagement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned Mach-O binaries or shell scripts from user-writable directories (~/Downloads, /tmp). Detect .dmg or .pkg installer execution followed by spawning of hidden processes or shell invocations. Correlate with prior email attachment or download activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Tree: User Interaction → Binary Execution → C2 Connection
suggestion.rationale: Fake recruiter malware flow: user clicks link or opens attachment → malware executes → establishes persistence/C2. Article title establishes this chain but pipeline detects no execution-to-C2 correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes spawned from browser/mail clients establishing outbound TLS connections to newly-registered domains, or C2 traffic patterns (regular beaconing, encoded payloads). Establish behavioral baseline for crypto-firm infrastructure and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Firm Employee Account Compromise Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: After fake recruiter malware executes, attackers typically move laterally using compromised employee credentials. No detection use case covers post-compromise credential harvesting or lateral-movement targeting crypto-firm infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious access to password managers, browser credential storage, or SSH key materials on infected macOS endpoints. Monitor for unusual API calls to crypto exchange platforms or internal admin tools from compromised employee sessions.

suggestion.title: MsBuild.exe Process Hollowing via Memory API Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Uses MsBuild.exe Process Hollowing'; this is the core evasion technique and should trigger detection for VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + SetThreadContext patterns against MsBuild.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MsBuild.exe performing suspicious memory operations (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext, ResumeThread) on remote processes. Process hollowing typically allocates executable memory, writes malicious code, and resumes a suspended thread.

suggestion.title: Unusual MsBuild.exe Execution with Suspicious Spawning Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies a 'variant' using MsBuild—MsBuild is a legitimate build tool and should rarely execute directly without Visual Studio/build context; detection should flag anomalous parents or atypical child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MsBuild.exe launched from non-standard parents (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, explorer.exe) or spawning child processes atypical for legitimate builds (reconnaissance tools, credential dumpers, C2 agents).

suggestion.title: MsBuild.exe Masquerading and Evasion Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'to Evade Detection' + masquerading as legitimate MsBuild.exe; detection should identify behavioral anomalies distinguishing legitimate builds from malicious code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MsBuild.exe for unexpected network connections (C2 beacons), file modifications outside standard build directories, or elevated API calls inconsistent with compilation workflows.

suggestion.title: PureLogs Malware Family Signature and Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'PureLogs' as the threat family; pipeline should surface known PureLogs hashes, C2 infrastructure, and behavioral markers (if publicly disclosed) for threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for known PureLogs process signatures, command-line patterns, dropped files, or C2 domains/IPs. Correlate MsBuild.exe abuse with PureLogs-specific behavioral indicators (if available in threat feeds).

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing Detection via Suspended Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Process hollowing inherently involves creating suspended processes, unmapping legitimate code, and injecting malicious payload; detection should flag this distinct injection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CreateProcessW/Ex calls with CREATE_SUSPENDED flag on MsBuild.exe or other legitimate executables, followed by memory mapping operations and process resumption without intermediate spawning.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Media Player Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' T1574.002 exploitation is the core delivery mechanism but generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate executables (HLS Installer, media players, chromium) loading DLLs from non-standard paths or with mismatched signatures. Alert when EXE and suspicious DLL coexist in temp/download directories and execute in immediate sequence.

suggestion.title: Fake Video Player Update Prompts Installing Malware Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update...Clicking the link downloaded a ZIP archive.' Masquerading as legitimate software update (T1036.004) on piracy infrastructure—no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archive downloads triggered by media player dialogs from non-vendor domains. Flag ZIP downloads from piracy TLDs (.ru, .top) initiated by browser or plugin processes in response to fake update prompts.

suggestion.title: Dual-Payload Archive Extraction and Execution (Legitimate + Malicious)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL.' This paired-payload pattern is a known malware distribution technique but no detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archive extraction containing both signed/legitimate executables and unsigned DLLs in the same directory, followed by immediate EXE execution that loads the paired DLL.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Injected DLL Logic
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device.' Persistence mechanism explicitly described but no detection use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL files in temp/download directories that create registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or WMI event subscriptions. Alert on persistence mechanisms established via DLL injection into legitimate processes.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Execution (SilentCryptoMiner Variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'a miner running on users' computers...the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Miner deployment and resource hijacking (T1496.001) mentioned but no detection case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect XMRig or SilentCryptoMiner process creation, sustained elevated CPU/GPU utilization, and outbound connections to known mining pools from media player or installer child processes.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan (RAT) Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Dual capability (miner + RAT) enables remote control and data exfiltration but no C2 detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for beaconing patterns and C2 communications from processes spawned by media player/installer executables, particularly connections to unfamiliar IP ranges or domains without legitimate business context.

suggestion.title: Typosquat Domain Registration for FIFA-Themed Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'threat actors spoofing FIFA websites'—typosquatting and homoglyph domains are the primary mechanism. Pipeline provided zero IOCs and no domain confusion detection. Phrase: 'spoofing FIFA websites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly registered domains with character substitution variants of FIFA properties (fifa.com, worldcup.com, fifatix.com). Flag registrations within 72h of major FIFA events, registered via privacy proxies, or with WHOIS creation dates <30 days old. Correlate with passive DNS showing rapid nameserver or A-record changes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Campaigns with FIFA Branding and Credential Harvesting Links
suggestion.rationale: Spoofing attacks require email delivery vector; article describes mass targeting to steal PII. No UC addresses phishing email campaigns. Phrase: 'threat actors spoofing FIFA websites to steal' implies email-driven initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with FIFA/World Cup theme, urgent language (verify account, confirm attendance, ticket redemption), sender spoofing (noreply@fifa.com from free email), and links to recently registered domains or non-FIFA-owned IPs. Flag bulk sends to similar recipient domains.

suggestion.title: PII Form Harvesting from Spoofed FIFA Registration Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states actors steal 'name, home address, and phone number'—form submissions are the collection mechanism. Pipeline missed credential_access phase entirely. Phrase: 'steal name, home address, and phone number'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to non-FIFA-official domains containing PII fields (fullname, street_address, phone, address). Detect suspicious form submissions with >50 entries from single IP. Flag POST parameters matching registration forms (name+address+phone pattern) to infrastructure not owned by FIFA.

suggestion.title: Domain Name Lookalike Registration and Infrastructure Setup
suggestion.rationale: Spoofing requires infrastructure provisioning; bulk domain registration patterns reveal campaigns. Pipeline extracted no infrastructure IOCs. No UC for setup/preparation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on domain registrations using keywords fifa, worldcup, fifatix, fifatickets with privacy registrars or bullet-proof hosters (bulletproof-hosting.com, bulletproof-ISP patterns). Correlate multiple domains sharing registrant email, nameserver, or hosting IP. Flag DNS setup with short TTLs (indicating rapid changes).

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration of Harvested PII from Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen names, addresses, phone numbers must be exfiltrated; no detection for data movement. Pipeline missed exfiltration phase. Phrase: 'steal name, home address, and phone number' implies large-scale collection and transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound transfers of structured data (CSV, JSON, SQL dumps) from web servers hosting spoofed domains to attacker infrastructure. Monitor for SFTP/SCP connections, HTTPS tunneling with large payloads, or cloud storage API calls (s3, azure blob) originating from phishing hosting IPs.

suggestion.title: Veeam Service Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'Privilege Escalation' as the attack vector via Veeam tool. Pipeline produced zero use cases despite this being the primary threat signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or suspicious child processes spawned by Veeam service binaries (VeeamBR.exe, VeeamDeploy.exe). Detect registry modifications under HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services correlating with Veeam process activity. Flag privilege escalation attempts from Veeam installation directories or unexpected elevation of user-launched Veeam tools to SYSTEM context.

suggestion.title: Veeam Service Binary Path Modification
suggestion.rationale: Common privilege escalation pattern: vulnerable backup service with writable binary path or service configuration. Article emphasizes Veeam tool vulnerability but pipeline surfaced no service-abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to Veeam service binary paths or service parameters in the registry via sc.exe, PowerShell, or direct registry writes. Correlate with non-Veeam service account activity. Flag service creation with Veeam keywords pointing to unexpected directories or followed by privilege escalation techniques.

suggestion.title: Unquoted Service Path - Veeam Components
suggestion.rationale: Veeam tools commonly run as services with SYSTEM privileges; unquoted paths enable DLL injection privilege escalation. Title signals privilege escalation but pipeline missed this canonical backup-tool abuse vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Veeam services with unquoted binary paths lacking proper ACLs. Monitor for DLL creation or modification in Veeam service directories (e.g., Program Files\Veeam) by non-system accounts. Alert on process execution from ambiguous path locations matching unquoted service path exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redirect from AI Chatbot to Cryptomining Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — implies URL-based delivery vector. Pipeline missed detection for link-click chains from known chatbot services to unfamiliar/malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP referrers from known AI chatbot domains (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) pointing to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Flag clicks that bypass user confirmation or open in hidden browser contexts. Correlate with known cryptomining infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Browser-based Cryptomining Activity Post-Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: user clicks malicious link → lands on cryptojacking page → JavaScript executes crypto miner. Article describes 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' but pipeline extracted no behavioral signatures for CPU-intensive mining or memory allocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high CPU usage from browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe) correlating with WebAssembly or JavaScript-based cryptomining libraries (e.g., Monero miners). Look for unusual memory growth and network connections to mining pools.

suggestion.title: Compromised or Malicious AI Chatbot API Response Content
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in attack: chatbot recommendation output was poisoned to return malicious links. Pipeline should detect anomalous response patterns (URLs not in training data, executable redirects, obfuscated links in conversational output).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot API responses for injected URLs, particularly those with short-lived domains, suspicious TLDs, or obfuscation patterns. Flag responses containing base64-encoded or URL-shortened links to cryptomining infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Registration Clustering (Cryptojacking Campaign)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' (plural). Pipeline should surface IOC clusters: newly-registered domains, shared hosting infrastructure, WHOIS patterns, or domain generation algorithm (DGA) signatures associated with cryptojacking campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate malicious domains used in redirect with domain registration metadata, WHOIS registrar patterns, and ASN clustering. Identify infrastructure shared across cryptomining campaigns or fast-flux networks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous User Query Patterns to AI Chatbot (Prompt Injection)
suggestion.rationale: Attack may have relied on compromised chatbot recommendations or adversary-controlled prompt injection. Pipeline should flag unusual input patterns designed to extract malicious links or bypass safety guardrails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot query logs for adversarial prompts testing guardrails, requests for specific recommendation types from new users, or patterns consistent with systematic prompt injection (iterative queries building to malicious output).

suggestion.title: Detect Password Spray Attack Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency'—the attack is named as a real threat vector that organizations must defend against. No detection UC was generated despite this explicit threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify accounts receiving 5+ failed authentication attempts within a 10-minute window, with each attempt using a different username or from different IPs, indicating password spray reconnaissance. Correlate logon failure events (4625 on Windows) across multiple user accounts from single or distributed source IPs. Exclude service accounts and test environments to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Detect Breached Credential Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials' and cites Verizon data that 'stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches.' This is an explicit attack scenario requiring detection for credential stuffing attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logon attempts using usernames and passwords known to be from public breach databases (cross-reference against HaveIBeenPwned, Credential Stuffing Lists). Prioritize detections where breach credential is used against different target domain than original breach source. Alert on multiple attempts within 24 hours using different breached creds against same account.

suggestion.title: Detect Incremental Password Reuse Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes user workarounds: 'adding a predictable "!" to the end of the last version' and 'minimal tweaks, changing a few characters.' These patterns indicate attempts to circumvent password history policies and suggest predictable variations attackers or insiders could exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password changes where Levenshtein distance between old and new password is minimal (1-3 character edits) or follow predictable appends (incrementing numbers, common suffixes like '!','#'). Cross-user baseline: if >5 accounts show identical pattern on same day, flag potential policy-evasion guidance. Reduce FP by excluding forced resets within 24h of prior change.

suggestion.title: cPanel Redis API Function Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/'—this is the canonical detection signature for exploitation attempts; pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel audit logs for the API call 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble'. Each match represents an exploitation attempt or successful compromise. Correlate source IP, timestamp, and subsequent root-privilege process spawning to confirm attack success.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Code Execution Post-cPanel API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—establishes direct privilege escalation to execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned with uid=0 that correlate temporally with cPanel/LiteSpeed API access or the redisAble function pattern. Focus on script interpreters (bash, python, perl, php) executing unexpected payloads with elevated context.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Version Inventory Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names affected versions: 'v2.3 through v2.4.4'—asset inventory should flag these as critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan cPanel deployments for LiteSpeed plugin version < v2.4.5. Cross-reference against patch deployment records. Flag unpatched systems 7+ days post-advisory as non-compliant.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Geographic/ASN Access to cPanel Redis Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'examine the IPs in the list, determine if they are valid'—IP-based anomaly detection is the primary detection method for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate cPanel administrative IPs by geography and ASN. Alert on requests to lsws.redisAble or cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble from non-baseline IPs, especially from non-US origins given CISA's federal agency focus.

suggestion.title: Redis Configuration State Changes via Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability location is 'lsws.redisAble function' related to 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features'—successful exploitation manifests as unauthorized Redis config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected enable/disable state transitions in Redis configuration on cPanel hosts. Correlate changes with preceding redisAble API calls and root-privilege processes. Alert if Redis is toggled outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Exploitation Activity Correlation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article provides granular attack chain: unprivileged remote → lsws.redisAble call → root execution. Detection should correlate the three events as a single exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlation rule: (1) Network connection to cPanel from external IP, (2) subsequent cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble API call, (3) root-privilege process spawning within 60 seconds. Flag all three-event chains as confirmed exploitation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Version Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product [were] published to the npm registry' — core attack vector. Pipeline produced no detection for unexpected package versions from trusted publishers or hash mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for version publishes attributed to TanStack maintainers with checksums deviating from upstream. Alert on versions published outside normal release cadence, from unexpected geolocation, or with suspicious metadata patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Malware Post-Installation Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing malware' payload — pipeline missed detection for credential access and exfiltration behavior after package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by npm-installed TanStack accessing credential stores (HKLM, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, /etc/shadow). Flag unexpected DNS/HTTP exfiltration from Node.js runtime or npm child processes with high credential-store access counts.

suggestion.title: Trusted npm Publisher Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article exploited 'trusted identity' — should detect publishing anomalies (unexpected geolocation, MFA bypass, publish from unknown CI/CD) for known package maintainers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate publishing activity per TanStack maintainer account (geolocation, IP ranges, publish cadence). Alert on publish from non-baseline geography, unexpected client signature, or missing expected MFA log entry.

suggestion.title: Software Supply Chain Integrity Monitoring — CVE-2026-45321
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'malicious versions' and active KEV status demand proactive hunting of installed TanStack versions. Pipeline should correlate fleet inventory against known-bad package hashes before federal remediation deadline (2026-06-10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference all deployed TanStack versions against CVE-2026-45321 vulnerability metadata and known-bad hashes. Flag installations of vulnerable versions; prioritize by remediation deadline compliance.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Code Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages typically execute post-install scripts to deliver payloads. Article implies execution-phase delivery. Pipeline missed script-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawns (powershell, bash, curl, wget) immediately following npm install of TanStack. Flag postinstall/preinstall lifecycle hooks executing processes outside Node.js paths or accessing sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Publish Event Timeline
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malicious versions 'published to the npm registry' — should detect publish bursts or publishing to secondary feeds by compromised accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid successive package publishes from single maintainer, publish of multiple major version bumps in short window, or publishes to both npm and alternative registries. Baseline: normal release cadence for TanStack project.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Suspicious Outbound Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised extension 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — direct indicator of C2 communication or payload delivery over network.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe processes in Nx Console context initiating unexpected HTTPS/HTTP connections outside expected package registry ranges (npm, GitHub). Flag unusual IP destinations or domains not associated with legitimate Nx/package repository infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Disk and Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states harvesting 'from multiple sources on disk and in memory' — indicates file-system access to credential stores and memory-dumping API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file-system access from Nx Console processes to .ssh, .aws, .kube, .gnupg, or browser credential directories. Also detect process API calls for memory inspection (ReadProcessMemory, ptrace) or execution of credential-dumping tools.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'malicious version of Nx Console was published' — supply-chain attack requiring inventory check against known-vulnerable extension versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed Nx Console versions against CVE-2026-48027 advisory; identify installations from compromised publication window. Correlate with first-execution timestamps to identify infection timeline.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution in Nx Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'obfuscated payload' delivery and execution — indicates deobfuscation and dynamic code execution within extension runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx/node processes spawning children with suspicious arguments (base64 strings, encoded PowerShell), loading unexpected system DLLs, or executing interpreted code (eval, exec patterns) within extension context.

suggestion.title: Nx Extension Installation Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vehicle is explicitly an 'extension' — suspicious extension loading or modification warrants detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx extension files modified post-installation, loaded from non-standard extension directories, or lacking vendor signatures. Correlate extension loading with subsequent process spawning or file-system credential access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 Vulnerability Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-10 — standard asset-exposure hunt for vulnerable Nx Console versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48027 matches; flag any systems with vulnerable Nx Console versions not yet patched. Prioritize findings by user privilege level and network exposure (dev machines, shared CI/CD runners).

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2026-8398
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-8398 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the canonical detection method. Pipeline generated no UC for this straightforward scan-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for vulnerability scanner findings matching CVE-2026-8398 across all assets. Correlate scan timestamps with patch dates; flag systems not patched by 2026-05-30 federal due date. Alert on any scanner report: Daemon Tools Lite version ≤ [vulnerable range] with CVE-2026-8398 match.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunting — Internet-Facing Daemon Tools Lite
suggestion.rationale: Article maps to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application', signaling external exploitation vector. Pipeline failed to generate exposure-hunt UC for systems running Daemon Tools Lite on internet-facing network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for network exposure: Daemon Tools Lite service/port signatures detected on external-facing interfaces (WAN, DMZ). Correlate with asset inventory to identify systems running Daemon Tools Lite in internet-routable network segments. Escalate any match given T1190 active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Activity — Daemon Tools Lite Abnormal Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability contains 'Embedded Malicious Code' implying post-exploitation payload. Article describes 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability'—suggesting code execution or privilege escalation post-initial-access. Pipeline generated no UC for detecting suspicious process spawning or memory activity under Daemon Tools context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes spawned by or running in context of Daemon Tools Lite (dtlite.exe, daemon.exe). Alert on: (1) unexpected child process launch (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe); (2) network connections from Daemon Tools process to non-whitelisted destinations; (3) file writes to system directories (C:\Windows, System32); (4) suspicious module loads. High confidence on vulnerable system + process anomaly.

suggestion.title: Continuous Automated API Surface Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' This describes systematic reconnaissance at machine velocity—a core attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential API requests from single source across endpoint variation or user context switching within minutes. Baseline normal API call rates per identity and flag sustained deviations (>5x normal frequency) with systematic parameter mutation patterns.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Enumeration and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'BOLA or IDOR... The vulnerability lives in the gap between intended behavior and actual behavior... no probe, no payload, no signature that can infer intent.' This describes resource-level access control exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests modifying object identifiers (user_id, invoice_id, org_id) in URL/body to read/write resources beyond authenticated user scope. Correlate with successful responses to cross-tenant/cross-user resource reads and authorization audit log gaps.

suggestion.title: Authentication Intent Subversion Testing
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as context-dependent vulns: 'authentication bypasses, and especially chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed auth attempts followed by successful privileged requests without re-authentication, malformed/missing auth headers accepting requests, or session tokens reused across different user principals within single API flow.

suggestion.title: Chained Vulnerability Exploitation Cascade
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' This requires detecting multi-step exploit chains that individually may not trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 3+ distinct API error codes or exception types from single source within 5-minute window (config disclosure → missing validation → escalation) followed by successful high-value data access. Flag sequences crossing from low-confidence to high-confidence exploitation steps.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Leakage via Parameter Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names: 'cross-tenant data leakage... None of these have a heuristic signature you can probe for... The vulnerability lives in the gap between intended behavior and actual behavior.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests iterating through tenant/organization identifiers (sequential org_id, account_id, workspace_id values) with successful data responses. Correlate returned data metadata tags to authenticated user's entitled tenant—flag mismatches.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing & IT Support Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' — foundational attack vector requiring detection of callback scheme patterns and domain impersonation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails directing recipients to call a number for 'IT support' or 'account verification,' especially from newly registered domains with typosquatted IT service names. Cross-reference phone numbers in email body against known corporate IT contact lists. Flag domains registered with misspellings of common IT support platforms or internal helpdesk names.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Protocol Access Abuse Post-Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' — legitimate RDP tool abuse following social engineering compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connections initiated immediately after high-risk phishing email opens or callback to external numbers. Alert on RDP access from non-standard client IPs, especially paired with rapid file access or external drive enumeration. Baseline IT support RDP patterns and flag deviations (off-hours, unusual source IPs, multiple simultaneous sessions).

suggestion.title: Physical Media Insertion & USB Drive Connection Post-Failed Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'If that attempt fails, SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and lists 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives' as IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on insertion of external USB devices or external hard drives outside of IT-provisioned asset classes and approval records. Monitor for rapid file copies to newly mounted storage media, especially from document repositories, shared drives, or attorney working directories. Cross-correlate with physical security logs or badge swipes indicating non-employee presence in office area.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized In-Person IT Support Access to Facilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns of 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' and 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate badge access logs with IT helpdesk staff rosters; flag entry badge swipes not matching known IT personnel on shift. Alert security teams to unauthorized personnel claiming to be IT support, especially during off-hours or in restricted document/data areas. Cross-reference facility access logs with IT ticketing system to verify claimed support requests.

suggestion.title: Ransom Email Extortion & Data Leak Threats
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound emails containing data exfiltration threats, ransom demands, or claims of stolen proprietary information from entities matching victim profile (law firms, financial services). Alert on emails from newly registered domains or compromised external accounts demanding payment in exchange for data deletion or suppression. Correlate sender domains against SRG IOCs and Luna Moth leak site announcements.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration for IT Helpdesk Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns' — infrastructure reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag newly registered domains with one-character or homoglyph variations on common IT support domain names (e.g., helpdesk-n[1] vs. helpdesk-i[l], supp0rt vs. support). Correlate domain registration patterns against victim organization names and known subsidiaries. Alert on DNS queries to typosquatted domains from victim networks and email clicks on links hosted on these domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized or default guest user accessing Yamcs MdbOverrideApi
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In Yamcs's default configuration (no security.yaml), the built-in guest user…' implying guest user has or can obtain ChangeMissionDatabase privilege by default. No UC detects initial unauthorized access to this sensitive API endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* from guest user accounts or from users whose role should not have ChangeMissionDatabase privilege. Baseline expected algorithm change frequency and alert on anomalous access patterns from guest accounts.

suggestion.title: Java.type() invocation in Nashorn algorithm text without ClassFilter validation
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'ScriptEngine used to evaluate user-supplied algorithm text in MdbOverrideApi.updateAlgorithm is constructed without a ClassFilter.' UC_18_2 partially addresses payload detection post-request, but no UC targets validation of algorithm text ingestion itself or ClassFilter configuration state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs or JVM startup parameters for: (1) absence of ClassFilter configuration in Nashorn ScriptEngine initialization, (2) exceptions or errors when ClassFilter validation is attempted, (3) algorithm text containing Java.type, java.lang.Runtime, ProcessBuilder patterns before being sent to Nashorn engine.

suggestion.title: Suspicious privilege escalation via ChangeMissionDatabase role assignment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' as requirement. No UC detects unauthorized role assignment, privilege grant events, or creation of new high-privilege accounts. This is a discovery/privilege escalation gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for assignment or modification of ChangeMissionDatabase role, particularly to guest accounts, service accounts, or user accounts outside normal administrative groups. Correlate role changes with subsequent MdbOverrideApi.updateAlgorithm requests.

suggestion.title: Authenticated user with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege modifies algorithm definition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this by overriding the algorithm.' Current hunts skip the privilege-gating condition; should baseline legitimate admin behavior and flag anomalous algorithm modifications by high-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH/PUT requests to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* with Yamcs user privilege checks for ChangeMissionDatabase. Baseline algorithm-modification velocity per admin account; alert on spike or modification outside change windows.

suggestion.title: Jython ScriptEngine evaluation of algorithm code with restricted Java classes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names the root cause: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text using Jython (via the JSR-223 ScriptEngine API) without enforcing a secure sandbox.' Current hunts miss the compilation phase; detection should trigger before shell execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs for JSR-223 ScriptEngine compilation events or warnings containing java.lang.Runtime, ProcessBuilder, getRuntime(), exec, or System references in the algorithm source text or exception stack. Flag as early-stage exploit attempt.

suggestion.title: Java Runtime.getRuntime().exec() invocation within Jython sandbox context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack payload as overriding algorithm with 'java.lang.Runtime' code. Direct execution of OS processes via Runtime.exec() within Jython is the critical execution step; current hunts only observe the downstream shell child process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Yamcs or JVM logs for ClassNotFoundException, SecurityException, or IllegalAccessException during Jython script execution when java.lang.Runtime, ProcessBuilder, or System.exec methods are referenced. Successful execution may not log; pair with UC_17_5 (shell spawning) for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm text contains Java import statements or class instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code injection of 'algorithm text' with embedded Java payloads. Valid Yamcs algorithms should not contain arbitrary Java imports (java.lang, java.io, etc.) or ProcessBuilder/Runtime instantiation. Baseline legitimate algorithm syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect PATCH request payloads to algorithm endpoints for presence of 'import java', 'new Runtime', 'new ProcessBuilder', or 'System.exec' strings. Flag as malicious algorithm override. Establish whitelist of permitted algorithm libraries.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Private Container Images
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication' — core attack vector. Pipeline missed the primary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET requests to private container image endpoints (e.g., /v2/<org>/<repo>/manifests) from unauthenticated sessions or IPs lacking prior auth tokens. Flag 401→200 transitions or missing Authorization headers on sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Private Container Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated bypass implies attacker can enumerate repos ('Gitea Vulnerability Exposes...') — discovery phase absent from pipeline reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential GET requests to container registry listing endpoints (/v2/catalog, /_/repos, or equivalents) from single source without auth credentials or with failed auth, especially if response includes repository names.

suggestion.title: Extraction of Secrets from Exposed Container Images
suggestion.rationale: Private images often contain embedded credentials, API keys, or config. Article implies disclosure of proprietary content — exfiltration detection missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-volume downloads of container image layers or manifests to external IPs after unauthenticated container registry access. Correlate with container image sizes and pull frequency anomalies.

suggestion.title: Gitea Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: authentication enforcement is bypassed ('without Authentication'). Pipeline should surface auth-bypass exploitation signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to protected endpoints (container registry, private repos) that succeed despite missing, malformed, or expired authentication tokens. Alert on auth header stripping or path traversal attempts to bypass auth middleware.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exposed Container Images
suggestion.rationale: Private images exposed may contain creds or deploy keys for internal systems — potential pivot point. Attack chain beyond initial disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exfiltration: monitor for successful authentications or privilege escalations using credentials extracted from container image layers (env vars, .ssh/config, docker config.json in image manifests).

suggestion.title: Malicious Extension Installation from OpenVSX or VS Code Marketplace
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'initially targeted developers with malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials.' No detection use case exists for compromise at the extension distribution layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code and editor process spawning for extension installation activity, track connections to OpenVSX and Microsoft extension registry during installation, and correlate with subsequent suspicious child-process execution or credential access patterns from the extension host process.

suggestion.title: Dormant Malicious Code Activation Post-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Glassworm operators planted dozens of dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update.' This persistence and delayed execution tactic requires detection of behavioral shift in previously benign extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline extension process behavior at installation. Trigger detection when previously-silent extension processes suddenly spawn children, access credential stores, or initiate network connections after an extension update event.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Solana blockchain: C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions.' This non-traditional C2 channel should be detected via network and process analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes making HTTPS connections to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, devnet.solana.com) from developer workstations or editor contexts. Correlate with metadata extraction or JSON parsing of blockchain transaction data.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Query for C2 Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'BitTorrent Distributed Hash Table (DHT): The GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys.' DHT queries are unusual from typical developer tools and should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BitTorrent DHT traffic (UDP port 6881-6889 or Mainline DHT queries) originating from VS Code, extension processes, or npm-related processes. Flag hardcoded peer discovery patterns and configuration key lookups.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Abuse for C2 Dead-Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Public calendar service: Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' Calendar API abuse for C2 is a detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Google Calendar API activity (calendar.google.com/calendar/api) from developer tools or extensions. Alert on Base64-encoded strings extracted from calendar event metadata or titles. Baseline legitimate calendar usage and flag anomalous query frequency or large data transfers via event fields.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction from Developer Tools and Wallets
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacks 'stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials.' This collection phase should be detected via process access and file system monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extension or npm processes accessing credential stores (.ssh, .git-credentials, .netrc), wallet files (.ethereum, .solana), and environment files (.env). Flag reads of in-memory credential buffers from editor contexts or unusual enumerate operations on credential directories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Poisoning Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Developer Supply Chain Attack Infrastructure' — core attack pattern for malware distribution through compromised repositories or package feeds. Pipeline produced no use cases despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package managers (npm, pip, maven, nuget) for unsigned or revoked-signature packages, unusual download frequencies from non-canonical mirrors, or packages with suspicious post-install scripts. Track developer workstations for execution of scripts extracted from newly-downloaded packages.

suggestion.title: Malware Dropper Execution from Package Sources
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks typically use dropper payloads embedded in legitimate-appearing packages. Title references 'GlassWorm Malware' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of scripts, batch files, or interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, bash, python) launched from package installation directories with unusual parent processes or low signing prevalence.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beacon from Compromised Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware typically establishes persistence and C2 channels. No C2 IOCs (domains, IPs, URLs) were extracted despite infrastructure takedown narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate developer workstation network traffic for connections to newly-registered domains, bulletproof hosting providers, or IPs associated with botnet C2. Alert on encoded/encrypted DNS queries or HTTP traffic with suspicious User-Agents from package installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Repository/Package Registry Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Infrastructure takedown implies law enforcement identified staging or distribution points. No detection suggested for compromise of development repositories or package registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized authentication to package repositories (failed then successful logins from novel IPs), API key creation/rotation outside maintenance windows, or package version rollback/re-publication patterns inconsistent with normal developer workflows.

suggestion.title: GlassWorm Family File Hash and Artifact Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies specific malware family 'GlassWorm' but pipeline extracted zero file hashes, executable names, or behavioral signatures for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create hash IOC lists and filename patterns for GlassWorm variants. Alert on file creation or process execution matching known malware hashes, suspicious filenames (dropper artifacts), or imported DLLs associated with malware analysis reports.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning + Malicious Software Repository Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'coordinated SEO poisoning operation' delivering users searching for six named utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear) to attacker-controlled domains. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of utility software from suspicious or newly-registered domains; correlate DNS lookups for utility names with downloads from non-vendor-official sources; alert on high volume of failed antivirus scans or unsigned binaries matching known software names.

suggestion.title: Malicious DLL Sideload from Extracted Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious ZIP from gleeze[.]com 'includes the legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded.' This is T1129 but no detection case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned DLLs co-extracted with legitimate-named executables from archive files in user directories; alert on DLL loads from TEMP/Downloads folders with mismatched signatures or timestamps; correlate ZIP extraction with immediate child process spawning.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Installation via Malicious msiexec Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'DLL uses msiexec.exe to install vcredist_x64.dll, which is a package installer for the ScreenConnect remote access tool'—a common persistence vector not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for msiexec.exe invoked from TEMP/Downloads or by unusual parent processes; correlate msiexec execution with vcredist-named packages and subsequent ScreenConnect C2 outbound connections; alert on ScreenConnect listeners established post-infection timeline.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing into Microsoft-Signed Utilities
suggestion.rationale: Article details SimpleRunPE.exe performing process hollowing into seven named Microsoft binaries (InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe). No detection use case covers this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on these seven .NET/system utilities spawned with anomalous parent processes (SimpleRunPE, RuntimeHost, vlc.exe) or from unexpected directories; flag process creation with mismatched command-line arguments; correlate with memory injection indicators or unsigned child processes.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Exclusion Modification via PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender.' This defense evasion step is not captured in any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell commands invoking Add-MpPreference or modifying registry paths under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions; alert on exclusion-list modifications shortly after suspicious binary execution or DLL loads from archive.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Tool Execution (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI)
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes with deployment of three named mining modules but no use case targets miner execution, C2 communication, or resource abuse. 'One of three mining modules is downloaded and executed.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution or persistence of gminer, lolMiner, or SRBMiner-MULTI binaries; monitor for sustained GPU utilization anomalies post-infection; flag outbound traffic to public mining pools or stratum protocols from non-datacenter systems; correlate with parent process genealogy from hollowed utilities.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly reference 'QR Codes' as World Cup attack vector. No UC generated despite QR-code-to-C2-redirect being established phishing variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails or landing pages with embedded QR codes pointing to newly-registered or suspicious domains. Correlate QR code scans with credential harvesting page load events and domain whois creation dates within 30 days of article publication date.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration for FIFA Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'typosquatting' as attack surface. Pipeline generated zero phishing infrastructure detection despite this being named technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and registrations with character substitution (fifa→fifaa, ticketing→ticketting) or Cyrillic homoglyph substitution targeting World Cup official domains. Track employee browsing to high-confidence lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Process Execution (Razing Ursa, unnamed variants)
suggestion.rationale: Keywords name 'wiper' and 'Razing Ursa' (known wiper deployer) but zero impact-phase detection generated. Critical gap for infrastructure protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file deletion patterns (>10k files/min) and disk formatting commands (cipher /w, dd if=/dev/zero) on World Cup venue or broadcast infrastructure. Alert on process creation for known wiper families correlated with Razing Ursa TTPs.

suggestion.title: Actor-Attributed C2 Communication (Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra)
suggestion.rationale: Three distinct threat actor names appear in keywords but pipeline extracted zero actor-specific threat intelligence. No kill-chain or IOC-based detection for named groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish attributed IOC feeds for Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra infrastructure. Alert on network egress to known C2 domains, beacon patterns (DNS queries at fixed intervals), and TLS certificate thumbprint matches for group-attributed infrastructure.

suggestion.title: World Cup-Themed Credential Harvesting Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Keywords list 'phishing' as primary attack vector. No credential-access detection generated despite clear initial-access/credential-theft progression in World Cup threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with World Cup, FIFA, ticketing, or venue lures requesting credential entry. Correlate phishing email clicks with failed login attempts within 2 hours and logins from anomalous geographies post-click.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering: Suspicious Login Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access' on April 10–14, 2026. Attacker obtained valid employee credentials and logged in. Detection must flag login anomalies: failed logins preceding success, off-hours access, impossible travel between locations, or device/IP changes inconsistent with employee baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee account with repeated failed authentication attempts followed by successful login from new geolocation, off-hours, or unfamiliar device. Cross-correlate with employee's historical login patterns and Carnival organizational data to establish baseline behavior.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Customer Data Exfiltration: Database Query and File Copy Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'bad actor illegally copied personal information' of 5.9M+ customers containing names, DOB, emails, genders, loyalty program data. Bulk extraction of 8.7M records would manifest as high-row-count SQL queries, batch export jobs, or large file copies on database servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for high-volume SELECT statements on customer tables (loyalty program, PII columns) executed by the compromised employee account. Alert on file copy or compression operations exporting >100K rows outside standard backup windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access Outside Employee Role Scope: Mariner Society Loyalty Program Query Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker accessed Mariner Society loyalty program data (Holland America brand). Compromised employee account likely has no legitimate business reason to query customer loyalty records. Access scope deviation from baseline role permissions indicates account misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-employee query permission baseline by role (e.g., customer service reps query bookings, finance queries transactions). Alert when account queries PII tables (customers, loyalty programs, crew) outside those baseline permissions or requests record sets 10x+ larger than historical queries.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Campaign: Carnival Employee Targeting and Credential Theft Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names ShinyHunters as threat actor claiming the breach. Article notes 'Over the past year, ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers' globally. This organization is a known repeat offender using social engineering. Email phishing or pretexting likely preceded credential compromise but article does not specify mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish threat signature on ShinyHunters social-engineering templates (domain spoofing, urgency language). Correlate suspicious emails arriving 48–72 hours before April 10 breach window to Carnival domains. Flag emails impersonating Carnival IT/HR requesting credential verification or system access resets.

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer Database Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly states 'millions of customers' personal information' was exposed, indicating large-scale data extraction. Pipeline failed to generate any exfiltration detection despite clear evidence of material data loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk export operations from customer database systems (e.g., SELECT * on cardholder/PII tables), followed by high-volume outbound transfers to external IPs or cloud storage. Monitor for unusual database query patterns aggregating customer records.

suggestion.title: Web Application Exploitation or Credential Compromise to Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Breach of cruise-line customer database almost certainly involved T1190 (public-facing app exploitation) or T1078 (valid compromised credentials). Pipeline did not suggest either attack vector despite this being standard pattern for retail/hospitality sector data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for SQLi, authentication bypass, or RCE patterns in web access logs. Correlate with anomalous database login activity from service accounts or unusual source IPs accessing customer data warehouses.

suggestion.title: Internal Data Staging and Collection
suggestion.rationale: Multi-million record breach typically involves staging data to temporary shares or staging servers before exfiltration. Article implies scale consistent with staged extraction; pipeline missed collection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of large archives, bulk data queries aggregating customer records into temporary tables, or file transfers to suspicious internal locations (dev shares, admin workstations, staging servers).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Data Warehouse or Core Database Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must traverse from initial compromise (web tier or compromised user) to customer data stores. This lateral movement phase is missing from kill-chain reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate initial compromise evidence with database access logs. Flag accounts or systems connecting to restricted data warehouse networks shortly after web exploitation or credential compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: BSC Testnet Smart Contract C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'BSC Testnet Smart Contracts for Takedown-Resistant Command and Control' — core threat vector not extracted. Pipeline should identify smart contract addresses and detect RPC/interaction patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/WebSocket connections to Binance Smart Chain testnet RPC endpoints (e.g., testnet.bscscan.com, testnet RPCs). Detect process execution with hardcoded contract addresses (0x...) or ABI-related strings in memory. Monitor for beacon-like callback patterns to blockchain infrastructure.

suggestion.title: ClearFake Social Media Account Takeover / Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'ClearFake' implies fake social media accounts or credential theft as initial access — no actor name or technique extraction. Should detect phishing/credential harvesting indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk credential submission attempts, anomalous geographic sign-in patterns from account creation, and rapid-fire API calls to enumerate/harvest accounts. Flag creation of typosquatted social media accounts. Detect phishing campaigns directing to fake login portals.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Address Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain-based C2 implies command responses and exfiltration routed through wallets — no wallet addresses or exfiltration indicators extracted. Should monitor for suspicious blockchain transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with cryptocurrency exchange APIs, MetaMask provider strings, or wallet address parameters. Detect network connections to blockchain explorers or mixers. Monitor for data encoding/upload to blockchain addresses or IPFS gateways.

suggestion.title: Takedown-Resistant Decentralized C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'takedown-resistant' design via testnet — implies detection evasion through decentralized infrastructure. Pipeline missed defense-evasion technique mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process memory containing web3.js, ethers.js, or similar blockchain client libraries. Alert on non-standard transport protocols (P2P, custom serialization) for C2. Monitor for C2 callback attempts to distributed/P2P infrastructure rather than centralized domains.

suggestion.title: Malware Process Execution with Blockchain Artifact Loading
suggestion.rationale: Campaign implies malware distribution but no file hashes or process execution patterns extracted. Should detect suspicious binary execution tied to blockchain operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process chains: Rundll32/Regsvcs/Regasm executing DLLs with blockchain functionality. Detect PowerShell execution with web3 module imports or contract interaction code. Alert on process creation with command-line arguments containing smart contract addresses or function selectors.

suggestion.title: Wallet Key / Private Key Exfiltration Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain-based scheme implies threat actor must manage wallets — no detection for private key theft or wallet compromise. Should detect key material exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access to common cryptocurrency wallet storage locations (.ethereum, .cardano, MetaMask profile). Detect process execution accessing browser extension credential stores. Monitor for base64-encoded or hex-encoded key material in process arguments, clipboard access, or file writes.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in Roundcube HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attackers inject SQL queries' — the pipeline should have generated detection for SQL injection payloads in Roundcube web requests. No such use case appeared.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Roundcube endpoints (e.g., /roundcube/, /webmail/) for SQL injection signatures (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comment sequences --//*). Correlate with web server error logs showing SQL syntax errors or 5xx responses from database-facing functions.

suggestion.title: Roundcube Process Database Connections Spike
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection attacks typically manifest as abnormal database query volume or malformed queries. Article describes injection of SQL queries but pipeline generated no detection for this behavioral signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal database query frequency from Roundcube PHP process. Alert on sustained elevation (>2σ) in query volume or detection of queries originating from unexpected user input parameters (e.g., email search, filter fields).

suggestion.title: Roundcube Authentication Bypass via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection in a webmail context typically targets authentication or user data retrieval. Article says attackers 'inject SQL queries' but does not explicitly scope the injection point—pipeline should flag authentication-bypass as highest-probability impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication to Roundcube user accounts preceded by HTTP requests containing SQL injection signatures in login parameters. Cross-reference IP, user-agent, and session tokens to identify accounts with atypical login patterns.

suggestion.title: Roundcube Database Error Log Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Failed SQL injection attempts will generate database syntax errors. Article identifies SQL injection as attack method; pipeline should surface detection of error-log spikes in database layer associated with Roundcube queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database error logs (MySQL/PostgreSQL) for syntax errors, invalid column references, or unexpected data-type mismatches in queries tagged as Roundcube-sourced. Correlate error timestamps with Roundcube access logs.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Following Roundcube Compromise
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection in Roundcube webmail enables attacker access to email data, user credentials, and account metadata. Article emphasizes severity (HIGH) and query injection; pipeline missed detection for post-compromise data staging/exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large-volume database queries selecting email bodies, attachments, or credential fields (user_login, password_hash) from Roundcube tables. Correlate with unusual outbound network connections from the Roundcube server (SFTP, SMB, HTTPS exfil channels).

suggestion.title: Executable Masquerading as Business Document via Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'phishing emails masquerading as business documents' delivering executable payloads. Pipeline produced zero detections for obfuscated attachment types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email attachments with double-extension patterns (.pdf.exe, .docx.scr) or suspicious executable MIME types delivered via external mail with business-document social engineering pretext in subject/body.

suggestion.title: Keylogger Process Execution from Suspicious Parent
suggestion.rationale: VIP Keylogger payload execution pattern — malware must spawn to capture keyboard input. No detection UC covers process execution post-phishing compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious parent-child relationships where Office applications, shell interpreters, or email clients spawn unexpected executables with names suggesting logging/capture functionality (contains 'key', 'log', 'capture', 'input').

suggestion.title: Keyboard Input Capture via Legitimate System APIs
suggestion.rationale: Keyloggers implement T1056.004 by hooking keyboard input. Article describes VIP Keylogger functionality but pipeline surfaced no credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious calls to GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx (WH_KEYBOARD), GetKeyboardState, or similar input interception APIs from unsigned or recently-created process binaries.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Registration for Keylogger
suggestion.rationale: Keyloggers require persistence across reboot. Article establishes malware persistence requirement; pipeline extracted no registry or scheduled-task detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious registry writes to HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce keys or Startup folders by processes spawned from email temp directories within 1 minute of user opening attachment.

suggestion.title: Keylogger C2 Communication Pattern
suggestion.rationale: VIP Keylogger must exfiltrate captured credentials via network. No mention of detection UCs for C2 channels or data exfil from malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious outbound connections (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS) from keylogger process to non-standard ports, newly registered domains, or IPs without recent legitimacy history. Correlate with failed credential attempts.

suggestion.title: Email Attachment Detonation in User Profile Temp
suggestion.rationale: Phishing delivery mechanism — attachments execute from user temp folders. No detection around this common post-click execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with parent residing in AppData\Local\Temp, %TEMP%, or Outlook cache folders within 2 minutes of email user interaction, especially for executable file types.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Malware Delivery from GHOSTYNETWORKS / OMEGATECH Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Use GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH to Host JS Malware Infrastructure' — this is the core threat but no detection was generated. Should detect outbound connections to these providers or script execution initiated by traffic from these ASNs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH IP ranges followed by process creation of JavaScript interpreters (cscript.exe, wscript.exe, node.exe) or child processes spawned by browser/email clients. Alert on delivery of .js or .jse files from these providers to client machines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Execution Post-Web Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes JS malware hosted on infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for the execution phase: script execution from temporary/download directories correlating with prior network connections to malicious infrastructure.
