suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows Script Host or Node.js child processes spawned from user Download, AppData\Local\Temp, or browser cache directories. Baseline script behavior; flag scripts that subsequently create network sockets or spawn cmd.exe/powershell.exe.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Reconnaissance: ASN / Hosting Provider Attribution
suggestion.rationale: GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH are named as hosting providers; these should be added to infrastructure threat models and monitored for organic resolution patterns and actor attribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain updated ASN/WHOIS records for GHOSTYNETWORKS and OMEGATECH; monitor for passive DNS queries or DNS zone transfers targeting domains registered under these entities. Cross-correlate with known malware C2 infrastructure databases (URLhaus, Shodan, etc.) for ongoing monitoring.

suggestion.title: Fake Recruiter Phishing Targeting Cryptocurrency Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Recruiter Lures' as the attack vector; pipeline generated zero initial-access detections despite this being the primary infection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with recruiter-impersonation indicators (LinkedIn/Indeed domain spoofing, job-posting URLs, generic greetings to targets in crypto sector) and suspicious attachment types. Correlate email metadata across cryptocurrency firm recipients within narrow timeframe to identify campaign pattern.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from User-Downloaded Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'macOS Malware' payload but no execution-phase detections generated; should detect suspicious process birth and binary launch patterns on Mac endpoints post-phishing delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution on macOS hosts following phishing delivery window, particularly unsigned binaries, processes spawned from /tmp or Downloads directories, or parent processes inconsistent with normal user workflows (bash launching compiled executable).

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain inherently requires malware to establish C2, but pipeline identified zero persistence or C&C phases; should detect exfiltration and remote control indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS hosts in cryptocurrency firms for outbound connections to newly registered or JINX-0164-attributed infrastructure. Flag unusual DNS requests from affected hosts; correlate with malware process execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Cryptocurrency Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Cryptocurrency-firm targeting strongly suggests credential theft objective (exchange access, signing keys, seed phrases), but pipeline did not map credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process activity consistent with credential harvesting on macOS (keychain access, clipboard monitoring, file enumeration of browser storage, password manager directories). Correlate with network beaconing to C2.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Removal or Deactivation Post-Incident
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' — this is a hostile action or evidence disposal that should trigger detection on GitHub audit logs showing account deletion, repository removal, or force-deactivation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub organization audit logs for unexpected account removal, mass repository deletion, or API token revocation by non-owner actors. Flag accounts deleted within hours of incident disclosure or researcher activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub PAT or OAuth Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Account removal implies prior compromise; 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' suggests credential theft or token abuse used to perform the deletion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PAT or OAuth token usage from unusual IP ranges or geographic locations prior to account removal. Monitor for token usage inconsistent with researcher's normal patterns.

suggestion.title: Public Zero-Day Disclosure Without Vendor Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures' and 'Microsoft Slams' — indicates disclosure policy violation, likely detected via CVE publication, GitHub PoC repos, or security mailing lists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for publication of unpatched Microsoft vulnerability details in public GitHub repos, security forums, or mailing lists. Cross-reference against Microsoft responsible disclosure timeline to flag premature disclosure.

suggestion.title: Researcher Account Takeover via Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Account removal post-disclosure suggests attacker gained control to suppress the researcher; 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' implies previous valid-credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate GitHub account access logs with changes to email recovery address, 2FA removal, or SSH key additions preceding the account deletion event.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Platform Vulnerability Disclosed Without MSRC Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates Microsoft vulnerability involved in public disclosure; should detect Microsoft CVE or security advisory activity correlated with researcher account removal timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MSRC publication delays or gaps; flag Microsoft vulnerabilities disclosed publicly before MSRC advisory. Correlate timing with researcher activity suspensions.

suggestion.title: Git Rebase Command Injection via Malicious Branch Name
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the "Rebase before merging" merge operation' using malicious branch names as the injection vector.
log_sources: Process execution logs from Gogs service
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs server process execution for git rebase commands containing unexpected --exec or similar command-injection flags. Correlate with suspicious branch names in pull requests that precede rebase operations.

suggestion.title: Rapid Account Creation → Repository Creation → Rebase Enablement Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers can 'simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' and that 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences where newly registered accounts immediately create repositories and enable rebase merging within minutes. Flag accounts created by unauthenticated users (leveraging default open-registration setting) that proceed to administrative configuration changes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Harvesting from Gogs Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' from all repositories on the compromised instance after RCE.
log_sources: Gogs service process file access logs
Filesystem access to .git directories and credential stores
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs server process for file system enumeration of multiple repository directories and access to credential storage paths (.ssh, .git/config, token files) in rapid succession after privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Account Provisioning via Default Open Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false) and no limit on repository creation (MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = -1), an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gogs instances with open registration enabled when multiple accounts are created from single or rapidly-rotating IP addresses, especially if accompanied by immediate administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Repository Modification via Automated Merge
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gain ability to 'modify any hosted repository's code' through pull request merge operations without requiring user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits merged into repositories without corresponding pull request approval events or user interaction. Flag rapid merges of pull requests containing code changes, especially on repositories owned by compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: SSH Key Exfiltration Enabling Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers can 'dump credentials...SSH keys' and subsequently 'pivot to other network-accessible systems' after initial Gogs compromise.
log_sources: SSH authentication logs on downstream systems
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gogs server compromise indicators with SSH authentication attempts from the Gogs server IP to other internal systems using newly-observed key material or credential pairs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via CIFS Kernel Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Allows Attackers to Gain Root Access' — the core threat indicator. Pipeline should have generated at least one use case for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged process transitions to root/SYSTEM context, especially following CIFS filesystem operations or mount attempts. Monitor kernel logs for CIFS subsystem errors or warnings that precede privilege escalation. Correlate uid/gid changes with timing of vulnerability exploitation window.

suggestion.title: CIFS Exploitation Attempt via Syscall Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Kernel vulnerabilities typically exploit memory safety flaws requiring specific syscall patterns; pipeline missed use case for detecting exploitation signatures targeting CIFS kernel module.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal syscall sequences targeting CIFS paths (cifs mounts, specific ioctl calls, memory mapping operations). Flag exploitation PoC tools or frameworks executing against CIFS subsystem. Alert on rapid mount/unmount cycles or memory manipulation near cifs kernel module space.

suggestion.title: CIFS Mount Operation from Unprivileged Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in 'CIFSwitch' (CIFS kernel subsystem); article states attackers gain root but does not detail exploitation mechanics. Pipeline should flag unusual CIFS mount initiations that may precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CIFS mount commands initiated by non-root or service accounts, particularly with unusual mount options or targets. Correlate mounts with subsequent privileged process creation or kernel panic events.

suggestion.title: MsBuild.exe Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'MsBuild.exe Process Hollowing'—process hollowing requires spawning or injecting into child processes. Standard MsBuild should not spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, or rundll32.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag MsBuild.exe (signed binary at C:\Program Files*\MSBuild\*\MSBuild.exe) creating child processes outside expected compiler tools (csc.exe, vbc.exe, rc.exe). Correlate parent-child process relationships and monitor for unsigned child processes or those executing from temp directories.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing via Kernel32 API Sequence from MsBuild
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Process Hollowing'—a defense evasion technique that injects code into suspended processes via VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, SetThreadContext, ResumeThread sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MsBuild.exe loading kernel32.dll, ntdll.dll and issuing memory manipulation syscalls (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory) against target process handles without corresponding legitimate Visual Studio build activity or project compilation telemetry.

suggestion.title: MsBuild.exe with Inline or Encoded Command-Line Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Process hollowing attacks disguise payload delivery through MsBuild /inline parameters, encoded project files, or script execution; legitimate MsBuild has predictable argument patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on MsBuild.exe invoked with /inline, base64-encoded arguments, project files from non-standard paths (AppData, Temp, Downloads, %PUBLIC%), or external URL references in command line.

suggestion.title: Process Memory Divergence: MsBuild Binary vs. Runtime Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Process hollowing creates a process that presents as MsBuild but contains injected malicious code. Behavioral telemetry (network connections, registry operations, file creation) will diverge from legitimate build operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference MsBuild process creation against downstream behavioral indicators: unexpected network connections, unusual registry modifications, or file writes to non-build directories. Flag if MsBuild terminates without generating standard build artifacts (obj/, bin/, .pdb files) or compiler logs.

suggestion.title: Zapier OAuth Token Exfiltration via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates account takeover; article likely describes credential compromise. OAuth tokens are the primary attack surface for SaaS account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth grant flows immediately followed by unusual API activity or login from anomalous IP. Look for interactive sign-in events followed by programmatic access patterns within 5 minutes, or Zapier API calls from IPs/user agents not matching initial login source.

suggestion.title: Zapier Account Access from Impossible Travel
suggestion.rationale: Account takeover indicator—attacker location likely differs from victim. Article title emphasizes 'full account takeover' which implies lateral movement post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful logins to Zapier where geographic distance from previous login in <12hrs is physically impossible (>5000km). Correlate IP geolocation with user's baseline locations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Zapier Workflow Modification or Execution
suggestion.rationale: Full account takeover enables attacker to modify automation workflows for data exfiltration or lateral movement. This is the 'impact' phase of the attack chain.
log_sources: connected app activity logs (Slack, email, etc.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of Zapier Zaps by accounts without recent change history, especially those adding new actions to sensitive connected apps (email, file storage, databases). Baseline normal Zap frequency per user and alert on 3x+ activity spike.

suggestion.title: MFA Bypass or Circumvention in Zapier Login
suggestion.rationale: 'Full account takeover' against a SaaS service typically requires bypassing MFA. Article likely describes specific bypass technique (prompt bombing, MITM, replay, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MFA challenge failures followed by successful non-MFA login, or logins where MFA was explicitly disabled/reset. Flag accounts with MFA requirement changes within 15 minutes of failed auth attempts.

suggestion.title: Zapier API Key Enumeration or Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Compromised accounts may expose API keys. Attackers often enumerate or reuse tokens across Zapier-connected services for persistence.
log_sources: network logs for Zapier API endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls using same token from multiple distinct IP addresses, user agents, or geographic locations within short timeframe. Alert on API key creation events followed by immediate use from non-standard clients.

suggestion.title: Zapier Integration Access to Sensitive Downstream Services
suggestion.rationale: Zapier integrates with email, cloud storage, CRM, databases. Full account takeover grants attacker access to all connected downstream services—critical for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Zapier-sourced API calls to downstream services (via Zapier's service account or delegated auth) that access sensitive data. Flag Zaps that export data to unauthenticated URLs, external email addresses, or new cloud storage destinations.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Recommending Suspicious or Newly-Registered Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — the chatbot itself is the delivery vehicle for malicious URLs. Pipeline produced no initial_access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot recommendation outputs for references to domains flagged as newly registered (<30 days), associated with mining-pool infrastructure, or exhibiting typosquatting patterns of legitimate services. Baseline legitimate recommendation domains per chatbot model and alert on high-confidence deviations with user click-through correlation.

suggestion.title: Cryptomining Process and Resource Hijacking Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is explicitly cryptojacking malware, yet pipeline produced zero impact-phase detections. Cryptomining leaves measurable CPU, memory, and network footprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained high CPU/GPU usage from browser processes or scriptable runtimes, correlated with outbound connections to known Monero mining pool IP ranges or domains (e.g., pool.monero.com, mining-pool patterns). Flag child processes spawned from browser with xmrig, stratum protocol, or cryptominer command-line signatures.

suggestion.title: User Clicks Chatbot-Recommended Link to Malware Domain
suggestion.rationale: The phrase 'Redirect Users' indicates user interaction is required to complete the attack chain. Pipeline missed T1204.001 (User Execution of Malicious Link).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate chatbot interaction logs with subsequent web proxy/URL filtering events. Detect users navigating to domains recommended by chatbot within <5 seconds of chatbot response. Escalate if destination domain hosts known cryptomining malware or hosts infrastructure associated with botnet C2.

suggestion.title: Password Spraying Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' to choose weak passwords, establishing this as an active threat. No detection use case was proposed despite the threat being named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts across multiple user accounts in short time windows, targeting accounts with weak or common passwords (e.g., users in banned-word lists). Correlate failed login counts from single source IP with password policy violation logs.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Reuse Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Breach password protection' blocking '5.4 billion known breached credentials,' implying attackers attempt to use stolen passwords in AD. No detection for this credential access method was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logon attempts using credentials that exist in public breach databases (e.g., Have I Been Pwned, Specops 5.4B dataset proxy via SIEM enrichment). Flag accounts whose password was recently reset after appearing in breach lists.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Password Reset Frequency Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states controls should 'detect compromised credentials' and trigger resets. If attackers gain AD access, rapid password resets by victims or forced resets by admins would be detectable as an Indicator of Compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal password reset rates for users (e.g., >3 resets in 24 hours outside of planned maintenance). Correlate with failed login attempts immediately preceding resets. Baseline by user role and adjust sensitivity to exclude helpdesk-heavy roles.

suggestion.title: Detect cPanel Redis Function Exploitation Log Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article provides detection command and states: 'If this command results in any output, we recommend you examine the IPs in the list' — pattern 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' is a direct exploitation indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when log entries contain 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' in cPanel directories. Extract source IPs and timestamp. This indicates exploitation of the vulnerable Redis function. Correlate with root-level process execution or privilege escalation events on the same host.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary Script Execution with Root Privileges from cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability outcome: 'enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' — unexpected privilege elevation from cPanel process is the attack success indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script interpreters (bash, sh, perl, python, ruby) spawned by LiteSpeed or cPanel processes with execution context UID=0 (root). Flag cases where parent process ran with insufficient privilege to legitimately escalate. Baseline expected cPanel administrative scripts separately.

suggestion.title: Inventory LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Versions v2.3 through v2.4.4
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists affected versions: 'versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4' — missing from any detection outputs, yet necessary for risk assessment and targeted patching
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint inventory for LiteSpeed cPanel user-end plugin version. Alert if version is between v2.3 and v2.4.4 (inclusive). Cross-reference against patch date (May 27, 2026) to identify systems with vulnerable installations. Severity: critical with 4-day federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Correlate Suspicious Source IPs from Exploitation Attempts with Post-Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article guidance: 'examine the IPs in the list...examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs' — exploitation detection alone is insufficient; analyst must link IPs to unauthorized activity
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract source IP from exploited 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' entries. Cross-reference against authentication logs, command execution logs (bash_history, auditd), and file modification times. Report any root-level commands or privilege escalation actions initiated from the same IP within the exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Network Detection of cPanel JSON API Exploitation Requests
suggestion.rationale: Plugin is 'user-end' and network-accessible; article confirms active remote exploitation — HTTP/HTTPS-level detection can intercept attempts before log-based indicators
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests with parameter 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' or other Redis admin API calls from non-administrative source IPs. Flag requests from unexpected geographic regions or known non-federal networks if context is US federal infrastructure. Generate alert with request content for investigation.

suggestion.title: npm Supply-Chain Compromise: Unexpected Package Version Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product...published to the npm registry'—supply-chain attacks require detection at installation and runtime. Recommend hunting for package.lock or yarn.lock modifications pulling CVE-2026-45321-affected TanStack versions, or runtime detection of unexpected TanStack package versions in node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager commands (npm install, yarn add, pnpm add) installing TanStack with version-range selectors that could pull the malicious release. Cross-reference installed versions in node_modules against known-vulnerable CVE-2026-45321 release. Alternatively, alert on first-time TanStack package execution where version matches KEV advisory.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Malware: Suspicious Process Spawning from Node.js Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing malware'—the compromised TanStack package will execute malicious code at runtime. Detection must cover child-process anomalies originating from Node.js executing user code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous child processes spawned by Node.js (node.exe, node process) where parent is application code (not npm/webpack toolchain). Specifically flag memory-read or credential-access APIs (e.g., OS.homedir() + file reads, browser credential stores, SSH key enumeration) when called from dynamically-loaded module context.

suggestion.title: Package Identity Spoofing: Installation of Lookalike or Elevated-Privilege npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions malware published 'under a trusted identity'—suggests package-name similarity, typosquatting, or account takeover. Detection requires comparison against legitimate package metadata or signature verification failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm package installations where (a) package name is similar to a known legitimate package (e.g., tanstack-query vs @tanstack/query), (b) package signature does not match known-good certificate, or (c) package version jumps unexpectedly or is unsigned in npm registry metadata.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: TanStack Installation Detection and Vulnerable Version Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Canonical pattern: scan for presence of TanStack, extract version, compare against CVE-2026-45321 vulnerability manifest (assume versions ≤ latest-before-patch-date are in scope).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for any asset with TanStack package installed. Extract version. Compare against CISA KEV entry version-range (if provided; if not, flag all pre-patch-date builds as high-risk). Prioritize scan on public-facing applications and development workstations with internet npm registry access.

suggestion.title: Network-Level Exfiltration: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware will exfiltrate stolen credentials over C2 channel. Article specifies 'credential-stealing'—implies outbound communication to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected DNS queries or TCP/UDP connections initiated by Node.js process, especially to IPs with low reputation, newly-registered domains, or domains with fast-flux characteristics. Baseline Node.js process network behavior per application—credential-stealing C2 will deviate. Flag connections to non-standard ports (not 443, 80) or unusual URIs (POST with credential-like payloads in plaintext or weakly-obfuscated).

suggestion.title: Nx Console Child Process Spawning Obfuscated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious Nx fetched 'an obfuscated payload'—execution is mandatory. Pipeline missed entirely. Cite: 'fetched an obfuscated payload that could harvest credentials'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Nx.exe or Node.js child processes with Base64-encoded, high-entropy, or obfuscated command lines. Focus parent-child relationships: Nx → suspicious spawns within seconds of install or update.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Disk Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk'. Standard paths (.aws, .ssh, browser ProfilePath, .kube, git) must be monitored. Pipeline produced zero credential_access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process handle opens or file reads to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/*, browser credential databases, .git/config, or .kube/config from Nx-spawned processes. Batch or sequential access within minutes is high-signal.

suggestion.title: Memory-Resident Credential Access via Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from...in memory'. Malware reading/dumping lsass, browser processes, or SSH agent indicates T1187 activity. No memory-access detections in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx child processes opening handles to lsass.exe, svchost, browser processes, or credential managers with PROCESS_VM_READ or PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION rights. Correlate with file access to disk stores.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Connection from Nx Process to C2
suggestion.rationale: Malware must exfiltrate harvested credentials. Article implies attacker callback: 'fetched an obfuscated payload' requires remote server. No C2/exfil detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Nx or Node.js child process making HTTPS/DNS to non-package-registry, non-CDN destinations. Baseline legitimate Nx behavior and flag anomalies; check against C2 feed. High entropy DNS queries or POST to unknown IPs post-payload fetch.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Installation or Version Update
suggestion.rationale: Initial access vector: attacker 'published' malicious extension. Installation or unexpected version changes, especially unpatched pre-KEV versions, are detectable. Cite: 'malicious version of Nx Console was published'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Nx CLI invoked for install/update from unofficial repo or package manager during KEV window (post-2026-05-27). Hash-based detection against known-malicious packages. Monitor registry for Nx installation paths created/modified.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Data Exfiltration via Obfuscated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Harvested credentials must be transmitted. Pipeline generated no exfiltration detections despite article describing full data pipeline. Cite: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large or repeated HTTPS POSTs from Nx processes with high entropy payloads, potential base64/hex encoding, or DNS tunneling patterns. Correlate timing with credential-access events (file opens, memory reads).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and instructs to substitute 'CVE-2026-8398' into the template. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoints for presence of Daemon Tools Lite using software inventory. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-8398 vulnerability databases. Alert on any installed versions; patch lag is explicitly cited as 'the silent killer' despite patch status.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'embedded malicious code' with high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Detection of unexpected execution or child process spawning from Daemon Tools is required to catch post-exploitation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Daemon Tools Lite process (dtlite.exe, daemon.exe) spawning unsigned child processes, interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), or legitimate tools (net.exe, tasklist.exe). Elevated execution or script interpreter spawning is anomalous.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Federal Patch Compliance by Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article sets federal patch due date 2026-05-30. Pipeline should generate compliance tracking UC; 'patch lag is the silent killer' is explicitly stated as risk even if scanners report 'not vulnerable'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all instances of Daemon Tools Lite. Flag unpatched or absent patch-date metadata. Escalate any instances still unpatched past 2026-05-30 federal due date for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Automated API Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns: 'autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed.' Zero UCs target systematic API reconnaissance. This is a baseline detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single source IP or service principal generating high-frequency 404/405 responses to sequential or fuzzed API endpoint paths within sliding 5-minute window. Correlation: requests to non-existent resources, followed by valid resource probing, indicates automated enumeration rather than organic application use.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Authorization Boundary Testing
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies BOLA and IDOR as critical context-dependent vulns: 'the vulnerability lives in the gap between intended behavior and actual behavior.' No detection for attackers systematically probing object-level access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authenticated requests to resource endpoints with incrementing or sequential object IDs (e.g., /api/invoices/1001, /api/invoices/1002) from single user/principal, especially when mixed with 403/401 responses. Flag successful 200 responses to resources not explicitly owned/scoped to requesting user.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'cross-tenant data leakage' as context-dependent threat requiring detection beyond signature-based scanning. Pipeline missed this distinct pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests where authenticated user (Tenant A) attempts to query or retrieve resources tagged with different tenant_id/org_id (Tenant B). Successful access suggests authorization enforcement gap. Correlate with resource download/export operations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Chained Vulnerability Exploitation Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' No UC captures temporal clustering of disparate exploitation attempts by single actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequence of attack stages within 10-minute window: (1) auth-bypass probe (unusual 401/403 patterns), (2) elevated-access exploitation (succeeds after expected to fail), (3) data exfiltration (large result sets/bulk exports). Single actor executing multi-step chain suggests coordinated compromise, not reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Credential Reuse Across Services
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses authentication bypasses and notes attackers operate 'on a schedule defenders can't keep up with'—requires detection of potentially stolen/reused credentials used for continuous probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API tokens/credentials used from multiple geographic origins within short time window, or requests to disparate services/endpoints within seconds (impossible for legitimate client). High request volume to non-primary endpoints using same credential also suspicious.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Detection for IT Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' This is explicit callback phishing with a phone number in the email body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails targeting law/financial org domains with urgent IT-themed language (password reset, security update, account verification) that include phone numbers or callback requests. Alert especially on emails from external/typosquatted domains impersonating IT helpdesk. Look for sender domain ≠ claimed IT department domain.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access Tool Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' Covers RDP and third-party legitimate tools used maliciously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected RDP sessions (port 3389, EventID 4625/4624 on target systems) or legitimate remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Supremo process execution) initiated from external IP ranges or unusual hours. Correlate with preceding phishing emails to same user. Alert on tool installation by non-IT users.

suggestion.title: USB Device Insertion and Rapid Data Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer.' Also lists 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives' as indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect USB/external storage device connections on systems classified as high-value (finance systems, legal document repos, executive machines). Alert on immediate large file-copy operations following device insertion. Correlate with preceding remote-access sessions or failed RDP attempts to same device.

suggestion.title: Mass Data Access Post-Remote Session by Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration via RDP sessions: 'exfiltrate data, usually through legitimate remote access tools.' Implies unusual data access patterns once RDP access granted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After confirmed RDP session to a target, look for rapid sequential access to document repositories, file shares, or sensitive folders (legal case files, M&A documents, financial records). Flag reads by service accounts or non-legal staff users. Combine with file-transfer indicators (SMB traffic volume, 7zip/RAR compression initiated).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration and DNS Query Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'attackers register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals...using typosquatted patterns.' Example: support-lawfirm-name.com instead of lawfirmname-support.com.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS lookups for suspicious domains similar to known victim domain names with IT-support keywords (support, helpdesk, admin, servicedesk). Flag newly registered domains (WHOIS age < 30 days) matching typosquatted patterns. Alert on user clicks/visits to these domains from phishing emails.

suggestion.title: Unidentified In-Person Physical Access to IT Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'SRG sends an individual in-person to the victim company's location' and lists 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' as indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate badge/access-log entries for unknown individuals with IT support role claims. Alert on: visitors to server rooms / wiring closets without supervisor escort, badge swipes by visitors outside expected hours, employees reporting unknown IT personnel requesting computer access. Pair with incident reports of suspicious behavior.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API PATCH to algorithm endpoints by unprivileged or anomalous user accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this'. Detect PATCH requests to algorithm endpoints from users lacking this privilege, or privilege escalation activity preceding the PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PATCH /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* from user accounts without ChangeMissionDatabase privilege in directory/RBAC system. Correlate user's last 30 days of API activity—new privilege usage or unusual request patterns indicate compromise or abuse.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm configuration modified without change control / audit trail entry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'overriding the algorithm lo[ad]'. Detection should capture modifications to algorithm text that bypass change management or appear in audit logs with gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PATCH requests to algorithm endpoints where the resulting audit log entry is missing, deleted, or timestamped inconsistently. Also flag algorithm rollback or re-creation within minutes of a PATCH, suggesting cleanup of injected code.

suggestion.title: Jython eval() or exec() on algorithm text without sanitization — ScriptEngine payload injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text using Jython (via JSR-223 ScriptEngine API) without enforcing a secure sandbox'. Requires application-level logging or WAF body inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Yamcs logs for eval(), exec(), or compile() calls on algorithm text. At WAF layer, inspect PATCH request bodies to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* for 'java.lang.Runtime', 'getRuntime()', 'exec(', or Jython import statements indicating code injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Image Pull Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'exposes private container images without authentication'; any registry audit log or container pull attempt lacking valid credentials should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry for HTTP 200 responses to image manifest or layer requests from unauthenticated clients (missing Authorization header or invalid token). Flag OCI pull operations originating from external IPs without corresponding credential validation checks in Gitea logs.

suggestion.title: Gitea API Authentication Bypass Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability description indicates broken authentication in Gitea itself; detect API calls to /api/v1/ or /api/v2/ endpoints that should require auth tokens but succeed without them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/GET requests to Gitea API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/repos, /api/v1/user) that return 200 or 403 (instead of 401) when Authorization header is absent or null. Compare against baseline of authenticated access patterns.

suggestion.title: Private Container Image Enumeration via Gitea
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'private' images are exposed; detect attempts to list or discover private container repositories in Gitea without valid project/team membership.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to catalog endpoints (/v2/_catalog or equivalent in Gitea) and repository list endpoints from sources lacking explicit authentication or team membership. Correlate with image manifest/layer pulls to detect automated scraping.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Container Image Access
suggestion.rationale: If Gitea is multi-tenant or organization-scoped, the vulnerability may allow access to images outside the requester's scope; detect image pulls referencing other projects/orgs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pulls of container images belonging to other Gitea organizations/projects when the client IP, user agent, or auth context does not align with that project's member list or public status.

suggestion.title: Automated Bulk Container Image Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows unauthenticated access; detect high-volume, rapid pulls of multiple private images within a short time window, suggesting automated scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate pulls/manifests/layers requests per source IP over 5-minute windows; alert on >10 unique private images pulled from a single unauthenticated source within that window, or sustained >5 req/sec to registry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Gitea Version Disclosure and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically fingerprint vulnerable Gitea instances before exploiting the auth bypass; detect enumeration of version endpoints or banner grabbing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to /.gitea/swagger.json, /api/v1/version, or HEAD requests to / from IPs not in baseline, or repeated requests to non-existent endpoints from a single source indicating version scanning.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code-Related Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'initially targeted developers with malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions' and 'Later attack waves extended to GitHub repositories and npm packages' — no detection for extension marketplace-based initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or update of extensions from OpenVSX, VS Code Marketplace, or npm that match known-malicious package names or exhibit code signing anomalies. Monitor for extensions that request network access immediately after installation or have unsigned manifests.

suggestion.title: Dormant Malicious Code Activation on Extension Update
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Glassworm operators planted dozens of dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update' — no detection for staged/dormant code activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden behavioral changes in extension processes post-update: new child processes, file writes to credential stores, or unusual network connections following extension version changes. Flag extensions that spawn processes inconsistent with their declared functionality.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop' — no detection for blockchain-leveraging C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process connections to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, api.devnet.solana.com) or direct Solana node IPs. Monitor for unusual HTTPS traffic to blockchain explorers. Cross-reference with known bot beacon IPs (e.g., 164.92.88.210).

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT-Based C2 Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys' — no detection for DHT abuse as C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound UDP traffic to BitTorrent DHT ports (6881-6889) or unusual DHT queries from non-torrent applications. Flag processes making DHT queries with hardcoded key patterns. Monitor for processes with dual blockchain+DHT communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Service as C2 Dead-Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths' — no detection for legitimate service abuse for C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual Google Calendar API calls (CreateEvent, UpdateEvent) from non-browser processes or with Base64-encoded strings in event titles. Monitor for repeated Calendar read operations by processes without calendar integration. Correlate with sinkhole IP beaconing.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential and Cryptocurrency Wallet Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' — no detection for credential access during extension execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect extension processes accessing credential manager vaults, SSH key directories (~/.ssh), .git credential stores, or hardened wallet software (MetaMask plugins, Ledger Live). Monitor for file enumeration across typical developer credential locations or registry reads targeting DPAPI master keys.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Tampering - Package Repository Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'developer supply chain attack infrastructure' and 'malware takedown disrupts' — implies malware was injected into build/distribution pipelines. No detection for staged malicious artifacts in package repositories or CI/CD systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repository staging environments for uploads of binaries signed with stolen or counterfeit developer credentials. Track anomalous package metadata changes (version bumps, build timestamps) that precede mass distribution. Correlate uploader IP geolocation against historical developer patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware C2 Beaconing from Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware (GlassWorm) implies persistence within developer machines or CI systems. Article does not detail which C2 domains/IPs were seized, but takedown context suggests active C2 infrastructure should be detected before disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS connections from development machines (git clients, IDE processes, npm/pip) to newly registered or infrastructure-as-a-service domains. Correlate with build server egress patterns and baseline against known package mirrors.

suggestion.title: Malicious Compiler/Build Tool Injection
suggestion.rationale: GlassWorm targets 'developer supply chain' — suggests injection into dev tools themselves (compilers, linkers, build scripts). No detection rule for modified build system binaries or suspicious process spawning from build orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from gcc, clang, make, gradle, maven, or webpack. Track file modifications to /usr/bin (Linux) or %ProgramFiles% (Windows) build tool directories. Baseline normal compilation artifact hashes.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Harvesting via Malicious IDE Extensions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack premise implies developer credentials or API keys were compromised. GlassWorm likely used IDE plugins or package downloads to exfiltrate .env, .git credentials, or SSH keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when browser-based IDEs (VS Code Web) or electron-based editors read from ~/.ssh or ~/.npm directories outside of normal auth workflows. Flag process access to shell_history files from non-shell parent processes.

suggestion.title: Backdoored Dependency Chain Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes supply chain attack. Malware disruption implies attacker compromised dependency resolution (package manager cache poisoning or registry redirect). No detection for npm/pip/maven lockfile tampering or mirror-swapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc, pip.conf, and Maven settings.xml for unexpected registry mirrors or auth token modifications. Alert when package lockfiles (package-lock.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml) are rewritten outside of expected dependency update workflows.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Compromised Utility Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the archive includes the legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded when launching the benign binary' targeting CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DLLs with unsigned or suspicious signatures loaded from the same directory as these specific legitimate utilities. Baseline legitimate DLL load patterns for each utility and alert on anomalous additions, especially when followed by msiexec.exe or PowerShell child processes.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Installation via Malicious msiexec with vcredist Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'msiexec.exe to install vcredist_x64.dll, which is a package installer for the ScreenConnect remote access tool' as the persistence mechanism deployed post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect msiexec.exe installations with vcredist_x64.dll or ScreenConnect installers sourced from non-Microsoft repositories or downloaded recently. Correlate with suspicious parent processes (rundll32, PowerShell, Explorer) and subsequent ScreenConnect service registration without IT ticket/approval.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing into Microsoft-Signed .NET Utilities (SimpleRunPE)
suggestion.rationale: Article documents SimpleRunPE.exe performing 'process hollowing into a legitimate .NET binary signed by Microsoft: InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe'—specific named targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of these seven specific Microsoft-signed utilities with unusual parent processes (explorer.exe, rundll32.exe, PowerShell) or unusual child process lineage. Monitor for memory injection patterns and subsequent spawning of mining processes or cmd.exe without legitimate context.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Exclusion List Poisoning via PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'malware invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender'—direct disable/evasion technique with minimal false positives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell.exe (or obfuscated variants) executing Add-MpPreference, Set-MpPreference, or Registry modifications targeting HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions with path/process arguments containing SimpleRunPE, RuntimeHost, vlc.exe, or mining-related keywords.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Tool Execution Preceded by Suspicious Hollowing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies deployment of 'gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI, all of them designed to use graphics processing units (GPUs)' as final payload after process hollowing chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known GPU mining tools (gminer.exe, lolMiner.exe, SRBMiner-MULTI.exe) where the process lineage involves InstallUtil, RegAsm, RegSvcs, MSBuild, AppLaunch, AddInProcess, or aspnet_compiler.exe as parents. Alert on high GPU utilization coupled with these execution patterns.

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoned Utility Download from gleeze[.]com Subdomains
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'users look for one of the aforementioned utilities and are presented with malicious links boosted in search rankings through SEO poisoning' with archives hosted on 'gleeze[.]com'—identifiable initial access IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of files named CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, DDU, FurMark, K-Lite, PDFgear (or close variants) from gleeze[.]com subdomains or non-standard legitimate vendor domains. Correlate with subsequent msiexec.exe, PowerShell execution, or ScreenConnect service installation within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: World Cup Event Infrastructure – Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords flag 'phishing' as a primary attack vector against World Cup targets. suggestion.title: QR Code-Based Initial Access – World Cup Phishing

Correlate QR code redirects to known malware-hosting infrastructure or credential-capture sites. Monitor for unusual URL shortener services linking to typosquatted domains.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration & Access – World Cup Event Context
suggestion.rationale: Keywords list 'typosquatting' as an attack vector. Article discusses attack surface for a high-profile event. No detection use case for monitoring typosquatted FIFA/CONMEBOL domains or alerting on user access to domains mimicking legitimate World Cup infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domain registrations resembling FIFA, CONMEBOL, UEFA, stadium names, or ticket vendors (e.g., fifa-org.com, fifatickets-secure.com). Alert on internal user DNS queries/HTTP requests to typosquatted domains. Correlate with phishing email campaigns.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Deployment Against World Cup Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'wiper'. Article threat model includes 'ransomware groups' and 'critical infrastructure' targeting. No detection use case for destructive malware deployment despite clear wiper threat call-out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of known wiper families (NotPetya patterns, destructive disk-wiping utilities) on infrastructure networks spanning stadiums, broadcast facilities, ticketing platforms. Alert on bulk file-deletion operations, MBR/partition-table modification, or system shutdown commands targeting event infrastructure.

suggestion.title: State-Aligned Actor Reconnaissance of World Cup Venues
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords mention 'state-aligned actors' and threat model covers 'critical infrastructure.' No detection use case generated for reconnaissance (network scanning, OSINT collection, credential stuffing) against World Cup venues/broadcast infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous scanning activity targeting World Cup venues, broadcast centers, stadium networks. Monitor for bulk credential-stuffing attempts against ticketing platforms, broadcast systems, and event coordination infrastructure. Flag reconnaissance queries for publicly-exposed infrastructure APIs.

suggestion.title: Threat Group Activity – Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra, Razing Ursa
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly names four threat groups as actors in World Cup attack surface. Zero threat-group indicators, TTPs, or actor-specific detection use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Develop actor-specific detection rules for Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra, and Razing Ursa. Alert on infrastructure, tooling, TTPs, and indicators attributable to each group targeting World Cup stakeholders. Cross-reference with threat actor profiling (preferred targets, tools, phishing lures).

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes npm malware; pipeline missed foundational detection for post-install hook execution spawning unexpected processes or network calls during 'AI-generated npm malware' installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/node process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget during package install. Alert on post-install scripts reaching external hosts, particularly those with high network entropy or recently-registered domains. Correlate npm install timing with child process creation anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token Exposure in Package Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'accidentally exposes threat actor's private GitHub token'—this is a credential IOC that must surface detection for token patterns (ghp_* prefixes) in package code, manifests, or registry metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regex-match GitHub Personal Access Token patterns (ghp_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,255}) in package source, package.json, and npm publish transactions. Flag packages containing hardcoded credentials or environment variables exfiltrating secrets.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain Attack - Suspicious Package Metadata or Author Account Anomalies

Flag packages with excessive post-install script size or obfuscation patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via npm Post-Install C2 Communication

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP from npm or node processes to newly-registered or privacy-protected domains, especially correlating with package install events. Flag DNS queries for typosquatted domains or raw-IP communications from npm context.

suggestion.rationale: Leaked GitHub token represents compromised identity; pipeline should detect downstream use of exposed credentials for unauthorized registry access, package enumeration, or API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry and GitHub API logs for authentication using tokens associated with this incident or showing credential-stuffing patterns. Flag rapid package publishes, registry enumeration, or API calls from non-standard user-agents immediately post-exposure.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is the critical privilege-escalation vector after installation.

suggestion.title: APK Installation from Fake App Store Phishing Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article details distribution 'via phishing websites masquerading as streaming services and cryptocurrency mining platforms' redirecting to 'portals mimicking Google Play' where users download malicious APKs. This is initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clicks on phishing URLs that redirect to fake app store domains, followed by APK downloads and installation. Flag installations from non-Google Play sources, especially those matching known phishing templates.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture and Screen Recording for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'capturing screenshots' as an enabled capability, enabling credential theft and surveillance of user activity (e.g., OTP entry during banking sessions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect screenshot/screen-recording API calls from non-system and non-security applications. Correlate with network egress to non-standard destinations (Telegram C2, attacker infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Malware-as-a-Service Payload Generation and Telegram C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'sales are conducted in private Telegram channels' and describes the APK builder enabling threat actors to generate custom payloads without coding. This is command-and-control and resourcing activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Telegram API communications and Telegram-to-C2 exfiltration patterns. Flag accounts conducting repeated payload generation via the APK builder or suspicious Telegram group pivots from known malware distribution channels.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee accounts with anomalous login patterns post-social-engineering: failed MFA followed by successful logins from new geographies, help-desk password-reset requests from unusual contact channels, or MFA bypass indicators. suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Employee Account to IT Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker escalating from single employee account to 'limited portion of the Company's IT system,' indicating lateral movement by April 22 discovery date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when compromised employee account accesses sensitive systems outside normal access pattern (Mariner Society database, IT administration tools, file shares) within 24 hours. Monitor for inter-system authentication chains and privilege escalation initiated by compromised identity.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Extraction from Mariner Society Loyalty Database
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exfiltrated data 'contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program' including 'names, dates of birth, emails, genders...data relating to status' — 8.7M records total representing selective database targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT/EXPORT queries to Mariner Society database extracting >5K rows of combined PII fields (name, DOB, email, loyalty tier). Flag export operations by non-DBA roles, off-hours bulk queries, or unencrypted data staging for transfer.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration - 8.7M Records Stolen
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'bad actor illegally copied personal information' and later 'stolen' terabytes of corporate data. April 22 discovery suggests exfiltration occurred during April 14-22 window after initial detection of unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalously large data transfers from compromised account to external cloud storage, personal accounts, or FTP endpoints. Alert on creation of multi-GB archives (7zip, tar) in temp directories by non-administrative users followed by network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Undetected Secondary Access
suggestion.rationale: 12-day dwell time between April 10 breach and April 22 confirmation, with 8-day gap after April 14 detection, suggests attacker maintained persistent access despite initial containment attempt on April 14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of secondary user accounts by compromised employee during April 10-22 window. Alert on permission escalation events, account delegation changes, or multi-hour interactive sessions (RDP/SSH) from compromised identity to IT infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Blockchain RPC Endpoint Contact from Suspicious Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'takedown-resistant command and control' via BSC testnet smart contracts—implies compromised hosts must query blockchain RPCs. Pipeline missed detection for process outbound to blockchain infrastructure (BSC testnets typically 97.testnet.binance.org).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation followed by DNS queries or connections to known BSC testnet RPC endpoints (e.g., *.testnet.binance.org, testnet RPCs on port 8545). Flag non-browser, non-wallet processes (excludes legitimate MetaMask/exchanges). Blockchain C&C queries are infrequent but persistent.

suggestion.title: Smart Contract Deployment from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states actors deploy smart contracts for C&C; pipeline did not suggest detection for contract deployment transactions. Requires monitoring blockchain state or wallet audit logs for unexpected deployment activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag smart contract deployment transactions (high gas txs with contract creation opcodes) from compromised accounts or newly-active wallets. Cross-reference deployment wallet address against C2 beacon patterns and command execution timelines.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Explorer Access Followed by Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: C&C via smart contracts implies exfiltration of command state via blockchain reads; article describes command polling mechanism. Pipeline missed detection for process querying blockchain explorers or accessing web3 libraries alongside command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate http.get or curl calls to etherscan-like explorers / blockchair with subsequent PowerShell/cmd execution. Look for decode-then-execute patterns where decoded payload originates from contract read operations (indicate exfiltrated command strings).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Traffic to BSC Testnet Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly uses BSC Testnet (not mainnet); this testnet-specific targeting is unusual and evasion-oriented. Pipeline did not surface testnet IP/domain indicators or detection for unusual BSC testnet connectivity from enterprise networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from non-development systems to BSC testnet nodes (e.g., 97.testnet.binance.org, testnet RPC IP ranges). Testnet usage indicates intentional evasion (low visibility, low transaction cost, fewer monitoring endpoints).

suggestion.title: ClearFake Malware Process Creation and Module Load
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'ClearFake' as the threat actor. Pipeline produced no actor-specific IOCs or process signatures. Should extract known ClearFake delivery vectors, initial payloads, and behavior signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ClearFake-attributed PE signatures, known parent-child process chains (e.g., Office macros → obfuscated PowerShell → web3.js import), and suspicious library loads (e.g., web3.py, ethers.js, Infura SDK). Look for process cmdline arguments containing contract addresses or RPC URLs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Wallet Transaction Activity Preceding C&C Polling
suggestion.rationale: Smart contract C&C requires deployed contract and funded wallet. Article describes attacker infrastructure on blockchain. Pipeline should detect funded newly-created wallets transferring funds to contract addresses, which precedes C&C activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate enterprise wallet account access (if any) with fund transfers on testnet, or flag internal users registering new BSC accounts followed by fund transfers. Use blockchain explorers (Etherscan, BscScan testnet) to monitor contract creation timestamps and match to malware execution timelines.

suggestion.title: Gogs Authenticated RCE via Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'any authenticated user execute arbitrary code.' Pipeline omitted the execution phase entirely. This is the primary attack vector and must have a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gogs HTTP 200 response (successful auth) with subsequent process spawning from Gogs service (git, gogs, or other git-service PIDs). Baseline normal child processes; alert on shell invocation (bash, sh, python, perl) or network tools (curl, wget, nc) spawned post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Gogs HTTP Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE triggered by authenticated user action. Pipeline missed HTTP-layer exploitation detection. Requires monitoring for anomalous API sequences or webhook payloads following valid login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authenticated Gogs sessions for unusual POST/PUT requests to repository endpoints, webhook creation, or file-upload endpoints immediately preceding process execution on the host. Flag sequences like: auth_success → PUT .git/hooks → bash execution.

suggestion.title: Gogs Process Outbound Command-and-Control
suggestion.rationale: RCE commonly leads to callback or data exfiltration. Article title 'arbitrary code execution' implies attacker gains runtime control. Pipeline missed network-based post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections initiated by Gogs child processes (not git-daemon normal remotes). Alert on connections to non-repository hosts, external C2 infrastructure, or data-exfil destinations. Establish baseline of expected git remotes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Gogs Sensitive File Access Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution' — attackers typically read /etc/passwd, config files, SSH keys, or cloud-provider credentials. Pipeline produced no file-access detection.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE escalation is standard attack progression (Gogs may run unprivileged). Article severity is HIGH but does not explicitly bound to user context — should detect sudo, su, or capability-drop attempts.

suggestion.title: FIFA Domain Typosquatting Detection

suggestion.title: Fake Employment Portal Detection (FIFA Brand)

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Detection (Multi-Field Payload)

suggestion.title: Ghost Stadium Campaign Attribution (300-Site Infrastructure)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk FIFA-related domain registrations, hosting patterns, SSL certificates, and nameserver configurations to identify the 300-site infrastructure. Cross-reference with Ghost Stadium attributed IP ranges, WHOIS privacy patterns, and domain reseller profiles.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Business Document Masquerade

Correlate with sender domain reputation and recipient uncommonness.

suggestion.title: VIP Keylogger Process Execution and Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'VIP Keylogger' as the specific payload. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no collection-phase detection for this malware family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for VIP Keylogger process signatures, file hashes, or registry implants (likely HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run). Monitor parent-child relationships where Office processes spawn suspicious children and detect low-level keyboard hook API calls (SetWindowsHookEx).

suggestion.title: Malicious Office Document Execution Triggering Child Processes

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect winword.exe, excel.exe, or powerpnt.exe launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or writing executables to %Temp% within seconds of document open. Flag unusual process trees and file write patterns immediately post-macro or document load.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Key or Scheduled Task Post-Keylogger Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware deployment for ongoing credential theft, implying persistence mechanism. Pipeline failed to infer T1547.001 and similar persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce for new entries post-phishing. Detect scheduled tasks with suspicious names or commands created after Office document execution. Alert on .lnk files in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup.

suggestion.title: Marimo RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Marimo RCE' as initial access vector; pipeline produced no use case for detecting exploitation of this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from web-application worker processes (e.g., Marimo runtime), particularly PowerShell, cmd, or Python subprocess execution. Correlate with HTTP requests to known Marimo endpoints or version-detection probes. Marimo RCE typically triggers immediate command execution with high confidence if environment variables or working-directory paths match web-service context.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Command Execution for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article title and 'LLM Agent to Move' phrase describe attacker using LLM agents for pivoting; no use case generated for detecting agentic lateral-movement patterns (e.g., LLM generating shell commands, interacting with APIs, or accessing internal services programmatically).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of short-lived credential usage, rapid sequential API calls, or shell commands that follow LLM-generation patterns (token-shaped payloads, repeated retry logic, structured JSON in command arguments). Flag process chains where execution appears to be driven by external LLM inference (e.g., Python/Node.js subprocess calls with stdin piped from HTTP response or API output).

suggestion.title: Multi-Pivot Lateral Movement Sequencing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Four Pivots' in title; pipeline did not generate use case for detecting sequential intermediate-host compromise (hop-by-hop lateral movement pattern).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound sessions from compromised host A → B → C → D (4 hops in title), looking for process execution on intermediate hosts that immediately spawns outbound connections to the next target. High confidence signal: credential reuse across multiple unrelated hosts within short time window, or process execution anomalies (e.g., unusual services spawning network tools) on intermediate systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Access from Web-Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Move to Internal Database' as final impact; no use case for detecting database queries or connections originating from a compromised web-application process (Marimo).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SQL queries or database connection attempts from web-application worker processes or their child processes, especially to internal databases not normally accessed by that application. Flag new credentials or service accounts used, large volume queries (data exfiltration), or schema enumeration queries (reconnaissance).

suggestion.title: Python/Agentic Framework Abuse for Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Marimo is a Python-based framework; article describes LLM-agent-driven attack. Pipeline missed detection for loading/executing dynamically generated code within Python environments (agentic tool-use pattern).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python subprocess calls with exec(), eval(), or __import__() targeting dynamically constructed module names or loading .py/.pyc files from temp directories. Correlate with LLM-library imports (e.g., langchain, llamaindex, transformers) and stdin/API-sourced payloads. Alert if child process spawned by Python has network connectivity (indicators of agent fetch/execute loop).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Internal API/Service Enumeration by Compromised App
suggestion.rationale: Multi-pivot attack suggests reconnaissance of internal services; article title implies step-by-step progression. Pipeline did not generate use case for detecting internal service discovery from web-application context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network scanning, port enumeration, or DNS resolution of internal service names (databases, APIs, configuration servers) originating from web-application processes. High-volume DNS queries, sequential connection attempts to common database ports (3306, 5432, 1433), or HTTP OPTIONS/TRACE requests against internal services indicate reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Execution from Downloaded Recruiter Lure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'macOS Malware' and 'fake recruiter lures' as delivery vector. Pipeline failed to generate execution detection. Should trigger on unsigned/suspicious processes spawned by user interaction with recruitment-themed downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of unsigned Mach-O binaries or scripts spawned within user temp directories or ~/Downloads immediately after user opens recruiter-themed email attachments or links. Look for process names mimicking legitimate tools (e.g., 'pdf_reader', 'installer').

suggestion.title: Recruitment-Themed Phishing Link in Email Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'fake recruiter lures' — core initial access vector. Pipeline generated no email/phishing detection rules despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with recruitment/job offer themes sent to crypto sector targets with suspicious sender domains, new/free email providers masquerading as recruiters, or domains with low domain age (<30 days). Include URL sandboxing and attachment detonation triggers.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via LaunchDaemon Creation from Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies macOS malware but no persistence detection rule. Attackers establishing persistence via plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons is standard for macOS malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .plist files in LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon directories by non-admin processes, especially those writing executable paths or scripts. Correlate with process spawn from initial malware execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound C2 Traffic from macOS Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware was deployed but no network-based detection. Malware payload likely establishes command-and-control; pipeline missed this phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic from recently-compromised macOS hosts to dynamic/suspicious domains (high entropy subdomains, newly registered, bulletproof hosters). Baseline expected crypto firm legitimate tools and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Fake Recruiter Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Fake recruiter lures commonly harvest credentials (LinkedIn, corporate credentials, 2FA codes). Article emphasizes social engineering but no credential-theft detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed/unusual authentication attempts following recruitment lure distribution.
