Look for users entering credentials into phishing portals (via SIEM beacon callbacks or browser sandbox) or abnormal IdP login patterns from crypto firm employees post-email campaign.

suggestion.title: File Hash Indicator Match on Malware Sample
suggestion.rationale: Article title references macOS malware but no file hash IOCs were extracted. Pipeline should have surfaced malware sample hashes (MD5, SHA-256) for endpoint blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create hash-based detection rules matching known JINX-0164 malware samples. Trigger on file creation or execution matching malware hashes observed in article/threat feeds. Include code signing checks (likely unsigned or spoofed certs).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Suspicious Workflow Execution — Credential Theft Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Megalodon 'relies on GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this executable supply-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows referencing environment variables matching TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|CREDENTIAL immediately preceding network-bound commands (curl, wget, nc, python with requests). Escalate if workflow author is newly-added to repository or organization. Correlate workflow execution with unexpected identity provider events (new SSH keys, PAT creation).

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Bulk Malicious Commits — High-Volume Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '5,700 malicious commits pushed to the impacted repositories on May 18' and '5,500 GitHub repositories infected.' Pipeline failed to surface detection for coordinated, time-clustered commit injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repositories receiving >10 commits from single new/unfamiliar author within 24-hour window. Inspect commits for additions to .github/workflows/ or CI/CD configuration. Alert on same author injecting commits across >50 repositories in single day. Require code review approval for all workflow modifications.

suggestion.title: Domain Fronting via CDN — TLS SNI / HTTP Host Header Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Underminr attack that 'allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity.' This is explicit T1090.004 but generated zero detection hypotheses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when TLS SNI and HTTP Host headers resolve to different domains. High-fidelity: SNI points to major CDN (Akamai, Cloudflare, CloudFront, AWS CloudFront) while Host header points to non-CDN or internal-only domain. Validate against legitimate corporate CDN usage patterns. Correlate with subsequent data exfiltration or C2 communication.

suggestion.title: Credential Environment Variable Access — Pre-Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon payload 'designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets' implies process-level access to environment variables. Pipeline did not map credential-access detection despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET, AZURE_CREDENTIALS, API_KEY, or ARTIFACTORY_PASSWORD. Escalate if process subsequently executes curl, wget, or creates authenticated connections. GitHub Actions containers are high-risk contexts; baseline normal credential reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow File Modification — Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon injected malicious workflows; detection should specifically monitor .github/workflows/ modifications as persistence vector for future payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits modifying .github/workflows/*.yml files containing new steps with shell commands, base64-encoded payloads, or credential references. Require explicit code review approval for workflow changes. Flag if commits lack human review or merged by service accounts. Cross-reference against repository's CI/CD baseline.

suggestion.title: Repository Authorship Shift — Account Compromise or Takeover Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article notes '5,500 GitHub repositories infected' and '5,700 malicious commits' — indicates coordinated account compromise. Pipeline should surface authorship anomaly detection, not just commit content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repositories where commit authorship shifts to unfamiliar accounts without corresponding 2FA/MFA events or documented onboarding. Aggregate: flag when single author injects commits into >100 repositories in 24 hours. Cross-check GitHub organization membership changes and SSH key additions.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Suspension Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal'—suggests content discusses account enforcement actions; responsible disclosure workflows often track researcher account status changes as an indicator of policy shifts or disputes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for researcher account suspensions, visibility restrictions, or forced repository deletions on GitHub. Correlate timing with public disclosure announcements or CVE publication timelines to detect whether account actions target researcher coordinating vulnerability fixes.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Disclosure Timeline Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures'—suggests article discusses responsible disclosure policy violations or timing disputes. Detection should flag when public vulnerability details appear before vendor patch availability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor public disclosure channels (GitHub issues, security-focused forums, Twitter) for zero-day technical details posted before Microsoft advisory date. Correlate publication timing with researcher account status changes to detect policy enforcement triggers.

suggestion.title: Gogs Process Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article claims 'remote code execution' on Gogs servers. Any RCE vulnerability enables shell/command spawning from the compromised service. Title: 'Attackers Run Malicious Code on the Server Remotely'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gogs or git-related parent processes spawning shell interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe) with suspicious arguments or in unexpected contexts. RCE exploitation typically results in immediate command execution as the web service user.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Gogs Service Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability enables attacker-controlled outbound connections. Post-exploitation C2 communication would originate from Gogs process, not typical for legitimate git hosting operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound connections from Gogs service account, particularly to non-standard ports, FQDN patterns associated with C2, or external infrastructure. Baseline legitimate Gogs traffic (clone/pull repos, webhook notifications) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: HTTP 4xx/5xx Spike on Gogs Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of 0-day vulnerabilities often generates error responses during fuzzing/payload delivery attempts before successful code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained HTTP 400/401/403/500/502 error rates from specific source IPs against Gogs endpoints, particularly to authentication or API routes. Correlation with successful RCE indicators (process spawning, file writes) strengthens confidence.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Commit Activity from New Sources
suggestion.rationale: RCE foothold enables attacker to manipulate repositories: inject backdoors into code, alter commit history, or exfiltrate source. Article specifies 'code execution on server,' implying write access to repo storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual commits from system accounts, API tokens, or new author email domains to sensitive repositories. Cross-reference against known developer identities. Anomalies in commit frequency or file modification patterns (e.g., bulk changes to config files) suggest automated compromise.

suggestion.title: Gogs Authentication Bypass or Privilege Escalation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 0-day; likely involves authentication bypass or unintended privilege escalation to admin context for code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login events or privilege grants to system accounts, unauthenticated API calls succeeding, or session tokens being generated outside normal authentication flow. Correlate with subsequent process execution from Gogs service context.

suggestion.title: File Write to Gogs Binary or Hook Directory
suggestion.rationale: Persistence or privesc could involve overwriting Gogs binaries, git hooks, or startup scripts with attacker-controlled code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to Gogs installation directory, git hook paths, or service startup scripts from unexpected processes or users. Monitor for signed vs unsigned binary replacements or script injections in post-receive/pre-commit hooks.

suggestion.title: Git Rebase with Shell Metacharacter Injection in Branch Name
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious branch name to inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the Rebase before merging merge operation.' The --exec flag enables arbitrary command execution within git rebase context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git rebase/merge operations for branch names containing command injection metacharacters (--exec, --, |, &, ;, backticks, $()). Alert on Gogs merge API calls where branch naming deviates from standard alphanumeric patterns. Correlate with unexpected child process spawning under Gogs service account.

suggestion.title: Rapid User Registration Followed by Repository and Pull Request Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' and 'the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user,' indicating sequential account→repo→PR creation from single source within minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new user account creation immediately followed (within 5-10 minutes) by repository creation and pull request submission from same IP. Alert on sequences where new account enables rebase merge and creates PR with non-alphanumeric branch names in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Private Repository Access via Compromised Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE enables attackers to 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos)' as the Gogs service process user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs service account process for file system access to repository directories outside the authenticated user's normal scope. Detect bulk git operations reading private repo contents or API calls enumerating repos the service account should not access.

suggestion.title: Credential Material Extraction from Gogs Storage and Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation article describes 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' accessible to RCE process running as service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gogs service account process reading credential storage paths (.ssh directories, token databases, config files containing secrets, password hash files). Monitor for bulk reads of user home directories or access to Gogs internal credential stores from single process context.

suggestion.title: Repository Rebase Merge Setting Enablement on New Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings' and identifies this as a prerequisite for successful exploitation of the merge operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repository merge strategy changes from default (merge commit) to rebase merge, especially on recently-created repos or those with anomalous activity patterns. Alert when this setting is enabled by new user accounts immediately after repository creation.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Account Executing Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via git rebase --exec flag injection, which executes 'arbitrary code remotely as the Gogs server process user,' resulting in shell or command execution subprocess spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) or unusual command utilities (curl, wget, nc, ssh) spawned as child processes of the Gogs service account. Alert on any code execution utilities launched by Gogs service with network communication, credential access, or privilege escalation characteristics.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL. Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' No detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL loads from non-standard paths following execution of legitimate but unusual executables (HLS-related, installer variants). Correlation: process creation of known-good EXE → subsequent DLL load from same working directory or archive-relative path.

suggestion.title: Fake Video Player Update Prompt Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described: 'player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update. Clicking the link downloaded a ZIP archive.' Also mentions variant: 'fake browser crash page.' Pipeline missed initial access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spurious update prompts from video playback contexts (Flash/plugin simulants, browser crash pages) redirecting to executable or archive downloads. Correlate browser/player process displaying dialog → network connection to suspicious domain → ZIP/EXE download.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive with Legitimate Executable + DLL Pair
suggestion.rationale: Delivery structure preserved across campaigns: 'archive contained a legitimate executable... alongside a malicious DLL.' Article states prior domain was file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu, now urush1bar4[.]online. No archive analysis detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP archives from suspicious domains (urush1bar4[.]online, .ru/.top pirate sites) containing both a legitimate executable and a large DLL without matching digital signature or unexpected export tables. Hash archive contents for clustering.

suggestion.title: XMRig/SilentCryptoMiner Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies payload: 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and tags mention 'XMRig'. Article says 'library contained the logic for deploying the miner.' No miner-specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XMRig process launch (command-line patterns: --pool, --wallet, stratum+tcp connections). Correlate with illegitimate parents (injected/side-loaded DLL context, unsigned/unsigned-mismatched parent). Establish baseline for CPU/memory volatility post-execution.

suggestion.title: RAT Module Persistence and C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Watchdog and RAT agent components mentioned in section headers but no detection use cases for RAT callback or persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound connections from miner processes or from injected contexts to non-standard ports. Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS callbacks from processes spawned by DLL side-loading chains. Establish watchdog process spawning from parent (RAT 'Watchdog' component) with suspicious network activity.

suggestion.title: DLL Injection into Legitimate Process with Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device.' Persistence mechanism details not extracted; no detection for post-injection artifact creation (registry, scheduled task, startup folders).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-DLL injection, monitor for registry modifications under Run/RunOnce/Services, creation of scheduled tasks, or modifications to startup folders by processes that previously loaded DLLs from archive/side-load contexts. Correlate injection event with persistence artifact creation within seconds.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Go process spawning with encryption file extensions
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'self-propagating Go encryptor'—implies the malware binary is Go-compiled and spawns child processes to encrypt files. No detection logic was generated for this core behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Go-compiled executable (file properties, imports GOGO strings) spawning processes that open file handles to storage paths (shares, local drives) with sequential encryption writes. Flag when ≥100 distinct files are modified with matching bitwise patterns within 60s.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via go-based worm propagation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'self-propagating'—core mechanism involves worm-like lateral spread. No lateral movement detection use cases were generated despite this being the central threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go process attempting remote execution or network share access on multiple internal IPs within short window. Monitor for SMB writes of executable or script files followed by remote WMI/PSRemoting calls from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation preceding mass encryption
suggestion.rationale: No elevation-of-privilege indicators extracted despite 'Elevation of privilege' being listed in article metadata keywords. Ransomware requires elevated context to encrypt system files and disable recovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate UAC bypass, token impersonation, or credential dumping activity immediately preceding Go process execution with high entropy file writes to system-protected directories.

suggestion.title: Service or boot mechanism tampering for persistence
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware groups typically establish persistence to re-infect or prevent recovery. No persistence-phase detections were generated despite 'human-operated' tag implying multi-stage intrusions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services modifications, disabled Windows Defender/recovery services, and scheduled task creation by non-SYSTEM processes. Correlate to Go process PPID.

suggestion.title: Extortion note creation and resource discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'Extortion'—core post-encryption step. No detection for ransomware note file drops, README creation, or victim profiling activity (discovery/collection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of README.txt, RESTORE_FILES.txt, or similar extortion notes in root directories post-file-encryption. Correlate to preceding directory enumeration and file metadata exfiltration.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Remote Code Execution Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw' — this is the Initial Access phase. Pipeline generated no detection despite explicit vulnerability exploitation in headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS endpoints for HTTP POST requests to administrative endpoints with suspicious parameters or malformed payloads. Alert on 4xx responses followed by successful 200 responses within 60 seconds, indicating vulnerability scanning followed by exploitation. Correlate with process execution events on the EMS host.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution Post-EMS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Deploy Credential Stealer' — this is execution and credential access. Pipeline failed to map to T1555, T1003 or generate process-level detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiClient EMS services with suspicious properties: unsigned binaries, creation in temporary directories (%TEMP%, /tmp), or network connections immediately after process birth. Credential stealer signatures typically include registry/browser-profile enumeration.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from EMS to Managed Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: FortiClient EMS is a management server with credentials and visibility across endpoints. Article title implies compromise leads to further activity — pipeline did not suggest credential-access or lateral-movement detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connection initiation from FortiClient EMS servers to managed client endpoints. Alert on mass-enumeration of AD groups or LDAP queries from the EMS host requesting credential material (e.g., password hashes, service account creds).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Local Stores and Browsers
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies T1555 (Credentials from Password Stores) and/or T1003 (OS Credential Dumping) — zero use cases generated for post-execution credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing browser credential stores (%APPDATA%\Chrome, %APPDATA%\Firefox, etc.), Windows DPAPI keys, or running credential-dump tools (mimikatz, procdump targeting lsass). Monitor for SAM registry hive access or LSASS process dumps.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Installation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer deployments typically establish persistence (T1547, T1053). Pipeline generated zero suggestions for detecting scheduled tasks, registry startup keys, or service installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce keys, ServiceControl Manager service creation events, or scheduled task creation with suspicious binary paths. Correlate with EMS compromise timeline (within 24 hours of exploitation).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised EMS
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies harvested credentials will be exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline did not generate C2 or exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and outbound connections from FortiClient EMS to non-org infrastructure, especially to newly registered or low-reputation domains. Monitor for HTTPS/TLS traffic with certificate anomalies (self-signed, mismatched SNI) originating from the EMS host.

suggestion.title: PIN Interception or Brute-Force Against Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One Captured PIN' enables vault theft. Pipeline generated zero detection for credential capture mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed authentication attempts against password-manager services (Google Password Manager APIs, local auth libraries) followed by successful access. Flag processes requesting sensitive authentication data (PIN, passphrase) outside normal GCP/Google client contexts. Detect credential-guard bypass or lsass.exe reads on Windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Password Vault Enumeration or Bulk Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Steals Entire Google Password Manager Vault'—exfiltration implies enumeration/bulk-read of vault contents. No detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Google Password Manager APIs (Chrome sync endpoints, Gaia credential APIs) requesting >N credentials in single query or rapid sequential queries. Flag memory reads targeting credential structs in Chrome/Chromium process memory. Monitor unusual process access to ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Login\ Data or equivalent vault storage.

suggestion.title: VaultJacking Tooling or Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Attack is named 'VaultJacking'—should be tracked as known malware/exploit pattern. No IOCs or malware names extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If VaultJacking is known to ship as standalone tool or trojanized extension, detect executions or DLL loads matching signature. Monitor for Chrome extension installation from non-store sources or privilege escalation preceding password-vault access. Flag processes spawning with credentials-access-related parents (e.g., browser child → injected process).

suggestion.title: Google Password Manager Vault Export or Backup Theft
suggestion.rationale: 'Steals Entire Vault' implies bulk export or backup access—likely export to file, sync theft, or unencrypted backup. Zero use cases capture this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation in temp or user-writable directories matching password-manager backup patterns (.sqlite, .encrypted, ~vault~). Monitor Chrome sync encryption key access (Chromium KDF operations, LocalState reads). Flag exfiltration of vault data to external cloud storage, email, or C2.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass or Session Hijacking via Captured PIN
suggestion.rationale: Captured PIN used to unlock vault implies either direct auth bypass or session reuse. No detection for token replay or stolen-session exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect re-use of a PIN or authentication token multiple times (especially from different IPs/devices). Monitor for Google account unlock or vault-unlock calls using weak/static credentials after an initial successful auth. Flag unusual device fingerprints or geo-impossible logins for accounts whose password-manager was compromised.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction via Local System Access
suggestion.rationale: VaultJacking implies local privilege or code execution on victim machine to access vault. Pipeline missed local-extraction detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process dumps (procdump, taskmgr) or WinDBG/gdb sessions targeting browser processes. Monitor for DLL injection into Chrome/Chromium. Flag screen-capture, input-capture, or clipboard-monitor processes running with elevated privilege on systems where password manager was accessed.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Installation via Compromised Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates MDM cannot protect dev machines; article likely covers supply-chain attacks where compromised devs install backdoored packages. No UC generated despite this being core to MDM limitations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual package manager invocations (npm install, pip install, go get) with suspicious source repositories or from non-standard working directories. Correlate with user risk scores and check for unsigned packages or packages installed outside normal CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Configuration Files and Secret Stores
suggestion.rationale: MDM article should discuss theft of SSH keys, API tokens, and credentials stored locally since MDM focuses on device management, not local file encryption. Pipeline missed this core vulnerability vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube/config, .env files, or git credentials files. Correlate with unexpected process execution from non-dev contexts or elevated privileges accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Source Code Exfiltration via Unmonitored Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article likely explains how MDM cannot monitor developer tool abuse (git clone, git push to external repos, IDE clipboard operations). Pipeline generated no exfiltration-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large code repository transfers via git, rsync, or developer IDEs to non-corporate git remotes. Alert on IDE plugins performing bulk file uploads or unexpected archive creation from source directories.

suggestion.title: Build Pipeline Injection via Developer Machine Compromise
suggestion.rationale: MDM gaps likely include inability to prevent compromised devs from injecting malicious build steps. No supply-chain or execution-phase detection for CI/CD manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to build configuration files (Dockerfile, .github/workflows, Makefile, build.gradle) outside normal code review workflows. Flag commits that alter build scripts without corresponding merge requests or signed reviews.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via MDM Policy Circumvention on Developer Machines
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'what MDM can't protect'; article likely covers evasion techniques. Pipeline missed defense-evasion phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to disable or unload MDM agents, clear security tool logs, or modify endpoint detection software. Monitor for process execution with names/paths spoofing legitimate tools or living-off-the-land binary abuse (LOLBins) by developer accounts outside normal context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Abuse via Developer Access Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev machines often have broader access (code repos, CI/CD, cloud credentials) than typical endpoints. Pipeline generated no lateral-movement detection despite MDM's inability to protect these vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH tunneling or RDP connections from developer machines to production infrastructure. Alert on lateral movement using stolen developer credentials (git push to sensitive repos, cloud resource access from unusual IPs using dev keys).

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Anomalous URL Recommendations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states chatbot recommendations redirect users to malware sites. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or detection logic for this fundamental attack vector. Must detect when chatbot recommendation behavior deviates from baseline or recommends known-malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline chatbot domain recommendations by category and geography. Alert on recommendations to unregistered/high-entropy domains, domains on threat-intel blocklists, or sudden topic drift in recommendations. Correlate with user-reported malware infections.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Process Execution from Download Chain
suggestion.rationale: Users follow chatbot link → download malware → execution. Attack explicitly involves malware payload but pipeline surfaced no execution detection. 'Cryptojacking malware sites' implies malware binary/script delivery and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cryptocurrency-miner signatures (xmrig, monero-mine, stratum protocol) spawned from browser processes or temp directories. Correlate file downloads from external domains with process creation showing miner characteristics (high CPU, mining-pool DNS names).

suggestion.title: Sustained High-Volume Outbound Connections to Mining Pools
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking inherently maintains persistent C2 to mining pools. Article describes ongoing cryptojacking but pipeline extracted no network-based detection covering mining-pool callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained outbound connections to known Monero/mining pool infrastructure (mining.monero.cc, pools.supportxmr.com, nanopool). Alert on high-volume TCP streams on non-standard ports. Correlate with host CPU/memory elevation.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Prompt Injection or Control Plane Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Root-cause attack: chatbot logic was corrupted or hijacked to serve malicious recommendations. Article implies chatbot recommendations are not user-initiated but maliciously seeded. Pipeline missed detection for the compromise itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline chatbot API request/response patterns. Alert on injection-pattern keywords in inputs ('ignore previous instructions', 'do not follow your rules'). Monitor for statistical outliers in recommendation outputs: sudden shift in domains recommended, response format changes, policy bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: For sustained cryptojacking, malware must establish persistence beyond initial execution. Article implies ongoing compromise but pipeline extracted zero persistence-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Run keys, scheduled tasks, cron jobs, or systemd services that point to miner executables or script interpreters. Cross-reference suspicious scheduled-task arguments with known malware signatures. Alert on registry/file changes correlating with cryptominer process execution.

suggestion.title: Distributed Password Spraying Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' toward weak password choice, but pipeline generated no detection use case for this credential-access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts distributed across different user accounts originating from the same source IP within a short time window. Password spraying deliberately spreads attempts across accounts to evade lockout thresholds. Alert when a single source IP generates ≥10 failed logon attempts within 10 minutes targeting ≥5 unique accounts.

suggestion.title: cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin v2.3–v2.4.4 Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability is being actively exploited, and poses a risk for all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4'—version range is primary indicator for scope determination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory or cPanel plugin registry for LiteSpeed user-end plugin installations. Flag any instance with version ≥2.3 and ≤2.4.4. Cross-reference against patch logs to identify unpatched systems eligible for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble Function Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article provides forensic command verbatim: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs'—this is the exploitation signature per vendor advisory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs for pattern cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble. Alert on any occurrence; extract source IP for further correlation. Flag as exploitation attempt with high confidence.

suggestion.title: Non-Privileged User Execution with Root Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—describes privilege escalation from zero privileges to UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events in cPanel/WHM context where spawned process UID=0 but parent process UID ≠0 and parent is not a privileged sudoer. Cross-correlate with cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble detections on same timestamp to confirm exploitation followed by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity Correlation from CVE-2026-48172
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'examine the IPs in the list, determine if they are valid, and if not, block them... examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs'—forensic activity following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract source IPs from cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble pattern matches. For each IP, analyze subsequent activity in system logs within 5–60 minute window: new user creation, SSH/RDP activity, file access, lateral movement to other systems. Correlate with internal baseline to detect anomalous post-exploitation behavior.

suggestion.title: Timeline of Plugin Deployment and Exploitation Window
suggestion.rationale: Combined with version detection, establishes when system was vulnerable (v2.3–v2.4.4) and when exploitation could have occurred relative to patch deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For systems identified running v2.3–v2.4.4, extract plugin installation and patch dates from logs. Flag any cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble patterns occurring between vulnerability window opening (plugin version ≥2.3) and patch application. Prioritize investigation for systems with exploitation detections.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Asset Inventory - CVE-2026-45321 TanStack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and references asset-exposure template. Federal remediation deadline 2026-06-10. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite unambiguous guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all endpoints with TanStack installed via npm list, package-lock.json inspection, registry keys, and application manifests. Cross-reference installed versions against CVE-2026-45321 vulnerability timeline. Surface unpatched instances for immediate remediation against federal deadline.

suggestion.title: npm Supply-Chain Integrity - TanStack Malicious Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article core vector: 'malicious versions of the product to be published to the npm registry under a trusted identity.' This is T1195.001 (Compromise Software Dependencies), not public-facing exploitation. Pipeline missed supply-chain attack entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/update for TanStack during known-compromised window (post-2026-05-27). Alert on version downgrades, unexpected lateral installations, package hash mismatches vs. lockfile. Monitor for TanStack sourced from non-official npm sources or installation timing anomalies.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Behavioral Pattern - TanStack Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article names payload as 'credential-stealing malware.' Pipeline kill-chain reconstruction was empty; credential-access phase entirely absent. Post-installation exfiltration is critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-TanStack installation, hunt for credential-dumping activity (lsass dumps, DPAPI key access, SAM registry reads, cmdkey exports, browser stores). Correlate abnormal authentication patterns or lateral-movement from TanStack-executing processes. Monitor credential exfiltration via HTTP POST to external C2.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Deployment - Secondary Payload Post-TanStack
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'Known ransomware use.' Pipeline kill-chain empty; impact phase entirely missing. Ransomware follow-on should be explicitly hunted as documented attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For endpoints with confirmed TanStack compromise, hunt ransomware indicators: bulk file encryption, ransom note creation, shadow-copy deletion, MFT modifications, system registry hardening changes (DisableWER, SafeMode mods), file-extension mass-rename. Correlate with credential-exfiltration timeline to confirm attack sequence.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Installation or Update Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised extension fetched an obfuscated payload'. Malicious version requires installation; need baseline of normal Nx Console activity and alerting on installation post-incident discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console installation/update events via npm, package managers, or VS Code extension APIs. Correlate with process execution and outbound network activity; baseline normal Nx processes and flag deviations in network behavior or child process spawning post-installation.

suggestion.title: Credential File Discovery and Unauthorized Access Post-Nx Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk'. Detect unusual enumeration and reading of credential storage locations following Nx process activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console or spawned child processes accessing .ssh, .aws, .config, .gnupg, browser profile directories, and credential manager APIs in unusual sequence or volume. High severity if combined with process lineage confirmation and rapid successive reads.

suggestion.title: Memory-Based Credential Scraping via Nx-Spawned Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from...in memory'. Detect credential API calls or memory-reading attempts from Nx or child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx or Nx-child processes invoking credential enumeration APIs (Windows Credential Manager, DPAPI, Keychain) or loading memory-reading libraries. Flag if process chain originates from Nx and makes multiple rapid credential API calls in short time window.

suggestion.title: Post-Credential-Harvest Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential exfiltration via 'harvested credentials' and 'obfuscated payload'. Detect unexpected outbound connections following credential discovery activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential discovery events (file access, API calls) with subsequent network connections from Nx processes to non-whitelisted external IPs or ports. Flag unusual protocol usage or high-volume data transfer post-discovery.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 Vulnerable Nx Console Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-48027 and federal patch due date 2026-06-10. Detect unpatched instances via package metadata and manifest analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package manager logs and installed package manifests for Nx Console versions matching CVE-2026-48027 vulnerable range. Cross-reference against patch date; identify fleet exposure. Escalate if detected version also shows credential access or network anomalies.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Patch Compliance and Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-05-30' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template reference. No UC generated despite direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Daemon Tools Lite installations across endpoints. Cross-reference against patched versions. Flag endpoints with unpatched Daemon Tools Lite as exposure points for CVE-2026-8398 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Process Execution and Module Load Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Daemon Tools Lite as the attack surface and notes 'unspecified vulnerability' affecting integrity and confidentiality—behavioral monitoring is necessary when patch status unclear. Article emphasizes patch lag risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Daemon Tools Lite process execution and associated DLL loads. Baseline normal behavior, alert on unsigned modules or execution from abnormal paths. Correlate with asset-inventory patch status.

suggestion.title: Known Exploited Vulnerability—CVE-2026-8398 Remediation Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status (actively exploited in the wild) and 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Even if scanners report patched, verification is required. Federal due date provides auditability requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner queries for CVE-2026-8398 against all endpoints. Cross-validate reported patch status against software inventory and process execution logs. Flag discrepancies and create remediation tasking for patch lag >7 days past due date.

suggestion.title: API BOLA/IDOR Enumeration via Sequential ID Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage' are context-dependent vulns attackers exploit. These attacks manifest as sequential or predictable ID probing in API requests (e.g., /api/invoice/1001, /api/invoice/1002). Detection should alert on rapid ID enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints for sequential or near-sequential parameter manipulation targeting object IDs (invoice IDs, user IDs, tenant IDs) within short time windows. Correlate with non-200 responses indicating permission errors before successful access grants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authorization Probe Patterns on API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pentester methodology as 'recon, probe, observe, reason, escalate' and notes AI now automates this reasoning. Authorization probes appear as repeated requests to API endpoints with varying auth headers or identity parameters, followed by access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect machine-speed authorization boundary testing: rapid sequence of requests to the same endpoint with different user/tenant tokens, 40x responses, followed by escalated access attempts with modified parameters.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Resource Access Attempts via API
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'the gap between intended behavior and actual behavior' and mentions 'User A should not be able to read user B's invoice' as the core context-dependent vulnerability. Detection requires baseline of expected tenant isolation and alerting on violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls accessing objects where the tenant/owner ID in the response differs from the authenticated user's assigned tenant. Flag successful returns of cross-tenant data (2xx responses for out-of-scope objects).

suggestion.title: High-Volume API Reconnaissance (Machine-Speed Probing)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers now probe 'continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' This manifests as volumetric API requests from single source exceeding normal user behavior, testing surface coverage rather than extracting data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline API request rates per user/client. Alert on sustained request rates 10x+ normal, particularly when requests span diverse endpoints with varied HTTP methods and parameters, indicating systematic surface enumeration.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Chain: Failed Auth to Unauthed Resource Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path' including 'authentication bypasses.' Chains appear as rapid transitions from failed auth (401/403) to successful access to restricted resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts on an endpoint with subsequent 2xx successful responses from the same source within seconds, indicating auth bypass exploitation or race-condition window abuse.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Tool Abuse Following Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' RDP/TeamViewer spawned outside normal context is a critical pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on remote access tool launches by non-IT users or from unexpected parent processes. Monitor for RDP/TeamViewer connections to external IPs outside business hours. Flag credential re-use on RAT tools within minutes of phishing delivery.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Email Resulting in System Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' Correlate phishing email delivery with subsequent unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate external phishing email delivery with successful system authentication or RDP session within 1–4 hours. Flag when phishing targets IT-related job titles or shared mailboxes. Alert on file moves to removable media post-phishing.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB/External Storage Device Connection and Data Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' and 'insert a storage device into the victim's computer.' Core physical attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-whitelisted USB device connections, especially during off-hours or concurrent with suspicious user logins. Monitor for large file copies to removable media. Flag UNKNOWN_DEVICE identifiers in connection logs.

suggestion.title: Physical Security Breach – Credential Use During Visitor Access Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers, as possible indicators of an SRG attack.' Bridge physical and logical access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference building badge/entry logs with system login events. Alert on any credential use within 30 minutes of unknown visitor access. Flag admin console or sensitive file-server access during visitor windows.

suggestion.title: Ransom Extortion Email and Victim Contact Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email' and 'will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them into beginning ransom negotiations.' Post-breach communication is detectable and reportable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound ransom threat emails (typical TTP: payment demand, leak-site URL, deadline, data sample). Flag mass outbound calls or emails to client/employee lists post-data-exfil. Alert on attacker leak site mentions in threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted IT Helpdesk Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Fake domain access should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries for domains with edit-distance 1–3 from known corporate IT support FQDNs (e.g., acme-support.net vs acme.com). Alert on employee credential submission to unapproved support portals. Ingest typosquatted domain registrations.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API exception in JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory or Janino compiler stack trace
suggestion.rationale: Article names the vulnerable component: 'org.yamcs.algorithms.JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory' and 'Janino Expression Engine'. Failed exploitation attempts or warnings during compilation would appear in Yamcs logs with class names, method names, or Janino stack traces—direct IOC for attack attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Yamcs application logs for Janino compiler errors, ClassNotFoundException, or reflection warnings tied to algorithm evaluation. Also look for stack traces mentioning 'JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory' or 'org.codehaus.janino'. These indicate attempted code injection against the vulnerable component.

suggestion.title: Yamcs unauthenticated or low-privilege user triggering algorithm modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this'. If algorithm endpoints are patched without proper privilege enforcement, or if authentication is bypassed, log the user context and privilege level tied to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs authentication and authorization logs for algorithm-endpoint changes by users without ChangeMissionDatabase privilege, or requests that succeed despite auth failure. Cross-reference HTTP 403/401 responses followed by 200/201 on the same endpoint within a short window.

suggestion.title: Yamcs system properties or environment variable disclosure in process tree
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker will likely enumerate system configuration. Article describes privilege requirement; attacker will probe Yamcs properties (e.g., via 'env', 'printenv', Java properties dumping). Look for shell children of Yamcs running reconnaissance commands or reading config files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for bash/sh/python spawned from Java/Yamcs parent running commands like 'env', 'cat /etc/*, 'printenv', 'uname', 'whoami', 'id'. Also file-read events on Yamcs config directories (e.g., ~/yamcs/etc/, /opt/yamcs/etc/).

suggestion.title: Janino or Java reflection API invoked dynamically outside normal Yamcs operation
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability leverages Janino for dynamic compilation of user input. In normal operation, Janino is called during controlled algorithm registration/startup. Detecting unexpected reflection or Class.forName() calls with user-controlled input would catch exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Yamcs JVM is instrumented with APM or Java security manager, hunt for unexpected Class.forName(), Method.invoke(), or Janino ScriptEvaluator instantiation tied to HTTP request parameters. The vulnerability is dynamic compilation of algorithm text; detecting the compilation trigger at the API boundary would isolate exploitation.

suggestion.title: Yamcs database write to algorithm or mission-database tables outside normal deployment
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires modifying algorithm definitions in the mission database. Direct database writes to algorithm tables by users without db-admin context would indicate lateral compromise or supply-chain insertion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs mission database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.) for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on algorithm-related tables. Correlate with the user making the change: if a service account or non-admin user is modifying algorithms outside a deployment window, flag for investigation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Detection — World Cup Event Lure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly surface 'phishing' as attack vector. Article discusses World Cup as attack surface; phishing around major sporting events is a known initial-access pattern by the actors named (Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, etc.). No detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with World Cup 2026 or FIFA-themed subjects/bodies targeting organizations with World Cup ticket sales, broadcast, or infrastructure roles. Correlate clicks on suspicious links with indicators of credential harvesting or execution of follow-on payloads.

suggestion.title: Typosquat Domain Registration & Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'typosquatting' as an attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection use case despite clear mention in article metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and web traffic for typosquatted domains mimicking official FIFA, World Cup, or tournament infrastructure sites (e.g., fifa2026.net vs. fifa.com). Alert on rare/new domain registration by known threat actors; correlate with phishing campaigns and credential-theft infrastructure.

suggestion.title: QR Code-Based Malware Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'QR Codes.' World Cup materials (tickets, signage) frequently use QR codes; actors listed may distribute malicious QR codes to redirect or deliver payloads. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clicks/scans of QR codes embedded in phishing emails or trojanized World Cup marketing materials. Alert on redirect chains from decoded QR URLs to known malicious or newly-registered domains. Cross-reference with actor infrastructure indicators.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Staging & Execution — Infrastructure Impact
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'wiper' malware. World Cup infrastructure (streaming, ticketing, broadcast) is a critical target; wipers indicate intention to cause operational disruption. Pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases or use cases despite this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known wiper malware signatures and behavioral patterns (mass file deletion, MBR/boot sector writes, large-scale encryption/overwrite operations) on systems hosting World Cup event infrastructure, broadcast platforms, or ticketing backends. Alert on discovery of wiper staging code or execution of destructive disk operations.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Deployment Against World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'attack surface'; severity is 'high'; description mentions 'ransomware groups' and 'critical infrastructure' as threat actors. Despite this clear indication, zero ransom-related detection use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known ransomware execution patterns (rapid file encryption, ransom note creation, communications with C2 servers) targeting ticketing systems, broadcast infrastructure, and World Cup organizing committee networks. Alert on bulk file modification and deletion, esp. of backup/recovery media.

suggestion.title: State-Aligned Lateral Movement & Persistence Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article description explicitly mentions 'state-aligned actors' targeting critical infrastructure. No kill-chain phases for lateral movement, persistence, or defense evasion were reconstructed despite clear reference to advanced persistent threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for lateral movement patterns within World Cup infrastructure networks: pass-the-hash attacks, lateral RDP/SSH connections from compromised systems, scheduled task creation for persistence, and bulk account creation or privilege escalation. Alert on anomalous network flows between broadcast/ticketing segments and external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivered via npm package; no detection UC for post-install script execution or behavioral anomalies in package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations followed by execution of scripts from node_modules/.bin or package.json postinstall hooks. Flag if parent process is npm/npx and child spawns PowerShell, cmd, or bash with unusual command-line arguments (crypto mining, C2 callbacks, token exfiltration).

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token Exposure in Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Threat Actor's Private GitHub Token' accidentally exposed; pipeline missed detection for hardcoded credentials and token pattern matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search logs, environment variables, and process command-lines for GitHub token patterns (ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}, github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9]+). Correlate token appearance with outbound network connections to non-GitHub hosts or API calls from unexpected geolocations.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Token Usage from Suspicious Context
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of npm credentials enables malware publication and account takeover; no UC for abnormal npm registry operations or authentication from compromised infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm CLI operations (npm publish, npm unpublish, npm access) from IPs outside threat actor's typical infrastructure. Flag if npm registry authentication occurs in same session as token exfiltration or C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Signature / Checksum Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions AI-generated malware and accidental token exposure, implying payload obfuscation or dynamic generation; missing detection for unsigned or re-published packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installation where package.json checksum differs from npm registry baseline, or where published metadata (author, version history) shows sudden changes. Correlate with first-seen or low-prevalence packages in environment.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Environment Variable or Build Log
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly mentions token exposure; pipeline missed detection for accidental credential leakage in CI/CD logs, npm scripts, or build artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm script execution and CI/CD pipelines for environment variable dumps, console.log() of sensitive values, or HTTP requests containing GitHub/npm token patterns. Flag if credentials appear in readable process listings or temporary files.

suggestion.title: npm Account Creation or Permission Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor with stolen token could create accounts or escalate privileges on npm; no detection for account anomalies tied to malware publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference npm API audit logs (if available) with token use. Alert on account creation, permission grants (--add-user, --set-scope), or package transfer from accounts with no prior publishing history. Correlate with malicious package publication timestamps.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'it abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' Core privilege escalation and persistence mechanism in this malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-system APK requesting then being granted Accessibility Service permission. Monitor for process chains where newly-installed app gains accessibility access and immediately modifies system settings or installs additional payloads.

suggestion.title: Fake Google Play Portal Phishing and Typosquat Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' Domain impersonation is the entry vector for infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS/TLS connections to domains mimicking play.google.com (typosquats, lookalike TLDs). Block downloads of APK files from non-Google Play domains. Monitor for Google Play certificate pinning bypass or self-signed certs on Play-lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: APK Icon Hiding and Google Play Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'can disable Google Play, hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device, or prevent sleep mode.' Explicit defense-evasion and anti-removal techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK installation immediately followed by uninstall/disable of Google Play or Google Play Protect. Monitor for launcher configuration changes that remove app icons. Detect system calls to hide packages from launcher or disable system packages.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception and Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists capability: 'intercepting financial transactions' and 'stealing specific data.' Malware monitors banking/payment app activity for credential or transaction capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-banking APKs acquiring camera/screenshot permissions and network access simultaneously. Monitor for processes with hooks into banking app processes or certificate installation (MITM on payment traffic). Detect unusual file creation/exfiltration from banking app cache.

suggestion.title: Custom Phishing Campaign via Impersonated Government Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Researchers spotted BTMOB campaigns that used an Argentinian government agency as a lure' and 'malware platform helps operators generate custom, localized phishing lures.' Indicates MaaS-driven campaign customization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly-registered domains impersonating government agencies (Argentina focus) with geolocation/language targeting. Alert on rapid subdomain generation consistent with phishing-as-a-service payload customization. Monitor for campaign infrastructure (hosts, registrars) with high APK-drop volume.

suggestion.title: Remote Control and Command Execution via Builder-Generated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote control capabilities' provided by malware; 'APK builder...provides easy customization of the payload.' Implies C2 channel for arbitrary command execution post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK network beaconning to unknown C2 domains post-installation. Alert on process execution initiated from accessibility service or other elevated permission context. Correlate screenshot/data exfiltration with outbound HTTPS/port 443 traffic to attacker-controlled IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system.' No detections generated for initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing-delivery indicators (suspicious links/attachments to corporate email) within 48 hours preceding unusual employee account activity. Cross-reference with failed MFA attempts or impossible-travel logins. Flag if employee account shows login from unusual geography or time-of-day immediately after phishing detection window.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Customer PII Access from Compromised Employee Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bad actor illegally copied personal information' and data 'contained...names, dates of birth, email addresses, genders...relating to...Mariner Society loyalty program.' No detection for unauthorized database queries or loyalty program table access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SELECT queries or data export jobs against customer/loyalty databases (Mariner Society schema) originating from compromised employee account or non-standard query tools. Alert on multi-million-row result sets or bulk COPY/BCP operations outside normal ETL windows.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration to External Leak Sites Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: Timeline shows 8-day lag between compromise detection (April 14) and exfil discovery (April 22). No detection generated for data transfer or compression artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large outbound file transfers (>100 MB) from compromised employee account to non-business IPs or hosting providers. Monitor for 7z/RAR/ZIP compression of .csv or .sql files in temporary directories during off-hours, followed by deletion of source files and compression archives.

suggestion.title: Identify ShinyHunters Infrastructure Reuse Across Carnival and Salesforce Victims
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'ShinyHunters...has been targeting Salesforce customers...claiming to have stolen billions of records in the Salesloft Drift campaign and the Salesforce Aura data theft attacks.' Carnival uses same Salesforce infrastructure; pipeline missed threat-actor context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Carnival breach timeline (April 10) against known ShinyHunters Salesforce compromise tooling and C2 patterns from public disclosures (e.g., Salesloft/Drift infrastructure). Flag Carnival systems for connections to IP/domain overlaps from Salesforce Aura incident forensics.

suggestion.title: Monitor Delayed Discovery of Exfiltration (8-Day Detection Gap)
suggestion.rationale: Article: breach April 10, unauthorized activity identified April 14, data copying discovered April 22. Eight-day gap suggests attacker evaded alerts or deleted logs. Pipeline missed evasion/persistence indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion of audit logs or IIS/application logs within 24 hours of employee account compromise. Flag credential-creation events (domain accounts, service accounts) between April 14–22. Detect enablement of disabled audit categories or Event Log clearing via wevtutil.

suggestion.title: Carnival Recurring Breach Pattern - Flag Historical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes prior breaches: March 2020, June 2021, August 2020, December 2020 via 'threat actors gained access to Carnival employees' email accounts.' Pipeline did not flag repeat-victim risk or suggest hardening email infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Given four prior breaches of Carnival employee email, escalate alerting sensitivity on email compromise indicators. Monitor for phishing campaigns specifically targeting Carnival/Costa/P&O/Princess brands (nine subsidiary names). Detect reuse of employee lists leaked in 2020/2021 incidents as re-targeting vectors.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections to BSC Testnet RPC Endpoints from Suspicious Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'ClearFake Uses BSC Testnet Smart Contracts for...Command and Control' — pipeline ignored the C2 mechanism entirely. Should detect connections to testnet-rpc.bsc.org, 97-rpc.bscscan.com, or hardcoded testnet node IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes initiating HTTPS POST to BSC Testnet RPC endpoints with Web3 JSON-RPC payloads (eth_call, eth_sendTransaction, eth_blockNumber). Alert if source is non-financial executable, originates from user %TEMP%, or runs with unsigned/invalid signature. Testnet communication from endpoints is rare and suspicious.

suggestion.title: ClearFake Malware Execution and Initial Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article names the threat actor/malware family ('ClearFake') but pipeline extracted zero indicators of malware execution, file creation, or process spawning. Missing entire execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClearFake execution through process artifacts: code signing anomalies, atypical child processes, suspicious DLL loads (especially crypto/networking libraries). Correlate with phishing delivery or drive-by download events. Process behavior after execution should show rapid blockchain RPC enumeration or connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Smart Contract Interaction via HTTP/HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: 'Uses BSC Testnet Smart Contracts' — article establishes contract interaction as primary C2 mechanism but pipeline did not generate detection for contract function calls, ABI encoding in HTTP payloads, or contract address patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing contract addresses (0x... hex strings) or Web3.js/Ethers.js patterns in payloads. Flag if non-development processes query blockchain explorers (etherscan, bscscan). Detect contract state-change transactions (sendTransaction) from malware-associated processes or anomalous source users.

suggestion.title: Testnet Infrastructure for Evasion and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'takedown-resistant' design via testnet — pipeline missed the defense-evasion and persistence angle. Testnet infrastructure is harder to identify and takedown than traditional domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect use of testnet RPC endpoints by non-development users and processes. Testnet communication is rare in typical enterprise traffic; any endpoint using BSC Testnet identifiers (97, testnet- prefixes) should be flagged for behavioral investigation. Correlate with known testnet node operators and blockchain infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet or Token Transfers as C2 Signaling
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain-based C2 often uses token transfers or contract state as dead-drop channels for commands. Article structure suggests this but pipeline generated zero indicators for this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes querying contract event logs (getLogs, eth_getEvents) or polling specific contract addresses repeatedly. Token transfer events or state changes on suspicious contracts can serve as command exfiltration. Establish baseline of legitimate crypto operations and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: DNS Enumeration of Blockchain Infrastructure Providers
suggestion.rationale: Malware using blockchain C2 typically discovers and enumerates RPC providers before connecting. Article does not detail this but it is standard reconnaissance for this attack pattern. Pipeline should anticipate it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of DNS queries for blockchain RPC providers (infura, alchemy, BSC nodes) or resolver services from suspicious processes. Rapid enumeration of multiple RPC endpoints suggests reconnaissance. Correlate with subsequent connections to those endpoints.

suggestion.title: Gogs Process Spawning Unexpected Shell or Interpreter Children
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'execute arbitrary code'—core RCE mechanism. Pipeline generated zero detection for anomalous process creation, the primary forensic signal of code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gogs process spawning bash, sh, powershell, cmd, or interpreters (python, perl) outside known Git hook contexts. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes per Gogs deployment; flag deviations with short parent-exec time deltas.

suggestion.title: Successful Gogs Authentication Followed by Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'any authenticated user'—attack requires valid credentials then RCE. Pipeline missed auth-execution correlation specific to Gogs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Gogs authentication success with process spawning by Gogs service within 60 seconds. Flag if child process is high-risk: curl, wget, netcat, encoding tools (base64, xxd), reverse shell patterns, or suspicious file access.

suggestion.title: Git Hook Creation or Modification via Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Common Gogs RCE vector exploits git post-receive or pre-receive hooks. Article doesn't name the attack vector but execution path likely involves hook injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation, modification, or execution of files under .git/hooks/* within Gogs-managed repositories. Flag hooks containing shell code, script interpreters, network commands, or Base64/hex encoding.

suggestion.title: Gogs Accessing Privileged or Out-of-Repository Filesystem Locations
suggestion.rationale: RCE by definition grants attacker filesystem access beyond repository scope. 'Arbitrary code' implies /etc, /tmp, credential stores, or system directories become readable/writable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Gogs process filesystem access patterns. Alert on reads/writes to /etc/*, /root/*, /tmp/*, /var/log/*, Windows Registry HKLM/HKCU outside Git data paths, or credential stores (SSH keys, .aws, .kube).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake domains impersonate fifa.com, but rely on minor spelling changes that users are likely to miss, such as fiffa[.]com' and alternative TLDs (.org, .xyz, .live, .sale). No detection rule captures this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations and DNS queries for FIFA/World Cup-related keywords with character substitutions (double letters, homoglyphs, adjacent-key typos). Alert on registrations of typosquatted domains within 30 days of tournament start (June 2026) across suspicious TLDs.

suggestion.title: Fake FIFA Employment Portal Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake employment portals like jobs-fifa[.]com or fifa-hiring[.]com' collect victim data. No rule for employment portal phishing pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to domains matching fifa-hiring* or jobs-fifa* patterns, particularly POST requests submitting form data (resume uploads, personal details) from non-FIFA IP space. Correlate with credential submission patterns.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign Detection via Ad Platform Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp' but no detection covers ad infrastructure abuse for FIFA fraud.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Ads and Facebook Ads API logs for campaigns targeting FIFA/World Cup keywords with links to suspicious domains. Flag ads with high click-to-conversion fraud ratios or linking to newly registered typosquatted domains.

suggestion.title: Premium FIFA Ticket Portal Fraud (Ghost Stadium Variant)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Ghost Stadium... uses more than 300 phishing sites, clones of the real FIFA portal, for premium ticket fraud' as specific campaign. No rule maps Ghost Stadium infrastructure or ticket portal clones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to domains hosting FIFA-cloned ticket portals (visual similarity + payment form presence). Flag payment card submissions to non-FIFA merchant accounts. Correlate requests from geographies outside official ticket distribution regions.

suggestion.title: Fake Merchandise and Streaming Service Fraud Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Bitdefender 'observed fraudulent activity... with fake merchandise, kits and collectibles, streaming services, and Panini sticker offers' but no use case addresses fake goods/service fraud pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor e-commerce transaction logs for World Cup merchandise sales from non-official vendors (check WHOIS, merchant registration). Flag payment processing to accounts registered in high-fraud jurisdictions targeting FIFA/World Cup keywords.

suggestion.title: Personal Information Harvesting from Fake FIFA Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'many of the fraudulent websites collect... names, physical and email addresses, phone numbers, banking/payment details, which could be used to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft' but no detection for form-based PII exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to typosquatted FIFA domains containing PII patterns (bank account numbers, full names + SSN, email + phone combos). Alert on bulk exfiltration of structured identity data (CSV/JSON serialization) from fake portals.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing Archive Delivery via Cloud Links
suggestion.rationale: PhantomMail campaign: 'Spear-phishing emails delivering malicious ZIP/RAR archives via Google Drive and 4sync links, using decoy PDFs or fake errors.' No detection UC generated for this primary initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails with archive attachments or cloud-hosted links claiming urgent system errors; detect extraction and execution of malware-bearing archives from Google Drive/4sync. Flag emails impersonating Ukrainian government, energy, or telecom entities.

suggestion.title: Fake CAPTCHA Command Injection (Zoom/LAPAS/Cloudflare Impersonation)
suggestion.rationale: PhantomClick: 'Fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix pages disguised as Zoom and LAPAS sites trick victims into running self-infecting commands through fake Cloudflare verification prompts.' Distinct from standard phishing—command execution following fraudulent verification pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect visits to domains impersonating Zoom/LAPAS/Cloudflare followed by suspicious PowerShell, cmd.exe, or script execution. Alert on browser→command-line execution chains originating from phishing-like pages.

suggestion.title: PowerShell RAT Credential Theft and Exfiltration (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay)
suggestion.rationale: Article names LegionRelay/PhantomRelay with explicit capabilities: 'file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup.' No detection UC for PowerShell RAT behavioral package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell executing dynamic script loading (Invoke-Expression, IEX), spawning credential access utilities, calling screenshot/screen capture APIs, accessing Telegram/WhatsApp process memory, or opening RDP sessions.
