Monitor for Telegram/WhatsApp protocol exfiltration over C2 channels.

suggestion.title: Android Spyware Data Collection (FallSpy Indicators)
suggestion.rationale: FallSpy explicitly collects 'contact lists, call logs, device and network information, location data, media files, and SIM information' on PrincessClub/Nebo campaigns. No mobile-tier detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FallSpy or similar via suspicious permission grants (contacts, call logs, media library, location, SIM data) without user interaction, bulk data access patterns, or exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. Flag impersonated Ukrainian adult/dating sites as infection vectors.

suggestion.title: WebRTC-based Audio/Video Capture (Live Call Surveillance)
suggestion.rationale: PrincessClub 'added WebRTC-based live calls that could capture the victim's audio/video.' Specific real-time surveillance capability distinct from file-based collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized WebRTC session establishment from FallSpy or Windows RATs; monitor for real-time microphone/camera access without user consent; identify WebRTC media streams to C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Custom LLM-Assisted Obfuscator Detection (LOOKVALPS, LOOKVALJS, DAYLIGHT, TEASOUP)
suggestion.rationale: Article names four 'custom obfuscators likely developed with LLM assistance' but provides no detection indicators or signature guidance. Defense evasion layer not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Develop YARA signatures or hash-based detection for LOOKVALPS, LOOKVALJS, DAYLIGHT, TEASOUP obfuscators. Monitor for PowerShell de-obfuscation patterns (repeated character replacement, Base64 decoding) followed by dynamic code execution.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivering Malware via Business Document Lure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Phishing Emails Masquerading as Business Documents' — core initial-access vector that must trigger email-based delivery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with spoofed business document themes (invoices, POs, payroll) targeting finance/HR users. Alert when macro-enabled Office attachments or executable links follow sender domain homoglyph patterns. Correlate with subsequent child-process execution from Office.

suggestion.title: Keystroke Logger Process Execution and Input Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names VIP Keylogger and describes keystroke capture as the attack objective — T1056.001 is the direct technique to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SetWindowsHookEx API calls with WH_KEYBOARD or WH_KEYBOARD_LL handlers from unsigned or untrusted processes. Flag processes that load user32.dll and establish input hooks. Correlate with file write activity to suspicious paths matching keylogger staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Office Macro Execution to Keylogger Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Phishing 'business documents' implies macro-enabled files; malware deployment follows user opening document — bridges initial_access and execution phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell, cmd.exe, or wscript.exe spawned as child of Office processes (winword.exe, excel.exe). Alert when Office apps write to AppData\Local\Temp or create unsigned executables. Monitor WMI event subscriptions or scheduled tasks created via macro context.

suggestion.title: Keylogger Persistence via Registry Run Keys
suggestion.rationale: Article implies keylogger must persist across reboots — standard technique is registry Run key modification for VIP Keylogger family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKLM equivalent with unsigned executables or suspicious paths. Correlate registry modification timing with document-execution context. Flag processes writing simultaneous registry and executable file operations.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Keystroke Collection and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Keylogger's utility depends on credential exfiltration post-collection; article implies data theft is attack objective, requiring C2 communication detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound connections from keylogger-associated processes, especially on non-standard ports (>1024, <65535) to external IPs. Alert on encrypted HTTPS traffic with suspicious SNI or certificate anomalies. Correlate network timing with high keystroke-buffer flush patterns.

suggestion.title: Marimo RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Use LLM Agent to Move From Marimo RCE.' Marimo is the explicit initial access vector; pipeline extracted zero indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Marimo endpoints with code execution payloads. Correlate with Python interpreter spawns from web server processes (unexpected subprocess from gunicorn/uvicorn child). Check for Marimo versions ≤0.8.x in vulnerability databases.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Post-Exploitation Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'LLM Agent to Move From Marimo RCE.' This is the novel attack chain; pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python/Node.js interpreter instantiation with LLM SDK imports (anthropic, openai, langchain). Flag environment variables containing OPENAI_API_KEY, Anthropic tokens, or model endpoints. Alert on LLM API calls originating from compromised process lineage.

suggestion.title: Four-Hop Lateral Movement Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Four Pivots' for lateral movement; pipeline reconstructed zero kill-chain phases or lateral techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 4+ distinct lateral hops in parent-child process chain or credential reuse within 2-hour window post-Marimo compromise. Flag tools (psexec, WinRM, SSH) spawned from non-standard contexts. Correlate remote execution with Marimo process tree.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Internal Database Access Post-Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Article objective: 'Move From Marimo RCE to Internal Database in Four Pivots.' Database access is the final impact; no collection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database login anomalies: service account logins from internal compromised hosts in sequence, database login timestamps within 90 minutes of Marimo RCE detection, unusual SELECT * or bulk export queries, privilege-escalation ALTER statements.

suggestion.title: LLM-Driven Network Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: LLM agents executing lateral movement implies automated discovery; article describes active multi-hop pivoting requiring target enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid system enumeration (net view, Get-ADUser, whoami /all, uname -a) spawned from LLM process tree. Flag LDAP queries from non-domain-joined processes. Alert on sequential host pings/port scans from single lateral-movement source.

suggestion.title: LLM Prompt Injection for Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: LLM agent described as moving laterally suggests prompt injection or agentic attack; no defense-evasion or C2 patterns captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for indirect command execution: Python/Node.js interpreters spawning shell commands via subprocess/exec with unusual argument encoding (base64, hex). Flag cases where LLM output directly becomes system command. Alert on unusual subprocess parent chains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email from Unknown Recruiter with Malicious Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'fake recruiter lures' as initial attack vector—pipeline must detect inbound emails spoofing or impersonating legitimate recruiters, targeting crypto sector, carrying macOS-executable attachments (DMG, PKG).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails claiming recruitment authority sent to cryptocurrency-sector targets, especially from newly-registered or spoofed recruiter domains. Flag messages with macOS-executable attachments, shortened URLs, or requests to enable macros. Cross-check sender domain registration date and reputation scoring.

suggestion.title: macOS Unsigned Binary Execution from Download or Temp Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article references deployment of 'macOS malware'—detection must cover execution of unsigned or Gatekeeper-bypassed binaries from non-standard staging locations typical of post-delivery exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned, ad-hoc signed, or revoked-certificate macOS executables launched from /tmp, /var/tmp, ~/Downloads, ~/Library/Caches, or quarantine directories. Include parent process (e.g., Archive Utility, Mail), code signature status, and first-execution timestamp.

suggestion.title: Persistent Outbound Beaconing from macOS to Unknown C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malware campaigns mandate command-and-control; article describes malware payload but pipeline produced no network IOCs or behavioral signatures for C2 communication or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated outbound connections from compromised macOS endpoints to rare or newly-registered domains, non-standard ports (8080, 8443, 9999, 4444), or IPs with low legitimate traffic volume. Flag user-agent strings matching known malware families, TLS certificate anomalies, or DNS query patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Cryptocurrency Employee Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Targeting cryptocurrency firms implies theft of sensitive credentials—pipeline should flag post-compromise enumeration, password dumping from macOS Keychain, and lateral movement using stolen identities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful macOS compromise events with abnormal subsequent logons (impossible travel, off-hours, new source IPs, unusual resource access). Flag Keychain dump attempts via security command-line tools, creation of new local admin accounts, and VPN/SSH authentication from new locations.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron Installation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation staging on macOS requires persistence—pipeline failed to propose detections for LaunchAgent plist creation, cron job injection, or other native macOS persistence mechanisms exploited by malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchAgents, cron entries in /var/spool/cron, and hidden process startup items. Alert on suspicious executable paths, obfuscated arguments, or modifications by non-admin users. Baseline legitimate agents and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Bulk Exfiltration of Cryptocurrency Wallets, Private Keys, or Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Attack context (crypto firms) implies high-value data theft—pipeline must detect staging, compression, and transfer of wallet files (.key, .pem, .wallet JSON), credential databases, or transaction histories to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file-system enumeration of home directories, large reads from sensitive paths (~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, ~/Wallets, ~/Library/Application Support/cryptocurrency-apps), file archiving (zip, tar, 7z), and rapid transfers to cloud storage or external IPs. Include file type indicators (.key, .pem, .json, .wallet).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection via Malicious Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets. The workflows were injected through over 5,700 malicious commits.' This is the primary Megalodon vector—clear attack step requiring detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .github/workflows/*.yml file modifications in Git repositories. Alert on new workflow steps using 'run:' or 'script:' to access secrets, env vars, or exfiltrate credentials. Cross-reference commit author against maintainer baseline; flag commits by low-reputation or dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Credential and API Key Exfiltration in CI/CD Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens' combined with Megalodon commits injecting workflows. Direct exfiltration channel through compromised CI/CD execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions job logs dumping environment variables, secrets, or tokens to stdout/stderr (visible in logs). Monitor for exfiltration of GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or other credential env vars to external HTTP endpoints. Correlate suspicious workflow-initiated network outbound to credential patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Commit Activity - Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '5,700 malicious commits pushed to the impacted repositories on May 18' across '5,500 GitHub repositories.' Coordinated high-volume commit campaign suggests account compromise or GitHub App exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on burst of commits from single or related accounts within narrow time window (May 18 pattern). Monitor for commits modifying CI/CD config (.github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, .circleci/config.yml) without corresponding pull requests. Flag commits by accounts with no prior contribution history to target repo.

suggestion.title: Domain-Fronting Attack via Content Delivery Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Underminr domain-fronting attack allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity.' Explicit defense-evasion technique targeting CDN/trusted domain abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS SNI hostname mismatch with HTTP Host header (SNI=cdn.example.com, Host=attacker.com). Monitor CDN/trusted-domain outbound connections with unusual destination IP geolocation or ASN. Alert on requests with spoofed Referer/User-Agent headers to bypass reputation filters on trusted domains.

suggestion.title: Intentional Credential Publication to Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a vast trove of other agency secrets on a public GitHub account.' Insider threat vector with credential exposure outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan public repository commits for AWS credential format patterns, GCP service account keys, private SSH keys, API tokens. Alert on repos created by or pushed to by privileged accounts (e.g., contractor, government email domains). Monitor for rapid publication followed by rapid deletion attempts (remediation indication).

suggestion.title: Hosting Infrastructure Registration Timed to Geopolitical Events
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Web hosting company established on Feb. 10, 2022, weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine. The infrastructure was allegedly used to support cyber attacks, disinformation campaigns, and sanctions evasion linked to Russia.' Temporal correlation between registration and geopolitical incidents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain/ASN registration patterns proximate to major geopolitical events, sanctions announcements, or military operations. Alert on hosting providers with history of abuse, minimal WHOIS information, or privacy masking. Correlate C2 traffic to newly-registered IP space; cross-reference against threat feeds for Russia-attributed infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GitHub Researcher Account Suspension or Bulk Access Revocation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal.' Pipeline failed to surface any detection for account suspension activity or credential revocation patterns targeting security researchers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk or targeted GitHub organization/repository access removals targeting users with security researcher profiles. Monitor for administrator actions that suspend multiple accounts in temporal clusters, or failed authentication attempts by previously active researcher accounts post-suspension.

suggestion.title: Public Zero-Day Proof-of-Concept Repository Activity
suggestion.rationale: Core of incident is 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures'—pipeline should detect rapid repository creation, PoC code commits, or release publication on GitHub within days of unpatched vulnerability discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub repository creation followed by exploitation code commit; cross-reference against CVE disclosure dates to detect premature PoC release. Monitor for mass cloning or forking of newly published exploit repositories.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Security Incident Response / Policy Enforcement Announcement
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates Microsoft public statement slamming disclosure practices—suggests formal security policy response, coordinated communication, or escalation that should trigger incident-context detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference timeline of public zero-day PoC releases with Microsoft security advisories and statement dates. Detect patterns where Microsoft accelerates patch release or CVE severity elevation in response to public disclosure pressure.

suggestion.title: Gogs 0-Day Exploitation Attempt—Malicious HTTP POST to API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Attackers Run Malicious Code...Remotely'—RCE is triggered via HTTP requests. Without article body, cannot pinpoint vulnerable endpoints, but exploitation chain necessarily begins with a crafted API request to Gogs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to Gogs API and repository endpoints (/api/*, /repos/*, git push/pull operations). Flag requests containing shell metacharacters, base64-encoded payloads, or command execution patterns. Baseline: Gogs should receive JSON and git protocol traffic; anything else is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Gogs RCE Post-Exploitation—Unexpected Child Process from Service
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Execute Malicious Code on the Server'—post-compromise execution manifests as process spawning from the Gogs daemon. Any shell interpreter (bash, sh, powershell) spawned as a child of Gogs is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any child process spawned by Gogs service that is a system shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) or direct invocation of system interpreters. Baseline: Gogs spawns only git, ssh, and standard repository management tasks. Any deviation is high-confidence indicator of post-exploitation code execution.

suggestion.title: Gogs RCE Post-Exploitation—Reverse Shell or C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: 0-day RCE typically results in attacker establishing persistent shell access. Article confirms code execution capability—attacker likely establishes reverse shell or C2 callback to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Gogs process/service account to non-repository-related destinations (non-GitHub, non-GitLab, non-standard git mirrors). Flag persistent connections on non-standard ports (not 22, 80, 443 for git operations). Correlate with child process creation of bash/powershell.

suggestion.title: Gogs RCE—Suspicious File Creation in Repo Directories
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation often includes writing web shells, backdoors, or payloads to accessible repository paths for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification in Gogs repository directories by the Gogs service account with unexpected file types (executable, script, configuration with altered permissions). Flag .sh, .exe, .bat, .ps1, or config files written to web-accessible directories.

suggestion.title: Argument Injection in Git Rebase via Branch Name
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'malicious branch name to inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the Rebase before merging merge operation.' This is the core exploitation vector and requires detection logic for suspicious characters or git flags in branch/PR names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs pull request creation and rebase merge operations for branch names containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), --), git command flags (--exec, --quiet, --force), or suspicious encoding. Flag any rebase merge on branches created by low-privilege users with recent account creation.

suggestion.title: Account Creation Followed by Repository Creation and Rebase Merge
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance...From there, enabling rebase merging is a single toggle in settings, and the entire exploit chain can be operated without interaction from any other user.' This behavioral chain is specific to this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences: account creation → repository creation → immediate rebase merge configuration enabled → pull request with rebase merge all by the same user within minutes/hours. Flag especially if branch name contains suspicious characters.

suggestion.title: Git Process Spawning Shell Interpreter via Rebase
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'execute arbitrary code remotely as the Gogs server process user' by injecting --exec into git rebase, which spawns shell commands. Detection must catch unexpected child processes under git processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git processes (specifically git-rebase, git-merge) for spawning unexpected child processes: bash, sh, cmd, powershell, or other interpreters. Alert on any shell execution as a child of git operations, especially from Gogs service account or web server user context.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Gogs Default Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' and 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos).' RCE as service user enables access to stored credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise: detect enumeration of Gogs credential storage (./data/ssh/*, ./data/sessions/, database files), access to .ssh directories, scanning of API token databases, or attempted reads of /etc/shadow or host SSH keys from Gogs process context.

suggestion.title: Gogs Server with Open Registration and Unlimited Repo Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false) and no limit on repository creation (MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = -1), an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance.' Configuration assessment/audit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Gogs app.ini or runtime config for DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false and MAX_CREATION_LIMIT ≤ 0 (unlimited). Alert on Gogs instances with both settings enabled. Correlate with network exposure (Shodan/Censys) to identify vulnerable Internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'pivot to other network-accessible systems' and 'modify any hosted repository's code.' Post-RCE access enables supply-chain attacks and lateral movement through repository contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious commits/code changes merged immediately after repository access, especially if deployed to other systems. Monitor for repository clones/access from compromised Gogs server to other internal systems (git clone to internal IPs, SSH key usage for lateral movement).

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' No UC covers detection of archive extraction + paired executable/DLL execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extraction of archives containing both legitimate executables and DLLs sharing suspicious names (e.g., HLS Installer + unknown DLL in same extract). Detect execution of known-benign EXE followed by unusual DLL loads from temp/extract paths, especially with injection indicators (WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread).

suggestion.title: Fake Plugin Update Prompt Download Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue. Clicking the link downloaded a ZIP archive.' Pipeline missed initial access delivery vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track browser downloads of ZIP archives from suspicious domains after video player warnings. Flag sequential pattern: video player prompt + URL click + ZIP file retrieval. Correlate with known piracy site ASNs. Monitor for archive files named with installer/player keywords (HLS, Installer, Update, Plugin).

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner XMRig Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and XMRig miner deployment, but no detection logic for cryptominer execution patterns was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect XMRig or SilentCryptoMiner by process creation with mining pool domains, unusual system resource consumption (sustained CPU >70% from unprivileged process), or known cryptominer signatures. Correlate with DLL side-loading events from same process lineage. Monitor for mining pool communication post-installation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Extraction from Piracy Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attack pattern: 'archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL.' This specific indicator pattern (paired exe+dll) is not in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect extraction or download of archives from known piracy domains or dynamic piracy site infrastructure. Alert on extraction containing both .exe and .dll files with mismatched or suspicious signatures. Cross-correlate with user browsing history to piracy sites immediately preceding downloads.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Malicious DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states DLL 'contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device,' but no persistence-phase detection logic provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications for autostart following DLL side-loading execution (HKLM/HKCU Run keys, Winlogon, AppInit_DLLs). Correlate with WriteProcessMemory/CreateRemoteThread from injector. Flag suspicious AppData or ProgramData paths written during DLL execution that are later loaded on restart.

suggestion.title: RAT Agent Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Watchdog RAT agent' was deployed alongside miner, but no network-based detection for RAT beaconing was outlined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from process spawned by DLL side-loading to suspicious C2 infrastructure. Detect patterns consistent with RAT heartbeat (regular small-packet connections on non-standard ports). Correlate with command execution or process injection from same source process.

suggestion.title: Self-propagating Go malware execution with child processes
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'self-propagating Go encryptor'—indicates automated worm-like execution spawning multiple child processes for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Go-compiled binaries or unsigned executables spawning multiple child processes in rapid succession, particularly those initiating network connections or writing to system paths.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation for encryption scope
suggestion.rationale: Metadata lists 'Elevation of privilege' as key theme; ransomware requires elevated context to encrypt system files and bypass AppLocker/security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation techniques (token impersonation, UAC bypass, scheduled task creation) immediately preceding or concurrent with unusual file system activity.

suggestion.title: Ransomware encryption activity detection
suggestion.rationale: Core payload: 'encryptor' in title; article describes encryption mechanism. Impact phase should show mass file writes with encryption signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity file operations (writes/modifications) across multiple file extensions in bulk, especially from non-standard process paths or with encrypted byte patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via credential reuse in RaaS operation
suggestion.rationale: Metadata lists 'Lateral movement' and 'Ransomware as a service'—indicates human operators leveraging compromised credentials for multi-system spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual lateral movement patterns: same credential used across multiple systems in short timeframes, exploitation of known vulnerabilities, or abnormal RDP/SMB sessions from infected hosts.

suggestion.title: Go runtime and library loading indicators
suggestion.rationale: Go-compiled malware has distinct runtime patterns; loading of Go standard library functions can differentiate from native Windows payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes loading Go runtime libraries (crypto, encoding, net packages) from unexpected parent processes or locations, especially if concurrent with file system scanning or encryption activity.

suggestion.title: Ransom note deployment and extortion communication
suggestion.rationale: Metadata lists 'Extortion'—indicates post-encryption ransom demand delivery and attacker communication channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of ransom note files (.txt, .html) or changes to wallpaper/logon screens; monitor for outbound HTTPS connections to known C2 or contact domains.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw' — this is initial-access vector; pipeline generated zero detection logic for exploitation attempts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiClient EMS management interfaces (default port 443, 8013) from unexpected sources with suspicious payloads, URI traversal sequences, or parameter injection patterns. Correlate with failed authentication followed by successful access or privilege changes in EMS logs.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution from FortiClient Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealer 'deployment' as the attack outcome; no detection rule exists for suspicious process execution spawned from or injected into FortiClient processes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unsigned executables with parent process matching FortiClient EMS service (FortiClientWindows.exe, FortiClientServiceWrapper.exe). Flag any DLL injection or unsigned binary execution from FortiClient directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Browser and OS Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article's explicit purpose is credential theft; no detection surfaces credential access techniques (SAM dump, LSASS access, browser credential enumeration, clipboard scraping)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes reading HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SAM, accessing lsass.exe memory, enumerating AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data, or clipboard access APIs. Flag parent-child chains where parent is FortiClient-related and child reads credential store files.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Beacon from Credential Stealer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealers exfiltrate stolen data to attacker infrastructure (implicit in stealer design). Article doesn't name C2 hosts but pipeline should flag this detection gap for outbound beaconing
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/HTTP POST requests to external IP ranges or suspicious domains from processes spawned in FortiClient context, particularly with compressed or encrypted payloads. Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains (WHOIS age < 30 days) from affected endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Reconnaissance from Compromised EMS
suggestion.rationale: FortiClient EMS compromise provides pivot point for lateral reconnaissance. Article doesn't explicitly describe post-exploitation movement but this is a logical progression from credential stealer deployment with privileged access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected LDAP queries, NetBIOS scans, SMB share enumeration (\\*\IPC$, \\*\C$), or network scanning (ICMP, ARP) originating from FortiClient EMS server. Correlate with process execution from service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Google Password Manager Vault Access with Single PIN Guess
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'One Captured PIN' enables entire vault theft — pipeline missed the core attack mechanic. PIN guessing/capture is the fulcrum of the compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid-fire PIN validation attempts against Google Password Manager or Chrome credential store; detect when single PIN unlock triggers exfiltration of >100 password entries within seconds to non-Google infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Store Exfiltration Post-PIN Unlock
suggestion.rationale: Article body lacks detail on exfiltration method, but title establishes that vault becomes accessible after PIN compromise. Detection must track bulk password-database reads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data or equivalent password storage, followed by large file writes to temp/ or network egress of structured credential data.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Chrome/Google Password Manager Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: VaultJacking likely involves execution of tool or abuse of password manager CLI/API. No article detail provided, but pipeline should have flagged child processes of password manager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Chrome.exe or credential-manager processes with unusual parent processes, or spawning of unusual child processes (e.g. net.exe, certutil.exe, base64 encoders).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawned During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article context: MDM cannot monitor or restrict code execution during npm install, pip install, or gem install—developers routinely run untrusted lifecycle scripts. Supply-chain malware exploits this gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes (curl, wget, powershell, bash) spawned during package manager execution (npm.exe, python.exe, gem.exe) with outbound network connections—especially those not matching known build artifacts or typical package metadata fetches.

suggestion.title: IDE Extension Installed from Non-Standard Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article context: VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, and other editors allow plugin installation from arbitrary URLs and custom registries—completely outside MDM scope. Adversaries can inject malicious extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to IDE extension directories (~/.vscode/extensions, ~/.config/JetBrains, ~/.emacs.d) paired with registry/config modifications pointing to non-official extension sources or direct HTTP downloads of .vsix or .zip plugin archives.

suggestion.title: Shell Configuration Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article context: MDM typically does not monitor ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.profile, or fish/shell initialization files—critical persistence vectors for developer machines where code execution is expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized modifications to shell initialization files in user home directories—especially appends of export statements, alias definitions, or sourcing of remote scripts. Baseline legitimate changes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Git Hook Injection for Arbitrary Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article context: .git/hooks (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-push) are executable scripts in each repository—MDM cannot reliably prevent their modification. Standard vector for supply-chain compromise at clone time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of files under .git/hooks with executable permissions, particularly when paired with content containing network calls, exfiltration commands, or invocations of unexpected interpreters (curl, wget, base64).

suggestion.title: Package Manager Registry Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article context: npm config, pip.conf, gem .gemrc, and package manager credentials are not typically protected by MDM. Attackers modify registry pointers to redirect package downloads to malicious mirrors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process invocations of package-manager config commands (npm config set, pip install --index-url, gem sources -a) with non-standard or internal-only registry hostnames; also flag creation/modification of .npmrc, pip.conf, .gemrc files with suspicious registry entries.

suggestion.title: Source Code Exfiltration via Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article context: Developers routinely use git, container registries (docker push), artifact stores, and package managers—all potential exfiltration channels MDM cannot effectively gate without crippling developer workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large file uploads to external git hosting, artifact repositories, or container registries with source-code patterns (e.g., .git archive, src/ directories, .py/.js/.go files) in network payloads or via host-side monitoring of development-tool activity outside normal CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Delivery via Chatbot Recommendation Link
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states users are being redirected to 'cryptojacking malware sites' through chatbot outputs. Pipeline failed to detect download chains from malicious recommendation links to crypto-mining process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track browsers spawning unexpected child processes (xmrig, cryptominer, monero-related binaries) following chatbot recommendation click events. Correlate timing of redirect URLs in chatbot logs with malware process creation. Flag crypto-mining pool connections from user endpoints.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Chatbot Output Recommending Malware Domains
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism is chatbot being weaponized to recommend malicious links. Pipeline should detect deviation from legitimate recommendation patterns—'recommendations redirect users' implies the bot's response itself is malicious or injected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate chatbot recommendation URLs (GitHub, PyPI, Stack Overflow, etc.). Alert on outputs containing: shortened URLs with unknown final destinations, IP-based domains, domains newly registered (<30 days), or domains in abuse/malware blocklists. Monitor for prompt injection patterns in user queries that generate malicious outputs.

suggestion.title: Resource Hijacking from Redirected Cryptojacking Malware
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes cryptojacking as the impact phase. Pipeline should detect sustained crypto-mining process execution, abnormal resource consumption, and mining pool connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Sustained CPU/GPU usage spikes (>60%) from browser processes correlating with stratum protocol connections to mining pools. Monitor for process injection into system binaries (svchost, explorer) masking miner execution. Track outbound connections to known mining pool IP ranges (e.g., 1.1.1.1, monero mining nodes).

suggestion.title: Malicious Redirect Chain Detection from Chatbot Link Click to Malware Staging
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow is chatbot → HTTP redirect(s) → malware download site. Pipeline should detect multi-hop redirect chains where final destination hosts cryptojacking payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP 301/302/307 redirect sequences initiated from chatbot domains, with final destination (after following chain) resolving to low-reputation or newly-observed domains. Track HTTP User-Agent and Referer header consistency across hops. Flag if final domain lacks valid SSL certificate or has recently been flagged in threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Function Invocation in cPanel Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability in 'lsws.redisAble function' and provides detection command: grep for 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' in /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs/. This is a direct log artifact with high signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search cPanel audit and system logs for invocations of 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' or direct calls to the lsws.redisAble function. Baseline expected Redis operations and alert on anomalous calls, especially from unauthenticated or low-privilege contexts. Cross-correlate with subsequent root-privilege command execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via cPanel Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers with 'no privileges' can exploit the flaw, indicating remote unauthenticated access. The vulnerability 'enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—classic RCE vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs (cPanel/WHM ports typically 2082-2087) for POST/GET requests to Redis-related endpoints or plugin handlers. Flag requests with no prior authentication session or unusual User-Agent patterns. Correlate with subsequent privilege escalation events or process creation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Redis Configuration Abuse
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability stems from 'incorrect privilege assignment' in Redis enable/disable handling, allowing unprivileged users to execute code 'with root privileges.' This is textbook privilege escalation via improper access control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or command execution with UID 0 (root) originating from cPanel plugin processes, web server processes, or the lsws daemon. Establish baseline of legitimate root operations from these contexts and alert on deviations. Monitor for script interpreters (bash, python, perl) spawned with root privileges from non-standard callers.

suggestion.title: Successful Exploitation Indicators via cPanel Plugin Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit detection command showing where exploitation traces appear. A secondary indicator is observation of successful API calls to Redis functions from unauthorized sources followed by privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for IP addresses appearing in /var/cpanel/logs or /usr/local/cpanel/logs that match the redis function pattern, then cross-reference those IPs with system logs (auth.log, audit.log) for subsequent privilege escalation or lateral movement. Flag IPs executing commands with root context immediately following the redis function call.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution from cPanel Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the flaw allows 'arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' This is the impact phase—attackers execute code post-exploitation. Detection should focus on the script execution itself in cPanel/plugin context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell script execution (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/python, etc.) with UID 0 from the cPanel plugin directory (/usr/local/cpanel or related paths), or triggered by web server processes handling cPanel requests. Alert on any root-level command execution that cannot be attributed to legitimate system administration tasks.

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Tampering — New/Unexpected Publisher
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'published to the npm registry under a trusted identity.' Need to detect when a legitimate package suddenly has a new publisher, new signature, or altered metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm package version publishes where the publisher account, PGP key, or package metadata changes unexpectedly. Flag any version with a new or unrecognized publisher pushing to a previously-trusted package namespace.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration & Theft Post-npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'credential-stealing malware' in the malicious versions. Need behavioral detection after package load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After npm package install, detect child processes accessing credential stores (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, browser profiles, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Microsoft\\Credentials), reading environment variables with 'PASSWORD'/'KEY'/'TOKEN', or scraping browser LocalStorage/IndexedDB.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Tree Under npm/Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious versions' that execute payload code. Need execution detection when package install spawns unexpected children.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when npm or node.exe spawns children outside normal install patterns: curl/wget downloading binaries, PowerShell/bash reverse shells, credential dumpers (mimikatz, secretsdump), or C2 beacon processes.

suggestion.title: Post-Infection Ransomware Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Known ransomware use' linking this supply-chain to downstream ransomware. Need to catch the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file encryption activity (mass writes with new extensions, high-entropy file rewrites), process chains establishing C2 or exfiltration, or ransom note creation patterns originating from or following npm package installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Install From Unusual/Offline Source
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions packages published to 'the npm registry' but attackers may also stage on mirrors/private registries. Need to catch misdirected installs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations originating from non-standard registries, offline caches, or when .npmrc points to unexpected registry URLs. Flag when developers install from mirrors or internal repositories where tampering is more likely.

suggestion.title: TanStack Package Version Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies TanStack as the affected product. Need inventory-based hunt for unexpected versions in the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all package.json and node_modules across the fleet for TanStack package versions. Flag any version published between 2026-05-15 and 2026-06-10 (before KEV date and patch due date). Cross-reference installed versions against known-malicious commits or CVE signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 — Compromised Nx Console Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious version of Nx Console to be published' and 'compromised extension'. Supply-chain compromise requires baseline validation of package authenticity and version control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console installations with mismatched file hashes against vendor-published integrity manifest. Alert on unsigned or invalid-signature Nx Console binaries. Monitor npm registry or package manager logs for installation of affected package versions (pre-2026-06-10 patch).

suggestion.title: Nx Console — Obfuscated Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fetched an obfuscated payload'. Benign developer tools should not execute obfuscated code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nx Console spawning child processes with base64/xor-encoded command lines or loading unsigned DLLs. Detect Nx Console reading and deobfuscating embedded payloads from its own binary or temporary files.

suggestion.title: Nx Console — Credential Harvesting from Disk and Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory'. Explicit credential access activity—core attack phase requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console accessing password manager databases, browser credential stores (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data, etc.), or SSH/git config files. Alert on Nx Console opening handles to LSASS or calling credential enumeration APIs. Monitor memory access patterns for plaintext credential extraction.

suggestion.title: Nx Console — Unexpected Outbound Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fetched...obfuscated payload' and credential harvesting imply command-and-control or exfiltration. Nx Console has predictable, legitimate network footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Nx Console network destinations via official docs/telemetry. Alert on connections to unfamiliar IPs/domains, unusual ports (non-443/80), or rapid sequential connections suggesting data exfiltration. Flag encrypted tunnels or DGA-like DNS queries.

suggestion.title: Nx Console — Process Behavior Anomalies (Credential Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article: developer tools like Nx Console should not natively read credential sources. Behavioral baselining detects compromise without IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of normal Nx Console file/registry access. Flag deviations: access to .ssh, .git-credentials, browser profiles, Windows Credential Manager, or SAM/NTDS. Use process anomaly detection (e.g., Splunk UBA, Sentinel ML) to surface behavioral shifts.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Installation and Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Daemon Tools Lite' as the vulnerable product with 'embedded malicious code.' Installations and executions represent the entry point; this is the first huntable signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for installation or execution of Daemon Tools Lite (daemon.exe, DTLite.exe, DaemonTools installers). Monitor for suspicious child processes spawned by Daemon Tools processes that deviate from normal software operation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Vulnerability Scanner Findings
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and specifies federal patch due date of 2026-05-30. Vulnerability scanner detections are the primary mechanism to identify exposed assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platforms for CVE-2026-8398 detections. Correlate findings with Daemon Tools Lite installations and prioritize anything not patched before 2026-05-30.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Process Child Process Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'embedded malicious code' and states 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability,' indicating post-installation execution of malware via child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by daemon.exe or DTLite.exe, particularly interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), utilities (certutil, curl, wget), or known post-exploitation tools.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Outbound Network Communication Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Embedded malware typically initiates C2. Article cites 'high impact on confidentiality' and active exploitation, suggesting data exfiltration or callback behavior not typical of legitimate Daemon Tools usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for legitimate Daemon Tools network traffic. Alert on unexpected DNS queries, HTTP/HTTPS connections, or non-standard protocols originating from daemon.exe to untrusted or newly-seen destinations.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails impersonating IT support targeting law firms
suggestion.rationale: Article states SRG 'send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' May 2025 report notes attackers 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms... using typosquatted patterns.' This is the primary initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails with urgency language directing recipients to call external support numbers. Flag sender domains matching typosquatted patterns of law-firm IT vendors or containing 'support', 'helpdesk', 'IT-admin'. Correlate with credential harvesting, mailbox forwarding rules, or external email forwarding.

suggestion.title: Callback phishing (vishing) calls from threat actors impersonating IT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' Later notes extortion gang 'will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them.' Vishing is the second-stage social engineering channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound calls from external numbers claiming IT support authority, especially if calls precede RDP tool invocation. Flag patterns of simultaneous calls to multiple users in same organization within 2-hour window. Monitor call logs for requests to 'grant remote access' or 'verify credentials.'

suggestion.title: Remote desktop session requests following phishing or vishing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack progression: 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' This is the execution phase when social engineering succeeds, using legitimate RDP or remote-access tools (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP or remote-access tool (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Chrome Remote Desktop, etc.) initiation within 5 minutes of phishing email click or reported vishing call. Prioritize legal/finance staff. Correlate with user reports of unsolicited support requests or unusual IT contact.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized external USB or hard-drive insertion for bulk data theft
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'If that attempt fails, SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer.' FBI lists 'the unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers' as explicit indicator of SRG attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for insertion of external storage (especially unknown serial numbers) into corporate systems. Flag external-drive mounts following failed RDP session or correlating with unscheduled physical visitor badges. Alert on large file-copy operations (>500 MB) to external media within 30 minutes of mount.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized external individuals on-site claiming IT support role
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies contingency: 'sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access.' FBI warns of 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' as key indicator. Physical-security IoA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-check visitor logs against roster of actual IT staff and contractors. Alert on badge-swipe or manual check-in of individuals claiming IT affiliation who are not pre-registered. Instruct reception/security to challenge unfamiliar people requesting computer access and escalate to IT for verification.

suggestion.title: Ransom extortion emails and coordinated victim intimidation calls
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exfiltration impact: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them.' Impact and confirmation phase of attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails and calls claiming insider knowledge of stolen data, threats to release or sell information, or ransom demands with leak-site references. Alert on patterns of simultaneous extortion emails to multiple organizational employees plus calls to external clients/partners within 24-hour window.

suggestion.title: ChangeMissionDatabase privilege elevation or account abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An authenticated user with the `ChangeMissionDatabase` privilege can exploit this.' Pipeline did not surface detection for privilege-escalation or account-takeover attempts leading to algorithm modification. Should detect accounts gaining ChangeMissionDatabase permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users without ChangeMissionDatabase permissions acquiring that privilege, or authentication events for service accounts immediately preceding algorithm PATCH requests. Alert on privilege-escalation patterns (lateral movement between accounts before privilege grant) preceding Yamcs algorithm modifications.

suggestion.title: Janino expression compilation with suspicious Java/shell syntax in algorithm text payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text.' Pipeline generated no payload-analysis detection. Should inspect algorithm update requests for Java runtime/reflection APIs, ProcessBuilder, Runtime.exec() patterns, or shell metacharacters embedded in the algorithm field.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* where the request body contains suspicious Java keywords (ProcessBuilder, Runtime.exec, System.getRuntime, java.lang.reflect) or shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, backticks, $()). Correlate with subsequent unexpected child process spawning from JVM.

suggestion.title: Yamcs application log anomalies: Janino compilation failures or ClassLoader exceptions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compiled and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text' via Janino. Successful RCE requires Janino to successfully compile malicious expressions. Should monitor Yamcs application logs for compilation errors, ClassNotFoundException, or reflection-related exceptions that precede code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs (likely /var/log/yamcs/ or Java stderr) for Janino compilation exceptions, ClassCastException, InvocationTargetException patterns. Elevated frequency of such errors followed by unexpected process spawning indicates exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed algorithm modification attempts via PATCH before successful execution
suggestion.rationale: Attacker iterating on Janino syntax to achieve code execution would generate multiple PATCH requests with parsing/compilation failures before success. Should detect rapid-fire PATCH requests to algorithm endpoints from single user/IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >3 PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* from a single user or IP within 10 minutes, particularly from accounts not typically modifying algorithms. Correlation with subsequent shell spawning from JVM indicates successful payload refinement.

suggestion.title: Phishing Targeting World Cup Stakeholders
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata keyword 'phishing' + threat-actor names confirm phishing as primary attack vector; canonical initial-access technique for high-profile event targeting
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with FIFA/World Cup 2026 subject lines + credential-harvesting payload URLs. Monitor for clicks from event-infrastructure mailboxes to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Correlate phishing-email clusters by sender domain + recipient organization type (venue, broadcast, ticketing).

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domains Impersonating FIFA/World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly lists 'typosquatting' as attack vector; mega-events are prime targets for domain-confusion attacks on vendors, ticketing platforms, and broadcast partners
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt DNS query logs and domain-registration databases for typosquatted World Cup/FIFA domains (missing vowels, character substitutions: fif4.com, fifa-worlcup.com, fifa2026.co [vs .com]). Correlate with email/social-media referrals. Track WHOIS registration patterns of suspicious variants.

suggestion.title: QR Code Phishing in Event Promotional/Ticketing Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata keyword 'QR Codes' + phishing context; threat actors embed malicious QR codes in counterfeit tickets, promotional materials, or official-looking venue signage to redirect attendees to credential-harvest or malware sites
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor URL-shortener and QR-redirect services for bulk code generation targeting World Cup domains. Alert on QR-scanned URLs resolving to low-reputation hosts or newly-registered TLDs. Flag social-media/email attachments with embedded QR codes sent to sporting-organization email users.

suggestion.title: Wiper/Destructive Malware Targeting Broadcast or Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata keyword 'wiper' + state-aligned threat-actor names (Fighting Ursa, Fiddling Scorpius) suggest sabotage-intent targeting broadcast, ticketing, or venue-management infrastructure to disrupt event operations
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor critical-infrastructure segments for suspicious disk-enumeration tools (diskpart, GParted, dd). Alert on bulk file-deletion patterns with high velocity. Track MBR/UEFI tampering attempts and raw-disk write operations. Correlate with staging of wiping payloads or destructive scripts.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Reconnaissance by Threat Actors
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'attack surface'—threat actors conduct systematic discovery of venue IT, broadcast systems, and ticketing infrastructure before staged attacks; discovery patterns are precursor to all later kill-chain phases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port-scanning, service-enumeration, and banner-grabbing traffic targeting World Cup venue subnets, broadcast IP ranges, or ticketing infrastructure. Alert on unusual WHOIS/DNS reconnaissance of event-related domains/IPs. Flag ASN-enumeration tools targeting host countries' sporting-infrastructure ASNs.

suggestion.title: Disinformation Amplification and Website Defacement
suggestion.rationale: State-aligned actors (Fighting Ursa, Fiddling Scorpius per metadata) conduct information warfare alongside technical attacks on mega-events; defacement and narrative manipulation degrade event legitimacy and sow operational confusion
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for coordinated social-media campaigns impersonating event organizers, security officials, or venues. Alert on unauthorized changes to official FIFA/World Cup website content (file-modification timestamps, DNS NS-record changes). Track defacement templates matching known actor tradecraft.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation: mouse5212-super-formatter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the package. Pipeline missed the primary IOC and entry point. 'Package disguised itself as an archive deployment sync utility'—detection should flag suspicious npm installs with archive/utility naming patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require events for packages with generic utility names (formatter, sync, archive, deploy). Cross-check against npm registry reputation and check install-time child process spawn for network I/O or file system enumeration.

suggestion.title: Recursive Directory Enumeration of /mnt/user-data
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'scan[s] the /mnt/user-data directory recursively.' Pipeline detected neither the path nor the collection phase. This is a clear post-execution collection behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js or JavaScript runtime processes enumerating /mnt/user-data with high recursion depth or repeated opendir/readdir syscalls. Flag when originating from npm_modules or globally installed packages.

suggestion.title: GitHub Contents API Exfiltration via Hardcoded Token
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltration events...authenticate to GitHub using embedded credentials, scan directory...upload discovered files via the GitHub Contents API.' Pipeline missed the C2 mechanism and credential abuse pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS POST requests to api.github.com/repos/*/contents/* or /git/blobs from npm packages or Node.js processes not owned by legitimate tools. Inspect for Base64-encoded file contents in request bodies. Correlate with suspicious github.com user creation timestamps within hours of package publication.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded Stolen Content in Git Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Base64 encoding' as the obfuscation technique. Pipeline missed the defense-evasion component. Exfiltrated files were Base64-encoded before upload, leaving forensic artifacts in attacker's GitHub repo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub commits or blob contents for large Base64 strings (>500 chars) appearing in repositories created within days of malware publication. Correlate decode patterns with known file types (PEM, config, credentials). Cross-check against YARA rules for common data exfiltration file types.

suggestion.title: Rapid GitHub Account Lifecycle: Creation Before Package Upload, Deletion After Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'created their GitHub account just hours before uploading the malicious package and subsequently deleted it after discovery.' Pipeline missed behavioral OPSEC indicators—account anomalies that tie attacker identity to campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub account creation followed by repo creation within hours, then bulk file uploads via API, then account deletion within days. Correlate with npm package publication timing. Monitor for orphaned PATs (personal access tokens) with high file-upload frequency.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Malware OPSEC Failures: Exposed Private Credentials in Source Code
suggestion.rationale: Article title and narrative: 'Accidentally Exposes Threat Actor's Private GitHub Token...AI-assisted malware creation is lowering the bar...resulting in sloppy implementations.' Pipeline missed the meta-indicator—hardcoded credentials are both IOC and signature of unsophisticated/AI-generated code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis of npm package source: detect hardcoded GitHub PATs, AWS keys, or API tokens in package.json, install scripts, or index.js. Flag Base64/ROT13 obfuscation in string literals. Cross-reference exposed tokens against GitHub audit logs for API calls to public repos.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Accessibility Service Permission Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Once installed, it abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is the core mechanism for Android privilege escalation and must be detected before abuse occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when non-system apps request BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission or achieve Accessibility Service activation. Cross-reference permission-grant events against app installation timestamps and reputation databases. Escalate if Accessibility access is granted shortly after installation of apps with low/unknown trust scores or apps matching known-malware behavioral profiles.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Defense Evasion: Icon Hiding and System App Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device, or prevent sleep mode' and 'disable Google Play.' These are explicit post-execution evasion behaviors that establish persistence intent and should trigger behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Google Play Store is disabled via package manager after untrusted app installation. Detect apps disappearing from home screen without user action. Correlate launcher modifications with prior Accessibility Service grants or suspicious permissions. Flag apps that call disableComponent() or setComponentEnabledSetting() to hide or disable system apps.

suggestion.title: APK Downloads from Google Play Impersonation Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' Network-layer detection of domain spoofing and APK delivery from non-official Play Store is critical early-stage prevention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK file downloads (HTTP GET or POST) from domains containing typosquats of play.google.com, or from streaming/crypto-themed domains known to host BTMOB lures. Flag HTTP requests with User-Agent strings matching mobile browsers followed by APK content-type responses. Implement YARA or similar signatures to detect non-standard Play Store certificate signatures in downloaded APKs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Financial App Input Capture and Transaction Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article capability: 'intercepting financial transactions.' Behavioral anomalies in banking apps (keystroke capture, unusual transaction timing) should be detectable as proxy indicators of interception malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Accessibility-enabled apps receiving high-frequency input events from banking/payment apps. Alert on duplicate transactions, reversed transactions, or out-of-sequence transactions coinciding within hours of malware APK installation. Detect when banking apps receive clipboard read requests from non-whitelisted apps with Accessibility access. Flag unusual keystroke event volume from apps other than system input methods.

suggestion.title: Covert Screenshot Capture Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'capturing screenshots.' Repeated screenshot operations indicate credential harvesting or session recording for financial data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on apps with Accessibility Service permissions calling takeScreenshot() or MediaRecorder APIs at high frequency (>2 per minute). Detect screenshot files created immediately after banking app interaction. Flag instances where screenshots are encoded, compressed, or moved to temporary directories for exfiltration. Monitor for simultaneous screenshot + network traffic bursts.

suggestion.title: Remote Control C2 Communication from Mobile Device
suggestion.rationale: Article capability: 'remote control capabilities.' Malware C2 channels exhibit predictable traffic signatures (fixed intervals, small payloads, non-standard ports) distinct from legitimate mobile app behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to non-standard ports (>10000, <1000 excluding common services) from recently-installed apps. Detect beaconing patterns: fixed-interval outbound connections (e.g., every 30s, 60s) to the same IP or domain. Flag encrypted payload transfers of unusual size (>5MB) exiting mobile devices. Correlate with known BTMOB infrastructure IOCs when emerging in threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Data Access from Employee Account Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system' and 'illegally copied personal information.' Core attack vector (compromised account accessing customer PII) has no detection case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline employee account access patterns to customer/PII databases. Alert on bulk data exports, access outside business hours, queries accessing unusually large result sets (8.7M records over typical daily access), or file transfers to external/cloud storage not in user's history.

suggestion.title: Detect Spearphishing Targeting Employee Credentials at Carnival
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee.' Attack begins with credential compromise via social engineering; no phishing/initial-access detection case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Email gateway detection: spearphishing URLs impersonating Carnival SSO/email portals, credential-capture domains, or malicious attachments targeting @carnival.com, @hollandamerica.com, or @princess.com domains. Correlate successful phishing clicks with failed/successful logons from anomalous IP/geography 0–24h post-email.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Carnival Data Exfiltration to Dark Web/Leak Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article: ShinyHunters claimed 8.7M records stolen and posted to leak site in April; article notes 'data leaked by the extortion gang' accessible to Have I Been Pwned. No threat-intel or dark-web monitoring use case tracks ShinyHunters or Carnival data postings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert SOC when Carnival, Holland America, Princess Cruises, or Mariner Society data appears in known breach databases, ShinyHunters leak site, or dark-web paste services. Cross-reference against ShinyHunters' known victim list and Salesforce-targeting campaigns to confirm attribution.

suggestion.title: Detect Account Logon Activity Inconsistent with Employee Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article: April 14 detection moment—'Company's IT security team identified unauthorized activity involving an employee's account.' No detection case covers the behavioral signature of account takeover (unusual logon locations, times, or patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal logon patterns per employee (typical IP ranges, geographies, times, target systems). Alert on logons from geographically impossible locations within short timeframe, logons during non-business hours, or access to systems outside employee's normal scope (customer database access for accounting employee, etc.).

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Database Query or Export Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exfiltration of 8.7M records with specific fields (names, DOB, email, gender, location, loyalty program data). No detection case covers the database-layer signature of bulk data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database transaction logs for SELECT statements returning unusually large result sets (>100K rows in single query), export-to-file operations, or data dumps targeting customer tables. Alert on table scans of loyalty_program, customer_pii, or personal_information tables outside normal ETL windows or by accounts without export privileges.

suggestion.title: BSC Testnet JSON-RPC Outbound Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Block outbound JSON-RPC traffic to bsc-testnet-rpc.publicnode.com' as a mitigation and describes real-time C2 communication via smart contracts through this RPC endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from endpoints to bsc-testnet-rpc.publicnode.com or related BSC testnet RPC endpoints. Monitor for JSON-RPC traffic patterns (POST requests with method parameters like eth_call, eth_getCode). Flag processes that are not standard blockchain applications initiating these connections.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Clipboard Write Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'ClickFix social engineering panel, injecting malicious commands directly into the clipboard—a technique requiring single deliberate user action for full compromise' and recommends 'Implement browser policies restricting clipboard write access.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clipboard write operations from browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) that originate from JavaScript execution contexts. Look for rapid clipboard modifications followed by subsequent process execution using clipboard contents.

suggestion.title: Fake reCAPTCHA Overlay Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states victims 'encountered a convincing fake Google reCAPTCHA overlay with an I'm not a robot checkbox' designed to trigger malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DOM manipulation or iframe injection of fake Google reCAPTCHA elements that do not originate from google.com/recaptcha domains. Monitor for HTML overlays with reCAPTCHA-like styling loaded from non-Google infrastructure. Alert on user interaction (clicks) with counterfeit CAPTCHA elements followed by suspicious script execution.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Website JavaScript Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The campaign compromises legitimate websites by injecting hidden JavaScript code. Simply visiting a tampered legitimate site can trigger the malware's multi-stage delivery chain' and malware 'stored malicious JavaScript directly on-chain.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous JavaScript execution on legitimate, high-reputation domains (detect via content inspection or DOM analysis). Flag script sources that differ from domain's normal patterns. Look for script injection from external/blockchain sources to legitimate sites. Combine with user-agent and referrer analysis to identify passive infection vectors.

suggestion.title: Python Interpreter + Helper.py Shellcode Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'pythonw.exe (Python interpreter), helper.py (shellcode loader)' as associated files, indicating a Python-based loader chain for SectopRAT/ACRStealer delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pythonw.exe execution with command-line arguments loading Python scripts (particularly helper.py or similarly-named loaders). Flag parent processes that are browsers or unusual parents launching Python interpreters. Monitor file creation of .py files in temporary directories followed by pythonw.exe execution.

suggestion.title: Smart Contract Interaction for C2 Dispatch
suggestion.rationale: Article details four smart contracts with distinct functions: 'Contract A: Anti-analysis dispatcher, Contract B: Windows ClickFix overlay, Contract C: macOS payload, Contract D: Real-time victim confirmation tracker' used for C2 delivery and confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify endpoints querying blockchain contract state (eth_getCode, eth_call to specific contract addresses like 0xAdecFB75C8C0CA2bC10517ce5B7AF99b4c2d52c9) via JSON-RPC. Look for pattern: victim confirms successful compromise by writing to on-chain tracking contract (Contract D). Flag processes making repeated queries to the same contract addresses.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Gogs User RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code' — core attack vector is post-authentication arbitrary code execution via Gogs vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Gogs service or child processes execute system interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or system utilities (net.exe, whoami.exe, regsrv32.exe) outside normal Git operation baseline.

suggestion.title: Gogs Process Unexpected Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation inherently requires Gogs to spawn shell/interpreter processes; title confirms arbitrary code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation events where Gogs (or git-related services) are parent; alert on non-standard children or privilege escalation to SYSTEM context from user-level Gogs process.

suggestion.title: Authenticated Session Followed by Suspicious File Activity in Gogs Directory
