suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path requires authenticated access followed by payload upload or config modification; title specifies authentication requirement before RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authenticated HTTP POST/PUT to Gogs endpoints with subsequent suspicious file writes to Gogs working directory, scripts directory, or executable deployment paths.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Outbound Network Initiation Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE compromise would enable attacker-directed network callbacks or exfiltration; threat actor must move laterally or establish C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Gogs process to non-repo-hosting, non-package-manager IPs; especially suspicious if initiated during or immediately after authenticated session spike.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain First-Contact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'fiffa[.]com' and notes phishing relies on 'minor spelling changes that users are likely to miss.' Pipeline missed all domain IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network connections to domains with edit-distance ≤2 from 'fifa.com' or similar high-value brands. Cross-reference against known malware C2 domains and check WHOIS registration dates clustering near event dates (Feb 2026 onward per Bitdefender timeline).

suggestion.title: Fake Employment Portal Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'jobs-fifa[.]com' and 'fifa-hiring[.]com' as fake employment portals used for fraud. No detection use case generated despite explicit indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to domains containing 'fifa' + 'hiring' or 'fifa' + 'jobs' variants with suspicious characteristics: no SSL certificate chain validation, self-signed certs, or mismatched CN/SAN. Monitor for credential submissions to these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign Click-Through Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp' but pipeline generated no detection for advertisement-sourced phishing traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP referers from Google Ads, Facebook ads, or Telegram/WhatsApp URLs (t.me, wa.me) that redirect to domains containing 'fifa' or known phishing domains. Correlate with credential-submission POST payloads to detect harvesting.

suggestion.title: Batch Personal Data Form Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article states phishing sites 'collect various types of data, including names, physical and email addresses, phone numbers, banking/payment details' but no detection use case captures form-based credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST submissions to suspicious domains containing field names like 'name', 'email', 'phone', 'bank_account', 'card_number', or 'ssn' in a single multi-field form. Alert on high entropy strings or patterns matching credit card/bank account formats.

suggestion.title: Ghost Stadium Phishing Infrastructure Cluster Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes 'more than 300 phishing sites' to 'Ghost Stadium' (Chinese threat actor per Group-IB), yet pipeline missed actor attribution and the possibility of infrastructure clustering via IP/ASN/registrar correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate shared infrastructure (IP space, registrar, nameserver, SSL cert CA, registration timing clusters) across phishing domains. Group by 300-domain cohorts using WHOIS/PDNS lookups. Ghost Stadium may reuse registrar, payment processor, or IP allocations.

suggestion.title: Regional Fraud Campaign Targeting Geo-Specific Users
suggestion.rationale: Bitdefender observed 'fraudulent activity around the World Cup brand targeting users in UK, Portugal, Spain, Algeria, US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Germany, and Australia.' No use case for geo-targeted phishing detection despite stated scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing campaigns with geo-targeting: users in the 9 named countries receiving FIFA-themed phishing emails in local languages or with locale-specific offers (e.g., 'Panini sticker' offers in Brazil). Correlate email headers + recipient geo + click-through timestamps.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing with Malicious Archives via Cloud Links
suggestion.rationale: PhantomMail campaign explicitly documented: 'Spear-phishing emails delivering malicious ZIP/RAR archives via Google Drive and 4sync links, using decoy PDFs or fake errors while deploying malware.' Multiple impersonation targets (Ukrainian government, emergency, telecom, energy) named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on external emails containing .zip/.rar attachments or body links to Google Drive, 4sync, Dropbox, or file-sharing services, especially targeting Ukrainian government, emergency, or telecom domains. Trigger immediate response on archive extraction and child process execution within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Fake CAPTCHA / Cloudflare Verification Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: PhantomClick campaign: 'Fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix pages disguised as Zoom and LAPAS sites trick victims into running self-infecting commands through fake Cloudflare verification prompts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser navigation to CAPTCHA or Cloudflare verification pages with domain typosquatting (e.g., cloudflare-verify.*, zoom-captcha-*) or SSL cert name mismatches, followed by cmd.exe or PowerShell spawning from browser parent process or context.

suggestion.title: PowerShell RAT with Credential and Telegram/WhatsApp Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: LegionRelay and PhantomRelay RATs: 'LegionRelay supports file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup.' 'PhantomRelay...supports dynamic script loading, and PowerShell and Windows command execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell with encoded/obfuscated payloads, DownloadString or IEX patterns, or dynamic module loading. Correlate with access to browser LocalState files, Telegram AppData directories, or WhatsApp Local\Packages folders, screenshot utility execution, or unusual file enumeration.

suggestion.title: WebRTC Microphone and Camera Hijacking by RAT
suggestion.rationale: PrincessClub campaign operators 'added WebRTC-based live calls that could capture the victim's audio/video.' Distinct collection mechanism not typical of commodity malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes other than legitimate communication apps (Teams, Zoom, Chrome, Firefox) requesting microphone or camera device access. Flag unusual WebRTC STUN/TURN server connections initiated from non-browser processes or from processes spawned by downloaders.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Loader Pattern (LLM-Assisted Obfuscators)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes custom obfuscators 'LOOKVALPS, LOOKVALJS, DAYLIGHT, and TEASOUP, all custom obfuscators that were likely developed with LLM assistance.' These likely precede malware execution and can be detected by signature or entropy analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect files or processes with entropy signatures of obfuscation, variable names with 'LOOKVAL*' or 'DAYLIGHT' patterns, or PowerShell/JavaScript execution with high obfuscation ratios. Monitor for deobfuscation operations (regex replacements, base64 decoding) followed by dynamic code loading.

suggestion.title: Fake Ukrainian Military Charity and Russian Military Login Portal Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: DroneLink uses 'Fake Ukrainian military charity websites themed around FPV drones.' Nebo uses 'Fake...Russian military communications login pages...likely designed to trick Ukrainian military personnel.' Infrastructure shared between campaigns, indicating coordinated hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify fraudulent military, charity, and emergency services websites via new domain registration, WHOIS registration timing, SSL certificate issuer anomalies, and typosquatting against known Ukrainian government and emergency services domains. Correlate browser access with user job role (military, government) and alert on subsequent file download or APK installation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Business Document Lure
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Phishing Emails Masquerading as Business Documents' — explicit initial-access vector. Pipeline generated zero email-based detection despite this being the primary intrusion mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with spoofed business-document characteristics (corporate letterhead, purchase order, invoice templates) from untrusted external senders targeting high-value users. Cross-reference attachment MIME types and real extensions; flag .docx/.xlsx with embedded macros or suspicious PE headers. Correlate with URL shorteners and fremail domains in sender field.

suggestion.title: VIP Keylogger Process Execution and Memory Injection
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name explicitly stated in title but zero execution-phase detections. Should detect process spawning, DLL injection, and keystroke-capture APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned executable or DLL execution following email attachment open. Monitor for SetWindowsHookEx (WH_KEYBOARD, WH_KEYBOARD_LL), GetKeyState, or GetAsyncKeyState calls from non-accessibility tools. Flag processes with parent explorer.exe or winword.exe spawning suspicious child processes with no command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Keylogger C2 Beaconing and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Keylogger implies captured data must reach attacker; no UC for command-and-control or exfiltration patterns. Missing detection for outbound communication from compromised hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound HTTPS or DNS queries from user workstations post-infection. Look for periodic beaconing (5–60 min intervals), high data-volume transfers to rare destinations, or communication to newly registered domains. Correlate with keylogger file hash or process behavior anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Document Auto-Execution and Macro Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phishing lure is 'business documents' — implying Office macro or embedded executable. No UC for document-based code execution or macro launching child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect winword.exe, excel.exe, or powerpnt.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or wscript.exe without user interaction. Flag Office processes with high child-process counts or network socket creation. Monitor for macro-enabled documents (.docm, .xlsm) executed from Downloads or temp directories.

suggestion.title: Keystroke Data Staging and Exfiltration File Activity
suggestion.rationale: Keylogger must write captured keystrokes to disk before exfil; no UC for file-creation patterns or suspicious file access in AppData or system temp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of hidden files (prefix '.') or temporary files in %APPDATA%, %LOCALAPPDATA%, or %TEMP% directories with rapid size growth. Alert on file write frequency spikes from low-privilege processes. Correlate with process hashes or command-line indicators matching known keylogger variants.

suggestion.title: Marimo RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Marimo RCE' as initial access vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero kill-chain phases despite this explicit vulnerability mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Marimo service endpoints (typically ports 5000, 8000) with payloads containing Python code injection patterns or `__import__`, `exec`, `eval` in request bodies. Alert on successful 200/302 responses followed by process execution.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Autonomous Exploitation Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'LLM Agent' orchestrating attacks—novel behavior pattern. Pipeline produced zero use cases for agent-based execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual Python subprocess chains or shell invocations where parent is a Python interpreter with high entropy arguments (base64 encoded payloads, API keys). Look for rapid sequential execution of discovery and lateral-movement commands consistent with agent decision-tree output.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Lateral Movement via Database Pivot Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Four Pivots' to reach database—unusual hop count. Pipeline failed to reconstruct any kill-chain phases or lateral-movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 4+ successive network connections where each hop originates from a newly-compromised host (via process creation or RDP/SSH). Flag when intermediate systems are accessed solely for outbound reconnaissance or credential harvesting before pivoting further. Alert on database connection attempts from internal hosts without recent legitimate access history.

suggestion.title: Database Access from Compromised Internal Pivot Points
suggestion.rationale: Article climax is 'Internal Database'—final objective. Pipeline generated zero detection rules for database-layer attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database login attempts from newly-observed internal IP ranges, especially from systems not listed in CMDB as data consumers. Correlate with process-execution events on the connecting host showing file exfiltration tools (7zip, WinRAR, rclone) or database dump utilities (sqlmap, mysqldump) spawned post-login.

suggestion.title: LLM API Usage in Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: LLM agent requires API calls for decision-making; likely used for automated discovery. Zero use cases generated for this command-and-control pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, or other LLM API endpoints from internal hosts or jump boxes post-compromise. Flag repeated calls within short time windows (< 5 min intervals) with payloads requesting enumeration tasks, privilege escalation advice, or lateral-movement recommendations.

suggestion.title: Fake Recruiter Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Fake Recruiter Lures' as attack vector; this is initial access via social engineering and should be detected via email analysis and user reports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails impersonating recruiters with job titles/LinkedIn profiles matching target organization's hiring patterns, especially those requesting resume upload or credential entry. Correlate sender domain reputation and presence of trojanized attachments.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution & Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'macOS Malware' delivered via recruiter lures; requires detection of suspicious process execution and persistence on macOS systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned/untrusted macOS binaries executed from Downloads or temp directories post-email delivery. Monitor for LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon creation, shell script execution from suspicious paths, and process spawning from applications like Mail.app.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Firm Data Exfiltration to C2
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets 'Cryptocurrency Firms'—expect data collection and exfiltration of credentials, wallet data, or private keys to command-and-control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound connections from macOS crypto-firm systems to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains; monitor for bulk data upload to personal cloud storage (GDrive, Dropbox, iCloud); flag credential database access followed by network transfer.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Recruiter Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Fake recruiter lures typically solicit credentials or sensitive personal data (SSN, tax forms). Detect credential entry or form-submission anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for password manager clipboard access or form-filling tool activity coinciding with attacker-controlled domain visits. Correlate with failed SSO login attempts or unusual authentication patterns shortly after recruiter email receipt.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LaunchAgent Installation on macOS
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware commonly persists via LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon plist files. Should be detected at file creation and daemon registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new plist files written to ~/.LaunchAgents/ or /Library/LaunchAgents/ directories, especially those containing executable paths to non-standard locations or referencing shell commands. Cross-reference with unsigned process execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH or Credential Reuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once inside crypto firm, attacker likely moves laterally to access high-value targets (crypto wallets, trading systems); macOS systems are common pivot points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH connection attempts from compromised macOS systems to servers outside normal admin baselines, especially targeting infrastructure with crypto/trading applications. Flag .ssh/config modifications and private key file access.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens'. Over 5,700 malicious commits injected workflows. No detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .github/workflows/*.yml modifications followed by token exfiltration patterns (curl/wget to external endpoints with env vars, base64-encoded credential dumps). Alert on workflow executions immediately following commit injection by low-privilege accounts or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Malicious Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious commits pushed to the impacted repositories on May 18' containing payloads to 'steal credentials, keys, tokens'. Supply-chain foothold vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits that reference or exfiltrate environment variables, secrets, or token files (AWS keys, GitHub tokens). Correlate repo commits with subsequent outbound HTTPS/DNS to non-whitelisted external domains carrying base64 or hex-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Domain Fronting for Traffic Obfuscation (Underminr)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'domain-fronting attack allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity'. No detection for this defense-evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with SNI/certificate mismatch (Host header misaligned with TLS certificate CN/SAN), or HTTP Host headers pointing to known CDN/content-delivery domains while certificate belongs to attacker infrastructure. Alert on requests to trusted domain fronts followed by redirects to attacker-controlled destinations.

suggestion.title: Intentional Secrets Publication to Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CISA contractor 'intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a vast trove of other agency secrets on a public GitHub account'. Signals compromised or malicious insiders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk push operations of >100 files containing AWS credentials, API keys, or classified metadata to public repositories. Trigger on commits containing patterns matching env vars, .aws/credentials, .ssh, or token definitions published without redaction.

suggestion.title: Malicious DICOM File Heap Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'heap overflow vulnerability through the exploitation of the DICOM file format' and 'MediaArea...four vulnerabilities in MediaInfoLib'. DICOM-based PACS systems 'automatically ingest files received over the network'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DICOM ingestion services (Pydicom, Orthanc, GDCM, MediaInfoLib) for crashes, abnormal memory writes, or privilege escalations following network-received DICOM file processing. Baseline heap allocations and detect oversized element values or malformed pixel data segments.

suggestion.title: CVE Enrichment Signal Desynchronization (KEV vs. GCVE Lag)
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights: 'KEV is structurally centralized...GCVE is decentralized, enrichment data...doesn't have to wait in a single queue' and 'actionable context arrives meaningfully faster than the traditional NVD pipeline'. Defenders may miss zero-days faster via GCVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts against CVEs enriched in GCVE but not yet in KEV/NVD. Cross-reference GCVE threat signals with network/endpoint logs for attack patterns matching exploit PoCs. Alert on scanning or exploitation of CVEs lacking official enrichment >48 hours.

suggestion.title: GitHub Researcher Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' — indicates an account security incident. Pipeline should detect account takeover indicators: login from unusual IPs, API token creation, organization changes, or public repository modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub accounts accessing sensitive repos with geographically anomalous login patterns, newly-created PATs, or cross-organization access in short time windows. Correlate with researcher identity verification to flag account takeover.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Disclosure Timeline Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures' — suggests timing or coordination of vulnerability announcements. If researchers disclosed early or coordinated with Microsoft, detect rapid CVE/advisory publication clustering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag disclosure patterns: multiple CVEs attributed to same researcher published within narrow time window, or public disclosures before vendor patch availability. Correlate with researcher account activity logs to detect potential unauthorized access to draft advisories.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Vulnerability Disclosure Policy Violations
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates 'Microsoft Slams Public Zero-Day Disclosures' — suggests policy violation or timing breach. Detect early or unauthorized disclosure of unfixed vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for premature public disclosure of vulnerabilities before vendor SLA (typically 90 days). Track GitHub commits/issues/comments referencing unpatched Microsoft CVEs or zero-days. Correlate timeline with patch Tuesday release schedules.

suggestion.title: Gogs Server Process Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Run Malicious Code on the Server' and body references 'Execute Malicious Code Remotely'—post-exploitation execution would manifest as Gogs spawning unexpected shell/command interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Gogs process (gogs, git service) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or other shell interpreters. Post-RCE execution typically involves attacker code running under the Gogs service account or web server user spawning command shells for lateral movement or data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Probe on Gogs HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates remote exploitation path; article body mentions vulnerability 'on the Server' suggesting web-based vector. Detection should capture unusual HTTP requests targeting Gogs endpoints prior to code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to Gogs endpoints with suspicious payloads (shell metacharacters, encoded script, path traversal sequences) or requests to version-detection URIs. Baseline legitimate Gogs traffic and flag deviations in request patterns, user-agents, or request sizes.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Crash or Restart Post-Request
suggestion.rationale: 0-day RCE exploits often crash the service during exploitation attempts. Title's '0-Day' and 'remotely execute' suggests unstable exploitation path that may leave service restart artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Gogs service unexpected restarts or crash events in a short time window (< 1 minute) following HTTP requests with exploit-like characteristics. Correlate HTTP activity (from UC #2) with service availability loss and rapid restart.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write Under Gogs Installation Directory
suggestion.rationale: RCE execution phase requires dropping malicious code; 'Malicious Code on the Server' implies file write to Gogs directories (templates, plugins, config) for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs install and data directories for unexpected .go, .sh, .py, or .exe file creation by the Gogs service account. Flag executable writes to web-accessible paths (public, templates, plugins) that do not match patch/update signatures.

suggestion.title: Network Outbound Connection from Gogs Process to External IP
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE execution for C2 communication or data exfiltration. Gogs server should not normally initiate outbound connections to external IPs outside administrative scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Gogs outbound communication (typically local git operations, webhook calls to registered services). Alert on new outbound connections to external IPs on non-standard ports (non-80/443) or to known malware C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Gogs Configuration or Secrets File Read by Web Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE actors typically harvest credentials post-exploitation. Gogs stores database credentials, API tokens, and SSH keys in config files; suspicious reads indicate lateral movement or privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file access events targeting Gogs config files (app.ini, database.yml), SSH key directories, or API token storage by non-admin users or unexpected process parents. Correlate with process spawning UC to establish exploitation-to-compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Branch Name in Pull Request with Command Injection Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase' via 'malicious branch name'—this is the core exploit primitive. Pipeline detected zero use cases for argument injection payloads in branch/ref names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git rebase command invocations spawned from Gogs web process (user 'git' or Gogs service account) where command line contains '--exec' flag preceded by branch name input from API/POST request. Look for URL-decoded or shell-escaped payloads in branch creation/PR merge requests.

suggestion.title: Rapid Sequence: User Registration → Repository Creation → Rebase Merge Configuration Change
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' and 'enabling rebase merging is a single toggle'—the attack requires three rapid actions. No use case for this behavioral chain exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication logs: account creation event → repository creation event → settings/merge configuration change enabling rebase merge, all from same source IP within 5-minute window on default-configured Gogs instance. Flag if NEW account (≤1 hour old) triggers sequence.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping: SSH Keys, API Tokens, 2FA Secrets Exfiltrated from Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states post-exploitation impact: 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)'—this is collection phase but pipeline generated zero detection for in-process credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RCE-spawned child process (e.g., shell via git rebase --exec) attempting to read Gogs configuration files, database files, or SSH key storage directories. Also look for file exfiltration (curl/wget to external IP) of .ssh/, .config/, or database backup files.

suggestion.title: Gogs Git Rebase Command with Untrusted Input in --exec Argument
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'argument injection security flaw' via '--exec' flag in rebase. Article cites this as attack path but pipeline created no specific detection rule mapping git rebase process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git-rebase child processes spawned by Gogs/git system user. Alert on rebase with --exec flag containing shell metacharacters, env var expansion ($VAR), command substitution ($()), or suspicious executables (bash, sh, curl, wget). Cross-reference with pull request metadata to identify branch name source.

suggestion.title: Private Repository Data Access by Non-Owning User via Compromised Gogs Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers can 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos)'—lateral data exfiltration post-compromise. Pipeline did not suggest detection for unauthorized repo access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git clone, pull, or API queries for private repositories from Gogs web process spawned via rebase merge operation. Baseline: legitimate user access patterns should not include reading repos outside their membership. Flag RCE-spawned process accessing repos without ownership/collaborator role.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH Keys or API Tokens Stolen from Gogs Server
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'pivot to other network-accessible systems' using dumped SSH keys and API tokens—lateral movement post-data-theft. Pipeline generated zero use case for credential reuse on adjacent infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SSH or API authentication events originating from Gogs server IP using credentials (API tokens, SSH keys) previously extracted from Gogs itself. Look for same bearer token/key used from Gogs host and then from attacker-controlled infrastructure or lateral targets.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process'—a core defense-evasion execution technique central to the infection chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where a legitimate media/plugin executable (e.g., HLS Installer) launches from user temp/downloads folder and loads an unsigned/untrusted DLL from the same directory. Alert on parent-child process chains combining legitimate binary execution with subsequent suspicious network or file activity.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser/Plugin Update Prompt Leading to Malicious Archive Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue. Clicking the link downloaded a ZIP archive'—the initial access technique that triggers the entire infection chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP/RAR archive downloads to user Downloads/Temp folders immediately following visits to known piracy streaming domains or following in-browser fake update prompts. Correlate browser user-agent strings or window titles containing 'update', 'plugin', or 'player' with subsequent archive creation.

suggestion.title: Mixed Legitimate-Malicious Archive Packaging and Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL'—a deliberate packaging pattern combining legitimate binaries with unsigned payloads to evade static detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archive extraction (RAR, ZIP, 7z) containing both a known-legitimate binary and unsigned/anomalous DLLs. Cross-reference extracted executable hashes against legitimate software catalogs. Flag if archive originates from known piracy domains (urush1bar4[.]online, .ru/.top TLDs hosting streaming content).

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner/XMRig with RAT Module Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and tags include 'XMRig, Miner'—indicating dual-purpose malware combining resource hijacking with remote control capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SilentCryptoMiner or XMRig process spawning (monitor for process names, command-line args, or module imports associated with these miners). Correlate with evidence of outbound C2 communication to known mining pool addresses and elevated sustained CPU usage (>60% for minutes). Alert if process established persistence (scheduler, registry, service creation).

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Reuse Across Campaign Iterations
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Previously...domain file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu...threat actor employed a new website, urush1bar4[.]online'—allowing detection via domain pivoting and infrastructure continuity analysis across campaign waves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on domains urush1bar4[.]online and file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu. Hunt for shared infrastructure patterns (registrant, ASN, SSL issuer, WHOIS privacy provider, nameserver) to identify related C2 or distribution infrastructure. Correlate DNS requests to these domains with archive downloads or DLL execution timeframes.

suggestion.title: Piracy Site Visitation Preceding Archive Download Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies distribution via 'illegal movie and TV show streaming sites' with '.ru and .top TLDs'—establishing browsing behavior as an initial access indicator preceding the full attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user web browsing to known piracy domains (maintained via threat-intel feeds) with subsequent suspicious file downloads (archives, executables) or process execution from temp/downloads directories. Flag .ru and .top TLDs hosting streaming content combined with fake update prompts or archive activity within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS RCE Exploitation via CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'critical' vulnerability in FortiClient EMS; pipeline extracted no CVE ID or version info. Expected: detection of exploitation attempts against exposed EMS management interfaces or suspicious post-exploitation process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to known FortiClient EMS admin paths (e.g., /admin/*, /api/v2/*) from unexpected sources, or sudden process spawning from FortiClient service accounts with high privilege demands.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution Post-EMS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title states deployment of 'credential stealer' but pipeline extracted zero malware indicators. Should detect child processes from EMS service, registry/LSA dumping attempts, or LSASS access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with handles to lsass.exe, mimikatz signatures, or secretsdump patterns; monitor for password filter DLL installation or SAM registry reads initiated from EMS-related service contexts.

suggestion.title: FortiClient Service Anomalous Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies C2 exfiltration; pipeline surfaced no network IOCs. Article premise requires outbound C2 from compromised EMS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from FortiClient process or spawned children to non-Fortinet CDNs, especially with high-entropy data transfer or connections on uncommon ports masquerading as legitimate services.

suggestion.title: Persistence via EMS Service Injection or Scheduled Task
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability → credentials stolen → likely follow-on persistence. Article does not mention but threat model requires it; pipeline ignored persistence entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new scheduled tasks created by EMS service accounts, DLL injection into FortiClient services, or registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys targeting FortiClient paths.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using Stolen EMS Admin Credentials
suggestion.rationale: EMS is centralized management system; stolen credentials enable domain-wide lateral movement. Pipeline missed this secondary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect EMS service account credentials used for SMB/RDP to non-EMS hosts, or rapid logon attempts from EMS server to multiple endpoints outside normal admin baseline.

suggestion.title: EMS Database or Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article titled credential stealer but EMS itself is a credential repository (endpoint configs, policies, management certs). Pipeline assumed only active stealer, not database dump.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk reads of EMS database files (typically SQL Server or PostgreSQL in Fortinet deployments), XML config exports, or encrypted policy archives transmitted outside EMS administrative network.

suggestion.title: Google Password Manager Vault Unlock via Captured PIN
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Steals Entire Google Password Manager Vault With One Captured PIN'—core attack vector. No use case generated despite clear credential-access event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful password manager vault unlock preceded by failed PIN attempts, vault access from new device/location within minutes of phishing campaign, or multiple vault exports in short window.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Exfiltration from Password Manager Vault
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'entire vault' stolen—wholesale credential export not modeled in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect export of password manager vault to non-corporate destination, bulk sync API calls to external storage (AWS, Azure), or credential database copied to USB/network share.

suggestion.title: PIN Compromise via Phishing or Malware
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires initial PIN capture; title implies compromised PIN but no detection for PIN-theft vector (phishing, keylogger, screen recording).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing URLs impersonating Google auth, malware with keylogging/screen-capture capabilities targeting password-manager processes, or credential-theft payloads in email attachments.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Account Recovery Preceding Vault Access
suggestion.rationale: Vault unlock implies prior account compromise; no detection for account-recovery abuse or session hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful account recovery using backup codes/SMS verification within 1 hour of failed login spike, followed by password manager vault access from new IP.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Extension or Password Manager Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: VaultJacking implies direct credential-store access; no detection for browser-level tampering or extension abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rogue extensions with password-manager permissions, unsigned DLLs injected into chrome.exe, or unauthorized modifications to Chrome profile directories containing credential databases.

suggestion.title: MDM Bypass via Supply Chain Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'What MDM can't protect' implies supply chain vectors (npm, pip, gem malware). MDM cannot prevent malicious package installation on dev machines if package registry is compromised or if attacker publishes to public registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious package manager invocations (npm install, pip install, gem install) with network IOCs (typosquatted or known-malicious registries). Alert on packages writing to unexpected paths (/usr/bin, /etc, /var/spool). Correlate with process execution immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: SSH Key Theft from Developer Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: MDM cannot protect unencrypted SSH keys stored in ~/.ssh on developer machines. Article likely covers local attack vectors MDM misses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file reads from ~/.ssh/ by non-SSH processes (rsync, tar, curl, SCP, browsers, Python scripts). Alert on bulk reads of private key files. Monitor for SSH key material exfiltration via process command lines or network.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Dev Tools
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines often run unpatched build tools, compilers, and local services with escalation paths. MDM typically doesn't harden dev-specific software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on calls to setuid binaries, sudo with NOPASSWD entries, or cargo/npm pre/post install scripts running with elevated privileges. Monitor for exploitation of known dev-tool CVEs (npm audit, cargo audit misses).

suggestion.title: Browser-Based Credential Harvesting from Dev Machines
suggestion.rationale: MDM cannot prevent attackers from harvesting credentials stored in browser password managers or GitHub/GitLab tokens in plaintext config files on developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on browser process access to AppData\Roaming (Windows) or ~/.config (Linux) where password stores live. Monitor for .env, .netrc, .aws/credentials reads by non-privileged processes. Flag exfiltration of credential files.

suggestion.title: Malware via Compromised IDE Plugins
suggestion.rationale: MDM cannot prevent installation of malicious VS Code, JetBrains, or Eclipse extensions. These run with developer privileges and can steal code, credentials, or inject backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin directory changes (extensions folders). Alert on network traffic from IDE processes to non-standard domains. Flag writes to IDE plugin directories outside normal update windows. Correlate with known malicious plugin hashes.

suggestion.title: Container Image Manipulation and Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines run Docker/Podman; MDM cannot prevent pulling malicious container images or building backdoored images locally before pushing to registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected docker/podman image pulls from untrusted registries or with abnormally large layer counts. Flag builds that execute network commands or write to sensitive paths. Monitor for image push events after suspicious local modifications.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious AI Chatbot Recommendation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes chatbot 'recommendations' as the attack vector. The phrase 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users' indicates the compromise is in the recommendation engine itself. Pipeline missed this initial-access pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual recommendation outputs from AI chatbot services pointing to newly-registered or suspicious domains. Correlate chatbot logs with external domain reputation. Flag high-entropy recommendation patterns diverging from baseline (indicators of prompt injection or model compromise).

suggestion.title: Detect Redirect Chains from Chatbot to Cryptojacking Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states recommendations 'redirect users to cryptojacking malware sites'—implying URL chains or intermediate redirectors. Pipeline generated no detection for redirect-based infection chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify redirect chains originating from known AI service domains (ChatGPT, Claude, Bard, etc.) where the final destination is flagged as cryptomining, suspicious, or newly-registered. Correlate user-agent (chatbot client or browser) with destination reputation and payload signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect Cryptomining Process Activity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is cryptojacking malware infection. Pipeline should have surfaced post-execution detection for xmrig, monero miners, or CPU-intensive unsigned processes typical of cryptomining payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning or execution of common cryptomining tools (xmrig, monero-miner, ccminer) or unsigned/suspicious processes with high sustained CPU usage and outbound connections to known mining pools. Correlate with recent downloads from user-reported chatbot recommendations.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Compromised AI Model Outputs Containing Malicious URLs
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is the AI model itself returning malicious content. Pipeline should flag detections for anomalous model outputs (e.g., recommendations diverging from fine-tuned behavior, unexpected URL injection patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM output logs for URL recommendations outside normal domain sets, newly-registered domains, or domains categorized as malware/phishing. Establish baseline recommendation patterns and alert on statistical anomalies. Cross-reference recommended URLs against threat-intel feeds in real-time.

suggestion.title: Detect User Downloads/Execution Following Chatbot-Recommended URLs
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain requires user to follow the recommendation and execute malware. Pipeline should have surfaced detection for file downloads preceded by chatbot-recommended domain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate proxy logs showing access to URLs matching chatbot recommendations with subsequent unsigned executable downloads or file writes to temp directories, followed by process creation with suspicious network activity.

suggestion.title: Alert on Newly-Registered Domains Coinciding with Chatbot Recommendation Surge
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking campaigns rely on short-lived infrastructure. Article implies redirection to 'malware sites'—likely newly-registered, bulk-registered domains. Pipeline should correlate domain age with chatbot recommendation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly-registered domains (<7 days old) appearing in chatbot recommendations or as redirect destinations from chatbot traffic. Correlate registration patterns with known cryptojacking infrastructure registrars. Alert on bulk registrations linked to single registrant or infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45321 TanStack Vulnerable Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious versions of the product to be published to the npm registry'—requires inventory and execution detection for TanStack installs during vulnerable window (2026-05-20 to 2026-05-27). Pipeline output was empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm install/update operations for TanStack package versions released between 2026-05-20 and 2026-05-27. Cross-reference against host inventory. Alert on NodeJS process execution with malicious TanStack versions loaded into node_modules, particularly in production or internet-facing contexts.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration: Post-Package-Installation Secrets Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing malware' payload explicitly—pipeline missed detection for suspicious credential access and exfiltration behavior following TanStack installation.
log_sources: SecurityEvent (4688 process access to LSASS, 4657 reg changes)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate TanStack package installation with subsequent credential-access indicators within 60 minutes: LSASS memory reads, .aws/credentials or .ssh enumeration, environment variable dumps (node.js process), unexpected authentication events, or outbound TLS connections from NodeJS to unknown C2 IPs.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Account Anomaly: Trusted Identity Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malicious versions published 'under a trusted identity'—indicates account takeover or credential compromise at registry level. Pipeline missed supply-chain source detection.
log_sources: authentication logs (2FA events, new device logins)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt npm account activity for TanStack maintainers during 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-27: new API tokens, publish events from atypical geography/IP, disabled 2FA, rapid consecutive version bumps, or republication of existing versions. Cross-match against known credentials leaked in recent dumps or account-takeover campaigns.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Execution Post-Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes 'known ransomware use'—indicates downstream lateral movement and impact. Pipeline generated no detection for ransomware deployment correlated with credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ransomware execution patterns on hosts where TanStack was installed and credentials were accessed: spawning of known ransomware process signatures, bulk file encryption (.encrypted extensions, CryptAPI calls), registry modifications disabling recovery (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\vss, Shadow Copies deletion), or ransom note (.txt/.html in root directories).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-45321 Inventory & Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Standard KEV hunt required by article template reference (asset-exposure), with federal due date 2026-06-10. Pipeline produced no templated Splunk SPL or Defender KQL for package-level vulnerability scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package inventories for TanStack presence. Match package versions against CISA KEV advisory for CVE-2026-45321. Generate remediation list prioritizing production, public-facing, and internet-exposed systems. Splunk: `index=main cve=CVE-2026-45321 OR package=TanStack | stats values(version) by host, owner` ; Defender: `DeviceSoftwareInventory | where SoftwareName contains "TanStack" | where SoftwareVersion between(2026-05-20, 2026-05-27)`.

suggestion.title: npm Artifact Integrity: Signature Verification Bypass or Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential-stealing malware in 'trusted' package—indicates either signature verification failure or trust violation. Pipeline missed detection for artifact integrity compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm installation logs for signature mismatches, integrity check bypasses (--no-audit, --ignore-scripts flags), or warnings suppressed on TanStack package downloads during 2026-05-20 to 2026-05-27. Cross-reference published tarball SHA-512 hashes against official TanStack GitHub releases for discrepancies indicating tampering.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Detected in Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states in Recommended Hunts: 'CVE: CVE-2026-8398 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Pipeline extracted zero UCs despite clear directive to hunt this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result flagging CVE-2026-8398. Cross-reference against asset inventory to identify unpatched Daemon Tools Lite instances prior to 2026-05-30 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Software Inventory Asset-Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' templates. Identifying Daemon Tools Lite installations is the prerequisite detection for exposure assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all endpoints with Daemon Tools Lite installed via software inventory, process execution (daemon.exe, DaemonToolsManager), or registry artifacts. Prioritize for remediation by federal due date.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Unauth­orized Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability has 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability'—typical of arbitrary code-execution flaws in system-level tools. Compromised Daemon Tools instances would spawn cmd/powershell as attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag parent process=daemon.exe or DaemonToolsManager spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shell/scripting children. Tune for absence of interactive user session or outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Post-Deadline Unpatched CVE-2026-8398 Systems
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date is 2026-05-30 per article. Any system running vulnerable Daemon Tools Lite after deadline is compliance violation and active exploitation target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-deadline query (2026-05-31 onward) for assets still flagged with CVE-2026-8398 and Daemon Tools Lite version <patched. Escalate as critical compliance and incident risk.

suggestion.title: Automated API Endpoint Enumeration at Machine Speed
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' Detection should identify rapid, systematic API discovery patterns inconsistent with human interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential API endpoint requests from single source over short time window (e.g., >50 unique paths per minute), particularly with 404/403 responses. Flag patterns inconsistent with typical client SDKs or documented API workflows.

suggestion.title: BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization) Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BOLA detection works by 'authorization probes guided by structural reasoning' to detect users accessing resources they shouldn't. Real attacks will manifest as sequential ID-manipulation attempts across objects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patterns of sequential API calls to resources differing only by object/user ID parameter, especially with mixed success/failure codes or data exfiltration post-access. Baseline per user/role expected ID ranges.

suggestion.title: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) Exploitation via Cross-Tenant Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists IDOR and 'cross-tenant data leakage' as context-dependent vulnerabilities without heuristic signatures. Exploitation manifests as unauthorized resource access by manipulating direct references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls where authenticated user accesses resources owned by different tenant/user ID. Flag if access pattern shows exploration (multiple different IDs) rather than single misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation of Multiple Vulnerability Steps
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' Detection must correlate seemingly low-risk actions into high-risk sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create correlation rule: failed authorization → privilege escalation attempt → data access. Alert if sequence occurs within 5min window. Baseline expected chains per user; flag novel sequences even if individual steps appear low-risk.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Detection via Systematic Probe Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as context-dependent vulnerabilities that AI can now detect through reasoning. Attackers will probe these systematically via API layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated authentication failures from single source followed by sudden successful access without credential re-submission. Flag session anomalies (e.g., bypass of MFA step, token reuse across identities).

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Voice Call - IT Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous inbound calls claiming to be internal IT support, especially those requesting immediate remote access enablement. Correlate with user-reported helpdesk impersonation tickets. Flag calls from external DIDs to legal/financial firms during business hours with IT support pretext.

suggestion.title: RDP Access Granted via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' RDP logons following phishing email or voice call within short timeframe are suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP successful logons (4624 Event ID 10) within 30 min of inbound phishing email or reported voice call requesting access. Focus on logons from external IPs to legal firm workstations, especially from users not typically receiving RDP requests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB/External Storage Device Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'By going to the victim's location in person, the malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.' Also listed as explicit indicator: 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected USB or external drive connections, especially to high-value targets (finance, legal workstations). Monitor for rapid file access to external media post-connection. Alert on unknown vendor IDs or multiple connection/disconnect cycles within short duration.

suggestion.title: Unidentified Personnel Physical Access - IT Support Pretext
suggestion.rationale: Article lists indicator: 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers.' In-person data theft requires physical facility breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate badge access events with facilities: flag entries by non-badged personnel in IT support uniform or claiming IT role. Cross-reference visitor logs with reported IT support calls within 4-hour window. Alert on CCTV: unknown personnel accessing server rooms or employee workstations.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with IT Support Portal Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Phishing emails direct users to malicious lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with links to typosquatted IT support portal domains (e.g., 'IT-support[.]firm[.]com' vs 'itsupport[.]firm[.]com'). Alert on clicks to single-character or homoglyph domain variants. Monitor for credential submission to lookalike portals.

suggestion.title: Extortion Communications and Ransom Threat Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients.' Post-exfiltration threat communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails threatening data disclosure, referencing recent data theft, or demanding ransom payment. Correlate threatening emails with prior data exfiltration events or known SRG leak sites. Monitor employee reports of extortion calls claiming access to stolen data.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API authentication + algorithm modification in sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated user with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit.' Pipeline missed the initial authentication/privilege check. Need to detect account with elevated Yamcs privilege suddenly modifying algorithms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user account with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege (via Yamcs RBAC logs) followed within minutes by PATCH /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* request. Flag if account is new to that privilege role or last used >90 days ago.

suggestion.title: Janino expression compilation with dangerous imports/methods
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text without enforcing a secure sandbox.' Need detection on the compilation phase itself, not just post-RCE shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs debug/info logs for JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory compilation errors or warnings. Alert if compilation output contains patterns like 'import java.lang.Runtime', 'ProcessBuilder', 'exec', or reflection APIs. Baseline normal algorithm compilation and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Database write to Yamcs algorithm table with suspicious content
suggestion.rationale: Article describes update to mission database algorithms as attack vector. Need detection at database transaction layer, not just HTTP API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on INSERT or UPDATE to [algorithms] table containing Java keywords (Runtime, exec, ProcessBuilder, getRuntime) or suspicious method calls. Correlate to user with ChangeMissionDatabase role.

suggestion.title: Unexpected privilege elevation to ChangeMissionDatabase role
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' as prerequisite. Missing detection for privilege escalation or new role grants that would enable this exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when user account is granted ChangeMissionDatabase role outside normal change window, or role is granted to account with no prior Yamcs activity. Flag if role grant precedes PATCH algorithm requests by <1 hour.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Template Filter Escape Attempts (SSTI Gadget Chain Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly demonstrates attack: `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}` to expose `this` context. No detection for filter-chain bypass patterns in template inputs.
log_sources: Application logs with template processing traces
HTTP request payloads (POST bodies, template variables)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs and request payloads for LiquidJS filter operators that are known to enable context escape: valueOf, inspect, __proto__, getBuiltinModule, execSync. Flag sequences where these filters are chained in template assignment or rendering contexts, especially if targeting dangerous properties like context.scopes or liquid.options.

suggestion.title: Dangerous Node.js Module Access via LiquidJS (child_process, fs module loading)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE mechanism via access to child_process module through object traversal: `r.liquid.options.fs`, `getBuiltinModule('child_process')`. No detection for when these modules are accessed in template-rendering context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate template-processing application activity with child_process or fs module loads/executions. Look for process spawning (cmd.exe, sh, bash, powershell) where the parent is a Node.js template engine and module access was preceded by suspicious filter operations within seconds.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Context Information Leakage (Error Responses / Debug Output)
suggestion.rationale: Article includes raw JSON context dump showing internal structure: `{"context":{"scopes":[{"r":"[Circular]"}],...}}`. Attackers use error responses to map object graph.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses containing LiquidJS internal context structures (Circular references, scopes arrays, registers objects, internal opts) in error messages or verbose output. Flag systematic requests followed by 500/502 errors containing such leakage, suggesting reconnaissance phase prior to exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious __proto__ or Prototype Pollution Patterns in Templates
suggestion.rationale: Article payload references `assign __proto__` pattern for prototype chain pollution. This technique bypasses intended template restrictions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for __proto__, constructor, prototype keywords in template assignment contexts or filter chains. Even single occurrences warrant investigation in a LiquidJS application, as legitimate templates have no reason to manipulate JavaScript prototypes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Against World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly list 'phishing' as a primary attack vector; description states 'ransomware groups, state-aligned actors' are threats. Pipeline extracted nothing despite this clear initial-access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with typosquatted World Cup domains, suspicious sender reputation, and attachment/link patterns associated with ransomware distribution. Flag emails targeting tournament infrastructure, vendor, or ticketing domains with credential-harvesting or malware payloads.

suggestion.title: QR Code Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'QR Codes' as attack surface; no use case generated despite this being a specific, detectable initial-access pattern distinct from standard phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails or documents containing embedded or referenced QR codes that decode to suspicious URLs (shortened URLs, newly registered domains, non-HTTPS). Flag execution of browsers or QR-scanning tools immediately following user interaction with such codes.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration and Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'typosquatting'; article discusses attack surface against world cup infrastructure. Pipeline should surface domain-registration and DNS/HTTP traffic detection for misspelled official domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains visually similar to official FIFA/tournament domains (single-character substitutions, homograph variants). Cross-reference against active phishing campaigns and known actor infrastructure. Alert on employee/staff click-through to typosquatted sites.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Execution and Mass File Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'wiper'; article context implies infrastructure targeting. Pipeline must generate detection for destructive post-compromise activity that would cause tournament disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file deletion operations (>1000 files in short timeframe), wiper-associated process execution (DiskPart, cipher.exe, shred utilities), Master Boot Record/partition table modifications, and sudden spike in file-access errors across critical infrastructure segments.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Encryption and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article description states 'ransomware groups' are primary threat actors. Keywords omit explicit ransomware indicators but context demands detection for encryption, ransom note creation, and infrastructure-wide propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file-encryption patterns (.exe/.bat processes creating .ENCRYPTED/.LOCKED files), ransom note drops (README.txt/HOW_TO_RECOVER.txt), SMB lateral-movement spikes, and encrypted RDP/SSH tunneling to external IPs typical of ransomware propagation.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor C2 Beaconing and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'state-aligned actors' by name (Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra, Razing Ursa). Pipeline must include command-and-control and exfiltration detections keyed to known infrastructure/behavior signatures for these groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline C2 domains/IPs associated with named threat actors. Flag outbound traffic to known actor infrastructure, anomalous DNS patterns (subdomain enumeration, DGA-like queries), and encrypted tunnel establishment from critical hosts. Cross-reference Shodan/passive DNS for staging.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation Post-Token Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious npm package distributed as supply-chain attack vector: 'AI-Generated npm Malware' — requires detection of package installation anomalies (unusual source, missing metadata, execution before install complete).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry requests and package installations for unsigned packages, packages from newly-created accounts, or installations that trigger unexpected child processes (Node.js script execution outside expected directories). Correlate with known malicious package hashes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token Usage After Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Core incident: 'Threat Actor's Private GitHub Token' exposed — requires detection of exposed credential use: API calls using exposed token, unauthorized repository access, branch protection bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls using personal access tokens from anomalous geolocations, unusual user-agents, or at times outside user's normal activity window. Monitor for token usage attempts after token exposure indicators (leaked in public commits, error messages, malware payloads).

suggestion.title: Secrets (Credentials/Tokens) in npm Package Source Code
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: malware exposed threat actor's GitHub token via npm package code itself — 'accidentally exposes' indicates hardcoded secrets. Requires detection of committed credentials in package publishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source tarballs for hardcoded secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS keys, API credentials) before/after publication. Alert on packages containing entropy-high strings matching credential patterns. Cross-reference exposed tokens against GitHub/AWS revocation logs.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Obfuscated Code Execution in npm Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'AI-Generated' malware, implying heavy obfuscation/evasion — requires detection of eval-like constructs, polymorphic payloads, and behavioral anomalies rather than signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes spawned from npm module directories with suspicious behaviors: outbound C2 connections, unexpected child processes (curl, wget, bash), file writes to sensitive locations, or unusual interpreter invocations (eval, Function constructors in require()d modules).

suggestion.title: npm Package Update/Installation Trigger Unusual Outbound Network
suggestion.rationale: Malware executed post-installation; article context suggests data exfiltration via exposed token or C2 callback after package install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package installations with subsequent network connections to non-standard destinations (not npm registry, GitHub, or expected CDNs). Flag connections to newly-registered domains, known C2 infrastructure, or data exfiltration services within minutes of package install.

suggestion.title: Detection of Redirects to Fake Google Play Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play' — traffic to domains impersonating the legitimate Play Store is detectable initial-access indicator; pipeline extracted zero use cases for this attack step
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for redirect chains (especially from phishing domains) resolving to domains mimicking 'play.google.com' or hosting lookalike Play Store interfaces. Flag redirects originating from streaming/crypto-themed domains to play-store clones.

suggestion.title: Detection of Accessibility Service Permission Grants to Untrusted Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction' — this is the privilege-escalation vector and warrants detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Accessibility Service permissions are granted to recently-installed apps, especially those not from official Play Store. Cross-reference with package installer source logs and privilege escalation behavior.

suggestion.title: Detection of Google Play Store / Play Protect Disable Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware allows operators to 'disable Google Play, hide its icon' — direct defense-evasion configuration; pipeline missed this defense-evasion step entirely
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to disable Google Play Store or Play Protect via pm disable-user, package manager modifications, or Settings intent manipulation. Alert on rapid disabling of security features post-installation.

suggestion.title: Detection of App Icon Hiding / Launcher Component Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware can 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device' — icon hiding is standard Android evasion tactic with detectable log signatures
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps requesting HIDE_FROM_LAUNCHER permission or disabling the MAIN activity component alias. Flag visibility toggles on recently-installed apps within first few minutes post-install.

suggestion.title: Detection of Malicious APK Installation from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps' from 'fake Google Play sites' — side-loaded APK execution is the execution phase with strong log signals
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK installations from external storage, third-party app stores, or adb side-loading. Correlate with recent user clicks on phishing links or browser downloads of .apk files.

suggestion.title: Detection of Financial Transaction Interception and API Hooking
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'intercepting financial transactions' as core BTMOB capability — malware hooking banking app APIs or injecting content into WebViews is the collection phase with detectable process-level signals
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process injection, shared library loading, or Java reflection APIs targeting banking/payment apps. Detect unexpected WebView content handlers or network traffic interception by non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system.' The social engineering attack is the initial compromise vector and should trigger detection of phishing attempts or unusual account enrollment patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor employee email systems for phishing/social engineering lures targeting IT personnel; detect unusual account logon patterns (new geographies, devices, times) within 24 hours of suspicious email delivery; flag failed and successful MFA challenges clustered in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Activity on Compromised Employee Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'On April 14, 2026, the Company's IT security team identified unauthorized activity involving an employee's account.' The unauthorized activity indicates anomalous use of the compromised credential that should be detectable via access pattern deviation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logons from the compromised employee account outside historical baselines (unusual times, geolocations, devices); flag rapid sequential access to multiple systems or data repositories; alert on access to resources the employee role should not access (e.g., IT infrastructure, executive systems, loyalty program databases).

suggestion.title: Bulk Exfiltration of Mariner Society Loyalty Program Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the bad actor illegally copied personal information... data contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program... included names, dates of birth, genders and data relating to status' and attackers claimed '8.7 million records' plus 'terabytes of internal corporate data.' Bulk data movement of structured PII must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-volume data downloads or copies from loyalty program databases; flag queries exfiltrating PII fields (name, DOB, email, gender, geographic location, loyalty status) in bulk; detect unusual data staging or archive creation followed by egress; alert on unauthorized access to the Mariner Society database from non-approved service accounts or employee accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Employee Account to Data Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative chain: employee account compromised (April 14) → unauthorized actor gains 'access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system' → accesses Mariner Society loyalty database. This progression implies lateral movement from the initial foothold to backend data systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RDP/SSH connections originating from the compromised employee account to server infrastructure; detect reconnaissance activity (file shares enumeration, network discovery) from the compromised account; flag escalated privileges or new logon sessions on backend database systems correlated with the compromised account's first activity.

suggestion.title: Attacker Persistence via Retained Credentials or Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Timeline indicates breach on April 10 but detection not until April 14 (4-day gap), and exfiltration continued through April 22 (12 days post-detection before Carnival took action). Prolonged dwell time suggests attacker maintained persistence despite detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple logons to the compromised account from different source IPs after initial detection (April 14–22); monitor for creation of new local or domain accounts with elevated privileges during the incident window; flag persistent connections or scheduled tasks created on compromised systems; alert on RDP/SSH sessions that span the 8-day post-detection dwell period.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Threat Group Activity Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly attributes breach to 'ShinyHunters extortion gang' and notes 'Over the past year, ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers... Salesloft Drift campaign and the Salesforce Aura data theft attacks.' Known-threat-actor activity should be enriched with historical TTPs and infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Carnival compromise indicators against ShinyHunters' known infrastructure from Salesforce/Salesloft campaigns (domains, IPs, email patterns); monitor for communications from known ShinyHunters distribution channels or marketplace listings; alert if Carnival employees receive phishing emails similar in pattern/payload to Salesforce customer campaigns attributed to ShinyHunters.

suggestion.title: ClearFake Malware Process/File Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ClearFake' as the malware. Pipeline should have surfaced process execution, registry, or file-based indicators tied to ClearFake installation. No attempt to create baseline detections around the named actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ClearFake-related process names, parent-child relationships, registry modifications, or file paths. ClearFake likely masquerades as legitimate software while maintaining hidden network communication to blockchain C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: BSC Testnet RPC Endpoint Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'BSC Testnet Smart Contracts' for C2; malware must discover and query BSC Testnet RPC endpoints. Pipeline failed to create detection for anomalous queries to blockchain RPC providers (rpc.testnet.binance.org, similar).
