suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections from dev-class hostnames (dev-, laptop-, workstation-) to AWS/Azure/GCP CIDR blocks within minutes of VS Code RCE indicators on source host.

suggestion.title: SSH Config or Key File Modification by VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE-to-pivot chain requires persistence: attacker must add SSH keys or modify config. Article implies this attack chain but pipeline surfaced no persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/config, or ~/.ssh/id_* outside change-control windows, triggered by execution context chain linking to VS Code RCE activity.

suggestion.title: Remote-SSH Extension Argument Injection in Process Command Line
suggestion.rationale: RCE vectors in SSH-based IDEs typically exploit shell metacharacter handling or argument injection in remote command construction; no detection generated for malicious SSH extension parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan VS Code/ExtensionHost command lines for shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes) in SSH connection arguments or suspicious ExtensionHost flags; compare against baseline Remote-SSH invocation signatures.

suggestion.title: Cloud CLI Tool Invocation Correlated with Dev Machine Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Post-pivot impact requires cloud API/CLI execution (aws-cli, Azure CLI, gcloud). Should detect cloud tooling spawned on compromised developer machine shortly after RCE indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate RCE/SSH indicators on developer host with subsequent aws-cli, az, or gcloud process creation, especially with env-var credential passing or non-standard user execution context.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credentials in Docker RUN Commands and Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Passing passwords via command arguments' and 'Use of default passwords'—credentials can be extracted from image layers, container metadata, and parent process environment at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dockerfile RUN directives and docker run commands for password flags (-p, --password, --secret). Alert on environment variables matching credential patterns (PASSWORD, API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD_HASH). Cross-reference image layer metadata against credential regex patterns.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Misconfigured Sudo in Containers
suggestion.rationale: Article section 'Attacks on sudo' and 'Insecure file permissions' highlight sudo NOPASSWD rules and overprivileged capabilities as container-to-host escape primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo executions within containers with NOPASSWD sudoers entries. Alert on containers running with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN. Monitor for non-root child processes calling getuid(2) repeatedly—sign of privilege boundary testing.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Vulnerable or Unsigned Base Images
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'Software vulnerabilities and compromise of update sources'—base images from Docker Hub often persist outdated libraries and unsigned layers, enabling supply-chain backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate container images by SHA256 and cross-reference against CVE feeds and image signature validation. Flag images pulled from non-approved registries. Alert on image promotion to production without OCI image signature or Docker Content Trust verification.

suggestion.title: Default Credentials Used in Containerized Services
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Use of default passwords'—containerized databases, SSH services, and web consoles often retain factory credentials, exploitable at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline successful authentication events for containerized services (postgres, mysql, redis, SSH). Alert on logins using common default accounts (admin, root, postgres, mongodb) from external networks. Correlate with container startup events to catch ephemeral instances.

suggestion.title: Lack of Container Layer Integrity Verification at Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article section 'Lack of integrity checks' notes containers frequently run without signature or hash attestation, enabling layer substitution and trojanization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate cryptographic baseline of approved container layers. Alert when container startup occurs with layer digest mismatch or missing signature. Monitor for image pull events where Docker Content Trust is disabled or skipped.

suggestion.title: World Cup Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'phishing' as a threat vector targeting World Cup infrastructure. No phishing use cases were generated despite this being a primary attack method mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spearphishing emails and URLs using World Cup lures, official tournament domains, or credential harvesting pages mimicking FIFA/venue ticketing systems. Flag emails with suspicious sender reputation, mismatched domains, or shortened/obfuscated URLs.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration for World Cup Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'typosquatting' as a threat vector. No detection use case was created for monitoring typosquatting domains targeting World Cup infrastructure or FIFA entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and passive DNS registrations for World Cup typosquatting domains (FIFA variants, official venue domains with character swaps, ticket vendors). Flag registrations by known typosquatting actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: QR Code-Based Malware Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords mention 'QR Codes' as an attack vector but pipeline generated no use cases for QR code exploitation. Should detect QR code usage in phishing and malware delivery campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email attachments and URLs containing QR code images or embedded QR data. Alert on QR codes pointing to known malware C2, credential harvesting pages, or suspicious shortened URLs. Cross-reference with World Cup-themed email subjects.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Execution Targeting World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'wiper' malware as a threat but no impact-phase detection use case was generated for wiper deployment or execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wiper malware execution via suspicious process cmdlines using disk/partition wiping tools (cipher.exe, format, dd), registry modifications targeting boot sectors, or large sequential file deletions. Correlate with lateral movement or persistence indicators in tournament IT environments.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse by Non-System Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'it abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is a high-confidence detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when non-system APKs (especially those from non-Google Play sources) request and receive Accessibility Service permissions. Look for permission grants immediately following suspicious app installation. Cross-reference against known-malicious package names or hash signatures.

suggestion.title: Installation from Non-Official App Store Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' This is the primary distribution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains that spoof Google Play (certificate mismatches, lookalike domains, redirects from phishing sites). Correlate with APK installations that follow within minutes. Flag if installation source is not play.google.com or official distributor domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious APK Permission Combinations for Financial Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'stealing specific data, intercepting financial transactions, capturing screenshots, and remote control capabilities' and customizable permission selection via builder. The combination of SMS/CALL + CAMERA + INTERNET is anomalous for most legitimate apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create a rule that flags APK manifests requesting unusual permission combinations: {READ_SMS OR READ_CALL_LOG} + CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO + ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + INTERNET. Priority increases if app claims to be a streaming service, crypto miner, or messaging app but requests financial-access permissions.

suggestion.title: Malware Builder Platform Activity (C2 Infrastructure)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The APK builder included in the offer provides easy customization' and 'sales are conducted in private Telegram channels' at $700/month. Detecting access to or use of the builder platform by enterprise users is a proxy detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS traffic to the BTMOB clearnet site (if domain is known) or Telegram bot interactions that match builder signature (APK customization requests, permission parameter exchange). Detect successful APK downloads followed by rapid re-upload/redistribution patterns.

suggestion.title: Phishing Lure Hosting Infrastructure (Fake Service Domains)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'distributed via phishing websites masquerading as streaming services and cryptocurrency mining platforms' and 'Argentinian government agency as a lure.' Domain registration and hosting patterns cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations that mimic legitimate streaming services or government portals using homograph variants or typosquatting. Cross-reference WHOIS changes, certificate issuer patterns, and temporal clustering (multiple registrations in same timeframe). Flag if domain serves APK binaries and has low ASN diversity.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'intercepting financial transactions' as a core capability. Detection requires monitoring for non-standard process injection or activity in banking/payment app sandboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for hooking/injection into banking and payment app processes (PayPal, Stripe, local banking apps). Detect if a child process spawns from an APK with Accessibility Services enabled and communicates over unexpected sockets. Look for process memory regions containing known banking APIs or transaction keywords.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system.' Initial access vector is explicit and must trigger phishing/social engineering detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee email accounts receiving phishing indicators followed by anomalous login within hours (atypical location, time, device). Correlate email security events with successful logons from the same account within 24-72 hours of social engineering attempt.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'illegally copied personal information' and ShinyHunters 'stole documents containing over 8.7 million records with personally identifiable information and terabytes of internal corporate data.' Massive data volume movement should be anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag single-user accounts executing queries or exports returning >1M rows from customer/loyalty databases, or copying GB/TB-scale data from file shares in a single session. Baseline normal data access volumes per role.

suggestion.title: Mariner Society Loyalty Database Anomalous Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'data contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program' with 'names, dates of birth, genders and data relating to status within the loyalty program.' Application-level detection on loyalty system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Mariner Society database for unscheduled bulk SELECT operations on customer_pii or similar tables; alert if non-admin account executes queries returning entire customer sets or loyalty tiers in one transaction.

suggestion.title: Extended Dwell Time Indicator (4-Day Access Window)
suggestion.rationale: Article timeline: breach April 10, unauthorized activity detected April 14, determination of data theft April 22. 4-day undetected access suggests insufficient real-time monitoring of new account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for account access patterns on day 1; trigger alerts within 6 hours if account suddenly accesses systems outside normal role scope. Reduce dwell-time detection SLA to <24 hours.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Salesforce Targeting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers and has breached hundreds of companies worldwide, claiming to have stolen billions of records in the Salesloft Drift campaign and the Salesforce Aura data theft attacks.' Carnival may use Salesforce; orgs should correlate with Aura breach tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Salesforce-using organizations: correlate Carnival breach April 10 timeline with known Aura/Drift-campaign email domains or phishing indicators. Monitor for accounts exhibiting Carnival-timeline-concurrent credential reuse or Salesforce API key exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized IT System Lateral Access from Employee Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gained access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system' after social engineering. Access was not to email alone but to backend IT infrastructure, suggesting lateral movement from initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised employee accounts accessing IT infrastructure (servers, backup systems, databases) outside normal job function. Flag RDP/SSH connections from employee workstations to data-center IPs, especially if preceded by phishing attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Following Gogs Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'authenticated user execute arbitrary code'—authentication is prerequisite for exploit trigger. Pipeline missed detection for execution phase post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child process spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) originating from Gogs process context (gogs, git-daemon, gitea-equiv binary) or user session within 5 minutes of Gogs authentication log entry. Execution from unexpected parent (web server proc) is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Git Hooks / Deploy Keys in Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Gogs is Git hosting platform; authenticated RCE likely routes through Git hooks, post-receive scripts, or SSH key abuse. Article doesn't detail mechanism but this is standard Gogs attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .git/hooks/ file creation or modification within Gogs repository directories, followed by shell invocations. Detect SSH key injection (authorized_keys write) in git user home or Gogs data paths.

suggestion.title: Authenticated User Creates / Modifies Repository Hooks in Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation indicator: authenticated user must add malicious hook. Article says 'any authenticated user'—this is the setup phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT to /api/v1/repos/{user}/{repo}/hooks or direct filesystem writes to .git/hooks/ subdirectories by non-repo-owner accounts or service accounts, especially with unusual Content-Type or payload size.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Data Exfiltration Post-Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'execute arbitrary code' but provides no IOCs for post-exploitation C2. Detection should assume attacker opens reverse shell or exfils data after code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After Gogs process or child execution detected, flag outbound network connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially ports 443, 4444, 8888, 9999 or ephemeral ranges. Combine with process lineage (parent=git/gogs daemon).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Gogs Process to System Account
suggestion.rationale: Gogs service typically runs unprivileged; real-world attacks escalate. Article doesn't detail if RCE is unauthenticated-to-admin or privesc is separate, but missing from analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process token elevation, sudo invocation, or UAC bypass attempts originating from Gogs process tree. Flag setuid/setgid binary execution (e.g., gpasswd, pkexec) by Gogs user.

suggestion.title: Gogs Admin Account Creation or SSH Key Injection
suggestion.rationale: Authenticated RCE often persists via new admin user or SSH backdoor. Article doesn't mention persistence mechanism; this is critical detection gap for post-compromise hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs user/org creation API calls (esp. with admin=true), SSH public key additions to non-user-initiated accounts, and direct database inserts into user tables. Correlate with RCE process execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain Malware Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Lazarus...compromised axios lead maintainer's credentials to publish malicious versions...injected trojanized code into affected systems' (100M+ weekly downloads). Pipeline extracted zero supply-chain detection despite explicit exploitation of npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installations from unusual sources, detect hash mismatches against published registry, monitor Node.js child process spawning for unexpected network connections, and alert on JavaScript execution loading non-bundled dependencies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti VPN Appliance Exploitation (PhiliKit/UNC5221 SPAWN)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PhiliKit, new implant assessed part of UNC5221's SPAWN toolset targeting Ivanti VPN appliances.' Pipeline failed to surface any detection for this named vulnerability campaign with specific infrastructure target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti VPN administrative interfaces for authentication anomalies, unusual privilege escalations, and known CVE exploitation signatures. Detect beaconing to UNC5221 C2 infrastructure post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Bootkit-Style Wiper Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Rusty Boots and MoKhargosh...demonstrated destructive potential including deployment of bootkit-style wiper and retaining destructive tooling.' Pipeline completely omitted any wiper/bootkit detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/suspicious driver loading, modifications to boot sector or bootloader registry hives, SYSTEM-context processes targeting disk structures, and attempts to disable recovery mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Rook Ransomware Lateral Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel...attempted to spread Rook ransomware within engineering company.' Pipeline extracted zero ransomware-specific detection despite named family and explicit propagation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Rook-specific file extensions and encryption patterns, detect file encryption APIs in rapid-fire succession, alert on SMB lateral movement to adjacent systems, and identify ransom note creation and C2 callback patterns.

suggestion.title: TigerRAT Command & Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel...deployed TigerRAT...within engineering company.' No detection use cases for TigerRAT beaconing, RAT capabilities (screen capture, exfiltration), or persistence mechanisms were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TigerRAT process creation patterns, detect C2 communication via HTTP/HTTPS beaconing, monitor for screen capture and file enumeration APIs, and identify persistence via scheduled tasks or registry run keys.

suggestion.title: North Korean Developer-Targeted Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Lazarus and DeceptiveDevelopment...invested in long-term relationship building...Kimsuky and Konni favored quicker...attacks' targeting 'developers and cryptocurrency ecosystem with social engineering schemes.' Pipeline failed to create detection for phishing/credential-harvesting targeting dev platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails impersonating cryptocurrency platforms and developer recruitment, flag unusual authentication from compromised developer accounts, monitor GitHub/npm API activity anomalies, and alert on attacker-controlled URLs in developer communities.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'fake domains impersonate the official fifa.com, but rely on minor spelling changes that users are likely to miss, such as fiffa[.]com, and use alternative top-level domains (e.g., .org, .xyz, .live, .sale)'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for domains matching FIFA typosquatting patterns (fiffa, fifa-*, *fifa) with non-standard TLDs (.xyz, .live, .sale, .org). Flag requests from inside the network, especially during World Cup period (June-July 2026).

suggestion.title: Suspicious FIFA Employment Portal Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names: 'fake employment portals like "jobs-fifa[.]com" or "fifa-hiring[.]com"'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on newly registered domains matching jobs-fifa*, fifa-hiring*, or *fifa-careers patterns. Cross-reference WHOIS data for suspicious registrar or privacy proxies. Correlate with known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign Promotion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'World Cup-related malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious World Cup 2026 ticket, merchandise, or hospitality ad campaigns across Google Ads, Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp. Flag campaigns linking to non-FIFA domains or newly registered infrastructure. Correlate click-through data to phishing site visits.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Banking Data Form Submissions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'collect from visitors various types of data, including names, physical and email addresses, phone numbers, banking/payment details, which could be used to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft, or run financial scams'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form submissions collecting multiple PII fields (name, email, phone, address, banking details) on suspicious domains. Alert when legitimate users submit banking information to non-banking sites. Correlate with known phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Ghost Stadium Phishing Infrastructure Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A major operation that Group-IB researchers attributed to a Chinese threat actor tracked as Ghost Stadium, uses more than 300 phishing sites, clones of the real FIFA portal'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clusters of phishing domains using similar SSL certificates, hosting infrastructure, or registration patterns consistent with Ghost Stadium's 300+ site operation. Flag mass domain registrations within FIFA namespace. Cross-reference with Group-IB threat intel.

suggestion.title: Fake Ticket/Merchandise Purchase Funnel Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'Starting in February, Bitdefender observed fraudulent activity...with fake merchandise, kits and collectibles, streaming services, and Panini sticker offers' with geographic targeting
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious ecommerce transactions for World Cup merchandise/tickets from users in targeted regions (UK, Portugal, Spain, Algeria, US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Germany, Australia). Alert on unusual payment patterns or multiple failed transactions followed by credential changes.

suggestion.title: Recruiter-Impersonation Email Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake recruiter lures' as the initial attack vector. This is the primary entry point but no phishing detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails impersonating recruiting professionals or services targeting cryptocurrency/blockchain employees. Alert on suspicious sender reputation, unusual recruitment messaging, requests for technical interviews, and attachments in macOS formats (DMG, PKG, ZIP).

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Downloaded Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'macOS Malware' as the payload, but no execution-phase detection for malware launched from email or browser was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or /var/tmp within minutes of email attachment interaction. Flag unsigned or revoked code signatures. Monitor for archive extraction (DMG mount, PKG installer) followed by hidden script or binary execution.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency-Industry-Specific Phishing Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'cryptocurrency firms' as targets but no detection correlates industry-specific lure content or targeting patterns against finance/blockchain sector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing emails where recruiter lure content is hyper-specific to crypto/DeFi job titles, blockchain technical skills, or crypto compensation discussions. Cross-reference sender domain reputation against whitelisted crypto recruiter services.

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Actor Infrastructure Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor 'JINX-0164' is explicitly named in the title but was not extracted, mapped to known campaigns, or correlated with any infrastructure indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of JINX-0164 infrastructure from prior reporting. Flag network connections to associated C2 domains, sender email addresses, code-signing certificates, and domain registration patterns matching historical actor behavior.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection — Credential & Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Megalodon supply chain attack...GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets. Workflows were injected through over 5,700 malicious commits pushed...on May 18.' Named campaign with explicit credential theft vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions .yml/.yaml files added in feature branches or forks that invoke credential-dumping tools, environment variable export, or calls to external data exfil endpoints. Correlate with commits pushed May 18+ timeframe and repo compromises with abnormal star/fork velocity. Alert on workflows reading .git/credentials or invoking curl/wget with output redirection.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credentials Exposed in Public Repository — AWS GovCloud
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and vast trove of agency secrets on public GitHub account.' Explicit credential exposure incident with AWS service scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on AWS access keys, session tokens, or service account credentials committed to any public repository. Cross-check exposed key ARNs against CloudTrail API activity within 1 hour of publication for unauthorized AssumeRole, ListBuckets, or describe operations from unexpected principals/IPs. Escalate if keys have admin or cross-account permissions.

suggestion.title: Domain Fronting Attack — TLS SNI/Host Header Mismatch for C2 Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Underminr domain-fronting attack allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity.' Named attack technique with specific evasion indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS SNI name mismatched against HTTP Host header, especially when SNI resolves to major CDN/trusted provider but Host header is anomalous. Flag encrypted traffic to CDN edge IPs with destination domain mismatch. Monitor for repeated SNI/Host pairs suggesting domain-fronting C2 beacons.

suggestion.title: Persistent APT Infrastructure — Russian-linked Bulletproof Hosting for Cyber Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article: '800 servers of hosting company established Feb. 10, 2022, weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine. Infrastructure allegedly used to support cyber attacks, disinformation campaigns, and sanctions evasion linked to Russia.' Indicators of APT-grade persistent infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference seized/sanctioned hosting provider IP blocks and ASNs against egress traffic. Flag DNS queries or external connections to Russian ISP space established post-Feb-2022 with bulletproof hosting signatures (thin whois, fast domain rotation, history of abuse). Correlate with disinformation/propaganda content delivery infrastructure patterns.

suggestion.title: DICOM File Processing Heap Overflow — Automatic Ingestion Attack Surface
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hospitals rely on DICOM-based PACS systems...often automatically ingest files received over the network...heap overflow vulnerability through exploitation of DICOM file format' and MediaArea vulnerabilities. Named exploitation vector in medical imaging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PACS and media processing software (Pydicom, GDCM, Orthanc, MediaInfoLib) for abnormal behavior post-file ingestion: unexpected process elevation, abnormal DLL loads, or child process spawning. Alert on DICOM/media files from untrusted sources (external email, web upload). Validate library versions against CVE databases for CVE-2023-* MediaArea heap overflow patches.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Prioritization Mismatch — KEV Conservative Scope vs. Global Exploitation (GCVE)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes KEV is 'structurally centralized, conservative...scoped to U.S. federal visibility' while 'GCVE makes room for multiple sources of exploitation evidence.' Implies regional detection blind spots for vulnerabilities with active global exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate KEV, GCVE, EPSS, and regional threat feeds for high-EPSS CVEs (>0.7) with active POC/exploitation signals missing from KEV. Prioritize patching for 0-day-adjacent or regionalized exploits visible in GCVE/GreyNoise but not U.S.-focused sources. Alert on exploit delivery (weaponized POC downloads, Metasploit module updates) for CVEs with global visibility gaps.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Suspension Correlated with Vulnerability Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' during zero-day disclosure period—this is a direct account compromise or policy-driven suspension event. Pipeline completely missed this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden GitHub account suspension or disabled-for-ToS events during active vulnerability disclosure windows. Correlate with public disclosure announcements and researcher publication timelines to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Uncoordinated Public Vulnerability Disclosure Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures' indicating coordinated or uncoordinated disclosure events outside responsible disclosure norms. This impact-phase detection requirement was completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vulnerability disclosure announcements on public channels (GitHub, Twitter, security forums, Hacker News) that precede official Microsoft patches by days or weeks. Establish timeline correlation with account suspension events.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Security Incident Response During Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: 'Microsoft Slams Public Zero-Day Disclosures' indicates Microsoft security incident response escalation. Should detect elevated incident-response team activation and emergency patch workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Microsoft security team activity patterns, incident-response workflow initiation, and emergency patching cadence that correlate with public vulnerability disclosure timelines to assess incident response tempo.

suggestion.title: Execution via DLL Side-Loading with Legitimate Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' This is a core execution technique that should generate a detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process executing from temp/download directories (legitimate installer) that loads a suspicious DLL from the same directory or sibling path. Flag if DLL loaded by signed executable but DLL is unsigned or has anomalous metadata. Monitor for HLS Installer variants launching unpacking processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Download: Legitimate Executable + DLL Pair
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery: 'The archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL.' This bundle pattern is unique to this attack and repeatable across victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on extraction of archives from pirate streaming/book sites containing both signed executables and unsigned DLLs in the same directory. Monitor for filename pattern 'HLS Installer' or variant chrome/firefox update patterns. Flag archive downloads from known pirate domains (urush1bar4[.]online).

suggestion.title: Fake Plugin/Browser Update Popup During Video Playback
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'When the user attempted to watch a video, the player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue.' This is the initial social engineering vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious update prompts followed by archive downloads from non-standard domains. Correlate browser update popups (especially from non-browser sources) with simultaneous ZIP downloads. Alert if update prompt hostname does not match legitimate plugin vendor.

suggestion.title: Persistence Establishment by Malicious DLL Module
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device.' Specific persistence mechanism not detailed, but article confirms persistence is a malware capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications or scheduled tasks created by processes spawned from archive-extraction events. Look for Run keys, RunOnce, or scheduled task creation by unsigned DLLs or their parent processes. Alert if persistence is established from temporary/Downloads directory sources.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner and RAT Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article title and tags confirm presence of both miner (evolved SilentCryptoMiner) and RAT: 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module.' Both should trigger detection for network beaconing and resource hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high CPU usage from processes spawned from archive extraction or DLL side-loading events. Detect connections to known mining pools (typically port 3333, 9332, etc.) or RAT C2 infrastructure. Flag traffic anomalies matching XMRig miner signatures or RAT beacon patterns.

suggestion.title: Distribution via Pirated Content Sites with Scale Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes scale: '2026 saw the discovery of new target sites with tens of millions of visitors.' Detection should account for mass-distribution campaign across multiple pirate domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users downloading archives from known pirate streaming/book domains (particularly .ru and .top TLDs). Correlation: if >N users in organization download from same pirate domain within 24 hours, escalate to mass-infection investigation. Cross-reference with organizational policy violations for pirated content access.

suggestion.title: Go binary execution with cryptographic loop detection
suggestion.rationale: Article titled 'self-propagating Go encryptor'—Go executables have distinct import tables and runtime signatures; should detect Go process execution followed by high-frequency file writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of Go binaries (identifiable via .go import metadata, specific entry-point patterns) launching with parent processes absent from enterprise baselines, immediately followed by thread creation and file-system enumeration.

suggestion.title: Self-propagation via admin-share lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Abstract emphasizes 'self-propagating'—should detect rapid SMB enumeration to multiple hosts and secondary execution on adjacent machines via ADMIN$ or C$.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single source process initiating sequential connections to 10+ internal IPs on port 445, followed by failed/successful authentication attempts and cmd.exe/powershell.exe child processes on remote endpoints within same parent tree.

suggestion.title: Bulk encryption with extension mutation
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware core behavior, keyword 'Extortion' confirms ransom demand phase—detect mass file writes with extension appending or replacement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process modifying 50+ files within 300 seconds, appending common ransomware extensions (.gentlemen, .locked, .crypt) or overwriting originals; correlated with sustained high CPU and memory allocation indicative of cryptographic operations.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation to SYSTEM via service or scheduled task
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'Elevation of privilege'; ransomware requires SYSTEM-level access to encrypt system files and disable defenses. Should detect service creation or task scheduling by unprivileged parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Non-SYSTEM parent process creating Windows Service or scheduled task with payload pointing to ransomware binary, followed by task/service execution yielding child processes with SYSTEM token.

suggestion.title: Ransom note and cryptocurrency wallet detection in dropped files
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords 'Extortion' and 'Ransomware as a service' indicate dual-extortion model; should detect ransom note creation and parsing for wallet/contact indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation matching ransom-note naming patterns (README, DECRYPT_ME, HOW_TO_DECRYPT, .txt/.htm in root or encrypted dirs) containing Bitcoin addresses, Tor .onion URLs, or email contact patterns matching known Gentlemen campaign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion via Windows Defender exclusion or DisableRealtimeMonitoring
suggestion.rationale: Human-operated ransomware (keyword) typically disables AV before spreading. Should detect registry modification to Windows Defender config or exclusion-path injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process modifying HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender (DisableRealtimeMonitoring=1) or HKCU exclusion paths; especially if parent is non-admin and modification occurs before encryption phase.

suggestion.title: Detect FortiClient EMS Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exploit critical FortiClient EMS flaw'—baseline attack vector requiring network/process monitoring for abnormal EMS traffic patterns, authentication bypass signatures, or error handling anomalies indicative of exploit delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS services for abnormal process spawning, suspicious network connections on EMS ports, or command-line arguments typical of exploit payloads. Flag authentication failures followed by code execution in EMS context.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Stealer Execution via FortiClient Process Tree
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'deploy credential stealer'—malware execution will occur as child or injected process descending from FortiClient EMS. Look for memory injection, unsigned child processes, or credential access APIs called from EMS context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process injection into FortiClient services, unsigned executables spawned by EMS, or suspicious DLL loads (credential access APIs like lsass, mimikatz patterns, browser vaults) linked to FortiClient parent process.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Credential Dumping
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies active harvesting from browsers, Windows Credential Manager, or memory—'deploy credential stealer' mandates detection of credential access patterns (lsass access, SAM registry reads, vault APIs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry access to HKLM\SAM, HKEY_CURRENT_USER credential stores, or APIs like CredEnumerate. Flag unusual lsass.exe access, browser vault/credential store enumeration, or keylogging hooks from non-system processes.

suggestion.title: Monitor FortiClient-Sourced Command and Control Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer exfiltration ('deploy stealer') implies C2 communication from compromised endpoint. Malware will beacon to attacker infrastructure from FortiClient or injected child process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiClient egress traffic; flag unusual outbound connections on non-standard ports, TLS cert mismatches, or DNS queries to newly registered domains from FortiClient process context. Correlate with credential access events.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Stolen FortiClient Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer harvest enables re-authentication attacks. Stolen EMS admin or endpoint credentials enable lateral movement to other managed endpoints or centralized infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for re-authentication or lateral access using compromised FortiClient EMS admin accounts (impossible-travel, unusual geographies, after-hours access). Flag spread to other managed endpoints via credential replay or EMS orchestration abuse.

suggestion.title: Detect FortiClient Service Modification or Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities often lead to persistence—attacker will maintain access post-exploitation via service hijacking, scheduled tasks, or registry autorun keys leveraging FortiClient trust.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to FortiClient service binary path, startup parameters, or DLL search order. Flag new scheduled tasks, run keys, or services added post-exploitation that reference FortiClient directories or executables.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged tool execution on MDM-enrolled dev machines
suggestion.rationale: Article examines gaps in MDM coverage — attackers leverage unmanaged development tools, package managers, or build systems that MDM cannot monitor or restrict. Need detection for execution of tools outside MDM inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of legitimate dev tools (npm, pip, cargo, gradle, maven, docker, git) with command-line arguments suggesting package installation, build execution, or code modification outside version control. Correlate against MDM-approved tool inventory to identify gaps.

suggestion.title: SSH key generation or git credential access on developer machines
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies credential and code-access attacks on dev machines — SSH key generation, git credential store access, or SSH config modification are core attack patterns MDM typically cannot intercept.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ssh-keygen execution, access to ~/.ssh directory, reads of git credentials (git-credential-store, ~/.git-credentials, keychain access on macOS), or modification of ~/.ssh/config. Include git config commands that disable certificate pinning.

suggestion.title: Local privilege escalation exploit execution on developer machines
suggestion.rationale: MDM enrollment does not prevent local kernel exploits or privilege escalation vulnerabilities from being exercised. Article likely discusses unpatched kernel or privilege escalation paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of known privilege escalation tools (sudo with NOPASSWD, polkit exploitation, setuid binary abuse, capability elevation) or suspicious elevation of privileges on dev machines. Alert on UAC bypass attempts on Windows or sudo auth attempts with unusual sources.

suggestion.title: Supply chain artifact tampering (package.json, requirements.txt, Dockerfile)
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines hold source code and build artifacts. Article implies attackers can modify code/build configurations without MDM detection. Need to detect tampering of dependency files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of dependency/build files (package.json, package-lock.json, requirements.txt, Gemfile, Dockerfile, build.gradle, pom.xml) by non-build processes. Correlate with unexpected child process execution (e.g., npm script execution without npm install). Alert on git commits without associated IDE/CLI git invocation.

suggestion.title: IDE plugin or dev tool installation without approval
suggestion.rationale: MDM cannot always audit VS Code extensions, JetBrains plugins, or homebrew/apt package installations. Article likely discusses extension marketplace attacks or plugin supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IDE plugin installation (code --install-extension, JetBrains plugin directory writes) especially from non-standard repositories. Monitor package manager installs (brew install, apt-get, pip install, npm install -g) for packages unknown to organization. Correlate with outbound HTTPS to suspicious plugin/package registries.

suggestion.title: Container escape or Docker socket abuse on developer machines
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines often run Docker or container runtimes; article likely discusses how attackers escape containers or access the Docker socket to escalate privileges or move laterally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for docker socket access (docker.sock writes/reads), container escape attempts (namespace breakouts, cgroup exploits), privileged container execution, or volume mounts of sensitive directories (/etc, /root, /) to containers. Alert on docker run with --privileged, --cap-add, or -v mounts of host system directories.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing to Cloud Account Compromise with MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' No detection use case generated despite clear initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed Entra sign-in attempts (risk indicators: impossible travel, token anomalies) within 4–24 hours of successful authentication from unusual device/location. Alert on MFA bypass indicators (conditional access policy rejection followed by successful auth). Query for AAD sign-in logs where RiskLevel > 'low' and successful login follows suspicious activity; cross-reference with device compliance and login IP geolocation history.

suggestion.title: Bulk Salesforce Data Export by Compromised User Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' No detection UC for SaaS bulk exfiltration pattern despite explicit mention of large-scale data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce API logs for bulk query operations (SOQL, REST API batch requests) executed by newly-compromised Entra-linked accounts. Flag requests that extract customer PII fields (names, emails, phone, addresses) in unusual volume or velocity. Baseline: compare monthly record pulls to peer accounts; alert on >5× deviation or any pull of >100k records in single session.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Cloud Identity to SaaS Platform Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes progression 'hacking the U.S. telecom giant Charter Communications in early April' via Entra to Salesforce—clear SaaS lateral movement. Pipeline failed to map this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 2–48 hours of Entra account compromise, detect first successful Salesforce login from the same compromised identity or API key provisioned to Entra service principal. Look for: application/service principal authorization events granting 'data export' or 'bulk read' scopes to previously-unused apps. Cross-reference Entra token issuance logs with Salesforce access logs to find token reuse patterns.

suggestion.title: CPNI Data Exfiltration from Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'some CPNI data' was exfiltrated and describes ShinyHunters' claim of stealing CPNI. No UC for detecting telecom-specific sensitive data (CPNI) theft despite this being a regulatory/compliance-grade indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any data access or exfiltration (via API, file transfer, or network tunnel) involving systems labeled or known to store CPNI. Create rule: detect reads of database tables/file shares with 'CPNI' classification or regex-matched phone/calling-pattern fields, followed by outbound transfer to non-Charter IP. Correlate with compromised user identity from initial-access phase.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Dark Web Leak Monitoring for Customer Data Dumps
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility' and 'leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' No proactive detection UC for monitoring threat-actor leak sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known ShinyHunters leak-site URLs and monitor for new posts; parse dump descriptions and sample data for org name, customer PII patterns, and record counts. Alert when: (1) org name appears in new post, (2) leaked email/phone counts overlap with internal user database, (3) post includes Charter-specific data (Spectrum branding, internal ticket IDs). Cross-reference leak date with exfil phase timeline.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Entra Account Activity Post-Vishing: Token Issuance and App Authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial compromise as credential theft via vishing. No UC specifically covers post-compromise token abuse or app-permission-grant patterns that would indicate account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After vishing/Entra compromise, monitor for: (1) refreshing of Entra refresh tokens by new device/IP, (2) grants of 'Application.ReadWrite.All' or 'Directory.ReadWrite.All' to previously-unseen service principals, (3) token-refresh events with anomalous user-agent strings or IP geolocation. Baseline: compare to historical token issuance patterns per user; alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Samba RCE Exploitation via SMB Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly asserts RCE in Samba; no execution-phase detection surfaced. Samba SMB vulns manifest as protocol-layer abuse or unsafe deserialization in smbd/nmbd daemons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected SMB negotiate/session-setup sequences from untrusted IPs to port 445/139, rapid connection resets, or malformed RPC/DCE payloads. Post-compromise, look for smbd/nmbd spawning shells or suid binaries.

suggestion.title: Samba Daemon Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: RCE in Samba runs code as smbd/nmbd user; no process-level detection rule suggested despite execution phase clear from title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on smbd/nmbd (PIDs from netstat -tulnp | grep samba) spawning bash, sh, perl, python, or curl/wget without corresponding legitimate file-transfer session. Filter known legitimate cron tasks.

suggestion.title: Samba Share Access Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: If Samba RCE succeeds, attacker gains file-system access; no share-enumeration or unusual-access detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Samba logs for failed/successful access to restricted shares, particularly followed by process execution. Flag accounts accessing shares outside their normal business pattern or at unusual hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Teams Account Impersonation as IT Helpdesk Staff
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Impersonate IT Helpdesk Staff'—the core attack narrative. Pipeline generated zero detections for this. Attackers create or compromise Teams accounts with helpdesk-like display names and send credential-harvesting messages to normal users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TeamsAdminAuditLog for newly created user accounts with display names or email addresses containing IT-related keywords (support, helpdesk, admin, IT security). Alert on bulk Teams direct messages from these accounts requesting password resets, MFA verification, or account confirmation from internal staff.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Teams Collaboration Feature Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Collaboration Features' being exploited. Pipeline did not generate any detections for Teams channels, file sharing, or guest access abuse—core attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk Teams channel or file invitations from newly created or low-tenure accounts. Flag external guest accounts granted elevated permissions to sensitive channels. Alert on Teams files with names suggesting credential/password templates shared by accounts impersonating IT.

suggestion.title: Teams Credential Harvesting via Phishing Messages
suggestion.rationale: Helpdesk impersonation inherently targets credential theft. Article describes this attack, yet pipeline missed credential-access phase detections entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Teams message history and audit logs for messages containing credential-request patterns ('verify password', 'confirm MFA', 'validate account'). Correlate sender accounts with abnormal MFA enrollments, password resets, or token-refresh anomalies in AAD logs occurring post-message.

suggestion.title: Rogue Teams Bot or OAuth App Creation
suggestion.rationale: Teams collaboration features can be weaponized via malicious bots or app integrations. No detection rules generated for API/bot abuse, a common Teams attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Teams audit logs for bot registrations or OAuth app consent grants initiated by newly created or suspicious service principals. Flag bots making unusual API calls (bulk file reads, user enumeration, message deletion) or requesting admin-level permissions.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Following Teams Helpdesk Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Impersonation is typically a precursor to credential compromise and account takeover. Pipeline did not flag sign-in anomalies or privilege escalation post-impersonation attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on targeted user accounts accessing Teams from geographically impossible locations or user agents inconsistent with baseline, within 24 hours of receiving Teams messages from IT-impersonating accounts. Escalate if followed by Teams admin-role assignment, forwarding rule creation, or SharePoint permission changes.

suggestion.title: Detect ScreenConnect Process Execution from Suspicious Origin
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers deliver ScreenConnect malware; no use case exists to detect execution. Phrase: 'deliver ScreenConnect Malware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect.exe or ConnectWiseScreenConnect.exe spawning from temp directories, user AppData, or unusual parent processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, explorer.exe). Alert on process creation with child processes indicating lateral movement or data exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Fake Adobe Document Cloud Phishing Link Clicks
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'fake Adobe Document Cloud pages'; no web/proxy detection rule. Phrase: 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy/URL filtering logs for requests to domains spoofing adobe.com, documentcloud.adobe.com, or visually similar variants. Flag if followed by ScreenConnect installer download or C2 beaconing. Correlate with email gateway logs for phishing links sent to target users.

suggestion.title: Detect ScreenConnect Remote Access Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Attack leverages ScreenConnect for remote control post-delivery; no C2 or persistence detection. Phrase: 'Deliver ScreenConnect Malware' and implicit C2 usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect.exe establishing outbound connections to non-standard ports (typical: 5938, 5939 or 443 with ScreenConnect UA). Monitor for persistent connections, multiple remote sessions from single endpoint, or connection to infrastructure not in baseline.

suggestion.title: Monitor for Credential Harvesting via Fake Adobe Login Forms
suggestion.rationale: Fake Adobe pages imply credential capture mechanism; no detection for form interception or credential submission logging. Phrase: 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to fake Adobe domains with form data matching Adobe credential submission patterns. Correlate with failed authentication attempts to real adobe.com shortly after, or subsequent ScreenConnect process execution.

suggestion.title: Block or Alert on ScreenConnect Installer Download from Suspicious Source
suggestion.rationale: Delivery mechanism is ScreenConnect binary; no file-based or download detection. Phrase: 'Deliver ScreenConnect Malware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect installer downloads (.exe, .msi) to non-standard directories (Temp, AppData, Downloads with unusual naming). Flag if downloaded via non-standard ports, with SSL/certificate anomalies, or followed immediately by execution.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Tool Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names HTTPSpy as newly deployed tool by Kimsuky; no detection UC produced. Pipeline should flag malware-as-tool introductions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of HTTPSpy binary or suspicious HTTP-based command channel patterns. Look for non-standard ports, user-agent spoofing, or SSL certificate mismatches typical of APT43 tools.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists HelloDoor as expanded capability; zero detection coverage. Should alert on first-seen malware families from tracked APT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HelloDoor execution via process creation monitoring, parent-child relationships with suspicious shells, and network callbacks. Cross-reference Kimsuky infrastructure for C2 domains.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Abuse for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'VS Code Tunnels' as attack vector; pipeline missed legitimate-tool abuse pattern. Article phrase: 'Expands Arsenal with... VS Code Tunnels'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code remote tunnel daemon spawning without user IDE context, unusual --tunnel-name patterns, or outbound connections to tunnel.dev infrastructure. Correlate with credential compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Infrastructure Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes new tool deployment by Kimsuky; pipeline should extract at least actor-attributed C2 domains, IPs, or SSL certificates. No IOCs provided despite tool deployment narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on known Kimsuky infrastructure (C2 domains, IP ranges). Monitor for HTTPS traffic to new certificate CN patterns associated with APT43 campaigns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Codex-Impersonating Application Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI'—describes masquerading attack. Pipeline missed the core delivery mechanism: trojanized application mimicking OpenAI's interface to trick users into running malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of suspicious binaries with names or window titles mimicking 'Codex', 'OpenAI', or 'Remote UI'. Monitor for unsigned executables masquerading as IDE extensions. Correlate with user reports of credential theft or unusual API activity.

suggestion.title: API Token Extraction from Codex Authentication Flow
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Steals OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens'—explicit token theft objective. Pipeline produced no detection for credential capture or token exfiltration from client memory or configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for access to OpenAI token storage locations (~/.openai, browser storage, environment variables). Flag processes performing memory dumps of Codex clients or reading configuration files. Detect unusual clipboard access capturing token material post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Fake Authentication UI for OpenAI Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Title 'Legitimate-Looking' + 'Remote UI' indicates fake login screen or credentials prompt. Pipeline failed to map this UI-based credential capture to input capture/phishing techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modal dialogs or window spawning with text matching 'OpenAI login', 'Codex authentication', 'API token required'. Flag HTTPS traffic to lookalike domains (typosquatting, homograph variants of api.openai.com). Monitor clipboard access immediately after credential prompt dismissal.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email or Message Delivering Codex Malware
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires initial delivery to users. Title implies social engineering but pipeline extracted no email/messaging-based detection for malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails impersonating OpenAI, GitHub, or JetBrains offering 'Codex plugin update', 'Remote UI beta', or 'IDE integration patch'. Flag attachment or link downloads of .exe, .msi, .dmg, .deb with Codex-themed names. Monitor execution from Download directories post-phishing interaction.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OpenAI API Usage from Stolen Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens enable unauthorized API calls. Pipeline missed post-compromise detection of token misuse (unusual usage patterns, new geolocation, off-hours requests).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI API audit logs for authentication from new IP geolocation blocks or ASNs post-incident window. Flag bulk token usage, fine-tuning jobs, or batch processing requests inconsistent with user's historical patterns. Detect token reuse across multiple client applications or simultaneous sessions.

suggestion.title: Code Signing Certificate Abuse — SmartScreen Bypass via Valid Sectigo Cert
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body center on 'Malicious RVTools Installer Abuses Sectigo Certificate to Bypass SmartScreen Warnings.' This is the core attack technique; pipeline generated zero detection rules for code-signing abuse or SmartScreen evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables signed by legitimate CAs (e.g., Sectigo) executing from unusual locations, user-writable directories, or spawning suspicious child processes. Flag SmartScreen suppression, zone.identifier removal, or trusted-path bypass on signed binaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious RVTools Process Execution — Installer Spawning Unexpected Children
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious RVTools installer'—inherently implies execution and child-process spawning. Pipeline did not suggest detection for RVTools launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or accessing registry/run keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RVTools installer or RVTools.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, RegEdit, or msiexec; modifying HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or equivalent; or writing to Program Files. Escalate if parent is from temp directory or has low file reputation.

suggestion.title: Revoked or Abused Certificate Chain — Sectigo Cert Reuse Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions specific CA (Sectigo) being abused. Pipeline did not recommend hunting for certificate serial/thumbprint reuse or monitoring for additional malware signed with the same certificate.

Alert on any binary sharing this certificate alongside low reputation scores, unusual locations, or suspicious behavior.

suggestion.title: Installer Parent-Child Process Chain — Staged Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious installers stage execution through helper processes and registry modifications. Article context implies payload drop and persistence; pipeline did not flag multi-generation process chains or installer-driven registry changes.

suggestion.title: SmartScreen Suppression and Alternate Data Stream Removal

Correlate with execution of unsigned or low-reputation binaries within 60 seconds of ADS deletion.

suggestion.title: RVTools Installer File Hash — Malicious Binary Reputation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies specific malicious RVTools installer with known hash(es), download URL, or C2 infrastructure. Pipeline did not extract or recommend file-hash-based or distribution-based detection.

Cross-reference with endpoint telemetry for suspicious spawning, registry access, or network connections.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation and Suspicious Child Process Execution

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Harvesting from Browser and Windows Credential Manager
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states NuGet 'Steals Banking Credentials'—no detection UC generated for credential harvesting from browsers, Windows Credential Manager, or DPAPI-protected storage despite this being the primary malware objective.

suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets'—no detection generated for cloud credential file access (.aws/credentials, .azure, GCP service accounts) despite this being explicitly mentioned as an attack objective.
