suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly list 'QR Codes' as attack vector. No detection coverage generated despite this being a novel/documented phishing delivery method for this threat landscape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with embedded QR codes (base64 encoded images or QR code attachments) sent to World Cup infrastructure operators. Alert on device camera activity or QR scanning tools scanning external URLs immediately post-email delivery. Flag QR decode activity pointing to credential harvesting or C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA/World Cup Infrastructure Domain Registration and Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata includes 'typosquatting' as explicit attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface detection for domains mimicking official World Cup or FIFA infrastructure despite being a documented tactic in the article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to domains with character-substitution or homograph patterns against FIFA, World Cup broadcasters, venues, and organizing bodies. Alert on email links to newly-registered domains with high homograph similarity to official infrastructure. Monitor credential submission events to typosquatted domains.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Execution Against Event Venue and Broadcast Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly cite 'wiper' but pipeline produced zero kill-chain impact phase or detection. State-aligned actors and ransomware groups commonly deploy wipers against critical event infrastructure for maximum disruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect MBR/partition enumeration followed by mass file deletion or device formatting on critical infrastructure servers. Alert on unexpected system shutdown/reboot sequences with no maintenance scheduling. Flag suspicious disk utility execution (cipher.exe, format.com, diskpart.exe) on broadcast/venue control systems.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from Fighting Ursa / Razing Ursa Attributed Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'state-aligned actors' (keywords: Fighting Ursa, Razing Ursa). Pipeline extracted zero actor names and zero C2 detection despite these being named APT groups with documented infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish DNS/IP sinkhole lists for known Fighting Ursa and Razing Ursa C2 domains. Alert on outbound connections to actor-attributed command servers from World Cup infrastructure networks. Monitor for DNS fast-flux or domain generation algorithm (DGA) patterns associated with these actor groups.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via World Cup-Themed Phishing to Officials and Operators
suggestion.rationale: Article description explicitly states threat model includes phishing attacks on critical infrastructure. Pipeline generated zero detection for credential theft initial access phase despite it being the documented attack chain entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential submission to World Cup-themed phishing domains. Alert on failed authentication attempts with credentials previously observed in phishing campaigns. Monitor for unusual login patterns (time-of-day, geography, device) immediately following phishing email delivery to infrastructure operators.

suggestion.title: Fake Google Play Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' This is the documented primary distribution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to domains closely resembling Google Play infrastructure from non-Google ASNs. Detect phishing landing pages that serve APK downloads instead of redirecting to legitimate play.google.com.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is the key escalation and persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on apps that request Accessibility Service permissions immediately post-install or enable Accessibility Services for non-accessibility applications. Detect system calls requiring elevated privileges following Accessibility grant.

suggestion.title: Icon Hiding After Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device' as a customizable payload feature. This is a documented defense-evasion technique for BTMOB.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps that disable launcher icons or hide app-drawer presence after installation. Detect package manager operations and activity alias modifications that remove visibility.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies core capability: 'intercepting financial transactions' alongside data stealing and screenshots. This is the primary revenue mechanism for operators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous proxy-setup activity from financial or banking apps. Monitor for apps hooking transaction-processing libraries or intercepting TLS traffic from banking applications.

suggestion.title: Multi-Payload APK Builder Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'APK builder included in the offer provides easy customization of the payload without any need to code.' Multiple samples share builder signatures despite different payloads and targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster APKs by builder signatures, certificate patterns, DEX structural entropy, and resource layouts to identify samples from the same code-generation framework. Enables detection of new BTMOB variants sharing the same builder.

suggestion.title: Custom Localized Phishing Lure Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'BTMOB malware platform also helps operators generate custom, localized phishing lures to match the campaign's topic.' Example: 'campaigns that used an Argentinian government agency as a lure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing campaigns in specific locales (Spanish-language, Argentine government agencies) with common C2 infrastructure. Detect phishing-email clusters that share builder signatures despite divergent social-engineering narratives.

suggestion.title: Authenticated RCE via Gogs Post-Receive Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code' — direct evidence of RCE post-authentication. Pipeline missed the entire execution phase detection despite HIGH severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs service processes for unexpected child process creation, especially shell/PowerShell spawns. Track HTTP POST requests to Gogs API endpoints known to handle repository hooks or git operations from authenticated users, correlate with subsequent command-line activity on the host.

suggestion.title: Gogs Service Spawning System Command Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: RCE inherently means arbitrary code execution reaches command shell. Article title establishes code execution but pipeline surfaced zero execution-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as child of Gogs-related process (gogs.exe, git.exe, or Gogs service account). Establish baseline for normal Gogs process tree; any deviation post-authentication is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Gogs Web Request to Potentially Exploitable Endpoints (Authenticated)
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies authenticated vector but no network-layer detection suggested. Pipeline should cover initial RCE attempt before post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authenticated Gogs sessions immediately followed by unusual POST/PUT requests to git-related endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/repos, /api/v1/user/repos, or hook/workflow endpoints). Correlate with subsequent command execution.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Commit or Hook Modification by User
suggestion.rationale: RCE in Git service often manifests as malicious hook injection. Title confirms authenticated exploitation but no pre/post-RCE artifact detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs repository directories for creation/modification of pre-receive or post-receive hooks outside normal deployment pipelines. Cross-reference with user authentication events immediately preceding file changes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Integrity Anomaly — axios Trojanization
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Attackers exploited the lead maintainer's compromised credentials to publish malicious versions of the library that injected trojanized code into affected systems.' Supply chain compromise of widely-used library with 100M+ weekly downloads demands detection of unexpected package version changes, unsigned releases, and injection of unfamiliar code paths into dependency trees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for unexpected version bumps on high-profile libraries (axios, etc.), particularly those lacking matching git tags or authored by unexpected account. Detect dev environment process execution of npm install/update followed by loading of JavaScript from unexpected file paths or network destinations.

suggestion.title: Ivanti VPN Appliance — PhiliKit SPAWN Toolset Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PhiliKit, a new implant that we assess to be part of UNC5221's SPAWN toolset targeting Ivanti VPN appliances.' Specific targeting of Ivanti VPN with custom implant necessitates detection of exploitation attempts, unusual API calls, and persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Ivanti VPN authentication failures with subsequent unexpected outbound connections, unusual administrative API calls, or deployment of files to system-critical directories. Flag persistence mechanisms typical of SPAWN variants (scheduled tasks, registry modifications).

suggestion.title: Bootkit-Style Wiper Deployment — Rusty Boots / MoKhargosh
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Two unattributed activity clusters, Rusty Boots and MoKhargosh, demonstrated both espionage capabilities and destructive potential – including deployment of a bootkit-style wiper.' Destructive bootkit deployment represents imminent impact; detection must precede execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect boot sector writes, MBR modifications, and UEFI/firmware tampering from unexpected processes. Monitor for execution of disk wipe utilities (cipher.exe /w, diskpart, dd) or writes to raw disk devices (\Device\PhysicalDrive*).

suggestion.title: TigerRAT Execution and C2 Communication — Andariel Reemergence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel in South Korea, where the group deployed TigerRAT and attempted to spread Rook ransomware within an engineering company.' TigerRAT deployment indicates active remote access compromise requiring behavioral and network detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TigerRAT process execution patterns (unusual parent processes, script execution from temp directories, encoded command lines). Identify C2 communication by flagging persistent outbound connections to non-standard ports and domains resolving via dynamic DNS.

suggestion.title: Developer Social Engineering — Credential Compromise of Maintainers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple groups continued targeting developers and the cryptocurrency ecosystem with social engineering schemes that can yield both direct financial gain and opportunities for software supply-chain compromise.' Developers as targets for credential harvesting, specifically maintainers of critical libraries, enables downstream supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual login patterns from maintainer accounts (geographic anomalies, off-hours access, new devices). Flag suspicious email (phishing indicators, urgency, requests for credential verification). Correlate failed authentication attempts with subsequent successful login from unusual location/device.

suggestion.title: Rook Ransomware Deployment Attempt — Andariel Nuclear/Hydrogen Interest
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel...deployed TigerRAT and attempted to spread Rook ransomware within an engineering company that appears to manufacture equipment relevant to liquid hydrogen handling and the nuclear industry.' Ransomware deployment against critical infrastructure sector requires immediate behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Rook ransomware execution by monitoring for mass file encryption operations, file extension changes to known Rook markers, and ransom note creation. Correlate with lateral movement to network shares and execution from unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names phishing domains: 'fiffa[.]com' and alternative TLDs (.xyz, .live, .sale, .org) impersonating fifa.com. Zero detection for users accessing these infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to FIFA typosquats and phishing domains. Trigger on access to fiffa.com, fifa-hiring.com, jobs-fifa.com and variants with non-.com TLDs. Correlate web proxy logs to identify affected users and session context.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Fake Employment Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake employment portals like jobs-fifa[.]com or fifa-hiring[.]com' collecting credentials. Missing detection for form submissions on these known malicious sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests with authentication/form-field payloads destined to phishing employment portals. Correlate with user identity to identify internal personnel reused credentials. Flag anomalous submission patterns (timing, repetition, geographic mismatch).

suggestion.title: Payment Data Harvesting on FIFA Phishing Sites
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites 'collect banking/payment details' for fraud. No detection for users entering payment information on malicious FIFA infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for form submissions containing credit card fields, bank account data, or payment gateway interactions on known FIFA phishing domains. Correlate with downstream fraudulent transactions originating from phishing site visitor IPs. Alert on PII exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign Detection - FIFA World Cup Fraud
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp.' Zero detection for fraudulent ads linking to phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web proxy logs with ad-click traffic patterns. Identify HTTP referrers from Google/Facebook ad networks pointing to FIFA phishing domains. Monitor Telegram/WhatsApp for shared URLs linking to fraudulent portals. Flag geographic/temporal anomalies in ad-driven traffic surges.

suggestion.title: Bulk FIFA Phishing Domain Registration Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Ghost Stadium uses more than 300 phishing sites.' Missing detection for identifying clusters of newly registered FIFA-themed infrastructure suggesting coordinated campaign buildout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration feeds for bulk registration of FIFA-themed domains with typosquatting patterns. Correlate registration timing, registrar, nameservers, and hosting IP ranges. Alert on clusters exceeding baseline variance in FIFA-related registrations.

suggestion.title: Fake World Cup Merchandise E-Commerce Fraud
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'fake merchandise, kits and collectibles, streaming services, and Panini sticker offers.' Missing detection for fraudulent e-commerce transactions mimicking official World Cup retail.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious e-commerce transactions for World Cup merchandise on unauthorized vendors. Monitor for payment failures followed by retry attempts from same card. Correlate customer complaints (undelivered items, account takeovers) with transaction IP/card profiles and geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing with Archive Delivery via Cloud Storage Links
suggestion.rationale: PhantomMail campaign described as 'Spear-phishing emails delivering malicious ZIP/RAR archives via Google Drive and 4sync links, using decoy PDFs or fake errors while deploying malware'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with links to Google Drive/4sync URLs followed by archive extraction and child process spawning from temp directories. Correlate email sender reputation against targets matching government/military/telecom sectors.

suggestion.title: Fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix Page Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: PhantomClick uses 'Fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix pages disguised as Zoom and LAPAS sites trick victims into running self-infecting commands through fake Cloudflare verification prompts'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP redirects to lookalike Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS domains with CAPTCHA styling. Alert on PowerShell or cmd.exe execution immediately following visits to these domains with command-line args containing encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: PowerShell RAT Execution with Credential Harvesting Behavior
suggestion.rationale: LegionRelay and PhantomRelay are PowerShell RATs supporting 'file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup'; article states they use 'dynamic script loading'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell with heavily obfuscated parameters, IEX/Invoke-Expression patterns, or dynamic script downloads. Alert on ProcessCreate events spawning from archive extraction contexts with multiple credential store access patterns (HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication, browser profile dirs).

suggestion.title: Browser Credential and Session Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: LegionRelay explicitly supports 'browser credential theft'; malware targets Chrome/Firefox/Edge profile directories for cookies and saved passwords
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual processes accessing browser credential databases (Chrome/Firefox/Edge SQLite files in %APPDATA%). Alert on LSASS handle opens from non-system processes, LocalAppData access from malware parents, and zip/rar compression of browser profile directories.

suggestion.title: Telegram/WhatsApp Messaging Platform Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: LegionRelay supports 'Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration'; PrincessClub used 'fake female Telegram personas' indicating account takeover as primary collection objective
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing Telegram/WhatsApp local databases (%APPDATA%\Telegram, %APPDATA%\WhatsApp\Local Store, tdata directories). Correlate with exfiltration of .db/.sqlite files or unusual account activity following malware execution on infected hosts.

suggestion.title: Audio and Video Capture via WebRTC and Malware APIs
suggestion.rationale: PrincessClub 'added WebRTC-based live calls that could capture the victim's audio/video'; FallSpy Android spyware collects 'call logs' and 'media files' indicating active recording capability
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebRTC connections from non-browser processes or suspicious JavaScript context. Alert on microphone/camera permission access by malware processes (DeviceIoControl calls to audio devices). Monitor for unexpected RTCP/RTP traffic on high-numbered ports from compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing via Fake Recruiter Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'fake recruiter lures' as attack vector. Pipeline did not detect this social engineering technique. Should detect suspicious LinkedIn/email recruiting outreach to crypto employees with malware payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LinkedIn connection requests or recruiter emails targeting crypto firm employees with credential harvesting links or suspicious file attachments. Correlate email headers showing domain spoofing or newly registered domain similarity to legitimate recruiting firms. Flag emails from untrusted senders offering remote positions to employees with crypto-adjacent job titles.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from User-Downloaded Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'macOS malware' delivery but pipeline failed to map execution techniques or log sources for macOS platform. Should detect suspicious binary execution, script launching, or code signing bypass typical of recruiter lure payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on macOS process execution from user Downloads or temp directories immediately following email attachment open. Monitor for suspicious code signing validation bypass, unsigned Mach-O binaries, or shell invocation from uninstaller/updater packages. Correlate with recent email receipt containing recruiter-themed subject lines.

suggestion.title: Command and Control from Cryptocurrency Firm macOS Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article implies post-compromise C2 but pipeline reconstructed zero kill chain phases. Should detect beaconing behavior typical of macOS malware families targeting financial infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect regular outbound connections from macOS endpoints at cryptocurrency firms to suspicious domains or IPs (uncommon geographic destinations, high ASN diversity). Monitor for DNS queries to newly registered or fast-flux domains. Look for process spawning with obfuscated command-line args or base64 encoding common in shell-based C2.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Targeting Cryptocurrency Private Keys or Wallets
suggestion.rationale: Threat targets crypto firms; should detect discovery and exfiltration of wallet credentials, seed phrases, or key material. Pipeline failed to surface this contexual threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag macOS process access to password managers, browser local storage directories, or plaintext wallet files. Monitor for unusual clipboard access (reading/writing seed phrases). Detect exfiltration of .plist files from ~/Library directories containing financial app credentials or API keys.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '5,500+ repositories infected...malicious commits pushed...containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets.' Direct supply-chain compromise via .github/workflows modification requires detection of unexpected workflow file changes and exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for commits modifying .github/workflows/ files from unusual authors or without review. Flag workflows containing credential-related string patterns (secrets, keys, tokens, env vars) followed by base64 encoding or unexpected HTTP egress to non-GitHub domains.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secrets Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically calls out Megalodon payload 'designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets'—represents post-compromise credential access from GitHub Actions runner context where secrets are environment-accessible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CI/CD job execution (GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins) that enumerates or exfiltrates environment variables, reads secret stores, or makes outbound calls to non-standard IPs/domains immediately after accessing secrets. Look for env dump commands (printenv, env, Get-ChildItem Env:) or curl/wget to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Domain-Fronting HTTP Header Mismatch (Underminr)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Underminr domain-fronting attack allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity.' Requires detection of SNI/Host header divergence and CDN abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS connections where TLS SNI certificate subject differs from HTTP Host header, or where SNI points to a small domain but Host header resolves to CDN/major provider. Baseline CDN legitimate use, then alert on anomalies pointing to unrelated domains.

suggestion.title: AWS Credential Usage Post-Public-Leak (CISA Breach)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and...secrets on a public GitHub account.' Requires detection of API calls using exposed credentials and cross-referencing against public leak databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for API calls from known-leaked AWS key material (cross-reference against GitHub secret-scanning feeds). Alert on GovCloud API calls from non-GovCloud IP space or first-seen principal ARNs shortly after leak date. Flag unusual API patterns (LIST, GET, DELETE) inconsistent with normal service role usage.

suggestion.title: Heap Overflow Exploitation in DICOM/Media Processing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'heap overflow vulnerability through exploitation of DICOM file format' and 'four vulnerabilities in MediaInfoLib.' Hospitals 'automatically ingest files received over the network'—RCE opportunity via malformed file ingestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PACS and media-handling processes (MediaInfo, Orthanc, GDCM consumers) for unexpected child process spawning, memory protection violations, or crash dumps following network file ingestion. Correlate file hashes of network-originated DICOM/media files against known exploit sample databases.

suggestion.title: GitHub Researcher Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal'—suggests account takeover or compromise followed by removal action. Pipeline extracted no use case for account security monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal GitHub authentication patterns (impossible travel, new IP origins, API token creation) followed by rapid account modifications or deletion events. Correlate with zero-day disclosure timing.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Public Disclosure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Public Zero-Day Disclosures'—pipeline should detect threat-intel IOCs (CVE numbers, vulnerability descriptions) and flag unsanctioned public disclosure. No use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for references to unpatched CVE identifiers in public repositories, GitHub gists, security forum posts, and researcher disclosures. Cross-reference with Microsoft's MSRC vulnerability timeline to identify off-cycle public disclosures.

suggestion.title: Researcher Account Retaliation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Framing suggests Microsoft is responding to researcher disclosure—detection should cover account-suspension workflows and potential legal/policy enforcement signals. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass account suspensions or content removals following security research publications. Track timing correlation between disclosure and account action.

suggestion.title: Malicious Git Branch Name Injection in Gogs Rebase Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation via 'pull requests that use a malicious branch name to inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the Rebase before merging merge operation.' No detection logic was generated for this critical signature-based injection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs rebase/merge operations where branch names contain git control characters, flag prefixes (--), command separators (&&, |, ;), or the literal string '--exec'. Flag pull requests initiated by non-admin users with branch names deviating from standard naming conventions (alphanumeric, dash, underscore).

suggestion.title: Rapid Gogs Account and Repository Creation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' with 'open registration enabled by default' and 'no limit on repository creation.' This provisioning sequence is a direct footprint of exploitation initiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new Gogs user accounts created followed within 5-15 minutes by repository creation from the same source IP, especially when DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false and MAX_CREATION_LIMIT=-1 are configured. Flag rapid multi-repository creation by newly-registered accounts.

suggestion.title: Git Process Child Execution Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation results in 'arbitrary code remotely as the Gogs server process user' via git rebase manipulation. Detection of git/git-rebase spawning unexpected shells or executables indicates successful command injection post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git, git-rebase, git-merge processes spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, bash, python, perl). Flag anomalous process lineage where git is parent to interactive shells or utilities outside normal merge workflows.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Gogs Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' from the compromised instance. Post-exploitation credential access is documented in the article's impact section.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Gogs/git processes reading from credential storage (.ssh/, .git/config, token caches, password files). Flag suspicious file reads from Gogs installation directories or user home directories by git-derived processes outside normal CI/CD patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cross-Repository Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers can 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos)' after code execution. Detecting unauthorized enumeration and access of unowned private repos indicates post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly-registered or low-privilege Gogs users accessing/reading repositories they do not own, particularly private repositories. Flag rapid sequential access to multiple unrelated repositories by the same user within tight time windows (under 5 minutes).

suggestion.title: Gogs Version Fingerprinting and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable versions (0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev) affecting 2,400+ exposed servers. Network reconnaissance targeting Gogs instances for version enumeration typically precedes exploitation chain initiation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Gogs version disclosure endpoints (/api/v1/version, /app.js fingerprinting, /robots.txt, HTTP headers) from external IPs. Flag repeated Gogs probing requests from single source across multiple internal targets.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Executable in Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process.' Core attack mechanism with no detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or untrusted DLL loaded by legitimate Windows executables from same directory. Flag specifically when legitimate EXE (HLS Installer, rundll32, svchost variants) loads DLL immediately after archive extraction, especially with absence of publisher signature or mismatched signing date.

suggestion.title: Fake Video Player Plugin Update Prompt Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When the user attempted to watch a video, the player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update.' Initial access vector via social engineering on piracy platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate extended dwell on known piracy site domains (.ru/.top TLDs) followed by ZIP archive download within 5-minute window. Alert on fake update prompts rendered by video player iframes on illegal streaming sites, correlated with executable/archive downloads.

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner and RAT Module Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and 'The library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence.' Named malware families with persistence and C2 capability but no detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for XMRig process spawning from temp directories with high CPU utilization and sustained process lifetime. Detect registry modifications to Run/RunOnce keys establishing persistence post-extraction. Flag secondary executable/DLL from same infection chain establishing outbound C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Piracy Site Archive Download Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies distribution from 'urush1bar4.online' (current) and 'file.ipfs.us.69.mu' (previous), explicitly stating archive structure: 'legitimate executable and a large malicious DLL.' Specific IOCs and pattern mentioned with no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ZIP downloads from known malicious domains (urush1bar4.online, file.ipfs.us.69.mu). Detect archive extraction followed by immediate execution of bundled executable + unsigned DLL pair. Monitor DNS traffic to these domains and correlate with file_exists/process_create events.

suggestion.title: Chromium/Browser Fake Crash Page with Concurrent Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors displayed a fake browser crash page... while simultaneously downloading an archive to the device with a name starting with chromium-patch-nigh.' Concurrent deception + malware delivery tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable/archive downloads with chromium/browser update-spoofing names (chromium-patch-*, browser-update-*, flash-player-update-*) from piracy domains. Correlate with JavaScript-injected fake error/crash overlay events. Flag simultaneous page crash notification + file download from same origin.

suggestion.title: Malicious Archive Extraction from Piracy Ad/Update Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full chain: fake update prompt display → archive download on click → extraction → DLL side-loading. No use case captures the temporal pattern of prompt-triggered downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation of archive tools (7zip, winrar, tar, expand.exe) following browser download events from piracy domains within <10 seconds. Alert on extraction to temporary paths followed by execution of contained executables. Flag parent process chain: browser → archive tool → unexpected executable.

suggestion.title: Detect Go-based ransomware execution via parent-process and binary-signature patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Go encryptor' as defining characteristic; Go binaries exhibit distinct binary signatures and runtime behavior (e.g., large binary sizes, characteristic string tables) that differentiate from native Windows executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events launching Go-compiled binaries (identifiable via .go runtime imports, characteristic sections, or entropy patterns) combined with suspicious parent processes or execution from unusual locations. Go ransomware often exhibits large memory allocations and crypto library imports.

suggestion.title: Detect self-propagation via network share enumeration and SMB lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'self-propagating'; keywords include 'Lateral movement'. This indicates programmatic discovery and propagation across network shares, requiring monitoring of SMB/RPC enumeration and remote execution attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid SMB connection attempts to multiple hosts from a single source, especially combined with file write attempts to admin shares (C$, ADMIN$) or execution via WMI/RPC. Look for sequences of NetUseAdd or WNetAddConnection2 calls indicating network discovery followed by lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Detect privilege escalation techniques preceding encryption activity
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'Elevation of privilege'; ransomware requires elevated context to encrypt system-critical volumes. Must correlate privilege escalation attempts with subsequent file encryption patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UAC bypass attempts (SetUserFTA registry modifications, token impersonation, DLL hijacking), RunAs execution, or scheduled task creation preceding abnormal file write patterns in system directories. Correlate privilege escalation events with subsequent encryption activity.

suggestion.title: Detect credential harvesting preceding lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagating ransomware requires valid credentials or session tokens to move laterally. Human-operated RaaS groups typically harvest credentials (LSA dumping, SAM extraction) before propagation begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of credential-dumping utilities (mimikatz, ProcDump targeting lsass) or suspicious system calls to RtlInitUnicodeString/RtlCopyUnicodeString. Correlate with subsequent lateral movement attempts using extracted credentials.

suggestion.title: Detect mass file encryption with ransomware behavioral signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware impact phase; core attack signature is encryption of large file counts within short timeframes across multiple directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file modifications (create/write events on common user file extensions: .docx, .xlsx, .pdf, .jpg) at high frequency (>100 files/minute) combined with creation of ransom note files. Alert on file extension changes to known ransomware suffixes or new extensions appearing suddenly.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 communications and data exfiltration by RaaS affiliate
suggestion.rationale: Keywords note 'Ransomware as a service' model; separate affiliate operators require C2 channels for coordination, payment negotiation, and exfiltration. Must detect outbound communications and data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from affected hosts to known C2 domains (require IOC list), abnormal DNS queries (DNS tunneling), or connections to Tor exit nodes. Correlate with large data reads from sensitive file paths and staging in temp directories.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Exploitation Attempt — Suspicious HTTP POST to Admin/API Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw' — requires initial-access detection. No UC generated by pipeline despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS servers for POST requests to /api/*, /admin/*, or /upload/* endpoints with anomalous headers (missing Authorization, malformed User-Agent) or oversized payloads. Flag 200 responses followed by unexpected child-process spawning within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Process Execution — LSASS/Registry Access & DLL Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deploy Credential Stealer' — pipeline failed to generate any detection UC for credential-access execution phase. Should detect memory-dumping and credential-store access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect credential stealer via: (1) process spawning with LSASS access (OpenProcess with PROCESS_VM_READ), (2) registry reads to HKLM\Security\SAM or HKU\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings, (3) suspicious DLL loads (crypt32, vaultcli, ntdll from anomalous process), (4) command-line tools (mimikatz, secretsdump) or encoded PowerShell executing credential-extraction cmdlets.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Compromised Endpoints — Beaconing & Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer inherently exfiltrates harvested data; article context implies active C2. Pipeline generated zero network-based detection UC for command-and-control or exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound beaconing from client endpoints to attacker infrastructure: (1) HTTPS/TLS to non-business ASNs or geolocations, (2) DNS queries to newly-registered or typosquatted domains, (3) persistent connections on high-numbered ports (>49152), (4) traffic volume anomalies (regular small exfiltration bursts post-infection).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from EMS to Protected Client Endpoints via SMB/WMI
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of endpoint-management server enables multi-system attack surface. Article context (plural 'threat actors,' 'deploy') suggests lateral movement, but pipeline missed this kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for: (1) SMB port 445 connections from EMS to previously-dormant client subnets, (2) WMI/RPC process creation (svchost.exe, rundll32.exe spawned with remote execution arguments), (3) file-transfer patterns from EMS to clients (e.g., .ps1, .exe, .dll writes via \\\\client\\c$), (4) PSEXEC signatures.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Service Installation or Scheduled Task Persistence from EMS Context
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence mechanisms not addressed by pipeline. Credential stealer must persist; should detect service/task creation from EMS or compromised EMS-spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: (1) services or scheduled tasks created by FortiClient EMS process or child processes, (2) registry writes to HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* from EMS context, (3) task creation via schtasks.exe with suspicious binaries or obfuscated arguments, (4) persistence mechanisms writing to Startup folders or WMI event subscriptions.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from FortiClient EMS Parent — Execution Phase Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation leads to code execution; article implies payload execution but pipeline failed to surface execution-phase UC. Should detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unknown binaries spawned from EMS processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect: (1) cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned by FortiClient/EMS service processes (fortisslvpn.exe, sslvpndaemon, etc.) with SYSTEM privileges, (2) non-whitelisted child processes from EMS binaries, (3) process creation with encoded payloads or IEX/DownloadString arguments, (4) processes with suspicious working directories or command-line lengths >200 chars.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Installation Outside MDM Control
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly addresses 'what MDM can't protect on developer machines' — implies unmanaged tooling as core gap. Developers install runtimes, IDEs, package managers, and CLI tools that bypass device enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution or installation of development tools (Python, Node.js, Go, cargo, gradle, Maven) from user temp directories, %APPDATA%, or non-standard paths. Correlate with parent processes that are not MSI installers or package managers. Flag unsigned binaries or those with zero VT detections.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Git or SSH Keys
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines hold Git credentials, SSH keys, and API tokens — MDM cannot control access to local .git/config, ~/.ssh/, or credential stores. Article topic necessitates detection of credential material access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads from .ssh directories, .git/config, .aws/, .kube/, or API key stores. Alert on process execution that accesses multiple credential files in sequence. Flag unusual parent processes (browsers, unknown scripts) reading SSH keys or GitHub tokens.

suggestion.title: Package Manager Supply Chain Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Development machines rely on npm, pip, gem, cargo without MDM control over package source validation. Malicious package install is plausible vector on unmanaged dev systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package manager invocations (npm install, pip install, cargo add) to non-standard registries or with suspicious registry redirects. Monitor for download of packages with names that typosquuat legitimate libraries. Alert on packages that execute scripts post-install from untrusted or newly-registered authors.

suggestion.title: IDE Plugin Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: IDEs (VS Code, IntelliJ, Visual Studio) support plugin ecosystems that execute arbitrary code and persist without MDM oversight — common persistence and code exfiltration vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin directories (.vscode/extensions, .IntelliJIdea/config/plugins) for unauthorized or newly-added plugins. Alert on child processes spawned by IDE that execute scripts or network calls. Flag plugin install from unsigned sources or with high entropy or obfuscated code.

suggestion.title: Unmanaged VPN or Proxy Bypass for Code Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines may tunnel code and credentials through personal VPNs or proxy tools MDM cannot inspect. Article theme suggests exfiltration bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning of VPN/proxy tools (OpenVPN, WireGuard, proxychains, mitmproxy) from developer-controlled directories or user-installed versions. Correlate with subsequent DNS or TLS traffic to personal cloud storage (Dropbox, Google Drive, OneDrive) or messaging services. Flag encrypted tunnels to non-corporate gateways originating from dev workstations.

suggestion.title: Build Artifact and Source Code Theft via Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines often access shared build artifacts, internal repos, and CI/CD credentials. MDM cannot prevent lateral movement if the machine is compromised and used as a pivot point to access source code repositories or artifact storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on developer machines accessing internal Git repos, Artifactory, Nexus, or S3 buckets from unexpected processes or at unusual times. Monitor for bulk cloning of repositories or downloading of artifacts in sequence. Flag access from processes not typically associated with development workflows (shells, file explorers, browsers).

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code Repository Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'exfiltrate Source Code.' Should detect large git clone/pull operations, bulk .git directory access, or repository export via legitimate tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git.exe spawning with clone/pull/archive targeting unfamiliar or high-volume repositories; correlate with large outbound network transfers to non-repo endpoints. Baseline normal developer patterns; trigger on >N repositories accessed in <M minutes or >X GB egress per session.

suggestion.title: API Keys and Secrets Exfiltration from Dev Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Secrets' as explicit exfiltration target. Detect reads/copies of .env files, .git/config credentials, ~/.ssh, API keystores, and cloud credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-developer-tooling processes accessing secrets paths (.env, .git/config, .aws/credentials, ~/.ssh, .npmrc, /etc/passwd variants). Combine with archival or staging detections (zip, tar, base64-encode of secrets files). Alert on bulk reads or copies from IDE/editor processes.

suggestion.title: Compromised or Trojanized Developer Tool Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'abuse Trusted Developer Tooling' implies tooling itself is compromised or MITM'd. Detect anomalous network and execution behavior from dev tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for legitimate package managers (npm, pip, maven, cargo) and source-control tools (git) connecting to official repos. Alert on connections to non-standard IPs, ports, or infrastructure; cross-reference process hash against published official binaries. Monitor for dev tool spawning shell interpreters or network utilities (curl, wget, nc).

suggestion.title: Rapid Compression and Staging of Source + Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration workflow: collection→staging→transfer. Detect compression of source trees (.git, /src) and secrets in single batch operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid tar/zip/7z operations targeting source directories and secrets paths within minutes of each other. Correlate with subsequent network uploads to external cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob, Dropbox, rclone) or unexpected egress IPs. Establish dev environment baseline; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Package Repository Authentication and Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Package managers (npm, PyPI, Maven Central) are core trusted tooling. Detect registry auth bypass, stolen tokens, and unauthorized uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc, pip.conf, .m2/settings.xml for suspicious registry endpoints or leaked tokens. Detect package-manager CLI commands from unexpected user/IP contexts. Alert on bulk package publish operations from compromised accounts or mass package downloads to non-standard directories.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as attack vector but zero IOC extraction. Vulnerability ID is the attack entry point and must be detected at exploitation time ('Attackers Use...Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Marimo instance logs and upstream proxies for HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-39987 exploitation patterns (code injection to vulnerable endpoint). Correlate with unexpected process spawning from Python/Marimo interpreter within seconds of request.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—this novel execution mechanism and its process signatures were not extracted. LLM-spawned system commands represent a distinct kill-chain step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) from Python LLM libraries or Marimo kernel processes with non-standard lineage. Flag execution of system commands (whoami, id, cat /etc/passwd) with parent process tied to LLM invocation or notebook evaluation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution via LLM Interface
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation 'for Post-Exploitation' implies attacker issues shell/system commands through LLM chat/API interface. Pipeline missed detection for this execution path—system command execution bridged through LLM responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell metacharacters and system commands in LLM request payloads or responses, followed by child process execution. Detect command execution from LLM runtime with arguments derived from LLM-generated or LLM-guided content.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Reconnaissance via LLM Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes LLM deployment 'for Post-Exploitation After' exploit—post-exploitation workflows universally include reconnaissance and discovery phases. Pipeline extracted no use cases for discovery/lateral-movement phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration commands (net user, Get-LocalUser, whoami, ls -la /etc, id) and network probes (nslookup, ping, nmap) spawned from LLM-related processes post-exploitation window. Correlate discovery-phase commands with prior CVE-2026-39987 exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Vishing-induced anomalous Entra authentication during attack window
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' in early April. Should detect logins inconsistent with employee baseline (impossible travel, new device, unusual time, MFA bypass).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra interactive logins from compromised employee showing impossible-travel distance from baseline, new device fingerprints, or repeated failed MFA challenges followed by eventual success. Correlate timing with early April 2026 and cross-reference with employee vishing-report submission or credential-reset requests.

suggestion.title: Salesforce bulk data exfiltration — customer PII and CPNI export
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, plan information, support ticket data, and some CPNI data.' Must detect high-volume record queries/exports outside normal admin activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk data exports, Reports job execution, or API queries returning >10k Contact/Account/CPNI records in single transaction, especially initiated by accounts outside normal data-export roles or during off-hours. Correlate with Entra login anomaly detection.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from cloud identity provider to SaaS—credential reuse across boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain explicit: Entra compromise → Salesforce data theft. Should detect when cloud-identity credentials immediately enable downstream SaaS access with divergent session context (device, geo, time).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra login anomaly (new device, impossible travel) with Salesforce API/UI authentication from identical source IP within 5-60 minutes using user account. Flag if Salesforce user_id shows first-ever login or deviates from historical access patterns (time, frequency, data accessed).

suggestion.title: High-volume data staging in SaaS prior to exfiltration — export-job clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes orchestrated theft of 42M records implying deliberate data consolidation. Should detect Salesforce bulk-export jobs, temporary data objects, or mass-download patterns preceding exfiltration window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clustering of Salesforce Reports, Data Export, or List export operations targeting Contact/Account/CPNI objects within 24-hour window, especially if generating cumulative output >5M records. Trigger on multiple export jobs by single user or service account.

suggestion.title: Dark web emergence of Charter Communications customer data — PII/CPNI fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' Describes 4.9M email addresses, names, phone numbers, physical addresses, plus 85k employee records. Should detect these artifacts in dark web markets/forums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web paste/market sites for Charter customer data bundles (email+phone+address triples), bulk contact lists, or internal employee directories. Cross-reference leaked data volume and field structure (4.9M unique emails, CPNI subsets, job titles in 85k subset) against threat-intel feeds and breach confirmations.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection for Phishing Content Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'turns ChatGPT web summaries into a phishing surface' — implies attackers craft malicious prompts to generate phishing content via summary feature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API calls with suspicious prompt payloads containing phishing indicators (urgency language, credential requests, urgent action demands) in summary or web-browsing requests. Correlate with outbound SMTP or webhook delivery of generated content.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Feature Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically leverages ChatGPT's 'web summaries' feature — detection should monitor for abnormal summary request patterns, URL injection attempts, or summarization of phishing/malware domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect burst or sequential ChatGPT API calls to web summary endpoint with URLs pointing to known phishing or attacker-controlled domains. Correlate with downstream email delivery or social-engineering campaigns.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Output Misuse for Phishing Kit Distribution
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability generates phishing content or HTML, downstream detection should identify generated phishing kits being persisted or exfiltrated via file shares, pastebin, or email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exfiltration of generated phishing templates, HTML payloads, or summary-derived credential harvesting forms from endpoints where ChatGPT integrations are active. Baseline typical ChatGPT output sizes and flag anomalous mass downloads.

suggestion.title: Trusted Relationship Exploitation via ChatGPT
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPT's trusted brand used to bypass email filters or user skepticism — detection focus on ChatGPT-domain or integrations embedding phishing in legitimate-looking summary emails or summaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails delivered with ChatGPT branding, headers, or generated content that route user clicks to attacker infrastructure. Monitor for summaries embedded with malicious links using URL shorteners or lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection via OpenAI API Keys or OAuth Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely requires API access — detect unusual authentication patterns, token reuse, or lateral movement from compromised ChatGPT API credentials into malicious phishing workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API authentication anomalies (geographic impossibility, rapid location changes, token rotation). Correlate API calls to summary endpoints with downstream phishing campaign telemetry.

suggestion.title: Detect Downloads from Domains Impersonating AI Platform Vendors
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' — trivial IOC and behavioral marker; no detection generated despite clear masquerading intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections or file downloads from domains matching OpenAI/Claude/ChatGPT naming patterns but with suspicious TLDs or typosquats. Pair with cross-referencing against known-good OpenAI CDNs (cdn.openai.com). Alert on executable downloads from these domains with download behavior inconsistent with legitimate app distribution.

suggestion.title: Detect Executable Downloads Following ChatGPT Share Link Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'published it through a shared chatgpt.com/s/ link' and users downloaded malware after visiting. No detection proposed despite clear browser-to-execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences: web access to chatgpt.com/s/* URLs (shared artifacts) followed within 5 minutes by executable downloads (EXE, MSI, DMG, PKG) with parent process chrome.exe, firefox.exe, or edge.exe. Elevated risk if executable is named with masquerading language (ChatGPT, OpenAI, Claude). Track file hash and raise alert on any execution.

suggestion.title: Detect VM/Sandbox Evasion via System Information Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine' — direct MITRE T1082 execution pattern with no detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned from unsigned/recent executables (potential malware) that invoke VM/hypervisor detection commands: systeminfo, wmic path Win32_ComputerSystem, Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem, vboxcontrol, qemu-ga detection, or checks for common VM artifacts (/proc/cpuinfo for kvm, registry queries for vmware/virtualbox). Correlate process creation with recent suspicious download or document open.

suggestion.title: Detect Cloaked Malware URLs via URLScan/Platform Divergence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' No detection for cloaking behavior or payload divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate URL click/access from employee device with security scanner submissions of the same URL. Flag URLs where scanner returns benign content (AR/VR, generic pages) but employee device downloads binary executable or shows post-compromise behavior (credential access, lateral movement). Cross-reference with Shodan/URLScan public history. Escalate if divergence signature matches known cloaking kits.

suggestion.title: Detect Google Ads Redirection to AI Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors used 'Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com' — attack vector requiring ad-click tracking and landing-page validation. No detection generated despite named attack method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network events where referrer is Google Ads domain (google.com/aclk or affiliate tracking) and final destination is legitimate AI platform (chatgpt.com, claude.ai) but URL path is /s/<uncommon-hash> or /s/<low-entropy-string>. Cross-reference artifact URL against known-safe shared prompts/conversations. Alert on artifact access immediately followed by out-of-band file download.

suggestion.title: Detect Infostealer Post-Execution Behavioral Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'earlier campaigns abusing AI platform sharing features have distributed infostealers' and references ClickFix payloads, but no behavioral detection proposed for credential/data harvesting post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After execution of unsigned binary from chatgpt/openai impersonation domain, detect infostealer indicators: child processes targeting browser credential stores (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), creation of temporary files in %APPDATA% or %TEMP% matching credential-staging patterns, network connections to non-standard ports (8080, 9090, 443 with non-SSL cert), base64-encoded data exfiltration, or rapid access to system files (SAM hive, LSASS).

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 vulnerability scanner detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions'—scanner signatures must flag unpatched PAN-OS instances. This is the foundational detection for a CISA KEV entry with active wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any PAN-OS instance unpatched for CVE-2026-0257 via vulnerability scanner or asset discovery. Escalate externally routable management interfaces. Cross-check with network exposure data to identify attack surface.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS authentication bypass on admin interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions.' Authentication logs should show bypass attempts or unauthenticated successful commands on admin channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin/management logs for successful privilege operations without preceding valid authentication event, authentication state violations, or direct privilege escalation in audit trails.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN session initiation post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as the exploitation outcome. VPN logs must show anomalous session creation from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session creation from IPs not in baseline allow-list, outside standard access windows, or from geographies inconsistent with organization. Flag sessions immediately following CVE-2026-0257 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Failed-then-successful authentication pattern on PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Typical bypass exploitation signature: attacker triggers detectable auth failures while probing, then succeeds via exploit. Article mentions 'bypass security restrictions'—this pattern indicates exploitation success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 3+ failed authentication attempts on PAN-OS admin interface with successful session establishment from same source within 5-minute window. Flag as high-confidence exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS management plane network exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies public-facing vulnerability. Detect inbound traffic to admin/management ports (SSH 22, HTTPS 443, API 10252) from untrusted network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to PAN-OS management interfaces from non-admin network ranges or from internet-routable sources. Baseline typical admin access paths; flag deviations correlating with CVE-2026-0257 scanning/exploitation.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS configuration drift post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once VPN access is established via CVE-2026-0257, attacker will persist by modifying firewall rules, user accounts, or VPN settings. Detection must catch unauthorized config changes on vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall rule additions, VPN user account creation, or admin credential changes occurring outside maintenance windows on instances flagged as vulnerable or post-exploitation. Cross-correlate with authentication bypass detections.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Client Installation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnet consisted of at least 17 million infected devices' and 'platform offers corporate, residential, and mobile proxies.' Indicates unauthorized proxy client installation on victim endpoints without knowledge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of undocumented proxy client software establishing persistence via registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or system services. Monitor for suspicious child processes or DLL injection from proxy client executables. Flag processes with network signatures matching residential proxy client beaconing.

suggestion.title: Proxy Botnet Command and Control Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: '200 servers used to host the infrastructure were located in the Netherlands' and 'seized several botnet servers from a hosting provider.' These servers directly controlled botnet endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify egress connections to seized server IP ranges in Netherlands hosting provider ASNs. Correlate against threat feeds listing seized infrastructure. Detect DNS lookups or HTTP requests to known Asocks C2 domains. Flag non-standard ports or protocol deviations in proxy client communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Hosting Provider Botnet Infrastructure Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hosting provider took the botnet offline because it was being used for criminal activities.' Abuse of hosting infrastructure is persistence and operational enablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hosting provider ASN/IP ranges for mass C2 server patterns: multiple accounts provisioning servers with identical C2 traffic signatures, rapid iteration of IP addresses, correlation with abuse report clustering, and threat feed blacklisting of provider IP space.

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Coordination from Distributed Proxy Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnets...used for illegal activities such as distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Coordination of 17M endpoints for synchronized DDoS is measurable attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate incoming DDoS traffic with known residential proxy IP ranges and ASNs. Detect synchronized traffic spikes from distributed proxy addresses targeting single victim. Distinguish attack-pattern traffic from normal proxy load-balancing by examining request distribution and timing variance.

suggestion.title: Asocks Malicious Proxy Service IOC Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'linked to a service called Asocks...advertises itself as a universal proxy service with 7 million IP addresses, 150 locations, and 100,000 clients.' Named malicious infrastructure with explicit operational scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and blacklist Asocks infrastructure IOCs: known domains, C2 IP ranges, ASNs, client software hashes. Alert on download/execution of Asocks client binaries on non-proxy-designated systems. Cross-reference internal detections against public Asocks infrastructure lists and resold proxy IP feeds.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Resource Hijacking via Proxy Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnets...used for illegal activities such as...cryptocurrency mining.' 17M-device botnet directed toward mining represents quantifiable compute resource hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy client hosts for anomalous sustained CPU/GPU load, memory pressure, and outbound traffic to mining pools. Detect execution of mining-specific processes (xmrig, xmr-stak) or monero pool communication (stratum protocol, port 3333). Flag child process creation anomalies under proxy client parent process.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT request body containing vm2 prototype pollution payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'By combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")` ... allows the escape' — exploit is delivered via HTTP request body to vulnerable vm2 application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests (POST/PUT to Node.js endpoints) for patterns indicating vm2 exploitation: Buffer prototype-chain access (__proto__, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__) combined with Function/constructor references. Elevated confidence if payload appears after vm2 import detected in application code.

suggestion.title: Node.js process loading vm2/NodeVM followed by Object prototype pollution operations
suggestion.rationale: Article shows exploit requires vm2 library be loaded then chains `Buffer.call.call` operations — detect library import + suspicious prototype chain access at application instrumentation level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js process with (a) require('vm2') or NodeVM instantiation, then (b) subsequent __proto__/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ property access on Buffer or Object prototype within same process context. Time window: <5sec between require and access.

suggestion.title: TypeError constructor leak from sandbox context (ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error, the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained' — this is the critical escape moment and may leave detectable error traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript error stack traces originating from vm2 sandbox context showing TypeError constructor resolution or ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE patterns combined with __proto__ chain access. Compare error context (sandboxed frame) against constructor origin (host frame).

suggestion.title: Process privilege/capability change after vm2 sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code' — successful escape would permit Node process to access host-level resources or spawn shells with elevated context not normally available to sandboxed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process spawning child processes (shells, system utilities) with file-system or network access to paths/resources outside normal vm2 sandbox scope. Baseline legitimate vm2 app capabilities first; look for capability expansion after suspicious Error/prototype chain activity.

suggestion.title: vm2 module/NodeVM instantiation in public-facing HTTP endpoint handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit via 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) — suggests vulnerable vm2 is reachable from external HTTP layer. Identify where vm2 is being instantiated in request handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Code-level detection: find vm2/NodeVM require() and new VM() calls within HTTP request handler chains (Express routes, API endpoints, middleware). High-risk: vm2 code instantiation in handler that accepts user input (request body, params, headers).

suggestion.title: vm2 package downgrade or version manipulation post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability in versions <=3.11.3. Attacker may downgrade to vulnerable version or tamper with package-lock.json/node_modules after gaining code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to vm2 version in package.json or package-lock.json (downgrade to <=3.11.3), or direct manipulation of node_modules/vm2 files. Correlate with Node process restart or npm install commands.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawning OS shell with reconnaissance commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes post-exploitation phase: 'Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="node"... FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe",...) ... Processes.process="*whoami*" OR Processes.process="*id*" ... OR Processes.process="*cat /etc*"'. This is the execution phase after sandbox escape succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OS shell binaries (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh) spawned directly from node/node.exe parent. Cross-reference against enumeration command indicators (whoami, id, hostname, /etc/passwd). High-signal pattern for vm2 sandbox escape.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package detection (<=3.11.3)
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt UC_5_3 establishes surface: 'Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\vm2\\package.json" OR ... "*/node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js"'. Covers discovery/exposure assessment phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for vm2 package.json or nodevm.js file presence/modification in node_modules. Correlate against version metadata to identify unpatched installations. High false-positive rate in development environments; filter to production servers.

suggestion.title: vm2 NodeVM initialization with nesting:true and undefined require option
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'strict equality (options.require === false)... bypassed by omitting the require option... When require is not specified, options.require is undefined, not false.' Direct detection of the bypassed security check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If available: log or SIEM integration for vm2 NodeVM instantiation. Search for instances with nesting:true where require option is absent or undefined. Requires app-level instrumentation; this pattern is difficult to detect at OS level without behavioral signals.

suggestion.title: NodeVM process builtin access — denylist bypass exploitation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'process and inspector/promises. Both can be used from sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives.' Pipeline should create dedicated detection for require('process') or getBuiltinModule('process') calls within NodeVM context, not just string matching in command line.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes loading or referencing the 'process' builtin via require() or inspector/promises during execution. This represents the active exploitation step where sandboxed code attempts to break out of the NodeVM sandbox. Would require code/memory inspection or module loading telemetry if available.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable NodeVM dependency in application codebase — asset discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vm2/NodeVM as a library with a denylist bypass vulnerability. Organizations should inventory which applications and services have vm2 as a transitive or direct dependency. Article states vulnerability allows 'sandboxed code to bypass the intended builtin restrictions' implying vm2 is often embedded in larger applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all systems and services where vm2 or NodeVM is installed as a package dependency, regardless of version. This establishes asset exposure baseline. Query package managers, SCA tools, and software inventory for vm2 presence. Prioritize public-facing applications and those accepting user-supplied code for sandboxing.

suggestion.title: Code execution via inspector/promises module — post-sandbox escape behavioral detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'inspector/promises' as a denylist bypass vector distinct from 'process'. Inspector module is Node.js diagnostic tool. Article: 'the denylist misses...inspector/promises'. Should have dedicated detection for this specific module access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes instantiating or calling into the 'inspector' or 'inspector/promises' modules from within a NodeVM sandbox context. This represents the inspector-specific exploitation path. Can be detected via command-line inspection for require('inspector/promises') patterns or module loading telemetry if available via EDR.

suggestion.title: Code submission to vm2 service with Promise manipulation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers to write code which can escape from VM2 sandbox'—no detection covers the INITIAL ATTACK VECTOR. Code with Promise.species, constructor chains, or Symbol introspection submitted via vm2.run() or sandbox entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vm2 sandbox entry points (vm2.VM(), vm2.run() calls) for code containing: Promise subclass definitions, Symbol.species getters, constructor.constructor chains, Function.prototype manipulation, mainModule.require chains. High-fidelity when correlated with subsequent child_process spawn from node.exe (UC_6_2).

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from node.exe post vm2 escape (integrity level jump)
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_2 detects child process spawn but not privilege escalation. Article implies 'arbitrary commands on host'—unprivileged Node.js should not spawn elevated shells. Missing: integrity-level and admin-context transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe parent→cmd.exe/powershell.exe child with integrity-level jump: initiating process (MEDIUM) spawning child (HIGH/SYSTEM). OR non-admin node.exe process suddenly writing to System32, registry HKLM, or accessing privileged resources post-escape.

suggestion.title: Failed resetPromiseSpecies sanitation bypass (Promise.species gadget chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article core technical detail: 'missing a call to resetPromiseSpecies to ensure that this has no special species.' No detection exists for the EXPLOITATION MECHANISM ITSELF—malicious code defining custom Promise.species inside vm2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Promise prototype pollution inside vm2 VM context: Promise[Symbol.species] getter definitions, thenable object chains, Promise constructor callbacks that inspect 'this' without reset, or any code path that exploits deferred resetPromiseSpecies() call.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47208 vulnerability present in software inventory (asset exposure)
suggestion.rationale: No detection for vulnerable package in deployment/CMDB. Article CVE is primary IOC but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Need inventory-based detection mapping vm2 package version to vulnerability window.
log_sources: Software inventory (SCCM, ServiceNow, cloud asset inventory)
