suggestion.rationale: After role promotion succeeds, attacker will query administrative surfaces to understand their new scope. Article mentions agents, issues, projects access after escalation. Detect queries to /workspaces/*/roles, /workspaces/*/members (list), or admin configuration endpoints within 5 minutes of successful role change.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful role-change PATCH (200/204) to same source issuing subsequent GET requests to administrative list/query endpoints (members, roles, permissions, settings). Timeline constraint: discovery queries within 5 minutes of privilege escalation indicate reconnaissance post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Workspace Owner Cardinality Spike — Sudden elevation of owner count
suggestion.rationale: The CVE allows arbitrary promotion to owner. A spike in workspace owner count, especially multiple promotions from a single source, is a strong signal of exploitation. Not explicitly in article but natural follow-up to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline owner count per workspace. Alert when owner count increases by >1 in a 1-hour window, or when multiple users are elevated to owner role from a single source IP/account in short timespan. Correlate against change requests or bulk provisioning windows to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Cross-Member Unauthorized Role Escalation — Non-Admin Promoting Other Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows any member to promote 'or others' to owner. Detection should flag when a non-admin/non-owner user successfully changes role for a different user. This is the lateral privilege model distinct from self-promotion.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with request/response metadata
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PATCH requests where (authenticated_user != target_user_id) AND (authenticated_user_current_role != 'owner') AND (response status = 200/204). This is privilege escalation of another user by a non-privileged account.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Software Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly delivers 'ScreenConnect Malware' (the RAT/RMM tool itself). Pipeline extracted no execution or C2 detection rules. Must detect installation, registry artifacts, and network callbacks typical of ScreenConnect post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: ScreenConnect installations are characteristically triggered from unusual download paths and create specific service names or registry keys. Monitor for process execution with ScreenConnect in the command line, service creation with known ScreenConnect identifiers, and outbound TLS/HTTPS connections to known ScreenConnect C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Fake Adobe Document Cloud Phishing Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages'—credential harvesting infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for HTTP requests to typosquatted or lookalike Adobe domains, and form submissions to non-Adobe origins masquerading as Adobe login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to domains with high string similarity to 'adobe.com' or 'documentcloud.adobe.com', or requests containing 'adobe' in the host but resolving to non-Adobe IP space. Flag form submissions (POST requests) to these fake domains containing credential patterns (email + password fields).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery of ScreenConnect Installer
suggestion.rationale: Title implies phishing delivery mechanism ('Hackers Use Fake... Pages to Deliver'). Pipeline extracted no email-based initial access detections or IOCs (sender, subject, attachment hashes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing .scr, .exe, .msi, or .zip attachments linking to or containing ScreenConnect installers. Flag emails with body text directing users to fake Adobe login pages. Correlate email delivery with subsequent DNS queries to known ScreenConnect C2 or fake-Adobe domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Non-Adobe Origins
suggestion.rationale: Fake Adobe pages are credential harvesters. Pipeline did not surface detections for successful credential exfiltration to attacker-controlled endpoints or POST requests with credential patterns to non-Adobe domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing email and password parameters sent to domains outside Adobe's legitimate IP space. Flag successful submissions (HTTP 200/302) that occur immediately after visiting lookalike Adobe domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download of ScreenConnect Installer from Non-Official Sources
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect delivery implies download of the malware binary from attacker infrastructure or compromised sites. Pipeline has no file-download or hash-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .msi, .exe, or .scr files with names containing 'ScreenConnect', 'Support', 'Remote', or similar terms from domains not owned by ConnectWise (legitimate ScreenConnect vendor). Flag followed by execution from %TEMP% or %Downloads%.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement via ScreenConnect
suggestion.rationale: Once ScreenConnect is installed, it becomes a lateral movement and persistence tool. Pipeline missed detections for ScreenConnect being used to pivot to other hosts or establish secondary C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect process spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or initiating network connections to internal IP ranges. Flag multiple simultaneous ScreenConnect connections from a single source to different internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack using 'fake video player updates' as initial access. Pipeline failed to map supply chain/trojanized software technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to download or execute video player updates from non-official sources, unsigned update binaries, or update processes initiating from web-download artifacts rather than official application paths. Monitor for update executables launched from TEMP, Downloads, or AppData/Local directories.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Process Execution Post-Software Update
suggestion.rationale: Article states miners are deployed; article body suggests execution follows update installation. No UC generated for post-installation payload activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect resource-intensive processes (xmrig, monero miners, etc.) spawned within minutes of software update completion. Alert on child processes of legitimate-appearing update utilities with high CPU/memory consumption or cryptomining signatures in command line arguments.

suggestion.title: RAT Command and Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions RAT (Remote Access Trojan) malware deployment, but no detection UC for C2 beaconing or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or network connections from recently-updated applications to suspicious domains or IPs. Alert on RAT-associated ports, DGAs, or domains known to host RAT infrastructure. Focus on outbound connections from injected/child processes of update mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks from Update Process
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage attack pattern (update → miner + RAT) implies persistence mechanism not identified. Article describes ongoing deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks, registry autorun entries, or startup folder artifacts spawned by or in the seconds following software update executable completion. Cross-correlate task creation with update binary path and payload process execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Resource Consumption Post-Update Installation
suggestion.rationale: Miners cause sustained CPU/memory spike; RAT causes network anomalies. No behavioral detection UC generated despite clear malware impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when system CPU utilization spikes >75% for sustained periods (>10 min) immediately following software update completion, especially if process is not identifiable in official software vendor libraries. Cross-check against baseline for user's typical post-update behavior.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Profile Engagement
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Using LinkedIn Social Engineering'—pipeline extracted zero detection for initial access. Should detect profiles impersonating recruiters, suspicious job postings targeting specific orgs/roles, or unusual LinkedIn API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LinkedIn traffic spikes from unusual geographies, repeated profile visits to HR/infosec staff, or download of bulk employee contact lists. Flag accounts created within 30 days of first targeting contact.

suggestion.title: macOS Custom Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline mentions 'Custom macOS Malware'—pipeline found no execution detection. Should detect suspicious binary launch, unsigned code, or staged malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: (1) execution of unsigned binaries from Downloads or temp; (2) process spawning shell interpreters from unusual parents (Safari, Mail); (3) code signing validation failures on newly-downloaded files.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via Launch Agents or Boot Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware typically establishes persistence—article does not specify mechanism, but pipeline should have flagged common patterns. Detection needed for .plist modifications, ~/Library/LaunchAgents writes, or cron/launchd abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons/, or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ by non-system processes. Alert if launchd spawns unexpected executables or scripts from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Application Bundle Delivery
suggestion.rationale: LinkedIn-delivered payloads often disguise malware as legitimate apps (.app bundles). Pipeline missing detection for unexpected bundle modifications, Info.plist tampering, or masqueraded applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or re-signed .app bundles in non-standard locations (~/Downloads, /tmp). Flag if application bundle contains executables in unexpected paths or calls shell scripts during launch.

suggestion.title: Detect VS Code Tunnel Reverse Shell Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes abuse of VS Code Tunnels as expanded C2 arsenal. Should detect port tunneling via devtunnels.ms or local tunneling process. ('VS Code Tunnels' appears in title as attack vector.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code.exe or codeserver.exe spawning with --tunnel flag or child processes establishing outbound TLS connections to devtunnels.ms. Alert on persistent devtunnels tunnel sessions in user profiles. Correlate with unusual RDP or SSH lateral movement following tunnel activation.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTPSpy C2 Beacon Traffic
suggestion.rationale: HTTPSpy is explicitly named as deployed tool. Requires IOC extraction (domains, IPs, certificate fingerprints) and behavioral detection for HTTP(S) beacon patterns. Article confirms HTTPSpy is active Kimsuky tooling. Need network baseline for this C2 family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTPSpy beacon signatures via HTTP header anomalies, User-Agent patterns, and POST intervals. Cross-reference with known Kimsuky infrastructure. Alert on HTTPS traffic to low-reputation IPs with self-signed certs or certificate pinning bypasses.

suggestion.title: Detect HelloDoor Backdoor Installation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: HelloDoor is explicitly named as expanded arsenal tool (article title). No existing IOCs provided. Pipeline should surface installation vectors (email, watering hole, supply chain) and persistence mechanisms (registry, scheduled task, startup folder).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HelloDoor binary execution (file name / hash TBD). Detect registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU indicating persistence (Run, RunOnce, scheduled task creation). Alert on suspicious service installations or WMI event subscription creation.

suggestion.title: Detect Kimsuky Credential Harvesting via Compromised Dev Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates expansion into developer tools (VS Code) as C2 vectors; Kimsuky historically targets credentials. Pipeline missed connection between tool abuse and credential access kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-access patterns post-tunnel activation: browser credential dumping (LSASS access), clipboard monitoring, form filling tools. Correlate code.exe spawning with credential manager or browser profile access. Alert on exfiltration of .git credentials or SSH keys.

suggestion.title: Detect Kimsuky Initial Access via Spear Phishing and Watering Hole
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'expands arsenal' implying continued initial access campaigns. Kimsuky signature includes targeted spear-phishing and watering holes. Pipeline should include pre-execution detection for phishing payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with Korean-language social engineering or geopolitics lures to policy/research targets. Detect suspicious Office macro execution or LNK file execution tied to public shares. Alert on anomalous PowerShell/CMD spawning from Temp or Downloads folders.

suggestion.title: Detect VS Code Tunnel Lateral Movement and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: VS Code Tunnels enable remote code execution and persistence across networked systems. Article does not detail but standard TTPs would include using tunnel for lateral movement. Pipeline missed persistence mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tunnel connections from unexpected source IPs or user accounts. Detect code.exe spawning in System or Service context (anomalous). Alert on tunnel port forwarding enabling SSH or RDP access to internal systems post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Codex Authentication Token Theft via Spoofed UI
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes theft of 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' through a 'Legitimate-Looking' remote interface. This is the core attack vector and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token exfiltration targeting OpenAI API endpoints. Detect browser/process interactions with domains impersonating Codex (homograph variants, typosquatted subdomains). Alert when authentication tokens are accessed from unexpected processes or transmitted to non-OpenAI C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Access to Codex Phishing Domain / Homograph Attack
suggestion.rationale: The 'Legitimate-Looking' UI is a phishing attack surface described in the title. Requires detection of spoofed Codex domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify access to domains with typosquatting or homograph variations of Codex, OpenAI, or legitimate code model platforms. Flag visits by developers or R&D staff to such domains, especially if credential entry or token access follows.

suggestion.title: Abnormal OpenAI API Token Usage / Abuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once tokens are stolen, threat actors abuse them for code generation, data exfiltration, or resource consumption. Should detect anomalous token activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI API audit logs for unusual token usage: geolocation anomalies, request volume spikes, non-standard endpoints, off-hours access, or requests from suspicious user agents. Correlate with credential exposure timeline.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Phishing / Social Engineering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack depends on social engineering to direct developers to fake Codex UI. Should detect phishing campaigns targeting developer communities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails or messages containing links to Codex lookalike domains, especially if sent to known developer/AI research communities. Correlate with phishing infrastructure (shared IPs, registrant data, SSL certs) and downstream token exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation with Credential Context
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states malicious NuGet package exfiltrates banking passwords. No detection use case was generated for NuGet-based initial delivery combined with credential access signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet package installation (nuget.exe, dotnet restore) where the originating package source is external or mismatched from organizational allowlists. Correlate with subsequent credential-access indicators (LSASS access, registry queries for credential stores, WMI queries for credentials). Anomalous package names impersonating legitimate SDKs (e.g., containing typosquatting patterns or unofficial version numbering) warrant immediate isolation.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from SDK/Package Initialization Code
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies passwords exfiltrated; pipeline detected zero credential-access phase or techniques. SDK/package loading provides execution context for malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes spawned by NuGet/package managers (dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe) that subsequently access LSASS, SAM hive, or browser credential stores. Flag network connections from these processes to non-standard ports or external IPs. Monitor for in-memory credential dumping tools (mimikatz patterns) or credential enumeration via WMI/registry queries initiated from package load context.

suggestion.title: Build/Development Environment Beaconing to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates exfiltration; no detection for command-and-control communication was proposed. Banking credential theft typically involves data transfer to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build and development workstations for outbound connections to IP ranges or domains not whitelisted for legitimate package repositories and CI/CD systems. Flag DNS queries from build agents to newly registered domains or known malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate with process trees originating from package installation to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted or Impersonation NuGet Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly names the attack as impersonating Sicoob SDK; no detection strategy was generated to catch lookalike package names in package manifests or restore operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement a baseline of legitimate package identifiers from organizational nuget.config and project files. Alert on installation of packages with names similar to known SDKs (Levenshtein distance or common typosquatting patterns: missing letters, numeric substitution, domain confusion). Cross-reference package source URLs against authorized package registries (internal Artifactory, official NuGet.org); flag pulls from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Registry Access by Package Runtime for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Banking password exfiltration implies registry enumeration (Windows credential manager, browser auto-fill stores). Pipeline did not map this access pattern to a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned from .NET/NuGet context querying HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication or HKCU\Software\[Mozilla|Google|Microsoft]\[Firefox|Chrome|Edge]\Profiles for credential enumeration. Flag unusual registry access frequency or access to multiple credential stores in a short window. Cross-correlate with network exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials' — package manager installation is the entry vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases for NuGet or dotnet CLI package downloads despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet.exe or dotnet CLI invocations with .nupkg source URIs or install commands, followed by child-process spawning outside expected build directories. Alert on connections to non-official NuGet repositories or packages with typosquatting indicators (Sicoob variants: sicoob-*, sicoob-client-*, etc.).

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — malicious postinstall/preinstall hooks steal credentials, yet zero use case detects npm spawn + credential file access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install or yarn add with child processes reading .env files, ~/.aws/*, ~/.azure/*, KUBECONFIG, or Registry paths (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\*\Credentials). Flag if access occurs within 5 seconds of package install completion.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Theft from Package Initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Steals Banking Credentials' — indicates malware execution during or after package install, but zero detection use case for process trees spawning credential-scraping tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NuGet or npm parent process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl with unusual command lines (credential store queries, registry dumps, password manager enumeration). Alert on child process network connections immediately following spawn.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials from Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Banking credentials are stolen ('Steals Banking Credentials') implying command-and-control callback or data upload, but pipeline generated zero exfiltration detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT or DNS queries from NuGet/npm-spawned processes to suspicious domains (non-Microsoft, non-npm registry hosts). Correlate with preceding file reads of credential stores and validate domain reputation against known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest vs. Content Integrity Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Malicious NuGet and npm packages likely contain obfuscated or unsigned payloads. Pipeline should flag packages with file-count or hash discrepancies but generated zero artifact integrity use case.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Leveraging ChatGPT-Rendered Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads'—core attack vector is weaponized pages delivered via ChatGPT
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to attacker-controlled web pages or ChatGPT-generated rendering endpoints. Flag emails with suspicious ChatGPT conversation URLs or encoded payloads designed to render login forms.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API calls and web.archive-like endpoints for prompts requesting HTML/CSS/JavaScript generation targeting credential harvesting, form injection, or page cloning. Detect encoding of payloads to evade filtering.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Login Forms Rendered by ChatGPT

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Process Execution with Unusual Arguments

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code Repository Access and Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'exfiltrate source code'—implies repository enumeration, cloning, or bulk file access. No detection logic captured despite being primary data-gathering phase.

suggestion.title: Credential and API Key Extraction from Developer Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'exfiltrate...secrets'—strongly implies API keys, tokens, .ssh directories, or .env files accessed. No use case addresses secrets harvesting despite it being explicitly named in title.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Data Exfiltration from Development Workstations

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Developer Machine to Repositories or CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: Trusted developer tooling abuse suggests initial compromise of dev workstation, then lateral movement to central code repositories or CI/CD systems. Article does not detail this but is implicit in 'trusted tooling' supply-chain angle.

suggestion.title: File Access Patterns from Marimo Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploited Marimo instance will read sensitive files for exfiltration. Article describes post-exploitation phase but no data collection/staging detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential reads of sensitive files (config files, credential stores, database binaries) from Marimo process or spawned children. Alert on file compression or reading of multiple files in rapid succession from sensitive directories. Correlate file reads with outbound network activity.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Attack Targeting Employee Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'they breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Initial access vector is precisely documented but entirely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound voice calls to corporate numbers with Entra sign-in spikes, unusual Entra risky sign-ins, or MFA failures within 1–2 hours. Alert on credentials used from atypical geographies or devices immediately following vishing social-engineering indicators (caller ID spoofing, domain impersonation).

suggestion.title: Entra Service Account Compromise Leading to Salesforce Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' → 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' Credential compromise event and lateral movement chain not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra user credentials accessing Salesforce OAuth/federated apps post-compromise. Flag impossible-travel sign-ins, sign-ins from new devices, repeated failed authentication followed by successful login. Monitor for changes to MFA enrollment or authentication method post-breach.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export from Salesforce CRM System
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers…' Massive exfiltration volume (42M records) is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce API calls and reports for bulk record exports (>1K records in <5 minutes). Alert on CSV/Excel downloads from Contacts, Leads, or Accounts objects. Flag unusual query patterns (SELECT * queries) and Export calls from user/service accounts post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Employee Directory Dump and CPNI Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A subset of approximately 85k records originating from an internal employee directory also included job titles' and 'support ticket data, and some CPNI data.' Targeted collection of sensitive internal data not modeled as detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk queries to internal employee directory tables or custom employee records in Salesforce. Flag access to CPNI-tagged fields (support ticket notes, network information) from non-telecom-operations accounts. Monitor for data exports immediately following account compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Trusted SaaS Application Access
suggestion.rationale: Attacker compromised one Entra account but accessed a separate Salesforce instance—a classic trusted-relationship/federation-based lateral movement. Article describes movement from 'employee Entra account' to 'Salesforce instance' without re-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for federation/SSO-based access to Salesforce from newly compromised Entra accounts. Alert when a low-privilege user account suddenly accesses admin-level Salesforce reports or system objects. Track OAuth token refresh patterns for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Data Publication Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the cybercrime group leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' Exfiltration confirmation and threat publication event—required for post-breach threat intelligence correlation and exposure scope assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference breach timeline and stolen data indicators (4.9M email addresses, CPNI, employee directory) against dark web leak site databases and threat feeds. Alert when confirmed Charter data appears on known ShinyHunters leak sites or underground forums selling bulk PII/CPNI.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Summary API Requests Containing Phishing URLs
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names ChatGPT web summaries as a phishing surface. Detection needed for requests to ChatGPT's summarize endpoints carrying phishing indicators (credential-harvest patterns, lookalike domains, typosquatting).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to OpenAI ChatGPT API endpoints with payloads containing known phishing domains, newly registered domains, or URLs with credential-harvesting parameter patterns (password reset redirects, SSO spoofs). Alert on abnormal request frequency or source IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Website Content Optimized for AI Summarization
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPhish vulnerability implies attackers craft web content specifically to exploit ChatGPT parsing behavior, injecting phishing payload into summaries that appear legitimate. Detection for obfuscated/encoded HTML structures that evade traditional phishing filters but mislead AI text extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web pages with encoded scripts, hidden text, or structural obfuscation designed to trigger phishing content extraction in AI summarizers while hiding from static filters. Correlate with responses from summarization services that yield credential-harvesting or brand-impersonation text.

suggestion.title: User Click-Through on URLs from ChatGPT Summaries to Phishing Sites
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPT summaries may legitimize or distribute phishing URLs to end users. Need detection correlating URLs extracted from ChatGPT outputs with subsequent HTTP requests to known or high-risk phishing domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate URLs present in ChatGPT summarization responses with user HTTP requests. Alert on users accessing phishing domains, newly registered lookalike domains, or credential-harvesting sites via URLs originating from ChatGPT summaries within short time windows.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Probing of ChatGPT Summarization Feature
suggestion.rationale: Attackers likely probe ChatGPT's summarization to refine phishing content, test which URL patterns bypass detection when summarized, or enumerate valid targets. Abnormal API request patterns indicate reconnaissance or payload tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or high-frequency requests to ChatGPT summarization endpoints from single IP/user/account with rotating phishing URLs, malformed payloads, or credential-harvesting parameters. Pattern suggests iterative refinement of phishing content.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT/Claude Share Link Phishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake outage notice is rendered through ChatGPT itself' via 'shared chatgpt.com/s/ link' — the core distribution vector. Pipeline missed the primary attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clickthrough events where user arrives at chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai/artifacts/* links originating from Google Ads referrer or suspicious email, especially if landing page renders download prompt or outage message. Monitor for share links that render HTML outside normal chat context.

suggestion.title: Malware Download from Cloaked Impersonation Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims' with 'harmless AR/VR company website' shown to URLScan but malware download to others — requires detection of domain behavior misalignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .exe/.dmg files from openew[.]app or similar domains spoofing AI platform download portals. Cross-reference threat intel feeds for cloaking indicators. Flag user-agent or IP-based content variation from single domain.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VM/Sandbox Detection Commands Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine' — clear post-execution discovery behavior that should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious command execution patterns post-malware install: registry queries for hypervisor/VM artifacts (e.g. HKLM\HARDWARE\ACPI, VirtualBox/VMware driver checks), WMI queries to Win32_ComputerSystemProduct, or commands like 'systeminfo' followed by hypervisor string parsing. High confidence indicator of malware-as-service behavior.

suggestion.title: Fake Outage Social Engineering Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'rendered outage notice' claiming 'website temporarily unavailable' urging download of desktop app — social engineering mechanism requiring behavioral detection on rendered content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when legitimate AI platform domains (chatgpt.com, claude.ai) serve unexpected content types (rendered HTML impersonating outage/status pages) or trigger suspicious desktop application downloads. Flag user workflow anomalies: visiting legitimate service → redirected to download page.

suggestion.title: Claude Artifacts ClickFix Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'attacks abusing Claude Artifacts' to host 'ClickFix-style lures that tricked users into executing malicious commands' — specific secondary vector requiring detection rules for command execution post-artifact interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for command execution immediately following user click-through from claude.ai/artifacts/* links. Flag PowerShell/cmd.exe invocation with suspicious parameters post-artifact visit. Correlate artifact URL in browser history with command execution timeline (within 5min).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-0257 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. This instruction produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-0257 against PAN-OS fleet. Cross-reference with asset inventory and exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances. Flag any unpatched assets; federal due date is 2026-06-01.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment on PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack outcome: 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection'. This attack step warrants detection but generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected VPN sessions on PAN-OS from anomalous IPs or outside maintenance windows. Correlate VPN auth logs with CVE-2026-0257 vulnerability status and authentication event gaps to detect exploitation.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability is 'authentication bypass'. Pipeline should detect exploitation attempts or access patterns consistent with authentication validation being skipped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor admin portal logs for authentication anomalies: successful privilege access without corresponding auth events, access from new/unexpected source IPs, or admin actions during non-maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Phone-Home Detection (17M+ Devices)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 200 coordinated servers controlling 17 million infected devices for DDoS and proxy abuse. Pipeline captured no kill-chain phase or C2 detection pattern despite explicit infrastructure numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass-convergence of outbound connections from multiple internal devices to a small set of external C2 servers. Botnet C2 typically shows high fanout (1000s devices → single server) and regular heartbeat intervals. Correlate DNS queries for proxy infrastructure (150 locations mentioned) against known residential proxy providers.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Traffic Abuse (Asocks Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet operated as proxy service with 7M IPs across 150 locations selling bandwidth ($5–$15/mo). Pipeline missed detection of devices acting as involuntary proxies—'owners did not knowingly participate' per article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect internal devices with anomalously high outbound egress for proxy traffic: sustained bidirectional data transfer to attacker-controlled collection points, geo-hopping between 150+ locations, or concurrent proxy-service client behavior (port monitoring, SOCKS/HTTP listeners on non-standard ports).

suggestion.title: Botnet Infection Persistence via Weak Device Hygiene
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'change default credentials,' 'apply firmware updates,' 'disable remote admin panels' as protective measures—implying infection exploited these exact gaps. Pipeline extracted zero initial-access or persistence detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices with default credentials active, firmware stale (no update in >6 months), or remote-administration services listening (SSH, RDP, Telnet on public IPs). Correlate with known botnet infection signatures or C2 phone-home patterns. High-risk if device belongs to ISP CIDR blocks or residential proxies mentioned in threat intel.

suggestion.title: Asocks Infrastructure Seizure (Hosting Provider Takedown)
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Asocks' as linked service and specifies '200 servers seized from a hosting provider' in Netherlands. Pipeline extracted neither the service name nor hosting-provider infrastructure indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Asocks domain and known C2 server IPs into threat-intelligence feeds. Block outbound traffic to seized infrastructure. Hunt for historical DNS resolutions, SSL certificates, or SSL/TLS sinkhole data for Asocks subdomains or peer infrastructure. Identify internal devices that ever resolved or connected to Asocks IPs.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet Activity Detection (Mass Attack Coordination)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet was used for 'distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Pipeline surfaced zero impact-phase detections despite this being a primary criminal use and observable via traffic anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound flood traffic from internal devices to single or related targets (volumetric DDoS signatures: UDP/SYN flood, HTTP GET floods, DNS amplification). Correlate with known botnet C2 communication preceding attack windows. High-sensitivity for devices in high-risk CIDR ranges or with proxy-service active.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Exploitation via Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'cryptocurrency mining' as one of three primary botnet activities (alongside DDoS and proxying). Pipeline extracted zero resource-hijacking detection despite this being easily detectable via CPU/GPU load spikes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained abnormal CPU/GPU utilization from unknown or suspicious processes, especially correlating with C2 communication or proxy-service activity. Monitor for known cryptominers (monero, ethereum) or obfuscated JavaScript/WebAssembly payloads. Flag if resource contention correlates with botnet command windows.

suggestion.title: Node.js process requiring vm2 module followed by prototype-chain access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")'. Detection of vm2 require() + subsequent __proto__ or prototype-member access in same process would directly identify exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Node.js processes loading vm2 (via child vm2.js process or module import telemetry). Correlate with command-line execution of Buffer.prototype manipulation (Buffer.call, __lookupGetter__) or subsequent unexpected child process spawning. High fidelity if __proto__ string appears in same process context.

suggestion.title: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error surge in Node.js application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error' as exploitation component. Legitimate production code rarely triggers this specific error; spike is anomalous and correlates with vm2 escape attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error frequency per Node.js application. Alert on 5× increase in 10-minute window. Cross-correlate with parent process id; if same Node.js PID spawns child process or file shortly after error spike, escalate to CRITICAL.

suggestion.title: HTTP request containing prototype-pollution payload targeting Buffer prototype
suggestion.rationale: UC_18_2 attempts HTTP detection but searches URL only. Article PoC must traverse network to server; add detection covering JSON/form-encoded body payloads with 'Buffer.call' or '__proto__' chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound web traffic (POST, PUT, PATCH) for prototype-pollution signatures in request body: Buffer.call.call, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, __proto__ as keys or values. Requires WAF with body inspection or proxy with full request logging. Medium confidence (can appear in legitimate code); escalate on source-IP reputation or context (attempted access to /admin, /api/vm).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package detection (≤3.11.3)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states patch applied to nodevm.js line 263 for versions ≤3.11.3; 'Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3) present on host' is a direct asset-exposure hunt from the narrative. Pipeline extracted no version constraints or package indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for vm2 package.json or nodevm.js files in node_modules paths; extract version strings and flag installations ≤3.11.3. Correlate with process execution to identify at-risk Node.js applications.

suggestion.title: Node.js sandbox escape via inter-process shell spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome: 'full RCE' via 'nesting:true without explicit require.' This manifests as Node.js spawning shell interpreters (cmd.exe, bash, sh) with reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd). Article shows concrete hunt: 'Node.js process spawning OS shell with enumeration commands.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when parent_process_name ∈ {node.exe, node} spawns child_process ∈ {cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, zsh} AND command line contains reconnaissance indicators (whoami, id, uname, hostname, /etc/passwd, cat /etc, net user, ipconfig, ifconfig).

suggestion.title: vm2 nodevm.js file modification or execution anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability resides in nodevm.js (line 263, strict equality bypass). Article recommends detection of file events on node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js (creation, modification). Pipeline missed this artifact-specific indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation, modification, or suspicious execution of nodevm.js or related vm2 library files. Flag unexpected process invocations of files matching paths */node_modules/vm2/lib/* or */node_modules/vm2/main.js.

suggestion.title: NodeVM/vm2 module load detection — runtime library initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes NodeVM as the vulnerability surface: 'NodeVM blocks several dangerous Node.js builtins.' No UC hunts for when the vulnerable library itself is imported or instantiated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes that require('vm2') or require('node-vm2') or instantiate NodeVM class. Monitor for node processes loading the vm2 npm package from package.json or via dynamic require().

suggestion.title: Sandboxed code accessing process module — denylist bypass attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the denylist misses process and inspector/promises.' No UC specifically hunts for sandboxed Node.js code attempting to access process module via getBuiltinModule().
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process.getBuiltinModule('module') calls or require('process') within Node.js child processes spawned by NodeVM. May require ETW/syscall-level inspection or JavaScript debugger integration.

suggestion.title: Node.js network connection post-shell spawn — post-exploitation C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes reaching 'host-side execution primitives' but no UC detects post-exploitation communication. After attacker spawns cmd.exe/powershell.exe, they will likely establish C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js spawning shell processes (UC_14_3) with network events from those child processes. Flag when cmd.exe/powershell.exe spawned by node.exe makes outbound network connections to non-RFC1918 addresses or high-risk ports.

suggestion.title: Repeated access denied to blocked builtins — failed sandbox escape detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies NodeVM intended to block module, worker_threads, cluster, vm, repl, inspector. Before successful escape via process/inspector/promises, attacker probes blocked builtins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated Node.js errors or exceptions attempting to require() blocked builtins (module, worker_threads, cluster, vm, repl). Multiple failed attempts in short window indicate reconnaissance/probing.

suggestion.title: File staging from Node.js in temp/user-writable directory — post-exploitation payload prep
suggestion.rationale: After RCE via process module, attacker will write malicious binaries or scripts to disk. Article doesn't describe this phase but is implicit in 'host code execution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes creating executable files (.exe, .ps1, .bat, .sh, .elf) in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, /tmp, /var/tmp directories, especially when paired with subsequent execution of those files.

suggestion.title: vm2 sandbox breakout via Promise species — attack chain detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific exploitation sequence: 'localPromise constructor...missing call to resetPromiseSpecies' enabling species override. Article narrates explicit attack chain (Promise manipulation → arbitrary command execution) but pipeline generates no kill-chain phases. Missing UC correlating the exploitation primitives (Promise.then manipulation) with post-exploitation spawning in same session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate code submission or file drop into vm2 working directory with child_process spawning by node.exe within 60s, with process tree rooted in script-execution (node <file.js> or node -e <code>). Baseline node.js application spawning patterns per environment first to reduce noise.

suggestion.title: JavaScript-hosted Promise constructor override attempt in vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability is in 'localPromise constructor' and the fix requires 'resetPromiseSpecies'. No UC directly detects Promise constructor patching or species assignment in JavaScript context. This is the ROOT CAUSE detection, not post-exploitation aftermath.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt .js file contents (or PowerShell script block logs if Node hosted in PS) for patterns: Promise.prototype[Symbol.species], Promise.constructor manipulation, or Symbol.species assignment within vm2 directories or node execution contexts. Requires file content inspection or script transcription at ingest.

suggestion.title: vm2 package.json replacement or modification post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses vulnerability in vm2 ≤3.11.3 library code itself. No UC detects tampering with or replacement of the vm2 module post-installation, which could indicate supply chain poisoning or local compromise escalation. Article phrase: 'package which can escape from the VM2 sandbox' implies the package is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hash changes or modification timestamps on package.json and .js files within node_modules/vm2/ after initial baseline. Alert on file rewrites or version downgrades to vulnerable range. Pair with npm audit logs if available.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI Promise introspection — sandbox escape pre-condition detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack requires 'async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI'. Pipeline missed detection for JSPI/WebAssembly.promising availability, which is the necessary environment precondition. Phrase: 'on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes loading WebAssembly modules with JSPI-enabled runtime flags or environment variables set. Look for process creation with --experimental-wasm-jspi flag or runtime inspection of Promise.prototype properties indicating sandbox manipulation attempts.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype.finally() species override — vm2 integrity violation
suggestion.rationale: The exploit mechanism is Promise.prototype.finally() species bypass that 'exposes a host-originate[d]' context. Pipeline failed to suggest hunt for Promise constructor tampering or species property access. This is the actual exploit, not post-exploitation shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reflection/introspection of Promise.prototype.finally or Promise[Symbol.species] modification within Node.js process. In Defender, correlate DeviceProcessEvents spawning node with Promise-related heap spray patterns or module loading of compatibility shims.

suggestion.title: Untrusted code execution context with async/await capability — vm2 configuration vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'untrusted code executed with async support'. Pipeline did not detect the precondition: vm2 instantiated with async=true option. Phrase: 'when untrusted code is executed with async support'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Node.js contexts using vm2 library, detect creation of VM instances with asyncRuntime=true or use of async/await patterns within sandboxed scripts. Flag if combined with code patterns attempting Promise manipulation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST to PraisonAI /a2a endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'An unauthenticated network client can send a JSON-…' to trigger exploit. UC_3_2 in article provides full SPL/KQL; pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound POST requests to */a2a* endpoint on listening ports (8000, 80, 443, 8080) from untrusted sources with HTTP 200 response, originating from public IPs targeting Python/uvicorn processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious child process spawned by PraisonAI uvicorn/python A2A server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes eval() tool leading to arbitrary code execution. UC_3_3 in article identifies shell/subprocess spawns from python/uvicorn parent; pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes (sh, bash, curl, wget, nc, powershell, or Python subprocess/os.system calls) spawned from uvicorn/python parents with a2a-server in command line, especially those accessing /etc/passwd or credential paths.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI A2A server started with 0.0.0.0 bind and missing auth_token
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'exposes an A2A server without configuring auth_token' + 'binds the server to 0.0.0.0'. UC_3_4 detects this configuration indicator; pipeline generated no hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for python/uvicorn process execution with a2a-server.py, praisonaiagents, or A2A keywords in command line. Identify instances binding to 0.0.0.0 (--host 0.0.0.0) or failing to include auth_token configuration parameter.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI execute_code subprocess with print.__self__ attribute access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation uses `print.__self__` to retrieve the builtins module. No UC targets attribute access patterns on print objects or __self__ lookups. Phrase: 'print.__self__ to retrieve the real Python builtins module'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes (especially those with 'praisonai' or 'execute_code' in parent process command line) where the child process command line or injected code contains patterns matching attribute access on print objects (e.g., print.__self__, print.__dict__, .__self__) or vars() calls targeting module-like objects. Cross-reference with process lineage to PraisonAI package locations.

suggestion.title: Dynamic __import__ instantiation from vars() in Python subprocess
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack flow: 'extract __import__ via vars() and runtime string construction'. Pipeline shows no UC for this exploitation technique. Phrase: 'from which __import__ can be extracted via vars() and runtime string construction'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python subprocess execution (especially from PraisonAI context) where the executing code contains patterns of builtin module introspection: vars() calls on objects, __dict__ access, or string-based __import__ calls. Look for sequences like 'vars(...)' followed by dictionary/getattr operations or 'getattr(..."__import__")' patterns.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI execute_code sandbox mode misconfiguration or bypass attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'subprocess sandbox mode' as the vulnerable context. Detection should verify PraisonAI is actually running in sandbox mode but still achieving RCE, indicating bypass. Phrase: 'execute_code() in subprocess sandbox mode can be fully bypassed'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PraisonAI process execution with unexpected parent→child process relationships. Specifically: if PraisonAI is configured/observed in 'sandbox' mode (detectable via config files, startup args, or documentation), but spawns unexpected OS shells or system utilities (id, whoami, cat /etc/passwd, env var access), flag as sandbox bypass. Focus on unusual subprocess chains.

suggestion.title: Multiple CVE correlation for PraisonAI version ≤1.6.39
suggestion.rationale: Article lists four related CVEs (CVE-2026-47392, CVE-2026-39888, CVE-2026-34938, CVE-2026-40158) but provides no detail on relationships. Detection should alert on ANY of these to catch variants of sandbox escape. Pipeline does not explain which versions map to which CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on presence of PraisonAI package with any version matching vulnerability range. Given multiple CVE assignments, treat all four as indicators of the same underlying issue class. If package management logs show PraisonAI versions between 1.6.30-1.6.39 or any version with a tag/build containing one of the four CVE IDs, escalate for patching verification.

suggestion.title: Code injection into PraisonAI execute_code via user input or prompt injection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attack requires providing malicious code to execute_code(). Detection should monitor for untrusted input fed to PraisonAI. Phrase: 'execute_code() can be fully bypassed' suggests attacker supplies input (prompt, file, API payload) that reaches the vulnerable function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If PraisonAI is exposed via API, web app, or chat interface: monitor for requests containing suspicious Python code patterns (e.g., __import__, __self__, vars(), getattr, eval, exec, open()) in input fields/payloads. Correlate with subsequent process execution from PraisonAI process tree.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI package installation on internet-facing or high-risk endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention threat actor distribution; exploitation is post-installation. Detection gap: ensuring PraisonAI isn't deployed on public-facing/external servers or dev machines where untrusted user input reaches execute_code(). Phrase: 'v1.6.37, subprocess sandbox mode' indicates installed configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts running vulnerable PraisonAI versions. Cross-reference with network exposure metadata: is this endpoint internet-facing, exposed on a public API, or accessible to untrusted users? Flag any internet-facing deployment as high-risk. Recommend air-gapping PraisonAI or restricting input to trusted sources only.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI package installation or pip import (pre-deployment indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code' module but no UC targets installation events. Detecting `pip install praisonai` or Python import of praisonai modules provides early-warning during installation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process execution of pip.exe/pip3 with 'praisonai' argument, or Python child processes with import statements for praisonai modules (via command-line or script content inspection). Include requirements.txt file references or setup.py with praisonai dependency.

suggestion.title: YAML config file creation or modification for PraisonAI deployment (0.0.0.0 binding)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per the recommended sample YAML' but no UC targets YAML configuration exposure. Defenders should hunt for yaml/yml files created in deployment or home directories with Flask host/port settings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .yaml or .yml files in common deployment paths (/etc, /home, /opt, /tmp) with content containing 'host: 0.0.0.0' or 'port: 8005' or 'praisonai'. Correlate with praisonai process execution.

suggestion.title: Flask authentication module bypass or disabled (source-code / runtime inspection)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication disabled by default' as the root cause. No UC detects disabled authentication. Look for generated api.py files with missing auth decorators, or Flask app initialization without auth middleware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For deployments with source-code access, inspect generated api.py for absence of @app.before_request auth checks or @require_auth decorators. At runtime, inspect Flask environ/app config for SKIP_AUTH=true or empty auth requirements. Correlate with port 8005 listener startup.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44338 / CVE-2026-47393 scanner/probe detection (automated exploitation attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'CVE-Detector scanner' user-agent in UC_5_5 but no dedicated detection. Scanners will probe /chat and /agents endpoints with specific user-agent, parameter payloads, or timing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to /chat or /agents endpoints from external IPs with user-agent patterns matching common CVE scanners (CVE-Detector, Nuclei, custom probers), or requests with LLM-injection payloads (system prompts, escape sequences in JSON bodies). Correlate multiple attempts from same source.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform member role mutation endpoint hit (CVE-2026-47407)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP PATCH/POST/DELETE requests to `/api/v1/workspaces/*/members*` endpoints with 2xx responses. Flag successful member role modifications, especially where requestor gains elevated permissions or modifies another user's role within the same workspace.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI open-registration followed by workspace privilege action (CVE-2026-47407)

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful account registration (POST /api/v1/auth/register 200–299) with subsequent role or member-mutation requests (POST/PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/*/members) in the same source IP within a narrow time window, indicating fresh account immediately leveraged for privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: API endpoint exploitation attempt detection (CVE-2026-47407 T1190 generic)
suggestion.rationale: Article maps to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' but pipeline did not decompose the specific attack surface: the `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}` resource tree with insufficient authorization checks.

suggestion.title: JWT token forgery exploitation — invalid/forged token usage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allowing token forgery for any user' but no detection searches for actual token signing/validation failures or attempts to use tokens signed with hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-me'. This is the core exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for failed JWT validation events, tokens that decrypt with hardcoded secret, or attempts to use admin/elevated-privilege tokens issued from unusual sources. Correlate timestamps of token creation with credential usage patterns.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV and PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET absence from startup config
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'safety check only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev' and 'default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev', meaning absence of these variables is the vulnerable state. Detection should trigger on deployments without explicit secret and environment configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uvicorn/praisonai_platform process launches where neither PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET nor PLATFORM_ENV environment variables are set or passed as command-line arguments. Compare against allowlist of legitimate production deployments.

suggestion.title: Configuration file / secrets file access prior to token abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover or confirm the hardcoded secret value before forging tokens. Article implies 'dev-secret-change-me' is public knowledge, but detection should capture attempts to access config files, environment variables, or source code repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for file access attempts on config directories, .env files, or praisonai_platform source code repositories immediately before suspicious authentication events or token-signed actions from anomalous principals.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: New service token or API key generation by newly-promoted owner
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Any workspace member can promote themselves or others to owner' and owner status grants elevated permissions. No mention of token generation in the article body, but privilege escalation to owner role would naturally enable API token abuse. Represents post-compromise persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful PATCH role-change to owner status, detect API token creation requests (POST /api-tokens or equivalent) from the same source IP/user within 10 minutes. New tokens created immediately after ownership change indicate persistence setup.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Cross-workspace membership queries by newly-promoted owner
suggestion.rationale: Article describes workspace-level privilege escalation but doesn't specify scope limits of owner-level access. Owner status may enable enumeration of other workspaces. Article notes 'Account Discovery: Cloud Account' (T1087.004) as a technique, suggesting account/workspace discovery is in scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30 minutes of a successful PATCH member role-change to owner, detect requests to /workspaces (enumerate all) or /workspaces/{other_workspace_id}/members (access other workspaces). Newly-promoted members immediately enumerating workspace ecosystem suggests privilege escalation into account/data discovery.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Application server role-update audit log inspection gaps
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in role authorization logic ('handler calls MemberService.update_role() which sets the target member's role...without proper authorization checks'). Detection should also cover gaps in audit logging or missing authorization context in application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application/API logs for PATCH /workspaces/*/members/* requests where the HTTP request source user_id differs from the target user_id being promoted (lateral member modification) and authorization context is missing or shows insufficient role. This identifies exploitation in real-time at the application layer.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform CVE-2026-47416: Demotion of existing workspace admins without legitimate owner authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that members can 'promote themselves or others to owner' and implicitly can modify roles. Legitimate owners should never be demoted without explicit actions. Detecting unexpected owner-role removal indicates potential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH /workspaces/*/members/* requests that change a user with owner role to a lower role (member/viewer), especially when no corresponding promotion of an alternate owner occurs. Demotion of legitimate admins coupled with member promotion is a classic privilege-escalation-via-account-manipulation pattern.

suggestion.title: Browser Spawning ScreenConnect Installer Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly chains delivery mechanism to payload: 'fake Adobe Document Cloud pages to deliver ScreenConnect' — implies user clicks link in browser, leading to ScreenConnect execution. Critical execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent-child process tree: browser (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) → ScreenConnect installer or executable (ScreenConnect*.exe, scupdate.exe). Combine with network event from fake Adobe domain immediately prior. High specificity if executable signature matches known ScreenConnect delivery hash.

suggestion.title: Access to Adobe Document Cloud Domain Lookalikes
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'fake Adobe Document Cloud pages' is explicit masquerading attack. Requires detection at network layer. No legitimate user would navigate to adob*.com, adobe-sync*.io, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DNS query and HTTP request to domains containing permutations of {'adobe','document','cloud','sync','drive'} that fail SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks OR resolve to IPs outside known Adobe ASNs (15169, 8075, etc.). Lower false-positive by checking domain registration age (newly registered) and IP geolocation (matches known attacker infrastructure).

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Service Installation Without IT Ticket
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect legitimate use is IT support; malware variant is post-exploitation persistence. Article describes delivery of ScreenConnect as malware payload, implying installation outside legitimate IT operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services registration for ScreenConnect* service creation on workstations. Correlate with absence of matching IT Ticketing System entry or MDM device management approval. Alert on service start outside maintenance windows or from non-IT principals.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Outbound C2 Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is ScreenConnect, which requires C2 callback to attacker infrastructure. Kill-chain phase detection for post-execution command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/443 or 8040 from ScreenConnect.exe process to non-Adobe IPs. Combine with process lineage (browser → installer) and lateral timing (connection within 60s of ScreenConnect process start). Known ScreenConnect C2 sinkhole lists reduce false-positives.

suggestion.title: Executable Download from Fake Adobe Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires file transfer: user clicks fake page → malware binary downloads. Detection at ingress-tool-transfer phase bridges initial access and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: (1) HTTP/HTTPS download from flagged Adobe lookalike domain, (2) file creation in Downloads/Temp/AppData with executable extension or known ScreenConnect installer filename pattern, (3) source/destination matching within 2 seconds. High confidence if file signed by unknown publisher or signature invalid.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Video Player Update Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Use Fake Video Player Updates' as delivery mechanism. This is classic supply-chain/trojanized software attack—should trigger detection on unsigned/unexpected update sources and update binary signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected or unsigned video player update binaries, especially from non-standard sources or with unsigned signatures. Track user downloads and executions of .exe files named with common video player patterns (vlc, media, player, etc.) from untrusted domains or email attachments.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Process and Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware 'Deploy Miner'—cryptomining component. Should detect abnormal CPU utilization, process creation of miners, and outbound connections to mining pools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high sustained CPU usage from unusual parent processes (especially post-update). Flag process creation with strings containing 'xmrig', 'monero', 'stratum' or mining-pool domains. Monitor for persistence of background processes spawned by video player executables.

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'RAT Malware' deployment. Should detect C2 beaconing patterns, reverse shells, and inbound remote access sessions post-update.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections from video player processes to non-standard ports or IP ranges. Flag reverse-shell indicators (common RAT signatures like cmd.exe spawned from network process). Alert on RDP/SSH login attempts immediately following fake update installation.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Fake Update Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware typically requires persistence mechanism. Should detect scheduled task creation, registry run keys, or startup folder modifications post-update execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scheduled tasks created shortly after video player update execution. Monitor for new run-keys under HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run or startup folder modifications with suspicious names. Look for parent process = video player executable.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Executable Launch from Temp/Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates are typically delivered as unsigned executables to user-writable directories. Should detect execution of unsigned binaries matching common update patterns.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Hidden Malware Payload Drop
suggestion.rationale: Fake updates often drop secondary payloads or obfuscate malware. Article does not specify delivery method details, suggesting possible in-memory injection or multi-stage delivery.

Flag plist entries calling unsigned binaries, scripts, or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate timeline with social-engineering artifact delivery.
