suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS POST requests from .NET processes to non-whitelisted domains, especially with payload patterns matching credential formats (base64 encoding, URL-encoded field names like 'password' or 'credential'). Correlate with NuGet package install timestamps within 15 minutes.

suggestion.title: Persistence via NuGet Package Initialization or MSBuild Target Hooks
suggestion.rationale: High-severity financial malware typically establishes persistence. Supply-chain compromises often use MSBuild .targets files or NuGet Package.OnLoad scripts for auto-execution on each build cycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .props or .targets files within project directories post-package install. Alert on NuGet.config changes adding unauthorized package sources or credentials. Monitor for NuGet package initialization hooks or custom MSBuild tasks executing from untrusted package folders.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via HTTPS/TLS Pinning Bypass or Certificate Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans and credential-stealing malware commonly bypass certificate validation to intercept encrypted credential channels. Malicious SDK likely disables or circumvents standard TLS verification to exfiltrate banking session data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET processes for registry modifications to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP or WinHTTP certificate validation settings. Flag if System.Net.ServicePointManager.ServerCertificateValidationCallback is set to accept all certificates within .NET application context originating from NuGet packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet/npm Package Installation with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states packages steal banking credentials. Pipeline produced no detection for package dependency resolution triggering credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet.exe or npm install processes spawning child processes with capability to enumerate credential stores (lsass.exe, ntlm auth, aws credentials). Flag installations of newly-registered packages with similar names to popular libraries (typosquatting) or unexpected privilege elevation during package restore. Correlate with API calls to credential managers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Install Script Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Banking credentials theft implies post-installation scripts or compiled payloads executing credential harvesting. Article mentions both NuGet and npm, both supporting pre/post-install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or cmd.exe invocation from package installation directories (.nuget, node_modules) with credential-reading arguments (Get-Credential, reading %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, parsing .aws/credentials, querying SecretStore). Look for child process spawns from dotnet.exe or node.exe in Package Manager contexts.

suggestion.title: Cloud Secret Manager Enumeration from Package Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'target cloud secrets'—attacker enumerates and exfiltrates cloud credentials (AWS, Azure, GCP). Pipeline missed this secondary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on environment variable reads from package install subprocesses (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, GCP_PROJECT_ID). Monitor for API calls to cloud secret managers (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager) from unexpected caller identity or process. Detect reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure/credentials during package restoration.

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band Data Exfiltration via Package Telemetry Channel
suggestion.rationale: Stolen banking and cloud credentials must be exfiltrated. Article does not detail C2, suggesting use of legitimate package manager or telemetry channels as covert exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS from NuGet or npm package restoration processes to non-standard domains (not api.nuget.org, registry.npmjs.org). Detect DNS queries for infrastructure associated with malicious package authors. Correlate timing of package installation with unusual HTTPS exfil volume or data size.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Detection: NuGet/npm Packages Impersonating Legitimate Libraries
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks commonly use package names similar to legitimate dependencies. Pipeline missed IOC extraction for malicious package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed NuGet and npm packages against allow-list of legitimate upstream libraries. Flag packages with similarity metrics (Levenshtein distance) to known libs or any package authored by newly-created accounts with metadata anomalies (no README, minimal version history, suspiciously high download count spike).

suggestion.title: Persistence via Compromised Package Auto-Update Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Sicoob malware stealing banking credentials suggests need for sustained access. NuGet and npm auto-update features create persistence vector not mentioned by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet.Config or package.json modifications adding untrusted package sources or disabling signature verification. Detect scheduler tasks or startup scripts set to auto-update or restore packages. Alert on repeated installations of known-malicious package versions even after manual cleanup attempts.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Phishing / Initial Access Campaign (Ukraine)
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Targets Ukraine with AI-Powered Cyberattacks' but no article content was parsed to detail initial access vector. Standard practice: assume phishing/watering hole given Russia-linked APT targeting sovereign nation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email campaigns with Ukrainian government or critical infrastructure recipients, sender domains spoofing legitimate government/energy agencies, or attachment types associated with initial dropper payloads (Office macros, RAR archives containing executables).

suggestion.title: AI-Powered Reconnaissance / Living-off-the-Land Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks' — suggests novel tooling or execution patterns. Pipeline should flag this as a marker for anomalous discovery or command execution, not just generic TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual combinations of discovery commands (whoami, net group, systeminfo) executed in short bursts or with atypical parent processes. Flag if discovery activity precedes C2 beaconing without human-like delay patterns (suggests automated/AI agent).

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Exfiltration Channel (Ukraine Critical Infra)
suggestion.rationale: APT targeting Ukraine implies collection of strategic interest (energy, comms, defense ministries). No exfiltration indicators parsed from article. Generic UC for data staging and transfer over C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers to non-Ukrainian IP ranges, high-volume DNS queries to newly registered domains (potential C2 rotation), and file compression/archive creation followed by network exfiltration within the same session.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Creation with Encryption Payload
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'ransomware uses SYSTEM scheduled task to encrypt'—T1053.005 is the direct attack vector. Pipeline ignored entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor schtasks.exe or TaskScheduler API calls creating tasks with /tr parameters pointing to suspicious executables. Alert on SYSTEM-context task creation by non-admin processes. Baseline admin-approved tasks and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM Context
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'elevated privileges' and 'SYSTEM scheduled task'—requires privilege escalation or token manipulation. Pipeline missed T1548 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-SYSTEM processes requesting SYSTEM-level token access or impersonation followed immediately by task creation. Flag UAC bypass attempts or direct SYSTEM token acquisition patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'encrypt local drives'—mass file encryption is T1486 impact. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections despite clear ransomware behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, high-volume file overwrites by SYSTEM-context processes. Alert on rewriting across multiple directories, unusual file extensions, or encryption-signature byte patterns. Correlate timing with scheduled task execution.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Abuse via Command-Line Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title references task creation mechanism—need detection for obfuscated /tr payloads or script-based execution. T1053.005 parameter abuse patterns undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on schtasks.exe with /tr containing: PowerShell, cmd.exe, script interpreters, encoded arguments, or indirect execution (rundll32, regsvcs). Flag parent processes that should not create tasks.

suggestion.title: LLM Service API Calls from Suspicious Source IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'Leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini' to execute attacks; pipeline missed detection for unauthorized or out-of-policy API calls to LLM endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls to OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Google (Gemini) endpoints from non-approved source IPs, especially from hosts flagged as malicious or from tor/VPN infrastructure. Correlate with credential spray or malware deployment.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload with LLM Generation Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes using ChatGPT/Gemini to 'Fuel Cyberattacks'; attackers are likely generating attack code or phishing content via LLM. Pipeline missed detection for code samples containing LLM-style phrasing, incomplete variable naming, or generic placeholder comments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell/Bash scripts or batch files executed from temporary directories with high entropy or LLM-characteristic patterns (verbose comments, generic variable names like 'var1', 'temp_data', repetitive control flow). Cross-correlate with recent ChatGPT API calls from the same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Linguistic Markers of LLM Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies GREYVIBE uses LLMs to 'Fuel Cyberattacks'; phishing is a common attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection for emails with LLM-generated content (excessive politeness, phrase repetition, generic salutations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with statistical NLP markers of LLM generation (e.g., high trigram entropy, unusual word-frequency patterns, over-formal tone in known informal sender contexts). Spike detection on emails mentioning urgency + account verification + link clicks.

suggestion.title: Compromised ChatGPT/Gemini Account Enrollment and Usage
suggestion.rationale: For GREYVIBE to 'leverage' ChatGPT and Google Gemini, they must have valid accounts or API keys; article provides no details on acquisition method, but pipeline missed detection for stolen-credential abuse against LLM services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI and Google Cloud audit logs for sign-in anomalies: geographic impossibilities, impossible travel, credential reuse, bulk API calls, or unusual prompt patterns (e.g., malware generation requests). Flag accounts with high token consumption in short time windows.

suggestion.title: Ingestion of LLM-Generated Attack Artifacts into Repository or CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: If GREYVIBE uses LLMs to generate malware or attack tools, the downstream use case involves git commits or artifact uploads. Pipeline missed detection for commits/uploads correlated with LLM API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git commits or artifact uploads (docker images, packages) with file timestamps or content signatures matching recent LLM API usage windows from anomalous IPs. Flag repositories with sudden appearance of high-complexity code in non-developer commits.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion: Public npm Package Installed Over Internal Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'leverage[d] 33 malicious npm packages' via 'dependency confusion campaign' — attackers register public packages matching internal package names, executing arbitrary code when build systems resolve public over private.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / package-lock.json resolution for version mismatches or unexpected registry sources (npmjs.org instead of internal registry). Alert if internal package name resolves to public registry version with timestamp mismatch vs. lockfile.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'profile developer environments' and 'collect reconnaissance data' — npm preinstall/postinstall scripts execute with access to developer environment variables (NODE_PATH, CI, git tokens, secrets).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by npm (node, sh, powershell) that enumerate environment (env, set, Get-ChildItem Env:) followed by outbound HTTP/DNS to non-package-registry domains. Baseline npm scripts and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Profiling attack requires data exfiltration; article implies C2 or data collection infrastructure. npm install with untrusted packages will reach external IPs not associated with CDN/jsdelivr/npmjs infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of npm dependency resolution network destinations. Alert on npm or node process connecting to IPs outside whitelist (npmjs.org, cdn.npmjs.com, registry.npmjs.org, github.com, etc.) during install phases.

suggestion.title: npm Package Requesting Unusual Build/Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'tradecraft'; profiling campaigns often bundle reconnaissance tools (curl, wget, lsof, netstat) or invoke system calls to gather host inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child process spawns from npm install for discovery commands (uname, whoami, systeminfo, Get-WmiObject, lspci, docker ps, kubectl get). Correlate with package reputation and recent first-seen timestamps.

suggestion.title: Package Update Anomaly: Sudden Version Bump or Patch Timestamp Misalignment
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion relies on version precedence; attackers publish higher version numbers (e.g., 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 on public npmjs, shadowing internal 1.x).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package.json resolved versions against npm registry release dates and author commit history. Alert on version jumps with mismatched author, zero git history, or publish timestamp within hours of resolution.

suggestion.title: npm Module Initialization Collecting System Inventory Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments' — entry point is npm module load (index.js, require() in postinstall hook).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hook npm require() via instrumentation or package-scanning tools to detect suspicious API calls: fs.readdirSync() on /proc, registry reads, AWS credential file access, git config read, docker socket access during initial module load.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Authentication Bypass' and 'Under Active Exploitation'—pipeline generated zero use cases despite clear exploitation threat. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect /sslvpn/portal endpoints for HTTP 401 errors followed by 200 OK on same session within 5 seconds, failed auth followed by successful session without re-entry, or requests from source IPs with no prior auth history establishing immediate VPN sessions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-0257 is named in title as 'under active exploitation' but pipeline failed to extract it as IOC or create CVE-specific detection. Organizations need signature-based blocking for active campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to PAN-OS GlobalProtect endpoints containing patterns indicative of CVE-2026-0257 exploitation (malformed SAML assertions, oversized auth parameters, specific User-Agent patterns). Correlate against affected PAN-OS version inventory.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GlobalProtect Session Characteristics Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Auth-bypass vulnerability allows unauthorized access; article implies active exploitation but pipeline provided no detection for resultant session anomalies (impossible travel, privilege escalation, lateral movement setup).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GlobalProtect sessions with impossible-travel indicators, logins from IPs with zero prior history, or sessions that bypass normal MFA workflows. Flag accounts accessing resources inconsistent with their normal baseline within 60 seconds of session establishment.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from GlobalProtect Foothold
suggestion.rationale: Successful auth-bypass provides gateway access; no use case detected for internal reconnaissance or lateral movement that would follow compromise via GlobalProtect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious GlobalProtect session establishment with internal network scans, port enumeration, or service discovery from that session's assigned internal IP within 5-60 minutes. Alert on internal-facing RDP/SMB/SSH attempts from newly-established GlobalProtect sessions.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated GlobalProtect Portal Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Auth-bypass vulnerability likely allows device enrollment without proper credential validation. Title emphasizes 'authentication bypass' but pipeline provided no detection for enrollment precursor vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect device registration/enrollment API endpoints for requests lacking valid authentication tokens, pre-shared key validation, or certificate pinning checks. Alert on enrollment success with spoofed hostnames or unregistered device types.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Bulk Code/Repository Export via Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Attackers Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling to Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets'—this is the headline attack vector. Pipeline missed basic detection for abnormal git clone/pull/export, npm/pip bulk downloads, or archive creation targeting source repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal volume or velocity of source code access/export via git, GitHub CLI, npm, pip, or IDE tooling. Flag bulk tar/zip operations on source directories followed by exfil-sized network transfers to non-whitelisted endpoints. Establish baseline for per-user/per-host dev activity and alert on >3σ deviations.

suggestion.title: Discovery and Exfiltration of Credential Files via Developer Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Secrets' exfiltration. Pipeline failed to identify detection for .env, .aws/credentials, .git/config, API token files being read, copied, or exfiltrated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to secret management files (.env, .aws/credentials, .ssh/config, .git/config, .kube/config). Alert on these files being cat'd, printed to logs, piped to exfil channels, or accessed outside CI/CD runner context. Flag environment variable exfiltration in process command lines or network payloads.

suggestion.title: Trusted Developer Tool Process Executing Suspicious Network I/O
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: legitimate tools being weaponized. Pipeline should detect when npm, git, pip, curl, wget, or IDE processes make outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure or unexpected cloud storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate network destinations for developer tooling (package registries, GitHub, AWS endpoints). Alert when npm, git, python, curl, or similar tools initiate connections to IPs/domains outside whitelist, especially to unresolved IP space, free-tier cloud infrastructure, or known C2/exfil platforms.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names CVE-2026-39987 as the exploit vector for initial access. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial-access detections despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Marimo application endpoints with payloads or parameters matching CVE-2026-39987 exploitation signatures. Flag suspicious method combinations, input encoding anomalies, or known PoC patterns targeting Marimo RCE vectors.

suggestion.title: Python Process Spawning with Embedded Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates post-exploitation phase, which necessarily involves command execution on the compromised host. No execution-phase detections generated despite 'post-exploitation' being central to the attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe or python3 child processes spawned from web-facing services or unusual parents, especially with command-line arguments containing eval(), exec(), subprocess, or __import__. Correlate spawning time with known Marimo exploitation window.

suggestion.title: LLM API Calls and Agent Library Initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—this is the novel attack vector and sole justification for 'critical' severity rating. Pipeline failed to generate detections for LLM library instantiation, API calls, or agent orchestration logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for import statements or process execution involving LLM frameworks (langchain, llamaindex, autogen) in Python processes post-RCE. Flag outbound HTTPS to known LLM provider domains (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, claude.ai) with Bearer-token or sk-* patterns in request headers or process environment.

suggestion.title: High-Frequency System Enumeration via Scripted Commands
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase inherently includes discovery and lateral-movement reconnaissance, but pipeline generated zero discovery-phase use cases. LLM agents would generate rapid-fire enumeration commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batches of system-enumeration commands (whoami, net user, quser, systeminfo, wmic logicaldisk) issued within seconds from a single Python process or dynamically-spawned shell. LLM-generated commands show syntactic variance and unusual parameter ordering vs. interactive typing.

suggestion.title: LLM Credential Leakage via Process Memory or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: LLM agents require API credentials (keys, tokens) to function. Post-exploitation agents would cache or exfiltrate these, but pipeline surfaced no credential-access or exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LLM API key patterns (sk-*, Bearer tokens with 40+ hex chars) appearing in process command lines, environment variables, temporary files, or outbound HTTP/S traffic. Flag processes making simultaneous connections to Marimo endpoints and LLM provider endpoints.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing (Vishing) Attack Targeting Remote Employee Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes: 'they breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' No detection use case for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Azure AD account sign-ins from anomalous geography within 1–4 hours of employee vishing complaints. Alert on credential resets, MFA enrollment changes, or conditional access policy modifications by newly-compromised identity. Correlate call logs (if available) to sign-in timeline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Azure AD Identity to SaaS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' No detection covering abuse of legitimate identity during SaaS lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Salesforce access patterns per Azure AD user. Alert on: data export/query operations by non-admin identities, bulk API reads (>10k records per query), historical data retrieval by Entra service accounts, access to customer tables outside role scope. Correlate with Entra sign-in anomalies.

suggestion.title: Mass Data Exfiltration Pattern – Telecom Customer Records
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exfiltration of '42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, phone types, plan information, support ticket data, and some CPNI data.' No collection/exfiltration detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single-session Salesforce bulk queries or report exports returning >100k customer records. Flag API token abuse for historical data dumps, unusual report scheduling, or export to non-sanctioned cloud storage. Correlate with Entra compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: CPNI and Regulated Telecom Data Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'some CPNI data' was stolen and mentions 'customer proprietary network information (CPNI) data.' Telecom-specific classified data should trigger heightened detection for access by compromised identities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Tag CPNI-classified fields (phone numbers, plan details, network configuration) in Salesforce. Alert on access by non-approved roles, service accounts, or identities showing compromise signals. Require approval for bulk CPNI export.

suggestion.title: Known Threat Actor Leak Site Publication – Dark Web Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the cybercrime group leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' No detection use case for monitoring ShinyHunters leak infrastructure or known threat actor publication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate dark web monitoring feeds and ShinyHunters indicators of compromise. Alert on: appearance of Charter customer records on known ShinyHunters leak site, file signature/hash matches to exfiltrated dataset, email/phone patterns matching publicly-confirmed breach data.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Summarization API Abuse for Phishing Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states ChatGPT web summaries are weaponized as phishing surface—detection must cover ChatGPT API summarization calls with phishing-indicative URLs: newly registered domains, credential-harvesting keywords in target page text, suspicious TLDs, URL shorteners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ChatGPT API summarization requests with target URLs exhibiting phishing markers (newborn domains, privacy-protected WHOIS, bulk registrations, typosquatting patterns, credential-form landing pages). Correlate downstream user clicks originating from ChatGPT results that route to phishing or credential-theft infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redirect Chains Originating from ChatGPT Output
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPhish leverages ChatGPT output as trusted phishing vector; redirects from ChatGPT summaries to credential-harvesting or malware infrastructure are a signature attack pattern requiring detection at proxy/network layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multi-hop redirect chains (3+ hops) originating from openai.com/api.openai.com summarization responses that terminate at newly-registered or known-phishing infrastructure. Flag landing pages requesting credentials, MFA tokens, or executing unsigned scripts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Page Injection Targeting ChatGPT Indexing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers craft pages with embedded phishing URLs specifically designed to be summarized by ChatGPT, exploiting the service as a content-distribution proxy. Detection requires identifying hosting infrastructure hosting phishing markers correlated with summarization API access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newborn domains hosting pages with phishing hallmarks (HTML form fields requesting credentials, POST endpoints exfiltrating data, obfuscated JavaScript) that appear in ChatGPT summarization API logs. Correlate domain registration timing, WHOIS privacy flags, and SSL certificate issuance with API call timestamps.

suggestion.title: Anomalous ChatGPT API Call Patterns Suggesting Phishing Campaign Automation
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale ChatGPhish campaigns would exhibit distinctive API usage: high-volume summarization requests, rapid URL iteration, geographic or temporal clustering. This differentiates from legitimate summarization workloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline ChatGPT API summarization frequency and URL entropy per user/API key. Alert on deviation: sudden 10x+ volume spikes, summarization requests with >90th-percentile URL diversity (indicative of broad phishing URL testing), requests from geographies associated with phishing infrastructure, or API keys associated with bulk-account registrations.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from ChatGPT-Delivered Phishing Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPhish terminates in credential theft; detection must cover phishing landing-page infrastructure and data exfiltration tied to summarization vectors, identifying successful compromise post-click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify credential-harvesting landing pages (POST forms requesting username/password/MFA, SSO-redirect interception) hosted on ephemeral infrastructure (newborn domains, bulletproof hosters, hijacked CDN endpoints) that correlate temporally and referentially with ChatGPT summarization requests. Detect subsequent authentication abuse or data exfiltration using compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: Malicious Google Ads Pointing to AI Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page.' This is the initial access vector via ad networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor click logs and web proxies for traffic from known malicious Google Ads to legitimate AI platform sharing URLs (chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts). Detect ad campaign IDs or landing pages with high subsequent malware download rates.

suggestion.title: Fake Outage Notices on AI Platform Share Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'rendered through ChatGPT itself' with HTML stating 'Download our desktop app to continue.' Attackers abuse AI rendering to host social engineering content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT/Claude share pages containing outage-related language ('temporarily unavailable', 'high traffic', 'download desktop app'). Alert on share pages with atypical redirect or download buttons. Monitor for suspicious HTML/CSS in rendered artifacts.

suggestion.title: Malware Downloads from OpenAI-Impersonating Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' hosting Windows and macOS malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads from domains similar to openai.com/chatgpt.com but with typosquatting patterns (openew, openai-download, etc.). Flag executables downloaded from non-official OpenAI/Anthropic infrastructure with ChatGPT/Claude branding.

suggestion.title: Cloaking Detection: Different Content Served to Security Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains returning different content based on User-Agent, IP geolocation, or referrer. Alert on domains that serve benign content to scanners (URLScan, VirusTotal) but malware/lures to end-user IPs. Monitor for CloudFlare/CDN abuse patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware VM/Sandbox Detection Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article notes downloaded malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious WMI queries (Win32_ComputerSystem, Hyper-V checks), registry queries to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services (vmmouse, vboxguest), or artifact checks (.vdi, .vmdk files). Alert on process execution chains starting from downloaded ChatGPT/desktop apps.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Claude Artifacts for ClickFix-Style Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Push Security also observed attacks abusing Claude Artifacts, Anthropic's feature for sharing rendered applications and content, to host ClickFix-style lures that tricked users into executing malicious commands.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Claude Artifacts/ChatGPT shares containing bash/PowerShell command snippets with copy-to-clipboard functionality. Alert on artifact links followed by unexpected process execution (curl, wget, powershell, cmd). Monitor for common ClickFix patterns ('sudo', 'chmod +x', 'curl | bash').

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to bypass security restrictions.' Exploitation attempts must be detectable on PAN-OS appliances via authentication logs, login failures preceding success, or request patterns matching known exploitation methods for CVE-2026-0257.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for authentication bypass patterns in PAN-OS authentication logs: failed login attempts followed by successful session establishment without valid credentials, or authentication log entries that deviate from normal authentication flow patterns known to indicate CVE-2026-0257 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection After Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as the attack outcome. After successful auth bypass, VPN session establishment must be monitored. Detection should focus on VPN sessions sourced from unusual geographies, IPs, or timing patterns inconsistent with legitimate access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN session initiation from IP addresses or user accounts that show no prior authentication history, especially during off-hours or from geographies misaligned with organizational footprint. Correlate with auth bypass indicators in PAN-OS logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Patch Status Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' CISA KEV federal due date is 2026-06-01, making this urgent. Pipeline must generate asset inventory detection for exposed PAN-OS instances and their patch versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all PAN-OS instances, flag any not patched to versions known to remediate CVE-2026-0257 (specific versions not provided in article but vendor will release advisory). Prioritize internet-facing management interfaces via passive DNS/passive HTTPS logs.

suggestion.title: Exposed PAN-OS Management Interface Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerability as in a 'public-facing application' and T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) applies. PAN-OS management console exposure is the attack surface; detection should flag management ports (443, 10443) responding from public networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PAN-OS management interface exposure via certificate fingerprinting (PAN-OS uses specific TLS signatures) or banner grabbing on typical management ports. Correlate with successful login events to detect if exposure was exploited.

suggestion.title: Device Compromise via Default Credentials Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states mitigation: 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong,' implying this was the infection vector. 'Owners of the devices...did not knowingly participate,' confirming botnet exploited credential weaknesses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed authentication attempts using common default credentials (admin/password, root/admin, etc.) against networked devices. Flag successful logins with default credentials from unusual geographies or rapid service enrollment post-infection.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '200 servers used to host the infrastructure' that 'controlled computers, tablets, and smartphones.' Detection of synchronized outbound C2 traffic from 17M devices is critical impact metric.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect coordinated outbound connections from enterprise/residential IPs to known botnet C2 IP ranges or domains. Alert on patterns of rapid connection handoff across geographies consistent with proxy service operation (150 locations mentioned).

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet used 'for distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Detecting botnet-coordinated traffic surges is primary impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on simultaneous traffic spike pattern from multiple IP addresses targeting the same destination. Monitor for characteristic DDoS amplification signatures or SYN flood patterns originating from botnet-associated CIDR ranges.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Abuse Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names Asocks service offering '7 million IP addresses, 150 locations, 100,000 clients' for proxying. Botnet abuse of this service requires detecting abnormal proxy traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid IP rotation from single source endpoints (multiple countries per session), unusual geographic mismatches between device location and proxy exit IP, or traffic routing through known compromised proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'cryptocurrency mining' as explicit botnet use case. Detecting mining processes and resource exhaustion is key impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known crypto miners (xmrig, monero-cli variants) or unknown processes consuming sustained 60%+ CPU with outbound connections to mining pool infrastructure. Flag memory-intensive processes spawned from unusual parents.

suggestion.title: Firmware Vulnerability Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'the latest firmware update has been applied' as primary mitigation, indicating devices were compromised through unpatched firmware vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate devices running outdated firmware versions post-disclosure. Monitor for HTTP/S requests to known firmware exploit kits or payloads matching signatures for CVEs affecting routers and IoT devices (D-Link, TP-Link, etc.).

suggestion.title: vm2 Sandbox-Escape PoC Strings in HTTP Request/WAF Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents exploit indicators: 'By combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__`, `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupSetter__`, and Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error...' These string signatures appear in attacker-supplied payloads and are high-fidelity indicators of exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing vm2 exploit strings (__lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, Buffer.call.call, mainModule.require, constructor.constructor). These indicate known-PoC exploitation payloads. High specificity with low FP rate when tuned away from dev endpoints.

suggestion.title: Node.exe → Shell Process Spawning (Post-Exploitation Behavior)
suggestion.rationale: Article states sandbox escape 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code.' Process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash.exe) from Node parent is definitive post-exploitation signal — legitimate Node apps rarely spawn shells unprompted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.exe spawning shell interpreters without legitimate application context. Baseline: such process trees are rare in normal operation and indicate code execution via sandbox escape. Correlate with vm2 module references in parent cmdline if available.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 Package Inventory (Versions ≤3.11.3)
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-47131 affects vm2 versions through 3.11.3. Article implies unpatched versions represent active exposure. Asset inventory hunt identifies vulnerable hosts before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory for vm2 package matching version pattern ≤3.11.3 (0.x, 1.x, 2.x, 3.0–3.11.3). Cross-reference CVE-2026-47131 vulnerability DB. Prioritize exposed/internet-facing nodes and instances with network listening ports.

suggestion.title: vm2 Module Import + Untrusted Code Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates vm2 API usage: 'const vm = new VM(); vm.run(attacker_payload)'. Detection on suspicious vm2 instantiation in Node command-line or source code (especially with dynamically-sourced payloads) indicates setup for sandbox-escape exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node processes with vm2 imports (require('vm2'), new VM()) paired with external payload sources (user uploads, API parameters, file reads). Legitimate vm2 users exist, but the payload *source* (untrusted input vs. hardcoded) determines risk. Requires code-level inspection or dynamic instrumentation.

suggestion.title: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error + Constructor Chain Access (Code Analysis)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically leverages Node.js 'ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error' to obtain 'the host's TypeError constructor.' This is an unusual error-construction exploit. Scripts or logs showing constructor.constructor, __proto__, or Error chaining indicate sandbox-escape attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script payloads or error logs containing constructor.constructor access chains, __proto__ manipulation, or repeated ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE patterns (artificially triggered as part of exploit). This requires code inspection or error-log deep-dive; not network-observable without payload capture.

suggestion.title: IoA: Node.js child_process spawn with shell from vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'nesting: true without explicit require still allows full RCE'. Attacker leverages vm2 sandbox escape to execute shell commands. Article code samples show child_process.execSync being called post-exploitation. Current hunts miss the *module-level* code execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Node.js processes that load vm2 module (via require/import tracking) followed by spawn/exec system calls to cmd.exe, bash, or sh. Correlate stack traces or module-load telemetry showing child_process invocation originating from vm2 context. High-confidence signal if preceded by file write to node_modules/vm2/.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion: CVE-2023-37903 patch bypass detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'patch bypass'. The core vulnerability is bypassing the CVE-2023-37903 fix via strict-equality check (options.require === false). T1562 (Impair Defenses) not mapped. Article states: 'The stric... check... is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vm2 source-code files (nodevm.js) being read immediately after patch deployment or version update. Detect processes loading old vm2 versions after package-lock.json update. Flag code patterns attempting to instantiate VM with explicit omission of require property (regex: /new VM\({[^}]*nesting\s*:\s*true(?![^}]*require)/ or similar to detect the vulnerable config.

suggestion.title: Package vulnerability exposure: vm2 <=3.11.3 across application fleet
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable version range (implied <=3.11.3). Current UC_20_3 hunts file presence but lacks version extraction and comparative asset analysis. No correlation with actual application code using vm2 with dangerous config.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json and package-lock.json files for vm2 entries. Extract version constraints and flag: (1) pinned to <=3.11.3, (2) unpinned/wildcard (implicit vulnerability window), (3) version mismatch between package.json and lock file. Correlate with Node.js processes from same application directory spawning shells. High-confidence asset if npm audit or dependency scanner confirms vm2 vulnerability.

suggestion.title: IoA: Nesting option enabled without explicit require constraint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability defined by configuration pattern: 'nesting: true + require undefined'. Article: 'When require is not specified, options.require is undefined, not false.' No hunt specifically detects this insecure configuration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt application source code (.js files) for vm2 instantiation patterns. Detect: new VM({nesting: true}) or new VM({nesting: true, ...}) where the 'require' property is NOT explicitly set to false or undefined. Pattern: /new\s+VM\s*\({[^}]*nesting\s*:\s*true/ without corresponding require constraint in same object literal. Combine with dependency check: is vm2 <=3.11.3 in package.json?

suggestion.title: Exploitation fingerprint: require() bypass via undefined vs false equality
suggestion.rationale: Core technical vulnerability: strict equality check fails when option omitted. Article: 'The check uses strict equality (options.require === false)... When require is not specified, options.require is undefined, not false.' This specific bypass pattern should be detectable in code or runtime state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command-line or script content attempting vm2 instantiation with explicit instrumentation to trigger the bypass (omitting require while setting nesting: true). Look for attacker tooling or PoC code containing: regex patterns that verify strict equality behavior or patterns testing undefined !== false. Behavioral signal: Node.js process with command-line arguments referencing vm2 config options without require safeguard.

suggestion.title: vm2 module file modification or downgrade post-installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'write code which can escape'—attackers may modify installed vm2 files or downgrade from patched to vulnerable version after initial deployment. Article states vulnerability affects versions '≤3.11.3' implying patch exists. Detection gap: file modification to vm2/lib or package.json downgrades not covered by UC_21_1-3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write operations to established vm2 package paths (node_modules/vm2/lib/*.js) or modification of vm2 package.json to downgrade version. Cross-reference timestamps with previous legitimate npm install to identify post-installation tampering.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype manipulation and Symbol.species access in Node.js process
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability mechanism: 'missing call to `resetPromiseSpecies` to ensure that `this` has no special species'—runtime manipulation of Promise.prototype or Symbol.species constructor is the exploitation trigger itself, distinct from static PoC code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe processes where stack traces contain Promise.then() manipulation inside vm2.VM context, or instances where Symbol.for('Symbol.species') is accessed followed by immediate child_process module require. Behavioral indicator: vm2.VM instantiation immediately followed by Promise constructor access.

suggestion.title: Process object access attempt and sandbox boundary violation from vm2 context
suggestion.rationale: Article technical description emphasizes sandbox escaping to 'execute arbitrary commands on the host system'—successful escape grants access to process object from isolated context. This is distinct from UC_21_2 (detecting spawning) and represents the escape moment itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to access forbidden process APIs from vm2 sandboxed context: process.exit(), process.cwd(), process.env, or child_process module access from node.exe with preceding vm2.VM context. Look for permission-denied exceptions that suddenly resolve to successful execution (indicating successful escape).

suggestion.title: Vm2 Promise.prototype.finally() tampering or species override
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'JSPI-backed Promise `.finally()` species bypass' and 'bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening.' Detection should look for code modifying Promise.prototype or prototype pollution in vm2 context, if JavaScript execution logs are available.
log_sources: custom app logs with JS execution traces
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Promise.prototype.finally manipulation, prototype chain walks accessing host constructors, or Object.defineProperty calls targeting Promise in Node.js context running vm2. Correlate with vm2 module usage.

suggestion.title: Vm2 instantiation with WebAssembly.promising or JSPI-backed async enabled
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability requires 'runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI (WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending).' Detection should identify vm2 configurations that enable the risky JSPI surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js process creation with flags enabling WebAssembly JSPI (--experimental-wasm-eh, --experimental-wasm-jspi, or similar), or vm2 instantiation code using sandbox config with jspi: true or async handlers that enable JSPI.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation shell spawning shortly after vm2 vulnerable-code execution
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attack succeeds by exploiting vm2 to break sandbox. Detection should correlate rapid succession of vm2 activity + shell spawn to filter legitimate use cases. UC_19_2 is too noisy without this temporal constraint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js spawning shell within 5 seconds of vm2 module load or vm2 script execution start. Requires process lifecycle correlation; filter out cases where Node.js is a known app framework (webpack, build tools, monitoring agents).

suggestion.title: Untrusted code vector into vm2 sandbox (file write + node execution)
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires 'untrusted code' to be executed in vm2. Article mentions 'User Execution: Malicious File' (T1204.002). Detection should look for file write to a controlled location followed by Node.js loading that file, especially if from browser cache, temp dirs, or user-writable locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to browser cache, temp directories, or user-writable paths followed by Node.js process reading/executing code from that location within 10 seconds. Flag suspicious parent processes (browsers, email clients, cloud sync).

suggestion.title: Vm2 sandbox breakout validation: Host global access from sandboxed context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes escape that exposes 'host-originate' resources to sandboxed code. If Node.js debugger logs or process memory inspection is available, detect code accessing the host's global scope, process module, or filesystem APIs from within a vm2 context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sandboxed vm2 code accessing 'process', 'require', 'global', 'Buffer', or filesystem APIs that should be unavailable. Requires code-level instrumentation or debugger integration.

suggestion.title: [LLM] PraisonAI A2A endpoint accessed without authentication headers (auth bypass exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exposes an A2A server without configuring `auth_token`'. Existing UCs detect the POST but not the failed auth scenario. Should trigger when /a2a endpoint is reached by unauthenticated clients (missing auth headers or failed Bearer token validation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP 200/403 responses to /a2a endpoints where Authorization header is absent, invalid, or empty. Correlate with JSON-RPC POST method requests. Client should be external/untrusted.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Python eval() execution with network-originated expressions in uvicorn/A2A process
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'implements Python `eval(expression)`' as the exploitation mechanism. Child process detections (UC_7_3) only catch post-eval shells, not the eval() invocation itself. Should detect eval() bytecode compilation or inspect process memory/file descriptors for stdin piping from network sockets.
log_sources: Defender DeviceProcessEvents with command-line argument inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for python processes with stdin redirected from network sockets (FD 0 open to 0.0.0.0 listeners), or parent process file descriptors showing open connections coinciding with child process spawning. Correlate timing of network POST to /a2a with subprocess creation.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Suspicious tool registration or plugin loading in PraisonAI A2A server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'registers a `calculate(expression)` tool implemented with Python `eval(expression)`'. No detection covers tool registration/plugin loading. Should detect dynamic tool loading, function registration, or decorator invocations that wire dangerous implementations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PraisonAI A2A server log output or Python debug logging for tool registration events, particularly where tool callables reference eval, exec, __import__, compile, or subprocess. Look for @tool decorators or tool.register() calls with dangerous function references.

suggestion.title: [LLM] JSON-RPC method invocation with code-injection-like expression payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on JSON-RPC POST sending malicious `calculate(expression)` payloads to trigger eval(). Existing UC_7_2 detects the POST but not payload signature. Should match JSON-RPC requests where method is 'calculate' or similar and params contain shell metacharacters, Python keywords (import, exec, __), or file paths.
log_sources: HTTP request body inspection (proxy, WAF, SIEM)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST bodies to /a2a endpoint for JSON-RPC 2.0 structure with method field matching known PraisonAI tools and params containing suspicious payloads: shell operators (|;><), Python keywords (__import__, exec, compile), or file-system paths (/etc/passwd, ~/.ssh).

suggestion.title: [LLM] Rapid sequential tool invocations from single JSON-RPC session (exploration/reconnaissance after RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack reaching 'real LLM-driven eval() tool execution'. After initial RCE, attacker typically escalates by invoking multiple tools (reading files, checking privileges, network connectivity). Should detect multiple distinct tool method calls from same source IP in short time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate JSON-RPC POST requests to /a2a endpoint by source IP. Flag when single source invokes 3+ distinct tool methods (e.g., 'calculate', 'execute_command', 'read_file') within 60 seconds, especially if tool methods are not typical for legitimate use patterns.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PraisonAI library installation (≤1.6.39) via asset inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability in 'v1.6.37, subprocess sandbox mode' and marks ≤1.6.39 as vulnerable range. Pipeline output published zero IOCs despite this foundational detection being prerequisite to all downstream hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search software inventory for praisonaiagents or praisonai package with version ≤1.6.39. Flag internet-facing or dev-tier hosts. Correlate with Python 3.x subprocess spawning within 48h as indicator of active use.

suggestion.title: Direct sandbox-escape signature: print.__self__ + builtins dict access
suggestion.rationale: Article documents core attack step: 'print.__self__ to retrieve the real Python builtins module, from which __import__ can be extracted via vars()'. Pipeline's UC_8_6 is incomplete; Defender KQL lacks regex to match whitespace obfuscation (print . __self__ with spaces).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python process command-lines or injected code containing print.__self__, __self__.vars, or regex-obfuscated byte variants. Flag correlation to parent mentioning praisonai, execute_code, or python_tools.py. Medium confidence fallback: any subprocess spawning bash/cmd/zsh as child of Python3.x with credential-read command.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI payload: runtime string construction to build __import__ calls
suggestion.rationale: Article describes explicit attack mechanism: 'runtime string construction' to dynamically build import statements and extract __import__. Standard code-execution detection misses this pattern if focused only on exec()/eval() keywords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python subprocess where parent cmdline contains dynamic string-building patterns: '__' in quotes adjacent to 'import', backtick-quote escaping, chr() byte construction, or hex/octal Unicode sequences. Pair with immediate child-process spawn (shell, curl, wget) to confirm impact.

suggestion.title: Credential exfiltration: shell spawned from PraisonAI context with env-read commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names impact: 'cat /etc/passwd', 'cat /etc/shadow', 'printenv', 'AWS_SECRET', 'OPENAI_API_KEY', '/proc/self/environ'. These credential-read patterns should be primary hunt trigger, not secondary behavioral indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell spawns (bash/zsh/sh/cmd/pwsh) with parent=Python/Python3.x and command containing: 'cat /etc/passwd', '/etc/shadow', 'printenv', 'env |', '/proc/self/environ', 'grep -i secret', 'grep -i api', or '/run/secrets'. Escalate to HIGH if parent ancestry includes 'praisonai' or 'execute_code'.

suggestion.title: Multi-CVE correlation: simultaneous detection of PraisonAI family CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists four CVEs (CVE-2026-47392, -39888, -34938, -40158) without relationship explanation. Pipeline should flag two-or-more of these CVEs detected on same asset as high-confidence breach signal, warranting immediate code-audit and supply-chain review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Where two or more PraisonAI CVEs surface on same host within same scan window or asset state, escalate to critical and trigger immediate response. Implies either persistent exploitation attempt or vulnerable library integrated into critical application.

suggestion.title: LLM agent framework input-to-execution flow: untrusted data to code execution
suggestion.rationale: PraisonAI's vulnerability stems from accepting external code input for execution. Organizations using this framework should hunt: external network source → local API endpoint → Python execute_code(). This indicates missing input sanitization in wrapper application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from non-whitelisted external IP → local service port → subprocess spawning Python → shell execution. Most useful in dev/test environments where untrusted code submission is expected; HIGH confidence in production without code-review gates.

suggestion.title: Failed workspace member authorization attempts across multiple workspaces
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes that `require_workspace_member(workspace_id)` is the access control gate. Attacker will likely probe workspaces they are not members of (generating 403 Forbidden responses) before finding misconfigurations. No detection exists for this reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for users generating 403 Forbidden responses to /api/v1/workspaces/{id} endpoints across 5+ distinct workspace IDs within 5 minutes. This indicates workspace enumeration or probing for IDOR misconfigurations. Baseline should exclude workspace admins with legitimate multi-workspace access.

suggestion.title: Cross-workspace resource access for user not in workspace member list
suggestion.rationale: Article describes nested resource lookup that bypasses workspace isolation. Core IDOR is: user accesses /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_B}/agents/{agent_id} without being a member of workspace_B. Detection must correlate workspace membership against accessed workspace IDs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each HTTP request to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/*, join against workspace membership records. Alert if user has successful response (200-299) but is not in that workspace's member list. Requires identity integration with web logs.

suggestion.title: Rapid mutations of multiple user roles within single workspace
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes privilege escalation via member-role manipulation. Legitimate role changes are infrequent; attacker escalating permissions will target multiple user accounts quickly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for users making 4+ successful role/permission changes to distinct user accounts via PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/members/* within 10 minutes. Correlate with whether the modifying user is a workspace owner or should have member-management permissions.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of workspace IDs via sequential/pattern-based requests
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify how attacker discovers target workspace IDs. If workspaces use sequential/guessable identifiers, attacker will enumerate them. Standard nested-resource detection (UC_6_3) alone does not catch workspace ID enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to /api/v1/workspaces/* generating 200 or 403 responses where the workspace_id parameters appear sequential, UUID-like with low entropy prefixes, or follow a guessable pattern. Alert if single user or IP probes 20+ workspace IDs in 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Successful data access to resource IDs not created by or assigned to accessing user
suggestion.rationale: After bypassing IDOR, attacker reads agent/issue/project details belonging to other workspace members. Detection requires baseline of 'normal' resource IDs each user should access (created_by, assigned_to, etc.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline each user's typical resource-access patterns (agents, issues they created or are assigned to). Alert when user successfully GETs resource details for agents/issues with creator/assignee not matching the user and not in user's workspace. Requires application-layer audit logging.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery Attempts via Known Secret
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JWT signing key defaults to hardcoded "dev-secret-change-me", allowing token forgery for any user'. Direct detection of attacker creating valid JWTs with the known secret should be pursued via application logs showing cryptographic library calls or token validation failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JWT token claims that mismatch the issuing service, or for rapid-succession token generation/validation cycles from external sources. Flag tokens signed with 'dev-secret-change-me' if cryptographic logs are available.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV=dev Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'A safety check exists but only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != "dev"; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is "dev"'. Configuration audit should detect deployments where PLATFORM_ENV is explicitly set to 'dev' or entirely unset in production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for praisonai_platform processes with PLATFORM_ENV unset or set to 'dev' in production namespaces/accounts. Flag as misconfiguration allowing default hardcoded secret.

suggestion.title: Cross-Workspace User Impersonation via Token Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token forgery 'for any user'. Detect cases where a single API token/source claims multiple conflicting user identities across workspace boundaries, or where token claims diverge from IAM mappings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API requests from same source IP/API client claiming different user_id claims across multiple workspace endpoints. Anomalous if user identities are not typically shared cross-workspace.

suggestion.title: Workspace member role enumeration before escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can promote 'themselves or others to owner'—attackers first need to discover valid user_ids and current role structure. Detect GET requests to /workspaces/{id}/members or /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} from authenticated sessions immediately before PATCH attempts to the same endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GET requests to membership endpoints (200 responses) followed within 5 minutes by PATCH requests from the same src/user. High volume of GETs before any PATCH suggests reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Failed role escalation attempts (403/401 on PATCH)
suggestion.rationale: If the application includes any validation, attackers may trigger 403/401 before finding a working endpoint or user_id combination. Detect repeated failed PATCH attempts to /members/{user_id} with 403/401 status from the same src.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ≥3 PATCH requests to /workspaces/*/members/* with status 401 or 403 from the same src/user within 10 minutes, followed by a 200/204—indicates role-change probing.

suggestion.title: Newly-elevated workspace owner making API calls to previously-inaccessible endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1213, T1530—post-escalation data access. Correlate a successful role-change PATCH (UC_4_2) with subsequent API calls to admin-only or elevated-privilege endpoints the requester did not previously access (e.g., /workspaces/{id}/settings, /workspaces/{id}/audit_logs, /workspaces/{id}/members with write methods).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track successful PATCH to /members/{user_id} with role→owner. Then validate whether that user_id made requests to elevated endpoints in the 15 minutes post-change. Use baseline API call profiles per user to flag anomalous resource access.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via newly-promoted owner account (cross-workspace abuse)
suggestion.rationale: Once escalated to owner in one workspace, attacker may use that access token/session to target other workspaces. Detect when a user who recently gained owner role in workspace A immediately accesses or modifies workspace B.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authenticated API calls from a user within 30 minutes of a role-change PATCH if the user is accessing a workspace_id different from the one where the escalation occurred.

suggestion.title: Workspace ownership change cascade (bulk re-role after escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: attacker escalates self to owner, then demotes legitimate owners and promotes accomplices. Detect when a newly-escalated owner immediately issues multiple PATCH requests changing other users' roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate a PATCH that grants owner role to user A with subsequent PATCHes from user A to /members/{other_user_id} within 15 minutes. Aggregate by workspace to detect bulk ownership consolidation.

suggestion.title: Session/auth token anomalies post-escalation (if SaaS provides session logs)
suggestion.rationale: Some platforms log token generation or session elevation. Article vulnerability allows privilege escalation without logout/re-auth. Detect elevated-permission API tokens issued to a user without corresponding auth/login events immediately prior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If auth logs exist, flag API tokens or sessions with elevated scope (owner-level) that were NOT generated by an explicit re-authentication event (login, MFA challenge, token refresh with privilege escalation). Indicates in-band privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Disable or Bypass Pre-Commit Security Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'forces the research right there while it's in front of you' via custom pre-commit hooks. Detection should monitor for developers circumventing these controls ('git commit --no-verify', environment variable overrides, hook removal) which would indicate an attempt to skip mandatory security scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for --no-verify flags in git commits, deletion of .git/hooks files, or environment variable overrides (GIT_HOOKS_SKIP, etc.) that would bypass pre-commit security scanning. Correlate with code commits that introduce known vulnerable patterns.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Spearphishing Link Click from Suspicious Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'LinkedIn social engineering' as attack vector; no detection for malicious links from fabricated/compromised LinkedIn profiles leading to download pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users clicking LinkedIn message links pointing to attacker-controlled domains. Correlate newly created/compromised LinkedIn profiles with bulk user connections and suspicious URL click patterns. Monitor for URL shorteners or redirect chains from LinkedIn to non-LinkedIn domains hosting file downloads.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Binary Execution from Downloads Folder
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom macOS malware deployment' without specifying execution detection; user downloads payload via LinkedIn and executes it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned binaries or scripts from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or email attachments. Prioritize parent processes like Finder, bash, or zsh spawning processes with non-standard code signatures or no signature verification.

suggestion.title: macOS LaunchAgent Persistence Registration
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware typically establishes persistence via launchd agents or launch daemons; article implies long-term compromise but no persistence detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons for .plist files containing suspicious executable paths. Correlate with process creation of launchd spawning previously-unknown binaries or shell scripts.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployed malware but provides no C2 IOCs; behavioral detection of malware reaching out to attacker infrastructure is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from user-writable directories making repeated outbound HTTPS connections to low-reputation domains or IPs on non-standard ports. Correlate with timing patterns suggesting heartbeat or tasking behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Shell Command Injection via AppleScript
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware frequently abuses osascript and shell interpreters for command execution; article mentions custom malware but execution mechanism was not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag osascript or shell (bash/zsh) execution with base64-encoded commands, inline script payloads, or suspicious function calls. Parent process should be unusual (not Terminal, IDE, or admin tools).

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Remote Access Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly cites 'VS Code Tunnels' as expanded arsenal. This is T1219 (remote-access software) abuse for unauthorized persistence. Pipeline generated zero detections for tunnel creation or anomalous code process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code.exe or CodeServer launching with --tunnel or tunnel-related CLI arguments, or unexpected tunnel.exe variants. Monitor for tunnel listener sockets on non-developer machines. Correlate with lateral-movement timeframes or off-hours process spawns.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Proxy Listener Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'HTTPSpy' as deployed tool. This is an HTTPS/HTTP proxy for traffic interception and credential harvesting (T1557, T1040). No detection rule for proxy bind operations or HTTPSpy process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPSpy binary creation/execution by hash or name; monitor for netstat/netsh rules creating local proxy listeners on ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443. Flag processes modifying WinINet proxy settings or installing root certificates in SYSTEM certificate store.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Backdoor Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'HelloDoor' as component of Kimsuky toolkit. Name pattern suggests backdoor; no detection rules generated for this implant's startup mechanisms, process spawning, or persistence indicators (T1547, T1574).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HelloDoor binary execution and registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU RunOnce, Run, or Services keys. Flag anomalous scheduled tasks, startup folder additions, or WMI event subscriptions created shortly after HelloDoor spawn. Baseline legitimate Hello* processes first.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Multi-Tool Deployment Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes orchestrated deployment of three distinct tools. Pipeline produced zero kill-chain reconstruction despite clear progression: initial access → tool deployment (execution) → persistence setup → C2 activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent-child process chains: suspicious interpreters (powershell, cmd, cscript) spawning legitimate tools (code.exe, svchost) with non-standard arguments. Alert on rapid sequential spawning of multiple tools within 5 minutes. Establish baselines for legitimate tool deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Traffic Exfiltration via HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: HTTPSpy as proxy explicitly handles data interception and exfiltration. Article positions it as C2 infrastructure component. No detection for HTTPS traffic anomalies, unusual port usage, or certificate pinning bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTPS egress per user/workstation. Alert on: high-volume HTTPS to rare destinations, HTTPS to non-standard ports (8443, 8880, 9443), missing SNI headers, self-signed certificates, or TLS version downgrades. Correlate with HTTPSpy process uptime.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Reconnaissance Post-Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Expanded toolkit implies reconnaissance phases. Title does not detail discovery activities, but APT toolkits always include initial enumeration (T1082, T1087). Pipeline's empty kill chain fails to surface this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-compromise discovery: whoami, net user, systeminfo, tasklist, ipconfig spawned shortly after tool deployment. Alert on LDAP queries targeting user/computer objects, registry enumeration of network adapters or installed software, or file-system enumeration of sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation Mimic Legitimate Library
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package impersonates 'Sicoob SDK'—the delivery mechanism is a trojanized package designed to fool developers. 'Malicious NuGet Package as Sicoob SDK' establishes initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect nuget.exe or dotnet.exe installing packages with names typosquatting legitimate libraries (e.g., 'Sicoob.SDK', 'sicoob-sdk' vs legitimate), from newly-registered NuGet feeds, or with mismatched publisher metadata. Correlate with developer machines or build infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from .NET Process Post-Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the package 'exfiltrates banking passwords'. Detection must capture credential access and exfil from processes executing NuGet-loaded assemblies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned from .NET runtime (dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe child processes) that enumerate credentials (LSASS access, browser store queries, Windows Credential Manager), then immediately open TCP/443 connections to non-whitelisted domains within 30s window.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Anomalous .NET Assembly in Package Cache
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized NuGet packages contain malicious .dll files. Detect when package installation downloads result in unsigned, recently-modified, or hash-mismatched assemblies vs. official vendor repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor %USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages and %ProgramData%\NuGet\Cache for .dll files with missing or invalid digital signatures, creation timestamps post-installation, or hashes not in NuGet.org official manifest. Correlate with process execution from same directory.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning or Code Execution from NuGet Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: The malicious assembly must execute to steal credentials. Detect when NuGet-cached assemblies directly spawn processes, load modules, or invoke unmanaged code (T1559 alternatives, P/Invoke).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when child processes are spawned from dotnet.exe with parent in .nuget\packages path, or when processes in that path load native .dll files (kernel32.dll, advapi32.dll calls for credential/registry access). Monitor for CLR profiler hooks or reflection-based code generation.

suggestion.title: Registry or File Modification by Package-Loaded Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages often establish persistence or disable security controls. Detect registry/file writes from NuGet-spawned processes to sensitive hives (HKLM\SYSTEM, HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HKLM or HKCU registry writes to Run, RunOnce, Startup, or security-related keys (Windows Defender, UAC bypass) from processes spawned by dotnet.exe. Track file system writes to system directories (System32, Program Files).

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band HTTP Exfiltration with Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies banking passwords are exfiltrated—network telemetry should show credential-sized data (typically <10KB per request) sent to attacker C2 infrastructure with POST/PUT methods characteristic of stealer beacons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) POST/PUT requests from dotnet.exe child processes or processes in NuGet cache to non-whitelisted, newly-registered, or geographically-anomalous domains. Alert on payloads containing URL-encoded strings matching credential patterns or encryption headers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet/npm Package Installation with Unexpected Child Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'malicious Sicoob NuGet steals banking credentials' — package installation is the initial compromise vector; malicious code executes post-install
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet.exe or npm installation processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or NET-based utilities within 5s of install completion. Baseline legitimate post-install tasks; alert on deviations accessing credential stores or system binaries.
