suggestion.title: LLM-Assisted Credential Harvesting Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase typically escalates to credential access. LLM agents can autonomously query directory services, dump memory, or generate social-engineering payloads. Pipeline did not surface credential-access detection for this attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LDAP/Active Directory queries or WMI calls spawned by LLM agent processes immediately post-exploitation. Flag attempts to acquire SeDebugPrivilege or TokenPrivileges from inference engine contexts. Monitor for unusual file reads from credential stores (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SECURITY, .ssh directories, /etc/shadow) by LLM-related processes.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via LLM Model Inference APIs
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation objective includes data collection and exfiltration. LLM agents can covertly exfiltrate sensitive data by embedding it in prompts or model request bodies as encoded payloads. Pipeline generated zero collection or exfiltration detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large or structured-data-containing prompts to LLM APIs with preceding file-read or database-query events (config files, credential stores, databases). Detect encoding/obfuscation in API request bodies (Base64 padding, nested JSON escaping, hex encoding). Alert on model API calls with embedded SQL queries, JSON objects, or CSV patterns within prompt fields, especially post-discovery phase.

suggestion.title: Marimo Service Runtime Behavior Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Successful CVE exploitation of Marimo would spawn unusual child processes, load untrusted libraries, or exhibit unexpected file I/O. Pipeline did not extract baseline Marimo behavior or post-exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish and alert on deviations from baseline Marimo process behavior: unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, Python with arguments), DLL injection attempts, or image loads from non-standard paths. Monitor Marimo's working directory for suspicious file writes to system directories. Track unusual network connections initiated by Marimo service account.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Voice Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' through 'a voice phishing (vishing) attack.' This is the initial access vector enabling all downstream activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag employee Entra accounts with failed MFA attempts or atypical logins (geography, device, time) preceding successful authentication. Alert on accounts with sudden API activity spikes or administrative actions within 24 hours of vishing indicators (internal call logs, user reports of voice calls).

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Customer Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'stole 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance' including 'customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, plan information, support ticket data.' Large-scale record extraction is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk exports (CSV, report generation, API calls returning >5k records per transaction). Monitor for queries accessing PII fields (email, phone, address) from newly-active or out-of-hours accounts. Flag accounts with no historical Salesforce access suddenly exporting customer data.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity to SaaS Lateral Movement Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: single compromised Entra account provided full access to Salesforce customer database. Detect when cloud identity compromise immediately enables sensitive SaaS data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra compromise indicators (failed MFA, impossible travel, anomalous locations) with immediate Salesforce login from same account. Flag API enumeration patterns (describe org, query limits, permission checks) in Salesforce post-Entra breach. Monitor for accounts accessing data repositories they have no business justification to access.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor IOC Enrichment: ShinyHunters Infrastructure Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ShinyHunters extortion gang' and states they 'leaked the documents...on their dark web leak site.' Pipeline must identify actor and track infrastructure across incidents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain and monitor known/suspected ShinyHunters leak site domains and Tor infrastructure. Alert on corporate outbound connections to Tor exit nodes or known ShinyHunters C2 ranges. Monitor darkweb feeds and threat actor forums for posts mentioning company name, employee names, or Salesforce data dumps.

suggestion.title: Telecom Regulatory Data (CPNI) Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: Charter is telecom provider; mentions 'some CPNI data' potentially exfiltrated. CPNI (Customer Proprietary Network Information) is FCC-regulated. Alert on bulk access to CPNI-marked records from anomalous accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk access to records tagged or labeled as CPNI. Monitor for exports of customer support tickets containing service plan details, call history references, or billing info from accounts without CPNI access history. Alert on Salesforce API queries using CPNI-specific fields with result sets >1000 records.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Summary URLs in Phishing Email
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'turns ChatGPT Web Summaries into a phishing surface' — implies threat actors embed malicious/social-engineering payloads in ChatGPT share URLs to bypass email gateway filtering. Zero UCs generated to detect this attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails from external senders containing ChatGPT conversation/share URLs (patterns: chat.openai.com/share/*, api.openai.com/conversations/*). Correlate with credential-entry events on attacker-controlled domains within 10 minutes of click.

suggestion.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Exploitation via Web Request Injection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name 'ChatGPhish' and mechanism 'web summaries' indicates attacker-supplied content is rendered/summarized by ChatGPT. No technical execution pattern (payload structure, endpoint, request morphology) extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to openai.com with suspicious parameter injection (HTML/JS/URL encoding in 'text', 'url', 'summary' parameters). Flag responses containing phishing domains, shortened URLs, or credential-harvest forms in summaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via ChatGPT Summary Payload
suggestion.rationale: Phishing surface implies credential harvesting. Article provides no IOCs (domains, attacker URLs) or payload examples. Need behavioral detection of the post-click attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email click on ChatGPT URL + credential entry on non-OpenAI domain within 5 minutes + logon failure or impossible-travel event on target account within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Malicious ChatGPT Installer Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware 'disguised as the ChatGPT desktop application' with Windows and macOS variants hosted at openew[.]app. No detection UC for masqueraded application delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads with filenames matching ChatGPT installers (e.g., ChatGPT-installer.exe, chatgpt-*.dmg) from domains not in OpenAI's infrastructure. Cross-reference against known legitimate OpenAI download CDNs. Monitor for process execution from %TEMP% or %DOWNLOADS% paths launching with names like 'ChatGPT' or 'OpenAI'.

suggestion.title: Network Callback to Malware Delivery Domain (openew[.]app)
suggestion.rationale: Article names openew[.]app as the impersonated 'OpenAI's desktop application download portal.' No IOC extraction or network detection UC despite this being the primary delivery point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries resolving to openew[.]app or network connections to IP(s) resolving from that domain. Flag any HTTP/HTTPS requests to openew[.] with paths matching software download patterns (/download, /install, etc.). Correlate with user-agent strings claiming ChatGPT or OpenAI.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Share Link Abuse for Phishing/Malware Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'attackers created a custom HTML page using ChatGPT's rendering capabilities and published it through a shared chatgpt.com/s/ link.' This abuse of AI platform legitimacy is a key attack vector not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT share link clicks (chatgpt.com/s/*) in user browsing, especially those rendered immediately before malware downloads. Flag links that render HTML/CSS with outage messaging or download prompts. Correlate with subsequent connections to non-OpenAI domains (openew[.], etc.) within 5 minutes of share link access.

suggestion.title: VM Detection Reconnaissance in Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Defense evasion technique not reflected in any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent processes (fake ChatGPT installer, downloaded .exe/.dmg) spawning child processes executing VM-detection commands: wmic os get virtualizationvendoridentity, systeminfo | findstr VMware, kstat -m vmxnet, hypercall patterns, Hyper-V registry checks (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Hyper-V). Combine with sandbox evasion signatures (exit on VM detection).

suggestion.title: Cloaking-Based Malware Delivery Site (User-Agent Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes site 'uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims... URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' HTTP-level evasion bypassing scanners not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to openew[.] where response content differs drastically based on User-Agent or IP reputation. Flag requests from non-security-platform IPs returning executable files while scanner/sandbox User-Agents receive benign HTML. Monitor for HTTP 302/301 redirects from openew[.] to legitimate AR/VR domains (cloaking fallback).

suggestion.title: Google Ads Redirection to Malicious AI Platform Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The "LLMShare" campaign... uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page.' Ad-based initial access vector with no detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ads.google.com/aclk or Google ad redirect clicks resolve to chatgpt.com/s/* links that subsequently redirect or render download prompts. Correlate ad-click user-agents and referrers. Flag unusual ad campaigns (typosquatting: ChatGPT, ChatGpT, ChatGpt, etc.) that resolve to share links instead of official OpenAI properties.

suggestion.title: Unpatched PAN-OS Systems Vulnerable to CVE-2026-0257
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal remediation by 2026-06-01 and explicitly states 'CISA KEV... only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' The asset-exposure template is referenced but no use case was instantiated to detect vulnerable systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for PAN-OS systems running versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-0257. Cross-reference against patch compliance baseline. Alert on systems lacking patches as of the federal due date 2026-06-01.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Session Establishment from Unknown Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability effect as 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection'—the direct post-exploitation action should be detectable through access logs and session anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN authentication success logs for sessions originating from IP addresses not in the baseline endpoint registry. Alert on VPN access from geographically anomalous locations or IPs with no prior authentication history in the organization.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Exploitation Pattern Against PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass security restrictions'—exploitation attempts should produce anomalous authentication patterns (rapid failed attempts, unusual sequences, protocol irregularities) distinct from normal login failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication sequences inconsistent with normal user behavior: rapid-fire failed attempts from a single IP, authentication success immediately following multiple failures, or authentication attempts from IPs never observed authenticating before.

suggestion.title: Default Credential Compromise on Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong' as remediation, confirming default credentials as the primary infection vector for 17M devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication using known default credentials (admin/admin, root/root, 192.168.1.1 logins, etc.) across routers, IoT, or network appliances. Baseline failed attempts and flag sudden success clusters. Correlate successful weak-credential logins with subsequent proxy-pattern outbound connections within hours.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing from Residential/Mobile IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 17M 'computers, tablets, and smartphones' controlled by C2 infrastructure—implying regular callback communications. Pipeline missed detection for infected-device command-and-control patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify periodic outbound connections from residential/mobile IP ranges to known C2 hosting providers (especially Netherlands infrastructure). Flag consistent beacon intervals, encrypted payloads to unusual destinations, and peer-to-peer command patterns. Correlate with known botnet families' heartbeat signatures.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Residential Proxy Service Activity
suggestion.rationale: Asocks advertises 'residential and mobile proxies'—the botnet's operational purpose. Pipeline should have generated detection for proxy-protocol abuse from consumer devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for proxy-protocol signatures (CONNECT tunnels, SOCKS handshakes, HTTP CONNECT) originating from residential/mobile devices to attacker-controlled destinations. Baseline typical proxy usage and alert on high-volume forwarded traffic, geographically dispersed destination patterns, or proxy service advertisements from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Boot-Time Persistence and Firmware Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining 17M infections across device reboots requires OS or firmware persistence. Article notes 'latest firmware update' as protective measure, implying firmware-level compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Registry Run/RunOnce/RunServices keys and Task Scheduler for suspicious auto-start entries on devices with proxy-traffic profiles. Detect unexpected firmware version changes, rollbacks, or unsigned firmware. Correlate boot-time hooks with known botnet persistence signatures (e.g., DLL hijacking, driver loading from suspicious paths).

suggestion.title: Network Device Scanning and Credential Stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Reaching 17M devices requires exploitation of vulnerable network hardware. Article implies large-scale scanning to identify targets with default credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning activity (port sweeps, repeated SSH/telnet/HTTP login attempts) originating from ASN/ISP ranges associated with botnet distribution. Flag sequential login attempts using known-default credential pairs. Correlate scanning sources with devices later observed exhibiting proxy behavior.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connection Surge to Proxy Service Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: 17M devices simultaneously providing proxy services implies coordinated connection establishment to C2 or proxy aggregation points. Article notes 200 servers seized for control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline and alert on sudden spikes in outbound connections to Netherlands-hosted infrastructure (seized provider IPs). Look for connection pools opening from a single device (proxy aggregation), or synchronized connection timing across device cohorts. Flag SSL/TLS traffic to infrastructure without matching certificate authority in trust store.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mass Snyk CLI Remediation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Snyk's new Remediation Agent is available to run locally...to remediate issues en masse.' and describes automated fix loops. Pipeline should detect anomalous remediation velocity, failed upgrade cascades, or tool invocation patterns inconsistent with normal developer behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, sequential snyk-cli invocations with fix/upgrade flags targeting multiple packages within short time windows (e.g., >20 upgrades/min), failed exit codes suggesting remediation rollbacks, or CLI execution from non-developer accounts or production-bound CI contexts.

suggestion.title: Compromised Dependency Upgrade via AI Remediation Logic
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights gap: 'AI models can see what's wrong, but they don't know...whether the package being upgraded to is still maintained.' and 'upgrades that break tests, or PRs that introduce more issues than they solve.' Pipeline should flag when automated fixes introduce known-compromised, unmaintained, or suspicious package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag dependency upgrade PRs generated by Snyk/CLI that upgrade to recently-published versions, unmaintained packages (no updates >1yr), publishers with low reputation scores, or package versions coinciding with CVE disclosures or typosquatting signatures.

suggestion.title: Snyk API Token Exfiltration or Misuse from Non-Development Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes context injection into LLMs: 'Snyk scans and injects the right context into your LLM' and mentions 'locally hosted models.' Pipeline should monitor token abuse, credential theft, or use in untrusted inference environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Snyk API token usage from unexpected geographic regions, IP ranges outside VPN/office, or from cloud AI inference providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, vLLM endpoints). Flag tokens used in non-development CI/CD runners or production EC2/Lambda contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious __proto__ manipulation in HTTP request (vm2 PoC pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article body and PoC explicitly describe exploitation using 'Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")' and '__lookupSetter__' to break sandbox. Detection rule UC_26_2 captures this in WAF/HTTP logs but pipeline failed to suggest it as a hunt. 'By combining Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__"), Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupSetter__, Buffer, "__proto__"), and Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error, the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests (GET/POST) containing the string patterns __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__, Buffer.call.call, or compileStreaming. These are vm2 sandbox-escape PoC indicators. Correlate against Node.js endpoints that accept user-supplied JavaScript. High FP risk if legitimate vm2 debugging or testing traffic transits the perimeter.

suggestion.title: Node process spawning OS shell after vm2 exploitation chain
suggestion.rationale: Article concludes sandbox escape 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code.' Logical follow-up is child shell spawning. Article phrase: 'the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained, which allows the escape from the sandbox. This allows attackers to run arbitrary code.' Detection rule UC_26_3 implements this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or nodejs spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, or wmic.exe with command line arguments containing child_process, execSync, require(), or mainModule.require. Correlate with parent process command line containing vm2, NodeVM, or new VM( to increase confidence. This represents sandbox-escape-to-execution.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 version inventory (<=3.11.3) across Node.js deployments
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects vm2 all versions up to and including 3.11.3. Asset inventory should detect vulnerable software to prioritize patching. Detection rule UC_26_4 shows the pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Node.js application inventory against CVE-2026-47131 vulnerability database. Flag any system with vm2 package version matching regex ^([0-2]\.|3\.([0-9]|10|11)(\.[0-3])?$) (versions 0.x–3.11.3). Link to software vendor notice that vm2 is no longer maintained; recommend migration to alternatives (isolated-vm, unsafe-vm, worker-threads).

suggestion.title: Node.js process with vm2 configured for nesting without explicit require restriction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the bypass: 'the check uses strict equality (options.require === false), which is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely. When require is not specified, options.require is undefined, not false.' Detection should target the vulnerable configuration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application source code (JavaScript files loaded by Node.js) for vm2 instantiation patterns where nesting:true is set without a paired require:false option. Flag configuration files or code that instantiate NodeVM/VM2 with incomplete sandboxing parameters. Can correlate with loaded npm packages to find applications using vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Host-level file/registry access from Node.js process after vm2 initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the exploit achieves 'full RCE'—successful sandbox escape transitions from sandboxed to host-level access. This represents the privilege escalation and escape event that should be detectable post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes that access host-level resources (C:\Windows, C:\Program Files, /etc, /proc, /var/log) after calling or loading vm2 library. Flag sudden access transitions from application-scoped directories to system directories from a single process context.

suggestion.title: Spawned shell processes with suspicious parent-child relationship patterns from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Sandbox escape followed by enumeration implies abnormal process hierarchy: normal node process → sandboxed code execution → unsandboxed shell spawning. Article keywords 'child_process', 'execSync' establish this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash, or other shell interpreters that in turn execute enumeration or reconnaissance commands (whoami, id, net user, etc.) in rapid succession. Focus on command-line arguments suggesting immediate execution (&&, ;, -c, -Command) rather than interactive shells.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47137 exploitation detection via Node.js runtime exceptions and stack traces
suggestion.rationale: Failed or successful exploitation attempts will generate exceptions, sandbox violations, or context-escape errors visible in Node.js logs before RCE fully occurs. Article describes a specific code path bypass, which may leave detectable traces in error handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js application stderr/stdout and logging for vm2-related errors, context violations, sandbox breach attempts, or exceptions referencing 'nesting', 'require undefined', or 'sandbox escape'. Correlate with processes invoking vm2 library from code paths that don't implement require restrictions.

suggestion.title: vm2 denylist bypass via process module access — JavaScript code pattern detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the denylist misses `process` and `inspector/promises`. Both can be used from sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives.' Direct code detection needed for calls to process.binding(), process.env access, or require('process').getBuiltinModule(). No existing UC captures this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .js or .mjs files created/modified by node processes containing patterns like 'process.binding', 'require("process")', or 'getBuiltinModule'. These indicate attempts to break out of the vm2 sandbox. Correlate file creation time with subsequent shell spawning from the same process.

suggestion.title: Node.js inspector protocol abuse — remote code evaluation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'inspector/promises' as a denylist bypass vector. The inspector module allows remote code evaluation. Detect unusual inspector protocol activation or runtime-eval patterns from unexpected code paths in node processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node processes with inspector module loaded or inspector protocol listening on non-standard ports. Flag unusual --inspect flags or dynamic Runtime.evaluate calls in debugger protocol messages.

suggestion.title: Sandbox escape via NodeVM container privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sandboxed code to bypass the intended builtin restrictions and execute code in the host process'. This is privilege escalation from sandbox → host. Detect any node process spawning privileged operations or writing to system-owned locations post-vm2 context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process creation by node.exe with access tokens differing from parent, or file write attempts to privileged directories (%windir%, %programfiles%, %systemroot%) by processes spawned from node contexts.

suggestion.title: vm2 vulnerable code in dependencies — supply-chain risk inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CVE-2026-47140' affecting vm2 package. Detect projects with vm2 imported in package.json or node_modules that may be exploitable. Complements UC_22_2 (asset-level) with code-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for package.json or package-lock.json files where vm2 is listed as a dependency with version matching vulnerable range (3.9.x - 3.11.3). Flag projects that import vm2 in any JavaScript files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious eval/dynamic code execution within Node.js — potential vm2 payload delivery
suggestion.rationale: The denylist bypass requires executing JavaScript code that calls getBuiltinModule or accesses inspector. Detection should flag eval(), Function(), or dynamic require() patterns in node process arguments or loaded files, especially in CI/CD or app-server contexts where vm2 is often deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe processes with command-line arguments containing eval(), new Function(), or import(dynamic_string) patterns. Correlate with vm2 package presence in %appdata% or project directories.

suggestion.title: VM2 runtime Promise/generator abuse during active execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the exploit as 'localPromise constructor was changed to call this.then(undefined, eater)' with missing 'resetPromiseSpecies' call—the manipulation happens at runtime during sandboxed code execution. UC_25_3 detects PoC in cmdlines (static), but no UC monitors Promise/generator chain manipulation *during* vm2 script execution or detects Symbol.species abuse mid-runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If JavaScript hook instrumentation available in Node runtime: flag Promise.then chains combined with Symbol manipulation or generator abuse within vm2-created contexts. Behavioral pattern: Symbol.species access + Promise constructor chaining + prototype mutation within milliseconds, followed by unexplained process fork.

suggestion.title: Sandbox boundary violation via constructor escape detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes this is a 'sandbox breakout'—crossing the vm2 boundary to reach host context. UC_25_2 detects post-breach child process spawns, but no UC detects the boundary-crossing moment itself: when vm2-sandboxed code first reaches Function constructor or host process object.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe for sudden transition from vm2 module context to unsandboxed context (requires vm2 internal instrumentation or access to process memory inspection). Detect when process object or require() becomes available to previously-sandboxed code execution context.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly module instantiation from Node.js process — JSPI exploit precondition
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit requires 'untrusted code executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI' and 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally()'. No detection validates the JSPI+WebAssembly precondition. WebAssembly.instantiate() or WebAssembly.Memory allocation is the technical trigger; missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js child process for syscalls to dlopen/mmap targeting WASM/JSPI libraries, or inspect Node heap for WebAssembly.Memory objects allocated before shell spawning. Cross-reference with vm2 module usage from parent process.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype.finally() invocation with species bypass indicators
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'bypasses expected Promise-species hardening and exposes host-originate'. Attack requires manipulating Promise constructor or overriding Promise[Symbol.species]. JavaScript-level payload would instantiate custom Promise constructor. No detection attempts to identify this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process loading unsigned JS payload from /tmp or unusual path, followed by require() of vm2 module and eval/Function() constructor invocation. Look for process memory containing 'Promise[Symbol.species]' or custom Promise constructor definitions in loaded modules.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm package containing vm2 sandbox-escape payload
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain likely begins with npm install of trojanized package (vm2-dependent or vm2 itself) containing JSPI+Promise.finally() exploit code. Article describes exploitation of 'untrusted code executed' within vm2—payload must arrive first. No hunt detects suspicious npm install followed by exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install (package-lock.json or yarn.lock modification) of vm2 or vm2-dependent packages with subsequent node process execution outside normal application directory + shell spawning within 48h. Escalate if npm install performed by unprivileged user but shell spawned as privileged.

suggestion.title: vm2 module tampering post-installation — payload injection into node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain persistence: attacker could modify installed vm2 lib/main.js or index.js after initial install. Article does not explicitly describe this, but package post-installation modification is feasible attack vector for this vulnerability class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file write/modify actions to /node_modules/vm2/lib/*.js or /node_modules/vm2/index.js at timestamps >24h after package installation. Correlate with Node process reexecution and child process spawning indicating payload activation.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Node.js sandbox escape — post-exploitation privilege jump
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1068 'Exploitation for Privilege Escalation' and T1611 'Escape to Host' indicate attacker gains elevated access post-sandbox-break. No hunt correlates vm2 vulnerability exploitation with subsequent privilege-escalation attempts (token impersonation, sudo execution, service manipulation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting node.js child shell process, escalate hunt severity if shell runs with higher privilege than parent Node.js process, or if subsequent process tokens/ACLs grant SYSTEM/root access. Correlate with access to sensitive files (/etc/shadow, /root/.ssh, Windows registry).

suggestion.title: Async/await code with suspicious eval or Function constructor in Node.js
suggestion.rationale: JSPI exploit specifically targets async Promise behavior. Article describes 'async support' as requirement. Legitimate Node.js rarely uses eval/Function constructors within async contexts for Promise manipulation. Behavioral signal worth hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search process memory or loaded module source code for patterns: 'async.*Promise', 'eval(', 'Function(', or 'new Proxy' combined within same scope. Enriched with confirmation that module loads vm2 and node_modules tampering is absent (distinguish payload from legitimate async libraries).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST to PraisonAI /a2a endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated network client can send a JSON-RPC request' to the /a2a endpoint. This is the primary attack delivery vector and should be detected at network ingress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /a2a* endpoints on ports 8000, 80, 443, 8080 from external IPs returning HTTP 200 without prior authentication. Correlate with uvicorn/python process spawns on target within milliseconds to confirm exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Child process spawning from uvicorn A2A server with eval() signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'LLM-driven eval() tool execution' leading to arbitrary command spawning. Python eval() execution followed by shell/utility child process creation is exploitation evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt shell interpreters (bash, zsh, cmd.exe, powershell) and utilities (curl, wget, nc) spawned from python/uvicorn parents running with a2a-server.py or praisonaiagents in command line. Elevated confidence if child process accesses credential files or API key environment variables.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI A2A server configured with 0.0.0.0 bind and missing auth_token
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'binds the server to 0.0.0.0' and 'without configuring auth_token' as two of three critical misconfigurations. This installation-phase configuration should be detected at process launch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on python/uvicorn process execution with a2a-server.py, praisonaiagents, or A2A+ keywords where command line binds to 0.0.0.0 and auth_token configuration is absent or commented.

suggestion.title: Credential exposure from API key environment variables post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article's Defender hunt explicitly includes detection for GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY access. Post-exploitation credential harvesting is a direct consequence of eval() RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt child processes of A2A server for env variable expansion, file reads to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_* patterns, or exfiltration attempts (curl/wget to external hosts) immediately after eval() execution signatures are observed.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Attribute access on print/builtins to retrieve __self__ reference
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states `print.__self__` is the escape vector to 'retrieve the real Python builtins module.' Detection of `__self__` attribute access on builtin functions or the `vars()` function calls post-access would catch earlier stages of exploitation before OS command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes (parent or child of praisonai) for ProcessCommandLine containing patterns like `__self__`, `vars(print`, or `getattr(print` followed by attribute enumeration. These are indicators of builtins-module reflection attacks.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Dynamic __import__ construction post-sandbox-escape attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes extraction of `__import__` via `vars()` and 'runtime string construction.' The construction of __import__() dynamically (e.g., via `__dict__`, string concatenation, or eval/exec) is distinct from static imports and indicates post-escape privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python process strings containing `vars()` followed by dynamic module access patterns (e.g., `["__import__"]`, string-built function calls, or `eval()`-style constructs within praisonai context) indicating module-loading after sandbox breakout.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Unexpected env / credential enumeration spawned by praisonai Python process
suggestion.rationale: Article implies arbitrary OS command execution post-escape. Use case UC_12_5 covers specific commands but misses the broader pattern: any discovery/enumeration command (printenv, env, cat /proc, ls -la, find, etc.) spawned by Python parent is abnormal and suggests exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by Python (parent=python/python3) where the child is an enumeration/discovery tool (printenv, env, hostname, id, uname, find, ls) AND the Python parent or grandparent is in a praisonai context (folder name, process name, or CWD contains 'praisonai'). This is abnormal for legitimate Python use.

suggestion.title: praisonai package installation via pip/poetry/conda
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'follow the documented quickstart' to deploy. No hunt captures the installation phase. Article phrase: 'Users who follow the documented quickstart (praisonai deploy --type api) get a server that...' implies installation precedes deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for pip/poetry/conda commands installing 'praisonai' package. Monitor for python -m pip install praisonai or similar. Captures supply-chain / first-deployment earlier than the deploy command itself.

suggestion.title: YAML/config file with 0.0.0.0 binding and port 8005
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability arises from 'binds to 0.0.0.0 per the recommended sample YAML'. No hunt detects this misconfiguration at the file level. Detecting dangerous config is higher-fidelity than behavioral post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for creation or modification of YAML/JSON/Python config files containing '0.0.0.0:8005' or '0.0.0.0' bound to port 8005. Correlate with praisonai process context. Detects misconfiguration before the service starts listening.

suggestion.title: praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code module execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names vulnerable code-generator: 'praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code emits a Flask API server with authentication disabled by default'. No hunt monitors imports or execution of this specific module, which is the root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Python interpreter executing or importing 'generate_api_server_code', 'praisonai.deploy.api', or related module paths. Monitor Python traceback logs for references to this module. Detects vulnerable code path directly.

suggestion.title: Flask application startup with debug=True or missing authentication middleware
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authentication disabled by default'. No hunt checks for source patterns indicating disabled auth (missing @auth_required decorators, debug=True, auth_enabled=False). Detects the vulnerability state before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Flask app files containing app.run(debug=True), app=Flask(__name__) with no auth middleware, or config with auth_enabled=False. Monitor generated api.py file creation in /tmp or user directories. Correlate with praisonai process.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability scan traffic to port 8005 (CVE-2026-47393 detection tooling)
suggestion.rationale: UC_13_5 mentions 'CVE-Detector scanner'. Article does not describe what legitimate detection tooling would scan for this CVE, but a secondary indicator would be known security scanner user-agents probing the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to port 8005 from known vulnerability scanner user-agents (Qualys, Nessus, OpenVAS, Shodan) or characteristic payload patterns (../, /api/, /swagger/, ?version=). Detects external reconnaissance of the vulnerable service.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform single-user rapid-fire nested-resource endpoint hits across multiple resource types
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability allows attackers to enumerate agents, issues, projects, labels, comments, and dependencies via IDOR. None of the existing UCs detect rapid sequential GET/PATCH requests across multiple resource types (agents → issues → projects → labels) by a single user within seconds, which is characteristic of IDOR fuzzing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: A single user or IP makes 10+ GET requests across different nested-resource types (/agents/*, /issues/*, /projects/*, /labels/*, /dependencies/*) within the same workspace within 30 seconds, with mixed 200/404 status codes — suggesting resource ID enumeration via sequential fuzzing rather than legitimate access patterns.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform workspace enumeration via 403 cascades on nested resources
suggestion.rationale: The article's vulnerability description implies that if an attacker is NOT a member of workspace X, the `require_workspace_member(workspace_id)` check fails. An attacker enumerating workspace IDs will trigger cascading 403 errors, forming a unique pattern not captured by the existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: A user repeatedly requests /api/v1/workspaces/{randomly-varying-uuid}/agents/* with 403 responses, then suddenly switches to 200 responses for a specific workspace ID — suggesting workspace ID enumeration followed by successful membership exploitation.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform comment or dependency resource IDOR cascade
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions comment_id and dependency_id as vulnerable nested resources but none of the UCs specifically target those resource types. Detection should focus on /comments/* and /dependencies/* endpoints which may have different access patterns than agents/projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: User makes GET requests to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/[comments|dependencies]/{id} with >5 distinct IDs in <1 minute, returning 200 across multiple IDs — suggesting direct resource enumeration without authorization re-check per resource.

suggestion.title: JWT token forgery via hardcoded key — abnormal authentication patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allowing token forgery for any user when PLATFORM_ENV is unset.' No hunt targets the exploitation itself (forged JWT tokens). Should detect authentication success with tokens signed by the hardcoded 'dev-secret-change-me' key or unusual account access following deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a praisonai-platform instance begins authenticating users with elevated privilege immediately after deployment of vulnerable version, or when JWT validation errors cease after credentials were previously invalid. Look for authentication logs showing account access from unexpected geographic locations or IPs in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Configuration drift: Missing PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET in production/staging environment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The JWT signing secret defaults to the hardcoded literal `"dev-secret-change-me"` when `PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET` is unset.' This is a discovery/defense-evasion indicator. Deployments in production clusters should always set this explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Kubernetes pods, Docker containers, or systemd services running praisonai-platform without PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET in their environment. Correlate process execution telemetry with configuration databases to flag deployments missing this variable.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Valid Accounts — post-JWT-forgery account assumption
suggestion.rationale: Article describes threat model where forged JWTs grant 'unauthorized access to any user account.' After forging a token, attacker assumes a high-privilege account (admin, workspace owner). Should detect unusual privilege escalation or lateral movement post-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a newly-authenticated user immediately performs administrative actions (workspace creation, user provisioning, role assignment) within praisonai-platform. Flag accounts with no prior privileged activity suddenly executing workspace deletions or bulk operations.

suggestion.title: Development environment escape — PLATFORM_ENV=dev in production deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A safety check exists but only fires when `PLATFORM_ENV != "dev"`; the default value of `PLATFORM_ENV` is `"dev"`, so the check is silently bypassed.' Explicit deployment of praisonai-platform with PLATFORM_ENV=dev in prod is a misconfiguration indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any praisonai-platform process launch in production Kubernetes clusters (indicated by node labels, namespace, or deployment metadata) with PLATFORM_ENV=dev or PLATFORM_ENV unset. Compare deployment environment (prod, staging, dev) against process environment variables.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'LinkedIn Social Engineering' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero detection for initial access phase despite title clearly establishing spear-phishing via LinkedIn as the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous LinkedIn profile interactions: newly created profiles with generic names (clones) rapid-fire messaging targets with specific job titles, profiles with no employment history messaging LinkedIn Premium users in target verticals, or messaging followed by external document sharing links.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Execution from Browser/Mail
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'custom macOS malware deployment' but pipeline generated zero detections for malware execution. This covers the execution phase after social engineering succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or gatekeeper-bypassed binary execution in macOS spawned from Safari, Mail, or Finder with parent processes unusual for legitimate workflows. Monitor for .app bundles or shell scripts executed from /tmp, /var/tmp, or Downloads directories immediately post-email or post-browser download.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Staging and Command-Line Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware implies local execution and potential obfuscation. Pipeline missed detection opportunities for persistence or execution-time artifacts described in malware analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash/zsh process spawning with suspicious arguments: curl/wget piped to bash, base64-encoded command arguments in zsh/bash, or suspicious launchd/cron modifications. Monitor for legitimate tools (curl, python, perl) being used as code delivery mechanisms from /tmp or user-writable paths.

suggestion.title: macOS Network Beaconing to Undocumented Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware typically establishes C2. Article body truncation prevents extraction of specific domains, but 'custom malware' implies command-and-control phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect macOS process establishing outbound HTTPS to rare/new domains (low historical prevalence), especially on non-standard ports or with unusual TLS fingerprints. Correlate browser process termination or mail process lifecycle with network egress to C2-like destinations.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake OAuth/Login Pages
suggestion.rationale: LinkedIn social engineering often includes credential theft; custom malware may drop phishing pages. Pipeline generated zero detections for credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with links to lookalike OAuth consent screens or LinkedIn login replicas served from attacker infrastructure. Monitor for attachment delivery of .scpt or .pkg files masquerading as job application confirmations, with high entropy or obfuscated content indicating code delivery.

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Threat Actor Attribution Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor name JINX-0164 is explicitly present in title but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or threat actor names. Attribution tracking is foundational for SOC workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain threat intelligence on JINX-0164 infrastructure and tactics: track previously-observed LinkedIn profile clones, malware hashes, C2 domains, and email sender addresses. Cross-correlate inbound emails/profile interactions with JINX actor IOC database and raise alerts on known attacker infrastructure or TTPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VS Code Process with Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states Kimsuky 'expands arsenal with VS Code Tunnels,' indicating abuse of legitimate Microsoft tooling for C2 and lateral movement. Standard endpoint baselines rarely flag VS Code spawning network connections or child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code.exe or codeserver process spawning child processes (cmd, powershell) or establishing network connections outside expected development workflows, particularly to non-standard ports. Correlate with absence of legitimate development context (IDE project files, git operations).

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Malware Deployment and Execution
suggestion.rationale: HTTPSpy is explicitly named as deployed tool but no detection logic was produced. Article indicates this is a primary C2/exfiltration mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPSpy binary creation, execution, and network signatures. Detect HTTP-based C2 communications with atypical User-Agent strings, malformed HTTP headers, or suspicious exfiltration patterns consistent with data-stealing malware.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Lateral Movement / Persistence
suggestion.rationale: HelloDoor is named in title but completely absent from pipeline analysis. Article context suggests this is a key element of the expanded toolkit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag deployment of HelloDoor binary via process creation, file write events, or network transfer. Monitor for lateral movement indicators following HelloDoor execution (SSH, RDP, WinRM abuse).

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Credential Phishing and Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Kimsuky 'expands arsenal'—typical Kimsuky pattern is spearphishing to establish initial access before deploying HTTPSpy/HelloDoor. Pipeline failed to reconstruct initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious email attachments (Office macros, LNK files) targeting known high-risk domains; correlate with subsequent VS Code, HTTPSpy, or HelloDoor execution within 1-24 hours. Flag accounts receiving spearphishing probing before campaigns.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Legitimate Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes VS Code Tunnels as part of 'expanded arsenal'—this represents masquerading (T1036) by abusing trusted developer tools. Pipeline did not flag this evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code tunnel activation outside office hours, from non-office IPs, or by users with no development-role indicators. Monitor for tunnel traffic tunneling non-development protocols (SMB, RDP, SSH) or exfiltration-pattern data flows.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious Sicoob NuGet'—poisoned package installation is the initial vector. Pipeline must detect NuGet restore/install operations from non-standard feeds or typosquatted package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag nuget.exe install, dotnet add package, or MSBuild restore operations targeting package sources outside Microsoft official feed or approved internal registry. Alert on version downgrades (legitimate v2.x → attacker v0.x), package names with character substitution (Newtonsoft.Json vs Newtonsoft.JSon), or packages with anomalous metadata (new maintainer, zero GitHub stars, publish date <7 days).

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Credential Access by Package Assembly Code
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Steals Banking Credentials'—compiled .NET code from malicious NuGet immediately accesses password stores, credential vaults, or environment variables storing banking/cloud credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET/dotnet.exe child processes spawned immediately after NuGet restore for: (1) CredentialManager API calls or %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials registry reads, (2) Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable() calls enumerating AWS_*, AZURE_*, GCP_* prefixes, (3) reads to %USERPROFILE%\.aws, %APPDATA%\docker, or cloud CLI config directories.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Hook Spawning Exfiltration Process
suggestion.rationale: Article headline includes 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets'—malicious npm postinstall scripts spawn PowerShell/curl/wget to harvest and transmit cloud credentials from development environment or CI/CD context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install postinstall/preinstall hook execution that spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, or wget with outbound network activity. Flag packages installed as transitive dependencies not explicitly in package.json. Alert on script execution reading environment variables and piping to curl/wget.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Exfiltration via HTTP/HTTPS C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'target cloud secrets' for theft—stolen credentials must be transmitted to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline should extract C2 domains, staging servers, or attacker-controlled paste sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests from package installation processes (NuGet, npm) to external domains with newly-registered DNS (<7 days), high-entropy domain names, or suspicious TLDs. Flag traffic containing URL-encoded environment variable patterns (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID) in query strings or POST bodies. Correlate with known credential-stealing malware C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion / Version Downgrade Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via package managers often exploit version confusion (internal package v2.x available → attacker publishes v0.x to public repo as fallback). Should detect before installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager lock files and download logs for: (1) version downgrades—legitimate version >1.0.0 suddenly installing 0.x, (2) packages fetched from public NuGet/npm when private enterprise feed is preferred, (3) mismatched package signatures or publisher certificates, (4) packages with maintainer account takeover indicators (new IP geolocation, unusual commit patterns).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment Variable Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'Cloud Secrets' as target—cloud credential environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, etc.) are being enumerated and exfiltrated by package code. This requires log-source awareness at OS level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command-line or API calls enumerating all environment variables (env command, Get-ChildItem Env:, getenv loops) within seconds of NuGet/npm installation completion. Flag for correlation with subsequent network egress or suspicious file writes to temp directories containing credential-like patterns.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing or Social Engineering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'AI-powered cyberattacks' — article body unavailable due to CSS truncation, but AI-assisted attack vectors typically manifest as unusually sophisticated phishing or pretexting. Should detect anomalous linguistic patterns, rapid iteration of similar messages, or statistical deviation from per-user baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound email or message campaigns with unusual sophistication-to-frequency ratio, or detection of LLM-generated text patterns (entropy, token-sequence novelty). Correlate sender reputation, TLD age, and body AI-fingerprinting tools.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Malware C2 Beacon Activity
suggestion.rationale: Any Russia-linked APT targeting Ukraine would establish command-and-control channels. Article title indicates active campaign; expect C2 callbacks, DNS tunneling, or HTTP beaconing typical of Russian-attributed tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to newly-registered or bulletproof-hosting domains, DNS queries for DGA-like patterns, or HTTP headers consistent with Russian APT malware families (Emotet, Turla, Gamaredon). Look for beaconing intervals and encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Living-off-the-Land Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Russian state actors typically abuse native Windows or Linux tools to avoid detection. Article mentions cyberattacks against Ukraine; expect T1059, T1047, or WMI abuse once initial access is achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cmd.exe, PowerShell, or wmic.exe with encoded payloads, unusual parent-child process chains (e.g., WINWORD spawning PowerShell), or Kerberos authentication anomalies (pass-the-hash, over-Kerberoasting).

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping or LSASS Access
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine-targeting campaigns from Russian APTs routinely perform credential harvesting post-compromise. Expected techniques include LSASS memory dumps or registry hives targeting SAM/SECURITY.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious lsass.exe access, in-memory dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump), or attempts to read %SystemRoot%\System32\config\SAM or SECURITY. Monitor for child processes of rundll32.exe targeting credential storage.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Encrypted Tunnels or Steganography
suggestion.rationale: Russian-attributed campaigns routinely exfiltrate data via VPN, Tor, or steganographic channels to avoid detection. Article title does not specify data theft, but Ukrainian infrastructure and defense organizations are high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous egress to VPN providers, Tor exit nodes, or high-entropy traffic. Monitor for DNS queries to privacy-oriented services. Flag large data transfers to external IPs during off-hours or from non-user assets.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry RunKeys, Scheduled Tasks, or WMI Event Subscriptions
suggestion.rationale: Once GREYVIBE establishes foothold in Ukraine, expect persistence mechanisms. Russian APT tradecraft includes WMI Event Subscriptions and scheduled tasks for resilient re-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and Run Once keys, new scheduled tasks with suspicious names or commands, and WMI Event Subscriptions (check WMI object classes EventFilter, EventConsumer, FilterToConsumerBinding).

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Scheduled Task Creation for Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task to Encrypt Local Drives'—scheduled task abuse is the attack vector; pipeline missed this entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on scheduled task creation/modification (SchTasks.exe or API calls) where the task executes under SYSTEM account with command-line arguments referencing file operations, encryption utilities, or batch file execution. Correlate against known ransomware command patterns.

suggestion.title: Data Encryption from Elevated Process (SYSTEM Context)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'With Elevated Privileges'—ransomware encrypting local drives under SYSTEM context is the impact phase; pipeline failed to map this to T1486.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file I/O patterns consistent with encryption (frequent write operations to known data directories, rapid file modification across multiple volumes) originating from SYSTEM or LOCAL SYSTEM process. Spike detection on file handle operations + entropy analysis on file writes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM for Ransomware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'With Elevated Privileges'—the ransomware achieves SYSTEM-level execution, likely a privilege escalation step preceding scheduled task abuse; pipeline missed T1548 family techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution spawning under SYSTEM context (e.g., via service start, scheduled task trigger, token impersonation). Correlate parent process (e.g., initial entry point) with SYSTEM child to identify privilege escalation. Alert if SYSTEM-spawned process then creates/modifies additional scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Command-Line Targeting Local Drives
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Encrypt Local Drives'—the scheduled task payload targets specific drive letters or mount points; pipeline did not suggest drive-targeting detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse scheduled task creation events for command arguments containing drive letters (C:, D:, E:, etc.), volume mount paths, or wildcard patterns. Alert on tasks with obfuscated commands, encoded payloads, or references to encryption-related binaries (e.g., cipher.exe, vssadmin.exe for shadow copy deletion as precursor).

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse for Malware/Phishing Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Leverage ChatGPT ... to Fuel Cyberattacks'. Pipeline generated zero detections despite this clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency API calls to OpenAI endpoints (api.openai.com) from suspicious sources or insider accounts. Flag sessions with repeated malware/phishing generation prompts or suspicious payload generation requests within ChatGPT conversations.

suggestion.title: Google Gemini API Abuse for Attack Payload Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Google Gemini' as tool for cyberattacks. No detection logic generated despite clear adversary tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Cloud API logs for Gemini API calls with prompts requesting malware code, phishing templates, or social-engineering scripts. Correlate with downstream file creation or email delivery.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / Jailbreak Attempts Against LLM APIs
suggestion.rationale: Adversary leverage of ChatGPT/Gemini implies prompt-injection or jailbreak techniques to bypass safety guardrails; none captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests containing known jailbreak patterns (e.g., 'ignore your instructions', 'roleplay as', 'assume developer mode') or prompt-injection markers in payloads to OpenAI/Google endpoints.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Campaign Tracking & C2 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor 'GREYVIBE' explicitly named in title but never mapped to any campaign signature, known infrastructure, or command-and-control indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline signatures for GREYVIBE infrastructure (domains, IPs, ASNs) from threat intel feeds and correlate with internal network traffic. Alert on connections to previously-observed C2 nodes.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Admin Authentication via Override Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'hackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account.' This is the primary attack vector and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect authentication logs for successful authentications to local administrator accounts, especially when override cookies are the authentication method. Flag all such events as override cookies should never be used for interactive admin access.

suggestion.title: Public Key Extraction from GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack mechanism: 'attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies.' This extraction step precedes the forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests that enumerate or retrieve SSL/TLS certificate material from GlobalProtect gateways and portals. Flag patterns where certificate data is accessed and then rapidly followed by authentication override attempts.

suggestion.title: VPN Session Establishment Following Forged Cookie Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks.' VPN session success after suspicious auth is the critical compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication events using override cookies (especially to admin accounts) with successful VPN tunnel establishment. Alert on any instance where VPN session is established without prior interactive gateway login.

suggestion.title: Failed VPN Session Setup After Successful Override Cookie Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session' in many incidents. Partial compromise attempts show the attack pattern even when unsuccessful.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify exploitation attempts via sequences of: successful override-cookie authentication → failed VPN session establishment → retry attempts within minutes. This pattern indicates active exploitation even when full access is not achieved.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication from Vultr and Dromatics Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article documents two identified attack sources: 'first observed exploitation on May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave of attacks detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems.' These are corroborated IoCs for threat hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any GlobalProtect authentication attempts (especially override-cookie auth) originating from Vultr ASN 20473 and Dromatics Systems infrastructure. Escalate immediately to incident response if authentication succeeds, as this matches known active exploitation infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Authentication Override Cookie Configuration Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'the flaw requires devices to be configured with authentication override cookies enabled and a specific certificate configuration.' Identifying vulnerable configurations is essential for scoping and prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all GlobalProtect gateways and portals to identify which have authentication override cookies enabled. For enabled instances, verify whether the same certificate is used for both HTTPS and override cookies. Flag as vulnerable if certificates are shared or if CVE-2026-0257 patches have not been applied.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Authentication Bypass' as the core vulnerability and states it is 'under active exploitation.' Pipeline produced zero use cases for detecting exploitation of the bypass itself—expects credential-less access or malformed auth tokens against GlobalProtect endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to GlobalProtect gateways (URIs: /globalprotect/*, /ssl-vpn/*) that either succeed without proper SAML/LDAP credential exchange, show repeated authentication failures followed by sudden success, or contain malformed authentication tokens indicative of bypass payloads.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Version Enumeration and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain begins with reconnaissance. Article mentions specific CVE (2026-0257) affecting PAN-OS; attackers must first discover vulnerable versions. Zero detection use cases for version fingerprinting or banner grabbing against GlobalProtect services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port 443 TLS banner grabs on GlobalProtect gateways, HTTP OPTIONS/HEAD requests to /globalprotect/ paths, parsing of version strings from HTTP response headers or HTTP 401/403 error pages containing PAN-OS identifiers.

suggestion.title: Post-VPN-Bypass Internal Lateral Movement and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation is active and ongoing. After authentication bypass, attackers pivot internally—zero use cases for detecting post-connection reconnaissance (network scans, credential enumeration, high-value target access) originating from VPN-authenticated sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous activity within 10 minutes of GlobalProtect session establishment: port scanning (nmap, masscan), LDAP/SMB enumeration queries (net view, dsquery), privileged credential requests, or connections to subnets not previously accessed by that user.

suggestion.title: Anomalous VPN Session Profile Matching Active Attacker Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies attacker-controlled sessions with non-standard patterns. Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting behavioral deviations: off-hours login, geographically impossible travel, concurrent multi-session logins, non-human client fingerprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GlobalProtect authentication events where: user logs in from country X at time T and country Y at time T+15 minutes (impossible travel), session duration >6 hours (atypical for interactive users), or client TLS fingerprint does not match known legitimate VPN client software.

suggestion.title: Command Execution and Payload Delivery via Authenticated VPN Tunnel
suggestion.rationale: Post-bypass, attackers execute commands or transfer tools through the VPN. Zero use cases for detecting command execution (PowerShell, bash, cmd.exe) or binary transfer initiated by VPN client IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation on internal systems with parent process or initiating network session tied to GlobalProtect VPN IP: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash execution within 2 minutes of VPN session start; also large inbound file transfers (>50MB) from external IPs routed through authenticated VPN.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Configuration/Credential Exfiltration Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers who bypass authentication may attempt to extract VPN credentials, policy configurations, or internal network maps from compromised PAN-OS appliances or client systems for follow-on attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access patterns on PAN-OS config directories (/opt/pancfg/*, /config/*) from non-privileged accounts, reads of PAN-OS .key or .xml policy files, or exfiltration of logs/credential caches from VPN client processes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code Repository Access and Compression
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'exfiltrate source code' and pipeline generated zero collection-phase detections. Typical attack: unauthorized git clone, repository archive (tar/zip), or bulk file copy targeting .git directories and source trees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git client (git.exe, git) or archiving tools (tar, zip, 7z) invoked by developer-account processes reading large volumes of source-tree files, especially outside business hours or from unexpected IP/geographic regions. Correlate: file-read volume spike on .git, .java, .py, .cpp, go.mod, pom.xml files followed by archive-creation or curl/wget uploads within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Secrets File Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'exfiltrate secrets'; pipeline missed detection for .env, API keys, certificates, and credentials. Phrase: 'Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor read-access to secret-storage locations (.env, .aws/credentials, .ssh, ~/.config/gcloud, Azure KeyVault calls, HashiCorp Vault queries) by developer processes, especially when followed by process spawning network exfiltration (curl, wget, Invoke-WebRequest). Flag if file-read timestamps cluster within 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Trusted Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Trusted tooling includes package managers (npm, pip, gradle); attackers abuse them to inject backdoors or exfil credentials. Pipeline should flag this execution vector but did not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm, pip, maven, or gradle spawning curl/wget to non-standard registries or attacker-controlled domains. Monitor package.json, requirements.txt, build.gradle modifications immediately before install commands. Alert on package-install attempts pointing to typosquatted or compromised registry endpoints (e.g., 'npmjs-official.com' vs 'npmjs.com').

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Hijacking and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Trusted developer tooling runs in CI/CD agents (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab Runners); compromise enables silent exfiltration. Title implies tool abuse; pipeline missed this execution and collection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows, GitLab pipelines, and Jenkins jobs for unauthorized modifications to secret-access, curl/wget invocations to external IPs, or additions of env-var exports to external endpoints. Detect runner agents invoking credential-dumping tools (git config --global, aws sts get-caller-identity, env | grep -i key). Alert on commits to .github/workflows or Jenkinsfile from unusual committer email or IP.

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Lateral Movement via Compromised Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Source exfiltration follows credential compromise (phishing, supply-chain attack). Pipeline should flag anomalous sign-ins and MFA bypass preceding access to code repos and secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: multiple failed MFA attempts or sign-in failures from external IP within 30 minutes, followed by successful authentication to GitHub, GitLab, or Artifactory from the same source, accessed from non-corporate network. Flag logins from cloud-shell services (AWS CloudShell, Azure CloudShell) as suspicious entry points for developer credentials.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration phase: source code and secrets offboarded to S3, Azure Blob, Dropbox, or attacker infrastructure. Title uses verb 'exfiltrate'; pipeline missed the final exfil-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on source-tree files (.git, .java, .py, .cpp, requirements.txt, pom.xml, .env) being compressed and uploaded to external cloud services (S3 put-object, Azure Blob upload, OneDrive/Dropbox API calls) within short time windows. Correlate with antecedent file-read events on secret-storage. Suppress known CD/CD pipeline transfers via IP allowlist.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as initial attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection logic for exploitation of this public-facing application vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Marimo instances for payloads targeting CVE-2026-39987. Establish baseline of legitimate Marimo API calls, then alert on anomalous request patterns, encoded inputs, or known exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: LLM Model Inference Process Spawned Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers deploying 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation' but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection. LLM inference must be detected as suspicious subprocess activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LLM framework execution (Python subprocess, ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, or similar) spawned from or within Marimo process context. Alert on process command lines containing model names (claude, gpt, llama, mistral) or LLM API calls in environment variables.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Credential or Local-File Access
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attack implies data/credential theft via LLM agent. Article context suggests LLM reading environment or filesystem but no credential-access detection case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-access events from LLM agent processes targeting .env files, /etc/passwd, AWS credential paths, SSH keys, or Windows credential stores (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Environment, LSA). Correlate timing with Marimo exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Communication from LLM Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation implies command-and-control or exfiltration. Article title confirms attacker control via LLM but no network-detection case was created for C2 or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/DNS/raw connections from LLM inference processes to external LLM API endpoints or C2 infrastructure. Flag exfiltration of local system data (environment variables, file contents, command output) embedded in API requests or DNS queries.

suggestion.title: Shell or Interpreter Execution from Marimo Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker control via LLM agent would require shell or interpreter spawning for post-exploitation commands. Article does not explicitly detail this but is typical of post-ex. No execution-level detection for interactive shells was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bash, sh, powershell, python, or perl child processes spawned by Marimo or LLM agent processes. Alert on high-entropy or obfuscated command lines. Baseline expected Marimo interpreter usage in your environment first.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing to Azure AD Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account'—this is the documented entry vector and should be detectable via sign-in anomalies post-vishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Entra sign-ins from impossible travel distance, new IP ranges, or off-hours access immediately following suspected voice communication attempts. Correlate employee phone call logs with subsequent auth events from atypical geolocations within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk Salesforce Data Export by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actors 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance'—indicates lateral movement into cloud CRM and mass data collection from single account session.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Salesforce reports or bulk exports accessing >10k records in a single session from the compromised user. Alert on non-standard API calls or data downloads with customer PII schemas (name, email, phone, address fields) in high volume.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Monitoring for Leaked Credential Dumps
